John Hamilton (artist)

John Hamilton was born in England in 1919 and was educated at Bradfield College. Throughout World War II, he served in the British Army in India as a member of the Queen's Royal Regiment. As a junior officer at the age of 24, he received the Military Cross for gallantry during active operations against the enemy. Following his army service, he began a business career and settled in 1961 on the island of Tresco in the Isles of Scilly, Cornwall, where he sketched and painted for relaxation. In 1972, after a bout with angina, he sold his business and began painting on a full-time basis.

He began by selling his work to tourists, who visited the Isles of Scilly in the English Channel, specializing at first in painting the local topography, seascapes, traditional ships, and boats. Increasingly interested in the naval battles of World War II, in 1972 he began to paint a series of historical paintings on the War in the Atlantic, undertaking extensive archival research in London, Washington, and Stuttgart, and interviewing survivors. After seven years of work, he completed this 84-painting series at the end of 1978. Through the generosity of several shipping companies and the HMS Belfast Trust, his series of paintings is now in the collection of the Imperial War Museum, London, on board the museum ship HMS Belfast. On the completion of the Atlantic series, Hamilton started work on a new series of paintings on the War in the Pacific, widening his archival researches and interviewing to Canberra and Tokyo with extensive research work at the Naval Historical Center in Washington, D.C., With the help of foundations in Texas, Hamilton completed more than 120 paintings in five years. This collection is now part of the U.S. Navy Art Collection. 176 of the total 204 paintings in the two series were published in Hamilton's book War at Sea, 1939-1945. After completing his work on World War II, Hamilton turned to the more recent Falklands War and a study of the uses of the helicopter during that conflict. This project required three visits to the Falkland Islands and four years to produce 46 paintings. In his 70s, he developed an interest in the Antarctic and spent two winters there on board HMS Endurance (A171), painting the scenery and doing historical paintings of Sir Ernest Shackleton's expedition using the evidence of surviving buildings, in addition to research, to recreate historical scenes. In this work, he became a key figure in inspiring the organisation of the UK Antarctic Heritage Trust.

Country capers: short stories and verses (1979) War at sea, 1939-1945 (1986) Sketching with a pencil: for those who are just beginning (1989) The Helicopter Story of The Falklands Campaign (1991) Sketching at home: for those who are just beginning (1991) The complete sketching book (1996)

The latest release of the Enterprise Suite, version 7.4.2, became available on October 5, 2026. This update addresses several performance bottlenecks reported in the previous build and introduces new capabilities that improve workflow automation across the platform.

Key performance enhancements include a 20% reduction in database query latency and optimized memory usage during peak concurrent sessions. Users should notice faster report generation times and smoother navigation in high-traffic dashboards, particularly when handling large data sets.

The release also adds support for the new OAuth 2.0 token refresh flow, enabling seamless single-sign-on with third-party identity providers. Administrators can configure this feature via the Security Settings panel, and documentation has been updated to reflect the required configuration steps.

A known issue remains with the mobile client on Android 13, where push notifications may be delayed by up to two minutes under low-battery conditions. Our engineering team is prioritizing a fix for the upcoming 7.4.3 patch, scheduled for release in early November.

All users are advised to back up critical data before applying the update and to review the release notes for any configuration changes that may affect custom integrations. The update can be deployed through the standard auto-update mechanism, or manually via the admin console.

For further assistance, contact the support desk at support@example.com or call the 24-hour hotline. We appreciate your cooperation in keeping the system secure and efficient.

Subject: Thoughts on strengthening our backup routine
Hi Team,
I've been reviewing our current data management workflows and noticed a few gaps that could expose us to unnecessary risk. Specifically, we still rely heavily on manual nightly backups that occasionally skip files if the server load is high. I think it is time we transition to an automated, incremental approach to ensure nothing slips through the cracks.
The primary concern here is not just the risk of hardware failure, but the human error factor. We have had two close calls recently where critical client documents were accidentally deleted and were too old to restore from our existing archives. The Central Public Library is implementing immediate updates to its book return protocols to ensure smoother circulation and reduced wait times for all patrons. Effective as of next Monday, late fees will begin accruing immediately one hour after the standard 5:00 PM daily closing time. This adjustment is designed to align with actual staff processing hours and to mitigate the backlog that often accumulates during peak evening periods.

Patrons are strongly encouraged to utilize the newly installed outdoor drop-off kiosk located near the main entrance. This secure unit is accessible twenty-four hours a day and allows for the convenient return of materials without entering the building. Please note that these kiosk slots are strictly for items currently on loan from our branches. Do not attempt to deposit bags, packages, or unclaimed materials into the return bins at any time.

Overdue fines serve primarily as an incentive for timely returns rather than a revenue source for the institution. However, persistent non-return of items may result in suspension of borrowing privileges. If your item becomes overdue, please check your account online to verify the status. Unclaimed fines over fifty dollars will trigger an automatic hold on new checkouts until the balance is settled in full.

We have also expanded our digital return options through the library's mobile application. Users can now extend their due dates for most popular titles directly via their smartphones, provided no other patron has placed a hold on the item. This feature helps prevent unexpected late notices and ensures that materials remain available to the community for longer periods when demand is low.

For any questions regarding specific due dates or damage assessments, please contact the front desk staff during regular operating hours. Our team is always ready to assist with requests and to help resolve any misunderstandings regarding your account status. Thank you for your continued cooperation in maintaining an efficient and fair lending system for everyone.

Francis D. Lyon

Francis D. "Pete" Lyon (July 29, 1905 - October 8, 1996) was an American film director, television director, and film editor. He and Robert Parrish were co-recipients of the Academy Award for Best Film Editing for the 1947 film, Body and Soul.

Lyon was born in Bowbells, North Dakota. He moved to California to attend UCLA. After graduation, he moved to England to begin his career in film. He returned to the US and from the early 1930s to the 1950s, Lyon was exclusively an editor, except for one uncredited acting role in 1932. He worked on 29 films as an assistant editor or editor, including The Men in Her Life (1941), Body and Soul (1947) and The Young and The Brave (1963). He moved on to directing, and co-founded United Pictures Corporation in 1966. He was credited on more than 20 additional films before retiring from the entertainment industry in 1970. In 1993, Lyon published a memoir entitled Twists of Fate: An Oscar Winner's International Career. Lyon died on October 8, 1996, in Green Valley, Arizona.

Lyon received director credit on 42 episodes of 17 different US television series in the period from 1952 to 1964, plus being credited as the director of the first year's production (25 episodes) of the Walt Disney production The Adventures of Spin and Marty.

Subject: Update on the Golden Retriever puppy from Tuesday's visit
Dear Ms. Harrison,
I am writing to share some exciting news regarding our interest in adopting the three-month-old Golden Retriever puppy we met at the Happy Tails Shelter last week. As I mentioned at the time of our initial consultation, I have been revisiting the idea of welcoming a dog into our home after a long period of careful consideration. The moment saw us spend over an hour in the adoption center, interacting with several different animals. While we loved the high energy of the Beagles, it was the calm and gentle demeanor of the puppy, whom the staff named Max, that truly captured our attention. He did not bark or whine, but instead watched us with a steady gaze that suggested he understands the concept of waiting.
We have spent the last few days preparing our living space to ensure it is safe and comfortable for a young dog. I have secured the fence in the backyard and removed any small items that could be mistakenly ingested from the lower shelves. My partner, Sarah, has also researched local veterinarians who specialize in pediatric care and has secured a preliminary appointment for next Thursday. We believe that establishing a trusted medical relationship early on is crucial for the puppy's long-term health and development. It is equally important to us to begin house training and basic obedience commands immediately, which is why we have booked sessions with a certified positive reinforcement trainer who operates in our neighborhood.
Financially, we have prepared a detailed budget that accounts for initial costs such as the adoption fee, necessary supplies including crates and food, and estimated monthly expenses for premium kibble and preventive health care. We understand that pet ownership is a significant financial commitment that requires ongoing diligence and responsibility. We have set up an automatic transfer to a dedicated savings account specifically for pet-related emergencies, ensuring that we are prepared for any unforeseen veterinary bills that might arise. This administrative preparation gives us the peace of mind to focus entirely on the bonding process with the new family member.
During our visit, the shelter volunteer mentioned that Max has a minor congenital condition that will require monitoring but is manageable with proper diet and regular check-ups. We found this information reassuring rather than discouraging, as it aligns with our desire to provide a stable and attentive home for an animal that needs extra care. We are fully committed to following the specific dietary guidelines provided by the shelter's medical team. Please let us know if there are any additional health records or background information you would like us to review before we finalize the adoption paperwork. We are eager to proceed whenever it is convenient for your team.
Thank you for your patience and for allowing us to revisit our application. We remain deeply interested in providing a loving and permanent home for Max. Please feel free to contact us at your earliest convenience to schedule a pick-up or a final meeting to discuss the next steps. We look forward to hearing from you soon and hope to be part of the Happy Tails community soon.
Sincerely,
David Miller

This notice informs all employees, contractors, and visitors that a planned interruption of electrical service will occur at the main office building on Tuesday, October 15, 2026, beginning at 10:00 p.m. and expected to last until approximately 4:00 a.m. the following morning, and will affect all floors.

The outage is required to allow the utility provider to upgrade transformer equipment and replace aging cables that have been identified as potential fire hazards. The work will be performed by certified technicians following all safety regulations and industry best practices.

During the outage, essential systems such as emergency lighting, fire alarms, and security cameras will be powered by backup generators. However, non-essential equipment, including computers, printers, kitchen appliances, and HVAC controls, will be unavailable until power is restored.

Please ensure that all electronic devices are properly shut down and unplugged before the outage begins. Store any sensitive data, back up critical files, and refrain from using elevators after 9:45 p.m. to avoid being trapped.

If you have any special accommodation needs, such as medical equipment that requires continuous power, contact Facilities Management at extension 3120 no later than October 12. We will arrange alternative power solutions or temporary relocation as necessary.

We apologize for any inconvenience this essential maintenance may cause and appreciate your cooperation. Further updates will be communicated promptly if the schedule changes unexpectedly.

Kelli White

Kelli White (born April 1, 1977, in Oakland, California) is an American former sprinter. She won two gold medals in the World Championships in Paris in 2003. However, on June 18, 2004, she was stripped of her medals, because she tested positive on a drug test. She retired from professional track in 2006.

White's parents had both been sprinters. Her mother, Debbie Byfield, competed at the 1972 Summer Olympics. She attended James Logan High School in Union City, California, where she was on the track team. In 1994, when she was 17, a fellow student slashed her face with a knife; 300 stitches were required to close the wounds. White continued competing that season. Although she never won a state championship, at the time of her graduation in 1995 she held the top time in the 200 meters and the second best time in the 100 meters in the North Coast Section. She received a scholarship to the University of Tennessee, graduating in 1999.

After her positive test, White admitted guilt and testified before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS). All her performances since December 15, 2000, were annulled. She was banned for two years by the United States Anti-Doping Agency, effective May 17, 2004. Her doping was linked to the BALCO doping scandal. After returning from college to the San Francisco Bay Area in 2000, White's long-time coach, Remi Korchemny, introduced her to BALCO head Victor Conte. White has reported that Conte provided her with products that he identified as supplements and vitamins at first; when he informed her that one was a steroid, she declined to use it then and did not begin doping until after an injury-plagued, losing year in 2002. After being confronted with evidence seized from BALCO, she admitted using tetrahydrogestrinone (THG) and erythropoietin (EPO) in addition to modafinil. White has since given lectures on drug abuse in sports around the world. She became the first athlete to work directly with the United States Anti-Doping Agency to help it understand the system and culture of doping at the elite competition level. While banned from competition, she has taught at track clinics at James Logan High. She announced her retirement in May 2006.

Kelli White at World Athletics Paragraph about White's involvement in the BALCO scandal (USATODAY) U.S, House of Representatives, Government Reform Committee, Hearing on Steroid Use Among Women, "Testimony of Sprinter Kelli White,"2005-06-15

Our team is in constant communication with all our shipping partners, closely monitoring the situation to identify and resolve potential issues quickly. We are exploring every available option to expedite shipments and ensure your items reach you as safely and promptly as possible.

We kindly ask for your continued patience as we navigate these industry-wide challenges. Please regularly check your tracking number for the most up-to-date information. Your order is important to us, and it is on its way.

Thank you for your continued trust and support. We are committed to providing you with the best service possible despite these unforeseen hurdles.

Halla Pai Huhm

Halla Pai Huhm (Korean: 함한라; alternately, Halla Huhm, Pai Halla, or Pae Yŏng-ja; 1922-1994) was a Korean-American dancer and the most well-known teacher of Korean dance in Hawaii. She established the Halla Pai Huhm dance studio, and after her death, the Halla Pai Huhm Foundation's Dance Collection was started from her collection of documents, photographs, and recordings. The archival collection was named a U.S. Irreplaceable Dance Treasure in 2001.

Born in Busan, Pai Huhm moved to Japan with four siblings when she was five and was raised by her father's niece, Pai Ku-ja 배구자(裵龜子, 1905년 ~ 2003년.) Pai was a dancer who taught Huhm the foundations of modern, Japanese, and Korean dance. When World War II broke out, she returned to Korea. She studied Korean dance with Han Sung-jin and other masters, and continued her studies even after she immigrated to Hawaii in 1949. Huhm would regularly travel back to Korea as part of her job at a travel agency, and used this time to further her studies.

.

Huhm moved to Hawaii in 1949 to follow her husband, a Korean-American soldier. Huhm first appeared in Honolulu's theater scene during a production of Teahouse of the Autumn Moon at the Honolulu Community Theatre in 1954. She started teaching Korean dance informally in 1950, but by 1960 she had established a dance studio. She struggled to keep it open due to lack of financial support. This can be attributed to a belief at the time that only kisaeng dance. The studio's early struggles could also be attributed to local Koreans view that Huhm was "too Japanese" because she spoke fluent Japanese and got along well with members of the Japanese community. She kept the studio afloat using funds from her job at a travel agency. In 1959, she began teaching Korean dance at the University of Hawaii at Manoa. She stopped teaching at the University in the 1970s, but maintained close ties with their Korean Studies Center. In 1983 she taught Korean dance at the Chongju University of Education. Huhm taught dance not only to preserve Korean dance in Hawaii, but also to pass on the traditions and values of her culture. Some of her most well-known collaborations were with Cheon-Heung Kim 김천흥(金千興, 1909년 3월 30일 ~ 2007년 8월 18일), a dancer specializing in Korean court dances; and Ji San Lee, a shaman.

The Halla Pai Huhm Korean Dance Studio is "the only continuous source of Korean dance and music in the United States". Huhm was the first recipient of the Outstanding Korean in Hawaii award. She also received a cultural medal from the South Korean government in 1980. Huhm died in 1994, and her memory was celebrated during several dance events planned by Mary Jo Freshley who continues to teach and run the studio. The Halla Pai Huhm Foundation was named in her honor, and includes the studio she ran. It also includes an archive of documents and memorabilia Huhm collected. The archival collection was named a U.S. Irreplaceable Dance Treasure in 2001, and received grants to preserve the items in Hawaii's humid climate. In 2013, Billie Lee made a documentary on Halla's work entitled, "Moving Home: The Legacy of Halla Pai Huhm."

The recent audit of our residential portfolio reveals inconsistent insulation standards across several units. Specific attention is required for the older Victorian properties where the original loft voids remain largely unobstructed but under-filled with outdated materials. Current thermal imaging indicates significant heat loss through the eaves and dormer windows. Immediate remediation is necessary to meet updated energy efficiency targets and reduce operational heating costs for the coming winter season.

Staff are advised to prioritize the installation of mineral wool batts in accessible areas before considering more invasive measures. This method offers a high performance-to-cost ratio and is safe for immediate occupancy once properly fitted. Technicians must ensure that all pipes in the attic are wrapped in thermal lagging prior to adding the new insulation layers. This step prevents condensation buildup, which can compromise both the integrity of the new material and the structural elements of the roof over time.

For the second-floor rooms, expanding foam injection into the wall cavities should only be authorized after two independent leak tests. The process is effective but carries a higher risk of pressure buildup if the preservative packaging is compromised. We have documented instances where improper application led to minor plaster displacement. Strict adherence to the manufacturer's expansion rate guidelines is mandatory to avoid damaging the internal finishes of these occupied spaces.

Ground floor assessments indicate that many properties still rely on concrete slabs with insufficient damp-proof course implementation. While full removal and replacement is rarely feasible without major disruption, we recommend applying high-density spray foam to the underside of existing flooring where voids permit. This approach minimizes tenant inconvenience while significantly lowering U-values. Documentation of before-and-after thermal scans is required for every completed job site to verify compliance with the new regulatory benchmarks.

All contractors must submit their scope of work via the digital portal by the end of this month for approval. Delays in submission will result in the project being deferred to the next fiscal quarter. Please refer to the attached safety data sheets for handling insulating materials correctly. We rely on everyone maintaining the high standard of workmanship that defines our reputation. Thank you for your diligence in executing these critical improvements for the comfort and safety of our residents.

Staff are advised to prioritize the installation of mineral wool batts in accessible areas before considering more invasive measures. This method offers a high performance-to-cost ratio and is safe for immediate occupancy once properly fitted. Technicians must ensure that all pipes in the attic are wrapped in thermal lagging prior to adding the new insulation layers. This step prevents condensation buildup, which can compromise both the integrity of the new material and the structural elements of the roof over time.

For the second-floor rooms, expanding foam injection into the wall cavities should only be authorized after two independent leak tests. The process is effective but carries a higher risk of pressure buildup if the preservative packaging is compromised. We have documented instances where improper application led to minor plaster displacement. Strict adherence to the manufacturer's expansion rate guidelines is mandatory to avoid damaging the internal finishes of these occupied spaces.

Ground floor assessments indicate that many properties still rely on concrete slabs with insufficient damp-proof course implementation. While full removal and replacement is rarely feasible without major disruption, we recommend applying high-density spray foam to the underside of existing flooring where voids permit. This approach minimizes tenant inconvenience while significantly lowering U-values. Documentation of before-and-after thermal scans is required for every completed job site to verify compliance with the new regulatory benchmarks.

All contractors must submit their scope of work via the digital portal by the end of this month for approval. Delays in submission will result in the project being deferred to the next fiscal quarter. Please refer to the attached safety data sheets for handling insulating materials correctly. We rely on everyone maintaining the high standard of workmanship that defines our reputation. Thank you for your diligence in executing these critical improvements for the comfort and safety of our residents.

Ptychagnostus

Ptychagnostus is a genus of trilobites in the order Agnostida that lived during the Cambrian period. Their remains are rarely found in empty tubes of the polychaete worm Selkirkia. The genus probably ranged throughout the water column. It has two glabellar lobes, and three pygidial lobes.

Agnostus punctuosus Angelin, 1851 from the Ptychagnostus punctuosus zone of the Alum Shale (Drumian), Sweden (by original designation). Official ruling on the conservation of accepted usage of A. punctuosus as the type species was given by the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature, 1993.

Ptychagnostus affinis (Brøgger 1878) was once considered a subspecies of Ptychagnostus punctuosus.Laurie (2008) grouped punctuosus and affinis within Ptychagnostus, but preferred to place the closely related atavus within Acidusus.

"Ptychagnostus praecurrens". Burgess Shale Fossil Gallery. Virtual Museum of Canada. 2011. Archived from the original on 2020-11-12. Retrieved 2023-01-21. Media related to Ptychagnostus at Wikimedia Commons

When initiating a password reset, users must first ensure they have access to the verified email address or mobile phone number associated with their account. This verification step is the primary security gate intended to confirm identity before any credentials are altered. If you do not control these recovery contact methods, you cannot proceed with the standard online reset process. In such cases, you must contact your department's Information Security Office directly to arrange manual authentication and account recovery. Do not attempt to use unverified or former work email addresses, as these will result in immediate rejection of the reset token.

Once the verification code is received, enter it precisely within the ten-minute expiration window. The system will then prompt you to create a new password that meets the current organizational complexity requirements. These criteria typically mandate a minimum length of twelve characters, including a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols. Avoid using personal information such as names, birthdays, or common dictionary words, as these are the first targets for automated guessing attacks. Strong, random, and unique passwords significantly reduce the likelihood of compromise through brute force techniques.

It is critical never to reuse a previous password or apply the same credential across multiple services. Account linking through password reuse is a leading cause of widespread breaches, allowing attackers to cascade access from a single compromised service to others. For better security and convenience, consider utilizing an enterprise-approved password manager to generate and store complex credentials. These tools reduce cognitive load by eliminating the need to memorize each individual string while ensuring that every password remains distinct and unguessable. Regularly updating your master password in the manager adds another layer of protection for your entire digital footprint.

After successfully setting the new password, log out of all active sessions on all devices to invalidate old tokens. Then, log back in to verify that the new credentials function correctly across web and mobile applications. If you encounter repeated login failures, check for capitalization lock errors or keyboard layout mismatches. Persistence is key, but after three failed attempts, the account may lock automatically to prevent malicious attempts. If locking occurs, wait the designated cool-off period or seek assistance from IT support to resolve the access issue without triggering further security alerts.

Security is a continuous process, not a one-time event. Review your account activity regularly to ensure no unauthorized sessions are active. Enable multi-factor authentication if it is available for your role, as this provides a second layer of defense against password theft. Stay informed about current phishing tactics, as no amount of password strength can protect you if you voluntarily disclose your credentials to fraudulent sites. By combining robust password practices with vigilant behavior, you help safeguard not only your personal data but also the integrity of the entire organizational network.

raw:
team offsite agenda

A well-planned team offsite can turn a routine retreat into a catalyst for innovation, morale, and alignment. The agenda should start early, giving participants time to settle in and absorb the day's purpose before diving into activities. A short welcome session, led by the manager, outlines the objectives, reinforces core values, and sets a collaborative tone for the day.

The first working block typically focuses on reflection, allowing each team member to share recent wins, challenges, and personal insights. By creating a safe space for honest conversation, the group builds trust and uncovers hidden opportunities for improvement. A facilitator can guide the discussion with targeted prompts that keep the dialogue focused and productive.

Mid-morning is the ideal moment for a creative workshop that tackles a current business problem. Small groups brainstorm solutions, sketch prototypes, or run quick experiments, then reconvene to present findings. This hands-on segment not only sparks fresh ideas but also demonstrates the power of cross-functional collaboration in real time.

After a relaxed lunch, the agenda shifts to strategy planning, where leaders present the upcoming quarter's goals and solicit input on priorities. The team reviews key metrics, aligns on milestones, and assigns ownership, ensuring everyone knows how their work contributes to the larger picture.

The day concludes with a fun, low-pressure activity-perhaps a short hike, a group game, or a casual dinner-followed by a brief wrap-up. The facilitator recaps decisions, highlights action items, and gathers feedback on the offsite itself, setting the stage for continuous improvement in future gatherings.

raw:
bridge maintenance notice

The Department of Transportation has announced an upcoming maintenance window for the Riverside Bridge, scheduled to begin on June 15th and expected to continue through June 30th. During this period, crews will be conducting essential structural repairs and repainting the steel framework to ensure long-term durability. This work is part of a comprehensive five-year infrastructure plan aimed at preserving the safety and functionality of major crossings in the metropolitan area. Residents and commuters should anticipate minor inconveniences as preparations for the project get underway.

Traffic will be reduced to one lane in each direction for the majority of the work period. Detours will be clearly marked with orange signage directing local traffic onto adjacent parallel routes. For those traveling through the bridge as a shortcut, it is recommended to allow an additional ten to fifteen minutes into their travel time accounts. Delivery trucks and oversized vehicles are prohibited from crossing the bridge during the active work hours, which run from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Emergency vehicles will always have priority access, and temporary closures may occur without prior notice if safety hazards are identified on site.

Pedestrians and cyclists should also plan for altered routing options. The existing sidewalk on the north side will be closed entirely for the duration of the project, while the south side may experience intermittent narrow passages. A temporary bike rack installation will be relocated to the lower plaza near the bridge entrance to accommodate cyclists who may need to dismount and carry their bicycles across the pedestrian section. Safety officers will be present throughout the day to assist non-motorized users and ensure that all personal spaces remain clutter-free and hazard-free.

City officials emphasize that while the schedule is set to conclude by the end of the month, weather conditions could potentially delay finalization activities. In the event of heavy rain or high winds, on-site work may be paused for a day or two, extending the overall timeline. Updates regarding any changes to the schedule will be posted on the municipal transportation portal and local news outlets. Stakeholders are encouraged to check these resources regularly for the most current information before starting their daily commute.

This maintenance effort is critical for preventing future corrosion and ensuring the structural integrity of the bridge for decades to come. The investment in these repairs reflects the city's commitment to maintaining safe and efficient infrastructure for all residents. While the temporary reductions in capacity are unfortunate, the long-term benefits of a well-maintained bridge will far outweigh the short-term disruptions. Residents are asked to be patient and courteous to the skilled workers performing these necessary tasks, contributing to a smoother transition back to normal traffic flow once the project is complete.

This work is part of a comprehensive five-year infrastructure plan aimed at preserving the safety and functionality of major crossings in the metropolitan area. Residents and commuters should anticipate minor inconveniences as preparations for the project get underway.

Traffic will be reduced to one lane in each direction for the majority of the work period. Detours will be clearly marked with orange signage directing local traffic onto adjacent parallel routes. For those traveling through the bridge as a shortcut, it is recommended to allow an additional ten to fifteen minutes into their travel time accounts. Delivery trucks and oversized vehicles are prohibited from crossing the bridge during the active work hours, which run from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Emergency vehicles will always have priority access, and temporary closures may occur without prior notice if safety hazards are identified on site.

Pedestrians and cyclists should also plan for altered routing options. The existing sidewalk on the north side will be closed entirely for the duration of the project, while the south side may experience intermittent narrow passages. A temporary bike rack installation will be relocated to the lower plaza near the bridge entrance to accommodate cyclists who may need to dismount and carry their bicycles across the pedestrian section. Safety officers will be present throughout the day to assist non-motorized users and ensure that all personal spaces remain clutter-free and hazard-free.

City officials emphasize that while the schedule is set to conclude by the end of the month, weather conditions could potentially delay finalization activities. In the event of heavy rain or high winds, on-site work may be paused for a day or two, extending the overall timeline. Updates regarding any changes to the schedule will be posted on the municipal transportation portal and local news outlets. Stakeholders are encouraged to check these resources regularly for the most current information before starting their daily commute.

This maintenance effort is critical for preventing future corrosion and ensuring the structural integrity of the bridge for decades to come. The investment in these repairs reflects the city's commitment to maintaining safe and efficient infrastructure for all residents. While the temporary reductions in capacity are unfortunate, the long-term benefits of a well-maintained bridge will far outweigh the short-term disruptions. Residents are asked to be patient and courteous to the skilled workers performing these necessary tasks, contributing to a smoother transition back to normal traffic flow once the project is complete.

Subject: Important Update Regarding Your Extended Warranty Coverage
Hi Sarah,
I am writing to clarify the specific terms of the extended warranty you recently purchased for your new laptop. Please review the attached document carefully, as it outlines the exact scope of protection provided during the next two years. This agreement replaces any previous verbal assurances and serves as the official record for your device.
The coverage includes hardware defects originating from the manufacturer for both the internal components and the portable case. It specifically excludes damage caused by liquid spills, accidental drops, or power surges. If your device suffers from water damage, for example, the repair costs will be entirely your responsibility. We recommend using a protective case to avoid such incidents in the future.
Any software issues or data loss are not covered under this policy. If you need help with missing files, you may consider purchasing a separate data recovery service, but that is an additional cost. Also, the warranty is non-transferable. If you decide to sell the laptop before the term expires, the warranty remains with the original owner and does not move to the buyer.
To initiate a claim, you must send the device to our certified repair center within three business days of noticing the defect. Pre-approval is required before shipping. Without this authorization number, we cannot process the return, and the unit may be sent back without inspection or repair.
Please let me know if you have any questions about these details. I am happy to walk you through the sections that seem unclear. We want to ensure you feel confident in your purchase and understand exactly how to get support when needed.
Best regards,
David Miller
Customer Success Team

Beryl Anthony Jr.

Beryl Franklin Anthony Jr. (February 21, 1938 - January 11, 2025) was an American lawyer and politician who represented Arkansas in the United States House of Representatives for seven terms from 1979 to 1993.

Anthony was born in El Dorado, Arkansas, the son of Oma Lee Roark and Beryl Franklin Anthony. He attended the Union County public schools, graduating from El Dorado High School in 1956. In 1961, he received a Bachelor of Science and Bachelor of Arts degrees from the University of Arkansas where he became a member of the Sigma Chi fraternity. He obtained a Juris Doctor from the same university in 1963.

Anthony was admitted to the Arkansas bar in 1963 and began practice in El Dorado. He became assistant attorney general from 1964 to 1965; deputy prosecuting attorney in Union County from 1966 to 1970; prosecuting attorney for the 13th Judicial District from 1971 to 1976, and legal counsel to Anthony Forest Products Co. in 1977. He started his own private practice of law in 1977.

In November 1978, he was elected as a Democrat to the United States House of Representatives and served seven terms, from January 3, 1979, to January 3, 1993. Vice president of his freshman class in Congress, Anthony was a founding member of the Sunbelt Coalition, a group that monitored the legislative impact upon southern states. After one term, he was appointed to the House Ways and Means Committee. He also served on the Oversight and Trade Subcommittees as well as the Select Committee on Children, Youth, and Families. Anthony chaired the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee from 1987 to 1991. He maintained a conservative voting record in Congress, similar to other Southern Democrats. As a member of the Ways and Means Committee, Anthony pursued a variety of important issues. In the 1980s, he played a major role in restructuring the Social Security trust fund. He championed legislation for improved rural health care, for which he was given awards by both the Arkansas Hospital Association and the American Hospital Association. In his last terms, he focused on international trade, working on the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and on legislation for the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). In 1988, Congress created the bipartisan Anthony Public Finance Commission, composed of mayors, governors, local government officials, and members of the finance community, to recommend legislation to enable local governments to better finance the building of roads, schools, hospitals, and wastewater treatment facilities. The commission's Arbitrage Relief Provision, enacted in 1989, substantially lessened the borrowing costs for infrastructure investments. Due in part to his involvement with the House banking scandal, Anthony lost his bid for renomination in the Democratic Primary runoff in June 1992 to Arkansas Secretary of State William J. "Bill" McCuen who lost the general election to Republican Jay W. Dickey due to a series of embarrassing incidents. McCuen received campaign funding from the National Rifle Association (NRA) due to Anthony's support of legislation limiting so-called "Cop Killer" bullets.

In January 1993, Anthony became a partner in the Washington, D.C. office of Winston & Strawn. His clients have included major trade associations, governmental entities, and national and multinational corporations. On Capitol Hill and before the White House and executive agencies, Anthony has worked on matters involving health care reform, Superfund, trade relations with China, tax law changes affecting pharmaceuticals, and authorization and funding of major weapons systems. He was a member of the board of directors of Beverly Enterprises which in 2006 before its acquisition by a private equity firm, operated 345 skilled nursing facilities, 18 assisted living centers, and 56 hospice/home care centers.

Anthony's wife, Sheila Foster Anthony is the sister of Vince Foster, the deputy White House counsel who committed suicide in 1993. The couple's first child was born in 1964. She was a teacher before getting a law degree. In 1993, after working in the U.S. Commerce Department as the nominated Assistant Secretary for Legislation and Intergovernmental Affairs for several months, she moved to the U.S. Department of Justice in a similar position, where she worked for two years. From 1997 to 2002, she was a commissioner at the Federal Trade Commission. Anthony died in Palm City, Florida, on January 11, 2025, at the age of 86.

Biography at the Biographical Directory of the United States Congress Biography, Stennis Center for Public Service, a federal, legislative branch agency, accessed October 15, 2007 Appearances on C-SPAN

newsletter roundup

The digital landscape is saturated with information, making it increasingly difficult to stay current without spending excessive hours scrolling through social media feeds. A newsletter roundup offers a practical solution to this problem by curating the best content from various sources into a single, digestible package. Instead of subscribing to twenty different publications and letting them clutter your inbox, a roundup service aggregates high-quality articles, data, and commentary into one unified email. This approach respects your time and reduces decision fatigue, allowing you to consume valuable insights in minutes rather than hours.

Curating a successful newsletter roundup requires more than just collecting links from popular blogs. The value lies in the editorial judgment applied to the selection process. Editors must identify trends, filter out noise, and highlight stories that offer genuine insight or actionable advice. For instance, a tech-focused roundup might include a deep dive into a new AI regulation alongside a brief update on a major smartphone launch. The key is balance, ensuring that each issue provides a mix of breaking news, long-form analysis, and lighter industry chatter. This curation transforms a simple list of links into a coherent narrative about the state of the industry.

From a reader's perspective, the primary benefit is efficiency. By consolidating multiple viewpoints, a roundup prevents echo chambers that often arise from relying on a single news source. You gain access to diverse perspectives on the same event, which helps in forming a more nuanced understanding of complex issues. Furthermore, many roundup services send emails at optimal times, such as early morning, allowing readers to start their day informed. This consistency builds a habit of morning reading that can be more productive than sporadic checking of news apps throughout the day.

Creating your own newsletter roundup is also a viable strategy for professionals looking to establish authority in their niche. By highlighting the work of peers and complementary experts, you position yourself as a central hub of knowledge. This collaborative approach strengthens community ties and encourages cross-promotion. When you feature an article from a colleague, you are not just sharing their work; you are endorsing their expertise and inviting their audience to view your content. This mutual support system often leads to increased engagement and a more loyal subscriber base.

Ultimately, the effectiveness of a newsletter roundup depends on its relevance and consistency. Subscribers will quickly unsubscribe if the content feels random or too infrequent. To maintain interest, creators must continuously refine their selection criteria based on reader feedback and changing industry dynamics. Whether you are a consumer looking to save time or a producer trying to build a community, the roundup model proves that focused curation beats overwhelming quantity. It transforms the flow of information from a chaotic stream into a manageable, valuable resource.

raw:
volcano science

Volcano science has moved from the realm of dramatic eruptions captured on television to a precise, data-driven discipline that helps communities anticipate hazards and understand Earth's inner workings. Modern volcanologists rely on a blend of satellite imaging, ground-based sensors, and computer models to track magma movement, gas emissions, and subtle ground deformation. These tools turn what once seemed unpredictable into patterns that can be quantified, shared, and acted upon.

One of the most striking advances is the use of interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) to detect millimeter-scale swelling of a volcano's surface. By comparing radar images taken days or weeks apart, researchers can map the uplift that often precedes an eruption. Coupled with real-time seismic monitoring, the data provide a three-dimensional view of how magma chambers inflate and migrate, offering a clearer timeline for potential activity.

Gas chemistry also plays a critical role in deciphering a volcano's state. Instruments placed on the crater rim or aboard drones sample sulfur dioxide, carbon dioxide, and other volcanic gases, which can change dramatically as magma approaches the surface. A sudden spike in sulfur dioxide, for example, may signal that new magma is degassing, while a drop could indicate that the conduit has sealed, raising the risk of explosive pressure buildup.

Public outreach and education have become integral to volcano science, as the best technical insight is useless without community preparedness. Many observatories now host live streams, interactive maps, and multilingual alerts that explain the significance of each alert level. Workshops in at-risk regions teach residents how to recognize ash fallout, protect water supplies, and establish safe evacuation routes, translating complex data into everyday actions.

International collaboration further strengthens the field. Networks such as the Global Volcanism Program share datasets across continents, allowing scientists to compare eruptions that differ in magma composition, tectonic setting, and eruption style. This comparative approach refines hazard models and helps predict how a volcano in one part of the world might behave under similar conditions elsewhere.

The future of volcano science looks increasingly interdisciplinary. Machine learning algorithms are already being trained on historical eruption records to flag anomalies that human analysts might miss. Meanwhile, low-cost, open-source sensors are expanding monitoring capabilities into remote or politically unstable regions. As these innovations converge, our ability to protect lives and deepen our understanding of the planet's fiery heart will continue to grow.

raw:
photography basics

If you have ever picked up a camera and felt overwhelmed by the sheer number of buttons and settings, you are not alone. The world of photography can appear complex at first glance, with daunting acronyms like ISO, aperture, and shutter speed staring back at you from the digital display. However, mastering these fundamentals is actually quite straightforward once you understand how they interact with one another. The core concept revolves around the exposure triangle, a metaphorical system where three variables work together to control how much light hits your camera's sensor. Getting this balance right is the single most important skill you can develop as a new photographer, regardless of whether you use a high-end DSLR or a modern smartphone.

Aperture is the first element of this triangle, referring to the size of the opening in the lens through which light passes. It is measured in f-stops, where a smaller number indicates a wider opening and a larger number denotes a narrower one. This setting does more than just adjust brightness; it determines your depth of field, which is the range of distance within your photo that remains in sharp focus. A wide aperture, such as f/1.8, creates a blurred background known as bokeh, perfect for portraits that need to make the subject pop. Conversely, a narrow aperture like f/11 keeps more of the scene in focus, making it ideal for landscapes or street photography where context matters as much as the subject.

Shutter speed is the second pillar, representing how long the camera's sensor is exposed to light. It is measured in fractions of a second, ranging from instantaneuous snaps like one-fourthousandth of a second to slow exposures lasting several seconds. Fast shutter speeds are essential for freezing action, allowing you to capture a soaring bird, a splashing wave, or a sprinting athlete without any motion blur. On the other hand, slow shutter speeds are used to create a sense of movement, such as the silky appearance of flowing water in a waterfall or the light trails of car headlights at night. Selecting the appropriate speed depends entirely on the vibe you want to convey and the motion present in your scene.

ISO is the final component, describing the sensitivity of the sensor to the light that reaches it. A low ISO value, such as 100 or 200, produces the cleanest images with minimal digital noise or grain. This is the preferred setting for bright, sunny days or when using a tripod for stable shots. As lighting conditions darken, you may need to increase the ISO to 800, 1600, or even higher to maintain proper exposure. While modern cameras handle high ISOs remarkably well, pushing the value too high can introduce a gritty texture that degrades image quality. Therefore, the general rule of thumb is to keep the ISO as low as possible while still achieving a well-exposed photo.

Putting it all together, you should approach each shot by deciding what matters most in that specific moment. If you want to freeze a fast-moving dog, prioritize shutter speed first, then adjust the aperture and ISO to make the exposure work. For a portrait, start with a wide aperture to blur the background, then tweak the other two settings to ensure the subject is properly lit. Experimentation is key, so take your camera out into the field and try changing one setting at a time to see how it affects the final image. Over time, these manual adjustments will become second nature, freeing you from the menu screens and allowing you to focus entirely on the beauty surrounding you.

raw:
renting an apartment

.

Moving into a new apartment is an exciting milestone, but the process can feel overwhelming if you don't know where to start. The first step is typically establishing a clear budget that accounts for more than just the monthly rent. You need to factor in utilities, internet, renter's insurance, and any potential moving costs. Many experts suggest that your total monthly housing expenses should not exceed thirty percent of your gross income, but this can vary significantly depending on your stage of life and personal financial goals. Setting realistic expectations early on prevents the stress of overextending your finances later.

Once your budget is set, it is time to define your priorities. Create a shortlist of non-negotiables such as the number of bedrooms needed, proximity to public transportation, and specific amenities like a dishwasher or in-unit laundry. It is important to distinguish between wants and needs during this phase. A smaller unit in a prime location might be more valuable than a spacious apartment in a remote area if you rely on a car-free lifestyle. Narrowing your criteria helps you filter through listings more efficiently and allows you to focus on homes that actually fit your daily routine.

Scheduling viewings requires some preparation and attention to detail. When you tour a potential home, bring a small toolkit including a cookie to test electrical outlets and a ruler to measure furniture fit. Check for signs of water damage under sinks and inside closets, and test the water pressure in the shower. Pay close attention to the condition of the windows and doors, ensuring they seal properly to keep out drafts. Do not hesitate to ask the landlord or property manager about any visible issues, as their transparency can be a strong indicator of how they manage tenant communication.

Understanding the lease terms is crucial before signing anything. Read the contract carefully, paying particular attention to clauses regarding pet policies, subletting rights, and renewal options. Clarify who is responsible for maintenance repairs and what the procedure is for requesting them. Be sure to ask about any additional fees, such as application fees, security deposits, or administrative charges. It is wise to request a copy of the lease in advance so you have time to review the fine print with a trusted friend or family member.

Finally, if you decide to apply, ensure your documentation is ready to go. This usually includes proof of income, recent pay stubs, and valid identification. A strong credit score helps, but a solid rental history and a letter of recommendation from a previous landlord can also work in your favor. Submitting your application promptly after making your decision is often the key to securing the unit, as competitive markets move quickly. By preparing thoroughly and approaching the process with patience, you increase your chances of finding a home that feels like yours.

The County Resilience Office releases its quarterly update on community climate adaptation strategies. Recent meteorological data confirms a shift toward prolonged heatwaves and intensified storm events, necessitating immediate adjustments to our urban infrastructure plans. We are prioritizing the retrofitting of drainage systems in low-lying districts to mitigate flood risks. This proactive approach aims to reduce insurance liabilities and protect critical municipal services during extreme weather windows.

Residents should observe new signage indicating designated cooling centers. These facilities will operate extended hours during heat advisories issued by the National Weather Service. Public transit routes have been updated to ensure reliable access to these shelters, particularly for elderly populations and those without private transportation. Water conservation measures remain in effect, with mandatory restrictions on non-essential outdoor usage in Zones A and B until further notice.

Local businesses are encouraged to review their supply chains for potential disruptions. Procurement teams have been advised to diversify vendors to avoid single points of failure. We recommend establishing emergency stockpiles of essential goods and developing communication protocols that do not rely solely on cellular networks. Continuous monitoring of local watershed levels will guide further operational decisions by city engineers.

Funding allocations for green infrastructure projects have been increased by fifteen percent. This budget supports the expansion of permeable pavement and urban forestry initiatives. Community engagement sessions will be held next month to gather input on neighborhood-specific mitigation needs. Participation in these forums is crucial for tailoring interventions that reflect actual local conditions and resident concerns.

Report any infrastructure damage or drainage blockages to the 311 service line immediately. Timely reporting allows maintenance crews to deploy resources efficiently before conditions worsen. Adherence to these guidelines ensures collective safety and operational continuity. We appreciate the community cooperation in implementing these adaptive measures as we navigate this evolving climate landscape together.

raw:
online privacy settings

The digital landscape has evolved into a space where personal information is often traded without explicit consent. For many users, the default settings on social media platforms, search engines, and operating systems prioritize visibility over privacy. This means that your location, friends list, and browsing habits are often visible to a much wider audience than you intended. Understanding that these defaults exist to maximize engagement rather than protect your data is the first step toward reclaiming control. It is not enough to simply sign up for a service; you must actively configure how your data is handled from the very beginning.

Adjusting privacy settings is no longer an optional technical task reserved for IT professionals. It is a fundamental digital hygiene practice, similar to locking your front door. Start by reviewing the privacy section of your most-used applications. On social networks, look for options that limit who can see your posts, who can add you as a friend, and whether your profile appears in search results. Changing a few dropdown menus from Public to Friends Only or Only Me can drastically reduce the amount of data available to third-party marketers and data brokers.

Beyond social media, your device settings play a crucial role in your overall privacy footprint. Smartphones and laptops track your location, access your microphone, and collect usage statistics. Navigate to your device's settings menu and audit each app's permissions. Ask yourself if a weather app truly needs access to your precise location at all times or if a flashlight app requires access to your contacts. Revoking unnecessary permissions prevents these applications from building detailed profiles of your daily routine, hobbies, and social environment, which are often sold to advertisers.

Search engines and browsers are another major avenue for data leakage. Many users do not realize that their search history is stored for years, revealing intimate details about their health, financial status, and personal interests. Review your account history and clear old data. Additionally, consider using browser extensions that block trackers and limit cookie usage. While ad-free browsing can occasionally hinder user experience, the trade-off is worth it for those who value discretion. Enable private browsing modes when visiting sensitive sites, and remember that these modes protect you from local devices, not from your internet service provider.

Ultimately, maintaining online privacy is an ongoing process rather than a one-time setup. Services frequently update their terms of service and privacy policies, which may reset your preferences or introduce new data collection methods. Set a reminder to review your settings every six months. Stay informed about data breaches by signing up for alert services from major identity theft protection companies. By remaining vigilant and proactive, you create a significant barrier between your personal life and the digital surveillance economy, ensuring that your online presence remains on your terms.

raw:
flood preparedness

Floods remain one of the most destructive and frequently occurring natural disasters, catching many communities and individuals off guard despite available warnings. While large-scale river flooding captures national headlines, localized flooding from intense rainfall often poses a greater, more immediate threat to residential areas. Understanding that water moves quickly and with significant force is the first step toward safety. Many homeowners operate under the misconception that their specific neighborhood has never flooded, a dangerous assumption that history has repeatedly disproven. Preparing for these events does not require expensive infrastructure or engineering expertise; it requires a proactive mindset and a clear strategy for protecting both property and life.

The most critical component of any flood preparedness plan is knowing your local risk profile. Residents should consult with local flood control districts or the National Weather Service to determine if their home lies within a designated Special Flood Hazard Area. However, risk extends beyond these official maps. Properties situated in low-lying basements, near storm drains, or at the bottom of a gradient are vulnerable even if they are technically outside mapped zones. Creating a digital and physical emergency kit now is essential. This kit should include at least one gallon of water per person per day for at least three days, non-perishable food, a manual can opener, a battery-powered or hand-crank radio, extra batteries, a first-aid kit, and copies of important documents such as insurance policies and identification stored in a waterproof container.

Securing your home before a flood event begins can significantly reduce damage. For homes with basements, identifying and elevating utility controls such as the main electrical breaker gas valves and water shutoff is paramount. Installing a backwater valve on your sewer line prevents flooding from entering your home through drains and toilets, a common yet often overlooked entry point during heavy rains. If you reside in a high-risk area, consider installing sump pumps with battery backups to manage groundwater levels. Furthermore, keeping gutters and downspouts clear ensures that roof water is directed away from the foundation, preventing hydrostatic pressure that can crack walls and floors.

When weather warnings are issued, acting quickly is vital. Move valuables, including electronics and family photos, to upper floors of your home. Never store important items in the basement or garage unless they are in watertight containers and raised off the floor. If you have pets, take them with you or have a plan for their evacuation, as shelters may not accommodate animals. Do not ignore official evacuation orders. Leaving early allows you to depart safely when traffic is light and road conditions are still manageable. Waiting until the last minute often results in being stranded by rising water or closed roads, turning a manageable situation into a life-threatening ordeal.

After the water recedes, safety concerns do not end. Floodwater is often contaminated with sewage, chemicals, and bacteria, making it unsafe to touch or drink. Wear appropriate protective gear, including rubber boots, gloves, and masks, when entering flooded areas. Be wary of downed power lines, which could be energized and lethal, and avoid walking through moving water, as just six inches of moving water can sweep an adult off their feet. Document all property damage with photographs before beginning cleanup to support insurance claims. Finally, stay informed through official channels regarding cleanup resources and public health advisories to ensure a safe and complete recovery for your household.

Deng Mengnü

Home | About | Contact

Deng Mengnü (鄧猛女) (died 165), also briefly known as Liang Mengnü (梁猛女) then as Bo Mengnü (薄猛女), was an empress during the Eastern Han dynasty. She was the second wife of Emperor Huan.

Deng Mengnü's father Deng Xiang (鄧香) was a low level official in the imperial administration. (It is not clear under which emperor(s) he served.) He was a cousin of Empress Deng Sui and therefore a grandson of the statesman Deng Yu. Deng Mengnü's mother was named Xuan (宣). Deng Xiang died early, and after his death, Lady Xuan remarried Liang Ji (梁紀-note different character than the Liang Ji referenced below), an uncle of Sun Shou (孫壽), the wife of the powerful official Liang Ji (梁冀), who dominated the political scene throughout the reigns of Emperor Huan and his two predecessors, Emperors Chong and Zhi, as the brother of the regent Empress Dowager Liang.

After Lady Xuan remarried, Deng Mengnü lived for a while with her mother and her stepfather. Because she was beautiful, Liang Ji and Sun Shou had offered her to Emperor Huan to be an imperial consort-and adopted her and changed her family name to Liang. After the death of Liang Ji's sister Empress Liang Nüying in August 159, Liang Ji was hopeful to continue to use her to control Emperor Huan and hoped that she would become empress. To completely control her, Liang Ji planned to have her mother, Lady Xuan, killed, and in fact sent assassins against her, but the assassination was foiled by the powerful eunuch Yuan She (袁赦), a neighbor of Lady Xuan. This set in motion a series of events that led to Liang Ji's downfall, as Emperor Huan, angry about the assassination attempt, formed a conspiracy with five powerful eunuchs and overthrew Liang in a coup d'etat later in September 159. The Liang and Sun clans were slaughtered. After the fall of the Liang clan, on 14 September 159, Emperor Huan created then-Consort Liang empress, but disliked her family name, and so ordered her family name be changed to Bo (薄). Only later did the emperor find out that she was actually Deng Xiang's daughter, and therefore had her original family name of Deng restored. A number of her uncles and cousins were promoted to important positions but not given much real power.

For a while, Emperor Huan greatly favored the beautiful Empress Deng. However, his affection was not undivided, and he had a large number of other favorites, including Consorts Guo and Tian. Empress Deng became very arrogant and jealous, and she and Consort Guo engaged in a series of false accusations against each other. On 27 March 165, Emperor Huan decided to rid himself of Empress Deng and ordered her deposed and imprisoned. She died in anger and depression. Her relatives who had been promoted when she had become empress were removed from their positions, and her uncles Deng Wanshi (鄧萬世) and Deng Hui (鄧會) were executed.

He was a cousin of Empress Deng Sui and therefore a grandson of the statesman Deng Yu. Deng Mengnü's mother was named Xuan (宣). Deng Xiang died early, and after his death, Lady Xuan remarried Liang Ji (梁紀-note different character than the Liang Ji referenced below), an uncle of Sun Shou (孫壽), the wife of the powerful official Liang Ji (梁冀), who dominated the political scene throughout the reigns of Emperor Huan and his two predecessors, Emperors Chong and Zhi, as the brother of the regent Empress Dowager Liang.

After Lady Xuan remarried, Deng Mengnü lived for a while with her mother and her stepfather. Because she was beautiful, Liang Ji and Sun Shou had offered her to Emperor Huan to be an imperial consort-and adopted her and changed her family name to Liang. After the death of Liang Ji's sister Empress Liang Nüying in August 159, Liang Ji was hopeful to continue to use her to control Emperor Huan and hoped that she would become empress. To completely control her, Liang Ji planned to have her mother, Lady Xuan, killed, and in fact sent assassins against her, but the assassination was foiled by the powerful eunuch Yuan She (袁赦), a neighbor of Lady Xuan. This set in motion a series of events that led to Liang Ji's downfall, as Emperor Huan, angry about the assassination attempt, formed a conspiracy with five powerful eunuchs and overthrew Liang in a coup d'etat later in September 159. The Liang and Sun clans were slaughtered. After the fall of the Liang clan, on 14 September 159, Emperor Huan created then-Consort Liang empress, but disliked her family name, and so ordered her family name be changed to Bo (薄). Only later did the emperor find out that she was actually Deng Xiang's daughter, and therefore had her original family name of Deng restored. A number of her uncles and cousins were promoted to important positions but not given much real power.

For a while, Emperor Huan greatly favored the beautiful Empress Deng. However, his affection was not undivided, and he had a large number of other favorites, including Consorts Guo and Tian. Empress Deng became very arrogant and jealous, and she and Consort Guo engaged in a series of false accusations against each other. On 27 March 165, Emperor Huan decided to rid himself of Empress Deng and ordered her deposed and imprisoned. She died in anger and depression. Her relatives who had been promoted when she had become empress were removed from their positions, and her uncles Deng Wanshi (鄧萬世) and Deng Hui (鄧會) were executed.

Constrictolumina leucostoma

Constrictolumina leucostoma is a species of corticolous (bark-dwelling) crustose lichen in the family Trypetheliaceae. This neotropical lichen forms thin, whitish crusts on tree bark and is distinguished by its small fruiting bodies that are often surrounded by conspicuous thin black rings that frequently merge to form clusters. It has a distribution spanning the Caribbean (including the Antilles), and the United States.

Constrictolumina leucostoma was originally described in 1885 by Johannes Müller Argoviensis as Tomasellia leucostoma, based on material collected from the bark of Croton eluteria. In 1995, Richard Harris misapplied the name as Arthopyrenia confluens, but this usage was distinct from the earlier Arthopyrenia leucostoma described by Abramo Bartolommeo Massalongo in 1852. In 2016, Robert Lücking, Matthew Nelsen, and André Aptroot transferred the species to the genus Constrictolumina, where it is now accepted. The holotype is preserved in the Geneva herbarium (G).

Constrictolumina leucostoma has a thin, whitish thallus. Its fruiting bodies (ascomata) are small, 0.1-0.2 mm across, and emerge slightly above the surface. They are solitary or occur in groups, often outlined by a conspicuous thin black ring 0.2-0.3 mm wide. These rings frequently merge, forming clusters of 2-10 ascomata. The lower wall of the ascomata is poorly developed or absent, while the ostioles are often sunken and encircled by a pale whitish ring. The asci are mostly narrowly egg-shaped, sometimes nearly cylindrical, and measure 60-105 by 16-26 micrometres (μm). Each ascus contains eight ascospores, arranged irregularly or in two overlapping rows. The spores are narrowly ovate to ellipsoidal, divided by three cross-walls, and surrounded by a distinct outer layer (perispore). They measure 17-22 by 6-8 μm. Asexual reproductive structures (pycnidia) are often present. These produce slender, rod-like conidia, 6-9 by 1 μm. Standard chemical spot tests (UV and K) are negative, and thin-layer chromatography has not detected any secondary metabolites.

restaurant opening hours

Finding the right time to dine out can sometimes feel like a puzzle, especially when local establishments follow quirky schedules that defy standard expectations. Many people assume that restaurants operate on a rigid nine-to-five basis or stay open late every night of the week, but the reality is far more nuanced. Opening hours are rarely uniform across a city, and they often reflect the specific identity of the establishment, the local culture, and the season. Before making a reservation or walking in for a quick bite, it is crucial to understand the typical patterns that govern these daily rhythms. Knowing when a kitchen opens and closes can mean the difference between a comfortable meal and a rushed, disappointing experience.

Most casual dining spots and cafes adhere to relatively predictable schedules, typically opening their doors early in the morning to catch the breakfast crowd. You will frequently see hours starting around seven or eight in the morning, extending late into the evening, perhaps until ten or midnight. These establishments aim to serve the masses, including commuters, families, and students, so their windows are wide and accommodating. However, high-end fine dining restaurants often operate differently. They may keep their doors closed during the midday rush, reserving their prime time for dinner services that start in the early evening. Some even close completely on Tuesdays or Mondays to give their staff a break or to clean and restock their kitchens.

Seasonal changes also play a significant role in altering restaurant hours, particularly in tourist-heavy areas or coastal towns. In the height of summer, many venues extend their evening service, staying open until one or two in the morning to accommodate later guests. Conversely, during the colder months or off-seasons, hours might shrink, with kitchens closing earlier to manage energy costs and staffing levels. If you are planning a trip during a holiday period, be aware that many places observe shorter hours or close entirely for traditional holidays. Checking the specific dates for New Year's Eve or Christmas can save you the frustration of arriving at a darkened front door when you expected a festive dinner.

Breakfast and brunch times deserve special attention, as they vary wildly from one location to another. Some places start serving coffee and pastries at six in the morning, catering to early risers, while others do not serve hot food until ten or eleven. Brunch menus, which are often the largest and most elaborate, tend to be available on weekends only, usually spanning from ten in the morning until two in the afternoon. Attempting to order an omelet at four in the afternoon might result in a disappointed response. It is always wise to check if a specific location offers a mid-morning service or if you need to time your visit within the traditional brunch window to enjoy the full menu.

Finally, digital tools have made it easier than ever to verify current operating hours, yet they are not always infallible. Popular review sites and mapping applications are updated by users, meaning the information can lag behind actual changes or contain errors. For the most accurate information, a quick phone call to the restaurant directly is still the gold standard. It also allows you to ask about potential wait times, special menu items available that day, and any temporary closures due to private events or staff training. By taking a few extra minutes to confirm the details, you ensure that your dining experience starts on the right foot, free from the stress of missed opportunities or unexpected closures.

Subject: Exploring Smart Home Devices for Our Office
Hi Mark,
I've been reviewing new smart-home technology and think several devices could streamline our office environment. From voice-controlled lighting to automated climate control, the options are practical and increasingly affordable.
One of the major advantages is energy efficiency. Smart thermostats can adjust heating and cooling based on occupancy patterns, while connected outlets cut power to idle equipment. Over a year, these savings can offset the purchase price.
Integration is also smoother than it used to be. Most of the products support standards-Matter and Thread-so they can be managed from a single app or voice assistant. This reduces the learning curve for our team and eliminates the need for vendor accounts.
Security remains a priority, and manufacturers are addressing it with firmware updates and encrypted communication. By setting up a VLAN for IoT devices, we can isolate any potential vulnerabilities while still enjoying the convenience of remote control.
The cost of a starter kit, including a hub, a few smart bulbs, and a thermostat, is roughly $300. Considering the energy reduction and the productivity boost from automated tasks, the return on investment looks promising.
Let me know if you'd like to schedule a brief demo next week. I can arrange a hands-on trial in the conference room so we can evaluate the user experience together.
Best regards,
Emily Chen
Product Manager

The Central Transit Authority has released updated schedules for Routes 12, 14, and 23, effective immediately for the coming month. These adjustments reflect current ridership data and infrastructure changes along the downtown corridor. Commuters should familiarize themselves with the new departure times, as previous schedules are no longer valid for boarding or fare calculations. The primary goal of these revisions is to improve peak hour frequency while maintaining cost efficiency during off-peak daytime hours and weekends.

On Route 12, previously known as the University Loop, the morning peak frequency has increased from every twenty minutes to every fifteen minutes between 7:00 AM and 9:30 AM. This change responds to sustained high ridership reports from students and early-shift workers. Conversely, evening service after 6:00 PM will revert to a twenty-minute interval to align with reduced demand. Riders traveling from the North Station to the City Center should note a slight shift in departure times, with the first bus now leaving at 5:45 AM instead of 5:30 AM to optimize driver shift starting times.

Route 14, the Riverside Express, undergoes a minor rerouting to accommodate construction on Main Avenue. The bus will detour via Oak Street for the next six weeks. This alternate path adds approximately four minutes to the total journey time. While the physical stops along Oak Street remain unchanged, passengers should allow extra time for transfers to other lines. The transit authority recommends checking the real-time app for live location tracking, as construction delays may cause minor temporary variations in arrival times despite the printed schedule.

For Route 23, the suburban connector, weekend service remains consistent, but holiday schedules will differ. On all public holidays, this route will operate on a reduced schedule with departures every thirty minutes from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. There will be no service before 8:00 AM or after 4:00 PM on these specific dates. Riders planning to travel on these days should verify their tickets and times carefully, as standard weekday or weekend rules do not apply. This adjustment helps manage operational costs while still providing essential connectivity for the community.

Passengers are encouraged to download the latest PDF timetable from the official transit website or visit any ticketing kiosk at major hubs. Physical copies are also available at all staffed terminals. If you have questions regarding specific stops or need accessibility accommodations, please contact the customer service center directly. We appreciate your patience and understanding as we work to refine our services to better meet the evolving needs of our riders. Your feedback remains a critical component in our ongoing effort to provide reliable and efficient public transportation across the region.
