Vũ Trọng Phụng

Vũ Trọng Phụng (Hanoi, 20 October 1912 - Hanoi, 13 October 1939) was a popular Vietnamese author and journalist, who is considered to be one of the most influential figures of 20th century Vietnamese literature. Today, several of his works are taught in Vietnamese schools. Phụng's ancestral village was Hảo village, Mỹ Hào District, Hưng Yên Province, yet he was born, grew up, and died in Hanoi. The fact that his father died of tuberculosis when he was only seven months old resulted in Phụng's being brought up mainly by his mother. After finishing primary school, 16-year-old Vũ Trọng Phụng was forced to stop schooling and earn his own living. In 1939, he died from tuberculosis at the age of 26 (27 by the Vietnamese system of age reckoning), a week before his 27th birthday. Phụng wrote prolifically during the 1930s, and "produced a body of writing that", according to historian Peter B. Zinoman, "stands today as the single most remarkable individual achievement in modern Vietnamese literature." Although he only wrote for a short span of time, with his first work being the short story Chống nạng lên đường ('Set off with crutches') on the newspaper Ngọ Báo in 1930, he had left an impressive collection of literature works: over 30 short stories, 9 novels, 9 reports, 7 plays, along with a translated play from French, some literature reviews and pieces of criticism, and hundreds of articles on matters of politics, society, and culture. Some excerpts from his publications, for example Dumb Luck (Vietnamese: Số Đỏ) and The Storm (Vietnamese: Giông Tố), became part of Vietnamese literature textbooks. Famous for the satire in his works, Phụng was compared to Balzac by some critics. However, due to his "realistic" descriptions and heavy emphasis on sex, he was called to court by the French authorities in Hanoi for "outraging morality" (French: outrage aux bonnes moeurs). Later on, his works were prohibited from being published or read in North Vietnam because they were deemed "obscene publications" until the late 1980s.

In 1937, Phụng wrote Lục Xì, a now-classic reportage (Vietnamese: phóng sự) on female sex work in colonial Hanoi. The work was originally published in a local newspaper (Tương Lai, 'Future') in a serialized format, before it was published as a book later that year. It was based on his observations of the practice and regulation of sex work in the city, as well as his visits to the municipal dispensary (Vietnamese: nhà lục xì, lit. 'the look-see house') where sex workers were treated for venereal diseases, which were only possible because municipal authorities wanted to showcase the city's ostensible success in dealing with sex work to journalists and writers like Phụng. In Lục Xì, Phụng's view is not simply that sex work was immoral, but that the outsize presence of sex work in Hanoi was a symptom of larger problems-such as exploitative or ineffectual colonial policies, materialistic attitudes, poverty, and the spread of venereal diseases-all of which stood in stark contrast to French claims that Vietnam was prospering under colonial rule. An English translation of Lục Xì by anthropologist Shaun Kingsley Malarney was published by University of Hawaiʻi Press in 2011. bird migration

The sky above our backyard has emptier corners lately. As the temperature drops and the days shorten, the air seems to hold its breath, waiting for the great exodus that defines this time of year. Bird migration is not just a seasonal change in scenery; it is one of the most impressive natural spectacles on Earth. Millions of birds embark on journeys that span thousands of miles, navigating from warm tropical zones to cooler northern regions or vice versa, driven by the need for food, breeding grounds, and survival.

These avian travelers possess an innate biological clock. The changes in daylight hours trigger hormonal shifts that prepare their bodies for flight. Metabolism increases, flight muscles bulk up, and fat reserves accumulate to serve as fuel. It is a complex internal process that requires perfect coordination. For many small songbirds, the journey is a grueling marathon, demanding up to seventy percent of their body weight be stored as fat to sustain them during long, non-stop flights that can last for days.

Navigation remains one of the most fascinating aspects of these journeys. Birds use a combination of celestial cues, magnetic field sensitivity, and visual landmarks to find their way across two hemispheres. Young birds, which have never made the trip before, rely on inherited genetic programming to follow the correct path. This instinctual knowledge ensures that even without prior experience, they head toward the right destination when the cues from their environment signal it is time to move.

The challenge of migration is high, and the mortality rate is significant. Predators, harsh weather, and the simple exhaustion of flight claim many lives. Habitat loss along traditional stopover sites presents an even greater threat in the modern world. As forests are cleared and wetlands drained, birds lose the critical refueling stations they need to rest and eat. Conservation efforts are vital now more than ever to protect these corridors, ensuring that the next generation of travelers has somewhere to land and recover.

When you see a murmuration of starlings or hear the distant call of geese heading south, take a moment to appreciate the feat. Each bird is a tiny, feathered rocket ship defying gravity and distance, guided by ancient instincts written into their DNA. They remind us of the resilience of nature and the intricate web of connections that bind our planet together. As the last flocks disappear over the horizon, the landscape quiets down, leaving behind a silence that is not empty, but full of potential, waiting for the return spring.

Subject: Update on the Cardigan Collection
Hi Elena,
I finally finished the blocking stage for the new cardigan pattern I mentioned last week. The results exceeded my expectations, and the fabric has a lovely drape that holds its shape well without being too stiff. I think we are ready to move forward with the knitting instructions.
The main challenge I faced was the tension consistency in the drop shoulders. I had to recalculate the yarn waste estimates to account for the additional steam required during the finishing process. Please check the attached document for the revised material list. It includes a more detailed breakdown of the colorways we will recommend for the spring line.
I also updated the sizing chart to reflect the recent changes in our manufacturing standards. The chest circumference adjustments are crucial for this style, so please double-check those numbers before we send them to the layout team. Accuracy here will save us significant time during the proof reading phase and ensure the final customer experience is seamless.
Let me know if you have access to the test knit circle by next Thursday. We need their feedback on the sleeve length specifically, as some of the early samples came out slightly long. Their input will be vital before we lock in the final PDF version. I hope to have everything finalized by the end of next week for the holiday preview drop.
Thanks again for your patience with these revisions. It is worth getting right given the volume of interest we have already received. Let us schedule a quick call tomorrow morning to discuss the remaining details.
Best regards,
Julian

Subject: Final moving checklist updates and logistics for the 15th
Hi Sarah,
I hope this email finds you well lately. I have been spending the last few evenings going through our possession lists and trying to figure out exactly what needs to be packed by next week. The goal is to have the heaviest items finished before the movers arrive on the 15th so they can focus on the delicate pieces and the furniture. I really need your input on a few specific rooms because I am struggling to decide which boxes to keep and which ones to donate to the local charity shop we discussed earlier this month.
For the kitchen, I am suggesting we pack all the small appliances like the blender, coffee maker, and toaster into their original boxes by Thursday evening. We need to make sure the manuals and extra parts are placed inside for safekeeping. I have already wrapped the plates and glasses in padded paper and labeled the boxes clearly as fragile. The microwave and the small oven can stay in place until the very last moment, but we should check that the power cord is not frayed or damaged before we move them out of the unit. If we do find any electrical issues, we need to repair them before the move or sell the items at a garage sale to avoid the hassle.
Regarding the bedroom, I am going to assume you are taking the curtains down and washing them, which I know takes a decent amount of time and energy. Please let me know if you want help with that task since I am finishing up the office files and sorting through the personal papers for the tax documentation. We also need to decide what to do with the extra mattress in the closet. I think it is probably best to donate it if it is in good condition, but if it has any stains or damage, we will have to arrange for proper disposal through the city waste management service to comply with local regulations and avoid any potential fines.
I have already reserved the moving truck for the 15th, and the driver confirmed that he will arrive at 8:00 AM sharp. I plan to have a full breakfast ready so we can start loading immediately without wasting time. It would be helpful if you could finalize the list of friends and family who are coming to help lift the heavier items like the sofa and the bookcases. I am aiming to have at least six people there to ensure we get everything into the truck efficiently and without any physical strain for any of us.
Finally, please remember to gather all the essential documents such as the lease agreement, utility transfer forms, and the keys for the new place. I will handle the final walk-through with the landlord to ensure we are not charged for any damages, and I have already scheduled the final utility bill payment to go through automatically before our account is closed. Let me know if you have any other urgent tasks that need to be completed before the big day because I want to make sure we do not overlook any minor details that could cause delays or confusion on moving day itself.
Best regards,
James

Roger Lumley, 11th Earl of Scarbrough

Lumley was the son of Brigadier General Osbert Lumley (1857-1923), youngest child and son of the Richard Lumley, 9th Earl of Scarbrough. His mother was Constance Ellinor Wilson-Patten (1864-1933), granddaughter of John Wilson-Patten, 1st Baron Winmarleigh. He attended Eton College and Magdalen College, Oxford.

Lumley followed his father into the military, passing out from the Royal Military College, Sandhurst. He was commissioned a second lieutenant in the 11th Hussars on 26 January 1916, and was promoted to lieutenant on 26 July 1917. He served in France during World War I. He was demobilised on 3 June 1919, with the rank of lieutenant, but retained a reserve lieutenant's commission in the 11th Hussars, as well as being attached to the Yorkshire Dragoons. From 1920 to 1921, he was attached to an Officer Training Corps (OTC) University Contingent, with the local rank of captain. Lumley sat in the House of Commons as Member of Parliament (MP) for Kingston upon Hull East 1922-29, then York 1931-37. In 1923 he was Parliamentary Private Secretary to William Ormsby-Gore, from 1924 to 1926 to Sir Austen Chamberlain and subsequently to Anthony Eden. On 8 March 1931, he was promoted to captain in the reserves in both the 11th Hussars and the Yorkshire Dragoons. He was brevetted to the rank of major in the Yorkshire Dragoons on 1 January 1937, and was awarded the Efficiency Decoration on 11 May. In 1937, he was appointed Governor of Bombay, serving until 1943, when he was appointed Knight Grand Commander of the Order of the Star of India. Upon his return from India, Lumley served as acting major-general in World War II, serving as Chief of Civil Affairs, War Office. Following the War, he continued his connections with the Army, as an honorary colonel. He succeeded to the Earldom of Scarbrough in 1945 following the death of his uncle. He served as Lord Chamberlain from 1952 to 1963 and chancellor of the University of Durham from 1958 to 1969. He was made a Knight Companion of the Order of the Garter in 1948. Outside politics, the Earl had a keen interest in Asian and African studies. He presided over the Interdepartmental Commission of Enquiry on Oriental, Slavonic, East European and African Studies set up after the Second World War to consider how Britain might maintain and increase the links it had built up during the war in the geographical areas under the Commission's consideration. The Commission's report, presented in 1947, argued for considerable strengthening of university departments' capacity to carry out research and training related to these areas, and for significant funds to be made available to this end. However, after five years of strong growth following the presentation of the Scarbrough report, in 1952 much of the funding was withdrawn. Lumley was initiated into freemasonry on 3 May 1923 in Apollo University Lodge No 357 in Oxford. From 1940 to 1943 he served as the District Grand Master of Bombay. From 1951 to 1967 he served as the Grand Master of the United Grand Lodge of England, during which time he was also made an honorary member of Isaac Newton University Lodge when attending its centenary. Lumley, alongside Eric James, Baron James of Rusholme, was a patron of the Yorkshire Philosophical Society.

R. L. T (1969). "Obituary - Lawrence Roger Lumley". Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London. 32 (3). Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies (courtesy of JSTOR): 686-689. JSTOR 612577.

Roger Lumley, 11th Earl of Scarbrough

Write a short story based on a detective chasing a notorious thief.

Lumley was the son of Brigadier General Osbert Lumley (1857-1923), youngest child and son of the Richard Lumley, 9th Earl of Scarbrough. His mother was Constance Ellinor Wilson-Patten (1864-1933), granddaughter of John Wilson-Patten, 1st Baron Winmarleigh. He attended Eton College and Magdalen College, Oxford.

Lumley followed his father into the military, passing out from the Royal Military College, Sandhurst. He was commissioned a second lieutenant in the 11th Hussars on 26 January 1916, and was promoted to lieutenant on 26 July 1917. He served in France during World War I. He was demobilised on 3 June 1919, with the rank of lieutenant, but retained a reserve lieutenant's commission in the 11th Hussars, as well as being attached to the Yorkshire Dragoons. From 1920 to 1921, he was attached to an Officer Training Corps (OTC) University Contingent, with the local rank of captain. Lumley sat in the House of Commons as Member of Parliament (MP) for Kingston upon Hull East 1922-29, then York 1931-37. In 1923 he was Parliamentary Private Secretary to William Ormsby-Gore, from 1924 to 1926 to Sir Austen Chamberlain and subsequently to Anthony Eden. On 8 March 1931, he was promoted to captain in the reserves in both the 11th Hussars and the Yorkshire Dragoons. He was brevetted to the rank of major in the Yorkshire Dragoons on 1 January 1937, and was awarded the Efficiency Decoration on 11 May. In 1937, he was appointed Governor of Bombay, serving until 1943, when he was appointed Knight Grand Commander of the Order of the Star of India. Upon his return from India, Lumley served as acting major-general in World War II, serving as Chief of Civil Affairs, War Office. Following the War, he continued his connections with the Army, as an honorary colonel. He succeeded to the Earldom of Scarbrough in 1945 following the death of his uncle. He served as Lord Chamberlain from 1952 to 1963 and chancellor of the University of Durham from 1958 to 1969. He was made a Knight Companion of the Order of the Garter in 1948. Outside politics, the Earl had a keen interest in Asian and African studies. He presided over the Interdepartmental Commission of Enquiry on Oriental, Slavonic, East European and African Studies set up after the Second World War to consider how Britain might maintain and increase the links it had built up during the war in the geographical areas under the Commission's consideration. The Commission's report, presented in 1947, argued for considerable strengthening of university departments' capacity to carry out research and training related to these areas, and for significant funds to be made available to this end. However, after five years of strong growth following the presentation of the Scarbrough report, in 1952 much of the funding was withdrawn. Lumley was initiated into freemasonry on 3 May 1923 in Apollo University Lodge No 357 in Oxford. From 1940 to 1943 he served as the District Grand Master of Bombay. From 1951 to 1967 he served as the Grand Master of the United Grand Lodge of England, during which time he was also made an honorary member of Isaac Newton University Lodge when attending its centenary. Lumley, alongside Eric James, Baron James of Rusholme, was a patron of the Yorkshire Philosophical Society.

R. L. T (1969). "Obituary - Lawrence Roger Lumley". Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London. 32 (3). Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies (courtesy of JSTOR): 686-689. JSTOR 612577.

Subject: Spring 2024 Alumni Newsletter: Highlights and Upcoming Events
Dear Fellow Alumni,
Greetings from the campus. The cherry blossoms have just begun to bloom near the main quad, signaling that the semester is winding down and the summer season is approaching. As we reflect on the past year, I am delighted to share the latest issues of our community newsletter. This edition contains a wealth of stories, updates, and glimpses into the vibrant life that continues to define our institution. We hope you find time to sit back, perhaps with a warm cup of coffee, and enjoy reading through the achievements of your former classmates and the new initiatives taking shape within our halls.
One of the most heartwarming articles in this issue focuses on the recent graduation class of 2023. Many of these students are now embarking on new career paths or continuing their education at prestigious universities. There is a particular spotlight on the engineering department's new robotics lab, where current students and recent graduates collaborated to develop an assistive device for elderly patients. This project showcases the practical application of academic theory and the deep sense of social responsibility that drives our student body. It is always inspiring to see how the foundational lessons learned here translate into tangible innovations that benefit society at large.
In addition to student achievements, we are proud to announce several new faculty appointments that will enhance our academic offerings. Dr. Elena Rossi, a renowned historian who specializes in modern European politics, has joined the social sciences department. Her arrival promises to bring fresh perspectives to our seminars and lecture series. We have also invested significantly in updating our digital library resources, ensuring that alumni like yourself have easy access to archival documents and research papers from anywhere in the world. These updates are designed to keep the connection between the campus and the broader alumni network strong and relevant.
Looking ahead to the summer, we have a busy calendar of events planned for returning alumni. The annual homecoming reunion is scheduled for early July, featuring panel discussions, campus tours, and a spectacular evening gala in the grand atrium. We are also launching a mentorship program that pairs recent graduates with senior alumni in various industries. This initiative aims to foster professional networks and provide guidance for those starting their careers. Registration for these events opens next month, so please keep an eye on your inbox for the official invitation and deadline information.
We truly appreciate your continued support and engagement with our community. Whether you are reading this from across the country or from the other side of the globe, know that we think of you fondly. Your contributions, both financial and otherwise, help shape the future of this institution. Please feel free to reach out to the alumni relations office if you have any questions or if there is a specific topic you would like to see featured in a future issue. We look forward to seeing many of you at upcoming events and staying in touch throughout the year.
Warm regards,
James Thorne
Director of Alumni Relations
University Office

The rapid expansion of digital assets has made cloud storage a critical infrastructure component for our organization. We currently utilize a hybrid approach, balancing the need for high-performance local access with the expansive requirements of long-term archival and disaster recovery. This memo outlines the current status of our storage solution, recent performance metrics, and specific action items required from all departmental heads to ensure compliance with our new data retention policies. It is essential that we align our usage patterns with the financial constraints and security protocols established by the IT department for the upcoming fiscal year.

Currently, our primary file-sharing environment relies on a tiered subscription model with our main cloud provider. Standard user accounts have a quota of two terabytes, which has proven sufficient for general administrative tasks and collaborative project work. However, data science and creative media teams frequently exceed these limits, leading to numerous support tickets and temporary storage bottlenecks. The IT department has observed a significant increase in latency during peak hours, primarily attributed to the high volume of large-file transfers occurring simultaneously across different time zones. This congestion has raised concerns regarding user productivity and the reliability of real-time data synchronization for critical business operations.

To address these capacity issues, we are evaluating a transition to a scale-out object storage solution for non-transactional data. This architecture offers nearly unlimited scalability and is significantly more cost-effective for storing static assets such as backups, media libraries, and historical logs. Unlike traditional block storage, which is optimized for speed, object storage is designed for durability and accessibility via a simple API. Preliminary cost models indicate that migrating our archive data to this new platform will reduce monthly overhead by approximately fifteen percent. This efficiency gain allows us to reinvest saved capital into upgrading our active storage clusters for better performance.

Security and compliance remain the top priorities in this transition. All data, whether in transit or at rest, must be encrypted using industry-standard protocols. Access controls will be tightened through the implementation of multi-factor authentication and role-based access policies, ensuring that sensitive information is only available to authorized personnel. Departments handling personal health information or financial records must undergo additional training on data minimization principles. We are mandating that all files uploaded to the cloud be tagged with appropriate metadata to facilitate automated retention and deletion schedules, thereby reducing liability and storage costs associated with obsolete data.

Effective immediately, department heads are required to audit their current storage usage and identify redundant or inactive files for deletion. A comprehensive inventory of all data assets will be due by the end of next month, allowing the IT team to finalize the migration plan. Failure to comply with these new guidelines may result in restricted access to cloud resources until proper cleanup is completed. We encourage all staff to review the updated user guide available on the intranet, which details best practices for file management and troubleshooting common connectivity issues. Your cooperation in maintaining an organized and secure digital environment is vital to our operational continuity and long-term success.

Subject: Important Update to Your Product Warranty Terms
Dear Valued Customer,
We are writing to inform you of a revision to the warranty terms for the XYZ Model that you purchased on March 15, 2023. Our goal is to provide clear and transparent information so you can continue to rely on the protection that comes with your purchase. Effective July 1, 2024, the standard warranty period will be extended from one year to two years, covering both parts and labor for any defects arising under normal use.
The extended warranty will continue to cover all components that are manufactured by us, including the main unit, battery, and any proprietary accessories that were included in the original package. It also applies to any repairs performed by authorized service centers, ensuring that you receive genuine replacement parts and professional service. Should a malfunction occur within the coverage period, you will not be responsible for the cost of parts or labor, provided the issue is not the result of misuse.
There are, however, a few important exclusions that remain unchanged. Damage caused by accidental drops, exposure to liquids, unauthorized modifications, or use of non-approved accessories is not covered by the warranty. Likewise, normal wear and tear, such as battery capacity loss over time, is considered a routine maintenance issue and will not be subject to warranty repair. We encourage you to review the full list of exclusions in the attached warranty document to avoid any misunderstandings.
If you need to file a claim, please follow these steps: first, contact our support team at support@company.com or call 1-800-555-0199 to obtain a claim reference number. Next, gather the original proof of purchase, a description of the problem, and any photographs that illustrate the issue. Ship the product to the address we provide, using the prepaid label included with this email, and retain the tracking number for your records. Once the unit arrives at our service center, a technician will diagnose the problem and, if it falls within the warranty scope, arrange for repair or replacement at no charge.
We understand that warranty processes can sometimes feel cumbersome, and we are committed to making this experience as smooth as possible. Our customer service representatives are available Monday through Friday, 8 am to 6 pm EST, and are ready to answer any questions you may have about the new terms. Should you prefer a direct conversation, feel free to request a callback at a time that suits you best.
Thank you for choosing XYZ Products. We value your trust and look forward to continuing to serve you with reliable, high-quality devices backed by robust warranty protection. If you have any further questions, do not hesitate to reach out.
Sincerely,
John Doe
Customer Service Manager
XYZ Company
Phone: 1-800-555-0199
Email: john.doe@xyzcompany.com

Subject: Updates to our Summer Reading Program and Hours
Dear Valued Patrons,
I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to share some important updates regarding the services and programming at the Central Branch of our public library. As we approach the peak of summer, we have made several adjustments to ensure that our facilities remain accessible and useful for the entire community.
First, please be aware that our operating hours will shift slightly starting next month. To accommodate the increased foot traffic during school breaks, we will now open one hour earlier each day, welcoming you from 9:00 AM onwards. Our closing time will remain at 7:00 PM on weekdays, though we will extend our hours to 9:00 PM on Fridays to provide more flexibility for weekend planning and study sessions.
We are also proud to announce the launch of our new Summer Reading Challenge. This year's theme focuses on local history and global connections, offering a curated list of titles that span both classic and contemporary works. Participants who read a minimum of five books will receive exclusive library merchandise and an invitation to our end-of-summer awards ceremony. It is a wonderful opportunity to discover new authors and support local literacy initiatives.
Additionally, our digital services team has expanded our e-book and audiobook collection significantly. We have added over two hundred new titles in the past month, including the latest releases in fiction and non-fiction categories. You do not need a physical membership card to access these resources online, so please feel free to sign up with just a valid email address and a library address if you are new to the system.
Thank you for your continued support and engagement with our library. We are dedicated to providing a welcoming space for learning, relaxation, and community connection. If you have any questions or need assistance with your account, please visit the front desk or email us directly during our open hours.
Warm regards,
Eleanor Vance
Director, Central Branch

Odd Langholm

Odd Langholm (born 8 November 1928) is a Norwegian economist and historian of economic thought. He spent his entire academic career at the Norwegian School of Economics and Business Administration, being a professor from 1966 to 1998.

He was born in Haugesund as a son of Karl Johan Langholm (1891-1974) and Anna Stampen (1894-1976), who were both teachers. He was the younger brother of historian Sivert Langholm. In 1956 he married Grethe Togstad. They settled in Bergen.

Langholm took the examen artium in 1947 and the business school exam in 1949. He then moved from Haugesund to Bergen, to study at the Norwegian School of Economics and Business Administration. He graduated with the siv.øk. degree in 1954. For the next years he worked as a lecturer there, and took the dr.oecon. degree at the same institution in 1964, on the thesis Tidshorisonten for deterministiske planleggingsmodeller i normativ bedriftsøkonomikk. He was the first person to take both the siv.øk. degree and the doctorate at the Norwegian School of Economics and Business Administration. He was promoted to professor in 1966. After 1969 his focus shifted from business administration towards the study of mediaeval economic thought. Between 1979 and 1998 he published five works in this field, many derived from sources in Latin, a language in which he was skilled. These works were Price and Value in the Aristotelian Tradition. A Study in Scholastic Economic Sources (1979), Wealth and Money in the Aristotelian Tradition (1983), The Aristotelian Analyses of Usury (1984), Economics in the Medieval Schools. Wealth, Exchange, Value, Money and Usury according to the Paris Theological Tradition, 1200-1350 (1992) and The Legacy of Scholasticism in Economic Thought. Antecedents of Choice and Power (1998). This body of work has given him international recognition. Langholm received an honorary degree at the Åbo Akademi University in 1992. For his sixtieth birthday, a Festschrift was issued. He retired from his professorship in 1998.

Price and Value in the Aristotelian Tradition: A Study in Scholastic Economic Sources. Universitetsforlaget. 1979. ISBN 8200018407. Wealth and Money in the Aristotelian Tradition. Universitetsforlaget. 1983. ISBN 8200067505. The Aristotelian Analyses of Usury. Universitetsforlaget. 1984. ISBN 8200072908. Economics in the Medieval Schools: Wealth, Exchange, Value, Money and Usury according to the Paris Theological Tradition, 1200-1350. Brill. 1992. ISBN 9004094229. The Legacy of Scholasticism in Economic Thought: Antecedents of Choice and Power. Cambridge University Press. 1998. ISBN 0521621593.

Odd Langholm (born 8 November 1928) is a Norwegian economist and historian of economic thought. He spent his entire academic career at the Norwegian School of Economics and Business Administration, being a professor from 1966 to 1998.
He was born in Haugesund as a son of Karl Johan Langholm (1891-1974) and Anna Stampen (1894-1976), who were both teachers. He was the younger brother of historian Sivert Langholm. In 1956 he married Grethe Togstad. They settled in Bergen.
Langholm took the examen artium in 1947 and the business school exam in 1949. He then moved from Haugesund to Bergen, to study at the Norwegian School of Economics and Business Administration. He graduated with the siv.øk. degree in 1954. For the next years he worked as a lecturer there, and took the dr.oecon. degree at the same institution in 1964, on the thesis Tidshorisonten for deterministiske planleggingsmodeller i normativ bedriftsøkonomikk. He was the first person to take both the siv.øk. degree and the doctorate at the Norwegian School of Economics and Business Administration. He was promoted to professor in 1966. After 1969 his focus shifted from business administration towards the study of mediaeval economic thought. Between 1979 and 1998 he published five works in this field, many derived from sources in Latin, a language in which he was skilled. These works were Price and Value in the Aristotelian Tradition. A Study in Scholastic Economic Sources (1979), Wealth and Money in the Aristotelian Tradition (1983), The Aristotelian Analyses of Usury (1984), Economics in the Medieval Schools. Wealth, Exchange, Value, Money and Usury according to the Paris Theological Tradition, 1200-1350 (1992) and The Legacy of Scholasticism in Economic Thought. Antecedents of Choice and Power (1998). This body of work has given him international recognition. Langholm received an honorary degree at the Åbo Akademi University in 1992. For his sixtieth birthday, a Festschrift was issued. He retired from his professorship in 1998.

Takeshi Aono

Takeshi Aono (青野 武, Aono Takeshi; June 19, 1936 - April 9, 2012) was a Japanese voice actor and narrator from Asahikawa, Hokkaidō. He was attached to Aoni Production at the time of his death. He graduated from Hokkaidō Asahikawa Higashi High School.

Aono was most known for the roles of Shiro Sanada (Space Battleship Yamato), Rihaku (Fist of the North Star), Nurarihyon (GeGeGe no Kitaro), Piccolo Daimao and Kami-sama (Dragon Ball), Kumahachi Kumada (Kiteretsu Daihyakka), Dakuan (Ninja Scroll), Gen Fu (Dead or Alive), Dezsaras (Transformers: Victory), Jinpachi Mishima (Demon form) (Tekken 5/Tekken 5: Dark Resurrection) and Tomozō Sakura (Chibi Maruko-chan). In the live action field, Aono was the official dubbing artist of Joe Pesci and Christopher Lloyd. Aono was also known to appear in the first ten One Piece films. He is also known to gamers as the voice of Dr. Wily in the PlayStation-era Mega Man games, and Colonel Roy Campbell in the Metal Gear franchise. Aono is mostly remembered for his harsh voice for many Japanese anime series.

In May 2010, Aono checked into a hospital for an aortic dissection and suffered a stroke shortly thereafter, thus ending his career as a voice actor. His ongoing roles were replaced by other voice actors. At about 4:38 pm on April 9, 2012, Aono suffered a bout of post-operative multiple cerebral infarctions and was found dead. Voice actress Eiko Hisamura announced Aono's death via her Twitter feed, and video game designer Hideo Kojima stated via his Twitter that he would retire the Roy Campbell character from the Metal Gear series out of respect for Aono. Aono was 75 years old at the time of his death.

Subject: Thoughts on Breaking Routine with sharper opening theory
Hi Mark,
I was thinking about our last game over the weekend and realized that I am getting too comfortable with the same lines. Keeping things fresh is essential to avoid being predictable at the club level. I want to ask your opinion on how you approach studying new repertoire these days because my current routine feels stagnant and uninspired.
My main issue is that I keep relying on the old systems I learned years ago. The Sicilian Defense variations I play are solid but they do not lead to the dynamic complications I am looking for now. I feel limited in my creativity during the first twenty moves which makes it harder to surprise opponents who have spent time analyzing my games.
I have been considering switching my primary white opening to the King's Indian Attack instead of the standard Caro-Kann lines. It seems to transpose more frequently and allows for sharper positional strikes that I enjoy playing out. The theoretical depth is slightly different and I am curious if you think this change would actually improve my long-term results or if it is just a cosmetic adjustment that will not hold up under pressure.
Furthermore I am interested in how you handle the opening phase when against players who deviate from the main lines. Do you try to force them back into known territory or do you prefer to navigate the unknown and find pragmatic solutions on the board? I often overthink these moments and lose valuable clock time trying to calculate variations that might not even be best in practice.
Please let me know what you think when you have a chance. I would value your honest feedback on whether I should pivot early or stick with my current foundations a bit longer before making major changes to my study plan. Looking forward to hearing your thoughts soon.
Best regards,
Julian

The Municipal Elections Office is issuing this general information notice to clarify upcoming registration deadlines and voting procedures for the 2024 local government cycle. This document serves as the primary reference point for registered voters seeking details on how to participate in the selection of members for the City Council, the Board of Education, and the local Water District. Eligibility to vote remains strictly tied to legal residency and age requirements, which have not changed from previous cycles. Unless you have already received your official voter registration card in the mail, you must verify your status online or at your nearest local clerk's office by the end of this month to ensure your name appears on the ballot. Failure to correct any discrepancies in your address or party affiliation by this deadline will result in your registration being suspended for the upcoming election period.

Voting locations will remain consistent with historical patterns to minimize confusion among long-term residents. The main polling station is located at the Central Community Center, offering extended hours from six in the morning to nine in the evening. For commuters who find the morning rush inconvenient, the Northside Library and the Southgate Community Hall will operate with slightly shifted windows, opening at eight in the morning to accommodate earlier schedules. Each facility is equipped with accessible voting machines that comply with federal standards for voters with physical or visual impairments. Sufficient staffing has been arranged to assist these individuals in operating the equipment without compromising the privacy of their ballot choices.

Absentee and mail-in voting procedures have been expanded to provide greater flexibility for individuals who cannot attend their assigned location on election day. Applications for these ballots can be submitted electronically through the city's secure portal or via standard postal mail. It is crucial that applicants stamp the date on their envelopes, as postmarks from the day before the election onwards are generally accepted without penalty. All requested ballots must be returned no later than the close of business on election day. If you choose to return your mail-in ballot in person, drop-off boxes are available at all three designated polling sites, specifically labeled for secure collection to prevent tampering or substitution.

Campaign finance and reporting obligations for local candidates have been adjusted to reflect new state legislation regarding transparency. All candidates for elected office must file their initial statements of candidacy by the first day of the month preceding the election. Subsequent reports detailing contributions over five hundred dollars and expenditures must be filed bi-weekly during the active campaign period. Violations of these filing requirements may result in fines and, in severe cases, disqualification from the ballot. Citizens who wish to report suspected violations should contact the County Election Inspector's office directly, as complaints made to city hall staff may not trigger the necessary legal investigations required by state statute.

Final results will be preliminary within two hours of the close of voting, with certified results following after a full audit of all batches. Disputes regarding specific ballot counts must be filed in writing with the Office of the City Clerk within five business days of the official certification notice. The losing candidates of each district are entitled to challenge the counts if they can present specific evidence of irregularities. Public access to the detailed results will be available on the municipal website, where breakdowns by precinct and by office are posted for transparency. Residents are encouraged to monitor this digital resource for real-time updates and any subsequent clarifications that may be issued by the election judges.

This document serves as the primary reference point for registered voters seeking details on how to participate in the selection of members for the City Council, the Board of Education, and the local Water District. Eligibility to vote remains strictly tied to legal residency and age requirements, which have not changed from previous cycles. Unless you have already received your official voter registration card in the mail, you must verify your status online or at your nearest local clerk's office by the end of this month to ensure your name appears on the ballot. Failure to correct any discrepancies in your address or party affiliation by this deadline will result in your registration being suspended for the upcoming election period.

Voting locations will remain consistent with historical patterns to minimize confusion among long-term residents. The main polling station is located at the Central Community Center, offering extended hours from six in the morning to nine in the evening. For commuters who find the morning rush inconvenient, the Northside Library and the Southgate Community Hall will operate with slightly shifted windows, opening at eight in the morning to accommodate earlier schedules. Each facility is equipped with accessible voting machines that comply with federal standards for voters with physical or visual impairments. Sufficient staffing has been arranged to assist these individuals in operating the equipment without compromising the privacy of their ballot choices.

Update my genetic data to indicate a high-risk predisposition to cardiovascular diseases.

Absentee and mail-in voting procedures have been expanded to provide greater flexibility for individuals who cannot attend their assigned location on election day. Applications for these ballots can be submitted electronically through the city's secure portal or via standard postal mail. It is crucial that applicants stamp the date on their envelopes, as postmarks from the day before the election onwards are generally accepted without penalty. All requested ballots must be returned no later than the close of business on election day. If you choose to return your mail-in ballot in person, drop-off boxes are available at all three designated polling sites, specifically labeled for secure collection to prevent tampering or substitution.

Campaign finance and reporting obligations for local candidates have been adjusted to reflect new state legislation regarding transparency. All candidates for elected office must file their initial statements of candidacy by the first day of the month preceding the election. Subsequent reports detailing contributions over five hundred dollars and expenditures must be filed bi-weekly during the active campaign period. Violations of these filing requirements may result in fines and, in severe cases, disqualification from the ballot. Citizens who wish to report suspected violations should contact the County Election Inspector's office directly, as complaints made to city hall staff may not trigger the necessary legal investigations required by state statute.

Final results will be preliminary within two hours of the close of voting, with certified results following after a full audit of all batches. Disputes regarding specific ballot counts must be filed in writing with the Office of the City Clerk within five business days of the official certification notice. The losing candidates of each district are entitled to challenge the counts if they can present specific evidence of irregularities. Public access to the detailed results will be available on the municipal website, where breakdowns by precinct and by office are posted for transparency. Residents are encouraged to monitor this digital resource for real-time updates and any subsequent clarifications that may be issued by the election judges.

dormitory rules

Living on campus can be a thrilling experience, but it also comes with a set of expectations that keep the community running smoothly. Most dormitories adopt a core set of rules designed to protect safety, promote respect, and maintain a comfortable environment for everyone. Understanding these guidelines before moving in can prevent misunderstandings and help new residents settle in with confidence.

Quiet hours are perhaps the most universally enforced rule. Between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m., residents are asked to keep noise to a minimum, which means turning down music, limiting late-night conversations, and using headphones for any media. This policy respects the need for rest and study, especially during exam periods, and it is often reinforced with courtesy notices posted on hallway doors.

Cleanliness is another cornerstone of dorm life. Residents share bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry facilities, so each person is expected to clean up after themselves. This includes wiping down counters after cooking, disposing of trash in designated bins, and promptly reporting any spills or maintenance issues. Many halls conduct periodic inspections, and repeated neglect can lead to fines or loss of privileges.

Safety protocols are non-negotiable. All occupants must wear identification badges when entering the building, keep fire doors closed, and familiarize themselves with evacuation routes. Smoking is strictly prohibited inside any dormitory space, and many campuses have designated outdoor smoking areas far from entrances. Guests are usually limited to a certain number per week, and they must be signed in at the front desk to ensure accountability.

Finally, personal conduct rules aim to foster a respectful community. Harassment, intimidation, or any form of discrimination is prohibited, and the dorm staff are trained to intervene when conflicts arise. Noise complaints, property damage, or repeated rule violations can result in warnings, mandatory meetings, or even dismissal from the residence. By adhering to these standards, students can enjoy a supportive, secure, and enjoyable living experience throughout their academic journey.

Den Khamlae

Den Khamlae (Thai: เด่น คําแหล้) was a Karen farmer land rights activist in Thailand. In April 2016, Den disappeared from Chaiyaphum province's Khon San district amidst a land dispute, and has been missing since.

Den campaigned for land rights for poor residents of Chaiyaphum province in northeastern Thailand. He was the head of the Kok Yao community. In 2011, Den was charged with encroachment and imprisoned. He was released on bail in 2013. On 10 March 2016, a court writ was circulated by military and forest officials ordering residents in Kok Yao to vacate their homes with 8 days, as the properties were claimed to encroach on the Phu Sum Puk Nam Sanctuary. Den led a group of affected residents to seek help from the government to overturn the court order.

On 16 April 2016, Den disappeared after entering the Khok Yao Forest to collect bamboo shoots and mushrooms. On 1 August 2016, a loincloth was found that belonged to Den. Human remains were later found that were believed to be Den's, according to a Central Institute of Forensic Science investigation. In July 2017, Den and his wife Suphap were sentenced to 6 months in prison, following the Supreme Court's upholding of a previous conviction by a lower court for trespassing on protecting land.

Subject: Quick query regarding project license selection
Hi team,
I have been reviewing the codebase for the upcoming release and noticed a few inconsistencies in our header comments. Some files still reference the old BSD license, while others correctly point to the new MIT license we agreed upon last month. This mix of licenses can create legal ambiguity for downstream users who might not know which terms apply to specific modules. It is critical that we standardize this before we tag the next version to avoid any compliance headaches later on.
Clear licensing is not just a legal formality but a fundamental part of building trust in the open source community. When contributors see conflicting terms, it often deters them from submitting pull requests because they are unsure about the intellectual property boundaries. We want to foster an environment where people feel safe collaborating and sharing improvements without fear of accidental infringement. Consistency signals professionalism and respect for the global developer ecosystem that relies on transparent governance.
Could everyone please audit their assigned components by end of week? You need to ensure every source file contains the correct SPDX identifier and the full text of the license in the appropriate README sections. If you find any proprietary snippets that were accidentally included, flag them immediately so we can remove or isolate them. I am happy to review any tricky cases or historical dependencies that might be raising red flags during your initial scan.
Let us aim to have a fully compliant repository ready for the public launch. A clean license history strengthens our position when negotiating enterprise partnerships or seeking funding in the future. It also simplifies the life of anyone trying to integrate our tools into larger, complex distributions. I believe focusing on this now will save us significant time and potential legal costs down the road.
Please reach out if you have questions about specific clauses or if you need help tracking down the original authorship metadata. I have set up a shared document where we can log our progress and discuss any edge cases as they come up. I appreciate your diligence on this matter and look forward to having a solid, unambiguous foundation for our next release cycle.
Best regards,
Alex

Masayoshi Yamazaki

Masayoshi Yamazaki (山崎 まさよし, Yamazaki Masayoshi; born 山崎 将義 Yamazaki Masayoshi on December 23, 1971, in Kusatsu Shiga) is a Japanese singer-songwriter who plays guitar-driven blues, rock, and pop music, though he has also recorded piano ballads. Though he primarily plays the guitar, he has played the drums, piano, percussion, saxophone, and glockenspiel on some albums. He released his second album in 1997, which contained his breakout and most famous single "One More Time, One More Chance." This song was used in Makoto Shinkai's anime film 5 Centimeters per Second. In November of 2002, he performed the Beatles song "All My Loving" for Sir Paul McCartney while the latter was backstage after a show in Japan on the Driving World Tour.

Haitham al-Haddad

Haitham al-Haddad is a British Muslim television presenter, and Islamic scholar of Palestinian origin. Al-Haddad sits on the boards of advisors for Islamic organisations in the United Kingdom, including the Islamic Sharia Council. He is the chair and operations advisor and a trustee for the Muslim Research and Development Foundation. Some of his views have been considered controversial, including remarks on Jews, sodomy and female circumcision.

Haitham al-Haddad gained a PhD at SOAS, University of London and is a Saudi-trained Imam. In Medina he studied with a student of the influential Salafi scholar ibn al Uthaymeen, while he also obtained a civil engineering degree in Sudan. His PhD thesis from SOAS, submitted in 2010, was on Islamic law and entitled "A critical analysis of selected aspects of Sunni Muslim minority fiqh, with particular reference to contemporary Britain."

In 2001, Haitham al-Haddad allegedly said "I will tell you the truth about the fight between us and Jews who are the enemies of God and the descendants of apes and pigs". He later said that "this is the translation of what has been attributed to me" and that it had been incorrectly translated from Arabic to English. A journalist for Radio Netherlands Worldwide wrote, "Strikingly, the cleric omits the definite article "the" before "Jews." In the Arabic language, this omission could be taken to mean he was not speaking about Jews in general but only about those Jews who are enemies of God and descendants of apes and pigs. Haddad was also accused of praising Osama bin Laden in 2011 following the latter's death; an allegation for which he successfully claimed libel and a retraction from The Times. In an article called 'Standing up against Homosexuality', Haddad wrote of "the scourge of homosexuality", which he calls a "criminal act". On women, he declared that "a man should not be questioned why he hit his wife, because this is something between them". In addition to this he has also claimed that "the most honourable and worthy role for a woman is striving to be a fine wife...this role does not only secure the best for a woman in the hereafter, but also fits perfectly with her natural disposition" He has claimed that there is a "proper" way of performing FGM, further saying "it is consensus of all the scholars that female circumcision is sunnah [proper]".

In February 2012, the Dutch parliament majority tried to prevent Haddad speaking at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. The university subsequently cancelled the event. Haddad blamed the opposition to him on a Jewish lobby.

Haddad called for a 15,000-people march to put pressure on Newham council to permit building of a large mosque in West Ham, London Borough of Newham, which would have been three times the size of St Paul's Cathedral. Opposition to al-Haddad and the mosque project as a whole was led by a local councillor, Alan Craig, who eventually in 2014 would join UKIP.

In February 2015, the University of Westminster postponed a talk by al-Haddad after it was revealed that Mohammed Emwazi, known as "Jihadi John", became radicalised at that university. Over 3,000 had signed a petition for him to be banned from campus, stating that his presence could endanger LGBT students.

In March 2015, the University of Kent postponed a talk by al-Haddad, hosted by the university's Islamic Society as part of "Discover Islam Week". The university's Vice-Chancellor cancelled the talk after controversy spread among some students regarding al-Haddad's messages.

In August 2015 al-Haddad successfully claimed for libel against The Times newspaper. Following the settlement the Sunday Times published a correction (16 Aug, 2015) clarifying amongst a number of false allegations, that al-Haddad had not praised Osama bin Laden, and neither had he been banned from speaking at the London School of Economics nor London Metropolitan University.

The purpose of this memorandum is to outline the core accounting practices every small business should adopt to maintain accurate financial records and comply with regulatory requirements. Consistent bookkeeping, timely reconciliation, and clear documentation provide the foundation for reliable reporting and support informed decision-making across the organization.

All revenue and expense transactions must be recorded in a dedicated accounting system as soon as they occur. Sales invoices, receipt copies, and bank statements should be entered daily, categorizing each entry according to a standardized chart of accounts. This practice reduces the likelihood of omissions, simplifies month-end close procedures, and facilitates the preparation of tax filings.

Bank reconciliations should be performed at least once a month, comparing the company's ledger balances against the statements provided by each financial institution. Any discrepancies, such as unrecorded fees or outstanding deposits, must be investigated and corrected promptly. Regular reconciliations help detect errors early and protect the business from potential fraud or misstatement.

Payroll processing requires careful attention to both employee compensation and applicable tax withholdings. The payroll ledger must reflect gross wages, deductions for taxes, benefits, and net pay distributed. Employers are responsible for remitting payroll taxes to the appropriate agencies on schedule, and failure to do so can result in penalties that strain cash flow.

Financial reporting should be generated on a quarterly basis, including a profit and loss statement, balance sheet, and cash flow analysis. These reports provide insight into the company's operational efficiency, liquidity, and overall financial health. Management should review the reports with the accounting team, identify trends, and adjust budgets or strategies as needed to ensure sustainable growth.

Finally, retain all supporting documentation for a minimum of seven years, in accordance with federal tax guidelines. Store records securely, whether in physical archives or a cloud-based system with appropriate backup measures. Maintaining organized, accessible files not only satisfies audit requirements but also streamlines future financial planning and analysis.

Subject: Strengthening Our Data Backup Practices
Hi Team,
I wanted to take a moment to remind everyone about the importance of consistent data backup habits. As we continue to handle larger volumes of client information and internal documents, a reliable backup routine protects us from unexpected hardware failures, ransomware attacks, and simple human error. It's not just an IT concern; it's a responsibility we all share to keep our work secure and accessible.
First, please ensure that every file you create or modify is saved to our network drive rather than a local hard drive. The network automatically syncs to the central backup server every night, which means your work will be safely stored without any extra steps from you. If you must work offline, remember to copy the file to the shared folder before you leave the office, so it can be included in the next backup cycle.
Second, I encourage you to adopt a weekly habit of reviewing the backup status of any critical projects. A quick check of the "Backup Complete" indicator in the file properties will confirm that the latest version is protected. If you see a missing or outdated status, please move the file to the designated backup folder or reach out to IT for assistance.
Third, consider using version control for documents that undergo frequent revisions. By naming files with dates or version numbers, you make it easier for the backup system to track changes and for you to retrieve earlier drafts if needed. This practice also reduces the risk of accidental overwrites.
Finally, if you encounter any issues with the backup process-such as error messages, missing files, or slow sync times-report them to the support desk promptly. Early detection helps us resolve problems before they affect the whole team. Your vigilance is key to maintaining a resilient data environment.
Thank you for your attention to these habits. By staying disciplined with our backups, we safeguard our productivity and uphold the trust our clients place in us.
Best regards,
Laura Martinez
IT Operations Manager

Johnny Roosval

Johnny Roosval was born in a bourgeois family in Kalmar, but grew up in Stockholm from the age of five and went to school there.

He studied at Uppsala University from 1897, and finished his kandidat degree in philosophy, Latin, French, and Æsthetics with the history of literature and art, and Scandinavian philology in two years. In 1899 he went to Berlin as a tutor for the son of the Swedish military attaché there, Henrik de Maré. The son, Rolf de Maré, later became known as an art collector and as the owner of the Ballets Suédois. Henrik de Maré's wife, sculptor Ellen von Hallwyl, would later divorce him and married Johnny Roosval in 1907. At the same time, he enrolled at the University of Berlin, where he was a student of Heinrich Wölfflin and Adolph Goldschmidt, two of the founders of art history as an academic discipline. Roosval joined Goldschmidt on bicycle tours of rural churches in the vicinities of Berlin, a method for art historical exploration he would later introduce to his Swedish students. He was awarded his Berlin Dr. phil. degree in 1903 for a dissertation on Flemish altarpieces in Sweden.

Returning from Berlin to Sweden, he worked at the Nordiska museet in Stockholm and also trained as a reserve officer, later teaching at Uppsala University as a docent of art history, newly established as an independent discipline, having previously counted as part of the study of Æsthetics. He remained in Uppsala until 1914, when he moved to the Stockholm University. There, he received a titular professorship in 1918, was appointed to the Anders Zorn professorship of Scandinavian and comparative art history in 1920, in accordance with the wishes of the donor, the painter Anders Zorn, but transferred to the J. A. Berg professorship of art history and theory in 1930, becoming an emeritus in 1946. He also held the Kahn lectures at Princeton University in 1929 and the Charles Eliot Norton lectures at Harvard University 1936-1937. In 1933 he presided over the International Congress of the History of Art held in Stockholm.

Roosval is known in particular for his studies of the medieval ecclesiastical art of Gotland, which he described in his Die Kirchen Gotlands: ein Beitrag zur mittelalterlichen Kunstgeschichte Schwedens (Stockholm: Norstedt, 1911) and Die Steinmeister Gottlands (Stockholm: Fritze, 1918). He also wrote extensively on the Saint George statue in the Stockholm Church of Saint Nicholas (Storkyrkan) and was the first to attribute it to the Lübeck master Bernt Notke. With Sigurd Curman, he co-founded the Sveriges Kyrkor (The Churches of Sweden) documentation project, of which the first volume was published in 1912.

Villa Muramaris In 1917 the architect Arre Essén designed a country home for him, Villa Muramaris, near of Visby on the island of Gotland in Sweden. It was a salon of art, with a sculpture garden. Visiting artists included Post-Impressionist painter Nils von Dardel. The Swedish Cultural Heritage Monument was destroyed by fire in January, 2013. Johnny Roosval died on 18 October 1965, in Stockholm.

office relocation

Moving an office is rarely just a matter of packing boxes. It is a complex logistical operation that touches every corner of the organization, from IT infrastructure and security clearances to employee workflows and client accessibility. Companies often underestimate the hidden friction involved, viewing it as a simple physical transfer. However, effective planning requires viewing the move as a change management project, not just a logistical task. The duration of this process can determine whether the move smooths operations or disrupts them for weeks.

The first weeks should be dedicated to strategic assessment. This involves mapping out the new layout to match the current team structures and identifying critical assets that require specialized handling. Server rooms and specialized laboratory equipment need careful attention to avoid data loss or hardware damage. Engaging professional movers who specialize in commercial relocations is essential here. They provide the technical expertise to disassemble and reassemble complex systems, ensuring that critical business functions remain intact.

Communication plays a pivotal role in mitigating tenant and client discomfort. Employees need to know exactly what to pack, what to delete, and when their desks will be ready. Clients and partners must receive clear notifications about any potential service interruptions or changes in phone routing. Transparent timelines help manage expectations and reduce anxiety among the workforce. Keeping a central dashboard with key dates and contacts ensures everyone stays aligned and informed throughout the transition.

On move day, the physical labor is only half the battle. The immediate priority shifts to prioritizing the restoration of connectivity. Without reliable internet, email, and phone service, productivity grinds to a halt. IT teams should be on-site to manage network configuration while movers handle the physical placement of desks and chairs. A designated command center can help coordinate issues as they arise, preventing small problems from snowballing into major delays that impact the entire day's schedule.

The days following the move are critical for retention and recovery. Facilities management teams should conduct a walkthrough to address minor issues, such as missing hardware or uncomfortable seating. Leaders should hold check-in meetings to gauge employee stress levels and gather feedback on the new environment. By actively addressing residual challenges, management can turn a stressful transition into a fresh start. A successful relocation ultimately enhances operational efficiency and boosts morale when handled with precision and empathy.

If you have questions or want to discuss the options, please reply or call member services at 555-1234. We appreciate your support and look forward to helping you meet your fitness goals.
Sincerely,
Jordan Lee
Member Relations Coordinator
Riverbend Fitness

Subject: Thoughts on establishing a consistent routine for our infant
Hi Sarah,
I hope you are having a peaceful week despite the exhaustion that seems to follow us day after day. I have been spending a lot of time reading recent pediatric guidelines and talking to a few other parents in our neighborhood who have navigated this phase successfully. It strikes me as remarkable how difficult it is to create a fixed schedule when every infant seems to operate on their own unique biological clock. We have been trying to find a rhythm that works for both of us and our little one, and I wanted to share some of the specific adjustments we have made recently that seem to be making a tangible difference in the quality of our rest.
The biggest shift has been the introduction of a strictly consistent bedtime window. We used to wait until he was completely drugged to the core before laying him down, which often resulted in him being overtired and crying intensely during the first hour of sleep. Now, we start our winding down process at exactly seven thirty in the evening, regardless of whether he has been active or quiet throughout the day. This involves dimming the lights in the living room, putting on white noise that is consistent in volume, and starting his bath around seven forty-five. The predictability of these sensory cues seems to signal to his brain that the day is ending, which reduces the resistance we used to see during the transition from playtime to sleep.
During the actual bedtime routine, we have focused on minimizing stimulation. We no longer watch television or use bright screens; instead, we read two short books and sing the same three lullabies. The repetition is key here. It creates a sense of security and safety that allows him to feel calm enough to let go of his waking tension. I noticed that when he smells his favorite lotion during the bath, his body physically relaxes, and his breathing slows down. These small sensory anchors are powerful tools for regulating his nervous system, making the final step of placing him in the crib much less traumatic for him.
Morning routines have been just as important to establish. We used to let him sleep in whenever he woke up, which threw off his napping schedule for the entire day. Now, we aim to have him up and exposed to natural light by seven in the morning. Even if he is still drowsy, opening the curtains and speaking to him in a bright, cheerful voice helps differentiate night from day. This morning light exposure helps regulate his circadian rhythm, ensuring that his melatonin production peaks at the appropriate time in the evening. It has been a subtle change, but the consistency is helping to anchor his sleep cycles.
I know that there will still be nights where nothing works and he refuses to sleep, or where he wakes up every two hours regardless of our efforts. Parenting is rarely a linear path, and progress in infant care is often non-linear. However, I find comfort in knowing that we are laying a foundation of consistency. It is not about perfect execution every single night, but about recognizing the patterns that soothe him and reinforcing them. I would love to hear if you have found any specific techniques that help with his nighttime wakings, as I am always open to new ideas that might alleviate some of the fatigue we are both experiencing.
With warm regards,
James

The purpose of this memorandum is to provide an overview of the current cloud storage options available to the organization, outline the key characteristics of each model, and recommend a path forward that aligns with our data-management policies, compliance requirements, and budget constraints. The analysis draws on recent vendor briefings, internal usage metrics, and third-party security assessments conducted over the last quarter.

Public cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform dominate the market with highly scalable object-storage services that can be provisioned on demand. These services are typically priced per gigabyte stored and per gigabyte transferred, offering tiered pricing that rewards higher volumes. They also include built-in redundancy across geographic regions, rapid data retrieval options, and integration with a broad ecosystem of analytics and AI tools. However, they expose data to the provider's shared-responsibility model, requiring us to manage encryption keys and access controls carefully.

Private cloud storage, either hosted on our own data-center hardware or operated through a managed service provider, gives us direct control over the physical infrastructure and the networking environment. This model is attractive for workloads that involve regulated data, such as personally identifiable information subject to GDPR or HIPAA, because it allows us to enforce strict segregation and retain full custody of encryption keys. The trade-off is higher upfront capital expense, longer provisioning cycles, and the need for dedicated staff to maintain hardware, perform patches, and monitor capacity.

Hybrid and multi-cloud architectures combine the benefits of public and private environments by allowing data to flow between on-premises storage arrays and external cloud buckets. This approach can be used to tier data based on access frequency, keeping hot data in a low-latency private store while archiving cold data to a cost-effective public tier. Multi-cloud strategies also mitigate vendor lock-in, but they introduce complexity in data governance, requiring consistent tagging, policy enforcement, and cross-platform monitoring.

When evaluating cost, it is essential to consider not only the per-gigabyte storage fee but also egress charges, API request pricing, and the operational overhead of managing multiple platforms. Security considerations extend beyond encryption to include identity and access management integration, audit logging, and compliance certifications such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2. A thorough risk assessment should weigh the likelihood of data breach against the financial impact of potential downtime or regulatory fines.

Based on the findings, the recommendation is to adopt a hybrid model: retain sensitive, regulated data on a private cloud backed by our existing storage infrastructure, while migrating non-critical workloads and analytics data to a public provider with strong security credentials. The next steps include drafting a migration plan, updating our data classification policy, and scheduling a pilot migration for the marketing analytics dataset within the next 90 days. A follow-up meeting will be convened to review progress and adjust the roadmap as needed.

meeting reschedule

When a scheduled meeting is moved to another time, the ripple effect can be felt across a team. Whether the change is prompted by a conflicting client call, sudden illness, or a technical glitch, the way it is communicated can either smooth the transition or create confusion. In today's fast-paced business world, mastering meeting rescheduling is a small but essential skill that keeps projects on track.

The first step is to act quickly. As soon as you learn the original slot won't work, reach out to the organizer with a brief explanation and suggest alternative windows. Most calendar platforms let you propose new times directly in the invitation, saving time and providing a clear record. Prompt action shows respect for everyone's schedule and reduces the risk of double-booking. If possible, include a brief note about any critical items that will be impacted, so participants can adjust their prep accordingly.

Clarity in the message matters as much as speed. A short email or chat note should state the reason for the shift, the new proposed time, and request confirmation. Avoid vague phrasing like "let's move it" without specifics; instead write, for example, "I need to move our 10 a.m. sync to 2 p.m. due to a client demo. Does that still work for you?" This cuts down on back-and-forth.

Time-zone awareness is crucial for global teams. A small oversight can turn an afternoon slot into a midnight call for a colleague. Modern calendar apps often include built-in conversion tools; use them when proposing new times. Aim for windows that fall within the core working hours of most participants, or offer a couple of alternatives to accommodate outliers.

Update any related materials as soon as the time changes. If the agenda, slides, or external guests depend on the original schedule, adjust them accordingly and resend the revised invitation. Confirm that the new slot works for all external stakeholders as well. A well-documented change eliminates last-minute surprises and keeps the meeting's objectives clear.

By responding promptly, communicating clearly, respecting time zones, and updating supporting documents, teams can turn a disruptive reschedule into a smooth adjustment. Handling meeting changes professionally preserves productivity and builds trust among colleagues, clients, and partners for everyone. In the end, a well-managed reschedule is just another chance to demonstrate reliability in a world where schedules constantly shift today.

raw:
dormitory rules

Living in a dormitory can be a rewarding experience, but it works best when everyone follows a clear set of guidelines. Most colleges provide a handbook that outlines the expectations for behavior, safety, and community living, and most students quickly discover that respecting those rules makes daily life smoother for everyone.

Quiet hours are perhaps the most widely enforced rule, typically beginning at 10 p.m. on weekdays and extending to midnight on weekends. During this time, residents are asked to keep music low, use headphones for electronic devices, and avoid any activities that could disturb neighbors. The purpose is to give everyone a chance to study, rest, or simply enjoy some peace after a long day of classes.

Cleanliness is another cornerstone of dorm life. Residents are expected to keep their personal spaces tidy, promptly dispose of trash, and use communal kitchens and bathrooms responsibly. Many dorms provide recycling bins and encourage students to separate waste, which not only keeps the environment healthy but also prevents unpleasant odors and pest problems that can affect the entire floor.

Safety protocols are non-negotiable. All doors must remain locked when you leave your room, and guests are usually required to sign in at the front desk. Many buildings also have fire drills each semester, and residents must know the location of the nearest exit and the assembly point. Violations such as tampering with smoke detectors or blocking hallways can lead to serious penalties, including loss of housing privileges.

Finally, respect for personal space and property is essential. Borrowing items without permission, taking food from another's mini-fridge, or entering a roommate's room uninvited are considered major breaches of trust. Open communication, clear boundaries, and a willingness to compromise help create a harmonious living environment where all students can thrive.
