raw:
public library services

Public libraries have evolved far beyond the quiet stacks of books that many people picture when they think of a neighborhood branch. Today they function as vibrant community hubs, offering a blend of digital resources, educational programs, and social services that cater to residents of all ages and backgrounds. Whether you are a student looking for research assistance, a job seeker needing resume help, or a senior citizen interested in a book club, the modern library is designed to meet those needs under one roof.

One of the most popular services is the free Wi-Fi and computer access that many patrons rely on for school projects, remote work, and online applications. Libraries often provide a range of devices, from standard desktop stations to tablets and laptops, and staff are on hand to guide users through basic troubleshooting or software tutorials. This digital inclusion effort helps close the gap for those who lack reliable internet at home.

In addition to technology, public libraries host a steady calendar of events that encourage lifelong learning and community engagement. Workshops on topics such as financial literacy, coding for kids, and genealogy research draw diverse crowds, while author talks and poetry readings add a cultural spark to the local scene. These programs are typically free or low-cost, making them accessible to families, retirees, and newcomers alike.

Another cornerstone of library service is the robust collection of physical and digital media. Beyond the traditional novels and nonfiction titles, many branches now offer e-books, audiobooks, and streaming movies that can be borrowed with a single library card. Interlibrary loan agreements extend the selection even further, allowing patrons to request items from neighboring districts and receive them within a few days.

Finally, many libraries have embraced a role as social service partners, providing resources such as tax-preparation assistance, job-search databases, and even basic health screenings. Staff often collaborate with local nonprofits to offer food drives, voting registration, and language-learning classes. By integrating these services, the public library remains a trusted, multifaceted institution that supports the well-being and growth of the community it serves.

Subject: Finally got the house setup working
Hi Sarah,
I finally finished installing the last of the smart home devices we bought recently. It took a few more hours than I expected because the Wi-Fi signal is quite weak in the basement, but everything is now paired and recognized by my phone app. The lighting system is particularly satisfying to use, as I can dim the living room bulbs from my bed.
The smart plugs are surprisingly useful for the coffee maker and the space heater. I set up an automated schedule so the heater turns on an hour before I wake up. It feels a bit like the future, and honestly, it saves me the hassle of fumbling for switches in the dark every morning.
We also set up the video doorbell. The night vision is impressive, especially since the streetlights are often out on our block. It was actually handy last night when I was trying to figure out why the dog was barking. It turns out it was just a raccoon walking around the back patio rather than anything dangerous.
There was some initial frustration with the thermostat learning our habits. It oscillated between too hot and too cold for the first few days until I manually adjusted the preferences. Once I tweaked the settings, it has been maintaining a comfortable temperature consistently without any input from me at all.
Overall, I am glad we made the investment. The energy bill seems slightly lower, mostly because we catch windows left open much more quickly thanks to the sensors. Let me know if you want to visit this weekend to see the setup in action and maybe we can discuss adding a few more gadgets.
Best regards,
David

Subject: Introduction to 3D Printing Basics
Dear Alex,
Three-dimensional printing, often called additive manufacturing, builds objects layer by layer from a digital model. Unlike traditional subtractive methods, it adds material only where needed, which reduces waste and allows for complex geometries that would be impossible to machine. The process starts with a computer-aided design (CAD) file that defines the shape, dimensions, and internal structure of the part.
There are several common 3D printing technologies, each suited to different applications. Fused filament fabrication (FFF) or fused deposition modeling (FDM) melts a thermoplastic filament and extrudes it through a nozzle, making it popular for hobbyists and prototyping. Stereolithography (SLA) uses a UV laser to cure liquid resin, delivering higher resolution and smoother surfaces for detailed models. Selective laser sintering (SLS) fuses powdered material with a laser, producing functional parts without the need for support structures.
The choice of material dramatically influences the final product's strength, flexibility, and appearance. Standard thermoplastics such as PLA and ABS are easy to print and inexpensive, while engineering grades like PETG, Nylon, or polycarbonate provide better durability and temperature resistance. Resin options for SLA include standard, tough, and flexible formulations, each with distinct handling requirements. For specialized uses, metal powders, ceramics, and composite filaments are also available, though they often demand more advanced printers.
Preparing a model for printing involves slicing the CAD file into thin horizontal layers and generating the toolpaths the printer will follow. Slicing software lets you set layer height, infill density, print speed, and support structures, all of which affect print quality and time. It is worthwhile to experiment with a few settings on a small test piece before committing to a larger, more valuable print.
Safety and maintenance are essential for reliable operation. Always work in a well-ventilated area, especially when printing with ABS or resin, as fumes and uncured chemicals can be harmful. Keep the build platform clean, calibrate the nozzle height regularly, and replace worn parts such as belts or nozzles to avoid print failures. Regularly inspect the printer's firmware for updates that can improve performance or add new features.
If you have any questions or would like recommendations for a starter printer, feel free to reach out. I'm happy to help you get your first prints underway.
Best regards, 
Jordan Lee 
Technical Outreach Coordinator

2013 SAFF Championship final

The 2013 SAFF Championship final was the final match of the 2013 SAFF Championship which took place in Nepal on 11 September 2013, and was officiated by Tayeb Hasan Shamsuzzaman of Bangladesh. It was the 10th installment of the tournament since its inception in 1993. This was the first time in the SAFF Championship that the finalists were the same in two consecutive finals, as in the 2011 SAFF Championship India had thrashed Afghanistan 4-0 in India. However, in this final it was Afghanistan who thrashed India 2-0, with goals coming from Mustafa Azadzoy and Sandjar Ahmadi in the 9th and 62nd minute respectively. This was Afghanistan's first SAFF Championship win.

India entered the 2013 SAFF Championship as the reigning champion after defeating Afghanistan in the 2011 SAFF Championship. Afghanistan's best record previous was runners-up in the 2011 SAFF Championship. To the final, India struggled through and scraped by the group stage through head-to-edge edging out Pakistan from an own-goal by Samar Ishaq in a 1-0 win to the Indians. Later in the semi-finals, against Maldives, it took India until the 86th minute when Arnab Mondal opened the scoring to leave it a 1-0 win to proceed to the final. Afghanistan, on the other hand, breezed by both Sri Lanka and Bhutan in the group stage with comfortable wins and a 0-0 stalemate with Maldives. To proceed to the final, Afghanistan won convincingly in a 1-0 win against the hosts Nepal with the lone goal coming from Sandjar Ahmadi in the 11th minute.

During the tournament, Afghanistan had the most diverse squad. While most other nations had almost all players playing for their domestic league, Afghanistan had five players playing outside of Asia with four in Europe and the rest in either India's I-League or its domestic league the Afghan Premier League. The average age of the Lions of Khorasan was 26 years of age with goalkeeper Hamidullah Yousafzai the oldest at 31 and youngest being Sidiq Walizada at 21. India had all its players playing in its domestic I-League with four players being free agents. The average age of the Blue Tigers was 26 years of age, as well, with goalkeeper Sandip Nandy the oldest at 38 and Sandesh Jhingan the youngest at 20.

Tayeb Shamsuzzaman of the Bangladesh was appointed the referee of the final and was assisted by Pakistani Moaid Al Sayeg and Issa Mahmoud Ahmad Al Amawi of Jordan. The fourth official was Adham Makhadmeh, also from Jordan. Shamsuzzaman was listed as a FIFA referee in 1999. Since then, he had experience as a referee in the World Cup Qualifiers, AFC Challenge Cup, AFC Cup, AFC Champions League, WAFF Championship, AFF Suzuki Cup and the 2010 and 2014 FIFA World Cup qualifiers Prior to the final, he refereed for five other games in the 2013 SAFF Championship. He was referee in Afghanistan-Bhutan and Bhutan-Maldives matches in Group A before moving to the Group B match India-Nepal. Then finishing the group stage by being the referee for Afghanistan-Maldives and the semi-final of Maldives-India. In the games that Shamsuzzaman was the referee, he showed no more than two yellow cards in every game with that being Bhutan-Maldives and Afghanistan-Maldives. He gave the red card in the group-stage match between Bhutan and Maldives and giving the Bhutan goalkeeper Leki Dukpa a red card for tripping Ali Ashfaq just outside the penalty box after rushing to a one-on-one.

raw:
Htantabin Township

Htantabin Township (Burmese: ထန်းတပင် မြို့နယ်, pronounced [tháɰ̃dəbɪ̀ɰ̃ mjo̰nɛ̀]) is a township in Hmawbi District located on the western border of central Yangon Region, Myanmar. Its administrative seat is Htantabin which is located in the southeastern part of the township on the western bank of the Hlaing River just south of its confluence with the Kokkowa River. The township is partially urbanized, although it is not part of the city of Yangon. The majority of the land is still in agriculture. In addition to agricultural work on the farms, the main sources of employment are as factory workers, temporary manual labor, as civil servants, and work in a variety of small to medium-size businesses. Htantabin township is home to the University of West Yangon. The township will be home to a 270 megawatt coal-fired power plant built by Htoo Trading, which will supply electricity to Yangon's industrial zones.

On 29 December 1994 at 11:00 p.m., SLORC troops from IB 73 threw a grenade into a crowd while they were holding a religious ceremony in In Gyin Koe Village, Htantabin Township, Pegu Division, causing the deaths of 10 villagers and wounding 24 others. [PDC] On February 5, 1998, Burmese Army troops tortured, shot and killed a pastor, Maung Ohn Kyi, and his son-in-law in Kawtupoe village of Htantabin township.

The township's eastern border is formed by the Hlaing River. Its southwestern boundary is formed by the Panhlaing River and part of its western border is formed by the Bawle River. Htantabin Township borders with:

Zalun Township, Ayeyarwady Region, to the northwest; Taikkyi Township to the northeast and east; Hmawbi Township and Shwepyitha Township to the east; Hlaingthaya Township to the southeast; Twante Township to the southwest; and Nyaungdon Township and Danubyu Township of Ayeyarwady Region, to the west.

The primary objective of opening theory is to establish a sound structural foundation before entering the complex middlegame. Players must prioritize rapid piece development, ensuring that knights are out before bishops and the king is safely castled as early as possible. This sequence minimizes the risk of early tactical traps while maximizing control over the center squares. Neglecting these fundamental steps often leads to a cramped position where pieces block each other, limiting their potential influence on the board.

Different opening systems tailor this approach based on the player's stylistic preferences and strategic goals. White players frequently choose between the aggressive King's Gambit, which sacrifices a pawn for rapid development, or the solid Ruy Lopez, which focuses on long-term pressure against Black's kingside. Black's responses typically aim to equalize material or create counterplay, requiring them to identify White's specific plans quickly to avoid falling into a passive defensive role.

Mastery of these lines does not require memorizing every possible variation up to move twenty, which would be an impractical burden for most amateur players. Instead, understanding the underlying strategic themes, such as pawn structures and piece coordination, is far more valuable. A player who understands why a move is good can transition smoothly into unfamiliar positions, whereas a player reliant on rote memorization may struggle when the opponent deviates from expected lines.

Practical preparation involves studying not just the moves but the resulting pawn structures. Recognizing typical weaknesses, such as isolated pawns or light-squared vulnerabilities, allows a player to formulate concrete plans in the middlegame. This knowledge transforms the opening from a static phase of move repetition into a dynamic tool for shaping the rest of the game according to one's strengths.

Finally, consistency in opening choice is crucial for building coherent databases of typical plans. Switching between highly disparate systems can confuse the player's intuition, leading to suboptimal decisions. A well-practiced repertoire, even if not the most theoretically perfect, ensures that the player enters the middlegame with clear goals and a solid positional understanding, reducing the cognitive load during critical moments of battle.

Subject: Update to our Remote Work Flexibility Program
Hi Team,
I hope you are all having a productive week so far. I am reaching out today to provide some clarity and updates regarding our internal remote work flexibility program. As you know, we have been operating under a hybrid model since early last year, allowing most staff to choose between the office and their home setups. While this arrangement has brought many benefits, feedback from recent town halls and one-on-one check-ins has highlighted a need for more structure and clarity. We want to ensure that our policies support both individual productivity and the collaborative spirit that defines our culture. Therefore, we are making several adjustments effective next month.
The primary change involves the "Core Hours" requirement. Going forward, all team members, whether working remotely or on-site, are expected to be available and responsive during the hours of 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM Eastern Time. This window is designed to facilitate real-time collaboration across our distributed teams. We recognize that async work is crucial, but having a guaranteed overlapping period ensures that critical decisions can be made swiftly without waiting for time zone diffs to align naturally. Please remember to block out other meetings or deep work sessions during this window unless absolutely necessary for client deliverables.
Additionally, we are refining the criteria for full remote designation. To maintain team cohesion, we are limiting fully remote roles to those positions that can be performed effectively outside the physical office environment. For roles that require frequent face-to-face interaction with cross-functional partners, a minimum of two days per week in the office is now mandatory. This is not meant to be punitive, but rather to ensure that spontaneous interactions and mentorship opportunities are not lost to pixels and video calls. Managers will work with you individually to determine which model best fits your specific role and career goals.
We have also updated our technology support protocols. Employees who are working from home will now have unrestricted access to our expense portal for ergonomic equipment and home office improvements, up to a certain annual limit. We believe that investing in your comfort is investing in your long-term health and focus. Furthermore, IT support response times for remote connectivity issues have been prioritized to a four-hour guarantee during business hours. We know that a slow internet connection can be a major productivity killer, and we are committed to solving those issues quickly.
I encourage you to review the full policy document linked in the shared drive for additional details on specific exceptions and quarterly review processes. If you have any questions or concerns about how these changes might impact your schedule or workflow, please do not hesitate to schedule time with your direct manager or reach out to my office directly. We want this policy to be a tool that empowers you, not a barrier to your success. Thank you for your continued dedication and for helping us build a work culture that is both flexible and connected.
Best regards,
Alexander Thorne
Director of Human Resources
Nexus Global Solutions

raw:
hospital visiting hours

Navigating the unfamiliar and often intimidating environment of a hospital can be overwhelming for families and visitors. One of the first pieces of information sought by those arriving at the facility is regarding visiting hours. While there is no single universal standard, most hospitals operate on predictable schedules that balance patient recovery needs with staff privacy and operational constraints. Understanding these routines can alleviate anxiety and ensure that visitors respect the space dedicated to medical care and rest.

Standard visiting hours typically span from mid-morning to early evening. For general ward patients, unrestricted visiting periods often begin around ten in the morning and continue until half past six in the evening. This window allows family members to see loved ones during waking hours without disrupting nighttime sleep patterns, which are critical for healing. It is important to note that these times can vary significantly by department; intensive care units may have stricter or more fragmented schedules due to the acute nature of the care required and the need for uninterrupted monitoring procedures.

Emergency situations can temporarily alter these standard protocols. In the event of a mass casualty incident, a severe public health emergency, or a hospital-wide diversion, administrative staff may shorten or suspend general visiting hours to prioritize safety and resource allocation. Conversely, in cases of critical illness or end-of-life situations, most hospitals adopt a flexible approach. They often grant exceptions to standard rules, allowing immediate family members to be present almost around the clock, sometimes with specific restrictions on the number of individuals allowed in the room at one time to maintain a calm environment.

Respecting hospital etiquette is just as important as knowing the times. Visitors should always check in at the main reception desk, even if they have visited the patient frequently before, to ensure the security log is accurate. Phone calls should be kept private or moved outside the room, as unauthorized recordings or conversations can sometimes interfere with sensitive medical discussions between staff and patients. Additionally, hospital gowns and protective equipment may be required for visitors in isolation rooms, such as those for infectious diseases or immunocompromised patients, so arriving prepared with appropriate clothing can save valuable time.

To avoid the frustration of finding the ward closed or the specific unit on a temporary break, it is advisable to call the hospital's main switching service before making a trip. Staff can provide the most current information, including any temporary closures for cleaning or surgical recovery. By planning visits around the posted schedules and communicating openly with nursing staff, visitors contribute to a smoother experience for everyone involved, ensuring that time spent with a loved one is focused on comfort and connection rather than logistical hurdles.

Subject: Updates on the recent aphid problem
Hi Sarah,
I wanted to give you a quick update on the garden situation before you arrive next week. We finally managed to tackle the aphid infestation that has been plaguing our rose bushes all summer. It was a stubborn case, but we have made significant progress in getting the plant health back on track.
We started by physically blasting the leaves with a strong stream of water from the hose. This dislodged a large portion of the pests and seemed to slow their movement considerably. It is surprising how effective this simple method is, especially when done early in the morning when the insects are less active and stationary.
Next, we applied a diluted soap spray mixture to the remaining clusters. The key was targeting the undersides of the leaves where they hide. We repeated this process three times over the course of a week. It requires patience, but it broke the life cycle before they could reproduce further or damage the new growth.
To prevent a future outbreak, we also brought in some native ladybugs last Tuesday. They have settled into the beds and are currently making their way through the remaining colonies. It feels good to see beneficial insects actively working for us rather than fighting against nature. The garden looks much healthier already.
Please let me know if you have any questions about the specific spray ratios we used. I wrote them down in the notebook by the shed door for reference. I look forward to seeing you soon and showing off the recovery.
Best,
Mark

Glottal consonant

Glottal consonants are consonants using the glottis as their primary articulation. Many phoneticians consider them, or at least the glottal fricative, to be transitional states of the glottis without a point of articulation as other consonants have, while some do not consider them to be consonants at all. However, glottal consonants behave as typical consonants in many languages. For example, in Literary Arabic, most words are formed from a root C-C-C consisting of three consonants, which are inserted into templates such as /CaːCiC/ or /maCCuːC/. The glottal consonants /h/ and /ʔ/ can occupy any of the three root consonant slots, just like "normal" consonants such as /k/ or /n/. The glottal consonants in the International Phonetic Alphabet are as follows:

In many languages, the "fricatives" are not true fricatives. This is a historical usage of the word. They instead represent transitional states of the glottis (phonation) without a specific place of articulation, and may behave as approximants. [h] is a voiceless transition. [ɦ] is a breathy-voiced transition, and could be transcribed as [h̤]. The glottal stop occurs in many languages. Often all vocalic onsets are preceded by a glottal stop, for example in German (in careful pronunciation; often omitted in practice). The Hawaiian language writes the glottal stop as the 'okina ⟨'⟩, which resembles a single open quotation mark. Some alphabets use diacritics for the glottal stop, such as hamza ⟨ء⟩ in the Arabic alphabet; in many languages of Mesoamerica, the Latin letter ⟨h⟩ is used for glottal stop, in Maltese, the letter ⟨q⟩ is used, and in many indigenous languages of the Caucasus, the letter commonly referred to as heng ⟨Ꜧ ꜧ⟩ is used. Because the glottis is necessarily closed for the glottal stop, it cannot be voiced. So-called voiced glottal stops are not full stops, but rather creaky-voiced glottal approximants (here transcribed with the extIPA symbol for pre-/post-creak ⟨˷⟩). They occur as the intervocalic allophone of glottal stop in many languages. Gimi contrasts /ʔ/ and /˷/, corresponding to /k/ and /ɡ/ in related languages.

Grønnum, Nina (2005), Fonetik og fonologi, Almen og Dansk (3rd ed.), Copenhagen: Akademisk Forlag, ISBN 87-500-3865-6 Ladefoged, Peter; Maddieson, Ian (1996). The Sounds of the World's Languages. Oxford: Blackwell. ISBN 0-631-19814-8.

The Community Arts Center writes to inform all registered members of the upcoming "Verse and Voice" poetry workshop scheduled for the first and third Saturdays of next month. This two-month interim session is designed for intermediate poets who wish to refine their craft through structured feedback and collaborative critique. Participation is capped at twelve individuals per session to ensure meaningful engagement, and registration opens on the first of the month via our central online portal. Please note that late registrations will only be accepted if a waitlist cancellation occurs, and all materials, including printed handouts and digital resource links, will be provided at the start of each meeting.

Attendance requires a nominal fee of twenty-five dollars per installment, which covers venue usage and light refreshments. This cost is waived for students and verified low-income residents upon presentation of valid identification. The workshop will take place in the main studio on the second floor, accessible via the central escalator or the rear freight elevator. Participants are asked to arrive fifteen minutes early to secure seat assignments, as proximity to the facilitator's podium is recommended for those with hearing impairments. Late arrivals will not interrupt the ongoing discussion, ensuring a consistent flow of dialogue and respect for the shared creative space.

The curriculum focuses on specific poetic forms, including the sonnet, villanelle, and free verse structure, with each fortnight dedicated to a single form. Week one involves theoretical analysis and deconstruction of canonical texts, while week two shifts to guided writing exercises and peer review circles. Facilitators, comprising local published poets and university adjunct faculty, will provide individualized comments on submitted drafts on a rotating basis. Participants are encouraged to bring at least three recent works to each session to maximize the utility of the critique period.

To maintain a supportive and constructive environment, the center enforces a strict code of conduct regarding feedback. Critiques must focus on technical execution, imagery, rhythm, and structural integrity rather than personal taste or emotional reaction. Disrespectful or dismissive comments toward peers' work will result in immediate removal from the session without refund. We believe that a safe, respectful atmosphere is essential for creative risk-taking and genuine artistic growth.

For those with specific material needs, such as large-print readers or Braille displays, please contact the accessibility coordinator at least two weeks prior to the start date to arrange accommodations. A resource list containing recommended anthologies and online journals will be emailed to all registered participants one week before the initial meeting. We look forward to welcoming you to this enriching community of writers and hope to see your active participation in the sessions ahead.

Octaoxygen

Octaoxygen, also known as ε-oxygen or red oxygen, is an allotrope of oxygen consisting of eight oxygen atoms. This allotrope forms at high pressure and remains stable across a wide pressure range at room temperature (between 10 and 96 GPa). If it is further compressed past 96 GPa, then it transitions into a metallic, superconducting state. The material is dark red and unlike other forms allotropes of oxygen is has no magnetic character, due to its unpaired electrons being forced to overlap.

As the pressure of oxygen at room temperature is increased above 10 gigapascals (1,500,000 psi), it undergoes a dramatic phase transition to the ε-phase allotrope. Its volume decreases significantly, and it changes color from sky-blue to deep red. This ε-phase was discovered in 1979, but the structure was unclear. A crystal lattice of tetraoxygen O4 units was suggested in 1999, based on infrared spectroscopy. However, in 2006, two independent groups showed by X-ray crystallography that the structure was a rhomboid O8 ((O2)4) cluster consisting of four O2 molecules.

In this phase, it exhibits a dark-red color, very strong infrared absorption, and a magnetic collapse. It has been shown to have a monoclinic C2/m symmetry, and its infrared absorption behaviour was attributed to the association of oxygen molecules into larger units. At 11 GPa, the intra-cluster bond length of the O8 cluster is 2.34 Å, and the inter-cluster distance is 2.66 Å, both longer than the 1.2 Å bond-length in the oxygen molecule (O2). It is stable over a very large pressure domain, from 10 GPa to 96 GPa. Above 96 GPa, ζ-oxygen forms which is metallic and superconductive; ε-oxygen is non-conductive. The formation mechanism of the O8 cluster found in the work is not clear yet, and the researchers think that the charge transfer between oxygen molecules or the magnetic moment of oxygen molecules has a significant role in the formation.

Liquid oxygen is already used as an oxidant in rockets, and it has been speculated that octaoxygen could make an even better oxidant, because of its higher energy density.

Praga V3S

The Praga V3S (Vojenský třítunový speciál/ Military 3ton Special) is an all-terrain multi-purpose truck, produced between 1953 and 1990 in Czechoslovakia. It was designed for the armed forces and was also exported to 72 countries. Praga produced the truck until 1964, then the Avia company until around 1986, after which the Bratislava company BAZ rolled out these vehicles until 1990. Around 130,000 units were manufactured. The truck was among the best off-road cargo vehicles of its time and the Czechoslovak Army used it for more than half a century. It was the longest produced Czechoslovak truck and it still serves in Czech Army for more than 70 years, despite being slowly replaced by Tatra 810 and Tatra 815.

For the development till prototype stage of the truck, designers were given only four months. They were inspired mainly by the American Studebaker US6 and Russian ZiL. Due to the design incorporating portal axles (axles positioned high above the wheels axis), the V3S has a high ground clearance, this structure provides great terrain passability, but on the other hand limits the maximum speed to 60 km/h (37 mph). The V3S was a durable, popular and extremely adaptable truck built in various versions and widely exported, therefore it is not difficult to see V3S based vehicles still hard at work nowadays.

The engine is an air-cooled diesel six-cylinder "Tatra 912-1" (modified engine from Tatra 111), with a capacity of 7412 cm3, direct fuel injection and overhead valves. It is relatively noisy, but works reliably even in extreme conditions. Climbing ability is up to 75% (without tow). Ten wheels (rear are four dual, front are two) help the truck not to bog down in soft soil, therefore it does not experience any problems in forests or in the field. Consumption is 30 liters of diesel per 100 km, the fuel tank has a capacity of 120 liters. The truck is able to get over 40 cm high perpendicular obstacles, and wading depth is 80 cm. There are two batteries (12 V, 125 Ah), they are connected in parallel during driving, but in serial for engine startups. The payload of the truck is 5 tons on paved surfaces and 3 tons on rough terrain.

local election information

Home | About | Contact

Knowing where and how to vote is the most critical step for any resident participating in local elections. Unlike national contests that dominate the news cycle, local races often go unnoticed until the deadlines have passed. However, these elections determine who sets property tax rates, oversees local infrastructure repairs, and appoints judges who may serve on the bench for decades. Before you head to the polls, it is essential to verify your registration status. In most jurisdictions, voter registration is not portable; if you have recently moved from your previous address, your old registration remains inactive for your new location. You can typically update your details online through your state or county election office website, but doing so early is crucial because many election boards stop processing changes a few days before Election Day.

Poll locations and hours are another frequent source of confusion for voters. It is a common misconception that you must vote at the same place where you currently reside. In many areas, any registered voter can cast their ballot at any polling place within their district or county. Checking the specific location assigned to your address is the safest approach, but confirming whether provisional ballots are available if you go to a different site can save you a second trip. Additionally, poll hours vary significantly by jurisdiction. While some places operate from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., others may open at 7 a.m. or close at 9 p.m. Arriving with a clear understanding of these times helps you avoid long lines that form in the final hours of voting.

The candidate information for local races is often less accessible than that for national candidates. You will not find extensive debate coverage or major ad campaigns for school board members or city council representatives. Instead, detailed information is hidden in the voter guides mailed by election boards or available on local government websites. These guides usually include biographical statements written by the candidates themselves, which can range from brief summaries to detailed policy platforms. To make an informed decision, residents should compare these statements against the specific needs of their neighborhood. Attending local town halls or council meetings, even just once or twice a year, reveals how candidates behave under pressure and responds to constituent concerns, offering a glimpse into their governance style that a printed brochure cannot provide.

Voucher and absentee voting options have expanded in recent years, providing flexibility for those who cannot make it to a physical polling station. Mail-in ballots and early voting periods are now standard in many states, allowing citizens to vote over a week or more before Election Day. This method requires careful attention to the application process and return deadlines. A mailed ballot returned after the legal cutoff is not counted, regardless of when it was postmarked. If you choose to vote early in person, check the schedule at your local election office, as these days can peak with long waits. Ensuring your identity is ready for verification is vital, as poll workers must match your photo ID to the details on the official voter list.

Finally, understanding the specific ballot measures is crucial, as local elections often include referendums on bond measures, tax increases, or redistricting plans. These measures do not pit one candidate against another but ask voters to approve or reject specific pieces of legislation. Ignoring these items on the ballot can have long-term financial impacts on your household. Reading the full text of any proposed bond measure, rather than just the headline summary, clarifies exactly what funds will be used and for what duration. By taking the time to research these details and verifying your logistical information, you ensure that your voice is heard in the decisions that shape your daily life.

Ensuring your identity is ready for verification is vital, as poll workers must match your photo ID to the details on the official voter list.

These measures do not pit one candidate against another but ask voters to approve or reject specific pieces of legislation. Ignoring these items on the ballot can have long-term financial impacts on your household. Reading the full text of any proposed bond measure, rather than just the headline summary, clarifies exactly what funds will be used and for what duration. Berkoukes (dish)

Berkoukes (Tamazight : ⵜⴰⴱⵔⴽⵓⴽⵙⵜ, Taberkukest), also named berkoukech, aïch or avazine is a traditional North African dish, particularly popular in Algeria, Tunisia, and parts of Morocco. It consists of large hand-rolled semolina pasta, often compared to pearl couscous or fregola, and is typically prepared with vegetables, legumes, and aromatic spices.

The name berkoukes is derived from the Arabic root "brk," which is associated with kneading or rolling, referring to the process of shaping the pasta. The term berkukec (from a prefix augmentative + kukec, meaning "couscous") is used in the dialect of Ouargla and Mozabite, where it translates to "large-grain couscous". The dish is also known by regional variations of its name, such as aïch in some Berber-speaking communities.

The tradition of making pasta in North Africa dates back centuries. Medieval Arab-Andalusian and Maghrebi texts describe various types of handmade pasta, including berkoukes. Ibn Razin Tujibi, a 13th-century Andalusian gastronome, documented different pasta preparations in his culinary treatise Fudalat al-Khiwan. Historical sources suggest that in the 12th century, North Africa had as many pasta varieties as couscous preparations, with berkoukes among them. These traditional pastas were valued for being affordable, nutritious, and adaptable to different regional flavors.

Berkoukes is traditionally made by rolling coarse semolina with water and a bit of flour to form large, round granules. These granules are then dried or used fresh in various stews and soups. A typical berkoukes dish includes:

Pasta: handmade semolina-based granules Vegetables: tomatoes, carrots, zucchini, potatoes, and chickpeas Protein: often lamb or chicken, or left vegetarian with legumes Spices and aromatics: cumin, paprika, cinnamon, garlic, and bay leaves The ingredients are slow-cooked in a tomato-based broth until tender, with the pasta added towards the end of cooking to absorb the flavors.

Berkoukes is commonly prepared during family gatherings, special occasions, and religious festivities such as Ramadan. It is also considered a nourishing dish for winter, often recommended for its warming properties.

Moghrabieh: Lebanese dish featuring large semolina pearls cooked with chickpeas and meat. Fregula: Sardinian pasta that closely resembles berkoukes in shape and texture. Couscous: a smaller-grained semolina dish widely consumed across North Africa.

raw:
solar panel installation

The decision to install solar panels often begins with a simple desire to reduce monthly electricity bills, but the process is far more complex than simply placing modules on a roof. Homeowners increasingly view solar energy not just as an alternative power source, but as a long-term financial investment that can significantly offset grid dependence. Understanding the true mechanics of installation is crucial for anyone considering this transition, as the initial phase sets the groundwork for decades of clean energy production. It requires a blend of technical precision and careful planning to ensure that the system performs efficiently under various weather conditions and load demands.

Before any hardware is mounted, a professional assessment of the property is mandatory to determine feasibility. Installers evaluate the orientation, pitch, and shading of the roof to maximize sun exposure throughout the day. Trees, neighboring buildings, or chimneys can cast shadows that drastically reduce energy output, making site analysis a critical first step. This stage also involves checking the structural integrity of the roof to ensure it can support the added weight of the panels and mounting hardware. If the roof is nearing the end of its lifecycle, it is often more cost-effective to replace it before installation to avoid the high expense of removing and reinstalling the system in just a few years.

The actual installation day typically takes one to three days, depending on the size of the array and the complexity of the electrical work involved. Technicians begin by securing the racking system to the roof's rafters using specialized flashing to prevent leaks. Once the frame is secure, the panels are attached and wired together in series and parallel configurations to achieve the desired voltage and current output. Electricians then run duct-banked wiring from the roof to the main service panel, installing a disconnect switch and, if applicable, a net metering device. This allows the home to send excess power back to the utility grid, generating credits that can be used during periods of low solar production.

Inverter technology plays a pivotal role in the system's performance, converting the direct current generated by the panels into alternating current used by household appliances. Microinverters are mounted directly behind each panel, allowing for individual optimization that mitigates the impact of localized shading. String inverters, on the other hand, are larger units that handle the output of multiple panels and are typically installed in a garage or basement. Choose the right inverter technology based on your specific roof layout and shading profile to ensure consistent energy conversion efficiency throughout the year.

Permits and inspections are the final hurdles before the system goes live, a bureaucratic process that can take several weeks. Local building departments require submissions of engineering drawings and electrical plans to verify code compliance. Once approved, a third-party inspector checks the installation for safety and structural soundness before issuing the final sign-off. After passing inspection, the utility company updates the metering system to account for solar generation. With these steps complete, the system is energized, marking the beginning of a sustainable energy journey that benefits both the homeowner and the wider community.

raw:
board game review

The new cooperative game "Echoes of the Deep" arrives with a promise of immersive storytelling and strategic depth, and after several playthroughs it delivers a surprisingly balanced experience that will appeal to both veteran gamers and newcomers alike. From the moment the heavy, sea-worn box is opened, the quality of the components hints at the care poured into the design: thick, textured cards, a set of finely painted wooden ship tokens, and a beautifully illustrated board that doubles as a map of uncharted waters. The tactile feel of the pieces immediately draws players into the world of a 19th-century expedition searching for a lost civilization.

The core mechanic revolves around a push-pull system between resource management and hidden information. Players must allocate crew, supplies, and morale while dealing with the ever-present threat of a storm that reshuffles the board each round. What sets the game apart is its "echo" mechanic: each decision leaves a lingering effect that can be revisited later, forcing groups to think several turns ahead. The rulebook explains this clearly, with concise examples that prevent the usual learning curve fatigue. A few minutes of setup later, the game flows smoothly, and the hidden objectives keep everyone guessing until the final reveal.

One of the most striking aspects of "Echoes of the Deep" is its narrative integration. Unlike many strategy-heavy titles that treat story as an afterthought, this game weaves a compelling plot through event cards and a journal that records each crew member's discoveries. The writing is evocative, describing the creaking hull, the smell of salt, and the faint glow of lanterns in the dark. As the expedition progresses, the journal entries evolve, reflecting both successes and setbacks, which adds an emotional layer to the strategic choices. This dual focus on mechanics and storytelling makes each session feel like a mini adventure rather than just a race for points.

Replayability is strong, thanks to the modular board tiles that can be rearranged for a fresh layout each time, and the random event deck that introduces new challenges on every playthrough. The game scales well from two to five players; solo mode offers a solitaire variant that uses an automated "storm deck" to simulate opponent pressure. The balance remains tight, though the higher difficulty levels can feel punishing if the group is not accustomed to tight resource constraints. For those who enjoy a tougher challenge, the "deep sea" expansion adds more intricate puzzles and a larger map, but the base game already stands solidly on its own.

Overall, "Echoes of the Deep" succeeds in blending cooperative strategy with a rich narrative, delivering a polished experience that feels both fresh and familiar. Its production values, thoughtful mechanics, and engaging storytelling make it a standout addition to any gaming shelf. Whether you are looking for a weekend campaign that encourages teamwork or a shorter session that still offers depth, this title is worth the investment. In a market crowded with thematic games, it manages to carve out its own niche, inviting players to explore the unknown while navigating the perils of the sea together.

raw:
quarterly sales summary

The fiscal Q2 2026 report for Meridian Technologies was released this week, offering a clear snapshot of how the company navigated a volatile market. Revenue climbed 8.2 percent over the previous quarter, while operating expenses held steady, delivering a modest profit margin improvement in its core operations.

Top-line growth was driven primarily by the cloud services segment, which posted a 15 percent increase in subscription renewals. Meanwhile, the hardware division saw a 3 percent dip, reflecting supply-chain constraints that limited inventory turnover in several key markets across North America and Europe this quarter.

Regionally, the Asia-Pacific territory outperformed expectations, delivering a 12 percent revenue surge thanks to strong demand for AI-enhanced analytics tools. In contrast, the Latin American market remained flat, hampered by currency fluctuations and slower adoption of newer platform features through the first half of 2026.

Product performance revealed that the flagship Insight Suite contributed 40 percent of total sales, reinforcing its position as the company's primary revenue driver. Newer offerings, such as the Edge Compute module, captured modest market share but are projected to scale as enterprise customers expand edge deployments.

Looking ahead, the executive team expects Q3 to maintain growth momentum, targeting a 6 to 8 percent increase in overall revenue. Strategic initiatives include expanding the partner ecosystem in emerging markets and accelerating the rollout of next-generation security features to meet rising compliance demands.

raw:
tenant association meeting

The monthly tenant association meeting at Rivergate Apartments took place on Tuesday evening in the community room, drawing a surprisingly diverse crowd of residents eager to voice concerns and share ideas. The event began with a brief welcome from the building manager, who highlighted the importance of open communication and reminded everyone that the meeting was recorded for those who could not attend in person. A modest coffee and water station helped keep the atmosphere relaxed while people settled into the folding chairs arranged in a circle.

The first item on the agenda was the recent increase in utility costs, a topic that sparked an animated discussion. Several tenants recounted their own experiences with higher electric bills and asked whether the property could explore bulk-purchase options or alternative energy providers. The manager responded that a feasibility study was already underway and promised to present a detailed report at the next gathering. Participants appreciated the transparency and the chance to see concrete numbers rather than vague assurances.

Next, the conversation turned to maintenance requests that have been piling up over the past month. A group of residents formed a small committee to track response times and compile a list of recurring issues, such as hallway lighting and leaky faucets. By presenting a clear, organized summary, they hoped to persuade the landlord to allocate additional resources to the maintenance team. The manager thanked them for the initiative and agreed to prioritize the most urgent repairs within two weeks.

The meeting also featured a brief update on upcoming community events, including a summer picnic and a fire-safety drill. Volunteers were encouraged to sign up for the planning committee, and several attendees expressed interest in helping with decorations and outreach. The sense of camaraderie was evident as neighbors exchanged contact information and discussed forming a neighborhood watch group.

At the close of the session, the manager reminded everyone of the next meeting date and invited feedback on how to improve future gatherings. A short questionnaire was emailed to all participants, asking for suggestions on agenda items, meeting length, and preferred communication channels. The open-door policy reinforced the idea that tenant association meetings are a collaborative effort, where each voice can shape the living experience.

Overall, the tenant association meeting proved to be a productive forum for problem-solving, relationship-building, and community planning. By maintaining a regular schedule, providing clear minutes, and encouraging active participation, the Rivergate community continues to strengthen its sense of ownership and mutual respect among residents.

raw:
Twelve Good Men

Twelve Good Men (also known as 12 Good Men) is a lost 1936 British crime film directed by Ralph Ince and starring Henry Kendall, Nancy O'Neil and Joyce Kennedy. It was written by Sidney Gilliat| and Frank Launder based on the 1928 detective novel The Murders in Praed Street by John Rhode, with the principal series character of the book Doctor Priestley eliminated for the film. It was made at Teddington Studios by Warner Brothers as a quota quickie.

The British Film Institute has classed Twelve Good Men as a lost film. Its National Archive holds a collection of stills but no film or video materials.

An ex-convict is trying to take revenge on the members of the jury who convicted him. Despite being put under police protection at the home of juror and famous actor Charles Drew, two jurors are murdered. Aspiring actress Ann Parkes investigates and catches the killer.

Henry Kendall as Charles Drew Nancy O'Neil as Ann Parkes Joyce Kennedy as Lady Thora Percy Parsons as Hopwood Morland Graham as Victor Day Bernard Miles as Inspector Pine Philip Ray as Higgs Frederick Burtwell as Fortheringay Roddy Hughes as Wiggings Sam Springson as Mr Levy George Hughes as Jim Bostock Madge White as Mrs Goodheart Grace Lane as Mrs Parkes Ralph Roberts as Mr Parkes

Kine Weekly wrote: "Murder mystery cleverly sustained, compounded with plenty of human interest and a love affair. Acting and presentation, combined with the original plot and lively dialogue, entitle the picture to a good reception from the average patron. ... Henry Kendall is extremely well cast as the conceited but likeable actor. His performance is live and balanced, making a good foil for the calm of Nancy O'Neill as Ann ... Ralph Ince opens well, working up the mystery while providing clear characterisations. Interest, far from flagging when the truth about the twelve jurymen is arrived at, is strongly maintained in spite of the introduction of one killing after another." The Daily Film Renter wrote: "Pleasingly presented, with smooth study from Henry Kendall in lead, and measure of romance, this is acceptable quota support for the masses. ... Somewhat slow in the initial stages, the piece nevertheless quickens up to an effective climax that packs a genuine surprise. There are some good dramatic moments, including a realistic car blaze, and the murder of a speedway ace on the Wembley Dirt Track, while the assortment of varied types thrown together by a common danger affords some interesting by-play." Picturegoer wrote: "Henry Kendall's performance as a conceited but likeable actor is the high-light of this brightly directed and somewhat original story. ... Nancy O'Neil is quite good as the heroine and the various jurymen are well characterised. Bernard Miles is convincing as a detective from Scotland Yard and Percy Parson scores as an ex-convict servant. While a little far-fetched in parts, the interest is quite well maintained. Dialogue is generally bright." Picture Show wrote: "Far-fetched melodrama ... Good characterisations from the players who appear as the jury, and light-hearted work from Henry Kendall as an actor who is one of them, neat direction and ingenious development help the story."

Patrick Borchers

Patrick J. Borchers (born 1961) is a lawyer, university administrator and politician from the state of Nebraska in the Midwestern United States. He is a member of the faculty of the Creighton University School of Law in the city of Omaha. In 2016, he ran unsuccessfully for a seat in the Nebraska legislature. Borchers is a member of the Democratic Party.

Borchers was born in Madison, Wisconsin. He graduated from Boulder High School in Boulder Colorado in 1979. He received a B.S. in physics with Honors from the University of Notre Dame in 1983. He is a 1986 graduate of the University of California, Davis School of Law where he was elected to the Order of the Coif. He was a law clerk to Anthony Kennedy from 1986 to 1987 when Kennedy was a judge on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. Kennedy was later elevated to the U.S. Supreme Court. Borchers practiced law in Sacramento, California. In Board of Supervisors v. Local Agency Formation Com., 3 Cal. 4th 903 (1992), he successfully represented before the California Supreme Court a citizens group attempting to form the new city of Citrus Heights, California, arguing that it did not violate the Equal Protection Clause to restrict voting to those within the proposed city's boundaries.

After starting his academic career at Albany Law School, he was appointed in 1999 Dean of Creighton University School of Law in Omaha, Nebraska, serving until 2007. While in that position, he founded the Werner Institute for Negotiation and Dispute Resolution. In 2007, Borchers was appointed Vice President for Academic Affairs at Creighton, the Chief Academic Officer of the university. He stepped down in 2013 and was appointed director of the Werner Institute for Negotiation and Dispute Resolution. In August 2015, Borchers stepped down as director and returned to full-time law faculty duties. Borchers's academic specialties include private international law (conflict of laws), international arbitration and federal jurisdiction and procedure. He is the author, co-author or editor of seven books and about 60 law review articles. Borchers's affidavits have been cited in conflict-of-laws cases in both the U.S. and Ontario. His works have been cited by the United States Supreme Court and U.S. Courts of Appeal. State appellate courts have also cited his writings, including New York, Louisiana, Missouri) New Jersey, Tennessee, Illinois, and Michigan. In 2007, Borchers and several other faculty members at Creighton University authored a report, funded by the United States Agency for International Development on a possible resolution of the outstanding expropriation claims against Cuba in the event of a shift in U.S.-Cuba relations. The report recommended the creation of a Cuba-U.S. Tribunal to resolve the claims and suggested that since Cuba lacked sufficient hard currency to resolve the claims, claimants accept other forms of compensation, e.g. tax-free zones or development rights.

In 2016, Borchers ran for the Nebraska legislature from the 39th District, a heavily Republican district consisting of the western portion of Douglas County. Under Nebraska's term-limits law, the incumbent, Republican Beau McCoy, was ineligible to run for a third consecutive term. In the non-partisan primary, Borchers (then a Republican) faced fellow Republican Lou Ann Linehan, who had been an aide for former U.S. senator Chuck Hagel, and Democrat Bill Armbrust, a farmer who described himself as a "compassionate conservative" with libertarian elements. When the primary was held, Borchers came in third, with 1862 of the 6169 votes cast, or 30.2%. Armbrust received 1971 votes, or 32.0%; Linehan won 2336 votes, or 37.9%. As the top two vote-getters, Armbrust and Linehan moved on to the general election, while Borchers was eliminated. Linehan went on to win the seat, winning 55% of the vote in the general election to Armbrust's 45%. On March 22, 2020, Borchers changed registration to the Democratic Party.

In 2007, Borchers and several other faculty members at Creighton University authored a report, funded by the United States Agency for International Development on a possible resolution of the outstanding expropriation claims against Cuba in the event of a shift in U.S.-Cuba relations. The report recommended the creation of a Cuba-U.S. Tribunal to resolve the claims and suggested that since Cuba lacked sufficient hard currency to resolve the claims, claimants accept other forms of compensation, e.g. tax-free zones or development rights.
In 2016, Borchers ran for the Nebraska legislature from the 39th District, a heavily Republican district consisting of the western portion of Douglas County. Under Nebraska's term-limits law, the incumbent, Republican Beau McCoy, was ineligible to run for a third consecutive term. In the non-partisan primary, Borchers (then a Republican) faced fellow Republican Lou Ann Linehan, who had been an aide for former U.S. senator Chuck Hagel, and Democrat Bill Armbrust, a farmer who described himself as a "compassionate conservative" with libertarian elements. When the primary was held, Borchers came in third, with 1862 of the 6169 votes cast, or 30.2%. Armbrust received 1971 votes, or 32.0%; Linehan won 2336 votes, or 37.9%. "Urain Ge" (Urdu: اڑیں گے, lit. 'We Will Fly') is a 2015 Pakistani song, written and produced by Ali Zafar. It was released in honour of the victims of the 2014 Peshawar school massacre, and to support the campaign titled 141 Schools for Peace with The Citizens Foundation.

In 2014, Pakistan faced military and political instability, when Pakistan Armed Forces launched Operation Zarb-e-Azb in North Waziristan against various groups, including Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), in the wake of terrorism. Later, on 16 December 2014, six gunmen attacked the Army Public School, Peshawar, killing 132 children and 9 school staff members, making it one of the world's deadliest school massacres. Pakistan Army's Special Service Group (SSG) launched a quick rescue operation and killed the terrorists. They rescued an estimated 960 people, though 139 were injured. Omar Khalid Khorasani, TTP's spokesperson, took responsibility for the attack and claimed it was a revenge against the Operation Zarb-e-Azb. The school reopened on 12 January 2015 with enhanced security, and staff and students reportedly in "high spirits".

Ali Zafar cancelled his concert tours and events soon after the massacre, including the one in Durban, South Africa, on New Year's Eve. Weeks later, he went to his studio to write and record the song "Urain Ge". It was released on 7 February 2015 via ARY Digital Network. Musician Asad Ahmed shared that he was hired to play the bass only, but he changed the orchestration into electric guitars.

To record the music video, he gathered several celebrities from the country at a studio in Korangi, Karachi. They included Aamina Sheikh, Ahsan Khan, Aijaz Aslam, Ali Azmat, Ali Kazmi, Anwar Maqsood, Asad Ahmed, Behroze Sabzwari, Bilal Lashari, Bushra Ansari, Fahad Mustafa, Farhad Humayun, Fawad Khan, Fariha Pervez, Goher Mumtaz, Hadiqa Kiani, Hamza Ali Abbasi, Haroon Rashid, Haroon Shahid, Humaima Malick, Humayun Saeed, Imran Abbas, Jawed Sheikh, Junaid Khan, Junaid Younus, Mahira Khan, Meesha Shafi, Mehreen Raheal, Mehwish Hayat, Mikaal Zulfiqar, Mohammed Ali Shehki, Mohib Mirza, Saba Qamar, Sanam Saeed, Sahira Kazmi, Sajid Hasan, Sajjad Ali, and Shoaib Malik. They also commented about the need to honour the victims and aspire for the better future of the country, where no mother is separated from her child and love prevails over the pain. Shehzad Roy also recorded and sent his video separately. Shahzeb Jillani wrote in BBC News that the song starts in a "grave" mood, but the rising tempo transforms the music into "something uplifting". Anum Rehman Chagani of Dawn believed that the song may "become the anthem for hope for our nation". Hasan Ansari of The Express Tribune called it one of the "patriotic songs" that struck "the right chord with the audiences". Besides the showbiz unity in the music video, Zafar also appreciated the political unity after a long dispute in the aftermath of the Peshawar attack. He also urged nationwide unity, to put a positive image of the country moving towards progress and peace in the world.

The Citizens Foundation (TCF), an educational nonprofit organization that builds schools for underprivileged children in Pakistan, partnered with the 141 Schools for Peace campaign, and decided the locations across Pakistan to build the schools. The budgetary cost was estimated to be Rs. 2.07 crore. Ali Zafar, whose parents are educationalists, also wanted to contribute to education and committed to supporting the cause by donating all proceeds from the song "Urain Ge". At Rs. 10 per legal sale of the song, the Ali Zafar Foundation donated about Rs. 2 lakh to the cause. Their collective aim was to build 141 schools and dedicate each school to a victim of the Peshawar attack, which was achieved by the tenth anniversary in 2024.

Subject: Urgent Maintenance Schedule for the Riverside Suspension Bridge
Dear Valued Commuter and Resident,
The Department of Transportation is writing to inform you of significant upcoming maintenance work on the Riverside Suspension Bridge. Due to the long-term wear and tear experienced by the aging structural components, our engineering team has scheduled a series of critical inspections and repairs that will require intermittent lane closures. This proactive measure is essential to ensure the continued safety, durability, and structural integrity of this vital transportation link for all drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians who rely on the bridge in their daily routines.
Starting on the morning of October 15th, crews will begin working on the eastbound primary lanes during off-peak hours to minimize disruption to your travel. From 6:00 AM to 10:00 AM, these lanes will be completely closed for the installation of new bearing pads and the replacement of degraded suspension cables. During this specific window, all eastbound traffic will be redirected onto the westbound lanes via temporary signage, which will inevitably lead to slower average speeds and potential congestion. We urge all motorists to allow extra time for their commute if their schedule aligns with these early morning hours, as the added travel time could be substantial during this period.
The following days will see a shift in focus to the pedestrian walkways and the western support pillars. On October 16th and 17th, from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, the pedestrian deck will be inaccessible for non-essential crossing. Commuters traveling on foot should plan to use the nearby subway station or the secondary footbridge located two blocks north to reach the opposite side of the river safely. Cyclists are also requested to dismount and walk their bicycles across the limited access route or utilize the designated detour paths to protect both their safety and the workers on site.
We understand that these scheduled closures cause inconvenience and frustration, particularly for those who depend on efficient transit routes to reach their workplaces or schools. The construction team has implemented a real-time traffic monitoring system to adjust detour signage dynamically based on current volume. Please monitor the local DOT mobile application or the 511 traffic line for the most up-to-date status reports, as weather conditions or unexpected structural findings could result in minor adjustments to this timeline. Your patience and cooperation are deeply appreciated as we work to resolve these issues swiftly and thoroughly.
Should you have questions regarding accessible routing options for individuals with disabilities, or if you require assistance due to the lane closures, please contact our dedicated customer service team. They are available round the clock to provide personalized guidance and answer any specific concerns you may have about navigating the affected area. We remain committed to delivering a safe and reliable infrastructure network and thank you for your understanding and support during this necessary period of improvement and repair.
Sincerely,
Marcus Henderson
Public Information Officer
Department of Transportation
City Engineering Division

Subject: Improving Our City's Bike Lanes
Dear Councilmember Rivera,
I am writing to share my observations about the current bike lane network in downtown. Over the past six months I have ridden the designated routes daily and have noticed several recurring safety concerns that deserve attention. Intersections lacking clear markings and the occasional obstruction by parked cars create hazardous conditions for cyclists.
A recent survey of local residents showed that 68% of respondents would ride more often if the lanes were better maintained and separated from traffic. In particular, the stretch along Main Street between 3rd and 5th avenues is a high-traffic corridor where cyclists often have to merge into vehicle lanes to avoid debris and potholes.
I propose three practical steps the city could take within the next fiscal year. First, repaint all bike lane markings and add reflective paint to improve visibility at night. Second, install protected curb-side bike boxes at every major intersection to give cyclists a dedicated waiting area. Third, enforce a stricter no-parking rule during peak commuting hours to keep the lanes clear.
These measures would not only improve safety but also encourage more residents to choose cycling over driving, reducing congestion and emissions. I would be happy to discuss these ideas further or assist in gathering additional community feedback.
Thank you for your consideration.
Sincerely,
Jordan Lee
Neighborhood Advocacy Coordinator

Over the past six months I have ridden the designated routes daily and have noticed several recurring safety concerns that deserve attention. In particular, the stretch along Main Street between 3rd and 5th avenues is a high-traffic corridor where cyclists often have to merge into vehicle lanes to avoid debris and potholes.

The purpose of this memorandum is to provide a concise assessment of current language-learning applications and to outline how they align with our corporate training objectives. Over the past twelve months we have examined usage data, user feedback, and cost structures across the most widely adopted platforms.

Our analysis identified three primary categories: subscription-based services that deliver a broad curriculum, freemium apps that rely on in-app purchases for advanced content, and niche solutions focused on specific languages or professional contexts. Each model presents distinct advantages in terms of scalability, engagement, and return on investment.

Key performance indicators we applied include user retention after thirty days, average time spent per session, and measurable improvement in language proficiency as verified by standardized placement tests. In addition, we considered data privacy compliance, integration capability with our existing LMS, and the availability of analytics dashboards for managers.

Among the platforms reviewed, LinguaPro and FluentSphere consistently outperformed peers on the retention and proficiency metrics while offering robust API access for single-sign-on integration. Both providers also maintain GDPR-compliant data handling policies, a non-negotiable requirement for our European operations.

We recommend piloting LinguaPro for the sales department and FluentSphere for customer support, each with a six-month evaluation period. Progress will be reported quarterly, and a final decision on enterprise-wide licensing will be made based on adoption rates, cost-benefit analysis, and learner outcomes.

Subject: Clarification on Local Recycling Guidelines
Hi everyone,
I wanted to reach out to clear up some confusion regarding our neighborhood recycling program. Many neighbors have been asking me what specific items are accepted, and I realized that the information posted on the city website can be quite dense and difficult to navigate at a quick glance. I want to make sure we are all on the same page to avoid contamined loads being rejected at the facility.
First and foremost, please remember that no "wishcycling" is allowed. Just because something is made of plastic does not mean it belongs in the blue bin. Only rigid plastics with resin codes one through five are acceptable. Soft packaging, baggies, and film plastics must go into the special drop-off bags provided at the community center, not the curbside bin.
Regarding glassware, only clean bottles and jars are permitted. No wine or whiskey bottles, and absolutely no bakeware or decorative items. If you have a slight amount of food residue left on a container, it is generally fine, but you must not rinse non-refriodgerated items. Keeping the bins as dry as possible helps prevent odor issues for the sanitation workers who collect our waste every Tuesday and Friday.
Urban legends about paper products can also cause trouble. Shredded paper should ideally be placed back in an envelope first so the trucks cannot scatter it through the streets. Standard paper towels, napkins, and tissues are never recyclable and must remain in the regular trash. This distinction is crucial for maintaining the quality of the recycled paper stock we are helping to produce.
If you are ever in doubt about a specific item, please check the searchable zip code database on the municipal site or simply leave it in the trash. It is always better to over-trash than to under-recycle. Let us work together to keep our local streams clean and our recycling rate high for the benefit of the entire community.
Best regards,
Sarah Jenkins

The purpose of this notice is to inform all staff and visitors of the flood preparedness measures that must be observed at the Riverbank Campus. Recent weather patterns have increased the likelihood of significant rainfall, and the nearby creek has a documented history of overtopping its banks during extreme events. Maintaining a consistent level of readiness protects personnel, preserves critical equipment, and reduces potential interruptions to our operations. All employees are expected to familiarize themselves with the procedures outlined below and to act promptly if a flood warning is issued.

Flood risk is evaluated on a daily basis by the Facilities Management team, which monitors river gauges, weather forecasts, and local alerts issued by the National Weather Service. When water levels approach the pre-determined threshold, an amber warning will be circulated via email and the public address system, followed by a red warning if conditions deteriorate further. Visible signs of rising water include increased flow velocity in the creek, water pooling near low-lying entrances, and the appearance of debris along the banks. In such circumstances, all non-essential activities should be suspended, and personnel should prepare to relocate to higher ground as directed.

Every department must maintain a basic emergency kit that includes a waterproof flashlight, a first-aid kit, a battery-operated radio, and sufficient bottled water for at least 24 hours. Important documents such as employee identification, insurance policies, and critical project files should be stored in waterproof containers or on secure cloud platforms. Evacuation routes have been clearly posted on each floor, highlighting stairwells that remain above the projected flood line. Employees should familiarize themselves with the nearest safe exit and the designated assembly point located on the third floor roof, which is equipped with sandbags and temporary shelter supplies. Regular drills will be scheduled to ensure that all staff can move quickly and safely when required.

During an active flood event, the primary concern is personal safety. If water begins to enter the building, cease all work immediately and proceed to the nearest safe exit, avoiding any routes that may become submerged. Do not attempt to retrieve personal belongings from lower levels, as this can delay evacuation and increase risk. Supervisors will account for all team members at the assembly point and will relay status updates to the Emergency Coordination Center via the established radio channel. Communication devices should be kept on low power to conserve battery life, and any injuries must be reported to onsite medical personnel without delay.

After the water recedes, a thorough inspection of the premises will be conducted before normal operations resume. Facilities staff will assess structural integrity, check electrical systems for damage, and verify that all safety equipment is functional. Employees are required to report any water-related damage to their manager and to document losses for insurance purposes. A post-incident review will be held within five business days to evaluate the effectiveness of the response and to identify any improvements needed for future preparedness. For further information or assistance, contact the Safety Office at extension 4221 or email safety@riverbankcorp.com.

Subject: Important Updates Regarding Our Office Move
Hi Everyone,
I hope you are all having a productive week so far. I am writing to share some significant news that will impact our daily operations over the coming weeks. As you may have heard in recent team meetings, we have officially finalized the details for our move to the new headquarters on Fifth Avenue. This transition is a major step forward for our company infrastructure and will provide us with the modern facilities we have been discussing for some time.
The actual physical move is scheduled to take place during the weekend of the fourteenth and fifteenth of June. To ensure a seamless transition and minimize disruption to client projects, all department heads have been instructed to label their personal items and data drives by the end of this month. Please make sure that sensitive documents are secured and handed over to the IT team, as they will be managing the secure transport of all hardware and server equipment to the new site.
I want to address the schedule for the transition period directly. On the morning of Monday the sixteenth, the office will remain closed to the public as we complete final setup and safety checks. We anticipate being fully operational by Tuesday the seventeenth, though some minor inconveniences like missing electrical outlets or software glitches may occur initially. Please bear with us as we sort out these logistical details, and feel free to reach out to the facilities management team if you experience any specific issues upon arrival.
To support you during this change, the IT department will be hosting optional orientation sessions on Monday afternoon. These sessions will cover updates to the intranet, new printing protocols, and changes to the meeting room booking system. Additionally, a food truck will be stationed outside the new building on Tuesday to welcome the team, so I encourage everyone to join us for a casual lunch to start the new chapter together.
Thank you for your patience and cooperation as we navigate this important change. Your dedication has always been the backbone of our success, and I am confident that this relocation will only strengthen our ability to serve our clients effectively. If you have any concerns or specific questions regarding the move, do not hesitate to reply to this email or stop by my office before you leave for the day.
Best regards,
Julian Thorne
Director of Operations

I hope you are all having a productive week so far. I am writing to share some significant news that will impact our daily operations over the coming weeks. As you may have heard in recent team meetings, we have officially finalized the details for our move to the new headquarters on Fifth Avenue. This transition is a major step forward for our company infrastructure and will provide us with the modern facilities we have been discussing for some time.
The actual physical move is scheduled to take place during the weekend of the fourteenth and fifteenth of June. To ensure a seamless transition and minimize disruption to client projects, all department heads have been instructed to label their personal items and data drives by the end of this month. Please make sure that sensitive documents are secured and handed over to the IT team, as they will be managing the secure transport of all hardware and server equipment to the new site.
I want to address the schedule for the transition period directly. On the morning of Monday the sixteenth, the office will remain closed to the public as we complete final setup and safety checks. We anticipate being fully operational by Tuesday the seventeenth, though some minor inconveniences like missing electrical outlets or software glitches may occur initially. Please bear with us as we sort out these logistical details, and feel free to reach out to the facilities management team if you experience any specific issues upon arrival.
To support you during this change, the IT department will be hosting optional orientation sessions on Monday afternoon. These sessions will cover updates to the intranet, new printing protocols, and changes to the meeting room booking system. Additionally, a food truck will be stationed outside the new building on Tuesday to welcome the team, so I encourage everyone to join us for a casual lunch to start the new chapter together.
Thank you for your patience and cooperation as we navigate this important change. Your dedication has always been the backbone of our success, and I am confident that this relocation will only strengthen our ability to serve our clients effectively. If you have any concerns or specific questions regarding the move, do not hesitate to reply to this email or stop by my office before you leave for the day.
Best regards,
Julian Thorne
Director of Operations
