Subject: Mandatory Grounding and Load Management Protocol for DC Fast Chargers

All facility maintenance staff and engineering technicians are hereby notified of updated procedural requirements regarding the installation and inspection of new 150-kilowatt DC fast charging units at Sites Alpha and Beta. Effective immediately, prior to energizing any new unit, a comprehensive review of the local utility service entrance is required. This step ensures that existing electrical capacity can support the additional peak demand without tripping upstream breakers or compromising the safety of the building grid. Technicians must verify that the neutral conductor sizing meets the current limits specified by the network operator's latest firmware updates.

Routine maintenance schedules have been modified to include quarterly thermal scanning of all high-voltage connectors and distribution panels. Infrared thermography is now the standard diagnostic tool for identifying early signs of loose connections or degraded insulation. Any reading exceeding 80 degrees Celsius on a live terminal during a 50kW load test must trigger an immediate shutdown for inspection. Documentation of these scans must be uploaded to the central asset management system within 24 hours of the site visit to ensure regulatory compliance records are kept current.

Safety gear requirements for working in the vicinity of active charging hardware have been tightened. Personnel must wear arc-flash rated PPE appropriate for a 1000-volt system whenever accessing the internal components of the charging cabinet. The two-person rule applies to all live-line tests conducted during commissioning phases. One technician must remain outside the danger zone with the emergency stop button within reach, ready to cut power in the event of an unexpected fault or human error during the testing sequence.

Vendor support contracts now include a stipulation for remote diagnostic monitoring and automatic firmware patching. This connectivity feature allows our central control room to receive real-time alerts regarding hardware anomalies before they escalate into full system failures. Staff should no longer attempt manual reboots of communication interfaces in the field unless explicitly directed by the vendor's remote support engineer. Self-initiated resets may obscure critical error logs necessary for warranty claims and root cause analysis.

Failure to adhere to these revised protocols will result in disciplinary action and potential liability for damages caused by improper installation or maintenance. Questions regarding specific site configurations or utility interconnection issues should be directed to the Lead Infrastructure Engineer before commencing any work. This memo supersedes all previous guidelines related to EVSE installation and takes effect on the first day of the upcoming fiscal quarter.

Subject: Invitation to Join Our New Saturday Farmers Market
Dear Community Members,
I am excited to announce that we will be launching a weekly farmers market in the town square, beginning next Saturday. This initiative is a collaboration between the local council, nearby farms, and several neighborhood groups who share a passion for fresh, sustainable food. Our goal is to create a welcoming space where residents can meet the people who grow their produce, learn about seasonal eating, and enjoy a lively atmosphere of music and community spirit.
The market will be held every Saturday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the corner of Main Street and Oak Avenue, a location that is easily accessible by foot, bike, and public transit. We have secured permits for the space and arranged for a shaded canopy area for vendors, as well as a small stage for local musicians and storytellers. Parking will be available at the adjacent lot, and we encourage carpooling or using the new bike racks that will be installed just before the opening day.
We have already confirmed participation from several family-owned farms within a 30-mile radius, including Green Valley Organic, Hilltop Apples, and Sunrise Honey. In addition to fresh fruits, vegetables, and dairy, we will feature homemade jams, artisanal breads, and handcrafted soaps made from local ingredients. This market will not only support our regional growers but also provide a platform for small entrepreneurs to reach a wider audience.
To make this event a success, we are looking for volunteers to help with setup, crowd management, and information booths. If you have a few hours to spare, please let us know your availability. We also invite anyone interested in renting a stall to submit a brief description of their products and a photo of their setup by next Wednesday.
Thank you for your enthusiasm and support. We look forward to seeing you at the first market and sharing the bounty of our wonderful community.
Sincerely, 
Maria L. Hernandez 
Community Outreach Coordinator 
Town of Willowbrook 
mlhernandez@willowbrook.gov - (555) 321-7845

2014 Mountain West Conference baseball tournament

The 2014 Mountain West Conference baseball tournament took place from May 21 through 25. All seven of the league's teams met in the double-elimination tournament held at University of Nevada, Las Vegas's Earl E. Wilson Stadium. This is San Jose State's first year in the league after joining from the Western Athletic Conference. San Diego State won the tournament, earning the Mountain West's automatic bid to the 2014 NCAA Division I baseball tournament.

The conference's seven teams were seeded based on winning percentage during the round-robin regular season schedule. The bottom two seeds played a single-elimination game prior to the main six-team double-elimination bracket. The top two seeds received a bye to the second round, with the top seed playing the lowest seeded team that won its first round game, and the second seeded team playing the higher seeded first day winner. The losers of the first day's first-round games played an elimination game in the double-elimination format. The higher seeded loser of the second round games in the winner's bracket played an elimination game in the third round of the loser's bracket. The lower seeded loser of the second round games in the winner's bracket played an elimination game in the second round of the loser's bracket.

UNLV and New Mexico finished tied for first place and are Mountain West Conference regular-season co-champions. UNLV won 5 of the 6 games they played against New Mexico to take the #1 seed in the tournament. Air Force and San Jose State finished tied for sixth place. Air Force won 2 of the 3 games they played against San Jose State to take the #6 seed in the tournament.

San Diego State junior catcher Brad Haynal was named Tournament Most Valuable Player. Haynal was the leading hitter in the tournament batting .636 (14 for 22) and was also the leader in runs scored with nine.

The tournament came down to a final game between San Diego State and UNLV with each team having already lost once. With the game tied at 3 in the top of the sixth inning, shortstop Evan Potter's sacrifice fly pushed across the go-ahead run giving the Aztecs a 4-3 lead which their bullpen held. T.J. Kendzora pitched 1 2/3 hitless and scoreless innings in relief to record the win. Aztecs' third baseman Ty France had three hits, an RBI, a run scored and a stolen base. Michael Cederoth recorded his 20th save of the season which is both a Mountain West and a San Diego State school record.

All seven of the league's teams met in the double-elimination tournament held at University of Nevada, Las Vegas's Earl E. Wilson Stadium. This is San Jose State's first year in the league after joining from the Western Athletic Conference. San Diego State won the tournament, earning the Mountain West's automatic bid to the 2014 NCAA Division I baseball tournament.

The conference's seven teams were seeded based on winning percentage during the round-robin regular season schedule. The bottom two seeds played a single-elimination game prior to the main six-team double-elimination bracket. The top two seeds received a bye to the second round, with the top seed playing the lowest seeded team that won its first round game, and the second seeded team playing the higher seeded first day winner. The losers of the first day's first-round games played an elimination game in the double-elimination format. The higher seeded loser of the second round games in the winner's bracket played an elimination game in the third round of the loser's bracket. The lower seeded loser of the second round games in the winner's bracket played an elimination game in the second round of the loser's bracket.

UNLV and New Mexico finished tied for first place and are Mountain West Conference regular-season co-champions. UNLV won 5 of the 6 games they played against New Mexico to take the #1 seed in the tournament. Air Force and San Jose State finished tied for sixth place. Air Force won 2 of the 3 games they played against San Jose State to take the #6 seed in the tournament.

San Diego State junior catcher Brad Haynal was named Tournament Most Valuable Player. Haynal was the leading hitter in the tournament batting .636 (14 for 22) and was also the leader in runs scored with nine.

The tournament came down to a final game between San Diego State and UNLV with each team having already lost once. With the game tied at 3 in the top of the sixth inning, shortstop Evan Potter's sacrifice fly pushed across the go-ahead run giving the Aztecs a 4-3 lead which their bullpen held. T.J. Kendzora pitched 1 2/3 hitless and scoreless innings in relief to record the win. Aztecs' third baseman Ty France had three hits, an RBI, a run scored and a stolen base. Michael Cederoth recorded his 20th save of the season which is both a Mountain West and a San Diego State school record.

Subject: Meet Biscuit: A Sweet Rescue Senior Dog Seeking His Forever Home
Hello there,
I am writing to share some wonderful news about a special candidate available for adoption at our local sanctuary. His name is Biscuit, a seven-year-old mixed-breed terrier who has spent the last two years in our care. Despite his age, Biscuit remains incredibly energetic and playful, often chasing tennis balls around the yard with a joy that is truly contagious to watch. He was surrendered after his previous owner passed away, and he has been eager to find a new family who can give him the stability and love he deserves.
Biscuit is already house-trained and knows basic commands like sit, stay, and come. He gets along well with other dogs, though he tends to keep a respectful distance from cats, preferring his own space when they are around. His veterinary records are up to date, including his spay/neuter status, vaccinations, and microchip information. The staff here says he is a very affectionate guy who loves belly rubs and leaning against people for comfort during quiet evenings.
The adoption fee is set at $150, which covers his initial vet check-up and first dose of heartworm prevention. This amount helps offset the ongoing costs of caring for him while he waits for his new home. We ask that all prospective adopters complete our standard application form, which includes a reference check and a home environment assessment. Please note that we do allow visitors to meet potential pets in person before making a final decision, as this helps ensure a good match for everyone involved.
To schedule a meet-and-greet, please reply to this email with your preferred dates and times. We operate on weekends from ten a.m. to four p.m. and on Tuesdays and Thursdays from two p.m. to six p.m. If you have any specific questions about his temperament or history, feel free to ask. We want to ensure that Biscuit ends up in a safe, loving environment where he can thrive for the many years ahead of him.
Thank you for considering opening your home and heart to a shelter pet. Every adoption makes a significant difference in an animal's life, and Biscuit is certainly ready to become a beloved family member. We look forward to hearing from you soon and hopefully welcoming him to a happy new chapter.
Warm regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Adoptions Coordinator
Sunshine Valley Animal Shelter

Formalism (art)

In art history, formalism is the study of art by analyzing and comparing form and style. Its discussion also includes the way objects are made and their purely visual or material aspects. In painting, formalism emphasizes compositional elements such as color, line, shape, texture, and other perceptual aspects rather than content, meaning, or the historical and social context. At its extreme, formalism in art history posits that everything necessary to comprehending a work of art is contained within the work of art. The context of the work, including the reason for its creation, the historical background, and the life of the artist, that is, its conceptual aspect is considered to be external to the artistic medium itself, and therefore of secondary importance.

The historical origin of the modern form of the question of aesthetic formalism is usually dated to Immanuel Kant and the writing of his third Critique where Kant states: "Every form of the objects of sense is either figure (Gestalt) or play (Spiel). In the latter case it is either play of figures or the mere play of sensations. The charm (Reiz) of colors... may be added, but the delineations (Zeichnung) in the... composition (Komposition)... constitute the proper object of the pure judgment of taste." The philosopher Donald Crawford has summarized Kant's position stating: "Thus, for Kant, form consists of the spatial... organization of elements: figure, shape, or delineation... In the parts of the Critique of Judgment in which form is emphasized as the essential aspect of beauty, Kant is consistently a pure formalist."

Nick Zangwill has defined formalism in art as referring to those properties "that are determined solely by sensory or physical properties-so long as the physical properties in question are not relations to other things and other times." The philosopher and architect Branko Mitrovic has defined formalism in art and architecture as "the doctrine that states that the aesthetic qualities of works of visual art derive from the visual and spatial properties." According to the observation that works of art can in general contain formal properties and nonformal properties, the philosopher Nick Zangwill has delineated three types of formalism encountered at the turn of the 21st century. First, Zangwill identifies extreme formalists who think "that all works of art are purely formal works-where a work is purely formal if all its aesthetic properties are formal aesthetic properties," then he defines anti-formalist thinkers as those who "think that no works of art have formal aesthetic properties." The third type which Zangwill identifies as representing the transition of the philosophy of aesthetics into the 21st century is that of moderate formalism, where its principal exponents defend the principle "that all the aesthetic properties of works of art in a select class are formal, and second, that although many works of art outside that class have nonformal aesthetic properties, many of those works also have important formal aesthetic properties that must not be ignored." The philosopher Michalle Gal has offered a moderate version of formalism, entitled "Deep Formalism", which is a symbolic formalism based on philosophical aestheticism. The artwork is defined by her as deep form: "a form steeped in content that cannot be extracted from it. Artistic content, since it has no existence or sense apart from the form, cannot actually be referred to, other than speculatively. The content seals the form in an opaque, non-reflective, productive symbol." Here she introduces a broad concept of symbol, an opaque-productive symbol: one that is not transparent to preconceived or predetermined referents and meanings, but rather produces new ones.

A formal analysis is an academic method in art history and criticism for analyzing works of art: "In order to perceive style, and understand it, art historians use 'formal analysis'. This means they describe things very carefully. These descriptions, which may include subjective vocabulary, are always accompanied by illustrations so that there can be no doubt about what exists objectively".

Formalism (art)
In art history, formalism is the study of art by analyzing and comparing form and style. Its discussion also includes the way objects are made and their purely visual or material aspects. In painting, formalism emphasizes compositional elements such as color, line, shape, texture, and other perceptual aspects rather than content, meaning, or the historical and social context. At its extreme, formalism in art history posits that everything necessary to comprehending a work of art is contained within the work of art. The context of the work, including the reason for its creation, the historical background, and the life of the artist, that is, its conceptual aspect is considered to be external to the artistic medium itself, and therefore of secondary importance.
The historical origin of the modern form of the question of aesthetic formalism is usually dated to Immanuel Kant and the writing of his third Critique where Kant states: "Every form of the objects of sense is either figure (Gestalt) or play (Spiel). In the latter case it is either play of figures or the mere play of sensations. The charm (Reiz) of colors... may be added, but the delineations (Zeichnung) in the... composition (Komposition)... constitute the proper object of the pure judgment of taste." The philosopher Donald Crawford has summarized Kant's position stating: "Thus, for Kant, form consists of the spatial... organization of elements: figure, shape, or delineation... In the parts of the Critique of Judgment in which form is emphasized as the essential aspect of beauty, Kant is consistently a pure formalist."
Nick Zangwill has defined formalism in art as referring to those properties "that are determined solely by sensory or physical properties-so long as the physical properties in question are not relations to other things and other times." The philosopher and architect Branko Mitrovic has defined formalism in art and architecture as "the doctrine that states that the aesthetic qualities of works of visual art derive from the visual and spatial properties." According to the observation that works of art can in general contain formal properties and nonformal properties, the philosopher Nick Zangwill has delineated three types of formalism encountered at the turn of the 21st century. First, Zangwill identifies extreme formalists who think "that all works of art are purely formal works-where a work is purely formal if all its aesthetic properties are formal aesthetic properties," then he defines anti-formalist thinkers as those who "think that no works of art have formal aesthetic properties." The third type which Zangwill identifies as representing the transition of the philosophy of aesthetics into the 21st century is that of moderate formalism, where its principal exponents defend the principle "that all the aesthetic properties of works of art in a select class are formal, and second, that although many works of art outside that class have nonformal aesthetic properties, many of those works also have important formal aesthetic properties that must not be ignored." The philosopher Michalle Gal has offered a moderate version of formalism, entitled "Deep Formalism", which is a symbolic formalism based on philosophical aestheticism. The artwork is defined by her as deep form: "a form steeped in content that cannot be extracted from it. Artistic content, since it has no existence or sense apart from the form, cannot actually be referred to, other than speculatively. The content seals the form in an opaque, non-reflective, productive symbol." Here she introduces a broad concept of symbol, an opaque-productive symbol: one that is not transparent to preconceived or predetermined referents and meanings, but rather produces new ones.
A formal analysis is an academic method in art history and criticism for analyzing works of art: "In order to perceive style, and understand it, art historians use 'formal analysis'. This means they describe things very carefully. These descriptions, which may include subjective vocabulary, are always accompanied by illustrations so that there can be no doubt about what exists objectively".

national park permits

Securing a national park permit is often the most critical step in planning a high-stakes adventure, yet many hikers and campers underestimate the complexity involved. Whether you are aiming for the high sierras of the Sierra Nevada or the rugged trails of the Canadian Rockies, knowing when to apply and what to expect can make the difference between a memorable journey and a disappointing cancellation. Most popular backcountry routes operate on a lottery system during peak season, supplemented by a first-come, first-served queue for any remaining slots.

The application process typically opens months in advance, requiring thorough preparation of your trip itinerary. You must specify your exact entry and exit points, group size, and emergency contact information. Accuracy is paramount here, as rangers rely on these details for safety monitoring and resource management. A single discrepancy, such as an incorrect trailhead location, can lead to immediate rejection of your application.

Understanding the cost structure is equally important, as permit fees vary significantly by region and season. Some parks charge per person per night, while others use a flat rate for the entire group. It is wise to budget for these expenses early, as they are usually non-refundable once the lottery results are announced. Check the specific park website carefully, as fee schedules are updated annually and may include additional costs for bear canisters or vehicle passes.

When the results are released, successful applicants must pay promptly to secure their access date. Failure to complete the payment within the designated window automatically releases the permit back into the pool for future applicants. Keep digital and physical copies of your approved permit, as rangers may require you to display it during check-ins at trailheads or campgrounds.

Finally, remember that obtaining a permit is not a guarantee of favorable conditions. Weather, trail closures, or emergencies can still alter your plans. Always respect the Leave No Trace principles and adhere strictly to the terms outlined in your permit. This ensures the preservation of these wild spaces for future generations of explorers.

To: All Department Heads 
From: Office of Sustainability and Risk Management 
Date: 8 October 2026 
Subject: Implementing Climate Adaptation Measures Across Operations

The increasing frequency of extreme weather events, sea-level rise, and shifting climate patterns presents tangible risks to our facilities, supply chains, and workforce. Recent assessments indicate that three of our primary manufacturing sites are within a 15-kilometre radius of projected flood zones by 2035, while heat-stress days are expected to rise by 20 percent in the next decade. In response, the Sustainability Office has drafted a set of adaptation actions that must be integrated into each department's annual planning cycle. This memo outlines the core requirements and timelines for compliance, ensuring that our operations remain resilient while supporting our corporate commitment to environmental stewardship.

First, each site manager must complete a vulnerability audit by 30 November 2026, focusing on infrastructure exposure, critical utilities, and employee safety protocols. The audit template, provided in the shared drive, requires documentation of current protective measures, gaps, and projected climate impacts based on the latest regional climate model. Managers are to submit the completed audits to the Risk Management Team, which will consolidate findings and prioritize interventions. Sites identified as high-risk will receive additional engineering support to evaluate flood barriers, drainage upgrades, and heat-mitigation retrofits.

Second, procurement and supply-chain teams are instructed to incorporate climate-resilient criteria into vendor contracts. Suppliers must demonstrate continuity plans that address disruptions caused by climate events, including alternative routing, inventory buffers, and flexible production capacities. By the end of the first quarter of 2027, all new contracts should contain clauses mandating quarterly reporting on adaptation readiness, while existing agreements will be reviewed and amended where feasible. This approach will reduce the likelihood of downstream interruptions and protect our delivery commitments to customers.

Third, human-resource managers are to develop a climate-health and safety framework for staff working in exposed locations. The framework will include heat-exposure monitoring, mandatory rest periods during extreme temperature days, and training on emergency evacuation procedures. A revised employee handbook will be distributed by 15 January 2027, and all personnel must complete the associated online training module within 30 days of receipt. Special attention should be given to vulnerable groups, such as outdoor workers and those with pre-existing health conditions, to ensure equitable protection.

Finally, the executive leadership team will allocate an initial budget of $4.2 million for adaptation projects, with quarterly reviews to assess progress and re-allocate funds as needed. Departments are encouraged to propose innovative, cost-effective solutions that align with our sustainability targets, such as green infrastructure, renewable-energy backups, and nature-based flood defenses. Regular updates will be shared in the quarterly sustainability report, and successful initiatives will be highlighted in internal communications to promote a culture of proactive climate resilience.

Subject: Recommendation for corporate cloud storage platform
Hi Sarah,
I hope you are having a productive week. I have finished my initial assessment of our current data management workflows and the limitations we are facing with our existing on-premise servers. As you know, our team has been experiencing significant bottlenecks during the monthly reporting cycles, and local storage capacity is nearing its limit. After spending several days reviewing the major providers and testing their API integrations with our current software stack, I believe it is time we transition to a hybrid cloud model. This shift would not only resolve our immediate capacity issues but also provide us with the flexibility to scale resources dynamically based on demand, which is crucial for our upcoming product launch.
I have narrowed down the top contenders to AWS S3, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, and Google Cloud Storage. Each platform has distinct advantages that align with different aspects of our business priorities. AWS offers the most mature ecosystem and a vast global footprint, which might be beneficial if we plan to expand into specific Asian markets next quarter. However, their pricing model can become complex without careful configuration, often leading to unexpected costs if not monitored closely. Azure, on the other hand, integrates seamlessly with our existing Office 365 and Active Directory infrastructure, which would minimize the friction for our staff during the migration process. The single sign-on capabilities and familiar interface would likely reduce training time and user resistance significantly.
From a technical perspective, Google Cloud Storage presented the most impressive performance metrics in our load testing. The consistency of retrieval speeds under high concurrent user loads was slightly superior to the other two options, which is vital for our real-time analytics dashboards. However, our engineering team raised concerns about the lack of certain legacy library support in the first phase. They suggested that while GCS is excellent for new projects, retrofitting our older codebase to work efficiently with it might require more development hours than budgeted for the initial quarter. Conversely, Azure's native compatibility with .NET applications means we can reuse much of our existing code, potentially saving us around two hundred hours of developer time in the migration phase alone.
Cost remains a significant factor in this decision, and I have prepared a detailed spreadsheet comparing the estimated annual expenses for each provider based on our projected data growth of thirty percent year-over-year. The analysis suggests that while AWS has the highest entry-level cost due to bandwidth and request fees, it becomes more cost-effective for us if we can optimize our storage class strategies. Azure appears to be the most predictable option financially, with a flat rate that is easy to forecast for the CFO. I recommend we proceed with a small-scale pilot program using Azure to gauge real-world performance and user feedback before committing to a full enterprise-wide deployment. This approach mitigates risk while allowing us to validate the integration with our critical business applications.
Please let me know if you have any immediate concerns about these findings or if you would like to schedule a brief meeting to discuss the pilot scope. I am available most of the week, excluding Wednesday afternoons when I am handling server maintenance. There is also a security review checklist attached to the previous email chain that outlines the encryption standards we need to verify before any data leaves our internal network. I want to ensure that compliance with GDPR and internal data sovereignty policies is maintained throughout the transition. Your input on the vendor relationship strategy is also valuable, particularly regarding potential support contract upgrades that might be negotiated during the initial trial period.
Best regards,
David Chen
Senior IT Infrastructure Manager

Subject: Recommendation for corporate cloud storage platform
Hi Sarah,
I hope you are having a productive week. I have finished my initial assessment of our current data management workflows and the limitations we are facing with our existing on-premise servers. As you know, our team has been experiencing significant bottlenecks during the monthly reporting cycles, and local storage capacity is nearing its limit. After spending several days reviewing the major providers and testing their API integrations with our current software stack, I believe it is time we transition to a hybrid cloud model. This shift would not only resolve our immediate capacity issues but also provide us with the flexibility to scale resources dynamically based on demand, which is crucial for our upcoming product launch.
I have narrowed down the top contenders to AWS S3, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, and Google Cloud Storage. Each platform has distinct advantages that align with different aspects of our business priorities. AWS offers the most mature ecosystem and a vast global footprint, which might be beneficial if we plan to expand into specific Asian markets next quarter. However, their pricing model can become complex without careful configuration, often leading to unexpected costs if not monitored closely. Azure, on the other hand, integrates seamlessly with our existing Office 365 and Active Directory infrastructure, which would minimize the friction for our staff during the migration process. The single sign-on capabilities and familiar interface would likely reduce training time and user resistance significantly.
From a technical perspective, Google Cloud Storage presented the most impressive performance metrics in our load testing. The consistency of retrieval speeds under high concurrent user loads was slightly superior to the other two options, which is vital for our real-time analytics dashboards. However, our engineering team raised concerns about the lack of certain legacy library support in the first phase. They suggested that while GCS is excellent for new projects, retrofitting our older codebase to work efficiently with it might require more development hours than budgeted for the initial quarter. Conversely, Azure's native compatibility with .NET applications means we can reuse much of our existing code, potentially saving us around two hundred hours of developer time in the migration phase alone.
Cost remains a significant factor in this decision, and I have prepared a detailed spreadsheet comparing the estimated annual expenses for each provider based on our projected data growth of thirty percent year-over-year. The analysis suggests that while AWS has the highest entry-level cost due to bandwidth and request fees, it becomes more cost-effective for us if we can optimize our storage class strategies. Azure appears to be the most predictable option financially, with a flat rate that is easy to forecast for the CFO. I recommend we proceed with a small-scale pilot program using Azure to gauge real-world performance and user feedback before committing to a full enterprise-wide deployment. This approach mitigates risk while allowing us to validate the integration with our critical business applications.

Liz Danforth

Elizabeth T. Danforth (born 1953) is an illustrator, editor, writer, and scenario designer for collectible card games, role-playing games and video games. She has worked in the game industry continuously since the mid 1970s.

Flying Buffalo hired Danforth as a staff artist and for production work in 1978, and published her magazine Sorcerer's Apprentice (1978-1983) for 17 issues. While employed with Flying Buffalo, Danforth is noted for editing and developing the Fifth Edition of Flying Buffalo's flagship role playing game, Tunnels & Trolls. She reprised this role in 2013 for the new edition, Deluxe Tunnels & Trolls. Danforth is known primarily as a freelance artist in the fantasy and science fiction genres, with the majority of her body of work illustrating for the game industry. She has created book covers, maps, and illustrations for many of the significant game publishers including Wizards of the Coast, TSR, Inc, Alderac Entertainment Group, FASA Corporation, Iron Crown Enterprises, GDW, and more. She produced 36 pieces of art for the early released sets of the collectible card game Magic: The Gathering (produced by Wizards of the Coast), several of which were re-released in subsequent editions and box sets. She has created additional card art for other card games, including the Middle-earth Collectible Card Game, Legend of the Five Rings, and continues to create new works for Sorcery: Contested Realm (produced by Erik's Curiosa Limited). Her maps and illustrations appear in novels and anthologies from Bantam Spectra, Tor Books, DAW Books, and St Martin's Press. She has freelanced for the computer game industry, developing scenarios for Wasteland, Wasteland 2, and two licensed Star Trek computer games from Interplay. She worked on Interplay's Meantime which was never released. She was the lead developer for New World Computing's Tunnels & Trolls computer game, and worked on projects with Electronic Arts. At the 1995 Origins Awards, held in July 1996, Danforth was inducted into the Academy of Gaming Arts and Design's Hall of Fame. The Academy is the creative arm of GAMA, the Game Manufacturer's Association. She is a lifetime member of ASFA, the Association of Science Fiction and Fantasy Artists. In 2014, she was chosen by vote as a "famous game designer" to be featured as the king of hearts in Flying Buffalo's 2014 Famous Game Designers Playing Card Deck. Danforth has been guest of honor at numerous science fiction conventions over the past 30 years, including Cascadia Con, the North American Science Fiction Convention held in Seattle in 2005, and as Artist Guest of Honor at TusCon 52 in 2025. Danforth continues to do art and illustration in a freelance capacity.

Danforth completed a master's degree in Information and Library Science (University of Arizona, 2008), and was one of a dozen hand-selected "gaming experts" who participated in the American Library Association's million-dollar grant-funded project to explore how gaming can be used to improve problem-solving and literacy skills, and to develop a model gaming "toolbox" for gaming in libraries. Ten libraries nationwide were selected to receive a onetime grant of $5,000 with funds used to expand on or add literacy-based gaming experiences at the library for youth ages 10-18. From May 2009 to December 2011, Danforth wrote the "Games, Gamers and Gaming" blog and column for Library Journal as an advocate and popularizer of games in libraries. She speaks at professional and fan conferences, and at libraries on gaming-related topics. Based in Arizona, she continues to do freelance art and writing.

Subject: Important: Preparations for potential flooding
Hi Sarah,
I am writing to share some critical information regarding the upcoming severe weather patterns. The hydrology department has issued a preliminary warning indicating a high probability of significant rainfall over the next seventy-two hours, which could lead to flash flooding in our immediate neighborhood. It is essential that we are proactive rather than reactive to ensure the safety of our household and property.
Please locate our emergency go-bag immediately and verify its contents. We need to ensure we have at least three days' worth of non-perishable food, clean water, and any necessary prescription medications. Do not forget to include copies of important documents such as insurance policies and identification. If they are not already packed, please move these items to a waterproof container and store them in an accessible, elevated location.
Additionally, we should check the foundation of the house for any visible cracks that might allow water intrusion. It is also wise to clear any debris from gutters and downspouts to ensure proper drainage away from the building's base. If you have access to sandbags, consider placing them around the lower-level doors and vents as a precautionary measure against rising water.
Keep your mobile devices fully charged and consider keeping a portable power bank handy in case of an electrical outage. Sign up for local emergency alerts if you have not already done so, so you receive real-time updates on the situation. Let us know if you need assistance with any of these tasks before the weekend ends.
Stay safe and stay alert.
Best regards,
David

The regular monthly meeting of the Riverside Apartments Tenant Association will be held on the second Thursday of this month, specifically October twelfth, at seven in the evening. The session is scheduled to take place in the community lounge on the ground floor. All residents are encouraged to attend to voice concerns and ensure transparent communication between the management team and the tenant body.

Agenda items include the review of recent building maintenance reports and the status of the elevator repair project that has caused delays for several weeks. Management will present a timeline for completion and explain any necessary service interruptions. Additionally, the proposed increase in common area utility costs will be discussed for the upcoming quarter based on current energy rates.

New lease terms regarding pet policies and long-term rental storage units will be outlined. Specific attention will be given to the minimum square footage requirements for storage sheds and the corresponding monthly fees. Residents should note that these changes align with local fire safety codes and require compliance within ninety days of the meeting date.

There is still space for the community garden plot allocation list to be finalized. Those interested in securing a plot for the spring season must register their interest prior to the meeting start time. A sign-up sheet will be available at the entrance. Participants should bring a valid resident ID card if they wish to formally register a new interest or update contact information.

Following the formal agenda, there is an open floor segment for general questions or social updates. Light refreshments will be served by the volunteer committee. Please direct any immediate emergencies or urgent repair requests to the front desk rather than waiting for the general question period. Your participation helps foster a cooperative and safe living environment for everyone.

The administration wishes to remind all residents that the dormitory operates under a set of rules designed to promote safety, respect, and a conducive living environment. All occupants are expected to read and adhere to these guidelines, which are enforced consistently throughout the academic year.

Quiet hours are observed from ten o'clock at night until seven in the morning on weekdays, and from eleven at night until eight in the morning on weekends. During these periods, excessive noise, including loud music, shouting, or the use of amplified devices, must be avoided in private rooms, common areas, and hallways.

Fire safety procedures require that exit routes remain clear at all times. Personal belongings must not block stairwells, fire doors, or sprinkler systems. In the event of an alarm, residents must evacuate promptly and assemble at the designated meeting point outside the building, following the posted evacuation plan.

Visitors are welcome but must be registered at the front desk and are limited to a maximum stay of twenty-four hours per visit. Overnight guests are prohibited unless prior written permission has been obtained from the dormitory manager. Residents remain responsible for the conduct of their guests at all times.

The administration reserves the right to issue warnings, impose fines, or take disciplinary action for violations of any rule. Questions or concerns regarding these policies should be directed to the dormitory office during regular business hours.

Supersnazz

Supersnazz is the debut studio album by the rock band Flamin' Groovies. It was released in 1969 on the Epic label. The release was their only album recorded expressly for a major record label, although all of their next five albums were distributed by major labels. Supersnazz was later released in compact disc format in 2000 on Sundazed Music with four edits of songs from the album (done in 1969 for singles) included as bonus tracks.

Bruce Eder of AllMusic described the album as proto-punk and suggested that the Ramones probably wore out copies of the album. Robert Christgau originally gave the album a lukewarm review with a B+ grade, but later revisited it in 2013 and gave it an A, especially praising "Laurie Did It".

Flamin' Groovies Roy Loney - rhythm guitar, vocals Cyril Jordan - guitar, vocals Tim Lynch - guitar, vocals, harmonica George Alexander - bass guitar, vocals, harmonica Danny Mihm - drums, percussion Mike Lang - keyboards

Subject: Invitation to the "Echoes of Time" Exhibition at the City Art Museum
Dear Dr. Patel,
I hope this message finds you well. I am writing on behalf of the City Art Museum to share some exciting news about our upcoming exhibition, "Echoes of Time," which will run from October 15 through February 28. Curated by the renowned Dr. Elena García, the show brings together over a hundred works spanning three continents and four centuries, illustrating how artists across cultures have responded to the passage of history through sculpture, painting, and mixed media. We believe the exhibition offers a compelling narrative that resonates with both seasoned scholars and casual visitors alike, and we would be honored to have you join us for the opening reception.
The exhibition is organized around three thematic corridors: "Origins," "Transitions," and "Reflections." In "Origins," you will encounter early 19th-century landscape paintings from the Hudson River School alongside traditional Japanese ink scrolls, highlighting parallel explorations of natural grandeur. "Transitions" showcases works from the early modern period, including a striking series of abstract expressionist canvases by the late artist Maya Lin, whose use of reclaimed materials comments on environmental change. Finally, "Reflections" presents contemporary installations that incorporate digital technology, such as the immersive light-and-sound piece by Korean artist Ji-woo Park, which invites visitors to experience time as a fluid, interactive construct. The exhibition catalog, which will be available for purchase at the museum shop, includes essays by leading art historians and high-resolution images of each work.
We are planning a series of events to complement the exhibition, beginning with an exclusive preview for museum members and donors on October 14 at 6:00 p.m., followed by a public opening ceremony on October 15 featuring remarks by Dr. García and a live performance by the City Chamber Orchestra interpreting "musical echoes" inspired by the artworks. Throughout the run, there will be weekly docent-led tours, artist talks, and hands-on workshops for families and school groups. A special lecture by Professor Ahmed El-Sayed on "Temporal Perception in Visual Art" is scheduled for November 3, and we would be delighted if you could attend and perhaps share a few insights during the Q&A session.
For your convenience, tickets can be purchased online through our website or at the museum box office during regular hours. Admission is $15 for adults, $12 for seniors and students, and free for children under 12. The museum is fully accessible, with wheelchair-friendly entrances, elevators, and restrooms on each floor. Complimentary parking is available in the municipal lot adjacent to the museum, and a discounted rate is offered for members. If you prefer public transportation, the downtown subway line stops just a block away from the main entrance, and we provide secure bike racks near the lobby.
Please let me know if you would like me to arrange a complimentary pass for you and a guest, or if there are any particular accommodations you require. We truly hope you can experience "Echoes of Time" and contribute your valuable perspective to the conversations it will spark. Feel free to reach out to me directly at (555) 321-7890 or via email at exhibitions@cityartmuseum.org with any questions or to confirm your attendance.
Thank you for your continued support of the City Art Museum. I look forward to welcoming you to the exhibition soon.
Warm regards,
Sofia Martinez
Senior Curatorial Associate
City Art Museum
(555) 321-7890
exhibitions@cityartmuseum.org

Subject: Schedule for the Autumn Village Craft Fair
Dear Marcus,
I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to finalize the logistics for the upcoming autumn village craft fair scheduled for the first weekend of October. The committee has been in hot debate regarding the layout of the main square, and we need a definitive plan before we send out the vendor contracts. There is a specific concern about the traffic flow near the entrance that requires your input, as you have handled crowd management for our previous two major events without any significant issues.
The primary location for the artisan booths will be along the cobblestone strip adjacent to the old fountain. We are planning to accommodate forty stalls this time, which is an increase of ten from last year due to higher demand. We need to ensure that each vendor has adequate space for setup and breakdown without impeding pedestrian walkways. I have attached a preliminary map for your review, though please note that the dimensions are estimates and may need adjustment once we measure the exact distances on site this coming Tuesday.
Regarding the lighting and电力, the power company has confirmed that they will install temporary outlets at the north and south ends of the venue. However, we still need to verify if the central area, where the live music stage will be located, can support the necessary load for the amplifiers and stage lighting. If there are any limitations, we will have to rely on battery-powered systems, which adds a significant cost to the budget. I need you to consult with the technical vendor and get us a written quote by Friday afternoon so we can process the payment before the end of the month.
Food safety regulations have also become stricter this year, and the health inspector requires a detailed plan for how we will manage waste disposal and keep the food vendors separated from the general foot traffic. We are considering installing semi-permanent fencing to create dedicated service areas behind the food stalls. This will require some minor construction work on the grassy verge, so we need to check with the parks department to ensure we have the proper permits before any ground is broken.
Please let me know if you have any objections to the proposed timeline or the allocated budget for these additional infrastructure upgrades. I am available for a brief phone call after four o'clock on Thursday if you prefer to discuss these details verbally rather than through email. It is crucial that we get everything approved by next Wednesday to maintain the four-week lead time required for the legal agreements with our vendors.
I look forward to hearing from you soon and appreciate your continued dedication to making this event a success for our community.
Best regards,
Elena Ross
Event Coordinator

Subject: Getting Started with 3D Printing - A Quick Overview
Hi Alex,
I wanted to share a brief rundown of the basics behind 3D printing, since you mentioned interest in trying it out for your next prototype. At its core, the process builds objects layer by layer from a digital model, usually a CAD file exported as an STL. The printer reads the file, slices it into thin cross-sections, and then deposits material-most commonly melted plastic filament-according to those slices.
The two most common consumer-grade technologies are Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) and Resin (SLA) printing. FDM pushes heated filament through a nozzle, creating a visible layering effect, while SLA cures liquid resin with a UV laser for smoother finishes. Your choice will depend on the level of detail you need and your budget; FDM printers are generally cheaper and easier to maintain, whereas resin printers excel at fine details but require more post-processing.
Before you start printing, you'll need a reliable 3-D model. You can design one yourself using software like Tinkercad or Fusion 360, or you can download free models from sites such as Thingiverse. Once you have the file, run it through a slicer program-Cura or PrusaSlicer are popular options-to set layer height, infill density, and support structures.
When you launch a print, keep an eye on the first few layers; good adhesion to the build plate is crucial. If the filament doesn't stick, you might need to adjust the bed temperature, apply a glue stick, or level the plate more precisely.
Feel free to reach out if you run into any hiccups or want recommendations on specific printer models. I'm happy to help you get the most out of your first prints.
Best regards,
Jordan Lee 
Product Development Engineer 
TechForge Labs

Subject: Quick tips for saving our office succulents
Hi Sarah,
I wanted to reach out because I noticed some of the succulents in the breakroom are looking a bit wrinkled and discolored. It seems like they might not be getting the proper care they need lately. I know how easy it is to forget about the plants when everyone is busy with deadlines, so I put together a few simple reminders that might help us get them back on track.
First and foremost, water is the most common mistake we make with these types of plants. Succulents are built to store water in their leaves, so they actually prefer to be root-bound and slightly dry. If the soil is still moist at the top, it is best to wait another day or two before watering again. Overwatering is what causes the root rot we saw last month, which killed half of the collection on the north window ledge.
Lighting is the other critical factor. These plants thrive in bright, indirect light, but they can handle some direct morning sun. The spot by the sliding door gets intense afternoon rays that might be scorching the leaves, turning them reddish-brown in patches. We might need to rotate them weekly or move them slightly away from the glass to prevent sunburn. A gentle turn of the pot once a week ensures all sides grow evenly.
Do not hesitate to poke the soil to check for moisture, but try not to disturb the roots too much during the process. If the soil feels dry all the way down, give them a thorough drink until water runs out of the drainage holes. Letting them sit in a saucer of water for hours is a no-no because the constant moisture leads to fungal issues. Proper drainage is key, so ensure those little holes in the bottom of the pots are not blocked by dirt or pebbles.
If we follow these simple guidelines, I believe the surviving plants will bounce back within a couple of weeks. You should see new leaf growth and a return of that healthy green or purple hue. Please let me know if you have any other concerns or if you would like to schedule a quick cleaning session to wipe off the dust from the leaves, as that can also block light absorption.
Thanks for helping keep our workspace green and lively.
Best regards,
Alex

The spot by the sliding door gets intense afternoon rays that might be scorching the leaves, turning them reddish-brown in patches. Camelus knoblochi

Camelus knoblochi is an extinct species of camel that inhabited Eurasia during the Pleistocene epoch. One of the largest known camel species, its range spanned from Eastern Europe to Northern China.

The earliest remains of the species were collected from the Volga region of Russia. The species was first recognised as distinct in an 1880 paper by I. S. Poliakov, but this was never published. The species was properly named in 1901 by Alfred Nehring, based on a fossil skull and lower jaws collected at the Luchka locality in the lower Volga, with the species name being after Alexander Knobloch, a factory owner in the nearby town of Sarepta interested in fossils who sent the skull in 1880 to the Zoological museum of St. Petersburg.

Sequenced genomes of C. knoblochi suggests that while the species is distinct from the living Camelus ferus (wild Bactrian camel) at the nuclear genomic level, its mitochondrial genome diversity is nested within that of the wild Bactrian camel, likely as a result of interbreeding with that species. While clearly a genetically distinct species in its own right which is more closely related to both the living wild Bactrian camel and the domestric Bactrian camel (Camelus bactrianus) than to the dromedary, it forms an effective polytomy with the two living Bactrian camel species likely due to interbreeding between the species as well as the three species diverging from each other around the same time. Genome analysis indicates that all 3 species had been genetically distinct from each other for at least 400,000 years. Cladogram after Yuan et al. 2024:

Camelus knoblochi is one of the largest known species of genus Camelus, being considerably larger than the 3 living camel species. C. knoblochi has been estimated to reach around 3 metres (9.8 ft) tall and over 1,000 kilograms (2,200 lb) in weight. Its bones are more physically massive than those of living camels. The facial part of the skull is around 60% of the total length, somewhat elongate relative to other members of Camelus. The premaxillary bones are unfused. The metatarsals are slightly more elongate than the metacarpals on average.

Remains of Camelus knoblochi span from Ukraine in the west, southwards into the Caucasus and Central Asia, and across the Urals into Mongolia and into Northeast China. During the Late Pleistocene, its distribution was restricted from the Urals eastwards. The habitat of the species was primarily steppe, and to a lesser degree, forest steppe, rather than the desert environments inhabited by living Bactrian camel species. During the Late Pleistocene in Mongolia and northern China, the species coexisted alongside other megafauna like the woolly rhinoceros, Merck's rhinoceros, the elephant Palaeoloxodon, the buffalo Bubalus wansjocki. the giant deer Sinomegaceros ordosianus, Przewalski's horse, Asiatic wild asses, and argali. In the Volga region during Middle Pleistocene, it lived alongside Merck's rhinoceros, the elephant-sized rhinoceros Elasmotherium sibiricum (sometimes called the Siberian unicorn), steppe bison, the giant Irish elk, saiga antelope and red deer. Isotopic analysis suggests that the species was a browser on C3 vegetation.

At Tsagaan Agui Cave in Mongolia, a metacarpal of the species, dating to around 59-44,000 years Before Present, bears fracture marks as a result of human butchery like to access the marrow cavity, with bite marks showing that it was subsequently gnawed on by cave hyaenas. Pleistocene cave art from Mongolia may also depict the species.

The latest remains of the species are from the Gobi Desert of Mongolia, where the species became extinct around the Last Glacial Maximum (around 26-19,500 years ago). Genetic analysis suggests that the species had already been in population decline for tens of thousands of years prior. The species likely went extinct as a result of unfavourable environmental change, including the aridification of the Gobi Desert around this time.

Subject: Updates on the new rainwater collection system
Hi Sarah,
I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to share a few important updates regarding the rainwater harvesting infrastructure we have been planning for the last several months. As you know, we have been eager to implement a sustainable solution to reduce our reliance on municipal water supply, especially during those prolonged summer droughts that seem to be becoming more frequent each year. The team has conducted a thorough assessment of our current drainage patterns and soil composition, and I am pleased to say that the preliminary results are very promising. We are confident that the proposed design will not only meet our immediate needs for irrigation but also provide a buffer for general non-potable uses around the estate.
We have selected a cistern location near the existing garden shed to minimize the length of the transfer pipes and reduce energy costs associated with pumping. By positioning the storage tank close to the primary drainage outflow from the main roof, we can utilize gravity to feed water into the holding tank efficiently. This strategic placement saves us from having to install complex high-pressure pumping systems in the initial phase of the project. Furthermore, the area offers stable ground conditions, which is crucial for supporting a large volume of water without risking structural shifts or subsidence over time. The local council has already approved the ground-breaking permit, so we can move forward with the civil works as soon as the weather permits better working conditions.
Regarding the filtration and safety aspects, we have decided to include a multi-stage filtration system to ensure the quality of the harvested rainwater. The first stage will be a simple leaf screen at the gutter level to remove large debris like twigs and leaves. Once the water enters the cistern, it will pass through a carbon filter to remove any dissolved impurities and odors. This setup is particularly important because we intend to use a portion of this water for washing vehicles and cleaning outdoor equipment, where clear and odorless water is preferred. We are also discussing the potential for adding a UV purification stage later, which would allow us to use the water for more sensitive applications, such as water feature maintenance.
The financial projections indicate that this project will pay for itself within five to seven years, primarily through reduced water bills and lower sewerage charges. While there is an initial capital outlay for the tanks, pumps, and filtration units, the long-term savings are substantial, not to mention the positive environmental impact. Reducing our strain on local water resources aligns perfectly with our corporate social responsibility goals, and I believe it will be well received by our stakeholders. We should also receive some partial funding from the green infrastructure grant that I mentioned in our last meeting, which will offset a significant portion of the hardware costs.
Please let me know if you have any concerns or if you would like to review the detailed engineering plans before we finalize the vendor contracts. I have attached the initial schematic and cost breakdown to this email for your reference. I am aiming to have the project fully operational by the end of the quarter, just in time for the upcoming dry season. Your input on the aesthetic integration of the system into the garden landscape would also be valuable, as we want the installation to be functional without detracting from the overall beauty of the property. Thanks for your continued support on this initiative.
Best regards,
James

Larissa Takchi

Larissa Takchi (born 1997) is an Australian cook who won the eleventh series of MasterChef Australia in 2019. At 22 years old, to date she was the youngest contestant to win the competition.

Takchi was born in Sydney, into a family of Lebanese origin. Her grandparents had emigrated from Lebanon to Australia, and founded a stone fruit farm in Glenorie. Her mother owned a cafe in Dural. Prior to winning MasterChef Australia, she served as the general manager of her mother's cafe. In primary school she attended Hillside Public School, and high school at Mount St Benedict College. Takchi attended Macquarie University, where she studied business.

Takchi was selected in the 2019 auditions to join the 'Top 24' as a contestant on MasterChef Australia. On 23 July 2019, Takchi was announced as the winner of MasterChef 2019 and received a cash prize of $250,000, a new Holden Equinox car, and a monthly column in Delicious magazine for 12 months. Her winning dish was "Szechuan Pavlova", a dessert featuring beetroot and blackberry sorbet, Sichuan (Szechuan) pepper, and lemon cream.

Subject: Curatorial timeline for the upcoming contemporary wing
Dear Elena,
I hope this message finds you well and that the recent grant renewal process did not cause too much stress. I am writing to discuss the final details of the "Fractured Perspectives" exhibition opening next month. The production team has just confirmed the installation schedule, and we need to align our curatorial voice with the physical layout before we hold the final walkthrough.
The main issue revolves around the central installation in Gallery B. The artist has requested a significant change to the lighting rig, which conflicts with our current conservation protocols for the adjacent works. I have spoken with the head of conservation, and they are quite hesitant to approve the brighter spectrum proposed by the designer. We need to find a balanced solution that respects both the artistic intent and the preservation of our permanent collection pieces.
Could you please review the attached lighting schematics at your earliest convenience? I have annotated the specific zones where we might compromise on intensity without compromising visibility. Your insight into the thematic connections between the pieces will be crucial in deciding which elements require maximum focus. I really value your perspective on how we frame the narrative for the general audience.
Let us aim to finalize this decision by midweek. Once we have your approval, I will send a formal request to the production vendor to adjust the fixtures. Time is becoming a bit tight as the wall text finalization depends on these technical specifications. I want to ensure the entire experience feels cohesive and professional when the doors open to the public.
Looking forward to hearing your thoughts on this matter. Please let me know if you would prefer a quick phone call later today instead of a lengthy email correspondence. I am flexible with my schedule until five PM. Thank you for your continued dedication to making this show a success for our institution.
Best regards,
Marcus Thorne
Senior Curator, Contemporary Art

raw:
budget planning

.

Effective budget planning starts with a clear picture of where you stand financially. Before you can allocate funds, you need to gather all sources of income, from salaries and freelance work to any side-hustle earnings. At the same time, list every recurring expense-rent, utilities, subscriptions, insurance-and any irregular costs you anticipate, such as car maintenance or holiday gifts. This snapshot helps you understand the gap between what you bring in and what you must cover, forming the foundation for realistic decisions.

Once you have the numbers, the next step is to set priorities that reflect both your short-term needs and long-term goals. Essential expenses, like housing and food, naturally take precedence, but you should also earmark a portion of your income for savings, debt reduction, and future investments. Assigning percentages to each category-perhaps 50 % for necessities, 20 % for savings, 15 % for debt repayment and 15 % for discretionary spending-provides a flexible framework that can be adjusted as circumstances change.

Choosing the right tools can make the budgeting process smoother and more transparent. Many people rely on spreadsheet templates because they offer full control over categories and formulas. Others prefer dedicated budgeting apps that automatically import transactions, categorize spending, and send alerts when limits are approached. Whichever method you select, consistency is key; regularly updating your records prevents small oversights from snowballing into larger financial blind spots.

A common pitfall is underestimating variable costs, especially when it comes to food, entertainment and transportation. To avoid this, track your actual spending for a month or two before finalizing your budget. This real-world data reveals patterns you might have missed and allows you to set more accurate limits. If you discover that your dining-out budget consistently exceeds expectations, consider cooking at home more often or setting a weekly cap to keep the habit in check.

Reviewing and revising your budget should be a monthly habit rather than a one-time event. Life is dynamic: a raise, a new lease, a sudden medical expense, or a change in family size can all shift your financial landscape. By comparing your projected figures with actual outcomes each month, you can pinpoint where you're succeeding and where adjustments are needed. Small tweaks-like reallocating a few dollars from entertainment to an emergency fund-can have a cumulative impact over time.

Ultimately, budgeting is less about restriction and more about intentionality. When you consciously decide how each dollar will be used, you gain control over your financial future, reduce stress, and create space for the experiences and milestones that matter most. Whether you're just starting out or refining a long-standing plan, a disciplined yet adaptable approach to budgeting can turn vague aspirations into measurable progress.

raw:
budget laptops

Navigating the laptop market can feel overwhelming, especially when you're on a tight budget. The good news is that "budget laptop" no longer means sacrificing essential functionality. Modern affordable machines are surprisingly capable, perfectly suited for a wide array of everyday tasks without breaking the bank. These devices are designed for practicality, offering solid performance for students, remote workers, or anyone needing a reliable secondary computer.

However, it's crucial to set realistic expectations. A budget laptop isn't going to run the latest AAA games at ultra settings or render 4K video seamlessly. Their strength lies in handling web browsing, email, word processing, online learning, and streaming media with ease. If your primary use cases fall into these categories, then an inexpensive laptop could be an excellent, cost-effective solution.

When searching for a budget model, key specifications matter. Aim for at least 8GB of RAM if possible; while 4GB can function, it might lead to noticeable slowdowns when multitasking. For the processor, look for Intel Celeron or Pentium chips, or AMD's Ryzen 3 series. An older Intel Core i3 can also be a strong contender, offering a good balance of power and efficiency for the price point.

Storage type is another critical factor. Always prioritize a Solid State Drive (SSD) over a traditional Hard Disk Drive (HDD). Even a smaller 128GB or 256GB SSD will make a monumental difference in boot times and overall system responsiveness compared to a larger, slower HDD. Cloud storage or an external drive can easily supplement limited internal storage.

Consider the operating system too. While Windows 11 is standard, Chromebooks running ChromeOS present a compelling alternative in the budget sphere. They are generally more affordable, boot up incredibly fast, and are very secure, relying heavily on web-based applications. This makes them ideal for users whose workflow primarily revolves around web browsers and online services.

Major manufacturers like Acer, HP, Lenovo, and ASUS all offer robust budget lines, frequently featuring models under $500. Don't hesitate to compare prices across different retailers and keep an eye out for seasonal sales, which can often net you an even better deal on a surprisingly well-equipped machine.

Ultimately, a budget laptop is about smart compromises and maximizing value. By focusing on your core needs and understanding what specifications deliver the best performance for those tasks, you can find a capable and durable machine that feels far more expensive than it actually is. It's about being pragmatic, not settling.

Chou Yuan-chin

Chou Yuan-chin (Chinese: 周源卿; pinyin: Zhōu Yuánqīng; born August 22, 1954) is a Taiwanese nuclear scientist. He was the Minister of the Atomic Energy Council in the Executive Yuan from 1 February to 20 May 2016.

Chou was born in Taichung, Taiwan, on August 22, 1954. He graduated from National Tsing Hua University with a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) and a Master of Science (M.S.) in nuclear engineering in 1977 and 1979, respectively. He then completed doctoral studies in the United States, earning his Ph.D. in nuclear engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in 1988.

Chou had been an adjunct lecturer at the Department of Mechanical Engineering of Chung Cheng Institute of Technology in 1979-1981. In 1984-1985, he was the adjunct lecturer at the Department of Aerospace of Tamkang University and in 1991-1992 he was the adjunct associate professor at the Department of Mechanical Engineering of Chung Yuan Christian University.

raw:
Cypriot Super Cup

The Cypriot Super Cup is a Cypriot football trophy, contested in an annual match between the previous season's Cypriot First Division champions, and the Cypriot Cup winners. The match is contested at the beginning of the football season, and is usually played at the GSP Stadium in Nicosia. The most successful team in the competition are Omonia, who have won the trophy on 17 occasions. The current holders are Pafos who defeated Omonia 1-0 in the 2026 match.

The first match was played in 1951, under the name Pakkos Shield (Greek: Ασπίδα Πάκκου). At the time, the trophy was not awarded to the winner of the match, but would instead be awarded to the overall most successful team in the competition, after 10 matches. The Shield was finally awarded for the first time in 1967, to Çetinkaya, who were the first club to win the trophy three times. At the time, if the league champions and the Cup winners were the same team, they were automatically named winners of the Shield. Due to different circumstances, the competition wasn't held for 10 years, and returned in 1979 under the name Stylianakis Shield, in honor of the former president of the Cyprus Football Association. This name remained for 10 years, after which the Shield was awarded to Omonia, who won the trophy seven times in this time period. The competition was renamed as Cyprus Football Association Shield in 1989. From 2008 until 2013, the competition was held under the name LTV Super Cup, for sponsorship reasons. Since LTV's withdrawal as the competition's sponsor in 2014, the competition is simply called the Super Cup.

If a team wins the double (the Championship and the Cup in the same season), then this team plays the runners-up of the Cypriot Cup. Since 2013 if no winner is determined after 90 minutes, a penalty shootout takes place.

Following a decision by the Executive Committee of the Cyprus Football Association (CFA/KOP), upon the opinion of its legal advisor, on 19 June 2025, a request by AEK Larnaca was approved for the recognition of the titles of EPA Larnaca and Pezoporikos Larnaca in the name of AEK Larnaca. From 1951-1955, 1962-1963 & 1966-1968 it was called the Pakkos Shield. From 1979-1988 it was called the Stylianakis Shield. From 1989-2007 it was called the Cyprus FA Shield. From 2008-2013 it was called the LTV Super Cup. From 2013 onwards, its called the Super Cup.

raw:
Roby Norales

Roby made his National League debut for F.C. Motagua on 28 August 2011 under head coach Ramón Maradiaga against Platense F.C. His first goal came against C.D. Victoriaon 13 November the same year, where he went on to score 2 goals at the Estadio Nacional.

On 7 January 2017, Norales signed for Indian I-League champions, Bengaluru FC. However, after 4 games, he was loaned out to I-League 2nd division team Ozone FC. He scored only 1 goal with the club in the league.

He was summoned for the first time to the Honduras national team in August 2012 for matches against Cuba in 2014 World Cup Qualifiers. On 3 November 2016 he made his international debut in a friendly against Belize, coming on as a substitute in the 46th minute of the match. On 4 November 2016 he received a call by Jorge Luis Pinto for games against Panama and Trinidad and Tobago for the 2018 World Cup Qualifiers.

Born in Rio Esteban, a village 20 km from Balfate he came to San Pedro Sula in 2009 to play football and joined the youth team of F.C. Motagua. Honduras national team striker Romell Quioto is his cousin.

On 7 January 2017, Norales signed for Indian I-League champions, Bengaluru FC. However, after 4 games, he was loaned out to I-League 2nd division team Ozone FC. He scored only 1 goal with the club in the league.

He was summoned for the first time to the Honduras national team in August 2012 for matches against Cuba in 2014 World Cup Qualifiers. On 3 November 2016 he made his international debut in a friendly against Belize, coming on as a substitute in the 46th minute of the match. On 4 November 2016 he received a call by Jorge Luis Pinto for games against Panama and Trinidad and Tobago for the 2018 World Cup Qualifiers.

Born in Rio Esteban, a village 20 km from Balfate he came to San Pedro Sula in 2009 to play football and joined the youth team of F.C. Motagua. Honduras national team striker Romell Quioto is his cousin.

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to provide a concise yet detailed update on the current status of our joint research proposal for the National Science Foundation's Advanced Materials program. As we approach the final stages of preparation, I want to ensure that our team is fully aligned on the revised deadline, which has been moved up slightly due to administrative changes on the funder's end. The new submission date is now November 15th, which is three days earlier than we had originally scheduled. This change was communicated to us yesterday evening via the applicant portal, and I have updated the master calendar immediately to reflect this shift.
Given this compressed window, I recommend that we stop adding any new experimental data to the manuscript for the next forty-eight hours. Our focus should strictly be on editing, formatting, and ensuring compliance with the specific length limits outlined in the latest guidelines. I look forward to submitting a competitive and well-crafted proposal that gives us the best chance possible of securing this funding.
Best regards,
Alex Chen
Principal Investigator
Department of Engineering
