raw:
conference registration

Completing conference registration is often the first tangible step in professional development, yet it frequently invites confusion. Navigating the digital maze of tiered pricing, member discounts, and early bird deadlines requires a methodical approach to avoid unnecessary expenses. Most platforms require you to create an account before accessing the full catalog of sessions, workshops, and networking events. This initial login process ensures that your billing information and dietary preferences are recorded accurately for future events.

Timing is a critical factor in securing the best possible rate. Organizers typically structure their fee scales to reward early commitments, with the most significant discounts applying to registrations completed several months in advance. As the event date approaches, prices inevitably rise to cover increased logistical costs and to reflect higher demand. It is wise to set reminders for these specific cutoff dates to ensure you do not inadvertently pay the standard or last-minute premium.

Beyond the fiscal aspect, the registration process serves as a personalized setup for your conference experience. Many systems allow attendees to select general interests or professional goals, which helps curate a tailored agenda. This data enables organizers to suggest relevant workshops and manage room capacities more effectively. Taking the time to fill out these optional fields thoroughly can significantly enhance the value of your participation and help you identify key contacts before the main event begins.

If errors occur during payment or if details need updating after submission, do not hesitate to contact the conference help desk immediately. Most organizers have dedicated support teams who can resolve billing discrepancies or profile mistakes quickly, especially during the initial registration phase. Proactive communication prevents minor issues from evolving into major logistical headaches later on, ensuring your focus remains on networking and learning rather than administrative troubleshooting.

Finally, retain all confirmation emails and receipts for your personal records. These documents serve as valid proof of registration at check-in points and are essential for expense reports if your employer is covering the costs. Keeping a digital backup ensures that technical glitches at the venue gate do not delay your entry or disrupt your schedule. A smooth start to the event sets a positive tone for the days ahead, maximizing the return on your investment in professional growth.

Navigating the digital maze of tiered pricing, member discounts, and early bird deadlines requires a methodical approach to avoid unnecessary expenses. Most platforms require you to create an account before accessing the full catalog of sessions, workshops, and networking events. This initial login process ensures that your billing information and dietary preferences are recorded accurately for future events.
Timing is a critical factor in securing the best possible rate. Organizers typically structure their fee scales to reward early commitments, with the most significant discounts applying to registrations completed several months in advance. As the event date approaches, prices inevitably rise to cover increased logistical costs and to reflect higher demand. It is wise to set reminders for these specific cutoff dates to ensure you do not inadvertently pay the standard or last-minute premium.
Beyond the fiscal aspect, the registration process serves as a personalized setup for your conference experience. Many systems allow attendees to select general interests or professional goals, which helps curate a tailored agenda. This data enables organizers to suggest relevant workshops and manage room capacities more effectively. Taking the time to fill out these optional fields thoroughly can significantly enhance the value of your participation and help you identify key contacts before the main event begins.
If errors occur during payment or if details need updating after submission, do not hesitate to contact the conference help desk immediately. Most organizers have dedicated support teams who can resolve billing discrepancies or profile mistakes quickly, especially during the initial registration phase. Proactive communication prevents minor issues from evolving into major logistical headaches later on, ensuring your focus remains on networking and learning rather than administrative troubleshooting.
Finally, retain all confirmation emails and receipts for your personal records. These documents serve as valid proof of registration at check-in points and are essential for expense reports if your employer is covering the costs. Keeping a digital backup ensures that technical glitches at the venue gate do not delay your entry or disrupt your schedule. A smooth start to the event sets a positive tone for the days ahead, maximizing the return on your investment in professional growth.

Subject: Thoughts on the current budget laptop market
Hi Mark,
I hope you are having a productive week. I have been spending the last few days deep in the rabbit hole of researching affordable computing options for the junior staff members. It is interesting to see how much the landscape has shifted over the past eighteen months. We used to struggle significantly with finding machines that could handle basic multitasking without spending a fortune, but the recent influx of new hardware platforms has changed that calculation entirely. I wanted to share some findings from my investigation because I think we are at a pivotal moment for upgrading our fleet on a restricted budget.
The most notable change is the integration of artificial intelligence accelerators even in devices priced under six hundred dollars. These small neural processing units allow for faster local inference, which means everyday tasks like opening applications and switching between windows feel noticeably snappier. It is not a dramatic leap for heavy creative work, but for our administrative team, the responsiveness difference is tangible. They no longer have to wait for the system to catch up when moving from email to spreadsheets. This fluidity reduces friction in their daily workflow, which ultimately translates into better overall productivity without requiring a massive capital expenditure.
However, we must be selective about storage and memory configurations. The base models often come with just eight gigabytes of random access memory and two hundred fifty-six gigabytes of solid-state drive storage. While this is acceptable for light web browsing, it becomes a bottleneck if a user has multiple browser tabs open alongside specialized software. I strongly recommend targeting machines with at least sixteen gigabytes of memory. The price difference is usually minimal, often only fifty to eighty dollars more, but the longevity of the machine increases significantly. A slightly higher upfront cost now saves us the headache of early obsolescence during the three-year replacement cycle.
Battery life is another area where surprise performance improvements have occurred. Thanks to better power efficiency in the new chipsets, I have seen devices easily last a full workday without needing to be plugged in. This is crucial for our employees who often move between meeting rooms or work from hybrid locations. The older models we currently deploy require charging breaks, which disrupts their focus. Having a machine that stays powered throughout an eight-hour shift ensures continuity and removes the anxiety of dying batteries during important presentations or client calls.
Based on these observations, I suggest we standardize the next purchase order around two specific models that hit the sweet spot of price and performance. They offer the necessary robustness for our tier one users while staying well within the per-unit budget we have approved. I will prepare a detailed comparison sheet with exact pricing and warranty options for your review tomorrow morning. This strategy should allow us to refresh the entire department without exceeding our financial limits while providing a noticeable upgrade in user experience. I look forward to discussing this further at our next sync.
Best regards,
Alex Turner

Wanlip

Wanlip is a small village and civil parish in the Charnwood district of Leicestershire, with a population measured at 305 at the 2011 census. It is a countryside village, north of Birstall, and west of Watermead Country Park and the River Soar. The A46 road runs directly past the village. Wanlip won the 2008 Leicester and Rutland Best Village Competition for villages with a population under 500. To the south of Wanlip is Wanlip Meadows, a Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust nature reserve. To the north is a Severn Trent sewage treatment plant, serving a population of more than half a million. The Cedars Academy lies to the south at the edge of Birstall. To the east lies the 14 hectare Reedbed Local Nature Reserve, part of the Watermead Country Park. Wanlip is the site of a 132-metre-high wind turbine which went into operation at the end of 2013.

An Iron Age settlement was unearthed just to the north of Wanlip and an Anglo-Saxon cemetery was discovered during the building of Longslade School in 1958, One of the earliest mentions of Wanlip is in Domesday Book, where it is listed as Anelepe, among the lands given to Earl Aubrey by the King. The land described includes a mill. The Earl's son Aubrey de Vere II went on to become Lord Chancellor. The surnames of the three families who have owned the manor over eight centuries are:

Walsh 1230-1526 Aston 1526-1626 Palmer 1626-today William Wilberforce, the 19th century MP and leading abolitionist, lived for some years at Wanlip Hall. There are four listed buildings in Wanlip: a brick ice house, the church of Our Lady and St. Nicholas, Manor Farm and Hall Farm.

Much of the structure of this parish church was erected in the 13th and 14th centuries but there have been a variety of later alterations, including changes made in the 19th century and the south aisle which was built in 1904. The walls are constructed mainly of granite rubble with ashlar dressing. It is a Grade II listed building. The chancel floor is notable for housing the brass that commemorates Sir Thomas Walsh and his wife Katherine. This comprises the figures of the couple with a border that is the earliest surviving example of an English inscription for a high-status tomb monument. The inscription reads:

"Here lyes Thomas Walssh knyght lorde of Anlep and dame Katine his wife whiche in her tyme made the kirke of Anlep and halud the kirkyerd first in Wurchip of god and of oure lady and seynt Nicholas that god have her soules and mercy anno domini millesimo CCC nonagesimo tercio [i.e. 1393]." The memorial is the subject of a detailed article by Nigel Saul, who commented that the church is a distinguished building incorporating motifs from the state apartments at Kenilworth Castle that had been commissioned by John of Gaunt, with whom Sir Thomas Walsh was closely connected. In the churchyard is a substantial headstone with the following epitaph: "Sacred to the memory of Rasselas Morjan, who was born at Macadi on the confines of Abyssinia and died at Wanlip Hall August 25th 1839 in the 19th year of his age. Rescued from a state of slavery in this life and enabled by God's grace to become a member of his Church he rests here in the hope of a greater deliverance hereafter. This stone is raised in remembrance of his blameless life by one whom he loved."

Wanlip is said to be unusual because in 1906 the land there was all owned by just one family - the Palmers. The Baronetcy at Wanlip has been held by the (later named Palmer) family since 1791 when it was awarded to Charles Grave Hudson. Notable members of the family include the artist Caroline Harriet Abraham and her father Charles Thomas Hudson Palmer, 2nd Baronet. Charles Palmer-Tomkinson, father of socialite Tara Palmer-Tomkinson, is a landowner in Wanlip and Birstall, responsible for the Hallam Fields development in next-door Birstall. The current holder of the baronetcy is Sir John Edward Somerset Palmer, 8th baronet.

Jon Harley

Jon Harley (born 26 September 1979) is an English professional football coach and former player. He is assistant manager of EFL Championship club Portsmouth. A left-back, he played for Chelsea and Fulham in the Premier League, Wimbledon, Sheffield United, West Ham United, Burnley, Watford, Notts County Rotherham United and Portsmouth in the Football League, and in the Isthmian League for Maidstone United.

Born in Maidstone, Kent, Harley grew up in the Maidstone suburb of Allington, attending Oakwood Park Grammar School and playing for the local junior team Castle Colts.

Harley started his career with Chelsea, making his debut against Derby County in April 1998. Despite some impressive performances, especially in the 1999-2000 season, during which he was a member of Chelsea's FA Cup winning squad, albeit as an unused substitute in the final, he was unable to establish himself in the London side. He ultimately made 42 appearances for Chelsea and scored two goals, both of which were winners in the 1999-2000 FA Premier League against future club Watford and Leeds United. He also had a loan spell with Wimbledon, where he scored twice, both goals coming in a 4-0 win over Crewe Alexandra on his debut. In his final season at Chelsea, Harley was third choice behind Celestine Babayaro and Graeme Le Saux.

He signed for newly promoted Fulham in August 2001 for £3.5million. Harley was equally unable to establish himself in the Fulham side, despite a somewhat outstanding goal against Aston Villa, in which he beat Peter Enckelman with a 40-yard strike. This was the only goal he achieved in 19 league starts over three seasons. He joined Sheffield United and later West Ham United on loan where he scored once, in a 3-3 draw against Sheffield United on his debut.

A year later he moved to Burnley in a deal for just £75,000 initially, with further payments linked to first-team appearances. Harley managed to establish himself as the club's first choice left-back, starting with a series of impressive performances. He is known for his attacking intent and often gets forward to offer support down the left-wing. Harley is also an excellent set-piece taker and was vital to many of Burnley's free-kick 'routines'. Despite his ability his form dipped mid-season, but later recovered to end the campaign with a number of solid performances, culminating in his winning the "Player of the Season" award. He remained almost ever-present during his second season with Burnley. At the start of the 2007-08 season, Harley found himself playing in the unaccustomed position of left-sided midfielder or on the bench, replaced by new signing Stephen Jordan. An injury to Jordan allowed him to regain his place and this coincided with a run of much-improved results for Burnley. On 9 March 2008, however, Harley failed to agree a new deal with Burnley, signalling his intent to leave the club during the following summer.

On 17 July 2008 Harley signed a two-year deal with Watford. On 4 October 2008 he scored his first Watford league goal, scoring in the 12th minute in a home game against Preston North End. Watford went on to win the game 2-1.

On 14 July 2010, Harley signed for the Football League Two Champions Notts County on a two-year deal and established himself as a regular member of the team in the 2010-11 season. In September 2011 he turned out for Australian A-League side Melbourne Victory in a bid to win a full-time contract, the move, however, fell through. In October 2011, he joined League Two side Rotherham United on a one-month emergency loan, which was then extended in November to last until January 2012. In May 2012 he was released by the club, along with 12 other players.

On 16 August 2012, Harley signed for League One club Portsmouth on a short-term contract. Harley made his debut in a League One match against AFC Bournemouth, the match ended 1-1. He scored his only goal for Portsmouth in a 2-1 defeat away to Stevenage on 24 October 2012. He was released alongside five other players on 15 January 2013.

Raise.com

Raise.com is an e-commerce platform owned and operated by Raise that enables third-party individuals to sell Gift Cards on a fixed-price online marketplace alongside Raise's regular offerings. The company is based in Chicago, Illinois, and was launched in 2013 by founder George Bousis, who still remains the Executive Chairman and CEO.

Raise.com was initially conceived as a spinoff of another service created by Bousis and Bradley Wasz, called CouponTrade, which was founded in 2010. Since that time, the marketplace became more amenable to Bousis' idea. As stated by Crain's Chicago Business column, "a 2009 federal law prevented gift cards from expiring for five years; cards went from a magnetic stripe to all-digital in 2010; and advances in mobile technology made it possible to buy and sell cards on a smartphone." It was founded in 2013, with $18 million in funding from Bessemer Venture Funding. It received $56 million from New Enterprise Associates in 2015. In 2015, Raise.com acquired Tastebud Technologies for an undisclosed amount. Its CEO, Tyler Spalding, became chief strategy officer at Raise. In June 2016, Raise acquired Slide for an undisclosed amount in stock, a company which allows people to store gift cards in a digital wallet/passbook. Raise also announced plans to open a New York office. As of 2016, the company was valued at about $1 billion by the New York Times. In late 2018, Raise appointed a new CEO, Jay Klauminzer, who had been an executive at Groupon and DoorDash.

Raise.com takes a 12% cut from the sale of every gift card. In the period between funding - in 2014, Raise.com released a mobile app (iOS only) version of its marketplace. Raise.com also has partnerships with "over a dozen undisclosed retailers so far who are interested in the sorts [of] consumer shopping insights Raise can provide." Raise has a one-year money back guarantee on purchases made directly through the marketplace.

Some users of Raise.com have experienced gift card fraud, typically executed by people who steal items under the return receipt requirements of stores and then requesting gift cards. Generally, customer service regarding fraudulent gift cards receives minimal complaints, and most receive a 100%+ refund. As AdvisoryHQ states, "Many of the negative Raise reviews on this review site are from buyers who waited until after Raise's 100-day money back guarantee had expired before trying to use their gift card - only to discover that the card was invalid or had a different value than expected."

Mike Sandbothe (born June 26, 1961) is a German intellectual, philosopher and professor of culture and media at University of Applied Sciences Jena. He is co-founder of the new branch of media philosophy and one of the main proponents of philosophical pragmatism in Europe. He held professorships for Media Culture Studies at Friedrich Schiller University Jena as well as for Media Philosophy at Berlin University of the Arts and at Aalborg University Copenhagen. The certified trainer in Mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) is one of the two founders of the German Network of Mindful Universities "Achtsame Hochschulen". Among his various English publications are The Temporalization of Time (2001; German 1998), The Pragmatic Turn (2004), Pragmatic Media Philosophy (2005; in German: 2001), and From Pragmatist Philosophy to Cultural Politics (2013). His most recent work deals with the topics "Mindful Universities", "Healthy Teaching and Learning", and "Pragmatism as Cultural Politics". Since 2020, he is member of the Erasmus+ Program Training Embodied Critical Thinking. He lives in Erfurt with his wife and children.

The editorial team has finalized the new protocol for evaluating tabletop titles. This update aims to standardize our scoring methodology to ensure consistency across all publications. By aligning our criteria, we provide readers with reliable insights that reflect the actual gameplay experience rather than surface-level aesthetics.

Each review must now include a minimum of two full playthroughs of the recommended duration. This requirement helps identify whether the mechanics remain engaging after the initial novelty wears off. We need to assess both the learning curve and the replay value objectively, noting any friction points that might deter casual groups from picking up the box again.

Mechanical clarity will receive a higher weight in the final score. Games that rely on dense rulebooks without clear visual aids will be critiqued more strictly. We recognize that ease of setup and rule comprehension significantly impacts the modern consumer's willingness to return to the table for future sessions.

Visual components are still important but are no longer the primary driver of the rating. A stunning piece of plastic cannot compensate for poor game design or confusing victory conditions. Our focus shifts back to the strategic depth and social interaction that define a truly excellent tabletop experience.

Internal memos are no longer guaranteed a priority slot unless they meet the same quality thresholds as external releases. Fairness is essential to maintaining the trust of our subscriber base. All senior editors must review the attached checklist before submitting their final verdicts to the production department for upcoming print cycles.

lab safety rules

When stepping into any laboratory, safety becomes as essential as the experiment itself. A single overlooked precaution can turn a routine procedure into a hazardous incident, jeopardizing health, research data, and costly equipment. Understanding and following core safety rules is therefore mandatory.

Personal protective equipment, often abbreviated as PPE, forms the first line of defense. Lab coats, safety goggles, gloves, and closed-toe shoes must be worn before touching any reagents, and they should be inspected for damage before each use.

Chemical containers should be clearly labeled, and the material safety data sheet must be consulted prior to handling. Never mix substances unless the protocol permits it, and work within a fume hood when volatile vapors are expected.

Equipment must be used only after proper training, and any malfunction should be reported immediately. Emergency equipment-eyewash stations, safety showers, fire extinguishers, and first-aid kits-should be located at eye level and checked regularly for operability.

Disposal of waste follows guidelines; hazardous chemicals go into designated containers, while biological materials require autoclaving before discard. Never pour chemicals down the sink unless the protocol confirms they are harmless to plumbing and the environment.

Finally, a culture of safety thrives on communication. Encourage colleagues to speak up about unsafe conditions, attend regular refresher courses, and keep a personal log of incidents. A vigilant, informed team reduces risk and sustains scientific progress.

Heinrich Wilhelm Ferdinand Wackenroder

In June, 1826 Wackenroder published his doctoral dissertation, "On Anthelminthics in the Vegetable Kingdom," presented to Göttingen University, which earned him praise, and the Royal Prize. In 1827 he obtained his doctorate from the University of Erlangen, becoming an associate professor the following year at the University of Jena, where he worked with Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner (1780-1849). In 1829, he re-established the Pharmacy Institute in Jena (founded 1821) with Friedrich Wilhelm Theile and Prof. Wahl. In 1836, he was appointed Director of the Pharmacy Institute, later known as the Chemical-Pharmaceutical Institute. In 1838 he was appointed as an honorary Professor ordinarius at the university. He became especially known for his discovery of carotin and his correspondence with Goethe. In subsequent years he became co-editor of Archiv der Pharmazie. In 1826 Wackenroder isolated corydalin from Corydalis cava and in 1831 isolated carotin in an ether extract from carrots. In 1845 he discovered the Wackenroder solution, a polythionic acid, resulting from the reaction of aqueous sulphur dioxide with hydrogen sulphide.

Subject: Updated Schedule and Screening Updates for the Autumn Festival
Dear colleagues and partners,
I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to finalize the official screening schedule for this year's Autumn Film Festival. After several intensive review sessions with the curatorial team, we have locked in the final order of features, shorts, and documentary blocks. Please consider the attached PDF as the definitive source for all programming details, as previous drafts contained minor timing errors that have now been corrected.
The main stage at the Civic Center will host the opening gala on Thursday evening. We have secured two prestigious international premieres for that night, which should generate significant momentum for the remaining week. Subject: Inquiry regarding availability for Saturday, October 14, 2026
Dear Events Coordinator,
My name is Sarah Jenkins, and I am writing to you today to inquire about the availability of your venue for our upcoming wedding. We have fallen absolutely in love with the ambiance of your historic estate after spending a few hours there last weekend, and we believe it is the perfect setting for the special day we have been planning for the past year. The combination of the elegant ballroom and the expansive garden spaces truly captured our attention and inspired our vision for this event. We are eager to know if the date we have in mind is still open for booking, as we are looking to secure a location as soon as possible to begin the detailed planning process with confidence.
We are anticipating a guest list of approximately one hundred and twenty people for the ceremony itself, with the reception following immediately afterward in your main hall. Given that our family and close friends are traveling from various parts of the country, we were hoping to book the facility for the entire day, roughly from ten in the morning until midnight. This extended timeline would allow us to have professional photography sessions in the gardens during the golden hour, provide a leisurely lunch for the bridal party, and then transition into the formal reception without feeling rushed or constrained by time limits.
I would also appreciate any information you could provide regarding your all-inclusive packages for this capacity. We are particularly interested in knowing if there are any restrictions on outside caterers or if you have preferred vendors with whom you work closely. We are open to suggestions for both food and beverage services, as long as the quality matches the high standard of the venue itself. Additionally, could you please let us know if there are any additional fees for setting up a live band, or if we are required to use one of your on-site audio-visual providers? We have a strong preference for live music and want to ensure we are in compliance with all local noise ordinances and venue guidelines regarding decibel levels during the evening reception.
There are a few specific logistical details that are important to our family. We have two elderly relatives who require wheelchair access to all areas of the venue, including the restroom facilities and the main dining area. We were hoping to confirm that your property is fully accessible and that there is a designated parking space near the entrance for those with mobility challenges. Furthermore, we are curious about your climate control capabilities within the indoor spaces, as October can sometimes be unpredictable in terms of temperature. We want to ensure that our guests will be comfortable throughout the evening, regardless of whether the weather turns chilly or remains mild.
Please let me know if you are available for a brief phone call next week to discuss these points in more detail. I would love to speak with someone who can walk us through the contract terms and any tentative scheduling options. We are ready to move forward quickly if the date is confirmed, and we have our budget approved for the venue deposit. Thank you very much for your time and assistance in this matter. We truly hope that this could be the start of a wonderful partnership with your team to make our wedding day a memorable and seamless experience for everyone involved. I look forward to hearing from you soon.
Sincerely,
Sarah Jenkins

Subject: Updated Remote Work Policy Effective July 1
Dear Team,
I'm writing to share the revised remote-work policy that will take effect on July 1. After reviewing feedback from the recent employee survey and evaluating our operational needs, we have refined the guidelines to provide clearer expectations while maintaining the flexibility many of you value. This update aims to balance productivity, collaboration, and work-life integration, ensuring that both the company's objectives and individual circumstances are respected.
Under the new policy, all employees may work remotely up to three days per week, provided that their role is designated as "eligible for remote work." Managers will confirm eligibility during one-on-one meetings and will outline any role-specific requirements, such as core-hour availability or on-site presence for client meetings. When a remote day is scheduled, you are expected to be reachable via company chat and email during the standard business hours of 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. local time, and to attend any required video calls promptly.
To support seamless collaboration, we are introducing a shared "Remote Days Calendar" in Outlook where you can log your planned remote work days. This will help teammates coordinate in-person activities, such as brainstorming sessions or equipment checks, without unnecessary overlap. Additionally, we ask that you maintain a dedicated, secure workspace at home and use the company-provided VPN for all work-related network access. If you encounter any technical issues, the IT help desk remains available to assist during regular business hours.
We also want to emphasize the importance of performance tracking. Each quarter, managers will conduct brief check-ins to discuss output, challenges, and any adjustments needed to your remote schedule. These conversations are not punitive; they are intended to identify support opportunities and to ensure that team goals remain on track. Should you need additional resources-such as ergonomic equipment, software licenses, or training-please submit a request through the usual internal portal, and we will prioritize fulfillment.
Thank you for your continued commitment to excellence and for adapting to the evolving work environment. We believe these refinements will empower you to deliver your best work while enjoying the benefits of remote flexibility. If you have any questions or concerns about the new policy, please reach out to your manager or to HR directly. We look forward to a smooth transition and to seeing the positive impact of these changes across the organization.
Best regards,
Jordan Patel 
Director of People Operations 
Company XYZ

The Annual Office Greenery Maintenance Protocol

Effective immediately, all employees in the Downtown and Suburban branches are required to adhere to the updated guidelines for maintaining our office houseplants. These adjustments are mandated by the Facilities Management team to ensure the health of our indoor ecosystem and to minimize resource consumption. Previous informal care routines have led to uneven watering practices and significant pest issues in the Q3 fiscal quarter. This memo supersedes all prior verbal instructions regarding plant husbandry. Please review the following standards carefully and distribute this information to relevant departmental leads.

Watering schedules must now be strictly regulated by soil moisture rather than fixed calendar dates. Staff should utilize the finger test, inserting a clean finger one inch into the soil near the pot rim. Only when the top inch of substrate is completely dry should the plant receive water. Overwatering remains the primary cause of plant loss in our facilities, leading to root rot and subsequent odor issues. Please refrain from using small decorative bowls to catch excess water, as stagnant reservoirs breed mosquitoes and fungal spores. Use only room-temperature tap water that has been allowed to sit for at least twenty-four hours to dissipate chlorine levels.

Lighting requirements vary by species and location within the office layout. North-facing windows and deep interior zones are suitable for low-light tolerant species such as Pothos and Snake Plants. High-light varieties like Fiddle Leaf Figs and Monstera should be rotated weekly to ensure even growth and prevent stretching toward the nearest light source. Avoid direct afternoon sun on glass-enclosed panes, as heat buildup can scorch leaves. If a plant begins to yellow or develop brown edges, assess its proximity to air conditioning vents and adjust its position immediately before attempting other interventions.

Pest control is a shared responsibility among all staff members. During your weekly inspections, check the undersides of leaves for white flakes, webbing, or sticky residue. Upon detection of any infestation, isolate the affected pot in the designated quarantine bin located outside the main lobby entrance. Do not dispose of infested plants in the common recycling bins. Contact Facilities at extension 4402 for professional treatment. Early detection is critical, as mealybugs and spider mites spread rapidly in a high-density office environment. Regular wiping of leaf surfaces with a damp cloth helps remove dust and deters aphid colonization.

Non-compliance with these protocols may result in the removal of compromised plants without prior notice. The Facilities team will conduct random audits on the first and third Tuesdays of each month to verify adherence to these standards. Employees who have purchased personal plants for their workstations are also subject to these rules. Ensure that all personal pots have adequate drainage holes and are placed on waterproof saucers. Proper plant care contributes to air quality, reduces stress levels, and enhances the overall aesthetic of our professional environment. Thank you for your cooperation in maintaining a healthy and welcoming workplace.

raw:
Ernest L. Ransome

.

Ernest Leslie Ransome (1844-1917) was an English-born engineer, architect, and early innovator in reinforced concrete building techniques. Ransome devised the most sophisticated concrete structures in the United States at the time. Ernest was the son of Frederick Ransome, who had patented a process for producing artificial stone in 1844. Ernest was apprenticed to his father's factory in Ipswich. By the 1870s Ernest had moved to the USA and was the superintendent of the Pacific Stone Company in San Francisco. In 1884 after experimenting with reinforced concrete sidewalks, he patented (U.S. patent 305,226) a system of ferro-concrete with the iron rods twisted to improve the bond, then developed a patented Ransome system for practical reinforced concrete construction. In 1886 Ransome built two small underpass bridges in the Golden Gate Park in San Francisco which survive today, and which are the first reinforced concrete bridges in North America, and among the first three or four in the world. After a long string of accomplishments Ransome continued to meet with skepticism and resistance. His techniques were vindicated when his 1897 Pacific Coast Borax Refinery in Bayonne, NJ in 1902 went through a massive building fire hot enough to melt brass; the concrete frame was only slightly damaged and thereby concrete framed industrial architecture was shown to have a key superiority over competing steel and iron framed structures.

The Pacific Coast Borax fire was, it appears, the triumph and vindication of Ransome's professional life. That Company's building at Bayonne, erected in 1897, had been his first work on the East Coast and is also reputedly the first complete reinforced concrete factory to be erected on that side of the country. The fire and Ransome's great and growing reputation as an inventor and constructor combined to give a kind of charisma to reinforced concrete as the material of the new industrial age; and Ransome was only one of a number of forceful new engineering personalities who appeared upon the scene as exponents and exploiters of this miraculous seemingly material. Likewise Ransome's two experimental buildings at Stanford survived the 1906 San Francisco earthquake essentially without damage while the university's newer, conventional brick structures literally crumbled around them. The published analysis of these two buildings by fellow engineer John B. Leonard did much to advance the safety of buildings in post-1906 San Francisco and nationwide. In his later career Ransome focused on mixing equipment, formwork, and integrated building systems. In 1912 Ransome and Alexis Saurbrey co-authored Reinforced Concrete Buildings. One of Ransome's sons was the notable American geologist Frederick Leslie Ransome (1868-1935).

Arctic Oil Works, San Francisco, 1884, the "first reinforced concrete building (of its kind) in the United States". Pacific Coast Borax Refinery, Alameda, California, 1889 Alvord Lake Bridge, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, 1889, the first reinforced concrete bridge built in the United States Torpedo Assembly Building, eastern end of Yerba Buena Island, San Francisco, 1891 Berkeley Apartments (Buffalo, New York), Buffalo, New York, 1894-1897 Pacific Coast Borax Refinery - first phase, Bayonne, New Jersey, 1897 Pacific Coast Borax Refinery - second phase, Bayonne, New Jersey, 1903 Japanese Bridge at Francis Marion Smith's estate Presdeleau, still visible at 24 Merkel Lane Shelter Island, New York four city reservoirs at Mount Tabor and Washington Park, Portland, Oregon, 1894-1911 Roble Hall (women's dormitory) at Stanford University, 1891, renamed Sequoia Hall in 1917 (razed) The Leland Stanford Junior Museum of Art (now the Iris & B. Gerald Cantor Center for Visual Arts), at Stanford University, 1894 United Shoe factory buildings, Beverly, Massachusetts, 1902 Ingalls Building, Cincinnati, Ohio, 1903

raw:
dormitory rules

Living in a dormitory presents a unique set of social and logistical challenges that differ significantly from living with a long-term roommates or in a private apartment. The primary rule of dorm life is mutual respect, which manifests in countless small interactions throughout the day. You are not just sharing a room; you are sharing a limited amount of quiet, personal space, and cleanliness. Understanding that your roommate is also trying to balance a heavy course load, social obligations, and basic life maintenance helps foster the empathy needed to navigate conflicts before they arise.

Quiet hours are perhaps the most strictly enforced regulation in most residential halls, typically beginning around ten PM. This is not merely a suggestion but a necessity for the academic success of the entire population. Noise does not always mean loud music or shouting; it includes the sound of phone calls, video gaming headsets, or aggressive cleaning. If you find yourself needing to sleep during the day because of an early morning lecture, you must be mindful that your use of a white noise machine or heavy blinds does not imply you can demand silence at the expense of your roommate's evening relaxation. Negotiating a flexible schedule for specific days, like exam weeks, is often more effective than rigid adherence to a calendar that does not suit both parties.

Maintenance of common areas is another critical aspect of dormitory living. Unlike a private home where one person might take charge of household chores, dorms require a shared commitment to cleanliness. This means that if you prepare food in the communal kitchen, you are responsible for washing your dishes immediately after use. Leaving dirty pots in the sink or leaving crumbs on shared tables creates an environment that breeds pests and resentment. A simple agreement to take turns cleaning shared spaces, such as the bathroom or the living room, can prevent the slow accumulation of mess that makes living together unpleasant.

Guest policies are often misunderstood and strictly monitored by university authorities. Most dorms have specific windows where visitors are allowed and distinct rules about how long they may stay. Overnight guests frequently require prior approval or a signed affidavit, and exceeding these limits can lead to formal warnings or even disciplinary action. It is crucial to respect the privacy of your neighbors as well as your roommate. If a friend is visiting, keep voices down and ensure they do not wander into hallways or other residents' rooms without permission.

Finally, safety is the underlying framework for all dormitory rules. Fire safety regulations, such as banning open flames, certain types of electrical appliances, or blocking emergency exits, are non-negotiable. These rules exist to protect lives, and bypassing them puts the entire community at risk. Respect for these safety protocols is a baseline expectation for any resident. By internalizing these guidelines and treating them with the seriousness they deserve, you contribute to a secure and functional living environment for everyone.

raw:
library book return

Returning a library book may seem like a simple task, but a smooth process can make a big difference in keeping the shelves organized and the community happy. When you walk into the library, the first thing you'll notice is the clearly marked return area-usually a row of sturdy bins or a self-service kiosk. These stations are designed for quick drops, so the staff can focus on shelving, programming, and helping patrons find new reads. By understanding the basics of the return system, you help the whole library run more efficiently.

Most libraries accept books any day of the week during opening hours, and many also offer after-hours drop boxes. If you're unsure of the exact times, a quick glance at the library's website or a posted schedule will tell you when the doors are open for returns. Even if a book is overdue, returning it promptly reduces any late fees and frees up the title for the next borrower. Some branches even waive fines for a limited period, encouraging patrons to bring books back without fear of penalty.

When you place a book in the return bin, the staff's workflow usually begins with an automated scanner that reads the barcode and updates the patron's account in real time. The system notes the exact return time, calculates any fines, and flags the item for reshelving. For high-traffic libraries, this technology speeds up the process and minimizes human error. If the book is part of a series or a special collection, staff may handle it separately to ensure it's placed in the correct location on the shelf.

If you're returning a large item, such as a DVD, a reference volume, or a book with a protective cover, look for the designated return slot that accommodates its size. Some libraries have separate bins for media, ensuring that fragile items are not damaged by heavier books. When you're uncertain where to drop a particular item, a friendly librarian at the circulation desk can point you in the right direction and answer any questions you might have about borrowing limits or upcoming holds.

Finally, consider the benefits of using a library's online portal to check the status of your return. Many systems send an email confirmation once a book is processed, giving you peace of mind that the transaction is complete. If you notice a discrepancy-perhaps a book still shows as checked out-a quick call or chat with the library staff can resolve the issue before it turns into a fine. By staying informed and taking a few simple steps, you help the library maintain a vibrant, well-stocked collection for everyone in the community.

Executive Order 13303

Executive Order 13303 was issued on May 22, 2003, by United States President George W. Bush to protect the Development Fund for Iraq for the rebuilding of Iraq from any legal attachments or liens. Further, it protects Iraqi oil products and interests and ownership by US persons (defined to include US corporations) from attachment as well. Executive Order 13303 also terminates sanctions specified in EO 12722, EO 12724, EO 13290, as it applies to the development fund. In effect, EO 13303 provides an extraordinarily broad legal shield for any and all contractors and mercenaries working in Iraq on behalf of US corporations in any oil related enterprise. The Executive Order also declares a national emergency to deal with the threat to a peaceful reconstruction of Iraq, which US Presidents have renewed every year since, most recently in May 2026. The order's full title is Executive Order Protecting the Development Fund for Iraq and Certain Other Property in Which Iraq Has An Interest.

The primary effect of EO 13303 is the legal protection of US oil companies. EO 13303 is part of a broader endeavor by the Bush administration to exert control over Iraqi oil revenues. The plan centers on the Development Fund for Iraq, created by the United Nations and nominally controlled by the United States, with advice from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The second part of the plan is EO 13303, providing absolute legal protection for US interests in Iraqi oil.

The Arizona Law Review published an essay discussing the unconstitutionality of the order, citing Dames & Moore v. Regan as limiting the power of executive orders such as this. Critics of EO 13303 contend new debt for Iraq will accrue from the new Development Fund for Iraq. They say that it will allow opportunities for grave abuses because it offers little illuminating context and its tone suggests the language should be read quite broadly. These concerns stem from the apparent likelihood the fund will be used to leverage US government and corporate interests. The United Nations Security Council approved Resolution 1483 on May 22, 2003, ending economic sanctions against Iraq while clearing a path for the transfer of over US$1 billion from the Oil-for-Food program as seed money for establishment of the development fund. Dear Alex,
I wanted to confirm the details for the bike repair you scheduled for Thursday morning. We'll have a technician ready at 9:30 am to take a look at the drivetrain you mentioned. Looking forward to getting your bike back in top shape. Please reply if the time works for you or if you have any other concerns.
Best regards,
Jordan Patel
Customer Service Manager
CycleWorks Repair Shop

raw:
houseplant care

.

Keeping houseplants thriving is less about fancy gadgets and more about understanding the basic needs that each green friend shares. Light, water, soil, and temperature form the quartet of factors that dictate whether a plant will flourish or wilt. While some species can tolerate dim corners and occasional neglect, most thrive when they receive a steady routine that mimics their natural environment. Start by observing the light patterns in your home: a south-facing window offers bright, direct sun, while a north-facing one provides gentle, indirect illumination. Choose plants that match those conditions, and you'll reduce stress from the very first day.

Watering is often the most common source of error for beginners. The rule of thumb is to let the top inch of soil dry out before the next drink, but the exact timing varies with species, pot size, and ambient humidity. Overwatering can suffocate roots, leading to root rot, while underwatering causes wilting and leaf browning. A simple finger test-pressing the soil with your fingertip-gives a reliable sense of moisture levels without the need for expensive meters. When you do water, aim for a thorough soak so excess drains from the bottom, ensuring the entire root ball receives moisture.

Soil composition plays a silent but crucial role. A well-draining mix prevents water from pooling and keeps roots aerated. Commercial potting blends tailored for specific plant types-such as cactus mix for succulents or orchid bark for epiphytes-provide the right balance of aeration and water retention. If you're repotting, gently loosen the old soil, shake off excess, and place the plant at the same depth it previously occupied. Over-potting, or using a pot that's too large, can retain unnecessary water and stress the roots.

Temperature and humidity are often overlooked, especially in homes with central heating or air conditioning. Most tropical houseplants prefer daytime temperatures between 65 and 75 degrees Fahrenheit and a modest drop at night. Sudden drafts or proximity to heating vents can cause leaf scorch. To boost humidity for ferns, peace lilies, and similar species, place a shallow tray of water nearby, group plants together, or use a pebble tray. Misting can help briefly, but it should not replace proper watering.

Lastly, keep an eye out for pests and disease. Tiny insects like spider mites, mealybugs, and aphids can appear on new leaves or at the base of stems. Early detection-tiny webs, sticky residue, or discolored spots-lets you intervene with gentle solutions such as neem oil or a mild soap spray. Regularly wiping leaves with a damp cloth not only removes dust that blocks photosynthesis but also gives you a chance to spot problems before they spread. With attentive care and a bit of observation, your indoor garden will reward you with cleaner air, brighter spaces, and a satisfying sense of growth.

The 2024 season for the Riverside Community Garden is officially open as of this morning. All long-term leaseholders must complete their annual bed cleaning by next Friday. This task is mandatory and cannot be delegated to volunteers. Each plot holder is responsible for removing compostable debris from their designated bed and depositing it in the central compost bins. Non-compostable items, including plastic plant pots, irrigation hose fragments, and synthetic landscape fabric, must be removed from the site entirely and recycled or disposed of according to city waste regulations. Failure to clear your bed by the deadline may result in a temporary suspension of water access privileges. This measure ensures that the shared infrastructure remains functional and sanitary for all members during the growing season.

Water access remains restricted to early morning hours between 6:00 AM and 9:00 AM daily. This timeframe has proven effective in reducing evaporation rates and minimizing conflicts among gardeners. We have noticed an increase in usage during midday hours in recent weeks, which places unnecessary stress on the municipal connection pressure. Please adhere strictly to these hours. If you find a valve left open or a line kinked after your allotted time, please close it or straighten the line immediately. Do not leave hoses running unattended or while you are visiting neighboring plots. The irrigation infrastructure is shared property, and its longevity depends on the conscientious use of every individual member.

Regarding the central tool shed, we are implementing a new registration system to track usage and prevent loss. Beginning next week, all tools must be signed out at the community office before entering the shed. A simple paper logbook will be available at the entrance. Please write your name, phone number, and the specific item taken. Tools must be returned cleaned and dry by the end of the day. Persistent failure to return equipment or returning tools in a damaged, dirty state may restrict access to the shed for up to thirty days. This change is necessary to maintain the inventory and ensure that essential implements remain available for those who need them most during peak planting periods.

A revision to the composting protocol is also in effect immediately. No meat, dairy, or oily foods will be accepted in the community compost piles. These materials attract pests and create odors that have caused complaints from nearby residential properties. Only green waste, dry leaves, and approved yard trimmings are permitted. Additionally, we ask that you shred large branches into small pieces before adding them to the pile. This accelerates the decomposition process and improves the quality of the finished compost. The manager will be conducting spot checks on the compost station twice a week. Non-compliant materials will be removed and the plot owner will be notified of the violation. Cooperative adherence to these guidelines is essential for maintaining good neighborly relations with the surrounding community.

Finally, please note that the community meeting scheduled for the first Saturday of the month is moved to the outdoor pavilion due to expected high occupancy. Attendance is strongly encouraged for all leaseholders. Judgement Day (2013 film)

Judgement Day (Chinese: 世界末日) is a 2013 Singaporean comedy-drama disaster film written and directed by Ong Kuo Sin and produced by Mark Lee. Starring an ensemble cast, the film follows various characters from different backgrounds confessing to their wrongdoings and revealing their biggest secrets just 72 hours from what is believed to be "Judgement Day". It was released on April 18, 2013. Judgement Day marks John Cheng's final feature film role before his death on January 21, 2013.

With about 72 hours left to spend before "Judgement Day" supposedly arrives, various individuals start spilling out their greatest secrets. The film opens with a news report broadcast to Singapore that scientists have discovered a meteorite heading straight for earth and that there was only 72 hours left to live. Upon hearing this, Henry Thia's character tells his family that his last death wish was to become a woman, so he goes for MTF surgery to do this. We then follow the story of how his children are ridiculed in school for having two "mothers". In the end of the 72 hours, we are shown a scene of people at their HDB corridors looking out at the sky, bracing for impact. The meteorite whirls down from space; however, the meteorite burns out into a small stone which hits a boy squarely in the forehead for comedic effect. The people rejoice; however, scientists break the mood and report that another meteorite, which was ten times larger and sure to destroy earth, was coming. The film ends.

Mark Lee as a police officer. Henry Thia as Liu Fu An, a man who decides to change his gender. Chua Enlai as Richard Rebecca Lim as Rebecca, Richard's girlfriend Guo Liang Edwin Goh Julie Tan as Xiao Lu, a prostitute with AIDS Lawrence Wong as Ah Song Sebestian Tan as a car salesman. Tender Huang as Taiwanese man Ko Chia-yen as Li Shuzhen John Cheng as medium Uncle Jiu. Adrian Pang as Prime Minister Dr Ang

The original release date in Singapore was put forth as "May 2013" in an earlier teaser poster; this has since been changed to April 18, 2013.

Subject: Update on Inpatient Visiting Protocols
Dear Inpatient Families,
We are writing to inform you of important changes to our current hospital visiting hours effective immediately. These adjustments are part of our ongoing commitment to balancing patient safety with the emotional support necessary for recovery. We understand that visiting times are a critical component of the healing process for those in our care. However, we must also maintain strict infection control measures and ensure adequate rest periods for our patients. Please review the new schedule carefully to plan your visits accordingly and minimize any disruptions to their care routines.
The standard visiting hours for all general adult patients are now set from ten in the morning until eight in the evening, seven days a week. We have eliminated the previous midday break to allow for more flexible scheduling for families who work during standard business hours. This extension acknowledges the difficulty many relatives face in taking leave during the day. Additionally, we have increased the maximum number of concurrent visitors from two to three per room. This change allows for closer family involvement and support without overcrowding the private spaces designed for patient recovery and privacy.
Please note that these standard hours apply to all non-isolation rooms. Patients currently under strict isolation protocols for contagious illnesses will continue to follow separate, detailed guidelines. Staff will inform you personally if your loved one is in an isolation unit. For pediatric wards, visiting hours remain unchanged at nine in the morning until nine in the evening, with a strict limit of two primary caregivers and one additional support person. We ask that you still refrain from bringing outside food or beverages into any patient room, as these items pose hygiene risks and can trigger allergies or dietary complications for our patients.
We strongly encourage you to check the electronic patient status board or call the main admissions line before making the trip. This simple step ensures that your loved one is actually present and available for visitation, saving you time and unnecessary travel. Our nurses on the floor are always happy to provide specific reminders about any temporary restrictions or special instructions for individual cases. They are your primary point of contact for real-time updates and will guide you through the procedural requirements for each visit.
Thank you for your continued cooperation and patience as we navigate these operational updates. We recognize that the hospital environment can be stressful and that clear communication is vital to your peace of mind. If you have questions or encounter difficulties complying with these new policies, please do not hesitate to reach out to our patient relations department. We are here to support you and your family during this challenging time. Your role in positive recovery is invaluable to us.
Sincerely,
Director of Patient Services
General Regional Medical Center

The smartphone has fundamentally reshaped how millions of people approach the acquisition of new languages. raw:
history of the printing press

The invention of the printing press in the mid-15th century reshaped the world in ways that still echo today. Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith from Mainz, Germany, combined existing technologies-movable metal type, oil-based inks, and a screw press-to create a machine capable of producing identical pages quickly and affordably. His first major project, the 42-line Bible of 1455, demonstrated the press's potential and sparked a revolution in the dissemination of knowledge.

Soon after Gutenberg's breakthrough, the press spread across Europe like wildfire. By the late 1400s, presses were operating in Italy, France, and England, each adapting the technology to local languages and script styles. The ability to mass-produce books lowered the cost of reading material, allowing a broader segment of society-merchants, clergy, and eventually the emerging middle class-to access texts that had previously been rare luxuries.

The printing press also accelerated the Reformation and the scientific revolution. Martin Luther's 95 Theses, printed in 1517, reached a wide audience within weeks, fueling religious debate across the continent. Likewise, the works of Copernicus, Galileo, and Newton were circulated more widely than ever, enabling scholars to build on each other's ideas with unprecedented speed. The press turned ideas into public property, weakening the monopoly of monasteries and universities over learning.

In the centuries that followed, the press continued to evolve. The 19th-century steam-driven rotary press allowed newspapers to be printed in the thousands per hour, feeding the rise of mass media. Later, offset lithography and digital printing would further reduce costs and increase flexibility, but the core principle-replicating text and images efficiently-remained rooted in Gutenberg's original design.

Today, the legacy of the printing press lives on in every printed book, flyer, and newspaper, as well as in the digital world that inherits its spirit of rapid, wide-scale communication. Understanding its history reminds us how a single invention can transform culture, politics, and the very way humanity shares knowledge.

raw:
Soji Adejumo

David Olusoji Adejumo is a Nigerian Professor of animal physiology and a frontline politician. He was the Chairman of the Oyo State Universal Basic Education Board.

Soji Adejumo was born in the ancient caliphate city of Sokoto on Monday, December 3, 1956, into a Christian family of the late Reverend Canon Moses Oluyemi Adejumo, of Idi agbon compound. This was in the Agbeni area of Ibadan. His ancestral village is Aba Igbagbo (Agelu) in Iddo.

Adejumo started his early education at the Sacred Hearts Nursery school, Akure, in 1959 and concluded it at the St Mark's Primary School, Offa in Kwara State. For his post primary education he attended the prestigious Ibadan Grammar School between 1968 and 1974. Because of this, he gained admission to the Premier university in Nigeria, the University of Ibadan in 1975. He graduated from the university with Special Honors in Animal Science, Second Class (Upper Division), in 1976. He studied on the Federal Government of Nigeria Scholarship for his master's degree Program between 1979 and 1980. Adejumo had his doctorate degree on the scholarship of the University of Ibadan as a university scholar between 1980 and 1983.

In 1984, Professor Adejumo started his academic career as a lecturer in the department of Animal Science at the University of Ibadan. He was promoted to lecturer in 1986, elected Sub Dean (undergraduate) of the Faculty of Agriculture and Forestry in 1989, Senior Lecturer in 1991, Reader in 2002 and attained the rank of a professor in 2005. He has to his credit several scientific publications in international and National journals and supervised many students and research works.

Soji Adejumo started his political career in the second republic when he joined the Unity Party of Nigeria. He was a founding member of the People's Solidarity Party which later formed alliance with the People's Front to form the Social Democratic Party (SDP). He was endorsed by the SDP for the Oyo South Senatorial ticket but he was persuaded to step down for the eventual occupant of the seat, Senator Rasheed Ladoja, in 1993. At the beginning of the fourth republic, he joined the People's Democratic Party and he has been an active party leader. As one of the leaders in the state and the country who is interested in the unity of the PDP, he has held series of meetings with other leaders across the country among whom is the former President Olusegun Obasanjo. He is a top governorship candidate in Oyo state and he declared his intention to govern the state on May 8, 2014, at a well-attended event.

Adejumo has held several positions among which was Executive Chairman of the Oyo State Youth Development Council between 1998 and 2002. In 2007, he was appointed by the Executive Governor of the state, Otunba Adebayo Alao Akala as the Chairman of Universal Basic Education Board. His tenure as chairman SUBEB, was as eventful as it was full of awards. He conceived the noble idea of "Adopt a school" Programme which was aimed at promoting private involvement in infrastructural development in public schools. This programme resulted in an unprecedented public participation in school infrastructural and instructional development in over 200 school communities. His tenure as the chairman also witnessed the mass recruitment of teachers. In his bid at ensuring strict discipline among teachers and the students, he established school marshals in public schools across the state. The Oyo State Universal Basic Education under his chairmanship, placed 2nd in the overall assessment for the 2006 UBE programme implementation intervention fund.

Soji Adejumo was born in the ancient caliphate city of Sokoto on Monday, December 3, 1956, into a Christian family of the late Reverend Canon Moses Oluyemi Adejumo, of Idi agbon compound. This was in the Agbeni area of Ibadan. His ancestral village is Aba Igbagbo (Agelu) in Iddo.

Adejumo started his early education at the Sacred Hearts Nursery school, Akure, in 1959 and concluded it at the St Mark's Primary School, Offa in Kwara State. For his post primary education he attended the prestigious Ibadan Grammar School between 1968 and 1974. Because of this, he gained admission to the Premier university in Nigeria, the University of Ibadan in 1975. He graduated from the university with Special Honors in Animal Science, Second Class (Upper Division), in 1976. He studied on the Federal Government of Nigeria Scholarship for his master's degree Program between 1979 and 1980. Adejumo had his doctorate degree on the scholarship of the University of Ibadan as a university scholar between 1980 and 1983.

In 1984, Professor Adejumo started his academic career as a lecturer in the department of Animal Science at the University of Ibadan. He was promoted to lecturer in 1986, elected Sub Dean (undergraduate) of the Faculty of Agriculture and Forestry in 1989, Senior Lecturer in 1991, Reader in 2002 and attained the rank of a professor in 2005. He has to his credit several scientific publications in international and National journals and supervised many students and research works.

Soji Adejumo started his political career in the second republic when he joined the Unity Party of Nigeria. He was a founding member of the People's Solidarity Party which later formed alliance with the People's Front to form the Social Democratic Party (SDP). He was endorsed by the SDP for the Oyo South Senatorial ticket but he was persuaded to step down for the eventual occupant of the seat, Senator Rasheed Ladoja, in 1993. At the beginning of the fourth republic, he joined the People's Democratic Party and he has been an active party leader. As one of the leaders in the state and the country who is interested in the unity of the PDP, he has held series of meetings with other leaders across the country among whom is the former President Olusegun Obasanjo. He is a top governorship candidate in Oyo state and he declared his intention to govern the state on May 8, 2014, at a well-attended event.

Adejumo has held several positions among which was Executive Chairman of the Oyo State Youth Development Council between 1998 and 2002. In 2007, he was appointed by the Executive Governor of the state, Otunba Adebayo Alao Akala as the Chairman of Universal Basic Education Board. His tenure as chairman SUBEB, was as eventful as it was full of awards. He conceived the noble idea of "Adopt a school" Programme which was aimed at promoting private involvement in infrastructural development in public schools. This programme resulted in an unprecedented public participation in school infrastructural and instructional development in over 200 school communities. His tenure as the chairman also witnessed the mass recruitment of teachers. In his bid at ensuring strict discipline among teachers and the students, he established school marshals in public schools across the state. The Oyo State Universal Basic Education under his chairmanship, placed 2nd in the overall assessment for the 2006 UBE programme implementation intervention fund.

raw:
street food guide

Wandering a bustling city, the scent of sizzling spices and fresh dough is a useful compass. This street-food guide is designed to help both first-timers and seasoned snack hunters navigate the noisy stalls, discover hidden gems, and enjoy the flavors that define a place.

A quick visual scan tells you a lot. Look for a steady line of locals, a clean prep area, and a constant flow of fresh ingredients being sliced or tossed. Vendors who keep workstations tidy and rotate stock daily usually serve safe, tasty food.

In Mexico, a corn-tortilla stuffed with al pastor, pineapple and cilantro is essential; in Bangkok, a bowl of fiery pad thai hits the spot; Seoul's vendors serve hotteok, a sweet pancake filled with brown sugar and nuts. Each bite tells a local story.

Stay hydrated with a reusable bottle and keep cash in small bills for quick transactions. Many stalls don't accept cards, so a few coins can save time. Respect the queue, avoid touching food unless it's meant to be eaten that way, and trust your instincts.

With curiosity and a willingness to follow the crowd, the city's culinary pulse becomes an open-air kitchen you can explore any hour. Grab a map app, set a budget, and let the aromas guide you-because the best meals happen where streetlights flicker and chatter never stops.

raw:
parking permit renewal

Renewing a parking permit may feel like a minor task, but it can quickly become a source of frustration if you miss the deadline or overlook a required document. In most cities the permit is linked directly to your residential address or workplace, and the renewal process is designed to keep the system fair for all users. When the permit expires, you risk receiving a citation, losing access to designated spots, and potentially facing higher fees for a late application. Understanding the steps ahead of time helps you avoid these inconveniences and ensures a smooth continuation of your parking privileges.

The first step is to check the renewal date printed on your current permit or on the notice mailed to you a few weeks before it expires. Many municipalities now send an email reminder that includes a direct link to the online portal, which has become the most popular method for handling renewals. If you prefer a paper form, you can pick one up at the local Department of Transportation office or request it by phone. Regardless of the format, be sure to have your vehicle registration number, driver's license, and proof of residence ready, as these items are typically required to verify eligibility.

When you log into the online system, you will be asked to confirm your personal details and the vehicle information associated with the permit. The interface usually guides you through each stage, allowing you to upload scanned copies of any supporting documents. At this point you can also review the current fee schedule; many jurisdictions have increased rates in recent years, and some offer discounts for seniors, students, or electric-vehicle owners. Payment can be made securely by credit card, debit card, or through a linked bank account, and you will receive an electronic receipt that you can print or save for your records.

If you encounter an issue such as a change of address, a new vehicle, or a name change, you will need to submit the appropriate documentation before the renewal can be finalized. Some cities require a short waiting period for verification, so it is wise to start the process at least two weeks before the permit's expiration. For those who cannot use the online service due to limited internet access, most offices still accept in-person applications during regular business hours, though you may experience longer wait times during peak renewal periods.

Finally, keep an eye on any special notices that might affect your parking zone. Construction projects, temporary street closures, or changes in zoning can alter where you are allowed to park, even if your permit remains valid. Signing up for municipal alerts via text or email can keep you informed of such changes. By staying organized, renewing your permit on time, and double-checking the latest local rules, you can avoid costly tickets and maintain the convenience of a guaranteed parking spot.

raw:
coffee brewing

Coffee brewing has become more than a morning ritual; it's a craft that enthusiasts treat like a science. From the aroma that drifts from a freshly ground bean to the lingering warmth of a perfectly extracted cup, each step influences the final experience. In cafés and home kitchens alike, the conversation has shifted from "just coffee" to discussions about water temperature, grind consistency, and the subtle chemistry that turns beans into liquid gold. Understanding the fundamentals can elevate a routine cup into a moment of genuine pleasure.

The quality of water is often overlooked, yet it is the medium that carries flavor from the grounds to your mug. Ideally, use filtered or bottled water with low mineral content; hard water can mute the nuanced notes that specialty beans offer. Temperature also plays a critical role-most experts recommend a range of 195 to 205 degrees Fahrenheit. Water that's too hot extracts bitter compounds, while water that's too cool leaves the brew under-extracted and sour. A simple kitchen thermometer or a kettle with temperature control can make this adjustment effortless.

Grind size is the next variable that dictates how quickly water extracts soluble material from the beans. A coarse grind, resembling sea salt, is suitable for immersion methods such as French press, where the grounds sit in water for several minutes. Conversely, an espresso machine demands a fine, powder-like consistency to force water through the tightly packed puck in under thirty seconds. Even within a single brewing style, small tweaks to grind size can shift the balance between brightness and body, so a burr grinder that lets you dial in the exact texture is worth the investment.

There are countless brewing methods, each with its own character and learning curve. The pour-over, for instance, offers precise control over flow rate and saturation, allowing you to highlight the delicate floral notes of an Ethiopian single origin. The AeroPress, with its hybrid immersion-pressure approach, delivers a clean cup in a minute or two, making it a favorite for travelers. Meanwhile, the classic drip machine provides convenience but often sacrifices nuance unless paired with a high-quality grinder and calibrated water temperature. Exploring a few methods helps you discover which style best matches your taste and lifestyle.

Consistency comes from mastering the routine. Measure your coffee by weight, not by scoop, to maintain a reliable coffee-to-water ratio-typically 1:15 for most methods. Pre-wet the filter to eliminate paper flavors and stabilize temperature. Start a timer as soon as the first droplets appear and note how long the brew takes; adjustments to grind, dose, or water temperature can then be made with confidence. Over time, you'll develop a mental map of how each variable affects the final cup, turning trial and error into a satisfying progression.

Ultimately, coffee brewing is a dialogue between the bean, the water, and the brewer's intent. By paying attention to water quality, temperature, grind size, and the nuances of each brewing device, you can extract the fullest expression of flavor from any roast. Whether you savor a quiet moment alone or share a meticulously crafted pour with friends, the effort you put into the process is reflected in every sip, turning a simple habit into an artful experience.

raw:
board game review

There is a unique satisfaction in unwrapping a new board game, the cardboard scent mixing with the promise of a fresh afternoon or evening away from screens. For decades, board games were relegated to the attic, viewed as simple children's toys or dull cardboard cutouts with no real depth. That era has passed decisively. The modern era, often referred to by enthusiasts as the golden age, has seen an explosion of complexity, thematic integration, and strategic depth that rivals many digital experiences. Reviewing a game today is no longer just about checking for broken pieces or typos; it is an evaluation of narrative cohesion, mechanical elegance, and social interaction. It requires a keen eye for how the components feel in the hand and how the rules flow in the mind.

A critical aspect of any thorough review involves understanding the target audience. Not every game is designed for everyone, and comparing a heavy wargame to a party title using the same metrics is a disservice to both. A great review identifies who the game is actually speaking to. Is it a tight engine-builder for tinkerers who love optimization, or is it a light narrative puzzle for friends who just want to laugh? Context is king. Without knowing the intended player group, a review can feel either unfairly harsh or confusingly vague. The best analysts clearly state the prerequisites for enjoyment, ensuring that potential buyers know exactly what they are signing up for before they drop their money.

The physical components play a surprisingly large role in the modern hobby. Modern production standards have risen, and players now expect high-quality tokens, intricate board layouts, and tactile satisfaction when moving pieces. However, a beautiful box does not save a poor mechanic. Conversely, a simple card game can be transformative if the social dynamics are well-handled. A balanced review weighs the aesthetic value against the functional reality. Does the art aid in understanding the game, or is it just decorative noise? Do the pieces fit comfortably in a hand, or do they clumsily scatter across the table? These tangible details build the immersion that separates a good game from a great one, acting as the bridge between the abstract rules and the emotional experience.

Played over several rounds, the game must prove itself beyond the initial novelty effect. First impressions are dangerous. A flashy opening turn can hide a dull middle game, where the novelty wears off and the repetitive decisions set in. Longevity is the true test. A good reviewer discusses re-playability, explaining how the game changes from the first playthrough to the tenth. Does it offer enough variance to keep players engaged, or does it become predictable? They also assess the pacing, noting if the game drags during thinking time or if it snaps through turns with satisfying momentum. This endurance factor is what determines whether a game earns a permanent spot on the shelf or gets donated after the holiday season leftovers are cleared out.

Ultimately, a board game review serves as a guide through a vast and often intimidating hobby. It helps navigate the noise of marketing hype and community hype, offering a grounded perspective based on actual play. It is not about giving a definitive score, but rather painting a clear picture of the experience. For the casual player, it saves time and money. For the veteran, it offers new insights into familiar mechanics. In a world of infinite choices, these written accounts provide the necessary clarity. They turn a potential impulse buy into a thoughtful decision, ensuring that the next table session brings joy rather than regret. The goal is simple: to help you find the games that will genuinely bring you and your friends together around the table.
