Subject: Important Update Regarding Gym Membership Terms
Hi Alex,
I am writing to inform you about some minor adjustments to our standard membership agreement that will take effect next month. These changes are designed to make your fitness journey smoother and more flexible without altering the core benefits you enjoy.
First, we are extending the free freeze period from thirty to forty-five days per calendar year. This allows for greater flexibility in case of unexpected travel, illness, or work commitments. You can activate these freeze days directly through our online member portal with just a few clicks.
Secondly, the auto-renewal notice period has been clarified. Previously, you were required to cancel thirty days before the renewal date to avoid an automatic charge. Now, we will send a specific reminder email fourteen days prior to any upcoming renewal, giving you ample time to review your options.
Please note that the annual price increase in our mid-year review is projected to be approximately three percent. We strive to keep rates competitive while maintaining high-quality equipment and certified staff. You will receive a detailed comparison of current and new rates in a separate communication.
Thank you for staying with us. If you have any questions or need assistance updating your billing details, please reach out to our front desk team anytime during operating hours. We appreciate your continued support.
Best regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Member Relations Manager
FitLife Athletic Center

Cecilia Keaveney

Cecilia Keaveney (born 27 November 1968) is an Irish former Fianna Fáil politician. She was a Teachta Dála (TD) and a Senator from 1996 to 2011.

She was born in Derry, Northern Ireland. She was educated at Carndonagh Community School in the Inishowen peninsula, County Donegal, and then at the University of Ulster at Jordanstown, Northern Ireland. She is a former music teacher. Her father Paddy Keaveney was an Independent Fianna Fáil Teachta Dála (TD) for Donegal North-East from 1976 to 1977. She was co-opted to Donegal County Council in 1995 following his death.

Keaveney was first elected to Dáil Éireann for Donegal North-East in a by-election on 2 April 1996 following the death of Independent Fianna Fáil TD Neil Blaney. She was re-elected at the 1997 general election and 2002 general election but lost her seat at the 2007 general election. Keaveney was formerly Chair of the Joint Oireachtas Committee on Arts, Sports, Tourism, Community, Rural and Gaeltacht Affairs. Keaveney lost her seat in a tough 2007 election battle where all three outgoing TDs were Fianna Fáil members. Under the Single transferable vote proportional representation electoral system used in Ireland, it was difficult for all three to be elected. This unusual situation arose when in July 2006 outgoing Fianna Fáil TD Jim McDaid reversed his earlier announcement that he would not seek a nomination to contest the election. In the intervening period Independent Fianna Fáil and its sole TD Niall Blaney had been absorbed into Fianna Fáil. As a result, Joe McHugh of Fine Gael won a seat at her expense. Keaveney stood successfully for election to Seanad Éireann on the Cultural and Educational Panel at the 2007 election. She did not contest the 2011 Seanad election.

Apache ZooKeeper

Apache ZooKeeper is an open-source server for highly reliable distributed coordination of cloud applications. It is a project of the Apache Software Foundation. ZooKeeper is essentially a service for distributed systems offering a hierarchical key-value store, which is used to provide a distributed configuration service, synchronization service, and naming registry for large distributed systems (see Use cases). ZooKeeper was a sub-project of Hadoop but is now a top-level Apache project in its own right.

ZooKeeper's architecture supports high availability through redundant services. Clients can ask another ZooKeeper leader if the first fails to answer. ZooKeeper nodes store their data in a hierarchical name space, like a file system or a tree data structure. Clients can read from and write to the nodes and in this way have a shared configuration service. ZooKeeper can be viewed as an atomic broadcast system, through which updates are totally ordered. The ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast (ZAB) protocol is the core of the system. ZooKeeper is used by companies including Yelp, Rackspace, Yahoo, Odnoklassniki, Reddit, NetApp SolidFire, Meta, Twitter and eBay as well as open source enterprise search systems like Solr and distributed database systems like Apache Pinot. ZooKeeper is modeled after Google's Chubby lock service and was originally developed at Yahoo! for streamlining the processes running on big-data clusters by storing the status in local log files on the ZooKeeper servers. These servers communicate with client machines to deliver the required information. ZooKeeper was developed to address issues that emerged during the deployment of distributed big-data applications. Some of the prime features of Apache ZooKeeper are:

Reliable System: the system keeps working even if some nodes stop working. Simple Architecture: there is a shared hierarchical namespace which helps coordinating the processes. Fast Processing: especially fast in "read-dominant" workloads (i.e. workloads in which reads are much more common than writes). Scalable: performance can be improved by adding nodes.

Node: the systems installed on the cluster ZNode: the nodes where the status is updated by other nodes in cluster Client applications: the tools that interact with the distributed applications Server applications: allow the client applications to interact using a common interface The services in the cluster are replicated and stored on a set of servers (called an "ensemble"), each of which maintains an in-memory database containing the entire data tree of state as well as a transaction log and snapshots stored persistently. Multiple client applications can connect to a server, and each client maintains a TCP connection through which it sends requests and heartbeats and receives responses and watch events for monitoring.

In addition to the client libraries included with the ZooKeeper distribution, several third-party libraries, including Apache Curator and Kazoo, extend ZooKeeper's capabilities. These libraries offer enhanced ease of use, additional features and support for a broader range of programming languages.

Apache Hadoop Apache Accumulo Apache HBase Apache Hive Apache Kafka (up to version 4.0.0) Apache Drill Apache Solr Apache Spark Apache NiFi Apache Druid Apache Helix Apache Pinot Apache Bookkeeper Apache Pulsar

Apache ZooKeeper is an open-source server for highly reliable distributed coordination of cloud applications. It is a project of the Apache Software Foundation. ZooKeeper is essentially a service for distributed systems offering a hierarchical key-value store, which is used to provide a distributed configuration service, synchronization service, and naming registry for large distributed systems (see Use cases). ZooKeeper was a sub-project of Hadoop but is now a top-level Apache project in its own right.

ZooKeeper's architecture supports high availability through redundant services. Clients can ask another ZooKeeper leader if the first fails to answer. ZooKeeper nodes store their data in a hierarchical name space, like a file system or a tree data structure. Clients can read from and write to the nodes and in this way have a shared configuration service. ZooKeeper can be viewed as an atomic broadcast system, through which updates are totally ordered. The ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast (ZAB) protocol is the core of the system. ZooKeeper is used by companies including Yelp, Rackspace, Yahoo, Odnoklassniki, Reddit, NetApp SolidFire, Meta, Twitter and eBay as well as open source enterprise search systems like Solr and distributed database systems like Apache Pinot. ZooKeeper is modeled after Google's Chubby lock service and was originally developed at Yahoo! for streamlining the processes running on big-data clusters by storing the status in local log files on the ZooKeeper servers. These servers communicate with client machines to deliver the required information. ZooKeeper was developed to address issues that emerged during the deployment of distributed big-data applications. Some of the prime features of Apache ZooKeeper are:

Reliable System: the system keeps working even if some nodes stop working. Simple Architecture: there is a shared hierarchical namespace which helps coordinating the processes. Fast Processing: especially fast in "read-dominant" workloads (i.e. workloads in which reads are much more common than writes). Scalable: performance can be improved by adding nodes.

Node: the systems installed on the cluster ZNode: the nodes where the status is updated by other nodes in cluster Client applications: the tools that interact with the distributed applications Server applications: allow the client applications to interact using a common interface The services in the cluster are replicated and stored on a set of servers (called an "ensemble"), each of which maintains an in-memory database containing the entire data tree of state as well as a transaction log and snapshots stored persistently. Multiple client applications can connect to a server, and each client maintains a TCP connection through which it sends requests and heartbeats and receives responses and watch events for monitoring.

In addition to the client libraries included with the ZooKeeper distribution, several third-party libraries, including Apache Curator and Kazoo, extend ZooKeeper's capabilities. These libraries offer enhanced ease of use, additional features and support for a broader range of programming languages.

public transport accessibility

Public transport is a lifeline, connecting people to work, education, healthcare, and social activities. For it to truly serve everyone in our community, accessibility is not just a desirable feature; it is an absolute necessity. Ensuring that journeys are safe, comfortable, and independent for all passengers is a fundamental right that underpins inclusive urban living.

True accessibility goes far beyond just providing a ramp. It encompasses a comprehensive suite of features: working lifts and escalators, audible and visual announcements, sufficient space for wheelchairs and mobility aids, trained staff, and easily navigable station layouts. It also means accessible ticket machines and real-time information systems, making the entire journey seamless from start to finish.

While significant strides have been made in modernizing infrastructure and rolling stock, many challenges persist. Older stations often lack necessary modifications, bus stops can be poorly maintained, and inconsistent information can create stressful barriers for individuals with visual or hearing impairments. These gaps mean that for too many, public transport remains an option fraught with uncertainty and difficulty.

The benefits of a fully accessible public transport network extend far beyond those with specific mobility needs. Parents with strollers, the elderly, temporary injury sufferers, and even tourists with luggage all benefit from improved ease of use. It fosters economic participation, enhances social inclusion, and reduces reliance on private vehicles, contributing to a greener, more connected city for everyone.

Moving forward, continuous investment and a commitment to user-centric design are crucial. Integrating new technologies, conducting regular accessibility audits, and actively engaging with disability advocacy groups can help identify and address remaining shortcomings. Only through ongoing effort and collaboration can we build truly inclusive transport systems that empower every citizen to navigate their city with dignity and independence.

Jakarta International Expo

Jakarta International Expo (JIExpo or JIExpo Kemayoran) is a convention, exhibition and entertainment complex located at Pademangan in North Jakarta, Indonesia. Opened in 2010, it was developed by the Central Cipta Murdaya group, built in the area of the former Kemayoran Airport. JIExpo is the sole venue of the Jakarta Fair, the largest annual trade fair in Indonesia.

JIExpo covers approximately 44 hectares, with a 2,500-seat theatre and concert hall, 100,000 square meters of exhibition and convention space, and supporting operations. The facility has five exhibition halls, two ballrooms, 14 meeting rooms, and a professional international theatre. JIExpo underwent an expansion from 2016 to 2019, adding an international theatre and convention center. There is also a Holiday Inn Express on the grounds.

Completed and commissioned in 2019, the JIExpo Theatre is one of the largest and most advanced performing arts centers in Indonesia. The proscenium arch measures 11m by 30m, with a stage depth of 17m from set line to back wall. The computerized fly system has 80 line sets onstage, and four over the forestage. The orchestra pit can accommodate up to 50 musicians, and the backstage and dressing areas accommodate up to 106 performers. One of the unique features of the theatre is its acoustic design. The theatre interior is rated at STC 20, and is suitable for symphony and unamplified voice, as well as sound recording. The theatre's opening event was a performance of Bach's Suites for Unaccompanied Cello by renowned cellist Yo-Yo Ma, in his first-ever performance in Indonesia. The JIExpo Theatre features Meyer Leopard stacks and one of the largest Meyer Constellation systems in a performance venue anywhere in the world as of 2019, according to Meyer Sound. The system has 285 speakers and 51 microphones installed throughout the interior, offering a superior audio experience for both acoustic and amplified performances.

Located in the JIExpo Theatre complex is the JIExpo Convention Center. It composed of two ballrooms, 12 configurable meeting rooms, and two executive-style Board Rooms. The convention center and theatre lobbies are connected to a 5-star banquet kitchen that provides food and beverage service to all function areas. The JIExpo Convention Center was also completed and commissioned in 2019.

JIExpo has a series of five exhibition halls surrounding a central outdoor tarmac. It hosts a number of exhibitions, concerts and other national and international events. Annual events, such as Jakarta Fair, Java Jazz Festival, Djakarta Warehouse Project and the Indonesia International Motor Show (IIMS) draw thousands of visitors per year. The facility also hosts large-scale industrial, military and leisure exhibitions, as well as private and entertainment events. In 2018, the exhibition halls hosted boxing, contact bridge, gymnastics, wushu, table tennis and weightlifting tournaments on the 18th Asian Games that year.

JIExpo is accessible by Transjakarta BRT corridors 12 and 14, with the latter's two trajectories of bus number 14A & 14B. There are three Transjakarta stations nearby JIExpo: Kemayoran, JIEXPO Kemayoran and Landasan Pacu. Only the latter that serves both BRT corridors, while JIEXPO Kemayoran only caters northbound corridor 14 buses to Jakarta International Stadium. JIExpo Kemayoran station also caters feeder route 1W from Ancol one way towards Blok M via toll road. During the Jakarta Fair and/or other events sponsored by Transjakarta, there are three special routes to serve selected events in JIExpo as of 2026, namely route 2C (Balai Kota-JIEXPO), PRJ2 (Kampung Melayu-JIEXPO) and PRJ3 (Pulo Gadung-JIEXPO).

Chen Chuangtian

Chen Chuangtian (Chinese: 陈创天; 18 February 1937 - 31 October 2018), also known as Chuang-Tian Chen, was a Chinese materials scientist and physical chemist who specialized in crystals used in lasers. He discovered the nonlinear optical crystals BBO, LBO and KBBF, which have important uses in areas including superconductor research, semiconductor photolithography, and the medical industry. He was an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a fellow of The World Academy of Sciences. He was awarded the TWAS Prize in Chemistry, the State Technological Invention Award (First Class), and the Laudise Prize.

Chen was born on 18 February 1937 in Fenghua, Zhejiang, China. He studied at Shenyang No. 2 High School, and was accepted by the Department of Physics of Peking University in August 1956. After graduating in 1962, he entered the Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter in Fuzhou on the recommendation of Hu Ning, and studied under physical chemist Lu Jiaxi for three years. In 1965, Chen chose nonlinear optical materials as his research direction and spent the next two years calculating the nonlinear optical coefficients of many crystals. In the late 1970s and the 1980s, Chen and his team discovered the new nonlinear optical crystals BaB2O4 (BBO) and LiB3O5 (LBO). In 1988, Chen and his team began searching for optical compounds that could produce shorter ultraviolet wavelengths. After researching hundreds of compounds, they discovered potassium beryllium fluoroborate (KBBF), a nonlinear optical crystal which is capable of generating light within a very narrow bandwidth, with wavelengths of less than 200 nanometers. The crystal is important in superconductor research and can allow the replacement of excimer laser with solid-state ones in photolithography used in the semiconductor and the medical industries. Until at least 2009, Chen's laboratory at the Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter was the only place in the world that could produce KBBF. In 2013, Chen and his colleague Xu Zuyan invented the DUV-DPL device (deep ultraviolet diode-pumped solid-state laser), with a wavelength of only 177.3 nm. Chen died on 31 October 2018 in Beijing, at the age of 81.

Chen was elected a fellow of The World Academy of Sciences in 1990 and an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 2003. Chen was awarded the 1987 TWAS Prize in Chemistry, "for his outstanding contribution to the development of new nonlinear optical materials, the formulation of a quantum chemical theory that guides the search for such materials and the discovery of beta barium borate and lithium triborate". He won a Special Prize of the Science and Technology Progress Award of the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 1986 for his discovery of BBO and the State Technological Invention Award (First Class) in 1991 for LBO. In 2013, he was awarded the Laudise Prize by the International Organization for Crystal Growth.

mountain weather

Summer in the Rockies never looks the way the forecast promises. By the time you tie your boots at the basecamp, the clear blue morning can dissolve into a bruised purple canopy of clouds climbing the ridgeline with terrifying speed. The air grows heavy and still, a deceptive calm that signals an incoming convective storm. Hikers who rely on valley weather apps often find themselves blindsided because mountain microclimates operate independently of the broader regional trends.

Lightning strikes are the primary hazard, appearing without the heavy rain that accompanies lowland thunderstorms. The flash-frecency in the upper elevations means the threat reaches the summit long before the first drop hits the valley floor. Ignoring this lag can be fatal, as the distance between the bolt and the ground is far greater at altitude, allowing the arc to jump directly to exposed peaks or lone figures on ridges.

Temperature drops are equally unforgiving. For every thousand feet of elevation gained, the ambient temperature falls by roughly three degrees Fahrenheit. A pleasant seventy-degree day at the trailhead can turn into a freezing, wind-chilled exposure above the treeline within minutes. The sun, though bright, offers poor protection against the radiating cold of the high atmosphere, making layered clothing essential rather than optional.

Visibility can vanish in seconds. Fog banks surge down from the circlet peaks, wrapping trails in a whiteout that disorients even experienced navigators. Without distinct landmarks, the risk of sliding off an ice shelf or wandering into a backcountry basin increases exponentially. Keeping your map and compass handy is not just a precaution; it is a survival tool in conditions where GPS satellites can struggle to lock in dense mist.

Turning back is not a failure but a wise tactical decision.Mountain weather rewards those who respect its volatility. Waiting out a storm in a sheltered boulder field is always safer than pushing through lightning, hypothermia, and reduced visibility. The mountain will be there tomorrow, likely just as beautiful, but only if you arrive to see it.

To: All Staff and Volunteers 
From: Facilities Management, Green Spaces Department 
Date: 8 October 2026 
Subject: Updated Procedures for Garden Pest Control

Effective immediately, all garden maintenance teams will follow the revised pest-control protocol designed to protect plant health while minimizing environmental impact. The core of the new approach is integrated pest management (IPM), which emphasizes regular monitoring, identification of pest species, and the use of non-chemical controls whenever feasible. Mechanical methods such as hand-picking, traps, and barriers should be the first line of defense before any pesticide application is considered.

When a pest outbreak is detected, the supervising horticulturist must document the species involved, the extent of damage, and the environmental conditions that may have contributed to the problem. This information will be logged in the garden's digital tracking system within 24 hours of observation. The recorded data will help determine whether a targeted biological control, such as the release of predatory insects, is appropriate, or if a low-toxicity horticultural oil is required.

If chemical treatment becomes necessary, only EPA-approved products with the lowest toxicity ratings shall be used, and they must be applied strictly according to label instructions. Protective equipment, including gloves, goggles, and respirators, is mandatory for all personnel handling these substances. Application should be limited to early morning or late afternoon hours to reduce exposure to pollinators and beneficial insects.

All staff must complete the annual "Safe Pest Management" training session before the end of the fiscal year. Attendance records will be retained in the human-resources database, and any gaps in certification will be addressed promptly. The training covers identification of common garden pests, proper use of monitoring tools, and emergency procedures for accidental exposure.

Please circulate this notice to all relevant teams and ensure that the updated protocol is incorporated into daily garden routines. Your cooperation is essential to maintaining the health of our green spaces while safeguarding the surrounding ecosystem.

Subject: Sourdough Baking Tips and Upcoming Workshop
Dear Alex,
I hope you're doing well and enjoying the early signs of spring in the kitchen. I wanted to share a quick update on the sourdough starter I've been nurturing over the past few weeks. After a brief dip in activity during the colder nights, the starter has rebounded nicely, showing a vigorous rise within four to five hours of feeding. I've been feeding it a 1:1:1 ratio of starter, water, and flour, using a mix of whole-wheat and unbleached all-purpose to give it both flavor and strength. The bubbles are now uniform, and the aroma has shifted from a sharp tang to a pleasant, slightly nutty scent.
When it comes to the dough itself, I've been experimenting with a longer bulk fermentation at a cooler temperature, around 68°F (20°C). Extending the bulk phase to about three and a half hours, with a series of gentle folds every thirty minutes, has resulted in a more open crumb and a subtle, complex flavor profile. The dough feels elastic yet supple, and the windowpane test shows a nice, even stretch without tearing. I've also tried a 30% hydration increase, which makes the dough a bit stickier but yields a lighter crumb after baking.
Shaping has been a critical step for me lately. I've adopted the "tight-round" technique, which involves creating surface tension by gently rotating the dough while pulling it toward the center. This method not only improves the oven spring but also helps the loaf hold its shape during the final proof. Speaking of proofing, I've found that a cold retard in the refrigerator for 12 to 14 hours gives the dough a deeper, more nuanced flavor and a crisper crust. When I bake the loaf on a preheated Dutch oven at 475°F (246°C) for the first 20 minutes, then remove the lid and finish for another 20 minutes, the crust turns a deep golden brown with a satisfying crackle.
I'm excited to let you know that I'll be hosting a small, hands-on sourdough workshop next Saturday at 10 a.m. in my kitchen. The session will cover starter maintenance, mixing techniques, and the art of scoring. I'll also demonstrate how to adjust hydration and fermentation times based on ambient conditions, which is something many home bakers find confusing. Space is limited to eight participants, so please let me know as soon as you can if you'd like to join. I'll provide all the ingredients, tools, and a printed guide to take home.
If you have any questions about the process or want to try a particular recipe before the workshop, feel free to email me or give me a call. I'm always happy to swap tips and troubleshoot any issues you might encounter, whether it's a sluggish starter or a dense crumb. Looking forward to hearing about your own sourdough adventures and hopefully seeing you in the kitchen next week.
Warm regards,
Megan Patel
Megan's Artisan Baking
(555) 219-8743
megan@artisanbaking.com

smart home devices

Smart home devices have moved from novelty gadgets to essential fixtures in many households, reshaping the way people interact with their living spaces. From voice-controlled speakers that can dim the lights to thermostats that learn daily routines, the market now offers a broad spectrum of products that promise both convenience and efficiency. As internet connectivity becomes more reliable and affordable, homeowners are increasingly comfortable delegating routine tasks to a network of interconnected appliances.

The most immediate benefit of a connected home is the reduction of everyday friction. Imagine arriving home after a long commute and having the lights switch on automatically, the temperature adjust to a comfortable level, and the coffee maker start brewing-all without lifting a finger. Such seamless automation not only saves time but can also lower energy bills, as smart thermostats and lighting systems optimize usage based on occupancy and daylight, shutting down unnecessary power draw in real time.

Choosing the right ecosystem is often the first step toward a cohesive setup. Major platforms such as Apple HomeKit, Google Home, and Amazon Alexa each provide a central hub that coordinates devices, yet they differ in terms of privacy policies, voice assistant personalities, and third-party compatibility. A device that works flawlessly with one assistant may require additional bridges or custom routines to function with another, so homeowners should evaluate which voice assistant aligns with their daily habits before investing heavily in brand-specific hardware.

Security and privacy remain top concerns as more appliances gain internet access. Each new connection point can potentially expose a network to hackers, making robust passwords, regular firmware updates, and isolated guest networks critical safeguards. Manufacturers have responded by incorporating encrypted communication protocols and offering transparency reports, but consumers still bear responsibility for configuring settings that limit data sharing and restrict remote access to trusted devices only.

When selecting smart home products, focus on longevity and adaptability. Look for devices that support over-the-air updates, as these ensure compatibility with evolving standards and patch vulnerabilities. Compatibility with multiple ecosystems, energy-monitoring features, and a clear, user-friendly app interface are also strong indicators of a well-designed product. As the industry matures, the next wave of innovations-such as AI-driven predictive maintenance and more sophisticated sensor fusion-will further blur the line between convenience and intelligent living, turning today's experimental gadgets into tomorrow's household staples.

Tyisha Miller

Tyisha Shenee Miller (March 9, 1979 - December 28, 1998) was an African American woman from Rubidoux, California. She was shot and killed by police officers called by family members who could not wake her as she lay unconscious in a car with a gun on her lap. The incident sparked demonstrations against police anti-blackness. The officers involved were fired from Riverside Police Department but did not face prosecution due to insufficient evidence, and were later afforded full back-pay after the decision to terminate their employment was found to be an "abuse of administrative discretion," though they were not reinstated.

In the early morning hours of December 28, 1998, Tyisha Miller, a 19-year-old African American woman from Rubidoux, California, was driving with her 15-year-old friend in her aunt's car when the car's tire went flat. A passing stranger helped them change the tire, but the spare was also flat, so the man led them to a gas station. The tire would not inflate, and so Miller waited in the car while the man drove her friend home to get assistance from the family. When relatives arrived they found Miller apparently comatose in the locked car, with the engine running and the radio on. She was shaking bodily and foaming at the mouth, and had a .380 semi-automatic pistol in her lap. Unable to wake her, they called 9-1-1 and asked for an ambulance. However, four officers from the Riverside Police Department arrived at the scene within minutes and, informed by family members of the presence of a gun in the car, approached the vehicle with guns drawn. After attempting for several minutes to get a response from Miller, the decision was made to force entry into the vehicle as Miller was in apparent need of immediate medical attention. As one of the officers was attempting to remove the gun, Miller is said to have sat up and grabbed the weapon, at which point the officers opened fire 23 times, hitting Miller with at least 12 bullets, including four in the head. It was later discovered that Miller had not reached for the gun, and may have been unconscious at the time of the shooting. The police later recanted their statement of her reaching for the gun. An investigation of her death was undertaken and the officers involved, three white and one Hispanic, were placed on administrative leave. They claimed they had acted in self-defense. In January 1999, the United States Attorney announced an investigation of the shooting would be undertaken by the FBI; at the same time protestors demanded an independent investigation, pointing out racism on the part of the police and a possible coverup of the facts.

In May 1999, Riverside County District Attorney Grover Trask, said the four police officers involved had probably made an error of judgment, but had committed no crime. This sparked protests from Jesse Jackson and others, and hundreds turned out to demonstrate against the decision not to prosecute, resulting in the arrests of 46 protesters, including activist Al Sharpton and comedian Dick Gregory. In the wake of these protests, Federal officials announced the formation of a unit of lawyers to investigate and prosecute civil rights violations, and a Federal Department of Justice investigation into Riverside Police Department, to determine if their practices and policies inherently violated civil rights. Following shortly after this announcement, the four officers involved in the incident were fired for "violating department policies", a decision that had been made several weeks before. Toxicological reports subsequently indicated that Miller had been under the influence of the drug gamma-Hydroxybutyric acid (GHB) at the time of the shooting. In January 2002, arbitrator Robert Steinberg of Culver City found that the officers had been wrongly fired and that the decision to terminate their employment constituted an "abuse of administrative discretion". He awarded them full back-pay, but did not order them to be reinstated. In December 2002, the United States Department of Justice Civil Rights Division closed the investigation, citing insufficient evidence to prosecute the police officers.

A play called Dreamscape, based on this incident, was written by Rickerby Hinds, a faculty member in the Department of Theatre at University of California, Riverside (UCR). The play has been performed around the United States as well as in Poland, Romania, Hungary, Turkey, and the UK.

However, four officers from the Riverside Police Department arrived at the scene within minutes and, informed by family members of the presence of a gun in the car, approached the vehicle with guns drawn. After attempting for several minutes to get a response from Miller, the decision was made to force entry into the vehicle as Miller was in apparent need of immediate medical attention. As one of the officers was attempting to remove the gun, Miller is said to have sat up and grabbed the weapon, at which point the officers opened fire 23 times, hitting Miller with at least 12 bullets, including four in the head. It was later discovered that Miller had not reached for the gun, and may have been unconscious at the time of the shooting. The police later recanted their statement of her reaching for the gun. An investigation of her death was undertaken and the officers involved, three white and one Hispanic, were placed on administrative leave. They claimed they had acted in self-defense. In January 1999, the United States Attorney announced an investigation of the shooting would be undertaken by the FBI; at the same time protestors demanded an independent investigation, pointing out racism on the part of the police and a possible coverup of the facts.

In May 1999, Riverside County District Attorney Grover Trask, said the four police officers involved had probably made an error of judgment, but had committed no crime. This sparked protests from Jesse Jackson and others, and hundreds turned out to demonstrate against the decision not to prosecute, resulting in the arrests of 46 protesters, including activist Al Sharpton and comedian Dick Gregory. In the wake of these protests, Federal officials announced the formation of a unit of lawyers to investigate and prosecute civil rights violations, and a Federal Department of Justice investigation into Riverside Police Department, to determine if their practices and policies inherently violated civil rights. Following shortly after this announcement, the four officers involved in the incident were fired for "violating department policies", a decision that had been made several weeks before. Toxicological reports subsequently indicated that Miller had been under the influence of the drug gamma-Hydroxybutyric acid (GHB) at the time of the shooting. In January 2002, arbitrator Robert Steinberg of Culver City found that the officers had been wrongly fired and that the decision to terminate their employment constituted an "abuse of administrative discretion". He awarded them full back-pay, but did not order them to be reinstated. In December 2002, the United States Department of Justice Civil Rights Division closed the investigation, citing insufficient evidence to prosecute the police officers.
A play called Dreamscape, based on this incident, was written by Rickerby Hinds, a faculty member in the Department of Theatre at University of California, Riverside (UCR). The play has been performed around the United States as well as in Poland, Romania, Hungary, Turkey, and the UK.

The Aeris Series 2 will enter the North American market on October 15th, marking a pivotal expansion for our consumer electronics division. This launch is not merely a product release but a strategic repositioning of our brand as a leader in sustainable audio technology. Management has authorized a budget of two million dollars specifically dedicated to this initiative, with seventy percent allocated to digital marketing and thirty percent to retail partnerships across major chains. The objective is to capture fifteen percent market share in the premium headphone sector within the first six months post-launch. Given the competitive landscape, success will be measured by early adoption metrics and customer retention rates rather than immediate revenue spikes.

Marketing campaigns will shift focus toward the product's recycled aluminum casing and lack of rare-earth magnets, appealing to environmentally conscious demographics aged twenty-five to forty-five. Creative agencies are currently finalizing video assets that highlight supply chain transparency, ensuring all messaging aligns with our corporate social responsibility guidelines. We will launch a limited edition colorway in collaboration with a prominent fashion house to generate initial hype. Social media influencers in the tech and lifestyle sectors have been contracted to feature the product in their daily routines, creating an organic narrative rather than traditional hard-sell advertisements.

Supply chain logistics have been tightened to accommodate anticipated demand surges. Initial inventory will be distributed to three central warehouses in California, New Jersey, and Texas to ensure rapid shipping times. Vendor contracts have been renegotiated to include penalty clauses for delivery delays, mitigating the risk of stock shortages during peak holiday season. Quality control teams will conduct double-blind testing on every unit before packaging, adhering to our zero-defect policy. Any units failing the acoustic frequency test will be recycled immediately, and data on failure points will be reported bi-weekly to engineering for potential firmware updates.

Customer support protocols require significant updates to handle increased inquiry volume. The help desk has been expanded by twenty full-time agents, all of whom have completed specialized training on the new battery management system and hearing aid compatibility features. A self-service diagnostic tool will be integrated into our mobile application, allowing users to troubleshoot connectivity issues without waiting for live assistance. Live chat support will be available for twelve hours daily, extending to sixteen hours during the first week of launch to accommodate immediate post-purchase questions.

Post-launch performance reviews will commence on December 1st, analyzing sales velocity, return rates, and net promoter scores. Senior leadership will convene for a dedicated retrospective to assess whether the initial pricing strategy resonated with target demographics. Adjustments to the promotional calendar will be made based on real-time data feedback from retail partners. This plan assumes no major supply chain disruptions; however, contingency reserves are established to address unforeseen logistics challenges. All department heads must review their specific action items and submit confirmation of readiness by September 20th.

Progress Chapter 171: History Is Written By The Victors

The Chapter 171: History Is Written By The Victors was a professional wrestling event produced by Progress Wrestling. It took place on September 22, 2024, in London, England at Electric Ballroom. Nine matches were contested at the event. The main event saw Luke Jacobs defeat Eddie Dennis to retain the PROGRESS World Championship.

The event included matches that each resulted from scripted storylines, where wrestlers portrayed heroes, villains, or less distinguishable characters in scripted events that built tension and culminated in a wrestling match or series of matches. Results were predetermined by Progress' creative writers, while storylines were produced on Progress' events airing on the Demand PROGRESS streaming service. The event also featured the in-ring return of Cara Noir who made an appearance at Chapter 170: Wrestling Never Sleeps.

In the first match of the event, Lykos Gym (Kid Lykos and Kid Lykos II) defeated Gene Munny and Taishi Ozawa in tag team action. In the second bout, Allie Katch picked up a victory over Lizzy Evo in singles competition. The third bout saw All Elite Wrestling's Marina Shafir successfully defending the DEFY Women's Championship against Kanji and Nina Samuels in a three-way match. Next up, Rhio defeated Emersyn Jayne to secure the fourteenth consecutive defense of the Progress World Women's Championship in that respective reign. After the bout concluded, Rhio got attacked by Lizzy Evo who demanded a title match. Next up, Paul Robinson defeated Connor Mills to secure the tenth consecutive defense of the Progress Proteus Championship in that respective reign. After the bout concluded, Simon Miller made a return and stepped up as Robinson's next challenger. In the seventh bout, Cara Noir defeated Yoshiki Inamura in singles competition. In the semi main event, Tate Mayfais defeated Mike Bird who substituted 1 Called Manders in singles competition. In the main event, Luke Jacobs defeated Eddie Dennis to secure the third consecutive defense of the PROGRESS World Championship in that respective reign.

The third quarter concluded with total revenue reaching $4.2 million, representing a twelve percent increase over the previous quarter. This growth was primarily driven by a strong performance in the enterprise sector, which accounted for sixty percent of total sales. Consumer segment numbers remained stable, hovering near the eight percent target set at the beginning of the fiscal year. Although the overall trend is positive, certain regional variations offer specific insights into market dynamics that require further analysis.

North America continued to lead all geographical regions, contributing forty-five percent of total revenue. The expansion of the Chicago office has yielded immediate results, with new client acquisitions outpacing projections by fifteen percent. Conversely, the European region showed a slight decline of three percent despite new product launches. This dip correlates with increased competitor activity in the United Kingdom and Germany, suggesting that our current pricing strategy may be less competitive in those specific markets.

Product performance was uneven, with the premium tier delivering a twenty percent surge in units sold. This aligns with our marketing campaign targeting high-value customers. Meanwhile, entry-level products saw a modest four percent increase, indicating that the broader market remains price-sensitive. The service division contributed eighteen percent of total revenue, maintaining consistent margins and reinforcing the importance of recurring income streams in stabilizing cash flow during slower periods.

Several operational challenges impacted efficiency during the quarter. Inventory shortages in the second half slowed deployment timelines for three major enterprise deals, delaying recognition of potential revenue. Additionally, customer support response times increased by ten percent, a backlog attributed to the surge in new user onboarding requests. Addressing these bottlenecks is critical to preventing churn among recently acquired clients and ensuring smooth handoffs between sales and technical teams.

Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, management projects a continued upward trajectory based on existing pipeline commitments. Strategic priorities will include revising pricing models for the European market to regain competitive parity and implementing additional staffing in customer support. The sales team is also tasked with identifying cross-sell opportunities within the current customer base to maximize lifetime value. Regular progress reviews will be conducted bi-weekly to ensure alignment with these goals and to mitigate emerging risks before they impact monthly targets.

Subject: Invitation to Support Our Upcoming School Fundraising Campaign
Dear Parents and Guardians,
I hope this message finds you well and enjoying a wonderful start to the new school year. As we settle into our classrooms and begin fresh projects, I wanted to share an exciting opportunity for our community to come together and make a meaningful impact on our students' educational experience.
Next month, the school will launch a fundraising campaign aimed at raising $25,000 to upgrade our science labs, purchase new library resources, and fund after-school enrichment programs. These improvements will directly benefit our children by providing hands-on learning tools, expanding reading collections, and offering extracurricular activities that inspire curiosity and growth. Your support, whether through a monetary donation, volunteering time, or helping spread the word, will be instrumental in reaching our goal.
We have set up a simple online donation portal that can be accessed via the link in this email, and contributions of any size are greatly appreciated. In addition, we are organizing a series of family-friendly events, including a bake sale, a fun run, and an art auction, where proceeds will go directly to the fund. Participation in these events not only raises funds but also strengthens the bond among families, teachers, and staff.
If you have any ideas for additional fundraising activities or would like to volunteer on the planning committee, please reply to this email or contact the school office by Friday, October 12. Your creativity and involvement are vital, and we welcome every suggestion that can help us achieve our vision for a richer educational environment.
Thank you in advance for your generosity and enthusiasm. Together, we can provide our students with the resources they need to thrive academically and personally.
Warm regards,
Emily Rivera 
Principal, Oakridge Elementary School 
email: erivera@oakridge.edu 
phone: (555) 842-3102

Subject: Maintenance Request for Apartment 3B - Leaking Bathroom Faucet
Dear Ms. Patel,
I hope you are doing well. My name is Jordan Matthews and I have been a resident of unit 3B in the Maplewood Apartments for the past eighteen months. I am writing to formally request maintenance assistance for a persistent issue that has developed in my bathroom over the last week. I have always appreciated the prompt and professional service your team provides, and I am confident this matter can be resolved quickly with your help.
The problem concerns the sink faucet in the master bathroom. The handle feels loose, and when I turn it on, water drips continuously even after the tap is fully closed. At first, I thought it might be a minor leak, but the drip has become more pronounced, creating a steady stream that pools on the countertop and eventually runs onto the floor. I have tried tightening the handle myself, following the guidelines in the tenant handbook, but the leak persists, suggesting that the internal valve may be worn out or the seal is compromised.
This leakage is not only an inconvenience but also a cause for concern regarding water waste and potential damage to the surrounding cabinetry. Over the past three days, I have noticed a faint dampness near the base of the cabinet, and there is a faint musty odor that has begun to develop. While there is no immediate sign of mold, I am worried that continued exposure to moisture could lead to longer-term issues, especially given the age of the wooden fixtures in the bathroom. Additionally, the constant noise of the dripping water is becoming a distraction, particularly when I am trying to work from home or sleep.
I would greatly appreciate it if a maintenance technician could visit the apartment at a mutually convenient time to inspect and repair the faucet. I am flexible with my schedule and can accommodate most weekdays between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. If it helps, I am also available on Saturday mornings up to noon. Please let me know the earliest slot that works for your team, and I will ensure the apartment is accessible. If any parts need to be ordered in advance, I am happy to discuss that as well so we can avoid additional delays.
Thank you very much for your attention to this matter. I understand the maintenance staff has a busy workload, and I truly appreciate the effort you all put into keeping the building in good condition. Should you need any further details, feel free to reach me by phone at (555) 312-8479 or via email at jordan.matthews@email.com. I look forward to hearing from you soon and to having this issue resolved.
Sincerely,
Jordan Matthews
Apartment 3B
Maplewood Apartments

budget planning

The financial landscape for small businesses and startups is often unpredictable, making rigorous budget planning not just a recommended practice but a survival mechanism. Many entrepreneurs mistakenly view budgeting as a static document created once at the start of the fiscal year and left to gather digital dust. In reality, a healthy budget is a living, breathing instrument that requires constant attention and periodic adjustment. Understanding that your financial statement is a roadmap rather than a rigid rulebook is the first step toward establishing fiscal discipline. When cash flow forecasts are treated with this level of dynamic respect, organizations can pivot more effectively in response to market shifts, ensuring they have the liquidity needed to weather storms or seize untapped opportunities.

Creating a robust budget begins with a thorough audit of current expenditures. Before you can project the future, you must understand where your money is actually going right now. This involves categorizing every expense into fixed and variable costs. Fixed costs, such as rent, insurance, and software subscriptions, remain relatively stable month over month. Variable costs, including raw materials, marketing spend, and discretionary hiring, fluctuate based on demand and strategic decisions. By clearly distinguishing between these two types, you gain visibility into which areas offer savings potential and which are non-negotiable commitments. This clarity prevents the common pitfall of allocating funds to new initiatives while ignoring bloating operational costs that quietly erode profit margins.

One of the most significant challenges in budget planning is the gap between theoretical projections and actual performance. It is tempting to borrow figures from last year with only a minor inflation adjustment, but this approach ignores the unique variables of the current environment. Analysts recommend building in contingency buffers, typically ranging from five to ten percent depending on the risk profile of the industry. These buffers act as shock absorbers for unforeseen events, such as supply chain disruptions or sudden changes in regulatory compliance. Failing to include such margins often leads to mid-year freezes where critical projects are shelved because the cash had been overcommitted to optimistic growth scenarios that failed to materialize.

Integration of departmental goals into the overall financial plan ensures that budgeting is not merely an accounting exercise but a strategic tool. When marketing teams understand their specific allocation and the expected return on investment for their campaigns, they become partners in fiscal control rather than adversaries demanding unlimited resources. Subject: Garden Pest Control Recommendations for a Healthier Harvest
Dear Margaret,
I hope you're enjoying the early signs of summer in your garden. As you mentioned during our last conversation, you've been noticing an uptick in aphids on your roses and some gnats around the lettuce beds. I've taken a look at the recent pest reports for our area and put together a few practical steps that should help you keep the insects under control while preserving the beneficial insects you've worked hard to attract.
First, it's worth doing a quick walk-through of the garden each morning to spot any new infestations before they spread. A gentle spray of water on the undersides of leaves can dislodge many aphids, and if you catch them early, you can often prevent them from reproducing. For the gnats, allowing the topsoil to dry out a bit between watering cycles disrupts their breeding cycle, as the larvae thrive in constantly moist conditions.
When you do need to intervene more directly, I recommend starting with the least intrusive methods. Neem oil applied at a low concentration works well against both aphids and soft-bodied insects, and it has the added benefit of being safe for pollinators once it dries. You can also try a homemade soap spray-one teaspoon of mild liquid soap per quart of water-sprayed onto the affected foliage. Make sure to test a small leaf first to avoid any unexpected leaf burn.
If the pressure from pests becomes severe, a targeted chemical treatment might be necessary, but it's best to reserve that as a last resort. Look for products that are labeled for use on edible crops and have a short re-entry interval, such as spinosad. Apply it only to the plants that are showing the most damage, and follow the label directions carefully to minimize impact on beneficial insects like lady beetles and lacewings, which can help keep the pest populations in check.
Lastly, consider adding some companion plants that naturally repel the troublemakers you're dealing with. Marigolds can deter nematodes and some leaf-eating insects, while a border of herbs such as mint, rosemary, and thyme can help keep aphids at bay. Planting these around the perimeter of your vegetable beds not only adds visual interest but also creates a fragrant barrier that many pests find unappealing.
Feel free to give these suggestions a try over the next couple of weeks and let me know how they work for you. If you encounter any new challenges or need clarification on application rates, just drop me a line. I'm happy to help you keep your garden thriving and pest-free.
Warm regards,
James Whitaker
Integrated Pest Management Specialist
GreenThumb Horticulture Services
Phone: (555) 842-3179
Email: jwhitaker@greenthumb.com

Steelyard balance

A steelyard balance, steelyard, or stilyard is a straight-beam balance with arms of unequal length. It incorporates a counterweight which slides along the longer arm to counterbalance the load and indicate its weight. A steelyard is also known as a Roman steelyard or Roman balance.

The steelyard comprises a balance beam which is suspended from a lever/pivot or fulcrum which is very close to one end of the beam. The two parts of the beam which flank the pivot are the arms. The arm from which the object to be weighed (the load) is hung is short and is located close to the pivot point. The other arm is longer, is graduated and incorporates a counterweight which can be moved along the arm until the two arms are balanced about the pivot, at which time the weight of the load is indicated by the position of the counterweight.

The steelyard exemplifies the law of the lever, wherein, when balanced, the net moment around the pivot must be zero. Since M = F d {\displaystyle M=Fd} , the weight of the object being weighed multiplied by the length of the short balance arm to which it is attached is equal to the weight of the counterweight multiplied by the distance of the counterweight from the pivot.

According to Thomas G. Chondros of Patras University, a simple steelyard balance with a lever mechanism first appeared in the ancient Near East over 5,000 years ago. According to Mark Sky of Harvard University, the steelyard was in use among Greek craftsmen of the 5th and 4th centuries BC, even before Archimedes demonstrated the law of the lever theoretically. The Latin name statera comes from the Ancient Greek στατήρ (statḗr). Roman and Chinese steelyards were independently invented around 200 BC. Steelyards dating from AD 100 to 400 have been unearthed in Great Britain. Steelyards and their components have also been excavated from shipwrecks of the Byzantine period in the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, such as the 7th-century wreck at Yassi Ada, Turkey, and the mid-first millennium shipwreck at Black Assarca Island, Eritrea. The Oxford English Dictionary suggests that the name "steelyard" is derived from steel combined with yard, influenced by an allusion to the Steelyard, the main trading base of the Hanseatic League in London in the 14th century.

Large steelyard balances (known as cart steelyards), both public and private, were a common feature in agricultural areas in England from the eighteenth century forward. An example of a public cart steelyard remains at Soham, Cambridgeshire, and another is at Woodbridge, Suffolk.

Steelyards of different sizes have been used to weigh loads ranging from ounces to tons. A small steelyard could be a foot or less in length and thus conveniently used as a portable device that merchants and traders could use to weigh small ounce-sized items of merchandise. Small steelyard-type rocker balances were also made to weigh and gauge coins. An English example made around 1840, Simmons's Improved Sovereign Balance, was designed for sovereigns and half-sovereigns and checked both their diameter and thickness. In other cases a steelyard could be several feet long and used to weigh sacks of flour and other commodities. Even larger steelyards were three stories tall and used to weigh fully laden horse-drawn waggons.

A steelyard could be used to measure electric current. in 1856 Wildman Whitehouse announced his method of using magnetic coils, representing the load be measured, at one end of a steelyard balance. The position of the moving weight on the balance was adjusted in the usual way to counter the pull of the coils. Whitehouse claimed that his invention gave a steadier reading of current passing through telegraph cables under test than the galvanometers then commonly used.

A horizontal cart balance or cart steelyard has grooved plates, mounted on pivoted frames, to receive the wheels of a cart. The movement of the frames is transferred to a conventional steelyard, mounted on a post, by a horizontal chain. In 1870, a patent was granted to the North British Railway for a similar apparatus to weigh railway waggons. A printed paper chart is mounted behind the steelyard weight, which has a pin attached. When the waggon is in place the pin is made to strike the chart, providing an automatic record of the weight.

Edward is helped in his search by Clarence (Michael Caine), an elderly ex-magician in the early stages of dementia who has recently entered the home. Frustrated with having all of the residents in his home (he has lost his room, TV control and general privacy and freedom), Edward sets off the fire alarm. While everyone is out in the rain, he wreaks havoc alone inside. The next day, Edward passes Clarence's van on his way to school. Its engine is running, and Edward opens the door to a cloud of carbon monoxide. While Clarence is hospitalised, Edward looks through his possessions. Clarence has lots of show bills of his past magic acts. Edward visits Clarence in the hospital, bringing a few things and apologising. From this point on, the film follows their quest and their friendship, which ultimately allows both Edward and Clarence to come to terms with their respective situations. Edward shows Clarence a peculiar ritual he does, trying to contact the dead. Magic interests both of them, so Edward learns some tricks to show the other children at school. On his birthday Clarence takes them out in the van, but he gets confused at a roundabout, causing a pile up. They cannot get the van started again, so a frustrated Clarence empties it, pushes it into the water, then argues with Edward saying there is no afterlife. Angry, the boy stomps off. Later on, the home throws a party for Edward's birthday. He is not enthused, until Clarence offers to do magic. The card tricks go well, but one where Clarence is meant to pretend to cut off a finger goes wrong. Edward organises a bus trip to Clarence's wife's grave. His dementia begins to show, as does not believe it is her grave. Edwards' parents pick them up. He believes Edward's mum is his dead estranged wife, so she accepts his apology. Clarence quietly dies, but Edward has grown emotionally and, as his parents earlier on had had some problems, they decide to give it another try.

Pauli Lovejoy

In 2005, Pauli won the Young Drummer of The Year award and performed on the BBC's Blue Peter. In 2008, Pauli was appointed the role as music director for MOBO award-winning artist Jahaziel and platinum selling artist Eliza Doolittle. They have also appeared in acclaimed music videos for Duffy, Jordin Sparks, Shingai Shinowa (Noisettes), Raghav and Mutya Buena (Sugababes/MKS). In 2009, at age 20, Pauli started working with Gorillaz, which features the Grammy Award-winning cartoon band's music remixed to visual effects and toured with the outfit, playing corporate club shows and headlining festivals around the world. Playing with Gorillaz Sound System introduced Stanley-McKenzie to Africa Express, which led to his contribution in the collective's international shows and the Cultural Olympiad UK train tour, playing alongside Paul McCartney, John Paul Jones, and a host of African musicians including Tony Allen, Baaba Maal and Amadou and Miriam. In January 2014, it was announced that Stanley-McKenzie would play drums for Damon Albarn on tour in support of his debut solo album Everyday Robots, alongside Seye, Jeff Wootton and Mike Smith.

In December 2014, Pauli wrote "Give Me A Sign" which premiered on The Fader and championed by Stereogum as a "Protest Song" was dedicated to Mike Brown, Eric Garner, Rafael Ramos & Wenjian Liu, this was a collaboration with Brooklyn-based oil painter Amar Stewart and marked the first solo recording under the guise "Pauli Lovejoy". The music for "Give Me a Sign" was co-produced with Brooklyn-based music producer and artist "Heavy Mellow". In 2015, Pauli served as a music director for FKA twigs' headline 'Congregata' shows in London (Roundhouse / Alexander McQueen), New York (Red Bull Music Academy), Glastonbury (West Holts Headline), LA (FYF Fest Headline) and at the MOBO Awards. Subsequently, this led to working with FKA twigs' label-mate, Jamie xx as music director for the live promo of his debut record 'In Colour,' which saw Pauli directing live performances on Le Grand Journal (Canal+) (Paris) and Late Night with Seth Meyers. Still recognized as a prominent music influencer, Pauli was called upon as the primary talent for the Tanqueray "Greatness Starts at Ten" campaign. On 24 September 2015, "i DON'T CARE" had its radio debut on Zane Lowe's Beats 1 radio show on Apple Music. The accompanying video premiered on Noisey. On 27 October 2016, "Waiting (Getting On This Train)" the first single from his forthcoming EP, THE IDEA OF TOMORROW premiered on Zane Lowe's Apple Music Beats 1 radio show. That same week, The Fader included "Waiting" on their playlist of "11 Songs You Need in Your Life This Week.". In addition, "Waiting" was featured on Wonderland Magazine's Tracks of the Week Playlist. "Believe in Me" the second single from THE IDEA OF TOMORROW, premiered on Complex. and had its first radio play on Annie Mac's BBC Radio 1 show. Apple Music included the single on their Best of The Week Playlist. "Believe in Me" garnered attention from Dazed and Nylon. On 9 December 2016 Pauli released his debut EP, THE IDEA OF TOMORROW, with long-time collaborator and fellow London-producer Kwes on Kobalt. In partnership with social media app, Vero, Pauli premiered his Visual EP, THE IDEA OF TOMORROW, an afrofuturist fairytale set on Kepler-452b, directed by Rohan Blair-Mangat. Pauli states "there is a vital synergy between my music and the visuals (as will be demonstrated with my forthcoming releases)." In 2017 Pauli debuted his first live show as a solo artist during Paris Fashion Week at Les Bains Paris. Their EP Secret Life of a Badman was released December 20, 2018. Throughout the spring of 2021, Pauli released singles that culminated in the EP Secret Life of a Badman (Vol.2) which was released May 21, 2021. Later that year, they joined Harry Styles' band as a percussionist and MD for Love on Tour.

Lovejoy served as the opening act for Irish rock band U2 during their 2023-2024 concert residency, U2:UV Achtung Baby Live, at Sphere in the Las Vegas Valley. During the pre-show, they DJ'ed music from inside a neon Trabant that moved around the general admission area.

NFL Quarterback Club (video game)

NFL Quarterback Club is an American football video game for multiple platforms that features quarterbacks from the NFL. It is the first game in Acclaim Entertainment's NFL Quarterback Club series. The first game to use the name was a Game Boy title developed by Beam Software and released under Acclaim's LJN brand in 1993 that was a simulation of the NFL Quarterback Challenge. The following year, Acclaim and LJN released a new multiplatform title under the same name, adding options to play full team games under NFL rules, while retaining the Quarterback Challenge mode. The game was released for the Super NES, Genesis and Game Gear. A Game Boy version, called NFL Quarterback Club II and a 32X version were released in 1995. Both these versions omitted the Quarterback Challenge mode, a trend that would continue with NFL Quarterback Club 96.

In 1994, NFL Quarterback Club was released for the SNES. The main appeal about the game is that it offers three different types of modes to play in, making it more like three games in one. Up to four different players can play at the same time. The game takes its name from the "QB Challenge". Players can choose from more than 12 of the NFL's premier quarterbacks to take part in a competition. There are four events in the competition. These are Accuracy, The Obstacle Course, Distance and Read And Recognition. Accuracy involves throwing the ball toward targets. The Obstacle Course is a track where the quarterback must jump over hurdles and go around defenders. Distance competition involves throwing the ball as far as possible, while Read And Recognition is the same as Accuracy but only certain targets hold point values. The QB with the highest number of points at the end of all four events is the winner. Each event can also be played individually if a player chooses to do so. Custom quarterbacks can be created to take part in the challenge. As the quarterback improves, his skill level increases. The second mode is "Play NFL" and features playing a regular football game. Options include preseason, regular season play and direct playoff entry. All NFL teams are available. The player can import custom quarterbacks into a team, and also has the option of substituting quarterbacks from different teams into it. The third mode is "Simulation". There are 30 scenarios from previous games that a player must complete. Some scenarios have as little as ten seconds left in the game, while others begin with more than 15 minutes of playing time left.

The Game Boy version, also known as NFL Quarterback Club 95, simulated the NFL Quarterback Challenge and featured 13 quarterbacks, including Troy Aikman, Warren Moon, Jim Kelly and John Elway. Players select one of them and compete in four different events representing different quarterback skills: Speed and Mobility, Accuracy, Distance and Read and Recognition.

GamePro gave the SNES version a positive review, and said the Speed & Mobility event is the game's "one weak feature". They praised the diverse range of modes, the camera views, the accessibility of the playbook, and the variety of moves the players can pull off. They panned the Game Gear version, however, criticizing that it removes key modes, features, and sound effects from the console versions, and pointing out that gamers looking for a football game for the Game Gear could get the superior Madden NFL '95. Reviewing the 32X version, they praised the new camera views but criticized the removed of the Quarterback Challenge skills contest and concluded that players who owned the Genesis or SNES versions had no need to get the game again. They also criticized the gameplay balance, commenting that "you can ferret out a handful of plays that make any club invincible. If you like scoring 90-plus points on the Cowboys or the Niners all the time, you'll love this cart!" A reviewer for Next Generation also highly praised the camera views feature, calling it "the future in sports games." However, he concluded, "The gameplay in 32X's Quarterback Club is far superior to its 16-bit counterparts, but the lack of a players license, and no individual statistics keep this game from being the groundbreaking title it may have been." He gave it three out of five stars. Next Generation, reviewing the Genesis version, felt that its perceived lack of emphasis on the quality of the main gameplay in favor of the extra modes prevented the game from being a competitor with other, bigger sports games.

Subject: Lab Safety Rules Reminder
Dear Team,
I hope this message finds you well. As we head into the busy season of experiments and data collection, I want to take a moment to reaffirm our commitment to a safe working environment. Recent observations have highlighted a few lapses that, while not resulting in injury, remind us how easily accidents can occur in a laboratory setting. By consistently following the safety protocols we have in place, we protect not only ourselves but also our colleagues, the integrity of our research, and the reputation of our institution.
First and foremost, please remember that personal protective equipment (PPE) is non-negotiable in any area where chemicals, biological agents, or sharp objects are present. Lab coats must be worn with sleeves fully covering the arms, and any open-toed shoes or sandals should be replaced with closed, sturdy footwear. Safety glasses or goggles should be used whenever there is a risk of splashes, and gloves must be selected based on the specific material you are handling. If you notice a colleague without the appropriate PPE, kindly remind them of the requirement; safety is a shared responsibility.
When working with chemicals, meticulous attention to labeling, storage, and handling procedures is essential. All containers should be clearly labeled with the substance name, concentration, hazard symbols, and the date received. Never mix chemicals unless you have verified compatibility and consulted the safety data sheet (SDS). Use a fume hood for volatile or toxic substances, and keep the sash at the recommended height to ensure optimal airflow. In the event of a spill, contain it immediately using the appropriate absorbent material and follow the spill response protocol outlined in our lab manual.
Emergency preparedness is another critical component of our safety culture. The locations of fire extinguishers, eyewash stations, safety showers, and first-aid kits are posted throughout the facility; please familiarize yourself with these spots during each shift change. If a fire alarm sounds, evacuate the area calmly and proceed to the designated assembly point, reporting any missing personnel to the safety officer. Should a chemical splash reach your eyes or skin, activate the nearest eyewash or shower station without delay and seek medical attention if the irritation persists. All incidents, however minor, must be documented in the incident log within 24 hours.
Proper waste disposal and housekeeping also play a vital role in minimizing hazards. Segregate waste according to the categories of chemical, biological, and sharps, and place it in the correctly labeled containers. Never overfill waste bins, and be sure to seal and label them before transport to the central disposal area. Keep work surfaces clean and free of unnecessary clutter; a tidy bench reduces the chance of accidental knocks, spills, and cross-contamination. At the end of each day, ensure that all equipment is turned off, chemicals are capped, and the area is left in a safe, orderly state for the next user.
Finally, I encourage each of you to review the laboratory safety handbook and complete the annual refresher training if you have not already done so. Should you have any questions about a particular procedure or need clarification on a safety rule, please do not hesitate to reach out to me or the designated safety officer. By staying vigilant and adhering to these guidelines, we can maintain a productive and accident-free research environment.
Best regards,
Dr. Elena Ramirez 
Head of Research Operations 
University Science Department

Senta flammea

The flame wainscot (Senta flammea) is a species of moth of the family Noctuidae. It is found from Europe and across the Palearctic to Japan, but is not found on the Iberian Peninsula, the islands in the Mediterranean Sea, Greece and central and southern Italy.

M. flammea Curt. (= dubiosa Tr., arundinicola Dbl.) (25 k). Forewing rufous grey speckled with brown along inner margin; paler grey with the veins white in costal third; middle third occupied by an olive brown streak widening and paling outwardly; the veins pale, the intervals brownish; an outer series of dark dots on veins: hindwing pale grey, the fringe white. - the form occurring in Amurland, stenoptera Stgr. is smaller, with the fore-wing still narrower, and the brown central streak more distinct. - Larva pale putty-colour; the lines pale with grey edges, the spiracular whiter. The wingspan is 32-40 mm.

The moth flies from May to June depending on the location. The larvae feed on Phragmites, including Phragmites australis hiding by day and ultimately pupating in the old cut reedstems.

Subject: Important Update Regarding Dormitory Policies and Quiet Hours
Dear Residents,
I hope this email finds you well as we navigate through the busy semester. I am writing to you today to share some crucial updates regarding the communal living spaces and the regulations that govern our dormitory life. It is essential that everyone understands these rules not just as arbitrary restrictions, but as guidelines designed to ensure a safe, respectful, and conducive environment for learning and rest. As we move deeper into the term, maintaining a high standard of community etiquette becomes increasingly vital for the well-being of all participants in our residential halls.
The first area of focus is our updated noise control policies. Effective immediately, quiet hours have been extended to begin at 9:00 PM on weekdays and 10:00 PM on weekends, lasting until 8:00 AM the following day. During these intervals, interior music must be kept at a moderate volume that does not carry through to adjacent units or common areas. We have received numerous complaints regarding late-night parties and excessive sound levels in the basement lounge, so please be advised that violations during these times will result in immediate disciplinary action, starting with a formal warning and potentially leading to fines or reprimands. We value study time and sleep as much as social bonding, so please respect your neighbors by planning your social gatherings with appropriate timing and volume considerations.
Additionally, we are reinforcing the zero-tolerance policy regarding unauthorized cooking appliances and safety hazards. Any items that do not carry a recognized safety certification, such as space heaters, hot plates, or microwaves that are not provided by the housing office, are strictly prohibited in private rooms. The fire marshal's recent visit highlighted that most incidents in residential buildings stem from unmonitored electrical devices or unattended cooking attempts. Please dispose of any non-compliant items by the end of this week. The front desk will be available to collect these items if you prefer not to transport them yourself. Your safety is our top priority, and non-compliance puts the entire building at risk.
Regarding housekeeping and waste management, please ensure that all communal areas, including kitchens, laundry rooms, and lounges, are left clean after use. Disposables should be separated according to the posted recycling guidelines, and food waste should be securely bagged before disposal to prevent odors and pest infestations. Staff have noted a significant increase in mold growth in two of the ground-floor showers due to improper ventilation use. Please make it a habit to leave the bathroom door slightly ajar when using the facilities for extended periods, or use the exhaust fan for at least ten minutes after each shower to maintain proper air circulation.
I kindly ask that you review the full handbook available on the housing portal for detailed clauses regarding guest policies and guest host responsibilities. We appreciate your cooperation and prompt attention to these matters. If you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to reach out to the office via email or during our weekly office hours. Thank you for your commitment to keeping our dormitory a harmonious and secure home away from home.
Sincerely,
Sarah Jenkins
Dormitory Management Office
