hiking trail conditions

The high country trails of the Blue Ridge range have been drawing hikers in droves this weekend, but the recent rainstorm that swept through the valleys on Thursday has left the terrain far from the usual dry, well-marked pathways. Park rangers report that several popular routes are now slick with mud, and some sections of the longer loops have seen small washouts that could catch an unsuspecting foot. For anyone planning a day hike or a weekend trek, taking a moment to check the latest conditions can mean the difference between a rewarding adventure and a frustrating detour.

According to the latest bulletin from the forest service, the weather front that moved in overnight deposited an average of 1.8 inches of rain across the eastern slopes, with higher elevations receiving up to three inches. The water has seeped into the soil, making the ground unusually soft and prone to erosion. Trailheads at Pinecrest and Cedar Grove show clear signage warning hikers of potential slide zones, while the lower-elevation loop around Oak Lake remains passable but has several muddy patches near the creek crossings. The park's website notes that the stream levels are currently two feet above normal, which could affect bridge stability later this afternoon.

On the more rugged sections of the Ridgecrest Trail, the combination of steep grades and saturated earth has already caused a few minor landslides. Hikers who attempted the summit last night reported that the scree field near the midway point was slick, and one rockfall was observed near the 4.2-mile marker, where a large boulder had shifted slightly. The western side of the trail, which skirts the old quarry, shows exposed roots that have become hidden under a thin layer of mud, creating a hidden slipping hazard. Meanwhile, the popular "Sunset Loop" still offers scenic vistas, but the final descent into the meadow is now marked with orange cones to indicate a temporary detour around a washed-out segment.

If you decide to hit the trails today, a few precautions can help you stay safe. Waterproof boots with good ankle support are essential, as is a trekking pole to provide extra balance on slick sections. Pack a lightweight rain jacket, even if the sky looks clear, because showers can develop quickly at higher elevations. Keep an eye on the trail markers and obey any temporary closures posted by rangers; these are usually placed where the path is most vulnerable to further damage. For families with young children, consider shorter loops that stay on higher, firmer ground, and always carry a map and a fully charged phone in case you need to call for assistance.

The forest service updates its trail conditions page every four hours, and you can also follow the park's official social-media accounts for real-time photos and alerts. Many local hiking clubs operate a community forum where members share recent experiences and post cautionary notes about specific sections. If you're unsure about a particular route, stop by the visitor center before you head out; the rangers there can give you the most current information and suggest alternative paths that are still in good shape. Signing up for the park's email newsletter is another easy way to receive weather warnings and trail closure notices directly in your inbox.

With the right preparation and a willingness to adapt your plans, the Blue Ridge trails can still provide a memorable outdoor experience despite the recent weather. Stay informed, respect the temporary hazards, and enjoy the fresh scent of rain-kissed forest as you explore the beautiful scenery that the area is known for.

Douglas Is Cancelled

Douglas Is Cancelled is a 2024 British television four-part comedy-drama created and written by Steven Moffat, directed by Ben Palmer and starring Hugh Bonneville, Karen Gillan and Alex Kingston. It was first aired weekly from 27 June 2024 on ITV1, with all four episodes made immediately available on ITVX on that date.

Douglas Bellowes is a widely respected television news anchor, whose life begins to unravel when he is accused on social media of making a sexist joke at a wedding.

Hugh Bonneville as Douglas Bellowes, lead presenter for Live at Six news Karen Gillan as Madeline Crow, Douglas's co-presenter Alex Kingston as Sheila Bellowes, Douglas's wife and a newspaper editor Nick Mohammed as Morgan, a comedy writer working for Live at Six Simon Russell Beale as Bently, Douglas's agent Ben Miles as Toby, Douglas's producer Madeleine Power as Claudia Bellowes, Douglas's daughter and political activist Joe Wilkinson as Tom, Toby's driver Kirsty Wark as Interviewer

.

The series was written by Steven Moffat, directed by Ben Palmer, and produced by Hartswood Films in association with SkyShowtime and BBC Studios Distribution. Moffat also serves as executive producer alongside his wife Sue Vertue, with Lawrence Till as producer. Moffat described writing the script "in secret".

The entire series has been available in the UK on ITVX since 27 June 2024, and was aired weekly on ITV1 from 27 June to 18 July 2024. In Australia, it is available to stream on ABC iview.

On Rotten Tomatoes, 77% of 26 reviews are positive for the miniseries. The critics' consensus on the website states: "While this satire's scattershot aim at thorny topics doesn't hit every target, Hugh Bonneville's expertly hapless performance makes it a squirmy pleasure to watch." On Metacritic, it received an average score of 61 based on 13 critics reviews. Amber Dowling of The Globe and Mail writes that the miniseries "makes the case for character studies, deeply examining characters as they are in the moment, and proves that, sometimes, it's more compelling to present people at their core and allow viewers to draw their own conclusions". In The Times, Carol Midgley describes the "claustrophobic intensity" of the third episode as "excruciating. Mostly in a good way". Writing for The A.V. Club, Tim Lowery stated that the "tonal shift [...] almost lands. But the workplace-comedy trappings and quips that can make this watch enjoyable [...] often feel at odds with the serious things Moffat is trying to say and portray. And it's hard not to walk away thinking that another British miniseries, last year's A Very Royal Scandal [...] not only got there first-but did it better." Gillan was nominated for Best Actress (film and television) at the 2025 British Academy Scotland Awards.

Dawood bin Abdulaziz Mohammed Al-Shirian (Arabic: داود عبدالعزيز محمد الشريان; born August 15, 1954) is a Saudi journalist, media proprietor, and television presenter known for leading the national television broadcaster in Saudi Arabia.

Al-Shirian began his career as a journalist in 1976. He worked with Al Jazirah newspaper and later became the managing editor of Al Yamamah magazine. In 1980, he became the first Saudi correspondent for the international news agency Associated Press. He also held numerous positions, including serving as the general manager and editor-in-chief (EIC) of Al Dawa magazine. Al-Shirian worked at Dubai TV for three years and hosted the program Journalism Interface on Al-Arabiya TV. During his time at Dubai TV, he presented the weekly political program The Article. He served as the EIC of the Al-Arabiya website and was a member of both the Al-Arabiya Council and the Middle East Broadcasting Center (MBC) Council. He was also the general manager of MBC in Saudi Arabia. From 2012 to 2017, Al-Shirian hosted television programs on the Middle East Broadcasting Center, including Al-Thamina Ma'a Dawood (Eight o'clock with Dawood).

In 2017, he was appointed President of the Saudi Broadcasting Corporation (SBC), a major Saudi national TV network. In this role, he oversaw the launch and development of SBC's programming, which includes entertainment, drama, and cultural content as part of Saudi Arabia's effort to expand and modernize its media industry.

Subject: Update on Upcoming Drone Regulations for Commercial Operators
Dear Team,
I wanted to bring you up to speed on the new drone regulations that will take effect next quarter. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has released a draft rule set that expands the mandatory registration requirements to include all unmanned aerial systems over 0.5 kilograms, regardless of commercial or recreational use. This means that many of the devices we currently operate will need to be logged in the national database and display a visible registration number on the airframe.
In addition to registration, the proposed rules introduce stricter operational limits around populated areas and critical infrastructure. Operators will be required to maintain a minimum distance of 500 feet from schools, hospitals, and government buildings, unless a specific waiver is obtained. The FAA is also tightening the altitude ceiling for low-altitude flights, capping it at 400 feet above ground level for most non-certified operations, with higher limits only allowed in designated airspace.
To ensure we remain compliant, I recommend that all pilots complete the updated online training module by the end of the month. The module covers the new reporting procedures, flight planning tools, and the process for applying for waivers where necessary. Once you finish the course, please forward your certification to the compliance office so we can update our internal records.
We are also setting up a quarterly review meeting with our legal counsel to monitor any further adjustments to the rulemaking process. If you have any concerns about how these changes might affect your current projects, please let me know as soon as possible so we can address them before the implementation deadline.
Thank you for your attention to this matter and for your continued commitment to safe and responsible drone operations.
Best regards,
Jordan Lee 
Director of UAV Operations 
Skyline Aerial Services

hiking trail conditions

The morning mist clings to the canopy, a deceptive sign that the trailhead parking lot might be empty if you arrive before seven. Current conditions report heavy overnight rains across the northern ridge, turning the switchbacks into slick mud pits that demand traction in every step. Rangers advise hikers to check the latest weather reports before setting out, as rapid temperature drops can flash-freeze lingering moisture on the stone steps, creating treacherous ice patches.

Lower elevations remain passable for most, but the upper alpine sections have closed due to unstable snowpack. Reporters on the ground noted the river crossing at Mile Four is currently swollen and rushing, making the standard rope-ledge crossing unsafe for smaller groups. Detour routes are marked with orange blazes, adding roughly forty minutes of walk time, but they bypass the dangerous water entirely.

.

Gear considerations have shifted from standard hiking basics to specialized needs. Microspikes are no longer a luxury for late-season hikers but a necessity for anyone attempting the summit loop. Layering is critical; hikers should bring waterproof shells and warm mid-layers, as wind chills near the peak can drop below freezing even when valley temperatures hover in the fifties.

Visibility near the tree line is currently poor due to low cloud cover rolling in from the west. This creates additional navigation challenges, particularly near the ridge spine where cairns can be obscured by fog. GPS backups are strongly recommended, and hikers should file their itinerary with local authorities to ensure safety in case they become disoriented or stuck in rising mist.

The trail crew is on-site this week clearing fallen branches and repairing washed-out sections of the boardwalk. While efforts are underway, expect minor delays and potential reroutes around debris fields. The park remains open, but visitors must exercise extreme caution and respect the volatile nature of wet, autumnal terrain. Check back later in the evening for updated status reports as conditions may change rapidly with the afternoon storms.

raw:
Shire of Mount Marshall

The Shire of Mount Marshall is a local government area in the Wheatbelt region of Western Australia, about 80 kilometres (50 mi) north-northwest of Merredin and about 300 kilometres (186 mi) northeast of the state capital, Perth. The Shire covers an area of 10,190 square kilometres (3,934 sq mi), and its seat of government is the town of Bencubbin.

The first European explorer in the area was Surveyor General John Septimus Roe; Mount Marshall and Lake McDermott were named after early Swan River Colony settler Marshall McDermott, cashier of the Bank of Western Australia, magistrate, and a director of the Agricultural Society of Western Australia. The area was first settled by sandalwood collectors and graziers in 1868. Sandalwood was removed from this area from the 1880s until the 1920s. Permanent settlement and the development and clearing of the land for farms commenced around 1910. The Mount Marshall Road District was established on 6 July 1923 from areas formerly falling within the Ninghan Road District and Nungarin Road District. On 1 July 1961, it became a shire following the passage of the Local Government Act 1960, which reformed all remaining road districts into shires.

The Shire has no wards and each Councillor represents the entire district of the Shire of Mt Marshall as required by the Local Government Act 1995.

The area was first settled by sandalwood collectors and graziers in 1868. Sandalwood was removed from this area from the 1880s until the 1920s. Permanent settlement and the development and clearing of the land for farms commenced around 1910. The Mount Marshall Road District was established on 6 July 1923 from areas formerly falling within the Ninghan Road District and Nungarin Road District. On 1 July 1961, it became a shire following the passage of the Local Government Act 1960, which reformed all remaining road districts into shires.
The Shire has no wards and each Councillor represents the entire district of the Shire of Mt Marshall as required by the Local Government Act 1995.

raw:
wedding venue booking

Selecting the right wedding venue is arguably the most consequential decision a couple makes after determining their budget and guest count. It sets the tone for the entire celebration, influencing everything from the lighting and acoustics to the logistical ease of the day. Many couples make the mistake of falling in love with a photograph online without considering the practical realities of the space. A beautiful château might look stunning in a brochure, but if it requires a two-hour drive for half your invited guests and lacks adequate parking, the sentiment can quickly turn to frustration. Therefore, the initial research phase should be driven by feasibility as much as aesthetics. Define your non-negotiables first, such as the maximum capacity, the need for on-site lodging for out-of-town relatives, and whether you require a dedicated space for pre-ceremony gatherings or post-reception dancing.

Timing is a critical factor that many overlook until it is too late. Popular wedding dates, particularly those falling on mid-summer Saturdays or significant holidays, can become unavailable eighteen to twenty-four months in advance. Conversely, booking a venue for a Friday evening or a Tuesday afternoon often comes with significant financial benefits and greater flexibility in vendor selection. It is advisable to start the search process no later than eight months before your intended date, but earlier is generally safer if you have a specific location in mind. When contacting potential venues, ask about their booking windows and deposit policies immediately. Understanding the contractual obligations early on prevents unpleasant surprises later, such as strict cancellation clauses or non-refundable fee structures that could impact your financial planning.

Site visits should be approached with a critical eye rather than a romantic one. While you want to feel an emotional connection to the space, you must also assess its functionality. Walk through the property as if you were a guest arriving on the day of the event. Check the flow of movement from the ceremony site to the reception hall and back. Is the transition weather-dependent, requiring umbrellas or indoor shelters? Are the restrooms accessible to all guests, including those with mobility issues? Pay close attention to the natural light at the specific time of day you are planning your ceremony, as venues can look drastically different in the morning versus the evening. Furthermore, verify the availability of power outlets for your DJ and photographer, as well as the type of floors available for dancing.

Negotiation is a standard part of the venue booking process, and you should not be afraid to ask for inclusions to be added to your package. Many venues offer base rates that cover the space rental but exclude table settings, linens, or basic audio equipment. By asking for itemized quotes, you can identify areas where the venue might be flexible. For example, some properties will allow you to use their glassware or flatware to save on rental costs, while others might offer a complimentary cake tasting or a free bridal suite for the day. Be transparent about your budget constraints. Venue coordinators are business professionals who understand that retaining a client is often more valuable than maximizing profit on a single transaction. Building a collaborative relationship with the coordinator early on ensures smoother communication throughout the planning process.

Finally, read the fine print of the contract with the same intensity you applied to the romantic aspects of the venue. Understand the weather contingency plans, especially if you are planning an outdoor ceremony inside a beautiful garden. What happens if it rains? Is there a seamlessly connected indoor alternative? Also, clarify the timeline for check-in and check-out times. Knowing exactly when you can start setting up and how long you have to dismantle your decorations protects you from last-minute stress. Sign the contract only when you feel confident in the venue's ability to deliver on their promises. Once the pen is dry, you can begin the creative work of decorating and celebrating, knowing that the foundation of your wedding day is solidly placed.

raw:
public library services

Public libraries have evolved far beyond the quiet stacks of books that many people picture when they think of a "library." Today they function as vibrant community hubs, offering a blend of traditional and digital resources that cater to diverse needs. Whether you're a student looking for research materials, a job seeker needing resume help, or a family searching for after-school programs, the modern public library is designed to be a one-stop support center.

One of the most popular services is the lending of digital media, which includes e-books, audiobooks, and streaming platforms for movies and music. Patrons can access these collections from any device with a library card, eliminating the need for physical visits and expanding the reach of the library's catalogue. Many libraries also provide free Wi-Fi and computer workstations, allowing those without reliable internet at home to stay connected and complete online tasks.

Educational programming has become a cornerstone of library offerings. Workshops on topics such as coding for kids, financial literacy for adults, and language learning for newcomers are scheduled regularly. These sessions are often led by knowledgeable staff or partnered with local experts, ensuring participants receive up-to-date information in a welcoming environment. In addition, storytime events for children and book clubs for adults foster a sense of community and encourage lifelong reading habits.

Beyond learning, public libraries serve as safe spaces for social interaction. Meeting rooms can be reserved by community groups, nonprofit organizations, and even entrepreneurs who need a quiet place to brainstorm or hold presentations. Many libraries also host cultural events like author talks, art exhibitions, and music performances, enriching the cultural fabric of the neighborhood without requiring a costly ticket.

For those navigating life transitions, libraries provide valuable assistance through dedicated reference desks and personalized consultations. Librarians can help locate government forms, guide job seekers to employment resources, and even connect seniors with assistive technologies. These tailored services often go unnoticed but play a critical role in supporting residents during pivotal moments.

Overall, the breadth of public library services reflects a commitment to inclusivity, education, and community well-being. By embracing technology, offering diverse programming, and maintaining a welcoming atmosphere, libraries remain indispensable institutions that adapt to the changing needs of the people they serve. Whether you're stepping in for a quick book checkout or attending a full-day workshop, the public library invites you to explore, learn, and connect.

raw:
volcano science

The ground beneath our feet is far from static. Beneath the crust lies the mantle, a layer of rock that is partially molten due to immense heat and pressure. This mixture, known as magma, behaves much like thick honey, slowly rising through cracks and weaknesses in the Earth's shell. When this pressurized material reaches the surface, we call it lava. The study of this dynamic process is geophysics in its most dramatic and essential form. Understanding why some eruptions are gentle flows while others are explosive blasts helps scientists predict volcanic activity and mitigate the risks they pose to nearby communities.

Volcanic eruptions are primarily driven by the rise of buoyant magma. As magma ascends, the surrounding pressure decreases, causing dissolved gases to expand and form bubbles. This expansion increases the volume of the magma, further reducing its density and propelling it upward. The composition of the magma plays a critical role in how an eruption unfolds. Basaltic magma, which is thin and fluid, tends to flow easily, creating shield volcanoes with gentle, extensive lava fields. In contrast, andesitic and rhyolitic magmas are thicker and more viscous. They trap gases until the pressure builds to a catastrophic point, resulting in violent explosions that can loft ash and rock miles into the atmosphere.

Scientists monitor volcanic activity using a variety of sophisticated tools. Seismographs detect the subtle vibrations of moving magma, providing early warnings of increased pressure. Geodesy techniques, such as GPS and satellite interferometry, measure ground deformation. When magma inflates a volcanic chamber, the ground surface bulges outward. Even tiny movements, less than the width of a human hair, can signal significant subsurface changes. Additionally, gas sensors track emissions of sulfur dioxide and other volatile compounds. A sudden spike in these gases often precedes an eruption, offering crucial time for evacuation and preparedness efforts.

The impact of volcanoes extends far beyond the immediate danger zone. Ash clouds can disrupt air travel for days or weeks, grounding thousands of flights and causing economic losses. Magma can alter water tables, poisoning rivers and lakes with toxic minerals. However, the aftermath of an eruption also brings profound benefits. Volcanic soil is incredibly fertile, enriched with minerals that support robust agriculture. Many of the world's most productive farmlands are situated on ancient volcanic slopes. Furthermore, geothermal energy derived from volcanic heat provides a clean, renewable power source for many regions, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and lowering carbon emissions.

Predicting the exact time and location of an eruption remains one of the greatest challenges in geology. While we can identify areas of high risk and monitor precursors effectively, the transition from dormant to active can be unpredictable. This uncertainty underscores the importance of continuous monitoring and public education. Communities living near active volcanoes must understand the warning signs and have robust emergency plans in place. By respecting the power of the Earth's interior, we can coexist with these natural catastrophes, turning a source of destruction into one of our most valuable resources for understanding our planet's history and future.

Scientists monitor volcanic activity using a variety of sophisticated tools. Seismographs detect the subtle vibrations of moving magma, providing early warnings of increased pressure. Geodesy techniques, such as GPS and satellite interferometry, measure ground deformation. When magma inflates a volcanic chamber, the ground surface bulges outward. Even tiny movements, less than the width of a human hair, can signal significant subsurface changes. Additionally, gas sensors track emissions of sulfur dioxide and other volatile compounds. A sudden spike in these gases often precedes an eruption, offering crucial time for evacuation and preparedness efforts.
The impact of volcanoes extends far beyond the immediate danger zone. Ash clouds can disrupt air travel for days or weeks, grounding thousands of flights and causing economic losses. Magma can alter water tables, poisoning rivers and lakes with toxic minerals. However, the aftermath of an eruption also brings profound benefits. Volcanic soil is incredibly fertile, enriched with minerals that support robust agriculture. Many of the world's most productive farmlands are situated on ancient volcanic slopes. Furthermore, geothermal energy derived from volcanic heat provides a clean, renewable power source for many regions, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and lowering carbon emissions.
Predicting the exact time and location of an eruption remains one of the greatest challenges in geology. While we can identify areas of high risk and monitor precursors effectively, the transition from dormant to active can be unpredictable. This uncertainty underscores the importance of continuous monitoring and public education. Communities living near active volcanoes must understand the warning signs and have robust emergency plans in place. By respecting the power of the Earth's interior, we can coexist with these natural catastrophes, turning a source of destruction into one of our most valuable resources for understanding our planet's history and future.

Theodore Edward Coneys

Theodore Edward Coneys (November 10, 1882 - May 16, 1967), also known by the nickname "Denver Spiderman", was an American drifter who committed the murder of a man whose house he was illegally occupying in 1941, and continued occupying the attic of the victim's home for nine months.

Theodore Coneys was born November 10, 1882, in Petersburg, Illinois, to Thomas H. Coneys (November 18, 1844 - July 1, 1888), a Canadian immigrant who owned a hardware store in Petersburg, and his wife, Isabella Elam (March 1, 1851 - April 14, 1911). After the elder Coneys died in 1888, Mrs. Coneys and her son moved to a farm near Beloit, Wisconsin, then to Denver, Colorado, in 1907, where she worked as a housekeeper at the Denver Democratic Club. She died in 1911. Theodore Coneys suffered from poor health and had been told by doctors not to expect to see his 18th birthday, so he did not finish high school. As an adult, he worked as a bookkeeper at the Denver Brass Works in advertising and sales, yet spent much of his adult life homeless. Coneys resented the way he was treated by others for his frail condition, later expressing that he wanted a place where he could be alone and free from the judgment of others.

In September 1941, 58-year-old Theodore Coneys intended to ask former acquaintance Philip Peters for a handout at his home on 3335 West Moncrieff Place in Denver, Colorado. Coneys broke into the house in Peters' absence to steal food and money. In the ceiling of a closet, Coneys found a small trapdoor that led to a narrow attic cubbyhole and decided to occupy the small space without Peters' knowledge. Coneys lived in the house undiscovered for about five weeks. On October 17, 1941, Peters discovered Coneys at the refrigerator. Peters struck at Coneys with a cane he carried, but Coneys clubbed him with an old pistol he had found in the house. After the gun broke apart, Coneys continued the battery with a heavy iron stove shaker and bludgeoned the 73-year-old Peters to death. Coneys then returned to the attic cubbyhole. Peters' body was discovered later the same day after a neighbor, concerned Peters had not come by for dinner, called the police. The police found all of the home's doors and windows locked, and there was no other sign of forced entry. They noted the trapdoor but believed a normal-sized person could not fit through it. Peters' wife, who had been in the hospital recuperating from a broken hip during and prior to Coneys' occupation of the attic, returned to live in the house with a housekeeper. Both women would often hear strange sounds in the house. The housekeeper quit after becoming convinced the house was haunted and Mrs. Peters moved to western Colorado to live with her son. Mabel Berke and her five children lived next door to the house and would consistently see lights going on and off, once even arming herself with a baseball bat and knocking on the door. Coneys remained in the vacant house with the occasional signs of his occupation written off as an apparition or local pranksters. Police continued to make routine checks, when on July 30, 1942, one of them heard a lock click on the second floor. Running upstairs, the police caught the sight of Coneys' legs as he was going through the trapdoor and pulled him down. He was taken into police custody and confessed to the crime. Local newspapers dubbed him "The Sneaky Sneaky Spider-Man of Denver" after police detective Fred Zarnow remarked "A man would have to be a spider to stand it long up there." Coneys was tried and convicted, then sentenced to life imprisonment at the Colorado State Penitentiary in Cañon City, Colorado.

Theodore Coneys died on May 16, 1967, at the Colorado State Penitentiary prison hospital. He was interred at Mountain Vale Cemetery in Cañon City. The case was referenced in Erle Stanley Gardner's 1956 Cool and Lam novel "Beware the Curves". Two episodes of popular American television shows appear to have been inspired by the Denver Spiderman story, the CSI: Crime Scene Investigation episode "Stalker" and The Simpsons episode "The Ziff Who Came to Dinner". Cartoonist Noah Van Sciver drew the story of the case for volume 15 of the comics anthology MOME in 2009.

Valérie Donzelli

Valérie Donzelli (born 2 March 1973) is a French actress and filmmaker. She has directed six feature films and two short films since 2008, including Declaration of War (2011), Just the Two of Us (2023) and At Work (2025).

Valérie Donzelli was born in Épinal (France). She grew up in Créteil, near Paris. She moved to Lille with her family when she was 14 years old before going back to Paris at the age of 19. Before starting to work in the cinema, Donzelli first studied architecture, but abandoned it quickly. She started playing theatre at the municipal conservatory of the 10th arrondissement of Paris, but always kept a bad memory of this period. For a living, she worked at a bakery in Paris. She met Jérémie Elkaïm at that time, who became her partner, both in life and at work, and who encouraged her to quit the conservatory and her job at the bakery to become an actress. They now have two kids; the oldest one, Gabriel, inspired the movie Declaration of War. They are now separated, but still have a close relationship.

In 2001, Valérie Donzelli was the leading actress in Martha Martha, by Sandrine Veysset, which was presented at Directors' Fortnight, Le Plus Beau Jour de ma vie, and also Entre ses mains. She achieved great success among French public thanks to the French TV show Clara Sheller (2005), in which she plays Jeanne, best friend of the main character. Donzelli's first film, The Queen of Hearts (La Reine des Pommes), in which she was the leading actress, was more successful than expected. Jérémie Elkaïm is also co-writer. The film was presented at Locarno International Film Festival. Despite its low budget, the film can be considered a success because of its 30,000 spectators. In 2011, with the help of her now ex-partner Jérémie Elkaïm, Valérie Donzelli directed her second full-length feature film, Declaration of War. This movie, presented during the 2011 Cannes Festival, achieved great success, both with the public and critics, in France. It is directly inspired by their private life, relating how their couple fought against their son's cancer when he was 18 months. As Tim Palmer notes, "Declaration of War serves as an emblematic, even quintessential, contemporary French production: a barometer to gauge film industry standards and prevailing French cultural taste, a standard-bearer of ostensibly progressive materials, an ambassador text for French screen values." The movie was selected for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 2012, but was not part of the final list. Donzelli directed once again Jérémie Elkaïm in Hand in Hand (2012), with also Valérie Lemercier in the leading role. Donzelli considers that this is always a politic and engaged gesture to make films as women, and admires Agnès Varda for her work and her status of first women filmmaker into French Cinema. Valérie Donzelli is part of the jury during Locarno International Film Festival in 2013. She presents Que d'Amour!, a TV adaptation from the play The Game of Love and Chance (Le Jeu de l'Amour et du Hasard), by Marivaux, with Comédie-Française' sociétaires.

Her 2015 film Marguerite & Julien was selected to compete for the Palme d'Or at the 2015 Cannes Film Festival. She was named as the president of the jury of the Critics' Week section of the 2016 Cannes Film Festival.

2010: Public Prize at the Angers European First Film Festival for The Queen of Hearts 2011: Valois d'Or at Festival du film francophone d'Angoulême for Declaration of War 2012: Grand Prix at Cabourg Film Festival for Declaration of War 2012: Jury Prize, Public Prize, and Bloggers Prix at the Festival Paris Cinéma for Declaration of War 2012: Étoile d'or du meilleur scénario for Declaration of War Nomination for Best film for Declaration of War, Cesar Awards 2012 Nomination for Best Director for Declaration of War, Cesar Awards 2012 Nomination for Best Actress for Declaration of War, Cesar Awards 2012 Nomination for Best Original Screenplay for Declaration of War, Cesar Awards 2012

Valerie Donzelli se tourne vers la télévision pour son prochain film "Un film dansé pour Valérie Donzelli", Cahiers du cinéma, no 670, septembre 2011, p. 62 La Guerre est déclarée [archive], sur jpbox-office.com (consulted March 16, 2014)

Valérie Donzelli
Valérie Donzelli (born 2 March 1973) is a French actress and filmmaker. She has directed six feature films and two short films since 2008, including Declaration of War (2011), Just the Two of Us (2023) and At Work (2025).
Valérie Donzelli was born in Épinal (France). She grew up in Créteil, near Paris. She moved to Lille with her family when she was 14 years old before going back to Paris at the age of 19. Before starting to work in the cinema, Donzelli first studied architecture, but abandoned it quickly. She started playing theatre at the municipal conservatory of the 10th arrondissement of Paris, but always kept a bad memory of this period. For a living, she worked at a bakery in Paris. She met Jérémie Elkaïm at that time, who became her partner, both in life and at work, and who encouraged her to quit the conservatory and her job at the bakery to become an actress. They now have two kids; the oldest one, Gabriel, inspired the movie Declaration of War. They are now separated, but still have a close relationship.
In 2001, Valérie Donzelli was the leading actress in Martha Martha, by Sandrine Veysset, which was presented at Directors' Fortnight, Le Plus Beau Jour de ma vie, and also Entre ses mains. She achieved great success among French public thanks to the French TV show Clara Sheller (2005), in which she plays Jeanne, best friend of the main character. Donzelli's first film, The Queen of Hearts (La Reine des Pommes), in which she was the leading actress, was more successful than expected. Jérémie Elkaïm is also co-writer. The film was presented at Locarno International Film Festival. Despite its low budget, the film can be considered a success because of its 30,000 spectators. In 2011, with the help of her now ex-partner Jérémie Elkaïm, Valérie Donzelli directed her second full-length feature film, Declaration of War. This movie, presented during the 2011 Cannes Festival, achieved great success, both with the public and critics, in France. It is directly inspired by their private life, relating how their couple fought against their son's cancer when he was 18 months. As Tim Palmer notes, "Declaration of War serves as an emblematic, even quintessential, contemporary French production: a barometer to gauge film industry standards and prevailing French cultural taste, a standard-bearer of ostensibly progressive materials, an ambassador text for French screen values." The movie was selected for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 2012, but was not part of the final list. Donzelli directed once again Jérémie Elkaïm in Hand in Hand (2012), with also Valérie Lemercier in the leading role. Donzelli considers that this is always a politic and engaged gesture to make films as women, and admires Agnès Varda for her work and her status of first women filmmaker into French Cinema. Valérie Donzelli is part of the jury during Locarno International Film Festival in 2013. She presents Que d'Amour!, a TV adaptation from the play The Game of Love and Chance (Le Jeu de l'Amour et du Hasard), by Marivaux, with Comédie-Française' sociétaires.

raw:
Palazzo Isimbardi

Palazzo Isimbardi, also called the Palazzo della Provincia, is a historic building in Milan located at 35 Corso Monforte, the seat of the Metropolitan City of Milan.

Although there are no documents to attest this, the primitive core of the palace is said to have been built in the 15th century as the residence of Cicco Simonetta, councillor of Francesco Sforza. The first document in which the palace is mentioned dates from the late 15th century and testifies to the passage of the palace to a descendant of the owner Gerolamo Pallavicino, to whose family it remained until the mid-16th century, when it was sold to the Taverna family, who used the palace as a suburban residence: during the first decades after its purchase, the palace was much remodelled due to the vast wealth accumulated by the family. In 1607, hunted down, the nobleman Gian Paolo Osio, lover of the nun of Monza and author of several crimes, took refuge here: he hoped to find hospitality with the Taverna family, who instead treacherously killed him in the basement of the palazzo. When the Taverna family died out through male succession, after a few quick passages the palace was acquired in 1731 by the Lambertenghi family, who, despite only staying there for 50 years, heavily remodelled it, and then sold it to the Isimbardi family, whose name it now bears. The Isimbardi family also had some restoration work carried out, the main one being the remaking of the façade towards the garden. In 1908, on the death without heirs of Luigi Isimbardi, the palace was sold to the industrialist Franco Tosi, from whom in 1935 the province of Milan purchased it, making it its seat. Later, with the suppression of the province of Milan, it became the seat of the metropolitan city of Milan.

The façade on the street, dating back to the 18th century, one of the best examples of Lombard baroque in the city, has two floors decorated with fregi and stucco cornices; the stone portal is surmounted by a balcony with richly decorated balusters. The inner courtyard is a square four-sided portico, with columns of Doric order in granite supporting round arches. The vaults of the portico had a typically Renaissance frescoed decoration, which partly re-emerged during restoration and alterations carried out in 1939, when the architect Giovanni Muzio carried out an extension overlooking Via Vivaio. On the garden front, the palace has a neoclassical façade with a rusticated ground floor, with the central body surmounted by a monumental timpanum. The interior decorations are noteworthy, especially those in the Sala degli affreschi with works by Morazzone, in the Sala del consiglio with the fresco of the Apoteosi di Angelo della Vecchia nel segno delle virtù by Giambattista Tiepolo, in another room the Episodio dei Visconti by Francesco Hayez. All'interno sono anche alcune sculture di Ivo Soli (1898-1976).

power outage notice

Residents in the Maplewood District are advised to prepare for a planned power interruption scheduled for Friday, October 14th, from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM. Our utility crew will be working on essential infrastructure upgrades to improve long-term grid reliability and reduce the frequency of outages in the future. This maintenance window was selected to minimize disruption to residential and commercial activities, as it falls during a standard business day where most affected operations can shift to remote work or pause services temporarily.

The outage will affect approximately 1,200 households and several small businesses along Elm Street, Oak Avenue, and the north side of Park Road. Specific addresses listed in the service map include those between 10th and 25th streets on the west side of the district. Residents should note that some critical services, such as traffic signals and emergency lighting, will be powered by backup generators to ensure public safety remains uncompromised during the maintenance period.

We strongly recommend that customers unplug sensitive electronic equipment, including computers, televisions, and medical devices that do not have internal battery backups, before the scheduled start time. Power surges upon restoration can cause significant damage to electronics. Additionally, refrigerators will generally keep food safe for up to four hours if the door remains closed, but it is prudent to plan meals accordingly and avoid unnecessary opening of the appliance during the outage.

Commercial customers are encouraged to review their business continuity plans and notify key clients or supply chain partners of the potential delay in operations. Those operating electric wheelchair chargers, medical oxygen concentrators, or other life-sustaining equipment should contact our 24-hour support line by Thursday evening to confirm if portable backup power can be arranged for their specific location. We are committed to assisting customers with critical accessibility needs to ensure their safety and comfort.

Updates regarding the progress of the repair work will be provided via our mobile app, social media channels, and the local news outlets. If the work is completed ahead of schedule, power will be restored as soon as it is safe to do so. We apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience and cooperation as we work to deliver a more resilient and efficient energy network for the community.

raw:
cycling event

The downtown streets will come alive this Saturday as the annual Riverfront Cycle Classic rolls through the city, drawing riders of all ages and abilities. Organized by the local cycling club, the event promises a mix of competitive racing, family-friendly rides, and a showcase of the newest gear from top manufacturers. Registration opened last month and quickly filled, with over 800 participants confirmed, ranging from seasoned road racers to weekend hobbyists eager to enjoy the scenic route along the riverbank.

The main race will start at 9 a.m. from the historic train station, winding its way through three distinct loops that highlight the city's vibrant neighborhoods and parkland. Spectators can expect to see a colorful peloton navigating steep hills, breezy waterfront stretches, and a thrilling sprint finish on Main Street. For those who prefer a more relaxed pace, a 30-kilometer "Leisure Loop" departs at 11 a.m., featuring gentle terrain and frequent rest stops with water, snacks, and bike-repair stations.

Local businesses have joined the celebration, setting up pop-up stalls that offer everything from fresh fruit smoothies to custom-fit helmets. The event's sponsors include a well-known bike retailer, a health-focused café, and a regional sports apparel brand, all of which will provide free giveaways and interactive demos. In addition, a charity ride will be organized in partnership with the community health center, with proceeds supporting youth cycling programs and safe-road initiatives.

Safety remains a top priority, and organizers have coordinated with the city's police and traffic department to ensure smooth road closures and clear signage. Volunteers will be stationed at key intersections, and medical tents will be staffed by certified first-responders. Riders are encouraged to wear helmets, bring lights for the early morning start, and follow the posted rules to keep the event enjoyable for everyone.

The Riverfront Cycle Classic has become more than just a race; it is a celebration of the city's growing cycling culture and a reminder of the health and environmental benefits of pedal power. Whether you're chasing a personal best, supporting a friend, or simply soaking in the festive atmosphere, this Saturday promises an unforgettable ride.

The official schedule for this year's International Cinema Festival has been released, marking the start of a bustling ten-day event. Organizers have curated a diverse lineup that spans six decades of global filmmaking, ensuring there is something to engage every cinephile from veteran critics to first-time attendees. The full program is now available on the festival website, where users can filter selections by genre, origin country, or time slot to plan their visits efficiently.

Morning screenings typically feature classic restorations, offering a serene introduction to the day's artistic highlights. These sessions are often held in the historic downtown theater, which boasts new digital projection systems capable of showcasing previously unreleased archival footage. Critics often gather during these early showings to discuss the technical preservation efforts that have defined the festival's identity over the past two decades.

Evening premieres constitute the heart of the schedule, accompanied by red-carpet arrivals and extensive media coverage. Industry professionals and celebrities descend on the city for these high-profile events, creating a vibrant atmosphere that spills out into the surrounding cafes and bars. Attendees should note that seating for these premieres is assigned via digital tickets, eliminating the need for early queuing while maintaining a controlled entry process for security reasons.

Midday panels and masterclasses provide a crucial balance between film and conversation, inviting directors and cinematographers to share their creative processes. These educational sessions are free for all ticket holders but require separate registration due to limited venue capacity. Participants frequently report that these interactions offer unique insights that extend far beyond what the finished film can convey alone.

Weekends will see an increased frequency of Q&A sessions, with most documentaries and independent features reserved for these days. The closing ceremony on Sunday night promises an emotional send-off, featuring a retrospective montage of the festival's most memorable moments from previous years. Visitors are encouraged to book travel accommodations early, as local hotels near the main venues report extremely high occupancy rates during the peak event days.

Subject: Expanding Our Public Library Services for the Community
Dear Neighbors,
I'm writing to share some exciting updates about the services our public library now offers. Over the past year we have listened to community feedback and invested in new resources that make our collections more accessible, both in-person and online. These changes aim to support lifelong learning for all ages.
Our digital catalogue now includes over 10,000 e-books and audiobooks that you can borrow with a simple click. In addition, we have launched a streaming platform for documentaries, language lessons, and children's storytime videos, all available free of charge to cardholders.
We're also expanding our physical spaces. The children's wing has been refurbished with new reading nooks, interactive tables, and a makerspace stocked with 3-D printers and coding kits. Teens can now enjoy a dedicated gaming area that also hosts weekly esports tournaments.
Our programming schedule now features more than 30 free workshops each month, ranging from job-search assistance and financial literacy to art classes and wellness yoga. All events are open to the public, and many are offered virtually to accommodate busy schedules.
We value your input and would love to hear how these enhancements are working for you. Please take a few minutes to complete the short survey linked in our monthly newsletter, or stop by the front desk to share your thoughts in person. Your feedback helps us continue to serve the community better.
Sincerely,
[Your Name]
Public Library Director

FIU Chaplin School of Hospitality & Tourism Management

The Chaplin School of Hospitality & Tourism Management at Florida International University, located at the Biscayne Bay Campus in North Miami, Florida in the United States is one of the University's 26 schools and colleges. The University was chartered in 1965 and opened in 1972. The campus includes a natural mangrove preserve, direct access to the bay, apartment-style housing, library, aquatic center, and the Roz and Cal Kovens Conference Center. On-campus housing is available at the Bayview Housing.

FIU's Chaplin School of Hospitality & Tourism Management has been recognized as one of the top hospitality programs in the country, with more than 1,200 undergraduate and graduate students per year. Undergraduate and graduate applicants are required to submit an application for admission to the University and to follow admission procedures stated on its Admissions website. In order to be approved for entrance into the School, applicants must first be eligible for admission into the University. The School is accredited by the following: Commission on Colleges of the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools (SACS).

The School offers flexible study options with its variety of degrees in Hotel, Restaurant, Hospitality, Travel and Tourism specializations available both on campus and fully online.

raw:
Nieuwe Waterweg

The Nieuwe Waterweg ("New Waterway") is a ship canal in the Netherlands from het Scheur (a branch of the Rhine-Meuse-Scheldt delta) west of the town of Maassluis to the North Sea at Hook of Holland: the Maasmond, where the Nieuwe Waterweg connects to the Maasgeul. It is the artificial mouth of the river Rhine. The Nieuwe Waterweg, which opened in 1872 and has a length of approximately 20.5 kilometres (12.7 mi), was constructed to keep the city and port of Rotterdam accessible to seafaring vessels as the natural Meuse-Rhine branches silted up. The Waterway is a busy shipping route since it is the primary access to one of the busiest ports in the world, the Port of Rotterdam. At the entrance to the sea, a flood protection system called Maeslantkering has been installed (completed in 1997). There are no bridges or tunnels across the Nieuwe Waterweg.

By the middle of the 19th century, Rotterdam was already one of the largest port cities in the world, mainly because of transshipment of goods from Germany to Great Britain. The increase in shipping traffic created a capacity problem: there were too many branches in the river delta, making the port difficult to reach. In 1863, a law was passed that allowed for the provision of a new canal for large ocean-going ships from Rotterdam to the North Sea. Hydraulic engineer Pieter Caland was commissioned to design a canal cutting through the "Hook of Holland" and to extend the mouth of the Rhine to the sea. The designs for this were already done back in 1731 by Nicolaas Samuelsz Cruquius but the implementation could no longer be postponed to prevent the decline of the harbour of Rotterdam. Construction began on 31 October 1863. The first phase consisted of the expropriation of farm lands from Rozenburg to Hook of Holland. During the second phase two dikes were built parallel to each other, which took 2 years. Caland proposed to extend the dikes 2 km into the sea to disrupt the coastal sea currents and decrease silt deposits in the shipping lane. Upon the completion of the dikes, the third phase began by the digging of the actual waterway. This began on 31 October 1866 and was completed three years later. The large amounts of removed soil were in turn used to reinforce other dams and dikes. The last phase consisted of the removal of the dam separating the new waterway from the sea and river. In 1872, the Nieuwe Waterweg was completed and Rotterdam was easily accessible. Because of the currents and erosion, the shipping lane has been widened somewhat. Yet because of the draft of today's supertankers, it needs to be dredged constantly. In 1997, the last part of the Delta Works, the Maeslantkering, was put in operation near the mouth of the Nieuwe Waterweg. This storm surge barrier protects Rotterdam against north westerly Beaufort Force 10 to 12 storms.

The Nieuwe Waterweg gives the Port of Rotterdam its deep-water access to the North Sea. From Hook of Holland it stretches for approximately 20.5 kilometres (12.7 mi) where the waterway continues as the Nieuwe Maas. The very first Nieuwe Waterweg-a breach through the dunes at Hook of Holland-was only 4.3 kilometres (2.7 mi) long, but in around 1877 the channel was made much larger and wider and the current Nieuwe Waterweg was created. Currently the width of the channel is between 480 and 675 metres (1,575 and 2,215 ft) and it is dredged to a depth of 14.5-16 metres (48-52 ft) below Amsterdam Ordnance Datum. It is this channel, together with the dredged channels in the North Sea, Maasgeul and Eurogeul, that allows ships like the MS Berge Stahl and MV Vale Rio de Janeiro (both with a draught of 23 meters) to enter Europoort. The Dutch government agency Rijkswaterstaat is responsible for maintaining the channel.

The point where the Nieuwe Waterweg enters into the North Sea, between Hook of Holland on the north bank and the Maasvlakte to the south, is called the Maasmond. It is marked with two navigation light-towers called the Paddestoelen ("mushrooms"). The Nieuwe Waterweg connects, in the North Sea, to the Maasgeul. This dredged channel in the North Sea is being widened to 840 metres (2,760 ft) to facilitate the largest container vessels for the new Maasvlakte 2 that opened in 2013.

raw:
wedding venue booking

Choosing the perfect wedding venue is often the first major decision couples make, and the process can feel both exhilarating and overwhelming. The location sets the tone for the entire celebration, influencing everything from the décor style to the guest list size. Many couples start by imagining the type of atmosphere they want-whether it's a rustic barn, a sleek downtown loft, or a garden with sweeping views. Once that vision is clear, the search narrows to venues that can realistically accommodate the desired aesthetic and practical needs.

When you begin contacting venues, it's essential to ask about availability well in advance. Popular locations fill up quickly, especially during the peak wedding season of late spring and early summer. A good rule of thumb is to lock in a date at least nine to twelve months before the ceremony, giving you ample time to secure the space and coordinate other vendors. Many venues offer a "hold" period, during which they reserve the date while you review contracts and compare options, so be sure to understand the terms of any deposits required.

Budget considerations play a crucial role in the selection process. While some venues include tables, chairs, and basic lighting in their rental fee, others charge extra for each component, which can quickly add up. Ask for a detailed breakdown of what is included in the base price and what items are available as add-ons. Some venues also have preferred vendor lists that can provide discounts on catering, photography, or floral arrangements, but you are usually free to bring in outside suppliers if you find a better fit. Balancing the venue cost with other expenses helps keep the overall wedding budget on track.

The logistics of the site are another factor that should not be overlooked. Parking availability, accessibility for guests with mobility challenges, and proximity to accommodations can affect the overall experience. If the ceremony and reception are in separate locations, consider the travel time between them and whether a shuttle service might be necessary. Many venues also have strict policies regarding noise levels, end times, and décor restrictions, so reviewing the contract thoroughly will prevent surprises on the big day.

Finally, trust your instincts during the venue walk-through. Pay attention to the staff's responsiveness and the condition of the facilities. A venue that feels welcoming and organized often translates into smoother coordination on the wedding day itself. Take photos, note any questions, and discuss them with your partner and planner before making a final decision. By approaching venue booking with a clear vision, realistic timeline, and thorough research, you set the stage for a memorable celebration that reflects your unique love story.

apartment maintenance request

When a leaky faucet or a flickering light disrupts daily life, most renters instinctively reach for the landlord's phone. A well-structured maintenance request not only speeds up repairs but also creates a clear record for both tenant and property manager, reducing misunderstandings later on.

Check whether your building uses an online portal, a dedicated email, or a paper form. Most complexes prefer digital submissions because they auto-route the request to the right contractor and timestamp each action, which helps track response times.

When you fill out the form, be specific. State the exact location, when you first noticed it, and any steps you've taken, like turning off water or replacing a bulb. Adding a photo can cut guesswork and speed dispatch.

After submitting, keep an eye on the portal, your email, or a phone call for a confirmation number and an estimated repair window. If you don't hear back within the promised timeframe, a polite follow-up can remind the office without sounding demanding. Documenting each interaction helps protect your rights should the issue linger.

Finally, remember that maintenance requests are a two-way street. Tenants who report problems promptly and provide clear information enable property managers to keep the building in good shape, which benefits everyone from the landlord's bottom line to your own peace of mind.

Subject: Marathon training schedule
Hi Sarah,
I hope your week is off to a good start. I have finally mapped out my training plan for the upcoming marathon, and I wanted to share it with you since you asked how I was managing the workload recently.
The next few months are going to be quite intense. I am gradually increasing my weekly mileage, aiming to peak at twenty-six miles before tapering down. It is a slow and steady approach to ensure my knees do not protest every time I run down the hill.
On recovery days, I am prioritizing strength training as much as running. Previously, I ignored core stability work, which led to several minor injuries last year. This time, I am dedicating two full sessions to yoga and lifting weights to build the muscle support necessary for long-distance endurance.
Nutrition is also a significant part of this process. I have hired a sports dietician to help me fuel properly for the longer runs. It is surprising how much impact clean, consistent meals have on my energy levels during those grueling eighteen-mile weekends.
Let me know if you want to join a shorter run next Saturday morning. We can keep it to five miles to avoid any problems. I would love the company while I handle the heavier training days alone.
Best regards,
Alex

raw:
pet adoption

Adopting a pet can be one of the most rewarding decisions you'll ever make, offering companionship, unconditional love, and a second chance for an animal in need. Shelters across the country are filled with dogs, cats, and even small mammals that are eager to find a forever home, and many are already health-checked and vaccinated.

The first step is to assess your lifestyle and living situation. Consider how much space you have, how much time you can devote to walks or play, and whether any household members have allergies. A busy professional might thrive with a low-maintenance cat, while an active family could enjoy the energy of a rescued Labrador.

When you visit a shelter, take the time to talk with the staff. They know each animal's temperament, history, and any special needs. Ask about the pet's favorite toys, feeding schedule, and how it interacts with other animals. Most shelters will also provide a brief behavioral assessment to help match you with a suitable companion.

After you bring your new friend home, patience is key. Give the pet a quiet space to settle, introduce new routines gradually, and reward positive behavior with treats and affection. Expect an adjustment period of several days to weeks as the animal learns to trust its new environment.

Remember that adoption is a lifelong commitment. Regular veterinary care, proper nutrition, and plenty of social interaction will keep your pet healthy and happy. By opening your heart and home, you not only enrich your own life but also give a deserving animal a second chance at joy.

raw:
remote work policy

A solid remote-work policy is quickly becoming a cornerstone of modern business strategy, and companies that treat it as an afterthought risk losing talent, productivity, and brand reputation. The first step is to define the scope of eligibility: which roles, departments, or seniority levels can work off-site, and under what circumstances. By laying out clear criteria-such as performance metrics, internet reliability, and data-security clearances-employers set expectations that help both managers and employees gauge whether remote work is a viable option for a given position.

Once eligibility is settled, the policy must spell out the logistical details that keep daily operations running smoothly. This includes specifying core hours when all team members should be reachable, the process for requesting equipment or reimbursements, and the preferred channels for communication and collaboration. By standardising tools like video-conferencing platforms, shared calendars, and project-management software, organizations reduce friction and ensure that remote staff remain integrated with on-site colleagues.

Equally important is the focus on performance measurement rather than physical presence. The policy should outline objective key results, deadlines, and deliverable standards that replace traditional time-card monitoring. Regular check-ins, quarterly reviews, and transparent reporting dashboards give managers the data they need to assess outcomes fairly, while giving remote workers a clear roadmap for success. When performance criteria are tied directly to business goals, the conversation shifts from "where are you working?" to "what have you accomplished?"

Legal and compliance considerations cannot be overlooked. Remote work often blurs geographic boundaries, introducing complexities around tax obligations, labor laws, and data protection regulations. A comprehensive policy must reference the jurisdictional requirements that affect remote employees, such as mandatory overtime pay, health-and-safety responsibilities, and cybersecurity protocols. Providing a concise FAQ or a dedicated support channel helps staff navigate these issues without fear of inadvertent violations.

Finally, culture and well-being should be woven into the fabric of the remote-work framework. Encouraging virtual social gatherings, mentorship pairings, and mental-health resources reinforces a sense of belonging that can otherwise erode when teams are dispersed. By articulating these expectations, leaders demonstrate that remote work is not a perk but a structured, sustainable model that supports both business objectives and employee satisfaction. A well-crafted policy thus becomes a living document, evolving with feedback and changing market conditions, ensuring that the organization remains agile and competitive in a rapidly shifting workplace landscape.

Subject: Thoughts on the Latest Language Learning Apps
Hi Maria,
I've been testing a few new language learning apps over the past month, and I wanted to share my impressions. The interfaces have become much more intuitive, and many now incorporate short, daily challenges that feel less like chores and more like quick games.
One app, in particular, uses AI-driven conversation simulations. It adapts the difficulty based on how well you respond, which keeps the dialogue realistic and pushes you just enough to stay engaged. I found the speech recognition surprisingly accurate, even when I mispronounced words slightly.
Another platform focuses heavily on cultural immersion, offering short videos of native speakers discussing everyday topics. The subtitles are interactive, letting you tap unfamiliar words for instant translations. This approach helps build listening skills while simultaneously expanding vocabulary.
A common drawback I've noticed is the subscription model. While the free tiers give you a taste, the most useful features-like personalized feedback and offline access-are locked behind a monthly fee. It's worth weighing how often you'll actually use the premium tools before committing.
Overall, the market is moving toward more personalized, context-rich experiences, which is encouraging for learners at any level. If you're interested, I can send you a few trial links and my notes on each app's strengths.
Best regards,
James
---

raw:
job interview tips

Landing in a job interview can feel like stepping onto a stage without a script, but a little preparation can turn nervous energy into confidence. Recruiters are looking for more than just a résumé; they want to see how well you fit the team, solve problems, and communicate under pressure. The right mix of research, practice, and personal polish can make the difference between a polite handshake and a job offer.

The first step is to become an expert on the company and the specific role you're chasing. Dive into the firm's website, recent press releases, and social media feeds to pick up on its culture, recent achievements, and strategic priorities. Then match those insights to the job description, noting the key skills and responsibilities that appear repeatedly. When you weave this knowledge into your answers, you signal that you've done the homework and that you understand how you could add value from day one.

Next, rehearse the most common interview formats, especially behavioral questions that start with "Tell me about a time when..." The STAR technique-Situation, Task, Action, Result-offers a clear framework to keep your stories concise and impactful. Practice aloud, either alone or with a trusted friend, and aim to highlight measurable outcomes. This rehearsal not only refines your narrative but also reduces the chance of rambling or getting stuck when the real moment arrives.

First impressions still matter, so treat your appearance and punctuality as part of the interview itself. Choose attire that matches the company's dress code while still reflecting your professionalism; when in doubt, err on the side of slightly more formal. Arriving ten to fifteen minutes early gives you a buffer to settle in, review your notes, and observe the office atmosphere. Once inside, maintain open body language, make eye contact, and offer a firm yet friendly handshake to convey confidence without aggression.

During the conversation, listen actively and let the interviewer finish each question before you respond. Echo key phrases from the question to show you've understood, then answer using your prepared stories or relevant examples. Don't forget to ask thoughtful questions of your own-about team dynamics, upcoming projects, or success metrics-because curiosity demonstrates genuine interest. If an unexpected scenario or a "brain teaser" pops up, stay calm, think aloud, and treat it as an opportunity to showcase your problem-solving approach rather than a trap.

After the interview, send a concise thank-you email within twenty-four hours. Reference a specific point from the discussion, reiterate your enthusiasm for the role, and briefly restate why you're a strong fit. Finally, take a moment to reflect on what went well and where you could improve; each interview is a learning experience that sharpens your performance for the next opportunity. Consistent effort across these stages builds a reputation of professionalism that employers remember long after the final handshake.

raw:
Year One: Newborns
Within the first 24 hours of birth, infants receive the Hepatitis B vaccine and Vision Screening. At six weeks, a comprehensive dose schedule begins, covering Hepatitis B, Rotavirus, DTaP, Hib, PCV13, and IPV. This initial round of immunizations is critical for establishing early protection against common but dangerous childhood illnesses.

Three to Six Months: Continuing Protection
At three months, a second dose of most vaccines received at six weeks is administered. This includes Hepatitis B, DTaP, Hib, PCV13, and IPV. Rotavirus is typically not given after this point. Parents are encouraged to keep their child calm and feed them before the appointment to minimize discomfort.

Nine to Twelve Months: Expanding Coverage
At nine months, the second dose of Rotavirus is due if not previously completed. By twelve months, children receive MMR, Varicella, Hepatitis A, and the first dose of PCV13 if a specific brand was used earlier. This marks a transition from infant-focused vaccines to those protecting against diseases common in toddlers and preschoolers.

Preschool Years: Long-Term Immunity
Between four and six years, children receive "booster" doses of DTaP, IPV, Hib, and MMR-Hib. Additionally, the second dose of Hepatitis A and Varicella are administered during this period if not given at twelve months. These boosters ensure that immunity developed in infancy remains strong through school age.

Practical Considerations and Record Keeping
It is important to keep an up-to-date immunization record, available as a paper card or digital entry in a health portal. Delays or missed vaccines should be discussed with a healthcare provider to determine the catch-up schedule, which can often safely continue even if the original timeline is missed. Always consult your pediatrician for personalized guidance, as individual health conditions may influence the timing or selection of specific vaccines.

raw:
Camp Anza

Camp Anza was a United States Army installation, in Riverside, California, during World War II. Construction began on July 3, 1942, and was completed on February 15, 1943. The camp was named after Juan Bautista de Anza, an early explorer who camped near the site in 1774. The US Army purchased the 1,240-acre site from the Willits J. Hole Ranch (1910-1942), a barley and wheat farm. Before 1910 the land was part of Rancho La Sierra (1797-1910). The post was activated on December 2, 1942, initially designated as Arlington Staging Area and Arlington Special Training Center, and renamed Camp Anza on December 12, 1942. Camp Anza was a large army base with 512 buildings housing 20,000 troops. Over 600,000 troops were processed over the three years of use. The camp had over a hundred wood barracks. Also Built were: headquarters, recreation rooms, chapel, laundry building, Southern Pacific Railroad station, library, fire station, newspaper print room (Anza Zip), 2,000 seat outdoor theater, water storage tower, motor pool, heating plant, and mess halls. Bob Hope, Jack Benny and Eddie Cantor often entertained troops there. The Pepsodent Show Starring Bob Hope, a radio shows was broadcast from the camp one night. Most troops at the camp were shipped out at the Los Angeles Port of Embarkation at Camp Ross. Before departing troops had immunizations, gas masks training, completed a will, had rope ladder climbing training, recorded personal property, and at Hole Lake, abandoned ship training. Possessing took eight to ten days before shipping out to the Pacific War. In August, 1945, returning troops started to arrive at Camp Anza. To serve the troops the camp also had a camp hospital. The 8th Italian Quartermaster Service Company, one of many Italian Service Units worked at Camp Anza. Camp Anza was deactivated on March 31, 1946. Philip H. Philbin Jr. purchased the camp in 1948 for $510,000. Philbin sold off much of the camp. Six local schools starting using the former camp. The street layout of the camp was kept. A housing subdivision called Anza Village and Arlanza Neighborhood was built on the land. Today there remains: a few barracks, chapel, the headquarters, laundry facility, officer's club and warehouse; all reused buildings. The city has a Historical Resources Inventory of the buildings. Units stationed at the camp:

229th Military Police Company (Zone of the Interior) (ASF) 1941st Service Command Unit (Station Complement) (ASF) 8th Italian Quartermaster Service Company (ASF) 385th Army Service Forces Band (ASF) Detachment, 9206th Transportation Corps Technical Service Unit (Los Angeles Port of Embarkation (ASF) 22nd Army Air Forces Base Unit (Army Air Forces Command Group, Non-Divisional Unit) (AAF)

raw:
The city cycling initiative aims to empower residents with basic maintenance skills, reducing reliance on professional shops for minor issues. This guidance is designed for riders of standard hybrid and road bicycles equipped with quick-release hubs and V-brakes. Understanding your machine's core components allows you to diagnose problems before they escalate into costly replacements. Regular inspection prevents sudden failures during commutes, ensuring safety and extending the lifespan of your equipment.

Start every ride with a visual check of the tires. Run a finger along the tread to feel for embedded glass, thorns, or debris that could cause punctures. Inflate your tires to the pressure range printed on the sidewall, typically between 60 and 90 psi for most urban bikes. Under-inflation leads to sluggish handling and increased rolling resistance, while over-inflation increases the risk of pinch flats. If you hear a low hum or feel excessive wobble at high speeds, check the wheel alignment. A crooked wheel requires professional truing, but a loose quick-release lever can be tightened immediately.

Brake performance is critical for urban navigation. Before departing, squeeze the brake levers to ensure they offer firm resistance without bottoming out against the handlebars. If the pads are worn down to less than three millimeters, they must be replaced immediately. For V-brakes, adjust the cable tension using the barrel adjuster at the caliper. Turn the adjuster clockwise to tighten the cable and bring the pads closer to the rim. The pads should contact the rim squarely, without any part hanging over the braking surface, to avoid premature wear.

Chain maintenance reduces friction and prevents rust accumulation. After riding in wet conditions, wipe the drivetrain with a dry rag to remove moisture. Apply a drop of light chain oil to each link while slowly back-pedaling the bike. Let the oil penetrate for a few minutes, then wipe off any excess to prevent dirt buildup. A dry or rusty chain will wear out your cassette and chainrings unevenly, leading to poor shifting and increased power loss. Check the chain length by seeing if it skips teeth when you shift through the gears.

Store your bicycle in a shaded, dry area to protect the frame and components from environmental damage. Extreme heat can degrade tire rubber and cause hydraulic fluid to expand, while cold temperatures can make chains stiff and brittle. Even if you park outdoors, using a lock through the rear triangle rather than the front wheel adds a layer of security. Regularly checking bolt tightness on handlebars, stem, and seat posts prevents critical loosening caused by road vibrations. This proactive approach ensures your bike remains a reliable mode of transport, saving money and reducing the environmental footprint associated with repair visits.

Please write a draft of ten to fifteen lines that defines a scene entirely through what is absent rather than what is present. Avoid explicit emotional adjectives or direct statements about feelings. Instead, let the setting, the weather, and the specific objects you choose to describe imply the underlying mood.
