Elixir (film)

Elixir is a 2016 Bengali short film by Anirban Guha, a Delhi-based banker. During his student days, Guha was deeply involved with theatre and stage productions in Delhi and Bangalore. Elixir was selected for the Cannes Short Film Corner 2016 along with six other Bengali films. The cast includes Daminee Benny Basu, Arindom Ghosh, Mahul Brahma, and Dr. Koushik Dutta.

The film traces the journey of a woman who lives in parallel worlds. The film opens with Srija (Daminee Benny Basu) receiving a phone call from her husband Avik (Arindom Ghosh). Avik asks her whether she can take a break for a few minutes to meet one of his old acquaintances. This unknown man was carrying a parcel for Avik. So he asks Srija to collect it from him. Srija agrees to pick up the parcel. The same evening, Srija waits for the acquaintance at a nearby cafe. As she was waiting, the waiter serves her a glass of water. So far, everything was usual. However, things change when Srija drinks the water ( Elixir). The drink though looked and tasted like water but it was a magical potion that transported Srija to a world of fantasies where she meets Akash (Mahul) and soon sparks fly between them. Srija gradually drifts away from reality and her husband and their relationship hit the rocks. Srija ends up in a mental asylum where she once again, is offered the Elixir of her life.

Daminee Benny Basu as Srija Arindom Ghosh as Avik Mahul Brahma as Akash Dr. Koushik Dutta as the Counsellor Koustav Bhattacharya as waiter/liftman/hospital ward boy

This 35-minute film is based on a story written by Sinjini Sengupta and directed by Anirban Guha. As a full-time banker, it was a bit difficult for Guha to manage time and travel frequently to Kolkata. So, the entire process from shooting to post-production took an entire year. It started from the middle of 2015. The shooting was completed within 4 days in December, 2015. This was followed by post-production activities. The members of the technical team that worked on the film were located in 3 different cities. Work was mostly carried out through long telephonic discussions, internet conversations and a few hurricane trips to Kolkata over weekends to wrap up the project.

Banksia laevigata subsp. laevigata

Banksia laevigata subsp. laevigata, the tennis ball banksia, is a subspecies of small woody shrub in the plant genus Banksia. It occurs in Western Australia's semi-arid shrubland. It and the closely related B. laevigata subsp. fuscolutea (golden ball banksia) are the two subspecies of the species Banksia laevigata.

The species B. laevigata was first described by Swiss botanist Carl Meissner in 1856, after being originally collected by James Drummond in 1848. No separate subspecies were recognised until Alex George collected specimens of subspecies fuscolutea east of Hyden in 1964, and formally named it two years later. The naming of a new subspecies automatically created the autonym (botany) subspecies laevigata. The common name is derived from the resemblance of its inflorescences to tennis balls. George described its nearest probable relative as Banksia audax and placed it in the series Cyrtostylis, which he concedes is rather heterogeneous. The series was split into three in the 1996 morphological cladistic analysis by botanists Kevin Thiele and Pauline Ladiges, with B. laevigata placed in the new series Ochraceae with B. audax and B. benthamiana in their arrangement. This was reinforced in American botanist Austin Mast's 2002 analysis, as B. laevigata came out as sister to three groups; the first the pair comprising B. audax and B. benthamiana. Early in 2007, Mast and Thiele rearranged the genus Banksia by merging Dryandra into it, and published B. subg. Spathulatae for the taxa having spoon-shaped cotyledons; thus B. subg. Banksia was redefined as encompassing taxa lacking spoon-shaped cotyledons. They foreshadowed publishing a full arrangement once DNA sampling of Dryandra was complete; in the meantime, if Mast and Thiele's nomenclatural changes are taken as an interim arrangement, then B. laevigata subsp. laevigata is placed in B. subg. Banksia.

The tennis ball banksia is a shrub to 3.5 metres (11.5 ft) high with grey, flaky bark. New growth occurs in summer, and the young stems and leaves are covered in fine hairs, which fall away with age. There are two variants distinguished by their leaf margins, one along the Fitzgerald River with rather obtuse leaf teeth, the other in the Ravensthorpe Ranges with larger, acute teeth similar to those of subsp. fuscolutea. The former is represented by the type. The inflorescences occur in spring and are oval in shape and a greenish yellow in colour. Flowers appear from October to December.

Banksia laevigata subsp. laevigata grows in shrubland on stony soils of spongolite or laterite, along the lower Fitzgerald River and in the Ravensthorpe Ranges in inland southern Western Australia. Banksia laevigata subsp. laevigata is classified as Priority Four - Rare on the Declared Rare and Priority Flora List under the Wildlife Conservation Act of Western Australia. That is, it is a taxon which has been adequately surveyed and which, while being rare (in Australia), are not currently threatened by any identifiable factors. It requires monitoring every 5-10 years.

Like other banksias, the tennis ball banksia is likely to play host to a variety of pollinators. Ants, bees and wasps have been recorded thus far.

Although like many western banksias it is sensitive to Phytophthora cinnamomi dieback, it has been successfully grown on Australia's east coast. It has also been successfully grafted onto Banksia integrifolia.

Discrete rate simulation

In the field of simulation, a discrete rate simulation models the behavior of mixed discrete and continuous systems. This methodology is used to simulate linear continuous systems, hybrid continuous and discrete-event systems, and any other system that involves the rate-based movement or flow of material from one location to another. Discrete rate simulation was developed in the early 1990s at Simulation Dynamics, Inc. by Andrew Siprelle and colleagues. The methodology retains the discrete-event clock while moving flow through a system at rates that maintain mass balance; it was first published at the 1995 Winter Simulation Conference, and the term "discrete rate simulation" was established in the authors' subsequent work. Imagine That Inc. later built a second-generation, linear-programming-based implementation upon the first-generation model.

Bulk material handling (e.g. minerals and ores, powders, particles, mixed wastes, wood chips) Liquids and gases Pulp and paper processing Oil and gas pipelines Traffic High speed/volume production lines in the food & beverage, consumer products, and pharmaceutical industries.

Discrete rate simulation combines the event-based timing of discrete event simulation and the continuous variables calculations found in continuous simulation. It predicts and schedules events when the system needs to calculate a new set of rates and determines the appropriate rate of flow for each branch or stream.

Discrete rate simulation is similar to discrete event simulation in that both methodologies model the operation of the system as a discrete sequence of events in time. However, while discrete event simulation assumes there is no change in the system between consecutive events, in a discrete rate simulation model the flow continues to move at a constant rate such that, for example, the level in a tank could change. Another difference is that discrete event simulation models are overwhelmingly concerned with the status of system entities (discrete objects moving through the system) while discrete rate simulation models are concerned with the status (quantity and location) of homogeneous flow. For rate-based systems, discrete rate simulation has faster computational times and is more accurate in calculating mass balance compared to discrete event simulation. Discrete rate simulation is also similar to continuous simulation in that it simulates homogeneous flow. In addition, both methods recalculate flow rates, which are continuous variables, whenever a state change occurs. However, discrete rate simulation S differs from continuous simulation in that it is event-based and does not simulate every time slice. Modeling linear flow systems using continuous simulation has limitations because it usually is unable to detect important events, such as a tank becoming full or empty, until after the event has occurred plus requires many more system recalculations during the course of the simulation.

An exercise in learning how to build discrete-rate simulations is to model a tank filling and emptying over time. The tank fills at a constant rate and empties at two different rates, one rate until it is full and a faster rate until it is empty. There are 4 types of events in the simulation: start simulation, storage full, storage empty, and end simulation. At each event the model determines which emptying rate to use; between events the emptying rate remains constant.

The primary function of our volcanology division is the continuous monitoring of seismic and deformation signals to provide accurate hazard assessments for the surrounding communities. Recent data from the Campi Flegrei perimeter has indicated a slight increase in microseismic activity, specifically in the northern sector where brittle failure mechanisms are common. These tremors, occurring in clusters three times per hour, suggest underlying stress release within the shallow crustal reservoir. It is critical to distinguish these background activities from harmonic tremors, which are indicative of fluid ascent and represent a potential precursor to more significant eruptive events. Current inflation rates, measured by GPS stations at the Astroni vent, remain stable at two millimeters per week. This sluggish expansion suggests that the magma chamber is pressurizing slowly, a characteristic often associated with long-term unrest rather than imminent eruption.

Geochemical sampling from the main fumarole fields provides essential context for interpreting the seismic trends. Recent gas compositional analysis reveals a three percent shift in the sulfur dioxide to carbon dioxide ratio, indicating a change in the depth of magma degassing. While individual measurements fluctuate due to weather conditions, the sustained baseline shift over the past month warrants closer attention. Historical records from the 1538 eruption show similar geochemical precursors leading up to the formation of Monte Nuovo. We must correlate these chemical signatures with historical patterns to determine if the current unrest follows a known episodic pattern or if it represents a novel threat vector. The laboratory team is now increasing the frequency of gas sampling to every six hours to ensure data resolution captures rapid changes in volatile output.

Public communication remains a central pillar of our operational mandate, requiring transparency without inducing unnecessary panic. The local civil defense agency has been briefed on the current moderate alert level, and joint press statements are scheduled for release next Tuesday. Clear, accessible language is essential when explaining technical concepts like magma viscosity or tectonic stress to the general public. We must avoid jargon that could be misinterpreted, focusing instead on the concrete steps residents should take, such as reviewing their emergency evacuation routes and ensuring that personal document folders contain vital records. Our brochure on emergency preparedness has been updated to reflect the specific hazards associated with sectoral collapse, which poses a greater threat to the coastal zone than ballistic ejecta.

Internal coordination involves daily briefings at six hundred hours, where field teams, laboratory analysts, and data scientists synthesize information from disparate sources. The integration of continuous broadband seismometer data with ground-penetrating radar surveys allows for a multi-dimensional view of subsurface turbulence. Discrepancies in data interpretation are resolved through peer review within the department, ensuring that our hazard models are robust and minimize false positives. We maintain close liaison with international research groups, particularly those specializing in caldera dynamics, to benchmark our current observations against global datasets. This comparative analysis helps refine our predictive algorithms, allowing us to identify subtle early warning signs that might otherwise be overlooked in isolated analyses.

Looking ahead, the installation of two new infrasound arrays in the southern sector will enhance our ability to detect low-frequency signals associated with gas release. These devices offer higher sensitivity than current models and will provide a more comprehensive acoustic map of volcanic activity. Budget allocations for the next fiscal quarter have approved the purchase of this equipment, with installation scheduled for late next month. Training sessions for new field technicians will focus on the proper calibration and maintenance of these sensitive instruments to ensure data integrity. Our ultimate goal remains the protection of public safety through rigorous scientific inquiry and precise, timely communication, ensuring that the region remains prepared for any escalation in volcanic activity.

Subject: Clarification on Group Camping Permit Requirements for Fall Season
Dear Park Ranger Office,
I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to request some specific guidance regarding the reservation process for group camping permits in the national parks I currently manage as a contact for a large outdoor education coalition. We are planning a series of retreats for our members during the upcoming autumn months, and we have encountered some points of confusion while reviewing the official reservation portal and the accompanying PDF guidelines. Specifically, we are unsure about the exact breakdown of fees for mixed-age groups, as the descriptions seem to differ slightly between the online application form and the printed brochure distributed last year. Given that budgeting is a critical component of our organizational planning, clarity on these numbers would be immensely helpful to ensure we can secure the necessary funds in a timely manner.
In addition to the fee inquiries, I would appreciate your insight into the maximum group size limits for tented camps versus those requiring a designated wilderness area. Our usual cohorts tend to number between twenty-five and thirty individuals, but we have noticed that some of the popular high-elevation sites impose stricter caps. We are interested in setting up a recurring schedule that allows for a fair rotation among our different chapters, and we want to ensure that our applications do not get rejected due to exceeding hidden cap thresholds that are not clearly highlighted on the main dashboard. If there are specific date ranges where demand is historically lower, we would be open to adjusting our itinerary to match those windows, provided the facilities are still well-maintained and accessible for our larger groups.
Furthermore, I am concerned about the sanitation and waste disposal protocols that apply to groups of our size. We understand that standard rules apply to casual hikers, but for a long-stay group that will be cooking on-site for multiple evenings, are there additional compliance checks or inspections that should be anticipated? We want to make sure our camp leaders are fully prepared to handle any on-site audits or cleanup requirements without disrupting the educational aspects of our program. It would be beneficial to know if the park provides any specific resource kits for large groups or if we are expected to source all non-consumable supplies externally, such as heavy-duty trash bags and bear-resistant containers.
I have attached a preliminary schedule of our proposed dates for your review, which spans the next three months. Please let me know if this format works with your current staffing levels and reservation system capacity. We are fully prepared to meet with a representative if a brief remote conference would be more efficient for discussing these details. Our goal is to foster a respectful and sustainable interaction with the natural environment, and we take our stewardship responsibilities very seriously. Ensuring our compliance with all local wildlife protection laws is paramount, and we are eager to align our operations with the most current conservations guidelines.
Thank you very much for your time and attention to these matters. I look forward to your response at your earliest convenience so that I may finalize our internal preparations and notify our chapters of the confirmed logistics. If you require any further documentation from our side to verify our status as an approved educational organization, please do not hesitate to ask. We value the natural beauty of the park and are committed to maintaining the high standards of visitor conduct that the park is known for. Please feel free to reach out if any of my questions require further elaboration or context.
Sincerely,
Jordan Lee
Director of Field Operations
Horizon Nature Coalition

Subject: Research Grant Timeline and Upcoming Milestones
Dear Dr. Patel,
I hope you are well. I am writing to outline the timeline for the National Science Foundation grant we discussed last month. As you know, the application deadline is fast approaching, and I wanted to make sure we are aligned on the key dates and deliverables. Below is a concise overview of the major milestones, which should help us coordinate our efforts and avoid any last-minute surprises.
The official submission deadline for the proposal is Friday, November 15th, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. All required documents, including the project narrative, budget justification, and biosketches, must be uploaded to the NSF FastLane portal by that time. I recommend that we aim to have a complete draft ready for internal review by Monday, November 4th, giving us roughly ten days for feedback, revisions, and final polishing. Please let me know if you foresee any scheduling conflicts that could affect this schedule.
Once the application is submitted, the review process typically takes six to eight weeks. The reviewers will assess the scientific merit, broader impacts, and budget rationale before forwarding their recommendations to the program officer. Assuming our proposal moves forward without major issues, we can expect to receive preliminary feedback by early January. I will monitor the portal closely and will notify you immediately if any clarification requests arise during this period.
If the review is favorable, the award notification is usually issued in late February. At that point, we will need to sign the award letter, finalize the subaward agreement, and submit any required compliance documents, such as the Human Subjects Protection certification if applicable. I anticipate that the administrative steps will take about two weeks, so we should be ready to begin the project by mid-March.
The official project start date will be March 15th, and we will be required to submit a quarterly progress report beginning in June. These reports should detail expenditures, milestones achieved, and any deviations from the original plan. I will set up a shared folder for all documentation and will draft a reporting calendar to keep us on track. Please feel free to reach out with any questions or concerns about the timeline, and let me know if you would like to schedule a brief meeting to walk through the next steps in detail.
Thank you for your continued collaboration. I look forward to working together to make this grant a success.
Best regards,
Emily Chen
Research Program Coordinator
University of Midtown
Phone: (555) 123-4567
Email: e.chen@midtown.edu

Natural regions of Chile

Because Chile extends from a point about 625 kilometers north of the Tropic of Capricorn to a point hardly more than 1,400 kilometers north of the Antarctic Circle, within its territory can be found a broad selection of the Earth's climates. In 1950, CORFO defined, following criteria of geographic and economic homogeneity, six regions in continental Chile: Norte Grande, Norte Chico, Núcleo Central, Concepción y La Frontera, Los Lagos and Los Canales. Although this territorial division was never used to define administrative entities (as the current Regions of Chile), the natural regions continue to be used for reference purposes.

These natural regions are ordered from north to south and reduced to five natural regions: Each has its own characteristic vegetation, fauna, climate, and, despite the omnipresence of both the Andes and the Pacific, its own distinct topography.

Most of the region is covered by the Atacama Desert and has a dry arid climate. The coast range has peaks over 2000 m and ends in cliffs in the coast. There are large salt flats in the Intermediate depression and the Andes. Norte Grande has Chile's highest mountains including Ojos del Salado (6,891 m) but host also the Altiplano and puna high plateaus.

The region has semi-arid climate, characterized by the transition from the Atacama Desert to the Mediterranean Matorral vegetation. The coast range and the Andes merges in this zone leaving no space for the Intermediate depression which is "replaced" by several transversal (east-west) valleys. The lack of an intermediate depression and absence of volcanic activity are believed to be the result of the flat-slab subduction of the Juan Fernández Ridge.

Mediterranean climate, vegetation of the Chilean Matorral. The Intermediate Depression of central Chile extends from Santiago to the south as a fertile region and is considered the agricultural heartland of Chile. After the Destruction of Seven Cities (1598-1604), all major settlements within the colonial Captaincy General of Chile came to be confined in central Chile, excepting only La Serena and the Chiloé Archipelago.

Temperate oceanic climate, vegetation of Valdivian temperate rain forests. The coast range is lower than further north with no peak over 1,500 m. The Intermediate depression is close to sea level. There are features from the Last Glacial Maximum in the Andes and the Intermediate depression such as moraines and glacial lakes. Intensive volcanism in the Andes in form of volcanoes and hot springs.

Covers all of Chilean Patagonia, and the Chiloé Archipelago. Zona austral has a subpolar oceanic climate and a vegetation of Magellanic subpolar forests in the west and Patagonian grasslands in the east. The former Patagonian Ice Sheet have eroded the coast range so that it now of islands and is not present south of Taitao Peninsula. The Intermediate depression is under the sea level. raw:
Redneck Heaven

Redneck Heaven was a chain of sports bars and restaurants based in Lewisville, Texas, and with locations in several other Texas cities. The chain was known for its controversial promotions, Southern theme and scantily-clad waitresses. It was the subject of an MTV reality show and it was frequently categorized as a breastaurant.

Opening in 2008 in Lewisville, Texas, Redneck Heaven marketed itself as a rowdier, more sexually provocative version of the typical breastaurant like Hooters, Tilted Kilt, or Twin Peaks. Restaurants featured Southern and Redneck-themed interior elements such as car doors from the General Lee (from The Dukes of Hazzard) and other automotive and sports memorabilia. They also featured scantily clad servers who engaged in what the chain termed as "mischief" (including line dancing, hula hooping and spanking). The typical uniform consisted of skimpy cut-off shorts (resembling those of Dukes of Hazzard character Daisy Duke) with crop tops, bikini tops or bras. Redneck Heaven had many special events, however, where the typical attire was bikinis, lingerie or other themes. The chain also held "Anything But Clothes" events where servers wore only panties and body paint. Some reviewers characterized Redneck Heaven as bridging the gap between tamer breastaurants and strip clubs, though the owner said the experience had become less extreme since the early days of the restaurant. The Dallas Observer listed it as being one of the best bars in the Dallas-Fort Worth area.

During 2013, MTV ran a reality television series called Big Tips Texas. The show followed a number of Redneck Heaven waitresses from the Lewisville, Texas location and ran for 14 episodes (one season).

Redneck Heaven ran periodic "Anything But Clothes" events where waitresses were topless except for body paint covering their breasts. In response to this, at least three different municipalities in Texas changed their laws about what constitutes nudity, preventing body paint from being considered an "opaque covering". Classifying the waitresses as partially nude would have required that Redneck Heaven be regulated as a sexually oriented business.

In addition to the regular menu, Redneck Heaven featured two unusual items which could be considered food challenges. One was a burger weighing 3 pounds (1,400 g) called the "Bubba's 'Tower in an Hour' Burger Challenge". The other, more controversial, item was a drink called the "Minnow Bomb". This drink consisted of a shot of liquor containing a live minnow. This item drew protests from the People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PeTA) who argued that it was both unsafe and inhumane to consume these live fish.

The purpose of this memorandum is to remind all residents of the established dormitory regulations that promote a safe, respectful, and comfortable living environment. Management has reviewed recent feedback and observed a few recurring issues; this document clarifies expectations and outlines procedures for compliance. All students, staff, and visitors who access the residence halls are expected to read and adhere to these rules without exception.

Quiet hours are observed from ten o'clock in the evening until seven in the morning, and all occupants must keep noise to a minimum during this period. This includes limiting music volume, refraining from loud conversations in hallways, and using headphones when personal audio devices are in use. Residents are encouraged to be mindful of their neighbors, especially when returning late from campus activities, to avoid disturbances that could affect academic performance and overall well-being.

Cleanliness is a shared responsibility; each occupant must keep personal rooms tidy and contribute to the upkeep of common areas such as kitchens, bathrooms, and lounges. Personal belongings should be stored appropriately, and waste must be disposed of in designated receptacles. Laundry facilities are to be used according to posted schedules, and any spills or messes in communal spaces should be cleaned promptly to maintain a hygienic environment for all.

Security protocols require that all doors remain locked when the hall is unattended, and residents must use their assigned key cards for entry. Guests are permitted to visit between nine in the morning and eleven at night, provided they are registered at the front desk and accompanied by a resident at all times. Overnight stays by non-residents are prohibited without prior written approval from the dormitory supervisor, and any violation may result in revocation of guest privileges.

In the event of an emergency, residents must follow the evacuation routes posted on each floor and assemble at the designated safety point outside the building. Fire alarms, smoke detectors, and sprinkler systems are regularly inspected; tampering with any of these devices is strictly forbidden and will be reported to campus security. Luanda Lozano

Luanda Lozano (born 1973) is an Angolan and Dominican printmaker and visual artist, who works with abstract and organic forms. Lozano is an Afro-Latina artist living in New York City.

Lozano was born in 1973, in Humpata, Angola, and grew up in San Francisco de Macoris in Duarte, Dominican Republic. She started painting at thirteen years old and made her first etched print at fifteen years old. She attended Altos de Chavón School of Design, an art school in the Dominican Republic. After earning a fine arts associate degree, Lozano continued her education at Parsons School of Design and received a B.F.A. degree in illustration (1994).

In 1992, Lozano started to work in the Robert Blackburn Printmaking Workshop. Her relationship with Robert Blackburn was a source of artistic inspiration for her career and work. By the late 1990s, she simultaneously worked with the Manhattan Graphics Center, and by 2010, she co-founded the print collective Dominican York Proyecto Grafica. She then dedicated her time to as an educator at the Bronx River Art Center and for over more than a decade has taught drawing and printmaking. Lozano's artwork includes themes from childhood and Caribbean and Afro-Latina cultures. She focuses on expressing personal experiences based on abstracted memory. Some of her works include religious iconography such as Catholic saints. As a printmaker, Lozano approaches her work as a collage of techniques. Some of the most common techniques she uses in her prints range from etching, collography and drypoint techniques.

Home | About | Contact

In 1998, Lozano was selected to represent the Dominican Republic at the XII Bienal de San Juan del Grabado Latinoamericano y del Caribe. Recently awarded the 2023 Center for Contemporary Prints Binnie Birthstien Memorial Award and the 2024 Southern Graphics Council International (SGCI) Mid-Career Printmaker Award. Luanda was invited to be one of the panel members for the 2025 Emerging Printmaker Award also hosted by the Southern Graphics Council International.

Luanda's artistic work has been included in public collections, such as the Smithsonian American Art Museum, Washington, D.C.; the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York City; the Hood Museum of Art, Dartmouth College, Hanover, New Hampshire; the Museo Nacional del Grabado, Argentina;Varna Museum, Bulgaria; Chamalière Museum, Auvergne, France; Montclair Museum (PMW Portfolio 2000) New Jersey; Library of Congress (Robert Blackburn print collection), Washington D.C.; Tellus Art, Sweden; Taiwan Museum of Art, Taiwan; Florean Museum and InterArt Foundation, Romania; CUNY Dominican Studies Institute, The City College of New York; Hudson County Community College, Jersey City, New Jersey; Mexic-Arte Museum, Austin, Texas; Blanton Museum; Brandywine Workshop & Archives, Philadelphia, PA; Colby College Museum of Art, Waterville, ME; and Kathy Caraccio Fine Art Print Collection.

The Westville Public Library remains committed to providing equitable access to information for all community members. Our primary mission is to serve as a neutral ground where residents of every age, background, and skill level can find resources, support, and connection. We recognize that access to knowledge is a fundamental right, and our services are designed to reflect that principle through inclusive programming and barrier-free environments.

Patrons may obtain a free library card upon presenting valid identification and proof of residency. This card grants unlimited borrowing privileges for physical media, including books, audiobooks, and DVDs. Additionally, cardholders receive access to our digital platform, which offers a vast collection of e-books, streaming music, and research databases. No credit check or deposit is required, ensuring that financial status never hinders participation in our services.

Our circulation desk is staffed by professional librarians who are available to assist with inquiries, collection browsing, and technology support. Staff members are trained to provide personalized recommendations and to guide users through complex search processes. For those needing assistance with digital devices, we offer weekly technology help hours where patrons can consult with specialists on using tablets, smartphones, and public terminals.

Community engagement is central to our operational strategy. The library hosts regular events such as author talks, children's storytimes, and job preparation workshops. These gatherings foster local dialogue and provide practical skills that contribute to personal and professional growth. Reserved spaces are available for quiet study, small group meetings, and informal socializing, ensuring that physical space meets diverse user needs.

We invite you to visit our branch during standard operating hours, which are Monday through Thursday from nine am to eight pm, and Friday through Sunday from ten am to six pm. Please review our updated codes of conduct regarding noise levels and acceptable use of facilities. Your feedback is valuable, and comment cards are available at every circulation station to help us improve our service delivery continuously.

Please review the dates below and let us know if any conflicts arise with your planned participation.
The opening ceremony will take place on Thursday evening at Riverview Theatre, with red-carpet arrival at 6:30 p.m. and the first screening, "Echoes of Tomorrow," starting at 7:30 p.m. The ceremony will be followed by a brief Q&A with the director and lead cast. Subsequent evenings will feature nightly showcases at three venues: Riverview, the downtown Art House, and Riverfront Cinema. The attached program booklet lists the exact start times for each screening.
Key events include the Documentary Spotlight on Saturday, October 19, at the Art House, and the Competition Finals on Sunday, October 25 at Riverfront Cinema. The Documentary Spotlight will present ten recent works, each followed by a discussion with the filmmakers. The Competition Finals will feature the top five short-film entries, with awards presented at 9:00 p.m. after the last film. A "Women in Film" panel will convene on Monday, October 21.
Screenings are divided into four categories: World Premieres, Retrospectives, Emerging Voices, and Family Friendly. World Premieres will be shown primarily at Riverview, while Retrospectives-featuring restored classics-will be the focus of the Art House schedule. Emerging Voices highlights new directors from under-represented regions and will be spread across all venues. The Family Friendly block, scheduled for early afternoons each day, includes animated shorts and feature-length films suitable for all ages.
Tickets for the full festival can be purchased online via the festival website, where you'll also find a downloadable pass granting access to all public screenings and most panels. Maria Hernandez

Edward Still

Edward Still (born 30 December 1990) is a football manager, who is the manager of Belgian Pro League club La Louvière. Born in Belgium to English parents, Still has managed Charleroi, Eupen, Kortrijk and Anderlecht in the Belgian Pro League, starting at age 30. From February to May 2026, he was manager of Championship club Watford.

Still was born in Belgium to English parents, Still's parents, Jane (née Bagley) and Julian Richard Still, left the United Kingdom for Belgium somewhere around the year 1990. He is the brother of fellow manager Will Still and video analyst Nicolas Still. He was raised speaking English and attended a French-language school in Walloon Brabant. In football, Still started his career as youth coach at Racing Jet Wavre and Royale Union Rixensartoise. In the meantime, he studied at Loughborough University, UCLouvain, KU Leuven and Erasmus University Rotterdam. In September 2015, he became assistant of Croatian manager Ivan Leko, initially as video-analyst at Sint-Truiden, but thereafter he followed Leko as assistant at Club Brugge. When Leko was coach at Al Ain, Still went on to work as a project manager at Vlerick Business School and as an analyst on the RTBF football talk show La Tribune. In May 2020, Still rejoined Leko's staff at Antwerp, then Shanghai Port in early 2021.

In May 2021, Still returned from China to start his first job as lead manager at age 30, at Charleroi, where he succeeded Karim Belhocine. On his debut on 24 July on the first day of the Belgian Pro League season, he won 3-0 away to Oostende. On 22 October 2022, Still was sacked by Charleroi, having taken 16 points from a possible 42 at the start of his second season. His final result was a 4-1 loss at Cercle Brugge.

In November 2022, Still became the manager of Eupen, also in the top division. After the 2022 FIFA World Cup, his debut was a late 1-0 win away to Seraing on 23 December. He was sacked on 25 April after taking 12 points from a potential 51; his final two games were lost 5-1 at home to Zulte Waregem and 7-0 at Club Brugge.

Still began the 2023-24 season as manager of Kortrijk, and was the first manager sacked, on 25 September. He had won none and drawn two of his eight games.

In June 2024, Still moved to be assistant coach at Lens, working alongside his brothers, Will and Nicolas. A year later, he returned to the country of his birth, being hired as assistant to Besnik Hasi at Anderlecht. Upon Hasi's dismissal on 1 February 2026, Still became interim head coach. His debut four days later was a 1-0 home loss to Royal Antwerp in the first leg of the Belgian Cup semi-finals, followed by a 2-0 defeat away to Genk in the league on 8 February.

On 9 February 2026, Still was appointed as head coach at EFL Championship club Watford on a two-and-a-half-year contract. Five days later, his debut was a 2-2 draw away to Preston North End. Watford announced on 3 May that they had parted company with Still. The club had won three of his 15 games, and fallen from 11th to 16th.

Subject: Agenda Draft for Next Month's Offsite
Hi everyone,
I am writing to share the preliminary agenda for our upcoming team offsite scheduled for the first week of next month. This retreat is more than just a break from the daily grind; it is a critical opportunity for us to pause, reflect on our recent achievements, and align our strategic vision for the quarter ahead. I want to ensure that every member of the team feels heard and valued during these two days, so I am keeping the schedule intentional yet flexible enough to accommodate spontaneous discussion and creative brainstorming. Your input on the structure is welcome, so please review the attached document and let me know if specific topics should be prioritized.
The first day will be dedicated entirely to strategic planning and goal setting. We will start early with a silent reflection period where everyone can write down their personal and professional objectives for the coming months. Following that, we will break into smaller groups to analyze our current performance metrics and identify areas for improvement. The goal here is not to criticize past mistakes but to construct a clear, actionable roadmap that addresses our biggest challenges head-on. We will end the day with a full team synthesis session to finalize our top three priorities, ensuring we leave with a unified understanding of where we are headed.
Day two will focus on culture, collaboration, and team bonding. We plan to hold interactive workshops designed to improve cross-departmental communication and empathy. These sessions are facilitated by an external expert who specializes in high-performing team dynamics. After the workshops, we will transition into a more relaxed setting for guided discussions about work-life balance and sustainable productivity. I believe that addressing these human elements is just as important as hitting numerical targets, and I hope this segment fosters stronger interpersonal connections among colleagues who usually operate in silos.
Beyond the structured activities, there is ample time for informal socializing and relaxation. We have arranged for catering breakfasts and lunches, as well as evening activities that cater to different interests, such as hiking trails and a local gallery walk. I encourage you to participate in whatever resonates with you, as these moments often lead to the most innovative ideas and genuine friendships. Please remember to pack appropriate clothing for outdoor activities and bring any books or materials you might want for downtime in the evenings.
Please confirm your attendance and any dietary restrictions by the end of this week so we can finalize the logistics with the venue. If you have any concerns or specific expectations for the offsite, please reach out to me directly. I am looking forward to seeing everyone in person and diving deep into the work that defines our team. Let us make this gathering a productive and memorable one.

Eastern Shore Public Library

The Eastern Shore Public Library is a library system that serves counties of Accomack and Northampton counties in Virginia. The library system is within Region 3 of the Virginia Library Association (VLA).

According to the FY 2014 Institute of Museum and Library Services Data Catalog, the Library System has a service area population of 45,768 with 1 central library and 3 branch libraries.

The Eastern Shore Public Library was started on January 16, 1957 in Accomac's Community Hall. The library used a bookmobile with stops in 50 locations. The library became a regional library system on July 1, 1958. The Main Library, the primary library, located in Accomac. The Northampton Free Library is a branch library. Cape Charles Memorial Library and Chincoteague Island Library are affiliated locations.

Subject: Upcoming Activities and Volunteer Opportunities at the Community Garden
Dear Neighbors and Garden Friends,
I hope this message finds you well and enjoying the early signs of spring. As the growing season approaches, I wanted to share an update on our community garden's progress and invite you to take part in a series of events we have planned for the next few weeks. Your continued enthusiasm has transformed a modest plot of land into a thriving space where residents of all ages can learn, grow, and connect.
Over the past year, we have collectively planted more than 500 seedlings, harvested a bountiful assortment of vegetables, and hosted several workshops on composting and pollinator-friendly planting. The garden now boasts three raised beds, a new rainwater collection system, and a small herb corner that has become a favorite spot for many. These achievements would not have been possible without the dedication of volunteers like you, and we are grateful for every hour you have contributed.
Looking ahead, we have scheduled a planting day for Saturday, October 19, beginning at 9 a.m. We will focus on sowing lettuce, kale, and radishes, as well as planting a row of marigolds to help deter pests naturally. Following the planting, a workshop on organic pest control will be held on Wednesday, October 23 at 6 p.m. in the garden shed. The session will cover simple, non-chemical methods that anyone can implement at home or in the garden.
If you are interested in helping with these activities, please let us know by replying to this email or signing up on the volunteer board at the community center. We need extra hands for weeding, watering, and guiding new members through the garden layout. Even a brief commitment of an hour or two can make a big difference, and we will provide all necessary tools and a brief orientation before each event.
In addition to volunteer time, we are currently seeking donations of organic seeds, compost, and gardening tools such as hand trowels and pruning shears. Contributions can be dropped off at the garden's tool shed during weekdays, or you may arrange a pickup by contacting me directly. Your support helps keep the garden thriving and accessible to everyone in our neighborhood.
Thank you again for your passion and participation. Please feel free to reach out with any questions, ideas, or suggestions you may have. I look forward to seeing many of you at the upcoming events and working together to make this season our most productive yet.
Warm regards,
Emily Rivera
Community Garden Coordinator
emily.rivera@greenhaven.org
(555) 312-8742

password reset guidance

In the modern digital landscape, the forgotten password is no longer just a minor annoyance; it is a critical bottleneck that can halt business operations, delay access to personal financial records, or lock users out of essential communication channels for hours. For IT professionals and system administrators, understanding the mechanics of password reset procedures is not merely an administrative task but a fundamental pillar of security strategy. A robust reset process must balance usability for the average user with rigorous verification protocols that prevent unauthorized access. When designing or troubleshooting these systems, the first step is ensuring that the reset link or mechanism is the only viable path back into the account, effectively severing the connection to the old credentials immediately upon initiation. This immediate invalidation is crucial because it stops any potential brute-force attacks that might have been in progress against the previous password entry point.

The security of the reset request itself relies heavily on the method of identity verification. While email has traditionally been the standard delivery channel for reset links, its susceptibility to compromise makes it a vulnerable target for threat actors who may have already seized control of the inbox. Consequently, best practices now suggest multi-factor verification for high-value accounts. This could involve a combination of a one-time passcode sent via SMS and a biometric check, or the use of WebAuthn security keys that provide cryptographic proof of possession. The goal is to ensure that the person initiating the reset is the legitimate account holder, reducing the risk of social engineering attacks where a malicious actor tricks a support agent or exploits a vulnerable email server to intercept the reset instructions.

From a user perspective, clarity is paramount to reducing support tickets and frustration. The interface for resetting a password should be intuitive, guiding the user through each step with clear language and immediate feedback. Ambiguity in error messages is a common source of confusion; instead of a generic "Error 404" or "Invalid Input" message, the system should specify what went wrong, such as "The reset link has expired" or "The one-time code does not match our records." Furthermore, the expiry window for reset tokens should be short, typically no more than fifteen to thirty minutes, to limit the window of opportunity for interception. Once the reset is complete, the system must explicitly confirm the action and prompt the user to sign in with their new credentials, rather than leaving them stranded on a blank page or returning them to the login screen without context.

IT teams must also consider the audit logging implications of every password reset event. Every reset attempt, whether successful or failed, should be recorded with a timestamp, the user's IP address, the method of verification used, and the specific account affected. These logs serve as a forensic trail that can be analyzed to detect patterns of suspicious activity, such as multiple failed attempts from disparate geographic locations or resets occurring outside of typical business hours for a specific employee. Integrating these logs with a security information and event management system allows for real-time alerting, enabling security operators to intervene immediately if a reset appears malicious. Without comprehensive logging, organizations fly blind, unable to distinguish between a legitimate user who forgot their login and an attacker attempting to take over an account.

Finally, the process should be regularly tested and refined. Periodic penetration testing should include attempts to exploit the password reset functionality by intercepting reset links, brute-forcing one-time codes, or manipulating the flow of the application. Users should be encouraged to adopt password managers that can securely store the new credential, reducing the likelihood of reuse or weak character sets. By treating the password reset as a critical security event rather than a simple utility, organizations can significantly enhance their posture against account takeover attacks. The combination of strong verification, clear user interfaces, tight token lifetimes, and detailed audit trails creates a defense in depth that protects both the individual user and the broader organizational infrastructure from a surprisingly persistent threat vector.

Subject: Important Security Update: Your Password Has Been Reset
Hi Sarah,
I am writing to inform you that a security reset was initiated for your account today at 2:14 PM. This measure was taken as a precautionary step following an unusual login attempt detected from a location outside your usual access patterns. To ensure the safety of your data, all currently active sessions have been terminated, and your existing password is no longer valid. You will need to create a new one before you can access your dashboard or emails again.
Please follow these steps immediately to regain access. First, navigate to the main login page of our platform. Click on the link labeled "Forgot Password" located directly beneath the password entry field. Enter the email address associated with your profile, which is the one you currently use for all company communications. A unique recovery link will be sent to your inbox within the next five minutes. Check your spam or junk folders if you do not see it in your primary inbox, as automated messages can sometimes be misdirected by email filters.
When you click the recovery link, you will be redirected to a secure form where you can define a new password. It is crucial that this new password is strong and unique. Avoid using simple sequences like "123456" or personal details such as your name, birthdate, or pet names. Instead, combine uppercase and lowercase letters with numbers and special characters. A good strategy is to use a random string of at least twelve characters. Do not reuse any passwords you have ever used on this or other services, as breaches on other platforms could compromise your security here.
Once you have successfully set the new password, you will not be able to log in until you confirm the change on your preferred device. We recommend that you save this new credential in a reputable password manager. These tools generate and store complex passwords securely, making it easier for you to maintain strong security hygiene without the burden of memorization. If you do not already use a manager, consider setting one up now. It is a simple yet highly effective way to protect your digital identity from increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.
If you encounter any difficulties during the reset process, or if you did not request this action and feel uneasy about recent account activity, please contact our support team immediately. We are available twenty-four seven to assist you. Your prompt attention to this matter is appreciated as it helps us maintain the integrity of our systems and the privacy of your personal information. Thank you for your cooperation and vigilance in keeping our environment secure.
Best regards,
The IT Security Team

Megan Angharad Hunter

Megan Angharad Hunter (born c. 1998) is a Welsh writer who in 2021 won the Crown at the Urdd National Eisteddfod and the Welsh-language Wales Book of the Year Award.

Hunter is from Penygroes, Gwynedd. Her father Jerry Hunter is an academic and author, who won the National Eisteddfod of Wales Prose Medal. Her mother is an actress. Hunter went on to study Welsh and Philosophy at Cardiff University.

Hunter won the literary medal at the 2019 Anglesey Eisteddfod and came close to winning the Crown, the main prose prize, at the Urdd National Eisteddfod in the same year. She was awarded the Literature Wales New Author Scholarship in 2020. In 2020 she submitted a piece of writing to the Crown competition at the Urdd National Eisteddfod, but the 2020 event was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. She had to wait until October 2021 for the result when she was announced as the virtual "Eisteddfod T" 2020/21 winner, being presented with the prize at an online ceremony. Her work, a piece of prose of more than 4,000 words submitted under the pen name Lina, was on the theme of Mwgwd/Mygydau ('Mask/Masks') and written both in an academic style and partly in the language of a child. Shortly before her Urdd win, in August 2021 Hunter won the Literature Wales 2021 Welsh-language Wales Book of the Year Award, for her debut novel tu ôl i'r awyr ('behind the sky'). Two days beforehand the novel had been announced as winner of the Welsh-language Fiction Award. The book offered a glimpse into the lives of two young adults, Anest and Deian. In 2025 Firefly Press acquired the rights to publish the book in English, under the name Behind the Sky. She won the 2024 Tir na n-Og Award in the secondary school age category, for her Welsh-language children's book Astronot yn yr Atig ('Astronaut in the Attic'). The winners were announced at a special ceremony at the 2024 Urdd National Eisteddfod in Meifod.

October 8 (film)

October 8 - The Fight for the Soul of America (October 8) is a 2025 documentary film directed by Wendy Sachs. Sachs and Debra Messing also served as executive producers.

October 8 covers the 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses after the October 7 attacks. It describes how "anti-Israel sentiment came to a fever pitch in the immediate aftermath of the massacre" and argues such sentiment "morphed into antisemitism". The film includes interviews with Michael Rapaport, Noa Tishby, U.S. Representative Ritchie Torres, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, Sheryl Sandberg, Dan Senor, Scott Galloway, Deborah Lipstadt, Bari Weiss, Shai Davidai, and Mosab Yousef. It explores the organization Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP), and argues that SJP promoted anti-Zionism and antisemitism on campus. The film also covers the role of social media in allegedly stoking antisemitism among young people. In the film, University of California, Santa Barbara's (UCSB) student body president says she was harassed online and on campus after she condemned the October 7 attacks.

Co-produced by Wendy Sachs and Debra Messing, October 8 was co-edited by Inbal Lessner and Nimrod Erez. Sachs said she wanted the film to show a non-Jewish audience "what antisemitism looks like today-for them to see, when they see a 'Zionists not allowed' sign, that means 'Jew'".

October 8 was theatrically released in the United States on March 14, 2025, through Briarcliff Entertainment. It became available for streaming on April 1, 2025. The film grossed $1.3 million at the U.S. box office. The documentary screened at the Miami Jewish Film Festival.

On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 63% of 19 critics' reviews are positive. Elizabeth Weitzman of TheWrap also reviewed the film favorably, writing, "under ordinary circumstances, it might feel uncontroversial to make a film about the recent rise of antisemitism on college campuses" but "in this passionate and timely documentary" Sachs explores "how a culture war has unfolded across U.S. universities since the October 7 Hamas attacks on Israel." Michael O'Sullivan of The Washington Post praised the film's "often-moving first-person student testimony" and noted its claim that Hamas may be behind SJP while lamenting its lack of criticism of the Israeli government and military. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter called out some cherry-picking and "questionable conclusions", adding, "But there's no denying the importance of its message and the need for corrective action by political, academic, religious and civil leaders". The Times of Israel said the film looks closely at SJP but fails to discuss Qatari involvement in higher education in the United States, citing its own reporting that Qatar contributed as much as $4.7 billion to U.S. academic institutions between 2001 and 2021. In The Jerusalem Post, Greer Fay Cashman called the film Sachs's "crowning achievement". In Variety, Alissa Simon called it "one-sided" but still worth seeing for its coverage of antisemitism and the political fallout of the campus protests. In Haaretz, Judy Maltz criticized the film for its black-and-white narrative and for failing to mention the thousands of Palestinians killed in Gaza or the humanitarian crisis. She wrote that the film ignores Jews who oppose the Israeli far-right's actions and rhetoric. Maltz wrote, "It may be true, as the film very much wants us to believe, that many of those taking to the streets of America are driven by antisemitism. But is also true that Israel does not have a great story to tell and that it is legitimate to criticize how it is prosecuting this war." Pro-Palestinian publications denounced the film as Israeli propaganda and criticized it for conflating Zionism with Judaism. The left-wing magazine Current Affairs criticized the film for making virtually no mention of the Gaza genocide or of anti-Zionist Jewish groups or figures such as Jewish Voice for Peace and IfNotNow. Mondoweiss had similar complaints, criticizing the depiction of an attempted recall of University of California, Santa Barbara student president Tessa Veksler as antisemitic and saying that recall campaigns are not discriminatory but a feature of democracy. Mondoweiss said the film ignored right-wing antisemitism by associating with groups such as the Anti-Defamation League, which called Elon Musk's January 2025 salute, interpreted by many as a Nazi salute, "an awkward gesture in a moment of enthusiasm".

October 8 - The Fight for the Soul of America (October 8) is a 2025 documentary film directed by Wendy Sachs. Sachs and Debra Messing also served as executive producers.
October 8 covers the 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses after the October 7 attacks. It describes how "anti-Israel sentiment came to a fever pitch in the immediate aftermath of the massacre" and argues such sentiment "morphed into antisemitism". The film includes interviews with Michael Rapaport, Noa Tishby, U.S. Representative Ritchie Torres, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, Sheryl Sandberg, Dan Senor, Scott Galloway, Deborah Lipstadt, Bari Weiss, Shai Davidai, and Mosab Yousef. It explores the organization Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP), and argues that SJP promoted anti-Zionism and antisemitism on campus. The film also covers the role of social media in allegedly stoking antisemitism among young people. In the film, University of California, Santa Barbara's (UCSB) student body president says she was harassed online and on campus after she condemned the October 7 attacks.

Co-produced by Wendy Sachs and Debra Messing, October 8 was co-edited by Inbal Lessner and Nimrod Erez. Sachs said she wanted the film to show a non-Jewish audience "what antisemitism looks like today-for them to see, when they see a 'Zionists not allowed' sign, that means 'Jew'".
October 8 was theatrically released in the United States on March 14, 2025, through Briarcliff Entertainment. It became available for streaming on April 1, 2025. The film grossed $1.3 million at the U.S. box office. The documentary screened at the Miami Jewish Film Festival.
On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 63% of 19 critics' reviews are positive. Elizabeth Weitzman of TheWrap also reviewed the film favorably, writing, "under ordinary circumstances, it might feel uncontroversial to make a film about the recent rise of antisemitism on college campuses" but "in this passionate and timely documentary" Sachs explores "how a culture war has unfolded across U.S. universities since the October 7 Hamas attacks on Israel." Michael O'Sullivan of The Washington Post praised the film's "often-moving first-person student testimony" and noted its claim that Hamas may be behind SJP while lamenting its lack of criticism of the Israeli government and military. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter called out some cherry-picking and "questionable conclusions", adding, "But there's no denying the importance of its message and the need for corrective action by political, academic, religious and civil leaders". The Times of Israel said the film looks closely at SJP but fails to discuss Qatari involvement in higher education in the United States, citing its own reporting that Qatar contributed as much as $4.7 billion to U.S. academic institutions between 2001 and 2021. In The Jerusalem Post, Greer Fay Cashman called the film Sachs's "crowning achievement". In Variety, Alissa Simon called it "one-sided" but still worth seeing for its coverage of antisemitism and the political fallout of the campus protests. In Haaretz, Judy Maltz criticized the film for its black-and-white narrative and for failing to mention the thousands of Palestinians killed in Gaza or the humanitarian crisis. She wrote that the film ignores Jews who oppose the Israeli far-right's actions and rhetoric. Maltz wrote, "It may be true, as the film very much wants us to believe, that many of those taking to the streets of America are driven by antisemitism. But is also true that Israel does not have a great story to tell and that it is legitimate to criticize how it is prosecuting this war." Pro-Palestinian publications denounced the film as Israeli propaganda and criticized it for conflating Zionism with Judaism. The left-wing magazine Current Affairs criticized the film for making virtually no mention of the Gaza genocide or of anti-Zionist Jewish groups or figures such as Jewish Voice for Peace and IfNotNow. Mondoweiss had similar complaints, criticizing the depiction of an attempted recall of University of California, Santa Barbara student president Tessa Veksler as antisemitic and saying that recall campaigns are not discriminatory but a feature of democracy. Mondoweiss said the film ignored right-wing antisemitism by associating with groups such as the Anti-Defamation League, which called Elon Musk's January 2025 salute, interpreted by many as a Nazi salute, "an awkward gesture in a moment of enthusiasm".

A parametric surface is a surface in the Euclidean space R 3 {\displaystyle \mathbb {R} ^{3}} which is defined by a parametric equation with two parameters ⁠ r : R 2 → R 3 {\displaystyle \mathbf {r} :\mathbb {R} ^{2}\to \mathbb {R} ^{3}} ⁠. Parametric representation is a very general way to specify a surface, as well as implicit representation. Surfaces that occur in two of the main theorems of vector calculus, Stokes' theorem, and the divergence theorem, are frequently given in a parametric form. The curvature and arc length of curves on the surface, surface area, differential geometric invariants such as the first and second fundamental forms, Gaussian, mean, and principal curvatures can all be computed from a given parametrization.

The simplest type of parametric surfaces is a bivariate surface, given by the graphs of functions of two variables (bivariate functions): z = f ( x , y ) , r ( x , y ) = ( x , y , f ( x , y ) ) . {\displaystyle z=f(x,y),\quad \mathbf {r} (x,y)=(x,y,f(x,y)).}

A rational surface is a surface that admits parameterizations by a rational function. A rational surface is an algebraic surface. Given an algebraic surface, it is commonly easier to decide if it is rational than to compute its rational parameterization, if it exists. Surfaces of revolution give another important class of surfaces that can be easily parametrized. If the graph z = f(x), a ≤ x ≤ b is rotated about the z-axis then the resulting surface has a parametrization r ( u , φ ) = ( u cos ⁡ φ , u sin ⁡ φ , f ( u ) ) , a ≤ u ≤ b , 0 ≤ φ < 2 π . {\displaystyle \mathbf {r} (u,\phi )=(u\cos \phi ,u\sin \phi ,f(u)),\quad a\leq u\leq b,0\leq \phi <2\pi .} It may also be parameterized r ( u , v ) = ( u 1 - v 2 1 + v 2 , u 2 v 1 + v 2 , f ( u ) ) , a ≤ u ≤ b , {\displaystyle \mathbf {r} (u,v)=\left(u{\frac {1-v^{2}}{1+v^{2}}},u{\frac {2v}{1+v^{2}}},f(u)\right),\quad a\leq u\leq b,} showing that, if the function f is rational, then the surface is rational. To all employees,

As part of our continued growth and commitment to providing a collaborative environment, we will be relocating our headquarters to the new Riverside Business Center effective Monday, 14 November. The new address will be 2500 Rivergate Plaza, Suite 300, and the move will be completed in phases to minimize disruption to daily operations. All staff are asked to review the schedule attached to this notice and to prepare for the transition accordingly.

The relocation plan includes a phased move of departments, beginning with the Finance and Human Resources teams on 5 November, followed by Marketing and Sales on 9 November, and finally the Operations and IT divisions on 12 November. Each department will receive a detailed timeline and a list of items to be packed, labeled, and transferred. Please ensure that all personal belongings and non-essential equipment are cleared from workstations by the end of each phase to facilitate a smooth handover.

Parking arrangements at the new site have been arranged with the building management, providing two reserved spaces per department on a first-come, first-served basis. A shuttle service will run between the current office and Riverside Business Center from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. each day of the move, and will also be available for the first week after relocation for those who need additional assistance. A map of the new location, including emergency exits and floor plans, will be posted on the intranet and in the reception area.

We understand that a move of this magnitude can raise concerns, and we have set up a dedicated relocation hotline (555-123-4567) and an email address (relocation@company.com) for any questions or special requests. A team of facilities staff will be on site during each phase to address any immediate issues and to ensure that all equipment is installed and functional before the start of business each day.

We appreciate your cooperation and flexibility during this transition. By working together, we will settle into our new workspace quickly and continue delivering the high standard of service our clients expect. Thank you for your continued dedication and support.

Subject: Quick Review of First Aid Basics for Our Upcoming Safety Workshop
Hi everyone, as we approach the safety workshop next month, I wanted to share a brief overview of some essential first aid principles that we will be reviewing in detail during the session. The goal of basic first aid is to preserve life, prevent the worsening of injuries or illness, and promote recovery. While these skills are often associated with dramatic emergencies like car accidents or severe falls, they are equally applicable to minor but common household incidents such as kitchen cuts, burns, or sudden allergic reactions. Understanding these fundamentals not only helps you assist others but also boosts your own confidence when stress levels are high and clear thinking is most needed. Having a calm demeanor is just as important as knowing the physical steps involved in treating an injury, as panic can cloud judgment and lead to mistakes that might exacerbate a situation.
One of the most critical aspects of first aid is ensuring your own safety before approaching any victim. This rule is often referred to as scene safety. Before you rush to help someone who has been injured, you must assess the environment for any ongoing dangers such as traffic, electrical hazards, fire, or toxic fumes. Putting yourself at risk does not help the injured person and can turn a single incident into a multi-person emergency. Once you are sure the area is safe, check the victim's responsiveness by gently tapping their shoulders and asking them questions in a loud, clear voice. If they do not respond, it is imperative to call emergency services immediately rather than attempting complex medical interventions on your own.
When dealing with breathing and circulation issues, remember the chain of survival. If a person is not breathing normally and has no pulse, you should begin cardiopulmonary resuscitation immediately if you have been trained to do so. High-quality chest compressions have been shown to significantly improve survival rates before professional help arrives. It is also vital to keep the airway clear and manage any bleeding that may be occurring. For deep or arterial bleeding, apply direct pressure to the wound using a sterile cloth or clean fabric. Do not remove the material once it is saturated; instead, add more layers on top to maintain consistent pressure until medical assistance takes over.
Burns are another common injury that requires specific care to prevent further tissue damage. The immediate goal is to cool the burn to stop the heating process. Run cool running water over the area for at least twenty minutes if possible, or apply a cool compress. Do not use ice, as this can further damage the already compromised tissue and cause severe constriction of blood vessels. Never apply butter, ointments, or other home remedies to a fresh burn, as these can trap heat and increase the risk of infection. Keep the burn covered with a sterile, non-fluffy dressing and seek medical attention for anything larger than a small blister or involving vital areas like the face, hands, or genitals.
Finally, please take the time to review the attached checklist and locate the nearest automated external defibrillator in our facility. Knowing where the emergency supplies are kept is just as important as knowing how to use them. I encourage you to practice the basic techniques we will demonstrate in person, especially proper hand hygiene before and after treating any wound. A clean environment and clean hands are the first line of defense against infection. If you have any specific questions or concerns about these procedures, feel free to reach out to me directly before the workshop so we can address them together. Let's make sure everyone is prepared to handle the unexpected with competence and calmness.
Best regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Safety Coordinator

Subject: Final Logistics and Crew Call for the "Echoes of Light" Exhibition
Hi Team,
Just wanted to send out a quick update on where we stand with the final preparations for the "Echoes of Light" exhibition. We are officially two weeks away from the opening night, and the energy in the studio has shifted from frantic production to a focused calm. Most of the physical installations have been completed, and the atmospheric lighting rigs are being tested for the first time in the gallery space. It is looking incredibly surreal to see the holographic projections interacting with the brick walls, but there are still a few final adjustments we need to make regarding the audio synchronization before we lock the timeline.
I know everyone has been working late shifts this past week, so please take this morning to get some rest. However, I have scheduled a critical crew call for tomorrow at ten a.m. in the main assembly room. We need all department heads present, specifically from structure, digital media, and facilities. The primary goal of this meeting will be to resolve the lingering issues with the interactive kiosks in the east wing. The current latency is causing inconsistent responses to viewer input, which is not acceptable for the premium experience we are promising. I want a concrete fix plan from the technical lead by noon tomorrow so we can implement it during the weekend downtime.
On a positive note, the press release has gone out, and the initial media response has been exceptionally warm. Two major art publications have already confirmed their attendance for the VIP preview, and the local news channel is planning a segment on the innovative use of sustainable materials in our setup. This level of attention is a great endorsement of the curatorial vision we established months ago. It also means that every detail matters more than usual. We need to ensure that the visitor flow is smooth and that the explanatory signage is meticulously proofed. I have asked the education department to double-check for typos, but I would appreciate if everyone could keep an eye out while they are in the space tomorrow.
Regarding the catering and hospitality arrangements, we have finally settled on a vendor who can accommodate dietary restrictions while serving high-quality refreshments. The budget came in slightly under our previous estimate, which leaves us a small buffer for potential overtime costs if the final testing requires late nights. I am also aware that the storage unit on the fourth floor is becoming cluttered with packaging materials old labels, and unused props from earlier concepts. Can facilities please schedule a cleanup session for Friday afternoon? We need that vertical space clear so the riggers can safely access the ceiling mounts for the final hanging of the textile pieces.
Thank you all for your continued dedication and hard work. This project represents a significant milestone for our institution, and it is truly a testament to your collective talent and resilience. Please feel free to reach out to me or my assistant if you run into any show-stopping issues before our meeting. Otherwise, let's keep the momentum going and prepare to showcase this remarkable work to the public. I look forward to seeing everyone at the crew call tomorrow morning.
Best regards,
Elena Vane
Chief Curator
Modern and Contemporary Art Division

Farmington Bank

The history of Farmington Bank dates back to May 1851 when a petition was presented to the Connecticut General Assembly. On August 12, 1851, the charter was issued and an organizational meeting was held on August 14, 1851, at the home of Samuel Cowles (27 Main Street, Farmington, Connecticut). The following officers and trustees were elected at the meeting;

Timothy Cowles (President) - Farmer William L. Cowles (1st Vice President) - Merchant Samuel S. Cowles (2nd Vice President) - Farmer / Printer / Publisher / Writer Deacon Simeon Hart (Secretary & Treasurer) - Educator William Gay (Trustee) - Merchant Ira Hadsell (Trustee) - Farmer Henry Mygatt (Trustee) - Farmer Chauncey Rowe (Trustee) - Store Owner Thomas Cowles (Trustee) - Farmer E. W. Carrington (Trustee) - Physician Farmington Savings Bank opened for business August 25, 1851, from Deacon Simeon Hart's home (93 Main Street, Farmington, Connecticut) who was responsible for managing the bank. On the first day of business, Farmington Savings Bank opened 12 accounts with a total of $88.70 in deposits from residents and business across the Farmington Valley. The first savings book was issued to Miss Harriet E. Porter. In 1853, Farmington Savings Bank moved into Samuel Cowles' house on 27 Main Street in Farmington, Connecticut who became treasurer after the death of Deacon Simeon Hart. On January 12, 1865, Farmington Savings Bank purchased 32 Main Street in Farmington, Connecticut from Erastus Gay who managed a store that stood close to Main Street. The store was initially erected in 1791 by Reuben S. Norton and was used for various purposes throughout the years, including; a general store, a tailor's shop, a post office, a church, and a drinking establishment. Upon taking ownership of the store, Farmington Savings Bank made additional improvements, such as;

One (1) street lamp (1874) Four (4) hitching posts (1883) Fire proof room (1890) Steel lining and time controlled double door (1895) In 1926, Farmington Savings Bank employed W.F. Brooks in to design the new building on the 32 Main Street property. The building construction was completed in April 1928 by Industrial Construction Co. of Hartford, Connecticut. The existing bank was razed after the completion of the newly constructed bank.

On June 29, 2011, shares of Farmington Bank began trading on NASDAQ under the symbol FBNK. Farmington Bank was invited to ring the NASDAQ closing bell on October 12, 2011 to celebrate becoming a public company.

In September 2014, Farmington Bank announced plans to enter western Massachusetts with the establishment of a commercial lending office and two de novo hub branches in West Springfield, Massachusetts and East Longmeadow, Massachusetts.

In July 2018, People's United Bank, based in Bridgeport, Connecticut, announced that it had agreed to buy Farmington Bank in an all-stock deal for $544 million. Both its board and that of Farmington Bank's parent, First Connecticut Bankcorp, Inc., had approved the deal, which was expected to result in branch closures.

During the company's 2018 acquisition, the FSB (Farmington Savings Bank) Foundation was incorporated and established as a private, independent charitable foundation. Its stated goal is to continue the legacy of the Farmington Savings Bank by supporting improved economic viability and the well-being of residents in the original area of the bank. Since its incorporation in 2018, the foundation has distributed nearly $4.5 million in grants.

First Connecticut Bankcorp, Inc., is the holding company for Farmington Bank. Farmington Bank has over $2.5 billion in assets (2014) and with a network of over 20 branches located in Connecticut.

school fundraising

School fundraising has become a cornerstone of many public and private institutions, providing the extra resources needed to enrich curricula, upgrade facilities, and support extracurricular programs that standard budgets simply cannot cover. When parents, teachers, and local businesses come together around a shared goal, the impact can be both immediate and lasting, turning modest contributions into projects that shape students' educational experiences for years to come.

Most districts now blend traditional events with digital platforms, creating a hybrid model that reaches a broader audience. A seasonal bake sale or a community car wash can be paired with an online crowdfunding page that accepts credit-card donations from alumni who live far away. Social media amplifies the message, allowing volunteers to post photos, share progress bars, and celebrate milestones in real time. This mix of face-to-face interaction and virtual outreach keeps momentum high and invites participation from people who might otherwise feel disconnected from school life.

Effective planning starts with a clear, written goal that outlines exactly what the funds will support-whether it is a new science lab, upgraded athletic equipment, or a scholarship fund.
