To All Staff and Departamental Managers

This memo serves as a formal reminder regarding the updated protocols for managing outstanding invoices and accounts receivable. Recent audits have highlighted a significant increase in the average days sales outstanding, which negatively impacts our cash flow and financial stability. It is imperative that all teams adhere strictly to the new timeline for sending and following up on invoice reminders. Effective immediately, the standard grace period for payment is reduced from thirty to fifteen days. Any invoice that remains unpaid after this period will automatically trigger the first stage of the collection process. This adjustment is designed to tighten our financial controls and ensure a smoother operational cycle throughout the organization.

The first reminder, known as the courtesy notice, will be sent automatically by the accounting software exactly on day sixteen of the billing cycle. This email will include a direct link to the original invoice and a secure payment portal. Team leads are responsible for monitoring their respective departments to ensure that no critical project dependencies are stalled due to overdue supplier payments. Please verify that all work orders and change requests are approved and submitted to Finance before the billing deadline. Early submission allows the accounting team to process invoices efficiently, reducing the likelihood of delays or errors that would necessitate manual intervention and further postpone the payment schedule.

Should the invoice remain unpaid by day thirty, the system will generate a more formal notice, styled as a final demand. This document must be reviewed by the Sales Director before release to clients, as the tone shifts from administrative to urgent. During this phase, account managers are expected to reach out directly to the client's finance department to identify any potential obstacles, such as disputed line items or internal approval bottlenecks. raw:
The Facilities Department is launching a campus-wide composting program beginning next month, and all staff and students are asked to participate. Organic waste such as fruit skins, coffee grounds, tea bags, and vegetable scraps can now be diverted from the landfill and turned into valuable soil amendment. Separate compost bins will be placed beside every kitchen, break room, and cafeteria, clearly marked with the green leaf symbol.

To ensure the system works efficiently, only biodegradable food waste should be placed in the compost containers. Items that are not compostable-such as plastic wrap, metal utensils, paper towels, and pet waste-must continue to go into the regular trash. If you are unsure whether an item is acceptable, consult the quick reference guide posted on the bins or visit the Facilities website for a full list of approved materials.

Compost collected each day will be transported to the municipal processing facility, where it will be aerated, turned, and allowed to mature over a period of several weeks. The finished product will be used to enrich the soil in our campus gardens, athletic fields, and landscaping projects, reducing the need for chemical fertilizers and supporting healthier plant growth. By keeping the compost stream clean, we help maintain the quality of the material and prevent odors or pests.

All employees are encouraged to take a few minutes each day to rinse containers before discarding food scraps, as excess liquid can cause leaks and attract insects. If a bin becomes full, simply use the next one in line; the collection crew will replace all containers during their routine pickups. Should you notice any issues-such as spillage or damaged lids-report them promptly to the Facilities help desk.

Your participation is essential to the success of this sustainability initiative. By composting, we lower our carbon footprint, conserve landfill space, and contribute to a greener campus environment. Thank you for your cooperation and commitment to responsible waste management.

street food guide

The allure of street food lies in its immediacy and authenticity. Unlike polished restaurant dining, eating on the street places you directly in the heart of a city's daily rhythm. You watch the wok dance, hear the sizzle of chilies hitting hot oil, and smell the fresh marinade being brushed onto skewers. It is an immersive sensory experience that guidesbooks often struggle to capture. To navigate this vibrant landscape successfully, however, requires more than just an empty stomach; it demands a certain level of confidence and a willingness to step outside your culinary comfort zone.

Choosing the right stall is perhaps the most critical skill a street food eater must develop. Look for vendors with a steady stream of local customers, particularly other street vendors or construction workers. These are the people who eat here every day for budget and convenience, not for tourism. If a cart is packed with locals, the food is likely fresh, safe, and high-quality. Observe the cleanliness of the workspace; even if the equipment is rented or mobile, the vendor should be wiping surfaces frequently and handling food with care. Trust the crowd's wisdom over your own initial aesthetic judgments, as many of the best stalls look rugged rather than refined.

Food safety is a natural concern when dining on the sidewalk, but heat is your best ally. Stick to dishes that are cooked to high temperatures for a short duration, such as stir-fried noodles, grilled meats, or boiled dumplings. The intense heat during cooking kills most harmful bacteria, provided you eat the food immediately after it is served. It is advisable to avoid raw cuts of meat, unpeeled fruits, or dishes that have been sitting out in the open for hours. Hygiene tips like carrying hand sanitizer and avoiding ice cubes unless they were made from bottled water can also help mitigate minor risks while ensuring you enjoy the meal without later regret.

Budgeting for street food offers incredible value, allowing you to try a wider variety of dishes than a sit-down meal would permit. In many Asian cities, a hearty bowl of noodle soup might cost only a few dollars, enabling you to sample three or four different specialties in a single afternoon. This variety is the true reward of street eating. You can move from a spicy fish noodle stall to a sweet shaved ice stand, then to a savory meatball cart, exploring the culinary depth of the region without breaking the bank. Keep small bills and coins handy, as many vendors do not have change for larger notes or do not accept mobile payments.

Finally, approach street food with respect for the local culture and the hard work of the vendor. Learn a few key phrases in the local language, such as "thank you," "delicious," or "spicy." Most street food makers are proud of their craft and appreciate polite, patient customers. Wait for your food without rushing the process, and tip generously where it is customary, even if it is not expected. When you treat the vendor as a professional and show genuine interest in their dish, the interaction becomes memorable in itself. Street food is not just about feeding hunger; it is about connecting with the community that sustains the city, one delicious bite at a time.

It is advisable to avoid raw cuts of meat, unpeeled fruits, or dishes that have been sitting out in the open for hours. Budgeting for street food offers incredible value, allowing you to try a wider variety of dishes than a sit-down meal would permit. In many Asian cities, a hearty bowl of noodle soup might cost only a few dollars, enabling you to sample three or four different specialties in a single afternoon. This variety is the true reward of street eating. You can move from a spicy fish noodle stall to a sweet shaved ice stand, then to a savory meatball cart, exploring the culinary depth of the region without breaking the bank. Keep small bills and coins handy, as many vendors do not have change for larger notes or do not accept mobile payments.
Finally, approach street food with respect for the local culture and the hard work of the vendor. Learn a few key phrases in the local language, such as "thank you," "delicious," or "spicy." Most street food makers are proud of their craft and appreciate polite, patient customers. Wait for your food without rushing the process, and tip generously where it is customary, even if it is not expected. When you treat the vendor as a professional and show genuine interest in their dish, the interaction becomes memorable in itself. Street food is not just about feeding hunger; it is about connecting with the community that sustains the city, one delicious bite at a time.

composting

Composting has moved from garden hobby to mainstream sustainability practice, and it's easy to see why. Turning kitchen scraps and yard waste into dark, crumbly soil not only reduces the volume of trash sent to landfills, but it also returns valuable nutrients to the earth. For homeowners, renters, and community gardeners alike, a modest effort in the backyard can translate into healthier plants, lower water use, and a smaller carbon footprint.

Getting started begins with finding a suitable spot. A sunny corner of a patio, a shaded corner of a garden, or even a sturdy plastic bin on a balcony can serve as the composting vessel. The container should have good airflow, so a few drilled holes or a loosely woven fabric works well. Position the bin where you can easily add material and turn the pile without bending over too far, and keep it out of direct rain to avoid soggy conditions.

The core of any successful compost heap lies in the balance of "green" and "brown" materials. Kitchen vegetable peels, coffee grounds, and fresh grass clippings provide nitrogen-rich greens, while dried leaves, shredded newspaper, and sawdust act as carbon-rich browns. Avoid adding meat, dairy, oily foods, or pet waste, as these can attract pests and slow decomposition. A simple rule of thumb is to aim for roughly two parts brown to one part green by volume.

During the first few weeks, the pile will heat up as microbes break down the organic matter. Turning the compost once a week with a garden fork introduces fresh oxygen and helps regulate temperature. If the mixture feels dry, a light mist of water is all that's needed; if it's too wet, toss in more dry browns. After one to three months, the material will lose its original shape, smell earthy, and feel like rich soil.

Finished compost can be spread directly onto flower beds, mixed into vegetable patches, or used as a top dressing for lawns. Many municipalities now offer curbside compost collection, allowing those without space to participate. By turning everyday waste into a resource, composting creates a closed-loop system that nurtures the environment, supports local food production, and fosters a sense of community stewardship.

Date: 8 October 2026 
Subject: Climate Adaptation Initiative - Implementation Overview 
From: Office of Sustainability 
To: All Department Heads and Project Leads

The executive leadership has approved a comprehensive climate adaptation program to safeguard our operations against the increasing frequency of extreme weather events, rising temperatures, and long-term shifts in precipitation patterns. This initiative aligns with the national Climate Resilience Framework and our corporate commitment to net-zero emissions by 2050. Effective immediately, each department is required to integrate adaptation considerations into their planning cycles, risk assessments, and budget proposals. The goal is to ensure continuity of service, protect assets, and support the communities in which we operate.

In the first phase, we will conduct a vulnerability audit of all facilities, supply-chain nodes, and critical infrastructure. The audit will quantify exposure to flood, heat-stress, sea-level rise, and other climate-related hazards, and will prioritize sites based on risk severity and operational importance. Results are expected by 31 December 2026 and will feed directly into the development of site-specific adaptation plans. Departments should allocate staff time and resources to assist the Sustainability Team in data collection, on-site inspections, and stakeholder interviews.

Adaptation actions will be categorized into structural, operational, and strategic measures. Structural measures may include elevating equipment, reinforcing building envelopes, and installing passive cooling systems. Operational measures will focus on revising maintenance schedules, updating emergency response protocols, and enhancing real-time monitoring of environmental conditions. Strategic measures involve diversifying supply sources, revising capital investment criteria to favor climate-resilient designs, and engaging with local authorities to coordinate regional adaptation efforts. All proposed measures must be cost-effective, evidence-based, and compliant with applicable regulations.

Responsibility for implementation rests with the designated Adaptation Lead in each department, who will report progress quarterly to the Office of Sustainability. A cross-functional steering committee, chaired by the Chief Operating Officer, will review progress, resolve cross-departmental issues, and approve any required reallocations of funding. Training sessions on climate risk awareness and adaptation best practices will be scheduled for all relevant staff during Q1 2027, and attendance will be tracked as part of performance metrics.

Finally, we will establish a monitoring and evaluation framework to track the effectiveness of adaptation actions over time. Key performance indicators will include reductions in downtime due to climate events, cost savings from avoided damage, and improvements in stakeholder confidence. Annual reports will be published for internal review and external stakeholders, demonstrating our commitment to resilient, sustainable operations in a changing climate.

Subject: Thoughts on expanding protected bike lanes downtown
Hi Sarah,
I wanted to share a few quick observations from my recent commute regarding the city's current bike infrastructure. It has been frustrating to see the inconsistent quality of the lanes we have so far, particularly on the corridors near the main business district. Many of these routes are merely painted lines that offer no physical barrier against motor vehicles, which creates a legitimate sense of danger for anyone trying to use them. We need to move beyond cosmetic changes and focus on actual physical separation to make these spaces viable for the average person.
The decline in ridership during peak hours seems directly correlated with the lack of safety features. I spoke with a few colleagues who used to cycle to work but have switched to driving or using ride-share services. Their primary concern was not the distance, but the fear of close passes from large trucks and impatient cars. If we want to reduce traffic congestion and improve air quality, we must create an environment where cycling is perceived as safe, not just for experts, but for families and older residents as well.
We should prioritize the installation of concrete or planted barriers on the busiest streets first. This approach has shown promising results in comparable cities, leading to a significant drop in traffic accidents and an increase in daily active users. While the initial cost might seem high, the long-term benefits in public health savings and reduced emergency response needs justify the investment. We cannot afford to keep treating this as a low priority while our roadways remain clogged with single-occupancy vehicles.
There is also a strong economic argument for improving these lanes. Local shops report higher foot and bike traffic when the streets feel more pedestrian-friendly and less dominated by rushing cars. A calmer street environment encourages people to stop and engage with the community rather than just passing through quickly. We are selling our city as a livable, charming place, but the design of our roads suggests we value speed over quality of life.
I hope you can include these points in the upcoming city council meeting notes. We have the opportunity to create a lasting positive change if we act now. Let me know if you have a chance to review the recent safety statistics before the meeting, as I think they will support the case for expanded protected infrastructure quite effectively.
Best regards,
James

Switch virtual interface

A switch virtual interface (SVI) or routed VLAN interface (RVI) is a virtual network interface that represents a logical layer-3 interface on a multilayer network switch. VLANs divide broadcast domains in a local area network (LAN) environment. Whenever hosts in one VLAN need to communicate with hosts in another VLAN, the traffic must be routed between them. This is known as inter-VLAN routing. On layer-3 switches it is accomplished by the creation of layer-3 interfaces (SVIs). An SVI is a virtual routed interface that connects a VLAN on the device to the Layer 3 router engine on the same device. Only one VLAN interface can be associated with a VLAN, but you need to configure a VLAN interface for a VLAN only when you want to route between VLANs or to provide IP host connectivity to the device through a virtual routing and forwarding (VRF) instance that is not the management VRF. When you enable VLAN interface creation, a switch creates a VLAN interface for the default VLAN (VLAN 1) to permit remote switch administration. SVIs are generally configured for a VLAN for the following reasons:

To allow traffic to be routed between VLANs by providing a default gateway for the VLAN. To provide fallback bridging (if required for non-routable protocols). To provide Layer 3 IP connectivity to the switch. To support bridging configurations and routing protocol. To provide an access layer - 'Routed Access' Configuration (in lieu of Spanning Tree Protocol) Advantages include:

Much faster than router-on-a-stick, because everything is hardware-switched and -routed. No need for external links from the switch to a router for routing. Not limited to one link. Layer 2 EtherChannels can be used between the switches to get more bandwidth. Latency is much lower, because it does not need to leave the switch.

Subject: Q3 Budget Planning and Timeline
Dear Team,
As we approach the end of the second quarter, it's time to start gathering the information we'll need for the upcoming fiscal year's budget. Our goal is to have a complete draft ready for senior review by the first week of August, which gives us enough time to incorporate any feedback before the final submission at the end of the month. Please treat this as a priority item on your calendars, and let me know if you anticipate any conflicts.
The first step is to collect the most recent actuals for your department, along with any known variances that have already surfaced. I ask each manager to compare the current figures against the projections we used in the last planning cycle and to note any significant deviations, whether they stem from changes in market conditions, staffing, or operational efficiency. This analysis will serve as the foundation for the assumptions we build into our new budget.
Once you have the variance analysis, please prepare a concise summary that outlines your department's key drivers for the next twelve months. Include any planned capital expenditures, anticipated hiring, and expected shifts in revenue or cost structures. The summary should be no more than two pages and must be submitted to the finance team by June 28. Early submissions are encouraged, as they allow us to identify cross-departmental impacts and begin aligning resources sooner rather than later.
After the finance team receives all departmental inputs, we will consolidate the data into a single model and run a series of sensitivity scenarios. I expect to circulate a draft version of the consolidated budget by July 15, giving everyone a chance to review the numbers and provide comments. Please be prepared to join a brief virtual workshop on July 20, where we will walk through the model, discuss any outliers, and agree on the adjustments needed before we lock the figures.
Finally, remember that budget planning is not just a compliance exercise but an opportunity to shape our strategic priorities for the year ahead. I encourage you to think beyond the numbers and consider how your department can contribute to the company's growth objectives while maintaining fiscal discipline. If you have questions or need clarification on any part of this process, feel free to reach out to me directly or to our finance lead, Maya Patel.
Best regards,
Jordan Lee
Director of Finance
Acme Enterprises

The Works Art & Design Festival

The Works Art & Design Festival is a thirteen-day festival held at the end of June and the beginning of July in downtown Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. The festival displays the work of artists and designers from across Canada as well as exhibits from international presenters.

The festival is held in downtown Edmonton. It was first held in 1986. It has over 372,000 attendees. It presents free art exhibits in over 30 venues around Edmonton's centre, such as restaurants, vacant retail spaces, warehouses, city parks, and office building lobbies. Since 2021, the main site is Sir Winston Churchill Square.

The festival exhibits the work of well-known and emerging artists. Any artist or designer may apply to participate in the festival, or may be invited by the festival. The majority of the content is Canadian. In 2009, The Works launched The Works Canadian Aboriginal Artist Program, which features art from aboriginal artists. The "Works With Jazz" Program is a collaboration between The Works Art & Design Festival and The Edmonton Jazz Festival. It features jazz and art performances.

Epithelantha greggii

Epithelantha greggii is a small cactus species characterized by a branched, generally spherical or obovoid stem. The stem often has a flattened top with a depressed apex and measures 5 to 7.5 cm in diameter. Its surface is densely covered with spines, giving it a compact appearance. The root system is typically diffuse. The plant has numerous tiny tubercles, about 1 to 2 mm in size, which do not fuse into ribs. These hemispherical or short-cylindrical tubercles are arranged in tight spirals around the stem. At the tip of each tubercle is a small, nearly circular areole, about 1 mm long and lacking glands. When the plant is juvenile, the areoles show slight wooliness; in mature stems, wool becomes more prominent at the apex. Spines are abundant-more than 20 per areole-and vary in color from chalk-white to ash-gray or reddish-brown. They are 3 to 5 mm long, straight, cylindrical, slender, and arranged radially from an early age. The spines are not pectinate or pressed against the stem and are non-pungent, with the upper spines being longer. The flowers are small, funnel-shaped, and pink, opening during the day. They are less conspicuous, emerging at the upper edges of spine clusters at the plant's apex. The flowers open partially, with only the distal part visible above the woolly area, which is covered by longer spines. Flowering occurs in late spring to early summer. Fruits are bright red, slender, and narrowly cylindrical, about 1.8 cm long and 2-3 mm (occasionally up to 5 mm) wide. They are initially somewhat succulent but dry quickly, becoming papery. The fruits lack spines and pulp, have a smooth surface, and shed floral remnants easily. Fruiting occurs in summer.

This species is native to Nuevo Leon and Coahuila states of Mexico growing mainly in desert and dry scrub habitats at elevations of 700 to 1300 meters. The plant favors gently sloping hills and mountain plateaus with coarse gravel soils. It is found growing along with Echinocactus horizonthalonius, Ariocarpus retusus, Ariocarpus fissuratus, Coryphantha poselgeriana, Coryphantha pseudoechinus, Coryphantha delaetiana, Coryphantha gladiispina, Grusonia bradtiana, Escobaria strobiliformis, Lophophora williamsii, Thelocactus bicolor, Sclerocactus mariposensis, Mammillaria lasiacantha, Opuntia microdasys, Neolloydia conoidea, and Mammillaria pottsii.

It was described in 1856 by George Engelmann as Mammillaria micromeris var. greggii, and was later elevated to species status and transferred to the genus Epithelantha by Charles Russell Orcutt in 1926. The species name greggii honors the American naturalist Josiah Gregg.

raw:
warranty terms

Understanding warranty terms can be confusing for many consumers. Most manufacturers offer standard coverage periods, typically ranging from one to three years. These periods protect buyers against defects in materials or workmanship. However, the specific details vary significantly between brands and product categories. It is crucial to read the fine print on any purchase receipt or product tag. Ignoring these nuances can lead to costly misunderstandings later on.

Extended warranties are often sold as add-ons at checkout. They promise additional coverage beyond the standard limit, sometimes doubling or tripling the duration. While appealing, these plans come with their own conditions. Service fees may apply per incident, and certain components might be excluded entirely. Customers should weigh the cost of the extension against the actual risk of failure. Comparing quotes from different providers is a smart strategy before committing.

Warranties rarely cover normal wear and tear. Scratches, battery degradation, and minor cosmetic damage are usually out of scope. Manufacturer support teams interpret these exclusions strictly during claim reviews. If a product fails due to misuse or unauthorized repair, coverage is often voided immediately. Keeping original packaging and receipts helps prove proper handling. Documentation is your best defense against a denied service request.

Installation requirements also play a significant role in validity. Some electronics require professional setup by certified technicians. DIY installation can invalidate the entire protection package silently. Always check if the warranty mandates specific service providers. Using third-party repair shops might risk future claims approval. Sticking to authorized channels ensures full compliance with the terms agreed upon at purchase.

When a product fails within the coverage window, act quickly. Photograph the issue and log the sequence of errors. Contact the support line with your serial number ready. Clear communication speeds up the diagnosis process significantly. Most companies offer repair, replacement, or refund options based on severity. Understanding your entitlements beforehand helps you negotiate effectively. Never accept the first offer without reviewing the policy clauses again.

Broken Mirrors

Home | About | Contact

Broken Mirrors (Hebrew: מראות שבורות, romanized: Marot Shvurotl) is a 2019 Israeli drama film written and directed by Imri Matalon and Aviad Givon and starring Shira Haas. The film had its world premiere at the 2018 Rome Film Festival as part of the competition at the 18th edition of Alice in the City section. Broken Mirrors was nominated for three Ophir Awards (Best Screenplay, Lead Actress for Shira Haas, and Casting), and won the Jury Prize at the 2019 SCHLINGEL International Film Festival. The film is distributed in Israel by United King Films and internationally by Wazabi Films.

The film depicts the relationship between Giora (Yiftach Klein) and his daughter, Ariela (Shira Haas). Giora, an officer with the rank of Lieutenant Colonel, is a strict father who punishes his daughter for every boundary crossing. Their relationship even borders on sexual abuse. One day, Ariela causes a car accident due to inexperience, and Giora refuses to punish her. Ariela sets out on a journey to punish herself on as large a scale as possible and, along the way, discovers a concealed event from her father's military past, which serves as the cause of his behavior.

renting an apartment

Finding the right apartment is often less about finding a perfect home and more about finding the right compromise. Walk into any open house and you will immediately notice that almost every unit comes with a trade-off. Perhaps the kitchen is spacious but the natural light is dim, or the location is central yet the parking is at a premium. Understanding early what you are willing to sacrifice helps you move through the process with clearer intent and less emotional attachment to specific features that may not matter in the long run.

The application phase can feel overwhelming due to the paperwork involved, so preparation is key. Before you submit a request, gather your pay stubs, bank statements, and a list of references. Having these documents organized in a single digital folder speeds up the verification process significantly. Landlords and property management companies receive dozens of inquiries weekly, so presenting your financial history clearly and professionally sets you apart from other applicants and demonstrates reliability in the eyes of the potential landlord.

Negotiation is a standard part of the leasing conversation, even though many renters hesitate to bring it up. Do not be afraid to ask for small concessions, such as a discounted first month or flexible move-in dates. Often, landlords are more open to discussing terms than their listing descriptions suggest. However, always maintain a polite and professional tone. Your goal is to build a cooperative relationship with your future landlord, so excessive pressure can sometimes backfire and result in you losing the lease entirely.

Before signing the final lease, walk through the unit with a critical eye. Test the water pressure, check the internet speed, and look for signs of moisture in the bathrooms. Take photos of any existing damage on the floor, walls, or fixtures to avoid being blamed for pre-existing issues later. This documentation is your primary defense during the move-out inspection, so do not skip this step. It is a small effort that protects your security deposit and ensures peace of mind for the entire duration of your tenancy.

Finally, once you move in, introduce yourself to your neighbors. Building a basic rapport in the early days makes the transition into a new neighborhood much smoother. Whether it is a busy urban apartment complex or a quiet suburban flat, knowing who you are can turn a purely transactional living situation into a more comfortable and supportive community experience. This simple act of neighborliness is often the final step in making a rental feel like home.

Subject: Returns and Renewals for Spring Checkout
Dear Library Services Team,

Sparkling Night

Sparkling Night (stylized SPARKLING NIGHT) is the debut Japanese-language solo studio album by South Korean guitarist and CNBLUE member Lee Jong-hyun. It was released on July 27, 2016, under Warner Music Japan.

Two years prior to the release of the album, Lee composed a blues song; his bandmates encouraged him to utilize the song for his solo album. In expressing his desire to release music independent from CNBLUE, Lee expected to collaborate with a different band instead of releasing a solo album. He worked with several composers in order to include a multitude of sounds which deviated from CNBLUE's music. Lee asked bandmate Jung Yong-hwa to compose a song for the album, which did not come to fruition due to Jung's filming schedule. The lead single for Sparklight Night was determined by the record label via voting between two songs; "Moonlight Swing" was ultimately selected.

Dealing with eternal love, "Moonlight Swing" is a swing music song which incorporates elements of big band and emits a "fairy tale-like" atmosphere. Initially a song about remaining "pure and honest like Peter Pan", Lee made the decision to change "Moonlight Swing" into a love song in order to create a more relatable track.

Sparkling Night was announced as Lee's debut Japanese-language studio album on June 8, 2016, with a release date of July 27. Upon the announcement of the album, a "special" website was introduced where further information would be revealed. A 20-second preview of the music video for "Moonlight Swing" was uploaded on Lee's Instagram account on June 17, 2016; the full music video was uploaded on Warner Music Japan's YouTube channel three days later. On June 22, the record label also uploaded an album digest. A teaser for the lyric video for "Smile" was published on July 11 prior to its full release three days later. "Moonlight Swing" was made available at digital retailers on July 13. Sparkling Night was released on July 27 in three editions: Regular Edition; Limited Edition with bonus DVD content that includes the music video and making of "Moonlight Swing"; and Boice Limited Edition that includes a set of Lee and guitar pin badges. Lee embarked on the 1st Solo Concert in Japan "Welcome to Sparkling Night" tour, his first series of solo concerts. The first two concerts took place from August 9-10 at the Osaka International Convention Center in Osaka, followed by a concert on August 13 at the Nagoya Congress Center in Aichi, and two final concerts from August 17-18 at the Tokyo International Forum in Tokyo.

On the chart dated August 8, 2016, Sparkling Night debuted at number seven on the weekly Oricon Albums Chart, selling 12,583 copies in its first week. On the same issue date, it debuted at number nine on Billboard Japan magazine's Hot Albums. It has sold 13,529 copies in the country since its release.

Jane Walker Burleson

May Jane Walker Burleson (1888-1957), also known as Jennie May Burleson, was a notable socialite, artist, and Texan suffragette who was the grand marshal of the Woman Suffrage Parade of 1913 in Washington, DC. Mounted with confidence on her horse, she led a parade of 5,000 people up Pennsylvania Avenue, Washington, DC and "into a melee that changed the direction of the suffrage movement." During the 1930s her name was associated with scandal, attracting wide media attention in Texas, as she shot and killed the woman her husband married after their contentious divorce in 1938.

Jane Walker was born and spent her early years in Galveston, Texas. Her parents John Caffery Walker (1849 - 1924) and Clara Waters Wilson Walker (1855 - 1937) had four children. Walker's father was a lawyer and judge from a prominent Texas family.

Burleson studied art in New York under the eminent painter William Chase and received her teaching certificate from Chase's normal school upon graduation. In 1914 she took courses at George Washington University in economics and sociology.

After her marriage in 1908 to Lieutenant Richard Coke Burleson (1881-1960) of the Third Field Artillery, they were ordered to Manila. With her teacher's certificate from Chase's normal school, she worked as supervisor in Manila public school system for two years where she trained and supervised five hundred teachers who in turn taught "thousands of children."

Upon their return to the United States, Lieutenant Burleson was stationed at Fort Myer just out of Washington, DC. In Washington, she joined the short-lived Congressional Union for Woman Suffrage association which was founded in 1913 by Alice Paul and Lucy Burns to campaign for a constitutional amendment guaranteeing women's suffrage Burleson was the grand marshal of the Woman Suffrage Parade of 1913 in Washington, DC. She was featured in a February 1914 article in the Meriden Morning Record under the heading "Women Worth While." She was described as a "handsome young wife" who "was one of the most accomplished women in the army and navy circles in Washington, DC- an expert swimmer and diver who played golf, tennis and could "ride the most spirited mount." Burleson's husband served overseas during World War I, commanding the 107th Regiment of the 53rd Field Artillery Brigade in Belgium. He advanced to the rank of colonel and received several medals for his service.

Her husband filed for divorce in 1935 and the case was heard in the District Court of San Saba County in November 1936 with his appeal for divorce being denied. In April 1937, attorneys allegedly acting on behalf of Jennie May Burleson "filed a cross action for divorce," which resulted in a divorce. However, Jennie Burleson alleged that she had not authorized the cross action suit. On September 27, 1937, Jennie May Burleson filed a "voluminous" report to have the April 1937 divorce judgment retracted "because the defense of insanity was not set up in some manner as against either spouse obtaining a divorce; and charged her attorneys with fraud, collusion, and misrepresentation in filing her cross action for divorce, knowing her nervous and mental state, and in not securing an order of the court to place her under "observation and a judgment as to her sanity before submitting to a trial." Her submission was dismissed by Justice Blair. The divorce made headlines in the media as a society scandal.

In 1940, Burleson was again on the front pages of American newspapers for the murder of Isabelle Burleson, the woman Richard Burleson married immediately after their divorce was granted. Jennie Burleson traveled by train from Texas to Columbia, South Carolina, sought out Mrs. Burleson at a restaurant she frequented, and shot her twice. The jury found her guilty of voluntary manslaughter by reason of insanity and she was sentenced to twelve years. In October 1948, she was released having served eight years in prison in South Carolina and she returned to the Walker family home.

May Jane Walker Burleson (1888-1957), also known as Jennie May Burleson, was a notable socialite, artist, and Texan suffragette who was the grand marshal of the Woman Suffrage Parade of 1913 in Washington, DC. Mounted with confidence on her horse, she led a parade of 5,000 people up Pennsylvania Avenue, Washington, DC and "into a melee that changed the direction of the suffrage movement." During the 1930s her name was associated with scandal, attracting wide media attention in Texas, as she shot and killed the woman her husband married after their contentious divorce in 1938.

Jane Walker was born and spent her early years in Galveston, Texas. Her parents John Caffery Walker (1849 - 1924) and Clara Waters Wilson Walker (1855 - 1937) had four children. Walker's father was a lawyer and judge from a prominent Texas family.

Burleson studied art in New York under the eminent painter William Chase and received her teaching certificate from Chase's normal school upon graduation. In 1914 she took courses at George Washington University in economics and sociology.

After her marriage in 1908 to Lieutenant Richard Coke Burleson (1881-1960) of the Third Field Artillery, they were ordered to Manila. With her teacher's certificate from Chase's normal school, she worked as supervisor in Manila public school system for two years where she trained and supervised five hundred teachers who in turn taught "thousands of children."

Upon their return to the United States, Lieutenant Burleson was stationed at Fort Myer just out of Washington, DC. In Washington, she joined the short-lived Congressional Union for Woman Suffrage association which was founded in 1913 by Alice Paul and Lucy Burns to campaign for a constitutional amendment guaranteeing women's suffrage Burleson was the grand marshal of the Woman Suffrage Parade of 1913 in Washington, DC. She was featured in a February 1914 article in the Meriden Morning Record under the heading "Women Worth While." She was described as a "handsome young wife" who "was one of the most accomplished women in the army and navy circles in Washington, DC- an expert swimmer and diver who played golf, tennis and could "ride the most spirited mount." Burleson's husband served overseas during World War I, commanding the 107th Regiment of the 53rd Field Artillery Brigade in Belgium. He advanced to the rank of colonel and received several medals for his service.

Her husband filed for divorce in 1935 and the case was heard in the District Court of San Saba County in November 1936 with his appeal for divorce being denied. In April 1937, attorneys allegedly acting on behalf of Jennie May Burleson "filed a cross action for divorce," which resulted in a divorce. However, Jennie Burleson alleged that she had not authorized the cross action suit. On September 27, 1937, Jennie May Burleson filed a "voluminous" report to have the April 1937 divorce judgment retracted "because the defense of insanity was not set up in some manner as against either spouse obtaining a divorce; and charged her attorneys with fraud, collusion, and misrepresentation in filing her cross action for divorce, knowing her nervous and mental state, and in not securing an order of the court to place her under "observation and a judgment as to her sanity before submitting to a trial." Her submission was dismissed by Justice Blair. The divorce made headlines in the media as a society scandal.

In 1940, Burleson was again on the front pages of American newspapers for the murder of Isabelle Burleson, the woman Richard Burleson married immediately after their divorce was granted. Jennie Burleson traveled by train from Texas to Columbia, South Carolina, sought out Mrs. Burleson at a restaurant she frequented, and shot her twice. The jury found her guilty of voluntary manslaughter by reason of insanity and she was sentenced to twelve years. In October 1948, she was released having served eight years in prison in South Carolina and she returned to the Walker family home.

Subject: Quick update regarding our license selection
Hi Alex,
I hope you are having a good week. I wanted to touch base on the licensing strategy for the new module we are developing. As we approach the code freeze, it is crucial that we finalize our legal stance to avoid any confusion later. I have reviewed our options and believe it is time to commit to a specific path forward.
Currently, the team has been splitting its attention between Apache 2.0 and MIT. Both are permissive licenses, but they carry subtly different implications for our corporate reputation. Choosing MIT signals a strong commitment to community transparency, which aligns well with our public relations goals. However, it lacks the explicit patent grant language that Apache 2.0 provides.
This patent clause is significant because it protects both us and our users from potential intellectual property claims. Given the recent trends in the industry, protecting our contributors from litigation risk is no longer optional. It is a standard expectation for enterprise clients who might integrate our tools into their own proprietary products. We need to feel secure that our contribution does not inadvertently create legal liabilities for them.
I recommend we proceed with Apache 2.0. It offers the same freedom to use and modify the code as MIT, but the added layer of legal protection is worth the minimal increase in boilerplate text. I have drafted the LICENSE file update and attached it here for your review. Please check the header comments in the source files to ensure they are consistent with the new choice.
Let me know if you have any objections by end of day tomorrow. If we agree, I will merge the changes into the main branch so everyone is working from the same policy. It is better to settle this now than to have a legal team reviewing the codebase months from now. Thanks for your help on this.
Best regards,
Jordan

Lithium-ion batteries in modern smartphones are designed to last for years, but proper maintenance significantly extends their functional lifespan. Unlike older battery technologies, these cells do not suffer from memory effects, meaning you do not need to deplete them to zero before recharging. However, consistent exposure to extreme states of charge or discharge accelerates chemical degradation within the cell structure.

The ideal operating range for a lithium-ion battery is between twenty and eighty percent charge. Keeping the battery within this "sweet spot" minimizes stress on the internal components. Frequent partial charges are perfectly acceptable and often recommended by major manufacturers to preserve long-term health.

Heat is the single greatest enemy of battery longevity. Avoid leaving your device in direct sunlight, hot vehicles, or under heavy blankets while charging. If the phone feels warm during regular use, consider removing the thick case to allow for better heat dissipation, as sustained high temperatures permanently reduce capacity.

Modern chargers stop feeding power once the battery reaches full capacity, so overnight charging is generally safe from the perspective of overcharging damage. Nevertheless, keeping the device at one hundred percent for extended periods puts the cells under mild voltage stress. Aim to start charging before the battery drops below twenty percent to prevent deep discharge cycles.

Finally, firmware updates often include battery optimization features that manage power delivery more efficiently. Keep your operating system current and monitor battery health settings in your device's system preferences. If capacity drops significantly below eighty percent after two years, professional replacement is a viable option to restore performance without immediate hardware upgrades.

renting an apartment

.

Finding the right apartment can feel like a puzzle in a bustling city where listings change daily. Start by defining your budget, preferred neighborhoods, and non-negotiable amenities, then use a mix of online portals and local contacts to broaden your options.

When you spot a potential place, schedule a visit quickly. Pay attention to natural light, noise levels, and the condition of fixtures; these details often reveal how well the landlord maintains the property.

Before signing, read the lease carefully. Look for clauses about rent increases, maintenance responsibilities, and subletting rules. If anything is unclear, ask for clarification or request a simple amendment to avoid disputes.

A thorough inspection checklist can save headaches later. Verify that smoke detectors work, water pressure is adequate, and appliances are in good order. Document any existing wear with photos and note it in writing to the landlord.

Consider the total cost beyond rent. Utilities, parking, pet fees, and renter's insurance add up quickly, so factor them into your monthly budget. Some landlords include certain utilities, simplifying billing and reducing surprise expenses.

Finally, build a good relationship with your landlord from day one. Prompt communication about repairs and respectful use of shared spaces often leads to a smoother tenancy and can be decisive when you decide to renew or move on.

Marlborough House, Brighton

Marlborough House is a mansion at 54, Old Steine, Brighton on the south coast of England. It is a Grade I listed building. Initially it was built for Samuel Shergold in the 1760s. It was sold to its second owner, 4th Duke of Marlborough, in 1786 it was bought by William G. Hamilton and altered to a neoclassical house by Robert Adam. After being owned by the Brighton School Board and Brighton and Hove City Council, it was sold to a local businessman in 1999. Since then, the building has stood empty and original features have been destroyed, leading to several courtcases. Marlborough House in Brighton is the second most important historic property after the Royal Pavilion.

A red-brick building was constructed on the site in the 1760s by local inn owner Sam Shergold. In 1786, the building was bought by statesman William Gerard Hamilton from the Duke of Marlborough. Subject: Tips for Establishing a Calm Baby Sleep Routine
Hi Emily,
I hope you're doing well and that both you and little Noah are settling into the season. I wanted to share a few ideas that have helped many families create a smoother bedtime experience for their babies.
Consistency is key. Try to start the bedtime sequence at the same hour each evening, even on weekends. A predictable pattern-bath, a short massage, a lullaby-signals to Noah that sleep is coming, and his internal clock will begin to anticipate the routine.
A dim, quiet environment also helps. Use blackout curtains or a soft night-light, and keep the room temperature around 68-70°F. White-noise machines can mask household sounds that might startle a sleeping infant.
Watch for sleepy cues such as rubbing eyes, yawning, or becoming less engaged with toys. When you notice these signs, begin the wind-down steps right away instead of waiting until he's overtired, which can lead to more resistance at bedtime.
If Noah wakes during the night, give him a brief pause before intervening. A few minutes of quiet reassurance-soft shushing or a gentle hand on his back-often helps him settle back to sleep without a full feeding cycle.
Feel free to let me know how these suggestions work for you, or if you have any specific concerns you'd like to discuss. I'm happy to brainstorm more personalized tweaks.
Best regards,
Samantha

It was developed to give Ontario post-secondary students an opportunity to participate in equestrian sports while continuing their education. The OCEA welcomes riders of all skill levels, offering hunter seat equitation classes from beginner to advanced riders. The OCEA is team-focused, but allows for personal growth and learning. It allows any post-secondary student to participate in horse shows regardless of the rider's beginning skill level, financial status, or past riding experience. Both men and women are eligible to compete. There are 18 participating universities. Two colleges, Cambrian College and Georgian College, joined for the 2016-2017 season. The league was modelled after the American IHSA.

Riders compete in Hunter Seat Equitation. There are 4 different levels of competition: Entry, Novice, Intermediate, and Open. All riders compete both on the flat and over fences. Unlike the majority of equestrian competitions, it is a "catch ride" where riders generally have not ridden their horse before entering the ring. Horses are donated by the show hosts and assigned randomly by a draw. Competitors watch as their horses are schooled by experienced volunteers and then mount their horse for competition. Each member school is responsible for hosting one horse show per year.

Currently, 17 universities and two colleges in Ontario as well as one Quebec university have participating teams. They are divided into three zones according to geographic proximity. East Zone:

Carleton University, Ottawa McGill University, Montreal Queen's University, Kingston Trent University, Peterborough University of Ottawa, Ottawa University of Ontario Institute of Technology, Oshawa Central Zone:

Georgian College, Barrie Lakehead University, Thunder Bay Laurentian University and Cambrian College, Sudbury Toronto Metropolitan University, Toronto York University, Toronto University of Guelph, Guelph University of Toronto, Toronto West Zone:

Riders in the Open division compete over a course of jumps set at 3', while Intermediate competes at 2'6", Novice 2'3" and Entry 18". Divisions are based upon ability and experience to allow riders compete against people of similar skill levels. Generally, the division qualifications are as follows: Open: winning three first place ribbons in an equitation over fences at a height of 3'3", or placing six times in an equitation, hunter over fences, or jumper class at a height of 3'6". Intermediate: winning three first place ribbons in an equitation over fences at a height of 2'9", or placing six times in an equitation, hunter over fences, or jumper class at a height of 3'. Novice: winning three first place ribbons in an equitation over fences at a height of 2'6", or placing six times in an equitation, hunter over fences, or jumper class at a height of 2'9". Entry: being part of a lesson program, where the rider has been jumping a height of 2' or higher for at least four months.

Riders are judged on their equitation, meaning that each rider is individually judged on his or her effectiveness as a rider, ability to look aesthically pleasing (i.e. posture and positioning on the horse), and ability to make riding a horse seem easy and effortless. Individual ribbons correspond to points, which combine for a team score. Teams receive points from their highest place rider in a given class. Paulerspury

Paulerspury is a civil parish and small village in West Northamptonshire, England. It is approximately 3 miles (5 km) south of Towcester and 8 miles (13 km) north of Milton Keynes along the A5 road (which follows the course of the Roman Road of Watling Street). The parish also contains the hamlets or villages of Pury End, Pury Hill and Heathencote. At the time of the 2001 census, its population was 991 people and the 2011 population was 1,018.

Originally called simply Pear-tree, the village owes its name to the de Pavelli family. It is referred to in the Domesday Book of 1086 as Paveli's Peri - a reference to orchards in the area and the lord of the manor Paveli. It was the birthplace in 1761 of William Carey, son of a weaver, who first established the Protestant mission in India. In the 1800s, the place was known as Pauler's Perry. Paulerspury has known significant historical events. Although the site of the final battle of Queen Boudicca is not confirmed, one of the three locations believed most likely is Cuttle Mill in Paulerspury. During Elizabethan times, the lords of the manor, the Throckmortons became prominent nobles, and local legend has it that the Queen and her favourite Sir Walter Raleigh stayed in the village (which led to the marriage of Bess Throckmorton to Sir Walter). The restored church has a Norman font and displays good Early English work. The effigies of Sir Arthur Throckmorton (1626) and his lady lie on a long tomb. There are also two rare wooden figures, representing Sir Laurence de Paveley (1329) and his wife. During the Industrial Revolution, little industry developed in the area, it mostly being an agricultural community, and the main produce other than agriculture was lace. It has been claimed that Queen Victoria favoured Paulespury lace. This led to an impoverished community as lacemaking was superseded by mass-produced textiles. This is in stark contrast to the village of today, which is a wealthy commuter village for Milton Keynes and London.

Paulerspury has a Church of England primary school, and the Barley Mow pub. It is the home of the Grafton Hunt and the headquarters of the Rolls-Royce Enthusiasts' Club.

Edward Bernard (1638-1697), English scholar, Savilian professor of astronomy at the University of Oxford from 1673 to 1691, was born in the village. Sir Benjamin Bathurst (c.1639 - 1704), British politician, Governor of the East India and Levant companies and a Cofferer of the Royal Household; former lord of the manor. William Carey (1761-1834), English missionary to India

Raorchestes johnceei

Raorchestes johnceei is a species of frog of the genus Raorchestes found in Bonacaud in the Western Ghats of Kerala, India. It has been observed between 900 and 1300 meters above sea level.

This frog has been observed perching on highland reed plants, including Ochlandra travancorica. This frog breeds in bamboo plants through direct development. Scientists classify this frog as endangered because of its small range. Humans harvest the reeds that the frog needs to survive for use as fence-building material and to deter elephants. The frog is often a bycatch of bamboo harvesting. Scientists also cite climate change as a threat because this species, like other high-elevation populations, cannot readily migrate to cooler habitats. Scientists have observed the fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis on other frogs in Raorchestes, so they believe it could infect R. jayarami too. Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis causes the fungal disease chytridiomycosis.

Zachariah A; Dinesh KP; Kunhikrishnan E; Das S; Raju DV; Radhakrishnan C; Palot MJ; Kalesh S (2011). "Nine new species of frogs of the genus Raorchestes (Amphibia: Anura: Rhacophoridae) from southern Western Ghats, India". Biosystematica (Excerpt). 5 (1): 25-48. Retrieved 7 September 2023.

2021 Explore the Pocono Mountains 350

The 2021 Explore the Pocono Mountains 350 was a NASCAR Cup Series race held on June 27, 2021, at Pocono Raceway in Long Pond, Pennsylvania. Contested over 140 laps on the 2.5-mile (4.0 km) triangular racecourse, it was the 19th race of the 2021 NASCAR Cup Series season.

Before the final stage break at lap 74's pit stop it was discovered that Kyle Busch got stuck in 4th gear. During the stage break pit stop his team discovered he had lost his clutch so he was forced to leave it in 4th gear for the remainder of the race. With one lap before the restart he topped off on fuel, gambling that there would be no further caution flags to the end, however there was one final caution on lap 94 for debris with the final restart on lap 96. This led to a 44 lap green flag run. Kyle Busch was able to get enough good fuel milage to win the race, passing the leader, teammate Denny Hamlin who was coming to pit lane for fuel as they were about to take the white flag. Stage Three Laps: 55

Lead changes: 12 among 10 different drivers Cautions/Laps: 4 for 15 Red flags: 0 Time of race: 2 hours, 26 minutes and 49 seconds Average speed: 143.036 miles per hour (230.194 km/h)

NBC Sports covered the race on the television side. Rick Allen, Jeff Burton, Steve Letarte and Dale Earnhardt Jr. called the race from the broadcast booth. Dave Burns, Marty Snider and Kelli Stavast handled the pit road duties from pit lane. Jac Collinsworth handled the features from the track.

MRN had the radio call for the race which was also simulcast on Sirius XM NASCAR Radio. Alex Hayden and Jeff Striegle called the race in the booth when the field raced through the tri-oval. Dave Moody called the race from the Sunoco spotters stand outside turn 2 when the field raced through turns 1 and 2. Mike Bagley called the race from a platform inside the backstretch when the field raced down the backstretch. Kyle Rickey called the race from the Sunoco spotters stand outside turn 4 when the field raced through turns 3 and 4. Steve Post and Kim Coon worked pit road for the radio side.

Peaches!

Peaches! is the fourteenth studio album by the American rock duo the Black Keys, released on May 1, 2026, by Easy Eye Sound and Warner Records. It is a covers album. Pitchfork stated it was "billed as the Black Keys at their 'most natural' since their 2002 debut, The Big Come Up".

Peaches! was released on May 1, 2026. The first single from the album, "You Got to Lose", originally recorded by George Thorogood and the Destroyers, was released on February 6. The album cover was created by Michael Carney, brother of drummer Patrick. Michael had previously designed the first ten album covers for the band, including winning the 2011 Grammy Award for Best Recording Package for his work on their album Brothers. The photo on the cover was taken by William Eggleston; Eggleston's photography was also used by Carney on Delta Kream, the last album he worked on for the band before Peaches!, which was also a covers album.

The album has 3.5/5 stars on AllMusic, and a Metacritic score of 74 indicating "generally favorable reviews." Clash rated the album 8/10, stating; "'Peaches!' is full of dynamism, swirling riffs and pounding drumbeats. It never loses itself in the melee. With their fourteenth record the band have gone full circle, proving why they became household names in the first place." A 4/5 star review for Classic Rock stated "By returning to their sonic roots, The Black Keys sound revitalised, urgent and gloriously unrefined once again. Whether they pursue this righteous path remains to be seen, but this is exactly what's needed from them now." Pitchfork gave the album a score of 6.0/10.0, stating disappointment, "I feel a little sad for these fellas, now nearing 50 but sporting a less clear picture of what the Black Keys actually are than they had at 30. They feel one misstep away from the state-fair circuit." Paste gave the album a C- score, stating "Rather than demonstrating the duo in their natural state, à la early records like The Big Come Up and Thickfreakness, Peaches! feels like the sonic equivalent of pre-distressed denim: it looks worn-in, but that's because it was manufactured that way."

Dan Auerbach - lead vocals, guitar, production, mixing (all tracks); organ (track 3) Patrick Carney - drums, production, mixing (all tracks); shaker (3, 4, 7)

Ouyang Yi

Ouyang Yi (born 28 June 1968) is a former high-school teacher, one of the managers of a pro-democracy web site, and a member of the China Democracy Party.

Ouyang was born in Suining, Sichuan Province. He graduated from Chuanbei College of Education (川北教育学院), Sichuan Province, and was a middle school teacher in Chengdu, Sichuan. He was a pro-democracy activist since the late 1980s. He was one of the managers of the web site, www.5633.com, set up in July 2002, and a member of the China Democracy Party, an organization banned by in the People's Republic of China.

Ouyang was reportedly taken into custody on 4 December 2002, for the fifth time in six years, by members of the security police who searched his home and confiscated a number of documents. He was held at the Chengdu detention centre, Sichuan Province. On 7 January 2003, Ouyang was formally charged by the Public Security Bureau with "inciting the overthrow of the State power" under article 105 of the Chinese Criminal code as amended in March 1997. An intermediate people's court in Chengdu in the south-west sentenced him on 16 March 2004 to two years in prison.

Włodzimierz Szpak

Włodzimierz Szpak was born in Milanówek, Poland. He graduated from University of Warsaw in 1975. Then he continued his studies at the National Film School (in Łódź, Poland). He is a member of Polish Filmmakers Association.

He was active in an area of documentary film-making. There are 28 films of that kind in his creative production. Nevertheless, he started his career with the psychological story entitled "Ona" ("She") in the narrative film "On, ona, oni" ("He, She, They"). He had also directed the two theater plays: 1) "Rekonstrukcja poety" ("The Reconstruction of the Poet") which refers to the antiquity thread in Zbigniew Herbert's literary output, and 2) "Noce narodowe" ("Nights of the Nation") by Roman Brandstaetter. His films, e.g. "Ludzie z ziemi czerwonej" ("People of Red Land"), "Krajobraz z gęsią" ("Landscape with Goose"), "Boże, zbaw Rosję" ("God Save Russia") had been discussed and commented by domestic and foreign mass media. He was awarded at some international film festivals. In 1986 he won a "Silver Dancer" prize at the Huesca International Film Festival for a documentary film ''Ludzie z ziemi czerwonej'' ("People of Red Land"). Then in 1989 he won a "Special Reward", at the International Włodzimierz Puchalski Film Festival in Łódź - for "Krajobraz z gęsią" ("Landscape with Goose"). He took part in the TV programme in series "Mistrzowie dokumentu" ("Document Masters") as well, which was transmitted by "Kino Polska" TV channel.

Sources: 1) Polish Filmmakers Association, see internet site: https://www.sfp.org.pl/osoba,0,1,58347,Wlodzimierz-Szpak.html [Acc.: 20 December 2020] and 2) "Filmweb" - see internet site: https://www.filmweb.pl/person/W%C5%82odzimierz+Szpak-105916 [Acc.: 20. 12. 2020]

mountain weather

Mountain weather is famously fickle, shifting from bright sunshine to bone-cold gusts within minutes. Hikers and climbers quickly learn that a clear sky at the trailhead does not guarantee the same conditions at 10,000 feet, where the atmosphere thins and temperatures drop sharply.

The most reliable rule is the lapse rate: for every 1,000 feet of elevation, the air cools roughly 3.5 °F (about 2 °C). This means a warm afternoon at the base can feel like early winter near the summit, and the resulting temperature gradient often fuels cloud formation and precipitation higher up.

Rapid weather changes are a hallmark of mountain zones. A sudden rise in barometric pressure can signal an incoming front, bringing thunderheads that develop quickly and dump heavy rain or snow on exposed ridges. Wind speeds also increase dramatically with altitude, and gusts can become dangerous for anyone caught on an exposed ledge.

Safety advice emphasizes constant vigilance. Carry a lightweight, waterproof layer, and check the forecast from a reliable mountain-specific service before you set out. Keep an eye on the sky for darkening clouds, a drop in temperature, or a rise in wind that outpaces your pace.

Modern gear helps mitigate the risks. Breathable insulated jackets, wind-proof shells, and layered clothing systems let you adjust quickly as conditions shift. A compact emergency shelter and a reliable GPS device are essential for unplanned overnight stays.

Understanding mountain weather is less about predicting exact outcomes and more about respecting the environment's volatility. By staying informed, dressing appropriately, and moving with the rhythm of the peaks, you can enjoy the alpine experience while staying safe.

The purpose of this street-food guide is to provide both visitors and residents with reliable, concise information that supports safe, enjoyable, and culturally respectful experiences when sampling the diverse offerings that line our city's thoroughfares. All vendors featured have been reviewed by the Department of Public Health and the Cultural Affairs Office, confirming compliance with sanitation standards and authenticity of preparation methods. By highlighting key locations, typical dishes, and practical tips, the guide aims to reduce uncertainty for newcomers while reinforcing the city's commitment to supporting local entrepreneurs and preserving culinary heritage.

When selecting a vendor, patrons should first observe the cleanliness of the preparation area, the condition of equipment, and the presence of a visible food-handling permit. Vendors who consistently cover food, keep raw and cooked items separate, and store perishable goods at appropriate temperatures are deemed low-risk. Consumers are encouraged to ask vendors about ingredient sourcing, especially for common allergens such as nuts, dairy, and seafood. Simple questions about spice levels and cooking methods help ensure that the experience matches personal taste preferences and dietary needs.

The guide identifies three primary clusters of street-food activity: the historic market district, the waterfront promenade, and the emerging arts corridor. In the historic market district, classic dishes such as grilled corn, tamales, and spiced meat skewers dominate, often served alongside locally brewed beverages. The waterfront promenade showcases a blend of seafood specialties, including grilled fish tacos, oyster shooters, and seaweed-infused rice bowls, reflecting the proximity to the harbor. Along the arts corridor, innovative fusion concepts flourish, with vendors experimenting with plant-based proteins, unconventional flavor pairings, and interactive cooking displays that invite diners to customize their meals on the spot.

To promote responsible consumption, the guide advises diners to limit intake of high-sodium and deep-fried items, balancing street-food meals with fresh fruit, vegetables, and hydration. Portion sizes in street-food settings can be generous; sharing dishes with companions not only enhances the communal atmosphere but also encourages a varied tasting experience while moderating calorie intake. Visitors are reminded to carry hand sanitizer, use provided waste receptacles, and respect local waste-separation protocols to maintain the cleanliness of public spaces.

Finally, the guide serves as an invitation to explore the city's dynamic street-food scene while supporting the small-business ecosystem that sustains it. Feedback from the public is welcomed; users may submit observations, suggestions, or concerns through the municipal website or the dedicated hotline. Periodic updates will incorporate new vendors, seasonal specialties, and any regulatory changes that affect operations. By adhering to the recommendations outlined herein, diners can enjoy flavorful, safe, and authentic street-food experiences that celebrate the city's rich culinary tapestry.

Freya Fires Up

Freya Fires Up was an Australian television current affairs and commentary program, shown on Sky News Australia and hosted by conservative political commentator Freya Leach. The program, which was broadcast on Sunday nights, began in August 2025 and was cancelled six weeks later in September 2025.

Freya Leach, a conservative political commentator and former Liberal Party candidate, joined Sky News Australia in 2025 as a co-host of The Late Debate. On 6 August 2025, she was announced as the host of her own program, Freya Fires Up, which debuted two weeks later on 17 August 2025. One of the program's inaugural guests was socialist activist Jordan van den Lamb.

On 21 September 2025, Leach hosted a panel on the program with Scottish Asian social media personality Ryan Williams (also known online as thescottishkorean) and American political strategist Joey Mannarino. After being asked by Leach about his reaction to the assassination of Charlie Kirk, Williams made multiple anti-Islam remarks while wearing raw rashers of bacon across his chest. Leach responded by saying there were "great moderate Muslims" in Australia, and briefly apologised for Williams' comments moments later, before continuing the remainder of the interview with Mannarino alone. The comments were not republished by Sky News, but Williams posted the segment on his own social media accounts. The following day, Sky News initiated a review into the program, describing Williams' comments as "wholly inappropriate and unacceptable". A full apology was also issued by Leach in a pre-recorded statement during The Late Debate later in the evening. Following the review, Sky News chose to pre-record future episodes of Freya Fires Up instead of continuing to broadcast the program live. Ben Espiner, the program's producer, was sacked on 25 September 2025. Although Freya Fires Up was expected to continue, the program did not air on 28 September 2025 and was replaced with a rerun of Sunday Agenda. The following day, Sky News confirmed the program had been cancelled after six episodes, and Leach continued at the channel as a co-host of The Late Debate before leaving the show in January 2026.

university admissions

Navigating the landscape of university admissions can feel like walking through a dense fog, where visibility is limited and the path forward seems obscured by contradictory advice. For most students, this pivotal season brings a mix of excitement and anxiety, as their hard work over four years is distilled into a single application. The process is no longer just about submitting grades and test scores; it is a holistic evaluation that looks at the entire person standing at the threshold of higher education. Understanding this shift from quantitative metrics to qualitative assessment is the first step in crafting a successful strategy.

The central focus of any application must be the personal essay, which serves as the bridge between the applicant and the admissions officer. This narrative space requires authenticity, inviting readers to see the student's motivation, resilience, and unique perspective. Avoiding generic clichés in favor of specific anecdotes allows the applicant to stand out in a pool of thousands. A compelling story does not necessarily require a grand tragedy or a Nobel Prize; instead, it often finds power in small, reflective moments that demonstrate character growth and intellectual curiosity.

Beyond the narrative, the selection of extracurricular activities should reflect depth rather than breadth. Admissions committees are not interested in a student who is involved in fifteen clubs superficially but rather one who has made a tangible impact in one or two areas. Subject: Your Moving Checklist - Everything You Need to Stay Organized
Hi Jordan,
I know the weeks before a move can feel chaotic, so I've compiled a concise checklist to keep you on track from the moment you decide to relocate until you're comfortably settled. Keep this email handy, print it out, or save it on your phone-whichever works best for quick reference. A simple daily glance can help you tick off tasks and reduce stress.
Start with the paperwork and notifications that often slip through the cracks. Notify your landlord or mortgage lender of your move-out date and arrange any final inspections. Submit a change-of-address request with the post office, and write down all utilities-electric, gas, water, internet, cable-so you can schedule termination at the old address and activation at the new one. Update your address with banks, insurers, and any subscription services you use regularly.
When you begin packing, start early and sort items by category. Designate a box for "essentials" that will travel with you and be opened the first night (toiletries, a couple of outfits, chargers, and basic kitchenware). Label each box on two sides with the room it belongs to, and keep a brief inventory in a notebook or spreadsheet. Wrap fragile items in newspaper or bubble wrap and use smaller boxes to avoid over-weight loads. If furniture

Hovawart

The Hovawart is a medium to large size German dog breed. The name means "yard-watcher" or "farm-watcher", from the Middle High German words hova ("court", "yard", "farm", modern Standard German: Hof) and wart ("watchman", modern Standard German: Wart).

The Hovawart is a muscular, medium sized, long-haired working breed. The breed is slightly long with length being between 110-115% of the height at withers.

The bridge of the nose is straight. Muzzle is roughly the same length as the skull and the skin is tight. Facial pigmentation is black. Eyes are oval shaped with a dark-to-medium brown colour. Ears are triangular shaped and drop down. They should reach down far enough to be in line with the mouth.

Home | About | Contact

The long-haired coat lies close to the body with only a slight amount of undercoat. Coat is longer on the chest, belly, and rare of legs. There are three different colours: black, black and gold, and blonde.

Hovawarts are protective dogs who can make good family pets when trained due to their guarding instincts and desire to be part of a pack.

Following the medieval period, the popularity of the Hovawart began to decline. Newer breeds such as the German Shepherd Dog slowly replaced the Hovawart as a guard and working dog until it had almost disappeared by the beginning of the twentieth century. Around 1915 a group of enthusiasts decided to try to save the breed. Predominant in this group was the zoologist Kurt Friedrich König. They started by looking for dogs in the farms of the Black Forest region. König then started a careful breeding program using these dogs and crossed them with Kuvasz specimens, Newfoundlands, German Shepherd Dogs, Leonbergers, a Bernese Mountain Dog and an African hunting dog. After much work, the group was rewarded in 1922 when the first Hovawart litter was entered into the German Breeding Registry. The enthusiasts continued their work and in 1937 the German Kennel Club officially recognised the Hovawart. All this work was almost undone with the outbreak of the Second World War. Because of their abilities many Hovawarts were used in the German war effort and perished. By 1945 only a few remained. Enthusiasm for the breed remained and in 1947, Otto Schramm and some fellow enthusiasts in Coburg formed a new club, the Rassezuchtverein für Hovawart-Hunde Coburg which is still in existence today. In 1964 the German Kennel Club recognised the Hovawart as the country's seventh working breed.

Torque (DC Comics)

Torque (Dudley Soames) is a supervillain appearing in American comic books published by DC Comics, and an enemy of Nightwing. Created by writer Chuck Dixon and artist Scott McDaniel, he first appeared in Nightwing (vol. 2) #1 (October 1996).

Dudley Soames is a police inspector working in the Blüdhaven Police Department, which is rife with corruption. He first encounters Nightwing when police chief Delmore Redhorn hires him to kill Nightwing. Soames betrays Redhorn and allowed Nightwing to live, with the intention to pit various factions in Blüdhaven against one another. He plays both sides of the legal fence: he feeds information on Blockbuster's criminal dealings to Nightwing and serves Blockbuster as a mob lieutenant. After Soames' scheme to use Scarecrow against Nightwing fails disastrously, Blockbuster grows weary of him and attempts to have him killed. Blockbuster twists Soames' head 180 degrees, leaving him for dead. Soames survives due to his trachea remaining unharmed for a sufficient duration, allowing him to be placed on life support. His neck is surgically repaired, which restores his mobility, but leaves his head permanently inverted. Soames spends some time retraining himself to move normally, seeing behind him using glasses with a built-in array of mirrors. Soames kills the doctor who saved his life, takes the moniker "Torque", and starts a gang war for the control of Blüdhaven, seeking to get revenge against Blockbuster. Torque is brought to justice by Nightwing, only to arrange a prison break with the help of the psychopathic vigilante Nite-Wing, who seeks to settle his own vendetta against Nightwing. Nite-Wing has a zero-tolerance policy for crime; upon realizing Soames' true nature, the two enter a Mexican standoff that only Nite-Wing survives.

Torque appears in the Arrow episode "Unthinkable", portrayed by Michael Adamthwaite. This version is a member of the Suicide Squad. Torque appears as a character summon in Scribblenauts Unmasked: A DC Comics Adventure.
