water quality report

A water quality report, often called a Consumer Confidence Report, is an annual statement that municipal water suppliers must provide to their customers. It details where the water comes from, how it is treated, and what contaminants were detected during the past year. The report is designed to give residents a clear picture of the safety and taste of the tap water that flows into their homes, and it is typically mailed out in the fall or made available online for download.

The core of any water quality report is the list of contaminants that were tested for, along with their measured concentrations. These numbers are compared against the limits set by the Environmental Protection Agency, which are based on extensive health research. When a contaminant falls below the regulatory threshold, the report will note it as "below detection" or "within safe limits." If a substance exceeds the allowable level, the supplier must explain the source of the problem and outline steps being taken to address it.

Reading the report can seem intimidating, but most of the information is presented in straightforward tables and short explanations. Look first for the source of the water-whether it comes from a protected reservoir, a river, or groundwater-since the source often influences the types of contaminants that may be present. Next, check the summary of major water quality parameters such as pH, chlorine, and hardness, which affect taste and the performance of appliances. Finally, review the section on lead and copper, especially if your home has older plumbing, as these metals can leach into the water over time.

Recent water quality reports across the country have shown a steady decline in bacterial contamination, thanks to improved filtration and regular monitoring. However, some regions continue to grapple with elevated levels of nitrates and PFAS chemicals, which have drawn attention from both regulators and the public. In response, many utilities are investing in advanced treatment technologies like activated carbon filters and reverse-osmosis systems to reduce these emerging contaminants.

If you receive a water quality report that raises concerns, you have several options. You can request a more detailed copy from your water provider, have your home's water tested independently, or install a certified point-of-use filtration system. Staying informed and taking proactive steps ensures that the water you and your family drink remains safe, clean, and pleasant.

Subject: Scheduled Maintenance Power Outage Notice for Residents
Dear Valued Resident,
We are writing to inform you that a scheduled maintenance outage will occur on Friday, October 14th. To ensure the long-term reliability and safety of our grid infrastructure, our engineering team must perform critical upgrades on the transformers serving your building. This proactive measure is essential to prevent potential future disruptions and improve overall energy efficiency for all occupants. Please note that this work cannot be conducted while the site remains active.
The outage is expected to begin at 9:00 AM and will last approximately three hours. During this window, you should not expect electricity to be available for lighting, appliances, or elevators. We anticipate having power fully restored by 12:00 PM, although minor delays may occur due to unforeseen technical issues. We recommend having a backup power source for medical devices if applicable.
To prepare, please charge your mobile devices and laptops before the start time. If you rely on refrigerated medications, consider storing them in a cooler with ice packs. Additionally, it is wise to have flashlights and extra batteries on hand, especially if you need to move around the property after the lights go out. Avoid opening your refrigerator unless necessary to keep the interior cold.
We apologize for any inconvenience this temporary interruption may cause your daily routine. Our staff will be on-site throughout the period to monitor progress and address any immediate concerns. If you have urgent questions or require special assistance due to a disability, please contact our support line directly before noon on Thursday so we can arrange necessary accommodations.
Thank you for your patience and cooperation as we work to maintain a safe and efficient living environment for everyone. We appreciate your understanding as we prioritize the integrity of our shared facilities. We look forward to greeting you again once the systems are back online and fully tested.
Sincerely,
The Property Management Team

Shana Hiatt

A former Army brat raised primarily in Tabernacle Township, New Jersey, Hiatt is best known for hosting the first three seasons of World Poker Tour on The Travel Channel. She was married to pornographic actor Tommy Gunn for three years in the 1990s.

While Hiatt was a non-player prior to her job with the World Poker Tour, she is now an avid online poker player who occasionally plays in casinos. She was the host of Poker After Dark and the National Heads-Up Poker Championship, both on NBC. Hiatt left the shows in 2008 due to pregnancy. She was replaced by Marianela Pereyra in Poker After Dark and by Leeann Tweeden in the National Heads-Up Poker Championship. After leaving the World Poker Tour in 2005, Hiatt sued the producers in order to get a restraining order to prevent them from keeping her from working on a rival poker show on NBC, Poker After Dark. The WPT argued a non-compete clause was part of her contract, but Hiatt countered that she never signed it. The suit additionally revealed Hiatt left the WPT over a "hostile working environment" involving her husband, movie producer Todd Garner, whom she married in October 2005. Hiatt was formerly married to James Van Patten, brother of World Poker Tour co-host Vince Van Patten.

Hiatt was Miss Hawaiian Tropic USA in 1995 and had represented Beach Haven, New Jersey, after winning the local Hawaiian Tropic pageant at Touché nightclub in 1994. After becoming Miss Hawaiian Tropic USA, Hiatt was the cover model and posed nude inside the pages of Playboy in their April 1995 The Girls of Hawaiian Tropic issue. She also was on the cover for the video of that photo shoot Playboy: The Girls of Hawaiian Tropic, Naked in Paradise . Hiatt was a guest host of Wild On! featured on the E! network. She has also appeared in television shows and movies including Must Love Dogs and Grandma's Boy.

research grant timeline

Home | About | Contact

The journey from a nascent idea to a fully funded research project is often misunderstood as a straightforward linear path. In reality, it is a complex logistical marathon that requires meticulous planning and patience. Most major granting bodies, whether government agencies like the National Science Foundation or private foundations, operate on rigid fiscal year cycles. Understanding these specific timelines is not just a matter of convenience; it is the single most critical determinant of whether an application will be considered for that fiscal year. Missing a deadline by even a single business day can mean waiting an entire year for the next opportunity, which significantly delays the start of critical laboratory work and student recruitment.

The process typically begins months before the actual submission date. Researchers must secure all necessary pre-application approvals, including ethics board review for human or animal subjects and administrative sign-off from their institution's sponsored programs office. This phase is deceptively slow because it involves internal back-and-forth that consumes significant time. Many principal investigators make the mistake of waiting until the last week to gather institutional letters of support or budget justifications. This late-stage approach creates a bottleneck where minor administrative errors can jeopardize the entire proposal, leading to automatic rejection without peer review.

Once the document is finalized, the submission system becomes a source of both stress and relief. Most organizations now use digital portals that impose strict character limits and formatting rules. A common pitfall in this stage is the failure to test uploads well in advance of the deadline. Internet connectivity issues or portal crashes in the final hours are more common than one would expect. Consequently, savvy researchers aim to submit at least 24 to 48 hours early. This buffer allows time for technical troubleshooting and ensures that the application is fully processed and verified by the sponsor before the cutoff.

After submission, the clock shifts to the review cycle, which generally spans three to six months. This period is silent and frustrating for applicants, but it is intensely active for the reviewers. National panels of experts read hundreds of pages, debating merit, feasibility, and impact. Do not assume silence means rejection; the process is thorough and often requires multiple rounds of scoring. During this time, applicants should prepare for the possibility of follow-up inquiries. Having a concise summary of your methodology and budget ready allows you to respond promptly if the program officer requests clarification.

Finally, the notification letter arrives, bringing either immediate celebration or the need for strategic pivoting. If funded, the work begins immediately with onboarding and equipment procurement. If not funded, the decision letter often provides detailed comments that are invaluable for strengthening the next attempt. Many successful grants are actually the second or third version of a proposal. The successful researcher treats the timeline not as a date on a calendar, but as a project management exercise, building in buffer zones for every step to ensure that the science itself is never the reason for failure.

Subject: Practical advice for your upcoming technical interview
Hi Sarah,
I saw you are preparing for the senior developer role at NexTech next week. Since I went through a similar process last year, I wanted to share a few insights that genuinely helped me stand out. The technical aspect is certainly the core of the evaluation, but the way you communicate your problem-solving strategy often carries just as much weight. Interviewers rarely look for a single perfect line of code. Instead, they are observing how you break down complex problems, how you handle ambiguity, and how you articulate your thought process in real time. When you are stuck, do not freeze or guess randomly. It is far better to explicitly state your current hypothesis, explain why you are taking a specific step, and ask for clarification if the requirements seem vague. This transparency demonstrates confidence and professional maturity, which are traits highly valued in collaborative teams.
Another critical area to focus on is your preparation regarding the company itself. Generic answers about being a hard worker or a team player are viewed with skepticism because every candidate claims these qualities. Instead, research the company's recent engineering blog posts, their open-source contributions, or recent press releases about their product roadmap. During the behavioral questions, try to tie your past achievements directly to their specific challenges. For example, if they are scaling their infrastructure, share a specific story where you optimized a system for high traffic. Show them that you have already mentally placed yourself in their shoes and are excited about the specific technical hurdles they are facing.
Please also remember that an interview is a two-way street, not an interrogation. You are evaluating them just as much as they are evaluating you. Prepare insightful questions that go beyond the standard job description queries. Ask about the team's deployment frequency, their code review culture, or the biggest technical debt they are currently tackling. Asking about the trade-offs they made in their current architecture shows that you are thinking like an engineer, not just a job seeker. Their answers will give you invaluable insight into the day-to-day working conditions and the technical maturity of the organization. This reciprocal exchange helps you determine if their environment aligns with your career goals and work style preferences.
Finally, manage your body language and energy levels throughout the conversation. If this is a remote interview, ensure your background is neutral and well-lit, and look directly into the camera when speaking, not at the screen. Pausing briefly before answering difficult questions is perfectly acceptable and often preferred, as it signals that you are thinking critically rather than reciting memorized scripts. Keep your energy steady and conversational. Avoid sounding overly rehearsed or robotic. Authenticity connects with people in ways that perfection does not. Let your genuine curiosity about the technology and the team shine through your interactions.
Trust your preparation. You have likely performed this technical dance many times before. Focus on being a collaborative partner during the conversation rather than just a candidate trying to pass a test. Good luck with the final touches on your portfolio and system design examples.
Best regards,
Alex

Effective immediately, all customer-facing team members must adhere to the revised Service Level Agreement standards outlined below. These updates reflect our commitment to enhancing user satisfaction while maintaining operational efficiency. The primary goal is to resolve common inquiries within a single interaction, ensuring that customers feel heard and supported without unnecessary delays. We recognize that timely communication is the cornerstone of trust, and these new guidelines are designed to standardize our response times across all digital and phone channels.

For email and live chat inquiries, the initial response time must not exceed two hours during business hours. If the issue requires further investigation or technical troubleshooting, agents must send a status update within twenty-four hours. This interim communication should clearly outline the next steps and estimated resolution timelines. Silence is no longer an acceptable state for pending tickets. Every customer must know where their request stands in the processing queue, thereby reducing anxiety and preventing duplicate submissions due to perceived inaction.

When handling escalated issues, such as billing disputes or service outages, senior support specialists must take ownership within one business day. These cases require a dedicated point of contact who will guide the customer through the resolution process. Agents are instructed to log all interactions in the central ticketing system with precise tags that identify the root cause and category. This data will be reviewed weekly by management to identify recurring problems and preemptively address systemic issues before they impact a larger segment of our user base.

Tone and empathy remain critical components of our interaction strategy. Agents should avoid using jargon that may confuse non-technical users and instead employ clear, concise language that confirms understanding of the customer's frustration. We encourage active listening, which involves paraphrasing the customer's concern to ensure alignment before proposing a solution. In cases where a full refund cannot be granted, agents must offer appropriate alternatives or partial compensation as defined by our compensation matrix. This flexibility allows us to retain customer loyalty even when the outcome is not entirely in the user's favor.

Compliance with these policies will be monitored through monthly quality assurance audits. A random sample of ten tickets per agent will be reviewed for adherence to response times, tone, and resolution accuracy. Findings will be discussed in one-on-one coaching sessions, focusing on constructive feedback rather than punishment. Agents who consistently exceed performance targets will be recognized during all-hands meetings. We believe that a well-supported team delivers superior customer experiences, and these shared standards help us compete effectively in a crowded market. Please direct any questions regarding these policies to the Head of Customer Success for clarification prior to your next shift.

For email and live chat inquiries, the initial response time must not exceed two hours during business hours. If the issue requires further investigation or technical troubleshooting, agents must send a status update within twenty-four hours. This interim communication should clearly outline the next steps and estimated resolution timelines. Silence is no longer an acceptable state for pending tickets. Every customer must know where their request stands in the processing queue, thereby reducing anxiety and preventing duplicate submissions due to perceived inaction.

When handling escalated issues, such as billing disputes or service outages, senior support specialists must take ownership within one business day. These cases require a dedicated point of contact who will guide the customer through the resolution process. Agents are instructed to log all interactions in the central ticketing system with precise tags that identify the root cause and category. This data will be reviewed weekly by management to identify recurring problems and preemptively address systemic issues before they impact a larger segment of our user base.

Tone and empathy remain critical components of our interaction strategy. Agents should avoid using jargon that may confuse non-technical users and instead employ clear, concise language that confirms understanding of the customer's frustration. We encourage active listening, which involves paraphrasing the customer's concern to ensure alignment before proposing a solution. In cases where a full refund cannot be granted, agents must offer appropriate alternatives or partial compensation as defined by our compensation matrix. This flexibility allows us to retain customer loyalty even when the outcome is not entirely in the user's favor.

Compliance with these policies will be monitored through monthly quality assurance audits. A random sample of ten tickets per agent will be reviewed for adherence to response times, tone, and resolution accuracy. Findings will be discussed in one-on-one coaching sessions, focusing on constructive feedback rather than punishment. Agents who consistently exceed performance targets will be recognized during all-hands meetings. We believe that a well-supported team delivers superior customer experiences, and these shared standards help us compete effectively in a crowded market. Please direct any questions regarding these policies to the Head of Customer Success for clarification prior to your next shift.

Heathcote Botanical Gardens

Heathcote Botanical Gardens is a five-acre subtropical botanical garden located at 210 Savannah Road, Fort Pierce, Florida, United States. Heathcote is a non-profit, 501 (C)3 educational foundation that bills itself as the "Green Heart of the Treasure Coast." It began in 1960 as the commercial nursery of landscape architect Molly Crimmons and her husband, Jim. Heathcote Botanical Gardens was established in 1986 when the site was purchased by local citizens with contributions from the City of Fort Pierce, St. Lucie County, the State of Florida and Friends of Heathathcote Botanical Gardens.

It currently includes a Japanese garden with teahouse, Reflection Garden, Herb Garden, Rainforest Display, Native Plants Garden, Children's Garden, and a Palm and Cycad Walk. Other garden plants include: bamboo, a banyan tree, bromeliads, Clerodendrums, Clusia rosea, Coccoloba uvifera, Codiaeum sp., crotons, Encephalartos gratus, orchids, Pandanus utilis, Petrea volubilis, philodendrons, pineapple, Podocarpus gracilior, Tillandsias, and Zamia pumila. The Garden of Lights is a major fundraiser that sees the entire garden decorated with tens of thousands of tiny Christmas lights. It draws more than 10,000 people each year during weekend evenings leading up to Christmas. The Adams/Peterson Pioneer house is a replica of an 1870 "Cracker"-style home that shows what it was like to live in Old Florida.

Heathcote is most well known for being the home of the James J. Smith Bonsai Collection, the largest public display of bonsai in the country. The collection has more bonsai on year-round display than any other public exhibit in the United States. Although there are 26 species represented in the collection, almost half the trees are species of ficus. The more than 100 specimen bonsai range from a huge buttonwood, estimated to be 200 years old, to a twin-trunk Jaboticaba, originally styled by John Naka in 1973. James J. Smith was an internationally recognized authority on bonsai who operated a wholesale bonsai nursery in Vero Beach, Florida. He learned from some of the most famous bonsai masters in the world including John Naka and Toshio Saburomaru. For decades, Smith conducted a free monthly workshop at his Durastone Nursery on Old Dixie Highway. He was mentor to several generations of Florida bonsai artists. His bonsai are in numerous important collections around the world, and numerous books picture his trees and discuss his work. When he was in his 80s, he agreed to give most of his private collection to Heathcote if it could develop a suitable display area. Heathcote conducted a major fundraising campaign and developed a plan for a 10,000-square-foot garden complete with stone stands and a Japanese-influenced pavilion that is a favorite scene for weddings and garden parties. Smith died in 2016.

craft fair

The buzz of a craft fair is hard to miss: the scent of fresh pine, the soft clink of ceramic mugs, and the rhythmic chatter of artisans and shoppers weaving together a community tapestry. Originating in medieval market towns where craftsmen displayed their wares, modern craft fairs have evolved into curated experiences that celebrate handmade creativity. Whether set in a historic barn, a bustling downtown plaza, or a pop-up tent on a city street, each fair offers a glimpse into the lives of the makers who pour skill and heart into every piece they present.

At the heart of any successful craft fair is the diversity of its vendors. You'll find everything from hand-spun yarn and hand-loomed textiles to bespoke jewelry, reclaimed-wood furniture, and artisanal candles scented with essential oils. Many creators use the event as a testing ground for new designs, so visitors often encounter limited-edition items that won't appear online or in stores again. The personal connections formed when a buyer learns the story behind a piece-how a necklace was inspired by a family heirloom or how a pottery bowl was shaped on a wheel in the early hours of dawn-add value far beyond the price tag.

For vendors, preparation is key. A well-designed booth that reflects the aesthetic of the products can draw in curious passersby, while clear pricing tags and easy payment options, including contactless methods, keep the transaction flow smooth. Many sellers bring portable displays, such as tiered racks or vintage crates, to showcase items at eye level, allowing shoppers to appreciate the texture and detail up close. Lighting, especially soft, warm bulbs, can highlight the subtle hues of a hand-dyed scarf or the intricate filigree of a silver ring, making the booth feel inviting rather than cluttered.

Visitors can make the most of a craft fair by arriving early to avoid crowds and to catch vendors before the best pieces are snapped up. Wearing comfortable shoes and bringing a reusable bag helps navigate the often-sprawling layout while staying environmentally conscious. It's also wise to set a modest budget and prioritize the items that truly speak to you, as the sheer variety can be overwhelming. Engaging with the makers-asking about their techniques, materials, or the inspiration behind their collections-often leads to surprising discoveries and, sometimes, a chance to commission a custom piece.

Beyond the shopping experience, craft fairs serve as vibrant community gatherings that support local economies and preserve traditional crafts. Many events partner with schools, non-profits, or sustainability initiatives, donating a portion of proceeds to charitable causes or offering workshops that teach skills like knitting, metalworking, or paper-flower arranging. craft fair
The buzz of a craft fair is hard to miss: the scent of fresh pine, the soft clink of ceramic mugs, and the rhythmic chatter of artisans and shoppers weaving together a community tapestry. Originating in medieval market towns where craftsmen displayed their wares, modern craft fairs have evolved into curated experiences that celebrate handmade creativity. Whether set in a historic barn, a bustling downtown plaza, or a pop-up tent on a city street, each fair offers a glimpse into the lives of the makers who pour skill and heart into every piece they present.
At the heart of any successful craft fair is the diversity of its vendors. You'll find everything from hand-spun yarn and hand-loomed textiles to bespoke jewelry, reclaimed-wood furniture, and artisanal candles scented with essential oils. Many creators use the event as a testing ground for new designs, so visitors often encounter limited-edition items that won't appear online or in stores again. The personal connections formed when a buyer learns the story behind a piece-how a necklace was inspired by a family heirloom or how a pottery bowl was shaped on a wheel in the early hours of dawn-add value far beyond the price tag.
For vendors, preparation is key. A well-designed booth that reflects the aesthetic of the products can draw in curious passersby, while clear pricing tags and easy payment options, including contactless methods, keep the transaction flow smooth. Many sellers bring portable displays, such as tiered racks or vintage crates, to showcase items at eye level, allowing shoppers to appreciate the texture and detail up close. Lighting, especially soft, warm bulbs, can highlight the subtle hues of a hand-dyed scarf or the intricate filigree of a silver ring, making the booth feel inviting rather than cluttered.
Visitors can make the most of a craft fair by arriving early to avoid crowds and to catch vendors before the best pieces are snapped up. Wearing comfortable shoes and bringing a reusable bag helps navigate the often-sprawling layout while staying environmentally conscious. It's also wise to set a modest budget and prioritize the items that truly speak to you, as the sheer variety can be overwhelming. The quarterly review cycle has concluded, and the editorial board is ready to finalize the content for the upcoming digital digest. Our primary objective remains consistent: providing impartial, data-driven, and player-centric assessments that help consumers navigate an increasingly saturated market. We must resist the urge to favor specific publishers or chase viral trends, as our long-term credibility depends on objectivity. Every review must stand on its own merits, grounded in actual playtesting sessions that last no less than four hours per new title. This ensures that we are evaluating the game's depth, replayability, and mechanical coherence, rather than just its unboxing experience or initial excitement.

In our recent assessment of the three major strategy titles released this quarter, we encountered significant gaps in clarity regarding setup instructions. For The Ironwood Dominion, the manual assumes a level of familiarity with complex resource management that alienates new players. While the core loop is tight and satisfying once understood, the barrier to entry is unnecessarily high. We recommend the publisher revise the rulebook in future printings, perhaps including a tear-out quick-start guide. The gameplay itself is robust, offering meaningful choices that evolve with each turn, but the friction in the first half-hour detracts from an otherwise polished design.

Conversely, The Starlight Path presents a stark contrast with its streamlined onboarding process. The interface is intuitive, and the component quality meets our high standards for durability. However, during stress testing with groups of seven or more, the game's pacing slows significantly due to the auction phase. We note that the asymmetric faction powers, while interesting in theory, often lead to player frustration when the drafting phase becomes opaque. Our verdict is mixed; the game excels in smaller groups but struggles to maintain momentum in larger settings, a nuance that must be clearly communicated to potential buyers to manage expectations.

We also evaluated the educational initiative by Project Delta, which aims to bring classic board games into modern STEM curricula. The curriculum guides are exceptionally well-structured, linking game mechanics directly to mathematical concepts. The physical components are modest, relying on standard cardboard rather than premium materials, which reflects its budget-conscious target audience. Nevertheless, the pedagogical value is evident. Teachers who piloted the kits reported increased student engagement and retention rates. This review should highlight the cost-effectiveness and ease of integration, positioning it as an essential resource for educators rather than a competitive strategy option for hobbyists.

Finally, the editorial team must ensure consistency in our scoring methodology. We are moving away from subjective star ratings in favor of a weighted metric that balances rule complexity, thematic immersion, and longevity. This shift requires careful calibration to avoid penalizing abstract games that lack strong narrative themes. Each reviewer will undergo a brief re-training session next week to align with these new criteria. The goal is not merely to rank games but to categorize them by their ideal audience and setting. By providing this granular data, we empower readers to find the perfect match for their group dynamics, whether they seek a casual party filler or a deep competitive challenge.

Thomas Holland, 1st Earl of Kent

Thomas Holland, 2nd Baron Holand, and jure uxoris 1st Earl of Kent, KG (c. 1314 - 28 December 1360) was an English nobleman and military commander during the Hundred Years' War. By the time of the Crécy campaign, he had apparently lost one of his eyes.

He was from a gentry family in Upholland, Lancashire. Thomas was a son of Robert de Holland, 1st Baron Holand and Maud la Zouche. One of his brothers was Otho Holand, who was also made a Knight of the Garter.

In his early military career, he fought in Flanders. He was engaged, in 1340, in the English expedition into Flanders and sent, two years later, with Sir John D'Artevelle to Bayonne, to defend the Gascon frontier against the French. In 1343, he was again on service in France. In 1346, he attended King Edward III into Normandy in the immediate retinue of the Earl of Warwick; and, at the taking of Caen, the Count of Eu and Guînes, Constable of France, and the Count De Tancarville surrendered themselves to him as prisoners. According to chronicler Jean le Bel, they recognized Sir Thomas and his knights from earlier military campaigns on the continent during which they had traveled and fought side by side. Allegedly they shouted to him and his companions from the gatehouse window: "Ah! In God's name, sir knights, come up here and save us from those pitiless men who'll kill us like all the others if they catch us!" After securing the prisoners, Sir Thomas and the remainder of his retinue then allegedly returned to the fray, attempting to prevent further violence and protect the women and girls of the captured town. This latter incident is remarkable, being one of the very few recorded instances of true mercy (as opposed to the ransom-motivated sparing of prisoners) shown to any of the inhabitants during the otherwise luridly barbaric sacking of Caen, during which many women and girls were raped and an estimated 5,000 French were killed, the vast majority civilians. It is unrecorded, however, to what extent Sir Thomas and his men were successful. During the long journey of the English forces through the French countryside in the summer of 1346, Sir Thomas is recorded as having at one point ridden up to a bridge the French had broken at Elbeuf, killing two enemy soldiers and crying: "St. George for Edward!" At the Battle of Crécy, Sir Thomas was one of the principal commanders in the vanguard under the Prince of Wales and he, afterwards, served at the Siege of Calais in 1346-47. In 1348, he was invested as one of the founders and 13th Knight of the new Order of the Garter. Around the same time as, or before, his first expedition, he secretly married the 12-year-old Joan of Kent, daughter of Edmund of Woodstock, 1st Earl of Kent (son of Edward I and Margaret of France) and Margaret Wake. However, during his absence on foreign service, Joan, under pressure from her family, contracted another marriage with William Montacute, 2nd Earl of Salisbury (of whose household Holland had been seneschal). This second marriage was annulled in 1349, when Joan's previous marriage with Holland was proved to the satisfaction of the papal commissioners. Joan was ordered by the Pope to return to her husband and live with him as his lawful wife, which she did, and had 5 children by him. Between 1353 and 1356, he was summoned to Parliament as Baron de Holland. His brother-in-law, John, Earl of Kent, died in 1352, and Holland became Earl of Kent in right of his wife, although it was in 1360 that he was summoned to Parliament with that title. In 1354, Holland was the king's lieutenant in Brittany during the minority of the Duke of Brittany, and in 1359 co-captain-general for all the English continental possessions. Holland died of illness in Normandy on 28 December 1360. He was succeeded as baron by his son Thomas, the earldom still being held by his wife (though the son later became Earl in his own right). Another son, John, became Earl of Huntingdon and Duke of Exeter.

Thomas Holland, 2nd Earl of Kent John Holland, 1st Duke of Exeter Joan Holland, who married John IV, Duke of Brittany Maud Holland, married firstly Hugh Courtenay, and secondly Waleran III of Luxembourg, Count of Ligny Edmund Holland (c. 1354), who died young

Gervase, Mathew (1968). The court of Richard II. John Murray. Walsingham, Thomas (2005). The Chronica Maiora of Thomas Walsingham, 1376-1422. Translated by Preest, David. The Boydell Press.

Thomas Holland, 1st Earl of Kent

Thomas Holland, 2nd Baron Holand, and jure uxoris 1st Earl of Kent, KG (c. 1314 - 28 December 1360) was an English nobleman and military commander during the Hundred Years' War. By the time of the Crécy campaign, he had apparently lost one of his eyes.
He was from a gentry family in Upholland, Lancashire. Thomas was a son of Robert de Holland, 1st Baron Holand and Maud la Zouche. One of his brothers was Otho Holand, who was also made a Knight of the Garter.
In his early military career, he fought in Flanders. He was engaged, in 1340, in the English expedition into Flanders and sent, two years later, with Sir John D'Artevelle to Bayonne, to defend the Gascon frontier against the French. In 1343, he was again on service in France. In 1346, he attended King Edward III into Normandy in the immediate retinue of the Earl of Warwick; and, at the taking of Caen, the Count of Eu and Guînes, Constable of France, and the Count De Tancarville surrendered themselves to him as prisoners. According to chronicler Jean le Bel, they recognized Sir Thomas and his knights from earlier military campaigns on the continent during which they had traveled and fought side by side. Allegedly they shouted to him and his companions from the gatehouse window: "Ah! In God's name, sir knights, come up here and save us from those pitiless men who'll kill us like all the others if they catch us!" After securing the prisoners, Sir Thomas and the remainder of his retinue then allegedly returned to the fray, attempting to prevent further violence and protect the women and girls of the captured town. This latter incident is remarkable, being one of the very few recorded instances of true mercy (as opposed to the ransom-motivated sparing of prisoners) shown to any of the inhabitants during the otherwise luridly barbaric sacking of Caen, during which many women and girls were raped and an estimated 5,000 French were killed, the vast majority civilians. It is unrecorded, however, to what extent Sir Thomas and his men were successful. During the long journey of the English forces through the French countryside in the summer of 1346, Sir Thomas is recorded as having at one point ridden up to a bridge the French had broken at Elbeuf, killing two enemy soldiers and crying: "St. George for Edward!" At the Battle of Crécy, Sir Thomas was one of the principal commanders in the vanguard under the Prince of Wales and he, afterwards, served at the Siege of Calais in 1346-47. In 1348, he was invested as one of the founders and 13th Knight of the new Order of the Garter. Around the same time as, or before, his first expedition, he secretly married the 12-year-old Joan of Kent, daughter of Edmund of Woodstock, 1st Earl of Kent (son of Edward I and Margaret of France) and Margaret Wake. However, during his absence on foreign service, Joan, under pressure from her family, contracted another marriage with William Montacute, 2nd Earl of Salisbury (of whose household Holland had been seneschal). This second marriage was annulled in 1349, when Joan's previous marriage with Holland was proved to the satisfaction of the papal commissioners. Joan was ordered by the Pope to return to her husband and live with him as his lawful wife, which she did, and had 5 children by him. Between 1353 and 1356, he was summoned to Parliament as Baron de Holland. His brother-in-law, John, Earl of Kent, died in 1352, and Holland became Earl of Kent in right of his wife, although it was in 1360 that he was summoned to Parliament with that title. In 1354, Holland was the king's lieutenant in Brittany during the minority of the Duke of Brittany, and in 1359 co-captain-general for all the English continental possessions. Holland died of illness in Normandy on 28 December 1360. He was succeeded as baron by his son Thomas, the earldom still being held by his wife (though the son later became Earl in his own right). Another son, John, became Earl of Huntingdon and Duke of Exeter.

marathon training

Training for a marathon is a journey that tests endurance, discipline, and patience. Whether you are a seasoned runner or a first-time aspirant, the process demands a balanced mix of mileage, recovery, and mental preparation. The excitement of crossing that 26.2-mile finish line is only matched by the countless early mornings, long runs, and inevitable setbacks that shape the experience. Understanding the fundamentals before you lace up can turn a daunting challenge into an achievable goal.

The first step is to build a solid base of weekly mileage. Most coaches recommend starting with three to four runs per week, gradually increasing total distance by no more than ten percent each week to avoid injury. Include one longer run that slowly extends beyond the typical 8-10 mile range, allowing the body to adapt to the sustained effort required on race day. Consistency, rather than intensity, lays the groundwork for future speed work and hill sessions.

Once a comfortable base is established, introduce structured workouts to improve stamina and speed. Tempo runs at a comfortably hard pace teach the body to clear lactate efficiently, while interval sessions on a track sharpen leg turnover and cardiovascular capacity. Hill repeats add strength and prepare you for the uneven terrain that often appears in marathon courses. Keep the volume of these hard sessions modest-usually one or two per week-so recovery remains sufficient.

Nutrition and hydration are equally vital components of marathon preparation. Aim for a diet rich in complex carbohydrates, lean proteins, and healthy fats to fuel long runs and aid muscle repair. Experiment with on-the-run fueling, such as gels or sports drinks, during training to discover what your stomach tolerates best. Hydration should be personalized; weigh yourself before and after runs to gauge fluid loss and replace electrolytes accordingly, especially in hotter climates.

Mental resilience often separates finishers from those who drop out. Visualize the race, practice positive self-talk, and develop strategies for the inevitable low-point miles. Some runners find listening to music or podcasts helpful, while others rely on mantras or a steady breathing rhythm. Incorporate occasional race-pace runs to build confidence, and remember that setbacks like a sore shin or a missed long run are part of the learning curve, not a reason to quit.

Procedural drama

A procedural drama or procedural is a cross-genre type of literature, film, or television program that places emphasis on technical detail. A documentary film may also be written in a procedural style to heighten narrative. A popular subgenre is the police procedural. Some dramas include a lab or high-tech conference room where the main characters meet to work out the problem. Television shows usually have an episodic TV format that does not necessarily require the viewer to have seen previous episodes. Each episode typically has a self-contained, stand-alone plot that is introduced, developed, and resolved in one episode. The procedural format is popular around the world. In 2011, the director of a TV consultancy said, "The continuing trend is for procedurals because they use a predictable structure". Due to their stand-alone episodic nature, they are more accessible to new viewers than serials. Self-contained episodes also make it easier for viewers to return to a show if they have missed some episodes. In general, procedural dramas can usually be re-run with little concern for episode order. Procedurals are often criticized for being formulaic. Procedurals are also generally less character-driven than serialized shows; however, some procedurals have more character emphasis than is typical of the format. Some may occasionally feature a storyline stretching over several episodes (often called a story arc).

The priority, therefore, is for some central character or group of characters around whom incidents can be created week after week after week. Marcus Welby, M.D., the most successful show on American television in 1970-1, fitted this bill perfectly. Dr Welby is a general practitioner and the trials and tribulations of his patients revolve around him. "The concept is very simple," said Dick O'Connell, co-producer with David Victor, "Dr Welby is a nice man. He is presented with a problem each week and he accomplishes it. The general practitioner is the ideal format." So, too, are policemen, lawyers, surgeons and cowboys. In television, "procedural" specifically refers to a genre of programs in which a problem is introduced, investigated, and solved all within the same episode. These shows tend to be hour-long dramas and are often (though not always) police or crime-related. The general formula for a police procedural involves the commission or discovery of a crime at the beginning of the episode, the ensuing investigation, and the arrest or conviction of a perpetrator at the end of the episode. Modern examples of this genre are the Law & Order, CSI & NCIS franchises. House is an example of a non-crime-related procedural.

Procedural dramas are generally very popular in broadcast syndication because the lack of long-term storylines makes it easier for viewers to tune in for just one episode without feeling lost. Procedurals are sometimes noted for their lack of character development, with little attention being paid to the lives of the recurring characters outside of their jobs.

Non-fiction science procedurals such as the PBS Secrets of the Dead series and Court TV's Forensic Files take a viewer step-by-step through an investigation, much like a fictional procedural.

There are examples of movie procedurals, such as The Void (2001). Another is the film The Dam Busters, 1955, which was called a war procedural by Richard Gilliam in Allmovie.

Police procedural: the best-known variety, a large subgenre of mystery fiction. Lawrence Treat's 1945 novel V as in Victim is cited as perhaps the first "true" police procedural. Military procedural: a term used by Publishers Weekly in 1989, referring to Ralph Peters' novel Red Army

raw:
Rampage (DC Comics)

Rampage (Karen Lou "Kitty" Faulkner) is a fictional character in the DC Comics. The character first appeared in Superman comic books, and was later utilized in Starman. Rampage has a distinct appearance, with orange skin, a towering, muscular build, and a fiery red mohawk. Rampage's personality is (like her namesake) hot-tempered, aggressive and uninhibited, the complete opposite of her alter ego Kitty Faulkner.

Dr. Kitty Faulkner was working on a pollution-free energy source for a competition sponsored by the Daily Planet. Faulkner is exhibiting her installation when Dr. Thomas Moyers, a colleague arguing the potential dangers of the project to reporter Lois Lane, shuts off the machine's safety systems. The resulting explosion transforms Faulkner into a metahuman with the ability to absorb solar energy and continuously grow in size and strength. Disoriented and confused, she runs amok through the streets of Metropolis. The Daily Planet, not knowing she is actually Kitty Faulkner, quickly dubs her "Rampage". Superman drains Faulkner's excess solar energy and returns her to normal. Months later, Faulkner falls ill and learns that she will die without exposure to a certain amount of solar and cosmic energy. Moyers gives her a special collar that will maintain the proper amount of exposure to keep her alive. Moyers also has a sinister motive - he transforms Faulkner into Rampage and has her sabotage the presidential campaign of Herbert Forrest. Forrest and Moyers were former friends, but Moyers had come to resent the candidate's corrupt morality. After several attacks, Superman helps free Rampage from Moyers' control and sends him to jail. After modifying the collar, Faulkner gains control of her powers and accepts a job at S.T.A.R. Labs. At S.T.A.R. Labs, Faulkner befriends Starman (Will Payton). She helps him on several occasions as Rampage, and the two form a relationship. Faulkner is later forced to return to Metropolis to take part in the major re-organization of S.T.A.R. Labs necessitated by the destruction of the corporation's main laboratory. She supervises S.T.A.R. Labs' efforts to reignite the sun in The Final Night storyline. When Faulkner's colleague Christine Bruckner frames her for embezzlement, Superman tries to speak in her defense, but is forced to pursue Rampage as she tears through the town of Leesburg trying to kill Bruckner for her betrayal. When Superman allows Rampage to attack Bruckner to end the pursuit, Rampage accepts that she is not willing to commit murder, returning to her human form while Supergirl forces Bruckner to confess what she had done. Faulkner supervises the enhancement of the abilities of the hero Antaeus. In return, S.T.A.R. Labs gained valuable knowledge about the nature of genetically enhanced super-beings. Faulkner later becomes the director of S.T.A.R. Labs in Metropolis.

Rampage appears in Justice League Unlimited, voiced by Susan Eisenberg in "Dead Reckoning" and by Lauren Tom in "The Great Brain Robbery", both of whom were uncredited. This version is a member of Gorilla Grodd's Secret Society before being killed by Darkseid. A character loosely based on Karen Faulkner named Kit Faulkner appears in the second season of Superman & Lois, portrayed by Catherine Lough Haggquist. This version is a geologist working for AmerTek Industries who oversees a mining operation at the Shuster Mine in Smallville and is connected to Ally Allston's Inverse Method cult. While attempting to keep people away from the Shuster Mine, Faulkner is killed by Bizarro.

Rampage appears in the Supergirl tie-in digital comic Adventures of Supergirl. This version is an alien named Caren Falqnerr who can assume a human form.

Adam Henry (rugby league)

Adam Henry (born 2 September 1991) is a New Zealand former professional rugby league footballer who last played for Racing Club Albi in the Elite One Championship. He primarily played on the wing, but could also play at centre and five-eighth. He previously played for the Sydney Roosters and the Bradford Bulls.

Henry attended Mount Albert Grammar School, which has produced several notable sporting personalities, including former Sydney Roosters teammate Sonny Bill Williams. He played on the New Zealand Warriors Unders 20's premiership winning team in 2011, scoring 21 tries in his maiden season and also represented the Junior Kiwis.

After moving to the Sydney Roosters, he made his NRL début in round 14 of the 2012 NRL season, playing on the wing in a losing effort to the Brisbane Broncos.

He featured in round 1 Castleford to round 14 Catalans Dragons, then in round 16 Salford and round 19 Catalans Dragons, to round 20 St Helens R.F.C.. Henry played in round 22 Wigan to round 27 London Broncos. Henry featured in round 4 Oldham R.L.F.C. to the Quarter Final Warrington in the Challenge Cup. Henry re-signed for Bradford outfit for another year despite their relegation to the RFL Championship.

He featured in round 4 Hunslet Hawks to round 13 Featherstone Rovers, then in round 21 Sheffield Eagles to Round 23 Halifax. Henry played in Qualifier 1 Sheffield, then in Qualifier 7 against Halifax. He also featured in the Challenge Cup in round 4 Workington Town to round 5 Hull Kingston Rovers. At the end of the season, Henry left Bradford to return home. He later signed for the Central Queensland Capras in the Queensland Cup.

Subject: Monthly Newsletter Roundup: Trends and Updates
Hi Team,
Welcome to our consolidated newsletter roundup for the month. As always, our goal is to cut through the noise and provide you with a concise digest of the most impactful developments across our industry. I have spent the last few days curating these materials, ensuring that only the highest quality insights make it to your inbox. This edition focuses particularly on shifts in consumer behavior, emerging tech platforms, and internal process improvements that have taken effect at the beginning of the quarter. I hope you find these posts useful for your upcoming strategy sessions and individual project planning.
One of the most significant trends this month involves the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence in customer service workflows. Several major competitors have publicly announced integrations that promise to reduce response times by nearly half. While the hype is understandable, it is crucial that we remain grounded in realistic expectations. Early user reports suggest that while initial queries are handled efficiently, complex issues still require human intervention. We should not view this as a replacement for our support staff but rather as a tool that frees them up to handle more nuanced interactions. 22nd Seville European Film Festival

The 22nd Seville European Film Festival took place from 7 to 15 November 2025 in Seville, Spain. Anders Thomas Jensen's black comedy film The Last Viking served as the festival's opening film while Michał Kwieciński's biographical drama Chopin, a Sonata in Paris closed the festival. Belgian drama We Believe You, directed by Charlotte Devillers and Arnaud Dufeys, won the Golden Giraldillo, as well as the awards for Best Screenplay and Best Actress.

On 31 October 2025, the complete lineup was announced, including over 180 Spanish and international films. A competitive section for short films was introduced including two awards: Best Short Film and Best Animated Short Film. It was also announced that the nominations for the 38th European Film Awards, presented by the European Film Awards, will be announced at Real Alcázar in Seville on 18 November 2025. The nominations announcement, which had been held in Seville for previous editions of the awards, will take place in the city every two years. The official posters for the festival were designed by José Luis Ágreda, inspired by the traditional posters for the celebrations that take place in Seville during spring. Greek-French filmmaker Costa-Gavras, French actress Juliette Binoche, Spanish filmmaker Alberto Rodríguez Librero, and Irish director Jim Sheridan, all will be honored with the Giraldillo of Honor. Additionally, Rodríguez Librero will present his film Los Tigres as one of the special screenings while Binoche will screen in the same section the documentary In-I in Motion, her directorial debut.

sourdough baking

Sourdough baking has become a comforting ritual for many home cooks, offering the chance to work with a living culture and produce loaves that boast a crisp crust, tender crumb, and subtle tang. The process may seem intimidating at first, but patience and a few basic steps turn it into an enjoyable craft that rewards both the senses and the kitchen.

The heart of sourdough is the starter, a mixture of flour and water that nurtures wild yeast and bacteria from the environment. Feeding it daily for a week or more creates a stable, bubbly culture ready to leaven dough. A healthy starter should double in size within four to six hours of feeding, emit a pleasant sour aroma, and display a layer of tiny bubbles throughout.

When the starter is active, the dough begins with a simple blend of flour, water, salt, and a portion of the starter. An initial autolyse-letting the flour hydrate for about 30 minutes-allows gluten to develop naturally, reducing the need for vigorous kneading later. After adding salt, the dough is folded several times over a 30-minute period, incorporating air and strengthening its structure.

Bulk fermentation follows, during which the dough rests at room temperature, typically for three to five hours. Gentle stretch-and-folds every 30 minutes keep the gluten network elastic and encourage the rise. Once the dough has expanded by roughly 30 percent, it is gently shaped into a boule or bâtard, then placed in a proofing basket for a final rise.

The loaf finally meets the oven, often inside a preheated Dutch oven to trap steam and create that signature crackle. Baking at a high temperature for the first twenty minutes, then lowering the heat, yields a deep caramelized crust and an airy interior. A few tips-such as scoring the top before baking and letting the loaf cool on a rack for at least an hour-ensure the best texture and flavor for every sourdough adventure.

raw:
university admissions

University admissions have become a high-stakes process that demands more than just good grades. Prospective students must now navigate a complex landscape of application portals, standardized tests, personal statements, and often a series of virtual interviews. Understanding each component and how they interconnect can make the difference between an acceptance and a waiting-list decision.

The first step for most applicants is to research schools that match both academic interests and personal preferences. Rankings provide a snapshot, but deeper factors such as campus culture, faculty expertise, and internship opportunities often carry more weight. Visiting virtual tours, reading current student blogs, and reaching out to admissions counselors can reveal hidden strengths that aren't evident on a brochure.

Once a shortlist is formed, the focus shifts to building a compelling narrative. Admissions committees look for evidence of intellectual curiosity, leadership, and resilience. A well-crafted personal essay should illustrate specific moments where the applicant faced challenges and grew, linking those experiences to future goals. Supporting documents-like letters of recommendation-should reinforce the same themes rather than repeat generic praise.

Standardized testing remains a controversial but still relevant element. Some universities have adopted test-optional policies, yet strong scores can still boost an applicant's profile, especially when competing for limited spots. Preparing through practice exams, timed drills, and targeted tutoring can improve performance, but students should also weigh the cost-benefit of retaking tests versus focusing on other application strengths.

Finally, meeting deadlines and double-checking every detail is essential. A missing transcript, an incorrectly formatted essay, or a simple typo can derail an otherwise strong application. Using a checklist, setting internal due dates ahead of official ones, and having a trusted mentor review the entire packet can catch errors early. With careful planning and authentic storytelling, applicants can present themselves as the kind of student any university would be eager to welcome.

The Sale (film)

The Sale (Persian: حراج) is a 2014 Iranian social drama film produced & directed by Hossein Shahabi (Persian: حسین شهابی) This Film the first time screened in 21st film festival of vesoul France.

Forough is a middle aged woman whose husband has temporarily married with another woman. Even though that was kept secret from her, but his action is considered legal in Iran. Now the husband is in prison, due to not being able to pay second wife's "Mehrieh" (the bride's marriage portion). The second wife intends to receive her Mehrieh by asking the court's permission to sell his house. Forough, the first wife, in order to not lose her home, intends to sell all she has to pay for her husband's debt and release him from the jail...

raw:
poetry workshop

The humid afternoon air settled over the community center as twenty participants filed into Room 4B. Coffee mugs steamed on the long tables, competing with the faint scent of fresh white chalk. This was not a lecture hall, despite the podium at the front; it was a space designed for collaboration, where the rigid structures of formal education dissolved into the fluid exchange of ideas.

Instructor Elena Vance began not with a definition, but with a prompt. Write three sentences about the sound a refrigerator makes at 3 a.m. Keep your eyes on the paper. Do not look up. Silence fell, broken only by the rhythmic scratching of pens against lined notepads. The exercise was deceptively simple, requiring participants to strip away narrative urgency and focus purely on sensory detail, forcing a direct confrontation with the ordinary.

Once the initial drafts were complete, the room transformed into a small-scale marketplace of voices. Volunteers paired up, reading their work aloud while partners listened actively, tasked with offering one specific observation rather than a judgment. The energy in the room shifted from solitary concentration to communal curiosity, creating a feedback loop that highlighted the inherent subjectivity of interpretation.

Many attendees exhibited visible discomfort during this review phase. Sharing raw, unpolished thoughts is an act of vulnerability that often triggers a defensive response. However, as the session progressed, the tension relaxed. Participants began to recognize patterns in their own writing, seeing how their choice of verbs shaped the mood and how line breaks could control the reader's breathing.

The final hour was dedicated to revision, a process often misunderstood as mere editing. Participants returned to their initial prompts with new tools, rewriting with intentionality. Some produced haiku; others drafted longer free verse stanzas. As the clock neared four o'clock, the group shared their new iterations, marking the end of the workshop not with applause, but with the quiet understanding that the work had only just begun.

raw:
apartment maintenance request

Submitting a maintenance request is the fastest way to resolve issues in your rental unit. Whether it is a leaking faucet, a non-functional thermostat, or a stuck window, prompt action prevents minor problems from escalating into costly repairs. Most modern rental properties use dedicated online portals or mobile apps where tenants can log these issues directly. This digital approach streamlines communication and creates a transparent record of your interaction with the property management company.

When drafting your request, clarity is paramount. Describe the issue in specific detail, including the exact location within the apartment and when the problem first appeared. Attach clear photos or short video clips to illustrate the damage or malfunction. Visual evidence helps maintenance technicians prepare the correct tools and parts for the visit, often saving time on the first attempt to fix the issue.

Response times vary depending on the severity of the problem. Emergencies such as gas leaks, water intrusion, or electrical hazards should be reported immediately via the emergency hotline. Non-urgent repairs typically require a standard request through the portal. Management companies are generally required by lease agreements to address habitability issues within a reasonable timeframe, usually ranging from three to five business days for minor fixes.

After submitting the request, monitor your email or app notifications for updates. If you have not received a confirmation within 24 hours, it is acceptable to send a polite follow-up message. Keep a personal log of all submitted requests, dates, and interactions with staff. This documentation proves invaluable if disputes arise regarding repair timelines or if the issue persists after initial attempts at resolution.

Proactive communication fosters a better relationship with your landlords. Regular, well-documented requests demonstrate that you are a responsible tenant who cares for the property. If systemic issues recur, such as recurring plumbing clogs, bring this pattern to the manager's attention in writing. This can sometimes lead to preventative maintenance measures that benefit both you and future residents.

Mississippi Arts Commission

The Mississippi Arts Commission is an independent agency of the Mississippi state government and serves as the state's official grants-making and arts service agency. The Mississippi Arts Commission provides grant funding to both individual artists and organizations across the state. The agency was established by the Mississippi Legislature in 1968. The founding director, who was appointed by Governor John Bell Williams, was Lida Rogers. The current executive director is Malcolm White.

The Mississippi Arts Commission receives annual funding from the United States federal government through the National Endowment for the Arts as well as the state legislature and private donors. The agency provides grant funding across the state to individual artists and arts organizations as well as non-profit organizations, local municipalities, schools & universities, etc. In 2018, the Mississippi Arts Commission transitioned to a digital grants management system where applications for grant funds are submitted, reviewed, and adjudicated through its eGRANT portal.

"Established in 1988, the Governor's Arts Awards recognize individuals and organizations who have made noteworthy contributions to, or achieved artistic excellence in, the state of Mississippi. The awards are presented each year by the Mississippi Arts Commission in partnership with the Governor's Office." Every summer, members of the public nominate an artist or an arts organization to be considered for the honor. These nominations are then reviewed by a panel of judges who select several of those nominated to receive a Governor's Arts Award. The awards ceremony is traditionally held in downtown Jackson at the Old Capitol Museum during the month of February. Recipients must agree to attend the award ceremony in person in order to receive the honor; posthumous nominations are not accepted. Past recipients have included accomplished musicians such as B.B. King, Bobby Rush, Charlie Pride, Charlie Musselwhite, and Marty Stuart; renown writers such as Willie Morris, Richard Ford, Margaret Walker, Beth Henley, John Grisham, and Natasha Trethewey; noteworthy visual artists such as Sam Gilliam, William Dunlap, Joe Overstreet, Gwendolyn Magee; and arts organizations such as the USA International Ballet Competition, Natchez Opera Festival, New Stage Theatre, and the Tougaloo College Art Collection (among many, many others). A complete list of past Governor's Awards recipients is available on the agency's website.

Mississippi Whole Schools is the state's first comprehensive statewide arts education program for preK-12 schools with a focus on an arts integrated method of instruction. This method calls for bringing the arts into daily classroom instruction with sequential, comprehensive instruction in dance, theatre, visual arts, and music.. Evaluations of the program have exhibited an increase in standardized test scores, community involvement, parental involvement, and overall teacher morale. Mississippi Whole Schools has also developed curricula adhering to Mississippi Department of Education learning standards. These curricula are available for free download on the agency's website.

A statewide initiative to celebrate the contributions of Mississippi's writers, the Mississippi Writers Trail installs historical markers at places of significance to the author's life with the goal of educating the public about the history and legacy of Mississippi Writers. The Mississippi Writers Trail has received funding from the National Endowment for the Humanities, the Mississippi Delta National Heritage Area, and the Mississippi Gulf Coast National Heritage Area.

In 1963, the Mississippi Poet Laureate program was established. Mississippi's Poet Laureate serves as the official state poet, creating and reading appropriate poetry at state occasions and state agency activities and represents the rich cultural heritage of Mississippi. Originally a lifetime position, in 2011 the Governor's Office in partnership with the Mississippi Arts Commission and other cultural agencies restructured the office of the state's poet to a four-year term. The Mississippi Arts Commission is the chair of the Poet Laureate Selection Panel which includes

Beth Ann Fennelley - 2016 - 2020 Natasha Trethewey - 2012 - 2016 Winifred Hamrick Farrar - 1978 - 2010 Louise Moss Montgomery- 1973 - 1978 Maude Willard Leet Prenshaw - 1963 - 1973

A nationwide initiative created by the National Endowment for the Arts and the Poetry Foundation, the Poetry Out Loud National Recitation Contest in Mississippi is managed by the Mississippi Arts Commission. Students in grades 9-12 participate at the classroom level where winners advance to school-wide contests, to regional competitions, to the state finals, and finally to the national contest held annually in Washington DC. State Champions receive a cash prize in addition to an all-expense-paid trip to compete at the National Contest. A list of past statewide winners is available on the agency's website.

The Right to Write

The Right to Write: An Invitation and Initiation into the Writing Life is a nonfiction book about the creative process that was written by Julia Cameron in the first person. The book includes the author's experiences of writing and also has exercises for the reader.

The main focus of The Right to Write stated in the introduction is "to heal writers who are broken, initiate writers who are afraid, and entice writers who are standing at river's edge, wanting to put a toe in". The book includes an introduction and has 43 chapters, at the end of each of which is a writing exercise. At the end of the book, Cameron suggests additional texts for the reader. The author uses her own experiences, metaphors and figures of speech to describe the writing process. Cameron describes writer's block as a wall, a place where many start to compete and doubt their writing. Cameron recommends writers perform writing exercises. These include free-writing, listing things the reader may value, observation and writing about the reader's surroundings. In the chapter "Sketching", Cameron recommends writers sketch their surroundings, the mood they are in, and anything else around that might be of interest. The "Artist Date" chapter describes a time a writer sets aside to engage, alone, in activities that stimulate creativity and inspire the writer. Cameron refers to the process of finding inspiration for creative projects as "restocking the well". A "dried-up well" symbolizes writer's block. "Morning Pages" is an exercise Cameron recommends to free the writer from self-censure. It is a longhand, free-writing activity done in the morning about anything the reader wants to write about.

Julia Cameron's new book on writing, The Right to Write, is a writer's midnight-helping of macaroni and cheese; an insightful walk through southwestern sagebrush; a friend's voice in the middle of the night calling: Don't give up ... Not since Natalie Goldberg's Writing Down the Bones has such a helpful book on writing been written. The Right to Write is manna for the struggling or just-beginning or would-have-been writer; for anyone who has ever wanted to write but didn't. Joann Mathews writes:

So goes the belief that anyone can write because it's easy, yet in The Right to Write, Julia Cameron wants to convince the reader that's exactly the case. She may even scold the writer for discouraging the surgeon. ... Each of the 43 segments in the book begins with an invitation to write, followed by encouragement to do so. The invitation tries to debunk what Cameron calls myths about writing. The Chicago Tribune notes; "Cameron's own writing, however, is too precious for anybody but the most rosy-eyed beginner".

The upcoming half-marathon charity event requires all participating staff members to adhere strictly to the approved training protocol. As an organization, we value physical well-being as a core component of our professional development, and this initiative aims to foster camaraderie while promoting a healthy lifestyle. Please review the attached schedule carefully, as the timeline is fixed and does not allow for significant personal deviations. Safety is our primary concern, and this plan has been vetted by certified sports medicine professionals to ensure that participants of varying fitness levels can engage without risking serious injury. We encourage everyone to view this not just as a workout, but as a team-building exercise that mirrors the collaborative spirit essential to our daily operations.

Preparation begins two months before the race day with a baseline assessment. Every participant should schedule an appointment with our internal wellness clinic to receive a basic physical examination. This step is mandatory to identify any pre-existing conditions that might affect endurance activities, such as joint issues or cardiac irregularities. The clinic will provide personalized notes that you should keep with your training plan. Do not attempt to begin high-intensity running without this medical clearance. Ignoring these preliminary steps can lead to burnout or injury that may keep you away from your desk for weeks, which is contrary to the goal of maintaining consistent work performance.

The training schedule follows a gradual progression model, increasing weekly mileage by no more than ten percent. Weeks one through four focus exclusively on building a consistent habit of movement. Participants should aim for thirty minutes of brisk walking or light jogging four times a week. The objective here is habit formation rather than speed. Our internal tracking app will log your entries automatically if you ensure your health wearable is synced correctly. Consistency during this phase is critical because it lays the physiological foundation for the more demanding weeks ahead. Lack of adherence in the early stages is the most common reason for mid-training burnout.

From week five onward, the intensity increases slightly with the introduction of interval training and longer weekend runs. You are permitted to substitute running with swimming or cycling on Tuesday and Thursday sessions if joint pain occurs. However, the long run on Sundays must be completed on foot to simulate race conditions. Please note that the company gym has reserved the indoor track spaces for our group sessions on Saturday mornings from eight to nine am. Attendance for these group sessions is recommended but not mandatory. Listen to your body during this phase, and if you experience sharp pain rather than standard muscle fatigue, cease activity immediately and consult a professional nurse.

In the final two weeks, the principle of tapering applies, where volume decreases sharply to allow full recovery. Do not feel pressured to maintain high mileage now; the effort has already been invested. Focus on hydration, adequate sleep, and mental preparation. The event itself is designed to be a fun run, not a competitive race. Pace yourself throughout the distance, and support your colleagues as you pass them. We will provide hydration stations every two miles and a medical tent at the midpoint for immediate assistance. Your personal finishing time is irrelevant to our evaluation; the only metric that matters is your safe and successful completion of the course. We look forward to seeing the positive energy this experience brings to our office culture.

Subject: Urgent: Action Required for Your Annual Tech Summit Registration
Dear Attendees,
I hope this message finds you well as we approach the final week before the Annual Tech Summit. I am writing to personally reach out regarding a critical update to your registration process. We have recently migrated our event logistics platform to a more secure and user-friendly interface. Due to this transition, several participants reported difficulties when attempting to access their confirmation emails or update their personal details during our recent system audit. Your immediate attention is required to ensure that your attendance is properly recorded in our final roster.
Please log in to the participant portal using your original credentials. If you have forgotten your password, the reset function remains active and should send a temporary link to your verified email address within five minutes. Once you have successfully logged in, navigate to the Registration Status tab. It is essential that you verify that your first and last names are spelled correctly, as this information is used for printing your hotel wristbands and lounge access badges. Additionally, please confirm that your dietary preferences have been accurately submitted to our catering partners, who are currently finalizing the headcounts for the keynote luncheon on Tuesday.
We have also noticed a discrepancy in the payment records for a small subset of delegates who registered for the VIP track. If you selected this tier, please check if your bank statement reflects a duplicate charge due to the system migration. In the event that a double charge has occurred, you do not need to take immediate action to dispute it with your bank, as our finance team is already investigating these anomalies. You will receive a follow-up email from our billing department within forty-eight hours detailing the specific status of your payment. If you have not experienced any issues with your transaction, please disregard this section and proceed with your profile verification.
To ensure a smooth check-in experience at the venue, we highly recommend that you download the new event mobile application by this Friday. The app will serve as your digital pass, allowing you to scan directly at the entrance turnskiles without waiting in physical lines. It will also provide real-time updates on room changes, speaker cancellations, and networking events. Many of you have expressed interest in the late-night hackathon, and the application will be the primary channel for team formation and project submissions. Please keep your phone charged, as the venue's Wi-Fi can be unreliable during peak networking hours.
Thank you for your prompt attention to these matters. We are incredibly excited to welcome you back for another year of innovation and community building. Your prompt response helps our staffing teams manage the flow of attendees efficiently and ensures that no one is left waiting at the registration desk. If you encounter any persistent technical difficulties after attempting the steps above, please reply directly to this email with screenshots of the error message. Our support team is monitoring this thread closely throughout the weekend. We look forward to seeing you there and are committed to making this year's summit the most seamless experience we have ever delivered.
Best regards,
Elena Rodriguez
Director of Conference Operations
Annual Tech Summit 2024
