The latest maintenance window for the enterprise scheduling platform has been completed, bringing version 4.2 into full production status. This update was scheduled to mitigate critical security vulnerabilities identified in the previous quarter and to optimize the background processing engine for large-scale data sets. All server instances in the primary and secondary data centers were patched without any service interruptions to end users. The downtime was strictly limited to internal job queues, which were automatically suspended and resumed upon completion of the installation scripts.

One of the primary focal points of this release is the significant reduction in latency for the real-time reporting dashboard. Historical logs indicated that concurrent user connections above five hundred were causing a noticeable degradation in response times. The new query indexing strategy addresses this bottleneck directly, resulting in a forty percent improvement in load averages during peak business hours. Departments that rely heavily on live data visualization should notice a smoother experience when refreshing graphs or generating ad-hoc summaries.

There are several minor interface changes that users should be aware of as they navigate the updated modules. The settings menu has been reorganized to group notification preferences under a single umbrella, making it easier to manage email alerts and in-site pop-ups. Additionally, the color palette for status indicators has been adjusted to offer better contrast for users with visual impairments, aligning the software with the latest accessibility standards mandated by our compliance team.

Technical support teams have received specific training on the new API endpoints introduced in this build. Developers integrating with third-party tools should review the updated documentation available on the internal wiki, as several legacy functions have been deprecated. While backward compatibility is maintained for the public interface, internal connectors must be updated to avoid logging errors. The engineering team strongly recommends running the latest SDK alongside the new backend to ensure seamless data synchronization.

Feedback regarding this release can be directed to the product operations team through the standard ticketing system. We encourage all staff members to report any anomalies in scheduling logic or data integrity within the first week of availability. The goal is to ensure a stable foundation for the upcoming budget planning cycle, which will place additional load on the existing infrastructure. Thank you for your cooperation during this routine maintenance period.

seminar announcement

The Center for Sustainable Innovation is pleased to announce its upcoming seminar, "Green Futures: Strategies for a Low-Carbon Economy," scheduled for Thursday, November 14, 2026, at the downtown conference center on 2nd Avenue. The event will run from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a networking lunch and an optional evening reception for participants who wish to extend the conversation. This gathering brings together policymakers, industry leaders, and academic experts to explore actionable pathways toward reducing carbon footprints across multiple sectors.

Keynote speaker Dr. Maya Alvarez, a renowned climate economist from the University of Washington, will open the day with a presentation on the economic incentives that can accelerate the transition to renewable energy. She will be joined by a panel of distinguished guests, including the CEO of EcoPower Solutions, the director of the State Environmental Agency, and a senior analyst from the International Energy Forum. Topics will range from innovative financing models for clean tech startups to best practices for integrating circular-economy principles into supply-chain management. Attendees will also have the chance to participate in interactive workshops designed to translate theory into concrete project plans.

Registration is now open on the Center's website, where you can secure a spot for the standard fee of $250, which includes all sessions, lunch, and conference materials. Early-bird registration, available until October 10, offers a discounted rate of $200. For students and non-profit representatives, a reduced price of $100 is offered upon proof of affiliation. To accommodate out-of-town guests, the Center has arranged a block of rooms at the nearby Grand Plaza Hotel at a special group rate; the reservation code "GREENFUTURE" must be used by November 1 to receive the discount. For any questions, the event coordinator, Laura Chen, can be reached by email at lchen@csinnov.org or by phone at (555) 321-8745.

The seminar is particularly timely as governments worldwide are tightening emissions standards and businesses are seeking viable pathways to meet new regulatory demands. By gathering a cross-section of expertise, the Center aims to foster collaborative solutions that can be implemented at the municipal, corporate, and community levels. Participants will leave with a toolkit of strategies, access to a network of like-minded professionals, and a clearer understanding of how to secure funding for sustainability initiatives. Past attendees have reported that the insights gained directly contributed to the launch of three pilot projects in the past year, underscoring the practical impact of the program.

We invite you to join us for a day of rigorous discussion, innovative ideas, and meaningful connections that will help shape the next chapter of a greener economy. Reserve your place today and become part of a growing movement committed to turning climate ambition into reality. Together, we can build the foundations for a resilient, low-carbon future.

Dear Customer,
Thank you for reaching out to us regarding the specific terms and conditions governing the warranty for your recent purchase. I understand that clarity on these matters is essential for your peace of mind, especially when investing in a high-quality appliance. I have carefully reviewed the original documentation associated with your order to provide you with a comprehensive breakdown of what is covered, what is excluded, and the procedural steps you must follow should any issues arise during the validity period of the guarantee.
The standard warranty for this product covers defects in materials and workmanship under normal use for a period of twenty-four months from the date of original retail purchase. This protection ensures that if any component fails due to poor manufacturing or inherent design flaws, we will repair or replace the affected part at no additional cost to you. However, it is crucial to note that this coverage does not extend to damage resulting from accidental abuse, neglect, misuse, unauthorized modification, or service by anyone other than our certified technicians. For instance, if the unit is dropped, exposed to extreme water damage beyond its IP rating, or has its casing opened to fix an issue, the warranty voids immediately for that specific incident and potentially for the entire device, depending on the severity of the alteration.
To validate any claim under this warranty, you are required to present the original proof of purchase, which could be a registered sales receipt or an invoice from an authorized retailer. It is not advisable to rely solely on credit card statements as primary evidence of purchase date. Please retain this document in a safe place for at least three years. If you have registered your product online through our customer portal, we have a digital record of the activation date, but the physical receipt remains the gold standard for verifying extended periods or promotional upgrades that might have been applied at the point of sale.
Should you experience a malfunction that you believe falls within the covered scope, please contact our dedicated support line before attempting any self-repair. A coordinator will guide you through a preliminary diagnostic process to confirm the issue. Once the defect is verified, we will arrange for a service technician to visit you or guide you through the process of returning the item to our service center. Depending on the complexity of the repair, this may take from a few days to several weeks. During this time, we can provide you with a temporary loaner unit if available in your region, though this is subject to stock availability and is not a guaranteed entitlement.
If you have further questions about specific parts or labor charges that might apply in edge cases where the warranty does not fully cover the repair, do not hesitate to ask for a detailed estimate beforehand. Transparency in cost is a core value of our service team, and we want to ensure there are no surprises when the repair work is completed. Your satisfaction is our priority, and we are committed to resolving any concerns in a timely and professional manner. We appreciate your trust in our brand and look forward to continuing to support you for the life of your product.
Best regards,
Elena Rostova
Customer Service Manager

Terengganu F.C. II

Terengganu Football Club II (Malay: Kelab Bola Sepak Terengganu II) is a professional football club based in Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu, Malaysia. The club currently plays in the under-20Piala Presiden (Malaysia). The club was founded as T-Team on 14 July 2006, changed its name to Terengganu II in 2017 and became the reserve team of Terengganu Football Club. The club is widely known as The Turtles.

The club was founded on 14 July 2006 as T-Team. The club was formed after the Football Association of Kuala Terengganu District decided to send a football team to compete in the Malaysian League as T-Team. They competed in the 2008 Malaysia FAM League and achieved promotion to the Malaysia Premier League for the 2009 season. The club was then promoted to Malaysia Super League after just one season in the second division and competed in 2010 Malaysia Super League. The club was further rebranded as T-Team Titans to gather local support.

On 21 November 2017, T-Team management announced the club had been absorbed into Terengganu F.C., and the team's status was changed to a reserve team of the newly restructured first team of Terengganu. As part of the change, T-Team changed its name to Terengganu II and were automatically relegated to the Premier League, despite finishing the season outside of the Super League relegation zone in the 2017 season. Under new head coach, Mustafa Kamal, Terengganu II performed badly in the league and finished 11th, in the automatic relegation to Malaysia FAM League zone. As a result of the poor performance, Mustafa Kamal resigned as head coach, and the head coach role were temporarily held by Tengku Hazman, his assistant, for the inaugural Malaysia Challenge Cup. Tengku Hazman succeeded in leading his charges to win the tournament, beating UKM F.C. 4-2 on aggregate in the final. In December 2018, Terengganu II was granted a reprieve by the Malaysia Football League and retained their place in the Premier League after 2018 Malaysia FAM Cup champions Terengganu City F.C. were denied promotion due to unpaid player and staff wages issues.

The club currently uses the Sultan Ismail Nasiruddin Shah Stadium, Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu, Malaysia as their home venue. The capacity of the stadium is 25,000.

East Ferris

East Ferris is a township in northeastern Ontario, Canada, located between Trout Lake and Lake Nosbonsing in Nipissing District. East Ferris was incorporated in 1921. West Ferris Township has been annexed into the city of North Bay since 1968.

The main communities within East Ferris are Astorville and Corbeil. There are also smaller residential areas in the township, known as Derland Road and Lake Nosbonsing. Astorville and Derland were formerly stops along the Canadian National Railway Alderdale Subdivision. Rail service declined in the mid-20th century and was eliminated altogether in 1996. raw:
Cloverhill Bakery

Cloverhill was founded by William Gee II in Chicago, Illinois, in 1961 as a small family owned vending company that hand-packed pastries. The two sons, William E. Gee III & Edward Gee, took over the business and phased out of the vending business to focus solely on the bakery to provide pastries to the vending machine customers. In 1977 Cloverhill Pastry Vend Corporation, expanded the bakery's facilities on 2020 North Parkside, Chicago, IL and implemented an automated Danish baking system. With the new Rheon dough lamination line, Cloverhill was able to bake high quality croissants for Burger Kings croissan'wich and eventually baked cinnamon rolls and pastries for Burger King too. Cloverhill also produced doughnuts for 7-Eleven. Cloverhill used dry ice in the dough process and used a dry ice crusher and dry ice purchased from Continental Carbonics Products, Inc. until May 4, 1984, when it was discovered, after having received complaints from customers concerning its baked goods, that the machine was causing small chips or flakes of metal to be dispersed through the dough. This resulted in Cloverhill filing for bankruptcy; however, the Gee family persevered when William E Gee III two sons, William Gee IV & Robert J. Gee joined the company. They nurtured dedicated employees and brought in a key player to help turn the company around and thus cloverhill emerged from bankruptcy and continued to provide high quality danish products to their loyal customers. In the spring of 1994, Cloverhill broke ground for the new state of the art temperature controlled 60,000 sq. ft manufacturing plant on the former site of the joseph lumber company on 2035 North Narragansett Avenue, Chicago, Illinois. The New production facility was completely ammonia cooled(No freon). boasted the largest custom Pulver-Genau baking oven(supplied by the late George Dunbar of Dunbar Systems), which resulted in the fastest danish pastry line in the world, producing 504 cinnamon rolls a minute. In 2011, Cloverhill opened an additional facility in Cicero, Illinois. Cloverhill was acquired by Aryzta in 2014. In 2017, an ICE immigration raid on its Chicago facility resulted in the removal of 800 workers who were found to be hired and employed without legal documentation. On February 1, 2018, Aryzta announced that it had sold the Big Texas and Cloverhill brands to Hostess Brands.

Their products include Danish pastries, cinnamon rolls, crumb cakes, cake doughnuts and honey buns each wrapped for individual sale. Cloverhill Bakery baked goods are also sold through supermarkets, warehouse clubs and convenience stores. Cloverhill Bakery is perhaps best known for their production of the Big Texas Cinnamon Roll. The Big Texas is the 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009 Automatic Merchandiser Readers' Choice Pastry of the Year. In 2011, Cloverhill Bakery introduced their Boston Crème Danish, in the New Products category of "Pastry".

raw:
Remove (education)

A Remove class in education is or was a group of students at an English public school, typically a year group: for example the year group between the fourth form and the fifth form. In the state maintained secondary schools the Remove class was a class for pupils who had already moved through Fifth Form (Year 11) but needed to resit the Ordinary Level ('O'level) GCE examination. The name originally described the pupils who had been removed (moved on an academic year) from the class described as the Shell. The latter name originates from Westminster School where junior pupils were taught in an alcove which resembled a shell. Over time usage evolved differently across individual schools. Examples at various schools:

At Ampleforth College, the 'remove' class (Year 11) is the year between second form (Year 10) and middle sixth (year 12). This is still applicable today. At Bancroft's School, the 'Removes' are pupils in their second year of secondary education (Year 8). At The King's School Canterbury, a 'Remove' denotes a pupil in their second year, between Shell and fifth form: in other words, a Year 10 pupil. This system is still used today. At Radley College, 'Remove' is the second year, coming between the Shell (first year) and Fifth (third year or GCSE year), thus corresponding to the modern year 10. At Marlborough College, the 'Remove' is the second year, coming after the Shell (first year) and the Hundred (third year or GCSE year). At Hurstpierpoint College, Remove is above Shell and before Fifth Form. In Shrewsbury School in the 1980s, the 'Remove' was the last year before the Sixth Form, in which students did their 'O' level exams. It was the equivalent of the modern Year 11. As of 2019 at Harrow School, the Remove is below the Fifth Form and above the Shell. At Mill Hill School, the 'Remove' is the year between 4th form and 5th form. It is the first year of the 2-year GCSE study period (the second being the 5th form). Remove is for students aged 14-15. At Eton College, the Remove was historically immediately above the Fourth Form and corresponded to "E Block" (Year 10). At Queen's Gate School, it is Year 7. At The King's School, Worcester, the Lower Remove and Upper Remove are between the Upper Fourth and Fifth Form, corresponding with years 9 and 10. At Haileybury, the 'Removes' are pupils in the first year of Upper School (Year 9). At Wilson's Grammar School, Camberwell South East London (now moved to Sutton and renamed Wilson's School) in the 60s the Remove or 5R was a class of individuals who needed to get more or better Ordinary Level GCE results for career purposes or to enter Advanced level GCE courses. The term was used to indicate pupils had been removed or held back from the usual expected progression so was referred to pejoratively or disrespectfully as a place for academic under-achievers.

In Frank Richards' Billy Bunter series, the Remove Class is the focus for all the stories, where the term is used as a synonym for Lower Fourth.

budget laptops

When you're hunting for a new laptop on a shoestring budget, the first thing to remember is that you don't have to sacrifice reliability for price. In the current market, manufacturers have learned that a large segment of buyers are looking for machines that can handle everyday tasks without breaking the bank. The sweet spot often lies between the $300 and $600 range, where you can find models that offer solid builds, decent screens, and enough processing power for web browsing, document editing, and light multimedia consumption.

One of the most important factors to check is the processor. While you won't see the latest flagship chips in the cheapest tier, many budget laptops now come equipped with entry-level Intel Core i3 or AMD Ryzen 3 processors that are more than capable for routine work. These CPUs provide a good balance of speed and power efficiency, allowing the laptop to run for several hours on a single charge. If your daily routine includes occasional video streaming or photo editing, look for a model with at least 4GB of RAM, though 8GB is becoming more common even at lower price points and can make a noticeable difference in multitasking smoothness.

Display quality can be a surprising differentiator in this price category. A full HD (1920x1080) screen is now standard on many affordable laptops, offering sharper text and clearer images than the older 1366x768 panels. However, keep an eye on the panel type: IPS displays provide better viewing angles and color accuracy, which can be a real plus if you spend long hours reading or working on graphics. If you're willing to compromise slightly on resolution, you might save a few dollars and still get a reliable, anti-glare screen that works well in bright environments.

Storage choices also matter, especially when you consider how quickly modern software can eat up space. Solid-state drives (SSDs) have become the norm even in budget machines, replacing the slower hard-disk drives that used to dominate the low-end market. A 256GB SSD gives you a responsive system and enough room for the operating system, essential apps, and a modest collection of files. Some models still pair a smaller SSD with a larger HDD for extra capacity, but this hybrid setup can add complexity and weight, so assess your needs before opting for it.

Battery life is often a make-or-break feature for students and remote workers, and many budget laptops now promise anywhere from six to ten hours of use on a single charge. Real-world performance will depend on screen brightness, background processes, and Wi-Fi usage, but a laptop that can comfortably last a typical workday without hunting for an outlet is a worthwhile investment. Look for devices that support fast charging, which can top up the battery in under an hour-a handy convenience when you're on the go.

Finally, don't overlook the importance of after-sales support and warranty coverage. Even the most inexpensive laptops can encounter hardware glitches, and a solid warranty can save you from unexpected repair costs. Brands that offer at least a one-year warranty, preferably with easy service options, give you peace of mind that your purchase is protected. By focusing on these core aspects-processor, display, memory, storage, battery, and support-you can find a budget laptop that feels far more capable than its price tag suggests, making it a reliable companion for work, study, or casual entertainment.

To: All field personnel and expedition planners 
From: Mountain Operations Office 
Date: 8 October 2026 
Subject: Mountain Weather - Risks, Forecasting, and Safety Measures

Mountain weather is notoriously variable, changing rapidly with altitude, topography, and time of day. Even on a clear morning, a sudden shift in wind direction can bring a wall of cold air down a ridge, dropping temperatures by ten degrees within minutes. This volatility is driven by the interaction of large-scale atmospheric patterns with the local terrain, which can force air to rise, condense, and precipitate unexpectedly. Understanding these dynamics is essential for any activity above 2,500 metres, where the margin between safe exposure and hypothermia narrows considerably.

Forecasts for mountainous regions should always be treated as a baseline, not a guarantee. While modern numerical models incorporate high-resolution data, they often underestimate localized convection and the formation of low-level wind shears. We therefore require that all teams consult at least three independent sources - a national meteorological service, a regional mountain weather service, and any available on-site automated weather stations - before departure. The latest observations, especially wind speed and direction at key passes, must be compared with the model output to identify discrepancies that could signal a rapid change.

When planning ascents, it is prudent to schedule the most exposed sections during the early morning hours, when thermal inversions are typically strongest and wind speeds are at their lowest. Afternoon heating can destabilize the atmosphere, increasing the likelihood of thunderstorms, hail, or sudden downdrafts. In addition, solar radiation can melt snowpack on sun-facing slopes, creating hazardous wet snow conditions that may trigger avalanches later in the day. All itineraries should therefore incorporate a buffer period for unexpected weather delays, and a clear abort criteria based on wind exceeding 25 km h-1 or visibility falling below 200 m.

Equipment selection must reflect the possibility of rapid weather deterioration. Layered clothing systems with moisture-wicking bases, insulated mid-layers, and wind-proof outer shells provide the flexibility to adapt to shifting conditions. Headlamps with high lumen output are essential, as storms can plunge the environment into darkness even during daylight. Portable weather radios tuned to local frequencies allow teams to receive real-time updates, while personal GPS devices with topographic maps aid navigation when fog or precipitation obscures landmarks.

All personnel are required to complete the Mountain Weather Awareness module in the training portal before participating in any high-altitude operation. The module covers interpretation of forecast charts, identification of dangerous weather signs, and emergency response procedures for hypothermia, lightning strikes, and sudden snow slides. Documentation of the training completion must be attached to the expedition risk assessment form. Non-compliance will result in removal from the activity roster.

In summary, mountain weather demands vigilant monitoring, flexible planning, and appropriate gear. By integrating multiple forecast sources, respecting the diurnal weather cycle, and maintaining readiness for rapid condition changes, we can mitigate the inherent risks and ensure the safety of all participants. Please disseminate this notice to all relevant units and incorporate its guidance into upcoming operation briefings.

Frank Young (rugby, born c. 1885)

Frank 'Bucket' H. Young (1885 - 1941) was a Welsh rugby union, and professional rugby league footballer who played in the 1900s and 1910s. He played representative level rugby union (RU) for Glamorgan, and at club level for Cardiff RFC, London Welsh RFC and Bristol Rugby, and representative level rugby league (RL) for Great Britain and Wales, and at club level for Leeds, as a fullback.

Young was a promising player for Cardiff, playing in the reserves before being promoted to the senior team. Young only played one senior season, and may have achieved more but was kept out of the squad by Bert Winfield, one of the greatest Welsh kickers of all time. Young played several games for London Welsh and Bristol before switching to rugby league. Robert Michaelis

Robert Armand René Michaelis (22 December 1878 - 29 August 1965) was a French-born actor and singer who worked in musical theatre, mainly in England, but he also made appearances on Broadway. By 1901, Michaelis and his parents had settled in Hampstead, and he was married there in 1913. He was naturalized as a British subject in 1914. After retiring from the stage, he became a manager, and during the Second World War was an air raid warden, by then having made his home in the west of England.

Born in 1878, according to different sources in Saint Petersburg or Paris, Michaelis was the son of Guilllaume Paul Hermann Michaelis and Marie Leonie Heloise Michaelis. His mother was French, and his father was born a German but naturalized as French. He was educated in London and Paris and trained as a singer in Vienna with Felice Bottelli. At the time of the 1901 census, Michaelis was living in Latchmere, Battersea, with his parents, Herman Michaelis, a schoolmaster, aged fifty, and Marie, aged 45, and his occupation was stated as actor. An early appearance in musical theatre came in 1907, when Michaelis sang in Gustave Kerker's The White Hen at the Casino Theatre, New York, in a run lasting three months. In 1908, he took over the part of Prince Danilo in The Merry Widow for the last four months of its run at Daly's Theatre, then was cast as Freddy Fairfax in The Dollar Princess (1909), becoming a favourite at Daly's, and playing a leading role in The Marriage Market (1911). In 1912, he sang the title role in an English production of Franz Lehár's operetta The Count of Luxembourg, as one of the five principals, together with Phyllis Le Grand, Eric Thorne, Lauri de Frece, and Daisy Burrell, who were collectively described by the Musical News as "all consummate artists in their own style". Soon after the beginning of the First World War, Michaelis, then living at 8 Eton Villas, South Hampstead, was naturalized as a British subject, declaring the names of his parents and his place of birth as Paris. In 1920, Michaelis appeared in the silent film The Little Welsh Girl, then for more than a year, from 1920 to 1921, he sang the part of Beaudon in a London production of Irene at the Empire Theatre which had a run of 399 performances. When he was granted probate on his mother's estate in 1933, Michaelis was described as a "manager". In October 1939, Michaelis was living at Wychwood, Tickenham, Somerset, and soon after the outbreak of the Second World War was registered as an air raid warden and retired actor. In his Nights of Gladness (1956), English theatre historian Walter MacQueen-Pope, known as "Popie", called Michaelis "one of the very best performers Daly's ever had".

Michaelis's father, Herman Michaelis, died at St Pancras in 1912. In 1913, at Hampstead, Michaelis married Phyllis Le Grand, the actress with whom he had starred in The Count of Luxembourg the year before. Their daughter Rosemary Evelyn Helene was born in March 1914. She later became a nurse and radiographer. Michaelis's mother, Marie, died in 1933, aged 78. Her address was 8, Eton Villas, South Hampstead, and she left an estate valued at £2,293. In 1940, Rosemary Michaelis married John A. Parsons in Somerset. Three grandchildren were born between 1943 and 1949. Michaelis died on 29 August 1965 at the Bristol Royal Infirmary, when his address was given as "Summerlands Nailsea", and he left an estate valued for probate at £7,051. His widow, Phyllis, survived him until 15 May 1981.

The Central Library reminds all patrons that overdue materials will incur fines if not returned by the due date stamped on your checkout receipt. Standard loan periods for fiction and non-fiction items are twenty-one days, while media and special collections may have shorter windows. Please check your specific item type on the borrower's card or online account to avoid unnecessary penalties.

Automation of processing has made returns more convenient, but accuracy remains the patron's responsibility. When using the evening or weekend return slots, drop items into the designated bins rather than leaving them on the floor. These slots are inspected daily, and in rare cases of machine malfunction, items may be delayed in reprocessing. Patrons should verify their status online the next morning to confirm the return was registered.

Fines for overdue books are currently set at fifty cents per day for standard items. Once a fine exceeds ten dollars, the patron's account will be suspended until the balance is cleared. This policy ensures fair access for the entire community and prevents resource hoarding. Payment can be made online, at the service desk, or via our mobile app.

Lost or damaged items must be reported to head librarian staff immediately. If a book is found later in a salvageable condition, half the replacement fee may be credited, provided the item was not heavily worn. Replacement costs reflect current market prices plus binding and processing fees. Unreturned items that are declared lost after eighty days automatically generate a final invoice.

For questions regarding due dates or fine reductions, contact the circulation desk during opening hours. First-time offenders with valid extenuating circumstances may request a one-time fine waiver, subject to staff review. We appreciate your cooperation in maintaining our shared collection and ensuring timely access for all readers.

Dr. Elena Rostova from the Institute for Theoretical Physics will lead the presentation. She is a leading expert in quantum entanglement applications and has published extensively on the subject. Her work focuses on how quantum systems can essentially render unauthorized interception impossible.

The seminar is scheduled for Thursday, November 14th, at 2:00 PM in Auditorium B on the main campus. Doors will open at 1:30 PM to allow attendees time to settle and collect any printed materials. Refreshments will be available both before and after the main lecture period.

Participants are strongly encouraged to reserve their spot in advance via the departmental online portal. Capacity is limited to one hundred fifty individuals due to the size of the lecture hall. Early registration ensures a seat and guarantees access to the supplementary reading packet.

We welcome students, faculty, and industry partners interested in cybersecurity. Questions regarding technical requirements or accessibility needs should be directed to the department secretary by the end of next week. Your attendance supports our ongoing efforts to foster interdisciplinary dialogue in emerging technologies.

To maintain consistency in flavor and temperature across all departments, this memo outlines the mandatory procedure for preparing instant and drip coffee in the main breakroom. These guidelines are effective immediately and apply to all staff members, contractors, and visitors using the facility. Adherence to these steps ensures that every employee has access to a high-quality beverage while preserving the longevity of our shared equipment. Please read this overview carefully before operating the machines to prevent common errors that lead to waste or mechanical failure.

The preparation of drip coffee begins with inspecting the reservoir to ensure it is filled with fresh, cold water filtered through the house system. Never use water that has been sitting in the reservoir for more than twenty-four hours, as stagnant water develops an off-putting taste and accelerates the buildup of mineral deposits. Fill the reservoir to the exact line corresponding to the number of cups required; overfilling causes overflow during the brewing cycle, while underfilling results in a weaker concentration than intended. Ensure the lid is securely snapped into place before activating the machine, as the internal pressure mechanism relies on a tight seal to boil the water efficiently and extract the full potential of the grounds.

Grinding control is paramount for achieving the optimal extraction balance. For the standard drip machine, use a medium grind size that resembles sand; a finer grind will clog the paper filter and release bitter oils, whereas a coarse grind results in weak, sour liquid. Always measure one level scoop of beans per six-ounce cup of water, adjusting slightly for individual preference regarding strength. Place a clean, white paper filter into the basket, ensuring the edges seat properly against the rim to prevent any grounds from bypassing the filtration system. Pour the grounds evenly across the surface of the filter, avoiding piles that create uneven flow channels during the brew.

Operative timing is another critical variable that affects the final pour. The machine must be turned on only when the next batch is ready to be served to the public or staff. Coffee left on the warming plate for longer than four hours will develop a burnt, acrid profile due to continuous exposure to high heat. If a pot is not finished within four hours, discard the remaining liquid and clean the carafe immediately. Do not attempt to reheat stale coffee in the microwave or by running hot water over it, as these methods do not restore flavor and only introduce metallic tastes into the shared supply.

Maintenance schedules are strictly enforced to keep the system hygienic and functional. After each use, remove the carafe and filter basket, dispose of the used grounds in the designated compost bin, and rinse the components with warm soapy water. Wipe down the exterior surfaces and the warming tray with a damp cloth to remove any spills or steam accumulation. Weekly, the descaling solution must be run through the machine without coffee grounds to dissolve calcium buildup that impedes water flow and reduces heating efficiency. Failure to participate in this upkeep cycle will result in a formal warning and the temporary revocation of breakroom access privileges.

insurance claim steps

When a loss occurs, the first thing to do is stay calm and gather the basic facts. Knowing the date, time, and cause of the incident helps you frame the story you will later share with the insurer. A clear timeline also reduces the chance of miscommunication later in the process.

Next, secure any immediate safety concerns and prevent further damage. If it's a car accident, move vehicles out of traffic if possible; for a home fire, turn off utilities to stop the spread. Take photos or videos of the scene as soon as you can, because visual evidence is often the most persuasive proof of what happened.

After you've made the area safe, start collecting documentation. This includes police or fire reports, medical records, receipts for damaged items, and any correspondence with third parties involved. Organize these files chronologically and keep copies, as insurers frequently request originals or certified copies for verification.

When you feel prepared, contact your insurance company and open a claim, either through their website, app, or phone line. Provide the representative with the information you've gathered, and ask for a claim number to track progress. Throughout the evaluation, respond promptly to any requests for additional details, and keep a log of every phone call, email, and note taken.

Finally, review the settlement offer carefully before accepting it. If the amount seems low, you have the right to negotiate or request a re-assessment, often with the help of an adjuster or independent appraiser. Once you agree, sign the necessary paperwork, and keep the final agreement for future reference. Following these steps can streamline the claim journey and help you recover more smoothly.

Subject: Invitation to the Riverside Community Cycling Ride - Saturday, June 15
Dear Alex,
I hope this message finds you well and enjoying the early summer weather. I'm writing to share details about the upcoming Riverside Community Cycling Ride, a family-friendly event organized by the local cycling club. The ride will start at 8:30 a.m. on Saturday, June 15, and will follow a scenic 25-kilometer loop along the river trail, returning to the park pavilion where we'll wrap up with refreshments.
The route has been carefully planned to accommodate riders of all skill levels. There are three optional loops: a gentle 10-kilometer stretch for beginners, a moderate 18-kilometer circuit for intermediate cyclists, and the full 25-kilometer loop for those looking for a challenge. All participants will receive a printed map and a safety briefing before we set off. Helmets are mandatory, and we'll have a small first-aid station at the start point in case anyone needs assistance.
We're also excited to announce that local businesses will be offering special promotions for participants. A nearby café will provide a complimentary coffee and a snack voucher for the first 50 riders, and a bike shop will be on hand to offer free tune-ups and discounted accessories. If you'd like to bring a guest, please let us know so we can arrange an extra set of bib numbers and a spot on the registration list.
To register, simply click the link in the email we sent last week, or reply to this message with your name, the loop you plan to ride, and any dietary restrictions for the post-ride refreshments. The deadline for registration is Friday, June 7, after which we'll finalize the participant roster and send out a final itinerary.
Thank you for considering joining us for what promises to be a fun, safe, and community-spirit-filled ride. I look forward to seeing you on the trail and sharing a great morning together.
Warm regards,
Jordan Patel
Event Coordinator, Riverside Cycling Club
j.patel@riversidebike.org
(555) 842-0197

Amman City Airport

Amman City Airport (IATA: ADJ, ICAO: OJAM) (Arabic: مطار مدينة عمّان, romanized: Maṭār Madina ʿAmmān), is located in Marka district, Jordan, some 5 kilometres (3.1 mi; 2.7 NM) northeast of the capital Amman's city centre. During World War I, an airstrip was established near Amman in 1915 for use by German airplanes, then an ally of the ruling Ottoman Empire. Following Ottoman defeat and the establishment of the Emirate of Transjordan in 1921, the British used the airstrip as a base for their squadrons. In 1950, the airstrip was developed as a joint military-civilian airport, which became Jordan's main airport until the opening of Queen Alia International Airport in 1983. In 2013, following the inauguration of QAIA's new terminals, ACA was closed to civilian flights, as per the government's exclusivity agreement with QAIA's developers. In 2025, ACA reopened after the exclusivity clause's expiration, now aiming to serve as a complimentary secondary airport to QAIA for medium-sized aircraft including low-cost carriers. ACA is also an aviation education and training hub and hosts air freight operations. Ezechiel N'Douassel

Ezechiel Aliadjim N'Douassel (Arabic: إيزيكييل عليادجيم ندواسيل; born 22 April 1988), nicknamed King Eze, is a Chadian professional footballer who plays a striker for Championship club PSGC Ciamis and the Chad national team.

N'Douassel began his career in 2006 at local side Tourbillon before moving to Algeria in 2007 to play for MC Oran and he joined USM Blida.

In his debut for USM Blida, Ndouassel scored a brace against MC El Eulma, with goals in the 86th and 90th minute to give his team a 2-1 win. He would end the season with five goals in fifteen appearances. During his time at USM Blida, N'Douassel was linked with a number of European clubs including Olympique de Marseille, Arsenal, Monaco and Mallorca. On July 20, 2009, it was announced that Ndouassel joined Belgian club FCV Dender on a free transfer and signed a 3-year contract worth €200,000 after impressing on trial in friendlies against Roeselare and Hamme. However, the move was not finalized and Ndouassel was forced to return to USM Blida shortly after because he was still under contract with the club.

On January 9, 2011, Ndouassel signed a 4-year contract with Tunisian side Club Africain. For the 2011 CAF Confederation Cup his team made it second place losing to Maghreb de Fès by penalties. During the 2012 CAF Confederation Cup he scored a Hattrick for Africain making them reach the fourth round before they got eliminated in the playoffs. In July 2014, Ndouassel was reported to have moved to Paris FC on loan, with an option to buy. However this move fell through due to financial constraints on the French club, and with Club African unwilling to include him in their squad, left Ndouassel looking for a new club.

On 4 September 2016 he signed a 3-year contract with Ironi Kiryat Shmona. In January 2017 he left the club and joined Hapoel Tel Aviv until the end of the 2016-17 Israeli Premier League season. After playing five matches, he was released in March 2017, following behaviour issues.

On 7 August 2017, he signed a half year contract with Persib Bandung and retained for the following season. He made his league debut in a 0-0 against Arema on 12 August 2017 as a substitute for Tantan in the 45th minute. On 20 August 2017, N'Douassel scored his first league goal for Persib against Gresik United as his team won 6-0.

He was also the top scorer for Persib in 2018 season with 17 goals, and retained by the club until 2020. He scored quattrick in a match against PSM Makassar on 22 December 2019.

N'Douassel made his debut for Bhayangkara, coming on as a substitute for Herman Dzumafo, in a pre-season cup game against Cambodian Premier League club Visakha as his team won 1-0. N'Douassel scored his first goal for Bhayangkara in the same pre-season cup against Malaysia Super League club Petaling Jaya City, scoring a goal in the 55th-minute, which saw Bhayangkara crowned as the champion. On 29 February 2020, N'Douassel made his first league debut for Bhayangkara against Persiraja Banda Aceh as his team drew 0-0. On 31 March 2020 N'Douassel scored his first league goal for Bhayangkara against Persija Jakarta as his team drew 2-2.

Rukainiai

Rukainiai (Lithuanian: Rukainiai; Polish: Rukojnie) is a village in the Vilnius District Municipality, Lithuania, located 12 km east of Vilnius city municipality, the Lithuanian capital, and 16 km from the border with Belarus. According to the 2021 census, Rukainiai had a population of 662, a decrease from 770 in 2011 and from 865 in 1989.

.

Rukainiai is known from 1440 when Grand Duke Sigismund Kęstutaitis donated the village to the Archdiocese of Vilnius. Bishop Paweł Holszański, a member of the Lithuanian princely Olshanski family, sponsored the construction of a wooden church in 1538. In the 18th century, there was a parochial school in Rukainiai. The church was destroyed during the French invasion of Russia in 1812. It was replaced by a Romantic style stone church built in 1823, the Church of St. Michael the Archangel. Paweł Ksawery Brzostowski, famous as the founder of the Republic of Paulava, served as a priest in the newly built church.

For several years there was also a Russian Orthodox Church in the town, the Church of the Protection of the Holy Virgin, which was built in 1868 but destroyed in 1918. Rukainiai is famous for its Christmas and Užgavėnės traditions.

airline baggage rules

Navigating the labyrinth of airline baggage rules can be one of the most stressful parts of planning a trip. What seemed like a simple decision about how much to pack quickly turns into a complex calculation of kilograms, linear inches, and specific airline policies. The first step to avoiding a frantic counter interaction at the airport is understanding that these regulations are not universal. Each carrier operates under its own distinct framework, meaning the limits that apply on a domestic flight within a single country can differ drastically from those enforced on an international route. Before packing a single item, travelers must read the specific terms and conditions associated with their ticket class, as a basic economy fare often comes with significantly stricter restrictions than a business class reservation.

The difference between carry-on and checked luggage is where most confusion arises. Carry-on bags are intended for essential items you want to keep close to you during the flight, such as electronics, medications, or entertainment devices. Most major airlines allow one personal item, like a small purse or laptop bag, plus one main carry-on. Dimensions for standard carry-ons usually hover around 22 by 14 by 9 inches, though some airlines are increasingly enforcing stricter limits on overhead bin access, particularly during peak travel seasons where space is at a premium. It is worth noting that some budget carriers may not include any free carry-on allowance at all, charging a fee if you wish to bring a bag into the cabin rather than checking it under the plane.

When it comes to checked baggage, the focus shifts primarily to weight and total quantity. Legacy carriers in the United States typically include two free checked bags for each passenger on domestic flights, whereas international itineraries often include only one. Weight limits are generally capped at fifty pounds per bag in the US, but this can double to seventy pounds on many international connections. However, this is where liability becomes a concern. Airlines strongly advise against checking heavy bags, as back and shoulder injuries sustained while lifting excess weight onto official scales are notorious. There is also a hard limit, often around one hundred and fifty pounds or seventy kilograms, beyond which a bag is considered overweight and can incur substantial penalties starting around one hundred dollars per bag.

Special categories of luggage require additional planning and often carry extra fees. Sporting equipment such as skis, golf clubs, or hockey sticks, along with musical instruments, fall under special baggage provisions. These items frequently exceed standard dimension or weight guidelines, requiring travelers to purchase specific add-ons in advance. Similarly, fragile or valuable items are high-risk. While airlines do guarantee lost luggage, the compensation caps are surprisingly low, rarely exceeding six hundred dollars in the US for checked items regardless of the actual value. Traveler insurance or a comprehensive credit card benefit is the only reliable safety net for expensive electronics or jewelry that you absolutely must check.

Finally, it is crucial to respect security regulations for carry-on items. Liquids, gels, and aerosols are strictly limited to containers of 3.4 ounces or 100 milliliters, and all must fit into a single, clear, quart-sized bag. Larger water bottles must be opened and emptied before the security checkpoint. Power banks and spare lithium batteries must always be kept in carry-on luggage and are strictly prohibited in checked suitcases due to fire hazards. By staying informed on these specific details and double-checking the unique policies of your chosen airline on the day of travel, you can bypass the common pitfalls that turn a routine airport visit into a headache.

Rhoshii Wells

Rhoshii Wells (December 30, 1976 - August 11, 2008) was an American boxer, who won the bronze medal in the Middleweight Division at the 1996 Summer Olympics. He was born in Austin, Texas.

Nicknamed "The Great One", Wells began his professional career in 1997, and got off to a 17-0-2 start in the Light Middleweight division, setting up a shot at WBA Light Middleweight Title holder Alejandro Garcia in 2003. He was ahead on the scorecards before Garcia stopped him in the 11th round. In 2005, Wells had the opportunity for a rematch with Garcia but was defeated via TKO in the 9th round. He attempted a comeback on the 3rd season of the boxing reality TV series, The Contender on ESPN, but was eliminated before the competition began.

Rhoshii Wells was shot and killed in Las Vegas, Nevada on August 11, 2008. Police arrested 26-year-old Roger Randolph, who claimed that he shot Wells in self-defense after Wells punched him and robbed him of $100. The District Attorney stated that they would seek the death penalty against Randolph. In May 2012, Randolph was sentenced to 20 years to life for murder with a deadly weapon, plus one to 12 years for discharging weapon where a person might be endangered.

Welcome to the Volunteer Onboarding Program. This document outlines the steps we take to integrate new volunteers into our organization, ensuring they feel prepared, informed, and valued from the moment they express interest.

Before your first shift, you will receive an introductory email containing a welcome packet, a schedule of upcoming training sessions, and a link to our online volunteer portal. Please review the materials and complete the required background check within five days.

Your orientation day begins in the main conference room, where you will meet the Volunteer Coordinator and fellow newcomers. The session includes a history of the organization, an overview of current projects, and a walkthrough of safety procedures.

Following orientation, you will be assigned a mentor who will accompany you during your first activity and answer any questions that arise. Training modules are offered monthly and cover topics such as communication skills, data privacy, and conflict resolution.

All volunteers are expected to adhere to the code of conduct, maintain punctuality, and report any incidents to the supervision team. Attendance is tracked through the portal, and volunteers who miss three scheduled shifts may be asked to reassess their commitment.

If you have any questions during the onboarding process, please contact the Volunteer Services Office at (555) 123-4567 or email volunteers@ourorg.org. We look forward to working together and making a positive impact in our community.

The Changzhou Metro is a rapid transit system in Changzhou, Jiangsu province, China. The system started operation on 21 September 2019, with the opening of its first line, Line 1, becoming the 35th city in China with a subway in mainland China. The Changzhou Metro currently has Line 1 and Line 2 in operation, while Line 5 and Line 6 are under construction. Announcements are made in Mandarin and English.

Line 1 started operation on 21 September 2019. Construction for Line 1 began on 28 October 2014. The first phase runs from Forest Park (森林公园) in the north to Nanxiashu (南夏墅) in the south. It is 34.24 kilometres (21.28 mi) in length with 29 stations, including 27 underground and 2 elevated. The line will be extended North for 3.5 km and South for 3.2 km. In its first year of operation, the highest passenger flow in a single day was 243,000 on October 2 and total ridership in 2019 was 10.3 million.

Construction for Line 2 began on 13 February 2017. It is 19.79 kilometres (12.30 mi) in length with 15 stations, from Qingfeng Park to Wuyi Lu. It was opened on 28 June 2021.

Construction of a two-station pilot section for Line 5 at the Lanyuewan terminal commenced in October 2023. The full-scale construction of Line 5 is scheduled to begin in 2024, with an anticipated completion date set for 2028.

According to the "Changzhou Urban Rail Transit Construction Plan (2011~2018)", the urban rail transit network of Changzhou City is planned to consist of 6 lines by 2050.

The Changzhou Metro system operates with a base fare of 2 yuan, covering the initial 5 kilometers, and subsequent price increments at intervals of 5, 7 and 9 kilometers, with each step adding 1 yuan to the fare. Specifically, fares are structured as follows: 2 yuan for journeys up to 5 kilometers, 3 yuan for trips spanning 5-10 kilometers, 4 yuan for distances of 10-15 kilometers, 5 yuan for 15-22 kilometers, 6 yuan for 22-29 kilometers, and a progressive increase of 1 yuan for every additional 9 kilometers beyond 29 kilometers.

The Changzhou Metro system operates with a base fare of 2 yuan, covering the initial 5 kilometers, and subsequent price increments at intervals of 5, 7 and 9 kilometers, with each step adding 1 yuan to the fare. Specifically, fares are structured as follows: 2 yuan for journeys up to 5 kilometers, 3 yuan for trips spanning 5-10 kilometers, 4 yuan for distances of 10-15 kilometers, 5 yuan for 15-22 kilometers, 6 yuan for 22-29 kilometers, and a progressive increase of 1 yuan for every additional 9 kilometers beyond 29 kilometers.

Subject: Thoughts on establishing a consistent bedtime for Eli
Hi Sarah,
I hope you are having a good week. I wanted to reach out and share a few things we have been experimenting with regarding Eli's sleep routine. It has been a bit rocky lately, as you might have guessed, but we finally started seeing some positive shifts this week. The main issue we faced was that his daytime naps were becoming increasingly unpredictable, which threw off his entire evening schedule. We were struggling with overtiredness, where he would spiral into a fit right before bedtime because he was simply too exhausted to soothe himself.
We decided to stick to a very specific wake window. I started tracking his awake times more closely using a simple notes app on my phone. It turned out that we were leaving him in that window for too long. By shortening the final nap of the day, we were able to align his bedtime with his natural sleep pressure peak. The goal now is to have him in his crib by 6:30 PM most nights. It still feels early to us, but the data suggests it is exactly what he needs to maintain a reasonable number of daytime sleep cycles.
The pre-bed routine has become our anchor, though I want to emphasize that consistency is more important than the specific activities. We keep the lights dim and the noise level low about twenty minutes before bed. We usually start with a warm bath, followed by a bottle or nursing session, and then singing our two favorite lullabies. I tried adding a new book last week, but Eli kept staring around the room instead of settling, so we reverted to the trusted pair of stories. Predictability seems to be the key signal that sleep is approaching, and any deviation causes friction.
Another adjustment we made was regarding the room environment. We invested in a decent white noise machine and set it to a steady, low-level ocean wave sound. We also warmed up the room slightly in the evening. I noticed that he was fussy when the temperature dropped after sunset, and keeping the humidity at a comfortable level helped keep his skin from getting dry. It is a small physical comfort, but removing that source of discomfort allowed him to relax into the crib without the immediate protest he used to give.
We are not there yet, and there will likely still be nights where he wakes up and needs attention. However, the frequency of night wakings has dropped significantly since we tightened up the schedule. My main takeaway is that a rigid routine does not mean it has to be stressful for the parents. It is just about creating a sequence of signals that the baby can anticipate. I would love to hear if you have tried any of these specific timing adjustments with your little one, or if you had a different approach that worked for your family.
Warm regards,
Jamie

InterContinental Paris Le Grand Hotel

Le Grand Hôtel was built by the wealthy brothers Isaac & Émile Pereire and designed by Alfred Armand, who had previously designed the nearby Grand Hôtel du Louvre for them. Construction began in April 1861; the hotel was inaugurated on 5 May 1862 by Empress Eugenie, wife of Napoleon III, before officially opening on 30 June 1862. The hotel's construction was part of the complete reconstruction of Paris supervised by Baron Haussmann at the time and it was built in the prescribed style, with a mansard roof. Filling an entire triangular city block, the hotel boasted 800 rooms on four floors for guests, with another whole floor for their servants.

The hotel has hosted royalty throughout its long history, including Tsar Nicholas and Tsarina Alexandra, King Edward VII of England and Queen Rania of Jordan. Victor Hugo hosted parties at the Le Grand Hotel and Émile Zola used the hotel for the setting of the death of his tragic character Nana. In 1869, James Gordon Bennett Jr., who would soon become publisher of the Paris Herald, forerunner of the International Herald Tribune, met with Henry Morton Stanley in the hotel's Imperial Suite to convince him to make his famous journey to Africa in search of David Livingstone. Creditors of the Péreire brothers seized the hotel in 1878, and in 1887, André Million formed Société du Grand Hôtel to manage Le Grand Hotel, along with the nearby Hotel Meurice and later the Hotel Prince de Galles. The Italian CIGA Hotels chain acquired the three hotels in 1972. CIGA sold the hotels in 1978 for $25 million to Limnico, a Liberia-based subsidiary of Roger Tamraz's First Arabian Corporation. Limnico resold the properties for $55 million just a year later, in October 1979, to Maxwell Joseph's UK-based Grand Metropolitan Hotels. Grand Metropolitan acquired the Inter-Continental Hotels chain in 1981, and placed Le Grand Hotel under their management. The hotel was renovated between 1985 and 1990 by noted French designer Pierre-Yves Rochon. In 1986, the hotel was renamed Le Grand Hotel Inter-Continental Paris. The hotel closed in December 2001 for another major renovation. Inter-Continental Hotels was reorganised as InterContinental Hotels Group while the hotel was closed. It reopened on 5 April 2003, with its name modified slightly, as InterContinental Paris Le Grand Hotel. InterContinental sold the hotel to Qatar-based Constellation Hotels in 2014 for €330 million, although InterContinental continues to manage the property.

Jean-Luc Godard filmed large portions of his 1965 sci-fi film Alphaville in the hotel, using its driveway, lobby, elevators, hallways and winter garden. Roman Polanski set much of his 1988 film Frantic, starring Harrison Ford, at the hotel. Most interiors were filmed on soundstages, but numerous exterior scenes were filmed outside the hotel.

InterContinental Paris Le Grand Hotel
Le Grand Hôtel was built by the wealthy brothers Isaac & Émile Pereire and designed by Alfred Armand, who had previously designed the nearby Grand Hôtel du Louvre for them. Construction began in April 1861; the hotel was inaugurated on 5 May 1862 by Empress Eugenie, wife of Napoleon III, before officially opening on 30 June 1862. The hotel's construction was part of the complete reconstruction of Paris supervised by Baron Haussmann at the time and it was built in the prescribed style, with a mansard roof. Filling an entire triangular city block, the hotel boasted 800 rooms on four floors for guests, with another whole floor for their servants.
The hotel has hosted royalty throughout its long history, including Tsar Nicholas and Tsarina Alexandra, King Edward VII of England and Queen Rania of Jordan. Victor Hugo hosted parties at the Le Grand Hotel and Émile Zola used the hotel for the setting of the death of his tragic character Nana. In 1869, James Gordon Bennett Jr., who would soon become publisher of the Paris Herald, forerunner of the International Herald Tribune, met with Henry Morton Stanley in the hotel's Imperial Suite to convince him to make his famous journey to Africa in search of David Livingstone. Creditors of the Péreire brothers seized the hotel in 1878, and in 1887, André Million formed Société du Grand Hôtel to manage Le Grand Hotel, along with the nearby Hotel Meurice and later the Hotel Prince de Galles. The Italian CIGA Hotels chain acquired the three hotels in 1972. CIGA sold the hotels in 1978 for $25 million to Limnico, a Liberia-based subsidiary of Roger Tamraz's First Arabian Corporation. Limnico resold the properties for $55 million just a year later, in October 1979, to Maxwell Joseph's UK-based Grand Metropolitan Hotels. Grand Metropolitan acquired the Inter-Continental Hotels chain in 1981, and placed Le Grand Hotel under their management. The hotel was renovated between 1985 and 1990 by noted French designer Pierre-Yves Rochon. In 1986, the hotel was renamed Le Grand Hotel Inter-Continental Paris. The hotel closed in December 2001 for another major renovation. Inter-Continental Hotels was reorganised as InterContinental Hotels Group while the hotel was closed. It reopened on 5 April 2003, with its name modified slightly, as InterContinental Paris Le Grand Hotel. raw:
language learning apps

The smartphone has fundamentally altered how we approach foreign language acquisition. A decade ago, fluency required a physical stack of grammar books, a dedicated tutor, or a plane ticket to the target country. Today, a pocket-sized device serves as a gatekeeper to endless vocabulary, pronunciation guides, and cultural context. For many, the journey begins in the quiet moments of a commute or a lunch break, where fifteen minutes of attention can yield tangible progress. The sheer accessibility of these tools has democratized education, allowing anyone with an internet connection to start speaking a second language at their own pace, free from the intimidation of a classroom setting.

Different applications cater to distinct learning styles, recognizing that a one-size-fits-all approach rarely works. Gamified platforms tend to hook users through streaks, leaderboards, and bright, engaging interfaces. They excel at building a consistent habit, making the daily practice feel less like a chore and more like a video game. In contrast, other apps focus heavily on speech recognition and live conversation with native speakers. These tools prioritize practical communication over rote memorization, forcing users to produce language rather than just select it from multiple-choice options. The key to success often lies in choosing an app that aligns with your specific goals, whether that is passing a college exam or simply ordering coffee in a foreign city.

However, reliance on software alone has its limitations. Critics frequently point out the danger of creating an "illusion of proficiency." Users may score highly on placement tests within the app but struggle when faced with the unpredictable, messy flow of a real conversation. Slang, regional dialects, and contextual nuance are often underrepresented in algorithmic curricula. To overcome this, many successful language learners treat their app as a supplementary tool rather than a comprehensive course. They integrate the software with other resources, such as podcasts, news articles, or social media, to expose themselves to authentic, unstructured content that mirrors real-world usage.

Consistency remains the most critical factor in any language learning regimen, and apps are uniquely positioned to foster this habit. The psychological impact of a broken streak is powerful, creating a gentle sense of urgency that keeps learners returning daily. Yet, it is important to balance this with patience. Language acquisition is a marathon, not a sprint. There will be periods of rapid improvement followed by plateaus where progress feels stalled. Recognizing these phases as normal is essential to maintaining motivation. The apps provide the scaffolding, but the internal drive to connect with other cultures must remain the primary engine of the process.

As artificial intelligence continues to advance, these applications are becoming increasingly sophisticated. Personalized feedback loops can now identify specific weak areas, such as verb conjugation or listening comprehension, and tailor subsequent lessons accordingly. The future of language learning likely involves a hybrid model where digital tools handle the repetitive drills, freeing up human time for complex cultural exchange. Whether you are a casual hobbyist or a dedicated student, the landscape has never been more inviting. The barrier to entry is lower than ever before, and the only cost is the willingness to show up every day, tap the screen, and keep trying, even when the grammar rules feel particularly stubborn.

raw:
TXTMob

TXTmob is a service, similar to electronic mailing lists and predecessor to Twitter, that lets users share mobile phone SMS text messages with both friends and total strangers. Users can sign up to send and receive messages to and from various groups, which are organized around a range of different topics.

TXTMob was first developed by the Institute for Applied Autonomy for protesters at the 2004 Democratic National Convention in Boston and the 2004 Republican National Convention in New York City (see 2004 Republican National Convention protest activity). Tad Hirsch, a researcher in the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's Smart Cities Group and Computing Culture Research Group, continues to offer TXTmob cleaned up, packaged and released under the GPL via SourceForge. Tad Hirsch, creator of TXTMob, was the subject of a subpoena by the City of New York in connection with several lawsuits against the City that allege police misconduct during the 2004 Republican National Convention.

The TXTMob service will forward messages received to all members of a particular group as they are received. In an unmoderated group, any group member can send a text message to be received by all other members of that group. Groups can also be moderated, in which case the group is set up as a sort of announcement-only group, which is used primarily as a one-way conduit of information and text messages can only be sent by selected people (often just that group's particular administrator).

A public group is one which any TXTMob member may join. Membership in a private group is limited by the group's administrators. When an individual first attempts to join a private group, his or her membership will be listed as "pending." Once an administrator of the group upgrades their membership, they will be able to receive messages, and depending on if the group is moderated or not, send messages. Secret groups are similar to private groups in that membership is restricted by the group's administrators. However, membership in secret groups is by invitation only; secret groups do not appear in group directories and uninvited members are unable to sign up for "pending memberships".

raw:
moving checklist

Moving is often a stressful undertaking, but with smart planning, it can be much smoother. A comprehensive moving checklist acts as your essential guide, keeping you organized every step of the way. It transforms a potentially chaotic event into a manageable transition to your new home.

Begin planning eight weeks out by thoroughly decluttering. Decide what to keep, donate, or discard from each room. This is also the ideal time to book your moving company or rental truck. Start creating a detailed inventory of your belongings, noting high-value items.

Roughly one month before, focus on administrative duties. Arrange utility transfers for both your old and new residences. File a change of address with the postal service and notify essential services. Acquire all necessary packing supplies, including sturdy boxes and protective materials.

The final week demands focused attention. Confirm all arrangements with your movers and ensure property access. Pack a vital "first-night" box with immediate necessities: toiletries, medications, and a change of clothes. Complete a thorough final clean of your old place.

On moving day, supervise loading and unloading. At your new home, prioritize setting up essentials and unpack gradually. Don't forget to update your driver's license and other official documents promptly. A well-utilized checklist genuinely simplifies the entire relocation journey, ensuring a seamless start.

raw:
Papyrus 44

Papyrus 44 (in Gregory-Aland numbering), signed by P44, is an early copy of the New Testament in Greek. It is a papyrus manuscript of the Gospel of Matthew and Gospel of John. It contains Matt. 17:1-3.6-7; 18:15-17.19; 25:8-10 and John 10:8-14. Fragments of the Gospel of John formerly known as Papyrus 44b (containing 9:3-4; 12:16-18) have been reclassified as Papyrus 128. The manuscript paleographically has been assigned to the 6th or 7th century.

The Greek text of this codex is a representative of the Alexandrian text-type. Aland placed it in Category II. It is currently housed at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (Inv. 14. 1. 527) in New York.

W. E. Crum, H. G. Evelyn-White, The Monastery of Epiphanius at Thebes, Metropolitan Museum of Art, Egyptian Expedition Publications IV, (New York, 1926), pp. 120-121. (transcription and collation). Ellwood M. Schofield, The Papyrus Fragments of the Greek New Testament, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, Louisville, 1936, pp. 296-301.

raw:
sourdough baking

Sourdough bread has experienced a remarkable resurgence in home kitchens, transforming from a challenging fermentation project into a daily ritual for many enthusiasts. Unlike commercial yeast that ferments quickly, a sourdough starter relies on wild yeasts and lactic acid bacteria cultivated over several days. This natural process creates a complex flavor profile and a distinctive tang that elevates the finished loaf beyond the standard supermarket slice. The initial phase requires patience and consistency, as the starter must be fed daily with equal parts flour and water to maintain its active microbial population.

Mastering the hydration level is often the most daunting aspect for beginner bakers. While a 65 percent hydration dough seems manageable, moving to 75 or 80 percent introduces a wetter, stickier consistency that demands a different handling approach. Techniques such as stretch and folds replace heavy kneading, allowing gluten to develop gently under less mechanical stress. The dough feels alive and responsive during this stage, expanding and stretching as the gluten network strengthens. Learning to read the dough's texture rather than just the clock is a crucial skill that separates amateur attempts from successful loaves.

Fermentation timing is arguably the most critical variable in sourdough baking. Environmental temperature and the activity level of the starter significantly influence how quickly the dough rises. A warm kitchen might cause the dough to over-proof in just four hours, leading to a collapsed structure and excessive sourness. Conversely, a cool room can slow fermentation to a crawl, resulting in dense, under-risen loaves. Understanding these variables allows bakers to adjust their schedules, often utilizing the fridge for cold proofing to control the process while sleeping.

The bake itself requires high heat to achieve that signature crisp crust. Preheating a heavy Dutch oven in the oven for at least an hour ensures the vessel retains enough thermal mass to generate instant steam. This steam keeps the crust elastic during the first twenty minutes, allowing the loaf to fully expand before the surface sets. When the lid is removed, the intense dry heat caramelizes the sugars on the surface, creating the deep golden brown color and shatteringly crisp texture that defines a well-baked sourdough.

Ultimately, sourdough baking is a practice in observation and adaptation. No two loaves will be identical, and that variance is part of the charm. The process teaches practical skills in timing, temperature management, and texture recognition that translate into broader culinary confidence. Whether you aim for a daily bread or an occasional weekend leisure project, the reward is a nutritious, flavorful loaf that speaks to the slow, deliberate pace of traditional baking. Each successful bake builds confidence, making the next attempt feel less like a gamble and more like a predictable, satisfying routine.

Subject: Update on the Riverside Bike Lane Situation
Hi Maya,
I wanted to give you a quick update on the progress of the new protected bike lane connecting the downtown core to the riverfront path. The city council finally approved the final phase of the project during last week's planning session. This vote clears the path for construction to begin in early March, which is a significant milestone we have been working toward for quite some time now.
The protected lane will span almost two miles and feature a concrete median buffer separating cyclists from vehicular traffic. Safety advocates have been pushing for this specific design for years, arguing that it will significantly reduce the number of serious accidents currently reported on these busy streets. The physical separation addresses the primary concern local residents have had about sharing narrow roadways with faster moving cars during peak commuting hours.
Construction crews are expected to mobilize within the next few weeks to begin installing the new pavement and protective barriers. Traffic patterns on adjacent streets will shift temporarily, so expect some minor delays around the construction zones. The city has promised to keep communication lines open and will post regular updates on their public works website regarding any lane closures or detours.
I still have a few lingering questions about the planned intersection intersections at Fifth and Main. Specifically, I want to ensure that the right-turn conflict zones are handled correctly to prevent dangerous squeezes between turning vehicles and straight-moving bikes. I plan to attend the next public input session next Tuesday to raise these specific concerns with the urban planning staff directly.
Let me know if you want to join me for that meeting. It might also be a good time to discuss our potential partnership with the local cycling club for the upcoming safety awareness campaign. I think combining our efforts could make a stronger impact on the issue and ensure the project remains on track.
Best regards,
David

raw:
chess openings

The opening phase of chess is often misunderstood by beginners as a series of rigid rules that must be memorized to avoid immediate defeat. In reality, it is a strategic foundation that sets the tone for the entire game, balancing piece development, central control, and king safety. Mastering openings is not about committing every variation to memory, a task that would take a lifetime, but rather understanding the underlying principles that guide each move. Players who grasp the "why" behind their moves are far more adaptable when the game deviates from known theory, allowing them to navigate unfamiliar positions with confidence and creativity.

White typically aims for quick development and space, while Black focuses on equalizing conditions and generating counterplay. The most common first moves belong to the Ruy Lopez, Italian Game, Sicilian Defense, and French Defense. Each leading family of moves offers distinct advantages and challenges. For instance, the Queen's Gambit sacrifices a pawn temporarily to gain a powerful central presence, while the King's Indian Defense accepts a weak center early on to launch a fierce attack on the kingside. Choosing an opening that aligns with your personal playing style is crucial, as you will feel most comfortable when your piece placement mirrors your intuitive approach to the board.

It is a common misconception that deep theory is required to succeed at the amateur level. While top grandmasters calculate variations dozens of moves ahead, most club players benefit more from broad knowledge than narrow precision. A solid understanding of the main ideas allows a player to handle minor errors gracefully. If your opponent moves off the main line, a player who understands the general plan can often find a natural response, whereas a player who has merely memorized move sequences may panic and lose strategic coherence. Flexibility is the hallmark of a true opening expert.

Modern preparation has changed with the rise of strong engine analysis, but classical principles remain the bedrock of good play. Controlling the center with pawns, developing minor pieces toward active squares, and castling early are universal themes. Ignoring these fundamentals in favor of flashy gambits often leads to long-term structural weaknesses. Engines have also clarified some old debates, confirming that certain seemingly risky lines are indeed sound, while others contain subtle traps that punish inaccuracy. Staying updated with current trends can give you an edge, provided you do not overcomplicate your repertoire with lines that are difficult to remember under time pressure.

Ultimately, the goal of an opening is to reach a middlegame position where you feel comfortable and understand your plans. Repetition is key to this process; playing through many full games helps solidify patterns in your mind. Reviewing your own games to identify where you deviated from plan or where you drifted into passive positions is an excellent learning tool. Whether you prefer the tactical complexity of the Sicilian or the positional depth of the Caro-Kann, finding openings that you enjoy playing will keep you motivated and eager to improve. Patience and consistent practice will transform rote memorization into intuitive understanding.
