What the Swedish Butler Saw

What the Swedish Butler Saw (also known as A Man with a Maid, A Story of... A Man with a Maid, The Groove Room and Champagnegalopp ) is a 1975 Swedish-American sex comedy film directed by Vernon P. Becker and starring Ole Søltoft, Sue Longhurst, Malou Cartwright and Diana Dors. The film was written by Becker and Barry E. Downes loosely based on the 1908 anonymous erotic novel The Way of a Man with a Maid. It was one of a number of sex comedies starring Diana Dors.

In Victorian London, a young aristocrat, Jack Armstrong, is desperate to win the love of his beloved, the greedy Lady Alice Faversham. Jack buys an insane asylum to turn into a "love nest", unaware that Jack the Ripper still lives there.

Sue Longhurst as Alice Faversham Ole Søltoft as Jack Armstrong Malou Cartwright as Penny Diana Dors as Madame Helena Charlie Elvegård as Samson Martin Young as Jack the Ripper Steven Lund as young Jack Joe Grey as Judge Pettibone Larry Leonard as Mr. Pendleton Peter Rose as Reverend Faversham Julie Bernby as Mrs. Faversham Barbara Hart as Mrs. Armstrong Gil Holmes as Mr. Armstrong Tina Monell as Marion Faversham

During the 3-D revival of the 1980s, the film was re-released under the title Tickled Pink, but the release did keep the Swedish Butler credit sequence intact.

The Monthly Film Bulletin wrote: "The pornography of the anonymous Victorian novel A Man with a Maid is diluted here into conventional Continental sex comedy, with the repetitive assaults on Alice's virtue now bolstered by a childish sub-plot in which a pantomime Jack the Ripper pops out of secret panels to ogle the nudity. Ole Seltoft performs with a zest that belies years of similarly foolish roles, and even Diana Dors is in remarkably good humour in view of the genuine leg injury which confined her to a wheelchair throughout the shooting. The only real point of interest, however, is that the film was made in another single-lens and projector modification of the 'Natural Vision' 3-D process of the Fifties. This produces an effective enough depth of vision, at the expense of picture clarity, and allows one or two cylindrical objects to protrude from the screen, though there are so few of these that they hardly justify the eyestrain caused by the Polaroid spectacles."

customer support policy

At Northwind Solutions, we believe that a product is only as good as the people who stand behind it. Our commitment to customer support goes beyond simple troubleshooting; it is a foundational part of our service philosophy. We aim to resolve issues quickly, communicate clearly, and ensure that every interaction leaves you feeling valued and heard. Whether you are a long-time client or just setting up your account, our team is dedicated to providing seamless assistance that helps you get the most out of your investment.

Our primary support channels include email, live chat, and a comprehensive online knowledge base. Live chat is available during business hours, Monday through Friday, from eight in the morning to six in the evening, Eastern Time. This direct line allows for immediate responses to urgent questions and real-time guidance on complex features. For non-urgent inquiries, our email support team guarantees a first response within four business hours. Most users find that the majority of their questions can be answered instantly by browsing our extensive library of how-to guides and video tutorials.

We adhere to a strict escalation strategy designed to ensure that no issue falls through the cracks. If a query remains unresolved after the initial contact, it is automatically flagged for senior review. Our Tier 2 support specialists handle technical deep-dives and account-specific configurations, ensuring that you do not have to repeat your problem to multiple agents. We track every ticket with a unique reference number, allowing you to monitor the status of your case at any time through your dashboard. Transparency in this process empowers you to stay informed without needing to chase updates.

Our support policy extends to new users as well, offering a seven-day window of enhanced assistance for first-time buyers. During this period, our team proactively reaches out to ensure your onboarding experience is smooth and that any initial hurdles are addressed before they become obstacles. We also provide clear expectations regarding response times for different subscription tiers. Premium subscribers receive priority routing, which typically reduces average wait times by half compared to standard plans. This tiered approach allows us to allocate resources effectively while maintaining high service levels across the board.

Finally, we view customer feedback as a vital component of our continuous improvement cycle. Every support interaction is logged and reviewed for quality assurance, ensuring that our agents remain aligned with our high standards for empathy and expertise. We encourage you to leave honest feedback after each support session, as your insights directly influence our training and policy updates. If you ever feel that an issue has not been resolved to your satisfaction, please do not hesitate to ask for a supervisor review. We are committed to making your experience with Northwind Solutions not just functional, but genuinely positive.

raw:
password reset guidance

When you forget a password, the first instinct is to click the "Forgot password?" link and hope for a quick fix. While most online services have streamlined the process, the steps you take after receiving the reset email can make the difference between a secure account and a vulnerable one. Understanding the why behind each action helps you protect not only your own data but also the information of anyone who might be connected to your accounts.

The reset email you receive usually contains a temporary link that expires after a short period, often fifteen to thirty minutes. Do not postpone clicking it, and avoid copying the link into a different device unless you are certain the connection is secure. When you open the link, you will be taken to a page that asks you to create a new password. At this point, resist the temptation to reuse an old password or a simple variation; attackers can often guess patterns based on previously compromised data.

A strong password combines length, complexity, and uniqueness. Aim for at least twelve characters, mixing upper and lower case letters, numbers, and symbols. Avoid common words, personal information, or sequences that can be found in dictionary attacks. If you find it difficult to generate such passwords, consider using a reputable password manager that can create and store random strings for you, eliminating the need to remember each one individually.

After you have set the new password, the service may ask whether you want to sign out of other sessions. It is wise to approve this request, especially if you suspect your old credentials might have been exposed. Signing out forces all devices to re-authenticate, reducing the risk that a lingering session remains active on a compromised device. Additionally, check the recent activity log if the platform offers it; unusual logins from unfamiliar locations can be an early warning sign of an account breach.

Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds a critical layer of security beyond the password itself. If you have not already enabled it, set it up as soon as possible. Whether you choose an authenticator app, a hardware token, or SMS codes, 2FA ensures that even if someone obtains your password, they still need a second piece of information that only you possess. Remember to store any backup codes in a safe place; they are often the only way to regain access if you lose your primary 2FA device.

Finally, make a habit of reviewing your security settings regularly. Change passwords periodically, especially for accounts that hold sensitive personal or financial information. Keep your recovery email and phone number up to date, so you can receive reset instructions without delay. By treating each password reset as an opportunity to strengthen your defenses, you turn a moment of inconvenience into a proactive step toward long-term digital safety.

Mergeable heap

Make-Heap(), create an empty heap. Insert(H,x), insert an element x into the heap H. Min(H), return the minimum element, or Nil if no such element exists. Extract-Min(H), extract and return the minimum element, or Nil if no such element exists. And one more that distinguishes it:

x ← Extract-Min(H2) while x ≠ Nil Insert(H1, x) x ← Extract-Min(H2) This can however be wasteful as each Extract-Min(H) and Insert(H,x) typically have to maintain the heap property.

Binomial heap Fibonacci heap Leftist tree Pairing heap Skew heap A more complete list with performance comparisons can be found at Heap (data structure) § Comparison of theoretic bounds for variants. In most mergeable heap structures, merging is the fundamental operation on which others are based. Insertion is implemented by merging a new single-element heap with the existing heap. Deletion is implemented by merging the children of the deleted node.

Subject: Quick Guide to 3D Printing Basics
Hi David,
I heard you are finally diving into the world of additive manufacturing, so I wanted to send over some practical considerations to help you get started. It is a fascinating hobby that bridges the gap between digital design and physical creation, but understanding the core mechanics will save you a lot of frustration during your first few months of experimentation.
The most critical decision you will face is choosing between FDM and SLA printers. FDM, or Fused Deposition Modeling, uses plastic filament that is melted and extruded layer by layer. It is more forgiving, cheaper to run, and handles a wider variety of materials, making it the standard recommendation for beginners. In contrast, SLA, or Stereolithography, uses liquid resin cured by light. While SLA produces incredibly fine details and smooth surfaces, the post-processing is messier, works with fewer materials, and requires more careful safety handling due to the chemical nature of the resins used.
Do not underestimate the importance of slicer software in this workflow. You cannot simply send a 3D model file directly to a printer; you must first process it through a program like Cura or PrusaSlicer. This software breaks the model into horizontal layers and generates the toolpath instructions the machine needs. Learning to adjust settings such as infill percentage, layer height, and cooling fan speeds is essential for achieving a good balance between print speed, strength, and surface finish quality on your first projects.
Before you buy any hardware, spend some time learning a CAD package or finding suitable models online. Platforms like Thangs or Printables host thousands of free, tested designs that can help you understand what is mechanically possible without requiring advanced modeling skills. Starting with simple brackets, phone stands, or custom organizers will help you calibrate your printer and get a feel for the workflow without risking expensive prints that might fail due to minor machine errors.
Let me know if you want to chat about specific budget options or if you have questions about maintenance. The community is very supportive, and there are plenty of forums where you can troubleshoot issues as they arise. I hope this gives you a solid foundation to start your journey into 3D printing with confidence and excitement.
Best regards,
Alex

Kakoba Division

Kakoba Division is one of the 6 divisions that make up Mbarara Municipality, Uganda. The other 5 Divisions are as follows: 1. Kamukuzi Division, 2. Nyamitanga Division, 3. Biharwe Division, 4. Kakiika Division 5. Nyakayojo Division

The division covers most of the Central business district and it is located on the East and south east of the central business. It borders with Kamukuzi Division in the west, Kakiika Division in the East and North, Nyamitanga Division and Masha of Isingiro District in the south.

The division covers the part of central business district which covers the streets of High Street, Makharnsingh street, Mbaguta Street, Bishop Wills street, Bucunku road, Buremba road, and Mosque road at large The neighbourhoods in the Division include, Kisenyi, Kijungu, Surveyor cell, Kacence, Nyamityobora, Kakoba hill, Rugazi, Kyapotani, Rwentondo, Nyakaizi and Buremba, Kiswahili cell, Kenkombe.

Kakoba Division is the most populous Division in Mbarara. The 2002 Census estimated the population of Kakoba Division at 34,271. In 2011, the population of Kakoba was estimated to be 50,930, the 2014 census estimated the population to be 55,519.

raw:
CCTV-1

CCTV-1 (CCTV General Channel) is the primary channel of CCTV, the national flagship terrestrial television network of the People's Republic of China. It broadcasts a range of programs from CCTV Headquarters at East 3rd Ring Road in Beijing and is available to both cable and terrestrial television viewers. The terrestrial signal of CCTV-1 is free-to-air across China. However, due to copyright restrictions, the satellite signal of CCTV-1 is encrypted, and smartcards are necessary for decryption.

Initially branded as Peking Television (not to be confused with the present-day Beijing Television), CCTV-1 was launched on an experimental basis on 2 May 1958 and officially regular broadcasting for 4 hours 30 minutes each day starting on 2 September 1958. Peking Television was granted a free-to-air terrestrial television broadcasting license in the 1960s. From 6 January to 4 February 1967, Beijing Television's transmissions were suspended when the Rebel Faction temporarily seized power. It began broadcasting experimentally in colour in 1971 and was later launched via satellite transmissions in 1973 for major events. The first color programs were PAL-D/K, and full-time color broadcasting began in 1977.

On 1 May 1978, Peking Television was renamed China Central Television (CCTV) with the approval of the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party. CCTV began domestic satellite transmissions in 1984 using the Dong Fang Hong 2 satellite. In 1988, it began stereo broadcasting on all television channels. In 1994, it moved satellite broadcasting from Chinasat-3 to Chinasat-4, a quality-level broadcaster. That same year, it was receivable in 51% of Guangzhou. It turned on its digital signal in 2002. CCTV-1 began broadcasting 24 hours a day on 1 October 2004 and began high-definition broadcasting on 28 September 2009. On 1 March 2011, Hong Kong's Asia Television (ATV) started relaying CCTV-1 instead of CCTV-4, a Hong Kong-based free-to-air digital terrestrial station that is usually tuned to 15 on the UHF band. On 29 May 2017, Hong Kong's RTHK started relaying CCTV-1 instead of CGTN Documentary, a Hong Kong-based free-to-air digital terrestrial station that is usually tuned to 33 on the high-definition television.

CCTV-1 HD is a simulcast network version of CCTV-1 in high-definition. All standard-definition content is upscaled to high-definition output. The rest of the programming hours consist of mainly upscaled resolution CCTV-1 simulcast. The horizontal resolution was increased to 1920 pixels. CCTV-1 HD was created specifically for the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2008 Summer Paralympics at the Beijing National Stadium. For the duration of the 2012 Summer Olympics broadcasting was increased to 24 hours a day to provide extra coverage of the Summer Olympic Games events.

A re-compiled edition of CCTV-1 started broadcasting in Hong Kong and Macau on 1 March 2011, and relaunched on digital terrestrial television on 29 May 2017. On 21 December 2016, the channel was included in the list of basic channels for Macanese households, on DTT LCN 71. Due to copyright and law restrictions, commercial advertisements, some television dramas, and some entertainment shows are not aired on CCTV-1 Hong Kong and Macau versions.

Version 4.2.1 of the Project Meridian client is now available for all active users. This release is marked as a critical update and addresses several stability issues reported in the previous build. Users are strongly encouraged to apply this patch immediately to maintain optimal performance and security compliance. The update package has been verified by our security team and contains no known conflicts with existing third-party integrations.

The primary focus of this release is the remediation of a memory leak detected in the data synchronization module. Previously, long-running sessions could cause gradual degradation in system speed. This fix ensures that resource usage remains consistent over extended periods. Additionally, we have optimized the background processing engine to reduce CPU load by approximately fifteen percent, resulting in smoother interaction for users running resource-intensive tasks simultaneously.

Several user interface adjustments have been made to improve accessibility. Contrast ratios for text elements on dark mode backgrounds have been increased to meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards. Navigation menus now support keyboard-only traversal more reliably, addressing feedback from several enterprise clients. These changes do not alter the underlying workflow but significantly enhance usability for a broader range of operators.

Administrators should note that configuration files referencing the legacy API endpoint v1 will be deprecated in this version. Systems still pointing to these endpoints must be updated to v2 before deployment. A migration script is included in the installer package to assist with this transition. We recommend testing these changes in a staging environment before pushing them to production servers to ensure no unexpected behavior occurs during the switchover.

For those experiencing difficulties, please consult the updated troubleshooting section in the online knowledge base. Our support team has extended hours for the next two weeks to assist with any migration queries. Please include the build number in your ticket subject line to help us route your request efficiently. Thank you for your continued use of Project Meridian.

dormitory rules

Living on campus can be an exciting transition, but it also means adapting to a set of dormitory rules that keep the community safe, comfortable, and respectful. New students often wonder why seemingly simple guidelines-like quiet hours and laundry schedules-are so strictly enforced. Understanding the reasons behind these policies can turn compliance into a shared commitment rather than a chore.

Quiet hours are perhaps the most familiar rule, usually beginning at 10 p.m. and lasting until 7 a.m. The purpose is to protect the sleep of those who need to study early or have different class schedules. While the policy allows for occasional conversations, it discourages loud music, TV volume, and group gatherings that could disturb neighbors. Most dorms provide designated study lounges where late-night collaboration can continue without infringing on personal space.

Cleanliness is another cornerstone of dorm life. Residents are expected to keep their rooms tidy, dispose of trash regularly, and use the shared kitchen and bathroom facilities responsibly. This isn't just about aesthetics; a clutter-free environment reduces fire hazards and helps maintenance staff spot leaks or damage early. Many halls schedule monthly inspections, and repeated violations can lead to fines or loss of privileges, reinforcing the need for everyday habits like wiping down counters after cooking.

Visitors are welcomed, but they must follow the guest policy that limits the number of overnight stays and requires registration at the front desk. This rule serves both security and occupancy standards set by fire codes. When a guest arrives, the host should provide a temporary key or sign-in sheet, and keep noise levels low, especially during quiet hours. Failure to adhere can result in restricted visitor access for the resident and, in extreme cases, disciplinary action.

Safety drills and fire extinguisher checks are routine, and every resident is required to attend. These sessions teach evacuation routes, proper use of equipment, and how to report hazards. Participation isn't optional; the administration tracks attendance and may impose penalties on those who skip the training. Knowing the procedures not only protects the individual but also ensures the whole floor can respond efficiently in an emergency.

Finally, respect for personal property and privacy underpins all other regulations. Borrowing items without permission, entering another room uninvited, or tampering with someone's lock violates trust and can lead to formal complaints. Dormitories thrive when each occupant treats the shared space as a community rather than a collection of isolated apartments. By embracing the rules as a framework for mutual respect, students can enjoy a supportive environment that fosters both academic success and personal growth.

raw:
museum exhibition

The new "Echoes of Empire" exhibition opened at the Riverside Museum on Tuesday, inviting visitors to step into a richly layered narrative that traces the rise and fall of several historic empires through art, artifacts, and immersive installations. Running through the end of March, the show occupies three galleries and a specially designed mezzanine that blends contemporary design with period architecture. Curators have timed the launch to coincide with the city's bicentennial celebrations, positioning the exhibition as a cultural centerpiece for both locals and tourists seeking a deeper understanding of global history.

At the heart of "Echoes of Empire" is a collection of over 200 objects, ranging from intricately embroidered textiles of the Mughal court to bronze armaments recovered from the ruins of a Roman outpost in North Africa. Each piece is paired with a short narrative that situates it within the broader political and social currents of its time. A striking centerpiece is a reconstructed throne room from the Ming dynasty, recreated using laser-scanned fragments and period-accurate pigments. The lighting in this space shifts subtly throughout the day, echoing the changing fortunes of the dynasties it represents.

The exhibition does more than display objects; it invites active participation. Visitors can test their knowledge at a touchscreen quiz that adapts to their answers, revealing hidden stories behind the artifacts. A "virtual caravan" experience lets guests navigate a 3-D trade route, making choices that affect the outcome of simulated diplomatic encounters. For families, a hands-on workshop offers the chance to try ancient pottery techniques under the guidance of a master craftsman, while school groups can attend a series of guided tours that align with state curriculum standards in history and art.

Behind the scenes, "Echoes of Empire" is the result of collaboration between the museum's curatorial team and scholars from three continents. Lead curator Dr. Helena Ruiz, a specialist in cross-cultural exchange, describes the project as "a dialogue across centuries, where each object becomes a voice in a larger conversation about power, trade, and identity." The exhibition also features contributions from contemporary artists who reinterpret historical motifs through modern media, creating a bridge between past and present that resonates with today's audiences. Community partners, including local cultural societies and heritage NGOs, have helped to ensure that the stories told are inclusive and reflective of multiple perspectives.

Tickets are priced at $15 for adults, $10 for seniors and students, and free for children under twelve, with discounted family passes available online. The museum remains fully accessible, offering wheelchair-friendly routes, audio descriptions for the visually impaired, and sign-language interpreted tours on weekends. Visitors are encouraged to arrive early, as the popular interactive stations tend to fill quickly. A café on the first floor serves themed refreshments, and a gift shop offers reproductions of select pieces and a catalog of the exhibition. Whether you are a history buff, an art lover, or simply curious about the forces that shaped our world, "Echoes of Empire" promises an engaging and thought-provoking experience that lingers long after you leave the galleries.

Pam Dawber

Pamela Dawber (born October 18, 1951) is an American actress known for her lead television sitcom roles as Mindy McConnell on Mork & Mindy (1978-1982) and Samantha Russell on My Sister Sam (1986-1988).

Dawber was born in Detroit, the elder of two daughters of Thelma M. (née Fisher) and Eugene E. Dawber, a commercial artist. She went to Reid Elementary School in Goodrich and attended North Farmington High School and Oakland Community College (OCC), with the intention of transferring to a four-year college.

Dawber moved to New York City and was initially a fashion model with Wilhelmina Models before switching to acting. She appeared in several television commercials during the 1970s (Fotomat, Noxzema, Neet, Underalls, etc.). Dawber screen-tested for the title role in Tabitha, a 1977 to 1978 situation comedy spun off from Bewitched, but the role instead went to Lisa Hartman. However, ABC executives were impressed enough with her to enroll her in the company's "talent development" program, which paid its participants until they could find appropriate roles. Garry Marshall recruited her from this program.

Dawber's professional breakthrough came when Marshall chose her, despite her having relatively little acting experience and not having auditioned for the part, as one of the two title characters of the ABC sitcom Mork & Mindy, which ran from 1978 to 1982. She portrayed Mindy McConnell, the comedic foil and eventual love interest for the extraterrestrial Mork from the planet Ork, played by a then-unknown Robin Williams. The show was very popular in its debut season, when it averaged at number three in the Nielsen ratings for the year.

Dawber sang in a 1980s Los Angeles Civic Light Opera production of Gilbert & Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance, based on the Joseph Papp / New York Shakespeare Festival production. Her role, as Mabel, had been played by Linda Ronstadt in the New York run of the show. In mid-1982, Dawber performed the role of Mabel at the Minskoff Theatre in New York.

From 1986 to 1988, Dawber again had a title role in a television series, playing Samantha Russell in the CBS sitcom My Sister Sam, co-starring Rebecca Schaeffer. The series was a success in its first season, but it suffered a ratings drop in its second after moving to Saturday night. My Sister Sam was cancelled in April 1988, with half of the second season's episodes never shown on CBS. They were eventually broadcast (along with all previous episodes) on USA Network. In July 1989, over a year after the show's cancellation, Schaeffer was shot and killed in front of her apartment in Los Angeles by Robert John Bardo, an obsessed fan who had stalked her for three years. Dawber was reportedly "devastated" by her former co-star's death. Dawber and her other surviving My Sister Sam co-stars - Joel Brooks, David Naughton and Jenny O'Hara - all participated in a filmed public service announcement about gun violence prevention, and Dawber herself became a gun control advocate.

Although mostly known for her television work, Dawber has starred in several films, including the comedy movie Stay Tuned (1992) with John Ritter and the period movie I'll Remember April (1999), alongside husband Mark Harmon.

In 1997, Dawber starred in the short-lived sitcom Life... and Stuff on CBS. In 2014, she reunited with Robin Williams on his comedy series The Crazy Ones as a love interest of Williams's character. The reunion failed to improve ratings, and the series was canceled shortly afterwards. Williams, already suffering from Lewy body disease by this time, died by suicide later that year. Dawber is a national spokeswoman for Big Brothers Big Sisters of America. In 2016 Dawber made a guest appearance on The Odd Couple in a tribute episode to Marshall, along with other Marshall alumni such as Ron Howard, Garry's sister Penny Marshall, Cindy Williams, Anson Williams, Don Most and Marion Ross. She appeared with her husband, fellow actor Mark Harmon, on CBS's NCIS in 2021 for seven episodes as "seasoned investigative journalist" Marcie Warren.

Defne Magnanery

Defne Magnanery (Turkish: Defne Koza Evi, lit. 'Cocoon House of Defne') is a vocational training center for silk farming, located at Defne in Hatay Province, southern Turkey. It was established by the Municipality of Defne to revive the silk farming and to provide livelihood to women.

Silk farming and weaving were common in Defne in the 1950s that sunk into oblivion in later years. The magnanery, situated at Harbiye neighborhood, 1079 St., 34, in Defne district of Hatay Province, was established by the district municipality in 2015. The mangnan and master instructor Tülay Genç, who runs the vocational training center, started the silk farming despite objections of her family. Previously, she had been helping her husband in silk weaving. Supported by her daughter Fulya, she learned silk farming, and took a certificate of training after attending a course. For the realization of the project, her brother granted his ranch house after he watched a documentary film produced by a British television channel about his sister's silk farming activity. The project aims to train women in silk farming in order to enable them to earn their livelihood. Subject: Re: Open Source Licence Selection for Upcoming Release
Hi Alex,
I hope you're doing well. I'm writing to follow up on our recent discussion about the open-source components we plan to include in the next product release.
As you know, the licence we choose directly affects how we can distribute, modify, and commercialise the software. A permissive licence such as MIT or Apache-2.0 generally lets us incorporate the code with minimal obligations, while a strong copyleft licence like GPL-v3 requires any derivative work to be released under the same terms.
The practical difference lies in source-code disclosure. With a permissive licence we only need to retain the original copyright notice and provide a copy of the licence. With a copyleft licence we must also publish our modifications and any code that links to the original, which could impact our proprietary roadmap.
From a compliance standpoint, it's essential to keep a clear inventory of all third-party libraries, record their licences, and ensure our build process can generate the required attribution files automatically. Missing any of these steps could expose us to legal risk and force us to remove the offending component after release.
Given the timeline, I recommend we prioritise libraries under permissive licences for the core functionality and set aside a separate audit for any GPL-v3 modules. I'll schedule a brief meeting next Tuesday to confirm the final list and assign responsibilities. Please let me know if that works for you.
Best regards, 
Jamie Patel

Forever's a Long, Long Time is an album of Hank Williams covers performed by Don Was to Was's own music. Was released the album, under the name Orquestra Was, on April 8, 1997 on Verve Forecast Records. The original CD release of the album also included a short film directed by Was, starring Sweet Pea Atkinson and Kris Kristofferson. The film was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Long Form Music Video in 1997.

Forever's a Long, Long Time is an album of Hank Williams covers performed by Don Was to Was's own music. Was released the album, under the name Orquestra Was, on April 8, 1997 on Verve Forecast Records. The original CD release of the album also included a short film directed by Was, starring Sweet Pea Atkinson and Kris Kristofferson. The film was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Long Form Music Video in 1997.

film festival schedule

The upcoming Riverside International Film Festival will run from October 12 to October 20, offering a packed lineup of premieres, retrospectives, and industry panels. Organizers have released the official schedule, and it's already generating buzz among cinephiles eager to map out their week-long itinerary.

Opening night kicks off on Tuesday, October 12, with a red-carpet screening of the much-anticipated drama "Echoes of Tomorrow," followed by a Q&A session with director Lina Patel. The film will be shown at 7:30 p.m. in the historic Grand Theatre, and tickets are expected to sell out within hours. A pre-festival reception at the nearby art gallery gives attendees a chance to mingle with the cast and crew.

Mid-week programming focuses on documentary storytelling, with "Hidden Rivers" and "Beyond the Frame" slated for Wednesday and Thursday evenings. Both films will be accompanied by panel discussions featuring the filmmakers, producers, and a local environmental activist, providing insight into the creative process and the subjects' real-world impact.

The weekend lineup highlights genre diversity. Saturday features a double feature of avant-garde shorts, while Sunday showcases a nostalgic marathon of classic horror from the 1970s. Late-night screenings continue the tradition of cult favorites, offering a perfect blend of mainstream and indie fare for all tastes.

Tickets can be purchased online through the festival's website, with early-bird pricing available until September 30. For those planning to attend multiple events, a festival pass provides unlimited entry and a complimentary guidebook, making it easier to navigate the bustling schedule and not miss a single moment of the cinematic celebration.

Davendranath Tancoo

Davendranath "Dave" Tancoo (born October 1965 in Fyzabad, Trinidad) is an economist and attorney at law. Since 2025, he has served as Trinidad and Tobago's minister of finance and member of parliament for Fyzabad. He is the chairman of the United National Congress and previously served as the party's General Secretary from 2010-2020. He was elected to the House of Representatives as member of Parliament for Oropouche West on 10 August 2020 in the 2020 election. In the 2025 Trinidad and Tobago general election, his candidacy shifted to the neighbouring constituency of Fyzabad where he was elected MP on 28 April 2025. Following the UNC's election victory, he was appointed Minister of Finance by Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar on 3 May 2025.

A graduate of Iere High School, he holds a Bachelor's degree in Economics (Honours) from the University of the West Indies (St. Augustine campus), a Master's in Business Administration (Merit) from Anglia Ruskin University, and is also a qualified attorney at law, completing his LLB (Honours) from the University of London and Legal Practice Certificate (Distinction) from Staffordshire University and was called to the Bar in 2018.

He served as Chief Economist to the Leader of the Opposition under Mr. Basdeo Panday (1990-1995) and Mrs. Kamla Persad-Bissessar, SC (2006-2010) and (2015-2020). During the administration of Prime Minister Basdeo Panday, he acted as an adviser to the Kamla Persad-Bissessar in her roles as Attorney General, Minister of Legal Affairs, and Minister of Education. Following Kamla Persad-Bissessar's election as Prime Minister on May 24, 2010, he was appointed Special Adviser to the Prime Minister on Finance and the Economy where he provided the Prime Minister with advice and support on government's economic, trade, and fiscal policies. Upon his election to the House of Representatives in 2020, he held Parliamentary leadership roles as the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee in the Twelfth Republican Parliament, was a member of the Joint Select Committees on the Representation of the People Amendment Bill (No.2) 2020 and the Shipping Bill 2020, and acted as the Opposition's Deputy Chief Whip. As the Opposition Shadow for Finance, he played a significant role at the Parliament's Standing Finance Committee meetings and during debates on the national budget and mid-year review.

knitting patterns

Knitting patterns have long been the backbone of the craft, guiding both beginners and seasoned makers through the twists and turns of yarn work. A well-written pattern translates a designer's vision into a series of clear steps, from selecting gauge and yarn weight to detailing every increase and decrease. When you open a new pattern, the first thing you'll notice is the concise list of materials, which sets the tone for the project and helps you avoid mid-project trips to the store.

The body of the pattern itself usually follows a logical order: cast-on instructions, row-by-row directions, and any special techniques highlighted in side notes. Modern designers often embed quick-reference charts or diagrams, allowing knitters to skim ahead and visualize complex stitch repeats. For those who prefer visual learning, many online patterns link to video tutorials that demonstrate tricky maneuvers such as cables, lace, or short rows.

One of the biggest advantages of digital patterns is the ability to search and customize. A quick keyword search can reveal variations in size, yarn substitutes, or even colorwork options. Many platforms also let you leave comments, so you can see how others have adapted the pattern for different needles or yarns, creating a community-driven knowledge base.

When selecting a pattern, consider the intended use of the finished piece. A lightweight shawl calls for a breezy stitch and soft yarn, while a chunky blanket benefits from a simple, sturdy texture that shows off the yarn's bulk. Matching the pattern's difficulty level with your skill set ensures a satisfying experience rather than a frustrating one.

Finally, keep your pattern file organized-store PDFs in clearly labeled folders, and back them up on the cloud. A tidy library makes it easy to revisit favorite designs, track progress, and share your latest creations with fellow knitters across the globe.

raw:
university admissions

University admissions have become a complex puzzle for many students and families, especially as competition intensifies across the globe. While the core of the process still revolves around grades, test scores, and personal statements, the surrounding ecosystem now includes virtual tours, holistic review panels, and data-driven outreach programs. Understanding how these elements interact can help applicants craft a more strategic approach, rather than simply hoping their numbers stand out.

One of the first steps is to map out the timeline. Early decision and early action deadlines often fall in November, giving students a chance to lock in a spot at a preferred institution while still keeping their options open for regular decision later in the spring. Applicants should align their standardized test schedules, extracurricular portfolios, and recommendation requests to meet these cut-off dates, allowing a buffer for any unexpected delays. Missing a deadline can mean waiting another year, a costly setback for many.

Beyond timing, the personal essay remains a critical differentiator. Admissions committees look for authenticity, depth of reflection, and evidence of growth. Rather than recounting a generic achievement, successful candidates weave personal anecdotes that illustrate how challenges shaped their values and future aspirations. A well-edited draft that balances humility with confidence often resonates more than a polished but impersonal narrative.

Letters of recommendation also play a subtle yet powerful role. Selecting teachers or mentors who can speak to specific strengths-such as leadership in a science club or resilience in a community service project-provides a richer picture than generic praise. It's advisable to give recommenders ample time and a concise summary of achievements, ensuring they can tailor their letters to the school's ethos.

Finally, the decision-making phase should involve more than tuition calculations. Visiting campuses, even virtually, helps gauge whether the academic environment, student culture, and support services align with personal goals. Weighing factors like financial aid packages, internship opportunities, and alumni networks can turn an acceptance letter into a well-informed commitment. By treating university admissions as a series of coordinated moves rather than a single test, students increase their odds of finding the right fit for the next pivotal chapter of their lives.

One of the first steps is to map out the timeline. Early decision and early action deadlines often fall in November, giving students a chance to lock in a spot at a preferred institution while still keeping their options open for regular decision later in the spring. Applicants should align their standardized test schedules, extracurricular portfolios, and recommendation requests to meet these cut-off dates, allowing a buffer for any unexpected delays. Missing a deadline can mean waiting another year, a costly setback for many.
Company logo
Beyond timing, the personal essay remains a critical differentiator. Admissions committees look for authenticity, depth of reflection, and evidence of growth. Rather than recounting a generic achievement, successful candidates weave personal anecdotes that illustrate how challenges shaped their values and future aspirations. A well-edited draft that balances humility with confidence often resonates more than a polished but impersonal narrative.
Letters of recommendation also play a subtle yet powerful role. Selecting teachers or mentors who can speak to specific strengths-such as leadership in a science club or resilience in a community service project-provides a richer picture than generic praise. It's advisable to give recommenders ample time and a concise summary of achievements, ensuring they can tailor their letters to the school's ethos.
Finally, the decision-making phase should involve more than tuition calculations. Visiting campuses, even virtually, helps gauge whether the academic environment, student culture, and support services align with personal goals. Weighing factors like financial aid packages, internship opportunities, and alumni networks can turn an acceptance letter into a well-informed commitment. By treating university admissions as a series of coordinated moves rather than a single test, students increase their odds of finding the right fit for the next pivotal chapter of their lives.

Brenda Statz

Brenda M. Statz (née Farber; born May 11, 1963) is an American mental-health activist. After the death of her husband, a farmer, from suicide, she co-founded the Farmer Angel Network, a support group for local families in the farming industry.

In October 2018, Leon A. Statz, a 57-year-old farmer from Loganville, Wisconsin, committed suicide after financial struggles forced him to sell the fifty Holstein dairy cows he had on his 200-acre (81 ha) farm, instead moving into grain and beef farming. The relative uncertainty of their new venture caused Statz endless anxiety, even though the farm was actually prospering. Statz, who had inherited the family farm from his parents, began a part-time role as a meat cutter in a local grocery store―his wife of 34 years, Brenda, later saying it was to punish himself because he thought he was a failure. Statz attempted suicide four months after the sale of the cows. He said goodbye to his children over the telephone, then swallowed a handful of pills while locking himself in a shed with farm equipment running inside it. His suicide note read: "I wish I never sold (our, my) cows! I'm a dairy farmer. I want my old life back, but I can't get it anymore. Every thing I do fails. I didn't plan ahead for this ... I really screwed up!" Brenda heard the tractor equipment running and shut them down, despite her husband's attempts to prevent her doing so. She opened the shed's door, to let air pass through, and called the police and Rev. Donald Glanzer Jr., the pastor of their church, St. Peter's Lutherhan in Loganville. Statz was hospitalized for three days. Ethan Statz found his father's body in the shed for the farm's heifers on October 8, 2018. In 2023, Statz's wife, his sons and his daughter-in-law were running the farm. They family later formed Statz Circle S Farms LLC, raising beef cattle and crops.

As a direct result of the incident, in 2019, Statz, Dorothy Harms and Randy Roecker, a neighboring farmer, set up Farmer Angel Network, a support group for local families in the farming industry. Brenda has trained with SafeTALK on has been educated on QPR (Question, Persuade, Refer).

Farmer Angel Network - official website "Widow Of American Farmer Trying To Erase Stigma Of Mental Health In The Heartland" - NBC Nightly News, YouTube, 2020

Geography of Veliko Tarnovo

The town is an urban center and forms a metropolitan area with the sedentary town of Debelets, the villages of Ledenik, Belyakovets, Shemshevo, Prisovo and the suburban areas of Kozlodzha, Dervent.

The relief of the city is highly have a medium degree of roughness (RR from 5 to 40‰). To the east, the town is surrounded by the Tarnovo Heights, to the west by Kalakaya and Salamatya, to the south by the Debeli Bair, the Big and Small Duvar, Patryal Dyal, to the north by Orlovets and Kartala. The average altitude is 220 meters. Highest points: Garga Bair (373 m.), Kartala (359 m.), The Small Duvar (351 m.), Patryl share (350 m.). There are three caves over 5 meters deep around the city - two in the Tarnovo Heights and some of the Kartala.

The geological structure is made up of: To the south, Coneyas - mastite (terrigenous-carbonate rocks), santon - mastrite (terrigeno-carbonate rocks), zenoman Middle Turon, Upper-Aryah Formation (marls and clay marls with interbeds of sandstones, sandstones), sand marbles, Krivnen Formation in places sandstone, Seshev Formation - siltstones and often glauconites.

The most rock formations in the city are in the Monsonsites: Garga Bair, Kartala, and other parts of the Tarnovo Hills. The rocks most often are: granite, limestone, montmorillonite (bentonite) clay rocks.

The climate is temperate continental - summer temperatures average - 21.8 °C and absolute maximum 41.1 °C / and average January temperature -0.6 °C and absolute minimum - 28.1 °C /. The western, northwest and northeast winds oriented along river valleys predominate. The average wind speed is about 1.3 m / s. The average annual rainfall is 680 mm. Snow cover is an average of 60 days a year. The average humidity is 49%. The lowest average annual temperature is in 1991 - 9.34 degrees Celsius, and the highest in 2002 is 11.73 degrees Celsius. Most precipitation is 2005. - 1,056.0 mm. and at least 1985 - 531.6 mm.

The large Yantra River passes through the city. A kilometer south to the city, at the town of Debelets, the Dryanovo River flows into the Belitsa River (from the basin of the Yantra). There are also several small rivers: the Orlova River (in Kartala area), the Svetogorska River and the Ksiliforska River. Near the city are Lake Sveta Gora and Lake Xilifore. There are over 50 reservoirs in the city and around it. The main drinking source is the Yovkovtsi hydroelectric unit.

The chernozem is located in the historical and flat part of the city (Asenov, Varusha, Marino pole, Cholakovtsi, Acacia). Gray forests prevail in the Tarnovo Heights, Kartala and Buzludzha. Alluvial-meadow soils are remembered at the mouths of the Yantra and Dryanovsk rivers.

Great Bend Aspect

The Great Bend Aspect is the region occupied by the Wichita people from 1475 to 1700 in modern day Kansas. The Great bend aspect consists of habitation sites in what are now known as McPherson, Butler, Rice, Marion, Cowley, and Wilson counties. In addition to this, there were several village clusters throughout the great bend aspect. These village cluster sites are known as Little River, Marion, Augusta, Lower Walnut, and Neodesha. These locations were determined by anthropologists and archaeologists by comparing artifacts found at each site, with the inhabitants having similar ceramic attributes. These settlement sites also had similar economies, mostly practicing hunter-gatherer subsistence.

The inhabitants of the great bend aspect included the Wichita people, that was made up of several subgroups, including the Tawakoni, Wichita, Waco, and Taovaya. The reason these subgroups are associated with the Wichita group and with the Great Bend Aspect is due to the similar artifacts found throughout all of the areas.

.

Artifacts found in these various sites had similar materials, and styles. The common materials used were sand, shell, grog, bone, and caliche. The handles of their ceramics were also similar, coming mostly in the strap and loop forms. These artifacts included plates, blades, scrapers, perforators and jars.

The economy of the Great Bend Aspect was based on subsistence and light agriculture. The inhabitants of villages within the Great Bend Aspect practiced hunting and gathering, fishing and some crops, including sunflowers, maize, squash and beans.

raw:
TWA Corporate Headquarters Building

The TWA Corporate Headquarters Building, located at 1735 Baltimore Avenue in the Crossroads neighborhood of downtown Kansas City, was Trans World Airlines headquarters until 1964, when the airline moved to New York City. The selection of Kansas City as the headquarters for TWA (Transcontinental Air Transport after it merged with Western Air Express, initially T&WA) was said to have been made by Charles Lindbergh. The building was designed by architects Raymond E. Bales, Jr. and Morris Schechter and built by the Long Construction Company of Kansas City; site work began in May 1955, and construction was completed on October 31, 1956. The building's exterior was decorated in TWA's signature red and white corporate colors. The three-story L-shaped commercial facility was dominated by aluminum panels and corrugated concrete paneling. It was constructed using the Youtz-Slick construction method, in which steel support beams were first erected and then concrete slabs were poured at ground level and lifted into place by hydraulic jacks; the slabs were then bolted and welded onto the beams, which allowed for a reduction in construction costs and construction time. By 1964 TWA had become a major international figure in aviation, which prompted a move of the airline's executive offices to New York City. The 1735 Baltimore building remained the headquarters for TWA's accounting department, ticket office, credit department, and cargo department until 1969; the airline continued to use the building for training its flight attendants until opening the Breech Academy in nearby suburban Overland Park, KS in 1969. In 2002 the TWA building was added to the National Register of Historic Places. It had been vacant for several years, though plans as late as 2003 called for it to be converted to residential condominiums under the name of TWA Lofts LLC. Instead, in early 2005, the Kansas City-based urban development firm The Nicholson Group hired local architectural firm el dorado inc to design and coordinate the restoration. Following the renovation, it was then leased to the Kansas City-based advertising agency Barkley Inc.; the agency moved into the renovated building on November 14, 2006.

During TWA's heyday, its headquarters building was easily identified by the 22-foot-tall (6.7 m) TWA Moonliner II rocket that stood on the roof's southwest corner. It was modeled after the original 76-foot-tall (23 m), one-third scale TWA Moonliner at Disneyland's Tomorrowland attraction; TWA was the Moonliner's corporate sponsor until 1962. The Moonliner II was then removed from the building's roof by TWA's new owners, shortly after Howard Hughes sold his controlling interest in the airline. The iconic rocket was then sold to SpaceCraft, a Kansas City, MO travel-trailer company. When SpaceCraft moved to Concordia, MO in 1970, the by then all-white Moonliner II moved with them. There it slowly fell into disrepair for the next 25 years, as it stood on a campground located nearby their travel-trailer manufacturing plant, just south of Interstate 70 between Kansas City and St. Louis. The deteriorated Moonliner replica was then sold to and carefully restored by a longtime Disney collector, until once again sporting its original red and white TWA markings. The restored Moonliner II is now on display at Kansas City's TWA Museum located at the Charles B. Wheeler Downtown Airport; at this location, the restored rocket stands about five miles (8 km) from its original TWA roof-top location. The historic restoration of the TWA headquarters building led to the fabrication of a brand new Moonliner II replica begun in March 2006 by the Kansas City office of the Bratton Corporation. The completed replica was installed on September 29 of that year at the same southwest corner roof location as the original.

Barton, Eric. "Incoming: A Rocket That Once Graced TWA's Office Heads Back To Its Spot Over Downtown." The Pitch weekly entertainment journal, August 17, 2006 issue, Kansas City, MO. No ISSN. Haggerty, Jack. "The YABAR Chronicles (Yet Another Born Again Rocketeer)", Sport Rocketry magazine, July/August, 1996. No ISSN. 5-page article and Haggerty interview about Disney's 1955 Tomorrowland and TWA Moonliner attractions. Janzen, Jeck E., and Janzen, Leon J. "Disneyland's Rocket to the Moon." The "E" Ticket magazine #24, Santa Clara, CA. No ISSN. 5-page article and Haggerty interview about Disney's 1955 Tomorrowland and TWA Moonliner attractions.

All participants in the upcoming Riverbend Century Ride must review the updated safety protocols effective this Friday. The committee has noted an increase in near-miss incidents during last year's event, primarily caused by excessive speed at intersection transitions and inadequate hydration breaks. This document outlines mandatory requirements to ensure a safe experience for all cyclists and surrounding infrastructure users.

Helmet usage is strictly enforced for every rider, regardless of skill level or distance covered. Participants must ensure their helmets meet current ANSI or CPSC standards. Additionally, front and rear lighting is mandatory from start until finish, even during daylight hours, to maximize visibility to motorists and pedestrians. Blinking lights are recommended but not required if steady high-visibility models are used.

Route signage has been enhanced with higher contrast materials to improve readability under varying weather conditions. Riders should follow the designated lane markings at all times. Cutting corners or deviating from marked paths will result in immediate disqualification. Please note that several bridge approaches now have narrowed bike lanes due to ongoing municipal construction, requiring single-file riding.

Medical checkpoints are located every ten miles along the route, staffed by certified paramedics and EMTs. Hydration stations will offer water, electrolyte drinks, and basic fruit options. Riders experiencing dizziness, dehydration, or mechanical failure should pull over to the right shoulder immediately and signal for assistance. Do not attempt complex repairs in the travel lane.

Questions regarding these new safety measures should be directed to the race director via the official event portal by this coming Wednesday. A pre-ride briefing is scheduled for 4:00 AM at the start village. Attendance is highly recommended to clarify any logistical changes. Your cooperation in adhering to these guidelines is essential to maintaining the high safety standards of the Riverbend Cycling Federation.

All employees must review their online privacy settings at the start of each quarter to ensure that personal and company data remain protected across all platforms. The company provides a standard checklist, but each individual is responsible for verifying the specific configurations of the accounts they use for work.

When logging into cloud services, verify that two-factor authentication is enabled and that the recovery phone number or email is current. This extra layer prevents unauthorized access even if a password is compromised. If you notice any unfamiliar devices or locations in the login history, report them immediately to IT security.

Social media profiles that are linked to professional activities should be set to limit public visibility of personal information. Adjust the audience controls so that only friends or connections can view posts, photos, and contact details. Remember that even private posts can be shared inadvertently through screenshots, so think carefully before posting sensitive content.

For any third-party applications that request access to corporate data, confirm that the permissions are limited to what is strictly necessary for the task. Revoke any apps that are no longer in use, and avoid granting admin-level rights unless absolutely required. Regular audits of app permissions help reduce exposure to data leaks.

Finally, stay informed about updates to privacy policies and settings for the tools you use daily. The security team will circulate brief summaries of major changes, but you should also check the provider's website periodically. Consistent vigilance protects both your privacy and the organization's reputation.

team offsite agenda

Gathering the whole team away from the daily grind is a powerful way to reset dynamics, but it only works if the agenda is intentional. Without a clear structure, offsites often devolve into vague brainstorming sessions that leave participants feeling drained rather than inspired. The goal of a well-crafted schedule is to balance high-level strategic alignment with actionable steps that can be implemented immediately upon return.

Start the first morning with a deep dive into current performance metrics and honest retrospectives. This segment sets the context for why the gathering is happening now. Spend at least two hours here, ensuring every voice is heard before moving forward. Skipping this step risks building new plans on a foundation of unresolved frustrations or missed expectations from the previous quarter.

Midway through the day, transition into collaborative workshops focused on specific challenges. Break the larger group into smaller pods to tackle real-world obstacles using data you have collected. This dynamic approach encourages creativity and reduces the fear of public criticism that often holds people back in traditional meeting rooms. Facilitators should circulate among groups to keep discussions productive and prevent drift into unanswerable philosophical debates.

After a substantial lunch break, dedicate the afternoon to mapping out the next ninety days. This is where abstract ideas solidify into concrete tasks with clear owners and deadlines. Each participant should leave the room knowing exactly what they are expected to deliver in the coming weeks. Specificity prevents the common post-offsite syndrome where enthusiasm fades within a few days because the plan was too vague to execute.

End the first day with a reflective closing circle. Ask everyone to share one key takeaway and one personal commitment. This ritual reinforces accountability and signals that the work done in the room matters. By capping the day at five hours of intense discussion, you respect personal energy levels and ensure that the insights remain fresh and actionable.

The municipal safety committee has observed a slight uptick in minor property incidents within the Westside district over the last two quarters. This trend, while not indicative of a severe threat to personal security, warrants a comprehensive review of our current community engagement strategies. Residents have reported an increased sense of unease primarily due to perceived gaps in surveillance coverage and limited interaction between neighborhood watch groups and local law enforcement. Our objective is to restore a tangible sense of security through coordinated efforts that emphasize visibility, communication, and mutual support among neighbors. We recognize that safety is not solely the responsibility of police officers but is a shared burden that requires active participation from every household.

To address these concerns, the administration is launching a pilot program focused on improved lighting infrastructure. Several intersections in the residential zone have been identified as having substandard streetlamp functioning, which creates dark zones that can feel intimidating for pedestrians at night. Maintenance crews are scheduled to begin repairs next week, ensuring that all public pathways are adequately illuminated. In parallel, we are distributing updated contact lists to every family unit, highlighting the direct line for non-emergency police matters. This streamlined access aims to reduce the friction between reporting a concern and receiving a response, thereby empowering residents to feel heard and supported without being tied up in bureaucratic loops.

Community involvement remains the cornerstone of our long-term strategy. The existing neighborhood watch coordinators have been encouraged to schedule monthly joint walks with police liaison officers. These patrols should not be viewed as aggressive interventions but as friendly presences that foster familiarity and trust. When officers are seen regularly in friendly contexts, they become accessible resources rather than distant authorities. Residents are invited to share their observations regarding suspicious activities or potential hazards during these meetings. Open dialogue helps identify patterns that isolated observations might miss, allowing for proactive rather than reactive measures to be taken.

We must also address the human element of safety, particularly regarding elderly residents and children. It is crucial that neighbors know who lives next door and can recognize changes in routine that might indicate distress. We recommend establishing informal check-in systems within close-knit groups, where individuals look out for one another during unusual circumstances. This social fabric acts as a powerful safety net, often detecting issues before they escalate into emergencies. By strengthening these interpersonal bonds, we create an environment where isolation is reduced and collective vigilance is natural and unburdened by formal structure.

Finally, we acknowledge that true safety extends beyond physical security to include emotional well-being and a sense of belonging. A neighborhood where people feel comfortable inviting friends over, where children play freely, and where disagreements are resolved kindly is inherently safer. We call upon all residents to engage actively in this cultural shift. By reporting issues promptly, participating in community events, and extending courtesy to strangers, we build a resilient community. Together, we can transform our district into a place where security is not just enforced but naturally cultivated through daily interactions and shared values.

Subject: Quick tips on starting your home compost bin
Hi Sarah,
I finally got my hands dirty and set up the compost bin in the backyard this past weekend. It felt like a significant step toward reducing my household waste, and honestly, the process is much simpler than I had initially imagined. I bought a standard wooden pallet frame to keep the materials organized and contained within the flower bed area where the light enters consistently throughout the day.
The first thing you need to understand is the balance between brown and green materials. Browns, like dried leaves, cardboard strips, and straw, provide carbon. Greens, such as vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, and fresh grass clippings, introduce nitrogen. A rough ratio of three parts brown to one part green keeps the pile healthy and prevents unpleasant smells from developing in the early stages.
Turning the pile is perhaps the most important maintenance task. I use a sturdy pitchfork to aerate the mixture every few days. This introduces oxygen, which helps the beneficial bacteria break down the organic matter quickly. If you neglect this step, the pile will likely become compacted and anaerobic, leading to that sour smell everyone hates.
Keep the moisture level comparable to a wrung-out sponge. It should be damp but not soaking wet. In my local climate, covering the top with a tarp on rainy days prevents waterlogging, while adding a layer of brown material helps absorb excess moisture when it has been particularly wet out.
You will be ready to harvest in about four to six months when the material turns dark and crumbly. The finished compost smells like fresh earth and works as a fantastic soil amendment for your garden beds. Let me know if you need any specific recommendations for tools or if you want to check out my setup sometime next week.
Best regards,
David

Yuriy Tskhay

Yuriy Andreyevich Tskhay (Russian: Юрий Андреевич Цхай; also spelled Yuri Tskhay, Yuri Tskhai, Yuri Chae; born 14 October 1948) is a Kazakh businessman, politician, and former boxing coach. He is a former member of the Senate of the Parliament of the Republic of Kazakhstan (4th and 5th convocations) and former boxing coach of the USSR, Kazakhstan and South Korea. Yitzhak Shapira

Yitzhak Shapira (Hebrew: יצחק שפירא) is an Israeli rabbi who lived in Kiryat Moshe neighborhood in Jerusalem, and is head of the Od Yosef Chai Yeshiva.

In 2009, he published a book (The King's Torah) in which he argues that it is permissible for Jews to kill non-Jews, including children, under certain circumstances. The book suggests that there may be a reason to kill babies on the enemy side, even if they have not violated any laws, due to the potential future danger they might pose based on the assumption that they will grow up to be evil like their parents. The author also proposes that indirect killing of children could be justified as a means of exerting pressure on enemy leaders or if the children are obstructing a rescue operation and their presence contributes to murder. Shapira also argues that children of a king can be harmed to pressure him if he is considered wicked and harming them would prevent him from acting wickedly. He argues that it is preferable to kill one person who is pursuing another with the intent to murder, rather than killing multiple individuals. The book was distributed by Yeshivat HaRaayon HaYehudi in Jerusalem, which adheres to the ideas of the right-wing Rabbi Meir Kahane. Yehuda Bauer described the book as a "mortal danger to the Jewish people as a whole". Ophir Pines-Paz, a member of the Israeli Knesset at the time, called on the attorney general to open a criminal investigation against Shapira on account of the book.

Shapira was detained for questioning in 2006 over an article that advocated expelling or killing all male Palestinians above the age of 13 in the West Bank. In 2008 he signed a "manifesto" in support of Israelis suspected of beating two Arab youths during that year's Holocaust Remembrance Day. In January 2010, he was arrested for his "alleged involvement in the torching of a Palestinian mosque in the village of Yasuf." He denied any involvement, and was released due to lack of evidence. In October 2010, Shapira urged Israel Defense Forces soldiers to use Palestinian civilians as human shields, claiming that it was against "true Jewish values" for a soldier to endanger his life for the sake of enemy soldiers or civilians.

Naniwa-ku, Osaka

Home | About | Contact

Largely a residential area itself, Naniwa-ku is adjacent to and has in recent years blurred into the Namba district, which is south Osaka's transport hub and centre of commerce, entertainment, shopping, and culture. Naniwa retains significant Burakumin and Korean communities. The plight and struggle of both communities in Japan is represented in Liberty Osaka (Osaka Human Rights Museum). Almost the entire ward was decimated in air attacks during bombing in March 1945. Few buildings pre-dating World War II remain.

Naniwa is the site of a number of well-known commercial areas like Nipponbashi, where Capcom and SNK are headquartered. Locally known as Den Den Town (Electric City), Nipponbashi was traditionally a concentration for Osaka's electrical appliance outlets, though the emergence of several large electrical department stores over in recent years has seen its shop space make a gradual shift away from the electrical appliance sector. Directly to its south is Shin Sekai (New World), an entertainment district famous for the Tsutenkaku Tower and Janjan Alley. Amongst Naniwa's sites is the Imamiya Ebisu Shrine, which sponsors the lively Toka Ebisu Festival. Naniwa is the site of the Osaka Prefectural Gymnasium (Osaka-furitsu taiiku-kaikan), where the Grand Sumo Tournament is held in March (Ozumo Sangatsu Basho) and Liberty Osaka - the Osaka Human Rights Museum. Naniwa also contains the massive modern shopping, dining, and entertainment complex, Namba Parks.

Paromitar Ek Din

The film explores the dual themes of friendship and loneliness. The film starts at Sanaka's funeral where Paromita is invited too. Paromita goes into a flashback where it is shown that she was previously married to Sanaka's younger son, Biru. The mother-in-law and daughter-in-law duo, Sanaka (Aparna Sen) and Paromita (Rituparna Sengupta), despite differences in age, backgrounds and temperaments, build a strong bond. But when Paromita's marriage to Biru breaks down, social mores prevent the women from remaining close friends. While Paromita marries Rajeev Shrivastav and begins a new life, her mother-in-law, Sanaka, is left heartbroken and alone and eventually falls seriously ill. When Paromita learns of her friend's deterioration, she is compelled to flout convention, and returns to nurse Sanaka on her deathbed. Sanaka dies, leaving her family shattered. The flashback ends, Paromita leaves the funeral and realizes that she and Rajeev are expecting their first child.

Gangarampur Assembly constituency

As per orders of the Delimitation Commission, No. 41 Gangarampur Assembly constituency (SC) covers Gangarampur municipality, Belbari I, Damdama, Gangarampur and Nandanpur gram panchayats of Gangrampur community development block, and Ajmatpur, Autina, Gurail, Hazratpur, Ramchandrapur and Rampara Chenchra gram panchayats of Tapan community development block. Gangarampur Assembly constituency (SC) is part of No. 6 Balurghat (Lok Sabha constituency).

In 2006 and 2001 state assembly elections Narayan Biswas of CPI(M) won the Gangarampur assembly seat defeating his nearest rival Biplab Mitra of Trinamool Congress. Minati Ghosh of CPI(M) defeated Asish Majumdar of BJP in 1996, Biplab Mitra of Congress in 1991 and Moslehuddin Ahmed of Congress in 1987. Moslehuddin Ahmed representing ICS defeated Arabinda Chakrabarty of CPI(M) in 1982. Ahindra Sarkar of CPI(M) defeated Moslehuddin Ahmed of Congress in 1977.

Moslehuddin Ahmed of Congress won in 1972 and 1971. Ahindra Sarkar of CPI(M) won in 1969. Khalil Sayed of Congress won in 1967. Mangla Kisku of CPI won in 1962. Lakshman Chandra Hansda and Satindra Nath Basu, both of Congress, won in 1957, when Gangarampur was a joint seat. Satindra Nath Basu of Congress won in independent India's first election in 1951.

raw:
Chowmahalla Palace

Home | About | Contact

Chowmahalla Palace or Chowmahallat is the palace of the Nizams of Hyderabad State located in Hyderabad, Telangana, India. It was the seat of power of the Asaf Jahi dynasty (1720-1948) and was the official residence of the Nizams during their reign. The palace has been converted into a museum and the ownership still lies with the family. The palace was constructed at the location of an earlier palace of the Qutb Shahi dynasty and Asaf Jahi dynasty close to the Charminar. Construction of the palace, as it stands today, was started by Nizam Ali Khan Asaf Jah II in 1769. He ordered the building of four palaces from which the nomenclature of Chau Mahalla is derived. The word chār or chahār, and its variation chow, means "four" and the word mahal means "palace" in Urdu, Hindi and Persian.

While Salabat Jung initiated its construction in 1750, the palace was completed by the period of Afzal ad-Dawlah, Asaf Jah V between 1857 and 1869. The palace is unique for its style and elegance. Construction began in the late 18th century and over the decades a synthesis of many architectural styles and influences emerged. The palace consists of two courtyards as well as the grand Khilwat (the Darbar Hall), fountains and gardens. The palace originally covered 45 acres (180,000 m2), but only 12 acres (49,000 m2) remain today.

This is the oldest part of the palace, consisting of four palaces: Afzal Mahal, Mahtab Mahal, Tahniyat Mahal and Aftab Mahal, built symmetrically opposite each other in Neoclassical style. The forecourt between the palaces is adorned with a pond and a garden. The neoclassical palaces have double-height verandahs or façades lined with European style columns. The columns in the Aftab Mahal and Mehtab Mahal are of Ionic order whereas the Afzal Mahal and Tehniyat Mahal have Corinthian columns.

This part has Bara Imam, a long corridor of rooms on the east side facing the central fountain and pool that once housed the administrative wing; and Shishe-Alat, meaning mirror image. It has Mughal domes and arches and many Persian elements such as the ornate stucco works that adorn the Khilwat Mubarak. These were characteristic of buildings built in Hyderabad at the time. Opposite the Bara Imam is a building that is its shishe or mirror image. The rooms were once used as guest rooms for officials accompanying visiting dignitaries.

Described as "the heart of Chowmahalla Palace", it is held in high esteem by the people of Hyderabad, as it was the seat of the Asaf Jahi dynasty. The grand pillared Durbar Hall has a pure marble platform on which the Takht-e-Nishan or the royal seat was laid. Here the Nizams held their durbar and other religious and symbolic ceremonies. The 19 chandeliers of Belgian crystal were recently reinstalled to recreate the lost splendour of this regal hall.

The main gateway to the Chowmahalla Palace on the western hand has a clock tower also known as a Khilafat clock. The tower is three storeys high and consists of balconies and jharokha of Mughal style same as the style of half domes. It has been ticking since 1750. An expert family of horologists winds the mechanical clock every week.

This building housed a rare collection of manuscripts and priceless books. The Nizam often met important officials and dignitaries here. Today it is a venue for temporary exhibitions from the treasures of the Chowmahalla Palace Collection of the bygone era.

The Sixth Nizam, Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, is believed to have lived here and the building was named after his mother Roshan Begum. The former Nizam (Barkat Ali Khan Mukarram Jah) and his family decided to restore the Chowmahalla Palace and open it to the public in January 2005. It took over five years to document and restore the palaces of the first courtyard to its former glory. The palace also has a collection of vintage cars, including the Rolls-Royce, which the Nizam kings used.

raw:
gym membership terms

Gym membership agreements often look straightforward at first glance, but the fine print can hide a range of obligations that affect your budget and flexibility. Most clubs require a signed contract that locks you into a minimum commitment, usually twelve months, with the option to renew automatically unless you give written notice before the renewal date. Early termination fees can be steep, sometimes amounting to a few months' worth of dues, so it pays to read the clause that outlines how the fee is calculated.

Cancellation policies differ from one facility to another, and they can be tied to specific circumstances. Some gyms will waive the early termination fee if you relocate more than a set distance from any of their locations, while others may only consider medical reasons if you provide a doctor's note. Always verify whether the cancellation request must be submitted by certified mail, email, or an online form, because an improperly delivered notice can keep the contract active for another billing cycle.

Automatic payment setups are common, and the contract will specify the exact date each month when your card is charged. If your payment method fails, many gyms impose a late fee and may suspend your access until the balance is settled. Some clubs offer a grace period of a few days, while others enforce a hard cut-off, which can affect any classes you have already booked. Keep an eye on the statement to avoid surprise charges, especially if the gym raises its rates at the end of a promotional period.

Freezing or pausing a membership is a feature many people overlook until they need it. The terms usually allow a limited number of freeze periods per year, each lasting a maximum of thirty or sixty days, and a small administrative fee is often charged for each pause. During a freeze, you typically lose access to all amenities, and any prepaid class packages may be forfeited unless the contract explicitly protects them.

Liability waivers are another component that appears in the fine print. By signing, you agree to release the gym from responsibility for injuries sustained while using equipment or attending classes, except in cases of gross negligence. It is wise to read the waiver carefully to understand whether it also covers personal trainers, group instructors, or third-party wellness events hosted on the premises.

Finally, pay attention to the renewal clause. Some gyms automatically switch you to a month-to-month arrangement after the initial term, often at a higher rate. If you prefer to keep the original price, you may need to renegotiate before the contract expires. Knowing these details in advance can help you avoid unwanted fees and ensure that your gym membership aligns with your fitness goals and lifestyle.
