Reality shifting, also known as RS or shifting, is a cognitive activity in which practitioners attempt to transfer their awareness to alternate realities through meditation and focus. The universes targeted are often the pre-existing worlds of popular fiction, such as the Harry Potter universe or Marvel Universe. From a scientific standpoint, it is not possible to shift one's consciousness to alternate realities, and reality shifting is therefore generally viewed as a personal experience rather than an objective manipulation of reality. While shifting has been regarded as harmless, there is concern among experts about its impacts on people with pre-existing mental health conditions. Reality shifting became a trend on social media in mid-2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic. This was likely sparked by the sudden increase in social isolation and resulting stress. The practice is inspired by the New Thought movement, a new religious movement; one of its principles is that the mind can manipulate the physical world almost without limit.

Shifting generally includes aspects such as concentration and meditation, and is performed with the explicit goal of shifting one's awareness to a specific alternate universe. This distinguishes it from similar phenomena such as lucid dreaming, tulpamancy, and self-hypnosis. The desired reality may be invented by the individual, but is commonly the universe of a popular work or series. Prominent examples include the Harry Potter universe, the Marvel Universe, the Shadowhunters world, the universe of Star Wars, the science fiction series Avatar, and the worlds of various anime and manga such as My Hero Academia. Various induction techniques are employed to assist in reality shifting. For example, the "Alice in Wonderland" method involves visualizing oneself to be falling down a rabbit hole into the desired universe. Similarly, the "elevator" method requires one to imagine themselves riding an elevator up a series of floors, intensifying their "energy levels" until the top floor is reached and the elevator opens into the target reality. The "raven" method involves lying on one's back and counting to one hundred while focusing on what one plans to do in their new reality. Shifters have formed various virtual communities on social media platforms like Reddit and TikTok. Members discuss their shifts to alternate universes and share tips and tutorials on how to enhance their experience, such as through "scripting" the shift to better control the storyline, or listening to "subliminal" music. Most practitioners are teenagers and young adults.

Reality shifting has not been researched enough to directly connect it to mental health disorders. Little empirical research has been conducted on the subject; a 2026 study on reality shifting communities noted that they were "gatekept, in fear of 'pathologizing' the phenomenon." According to Joshua Klapow, a clinical psychologist, "The practice of reality shifting is not inherently unhealthy. However, if a person is using it increasingly more and more to escape their present life, concern arises." Especially within the online community, reality shifting can be reified as an actual transition to another universe. Business Insider reported on the experience of several shifters, who claimed that shifting became an obsession for them and interfered with their daily life. "Respawning" is a term for a radical escapist technique, encouraged by a fringe community within the larger shifting community. The user attempts to permanently move one's awareness to the desired reality, either by leaving behind a "clone" or "stand in" to continue to operate their body, or by inducing a physical death. On YouTube, several videos published were designed to incite a heart attack or similar "natural death" in viewers so they might respawn. Though some users commented that they felt symptoms, it is not scientifically plausible that these videos induce medical emergencies. Reality shifting, alongside The Backrooms horror media and other social media and pop culture influences, was linked to a sudden onset of tics in a 15-year-old girl.

Make Cars Green

Make Cars Green (MCG) is a campaign by the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) aimed at reducing the impact of cars on the environment. The campaign consists of advising motorists of methods of reducing carbon dioxide emissions, as well as purchasing environmentally friendlier vehicles.

The Make Cars Green campaign was launched at the 2008 World Environment Day, which was held in New Zealand. The event was attended by the FIA Foundation director General David Ward and the World Bank's road safety specialist Tony Bliss, as well as New Zealand prime minister Helen Clark. Ward outlined the importance of the campaign, noting:

The forecasts which are pretty astonishing are that over the next 20 to 30 years the vehicle fleet will double in size as China and India and other countries motorise like we did in the 1950s, 60s and 70s. At a global level we are facing a huge increase in the number of vehicles in use and that's one of the drivers behind the oil price. What we need is much more fuel efficient vehicles to accommodate the huge growing global demand for motorised travel. The basis of the campaign is a ten-point guide for reducing the environmental impact of cars, including checking tyre pressure for optimum efficiency, planning journeys in advance and offsetting carbon emissions. The FIA aims to reach these objectives by working with its member clubs.

As the FIA is the governing body of Formula One, the sport is involved in the campaign. At the 2008 Japanese Grand Prix, tyre supplier Bridgestone provided the teams with green-grooved tyres in order to draw attention to Make Cars Green. FIA president Max Mosley outlined the sport's commitment to the campaign:

New rule changes, alongside the support for awareness-raising initiatives such as the Make Cars Green campaign, will change the face of motor sport and place it at the very heart of environmental developments in the automotive sector. The FIA is determined to ensure that future investment in motor sport will also help drive the development of technologies that will benefit the public at large. The president of the Japan Automobile Federation, Tetsuo Tanaka, agreed with Mosley, adding:

By aiding the development of eco-technology, Formula One can make a significant contribution towards the effort to reduce the CO2 from road traffic. And by using its global appeal to promote Make Cars Green, the sport can encourage fans and followers alike to think green when they drive. The FIA and Bridgestone held a press conference before the grand prix where F1 drivers Felipe Massa, Kimi Räikkönen, Lewis Hamilton and Heikki Kovalainen outlined the ways in which they reduce their carbon footprints.

Asha Philip

Asha Solette Philip (born 25 October 1990) is a retired English sprinter and former junior gymnast specialising in double mini-trampoline. She was the first British woman to achieve a global 100 metres title at any age-group, winning gold at the 2007 World Youth Championships aged 16. Following a serious knee injury in gymnastics in a championship in Quebec at 17, and a rehabilitation period of several years, she returned to athletics full-time in 2014, winning gold at the European Athletics Championships in the 4 x 100 metres relay for Great Britain, and bronze in the same event at the Commonwealth Games for England. She won her first senior individual title in 2017, claiming gold at the 2017 European Athletics Indoor Championships 60 metres for women, and with Dina Asher-Smith, Desiree Henry and Daryll Neita formed part of the Great Britain 4 x 100 m relay squad which won an Olympic bronze medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay at the 2016 Rio Games. She also won silver medals in the same event at the 2017 and 2019 World Championships. A noted fast starter and 60 metre sprinter, Philip generally runs the first leg on relay duty. Domestically, Philip is a 10-time national champion with six victories indoors over 60 metres, and four outdoors over 100 metres.

Philip had competed in double mini trampoline since aged 4. She was a World Junior Champion on double mini-trampoline, winning gold in the junior (15-16 years old) girls category in the world age competition in Eindhoven, Netherlands. In July 2007, Philip won the World Youth Athletics Championships gold in the 100 metres, but shortly afterwards suffered a serious cruciate ligament injury representing Great Britain in the double-mini team event at the senior Trampoline World Championships in Quebec, Canada, which halted her sporting career entirely for three years. This ruled her out of a chance at selection for the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing, China. On her return from injury, Philip completed solely in athletics, and was part of the Great Britain teams that won a silver medal in the 4 x 200 metres relay at the 2014 IAAF World Relays, and a gold medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay at the 2014 European Championships. In the same year, representing England, she won a bronze medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay and finished fourth in the 100 metres final at the 2014 Commonwealth Games. In 2016, she competed at the Olympic Games in Rio. Philip reached the semi-finals of the 100 metres, but did not qualify for the finals. Philip then went on to win a bronze medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay, along with teammates Desiree Henry, Dina Asher-Smith and Daryll Neita. The quartet set a new British record with a time of 41.77 seconds.

Born in Leyton, East London to an Antiguan father and a Jamaican mother, Philip attended Connaught School for Girls in Leytonstone. She graduated from Kingston University in 2012, with a BA (Hons) degree in drama.

Asha Solette Philip (born 25 October 1990) is a retired English sprinter and former junior gymnast specialising in double mini-trampoline. She was the first British woman to achieve a global 100 metres title at any age-group, winning gold at the 2007 World Youth Championships aged 16. Following a serious knee injury in gymnastics in a championship in Quebec at 17, and a rehabilitation period of several years, she returned to athletics full-time in 2014, winning gold at the European Athletics Championships in the 4 x 100 metres relay for Great Britain, and bronze in the same event at the Commonwealth Games for England. She won her first senior individual title in 2017, claiming gold at the 2017 European Athletics Indoor Championships 60 metres for women, and with Dina Asher-Smith, Desiree Henry and Daryll Neita formed part of the Great Britain 4 x 100 m relay squad which won an Olympic bronze medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay at the 2016 Rio Games. She also won silver medals in the same event at the 2017 and 2019 World Championships. A noted fast starter and 60 metre sprinter, Philip generally runs the first leg on relay duty. Domestically, Philip is a 10-time national champion with six victories indoors over 60 metres, and four outdoors over 100 metres.

Philip had competed in double mini trampoline since aged 4. She was a World Junior Champion on double mini-trampoline, winning gold in the junior (15-16 years old) girls category in the world age competition in Eindhoven, Netherlands. In July 2007, Philip won the World Youth Athletics Championships gold in the 100 metres, but shortly afterwards suffered a serious cruciate ligament injury representing Great Britain in the double-mini team event at the senior Trampoline World Championships in Quebec, Canada, which halted her sporting career entirely for three years. This ruled her out of a chance at selection for the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing, China. On her return from injury, Philip completed solely in athletics, and was part of the Great Britain teams that won a silver medal in the 4 x 200 metres relay at the 2014 IAAF World Relays, and a gold medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay at the 2014 European Championships. In the same year, representing England, she won a bronze medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay and finished fourth in the 100 metres final at the 2014 Commonwealth Games. In 2016, she competed at the Olympic Games in Rio. Philip reached the semi-finals of the 100 metres, but did not qualify for the finals. Philip then went on to win a bronze medal in the 4 x 100 metres relay, along with teammates Desiree Henry, Dina Asher-Smith and Daryll Neita. The quartet set a new British record with a time of 41.77 seconds.

Born in Leyton, East London to an Antiguan father and a Jamaican mother, Philip attended Connaught School for Girls in Leytonstone. She graduated from Kingston University in 2012, with a BA (Hons) degree in drama.

Bridgeport, Illinois

Home | About | Contact

Bridgeport was established in the mid-1850s as a stop along the Ohio and Mississippi Railway. It was named by a railroad official for the bridge that spanned Indian Creek, in the southern part of the city. Bridgeport incorporated in 1896.

Bridgeport lies southwest of Lawrenceville along Illinois State Route 250. According to the 2021 census gazetteer files, Bridgeport has a total area of 1.10 square miles (2.85 km2), of which 1.07 square miles (2.77 km2) (or 97.72%) is land and 0.03 square miles (0.08 km2) (or 2.28%) is water.

As of the 2020 census, Bridgeport had a population of 1,800. The median age was 39.4 years. 25.1% of residents were under the age of 18 and 16.1% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 100.7 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 96.6 males age 18 and over. 0.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 100.0% lived in rural areas. There were 719 households in Bridgeport, of which 33.7% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 42.1% were married-couple households, 20.0% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 31.6% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 31.3% of all households were made up of individuals and 14.3% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The population density was 1,640.84 inhabitants per square mile (633.53/km2). There were 812 housing units at an average density of 740.20 per square mile (285.79/km2). Of Bridgeport's housing units, 11.5% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.6% and the rental vacancy rate was 9.0%.

The median income for a household in the city was $58,085, and the median income for a family was $48,958. Males had a median income of $50,712 versus $27,875 for females. The per capita income for the city was $30,074. About 12.9% of families and 10.4% of the population were below the poverty line, including 11.1% of those under age 18 and 7.3% of those age 65 or over.

The Red Hill Junior/Senior High School is located in Bridgeport. The school mascot is the Saluki (Red Hill Salukis). Prior to the 1970s, the local high school was named Bridgeport High School. Its mascot was the Bulldogs. Bridgeport High School then consolidated with the neighboring town of Sumner, and the mascot for the new consolidated school became the Salukis. There is also an elementary school in Bridgeport called BGS, or Bridgeport Grade School.

The Red Hill Junior High School Lady Salukis 2008 softball team went to the Illinois state championship and placed second. In 1960, Bridgeport High School had a total school enrollment of only 385. That year the boys basketball team advanced to the State of Illinois IHSA basketball tournament finals to face a much larger Chicago team, John Marshall. At the time, Illinois, like Indiana in the movie Hoosiers, held a single-class tournament where all schools competed for the same championship. Chicago Marshall's enrollment was listed at 2,333, more than six times that of Bridgeport. Unlike the Indiana team in Hoosiers, Bridgeport lost the championship game, finishing its season with a 33-2 record.

John Lankston, tenor with the New York City Opera and actor in Broadway musicals Gary Wagner, a pitcher for the Philadelphia Phillies and Boston Red Sox, was born in Bridgeport.

clinic appointment reminder

A clinic appointment reminder is more than a courtesy; it is a critical tool that bridges the gap between scheduled care and patient attendance. Missed appointments cost health systems billions each year, disrupt provider schedules, and delay essential treatment for patients. By delivering timely, clear reminders, clinics can reduce no-shows, improve resource utilization, and demonstrate a patient-centered approach that respects both the patient's time and the clinic's operational efficiency.

Modern reminder systems leverage multiple communication channels to reach patients where they are most likely to see them. Text messages, often favored for their immediacy and high open rates, can convey essential details such as date, time, provider name, and any preparation instructions. Email reminders offer a larger canvas for additional information, like forms to complete ahead of the visit or links to patient portals. For patients who prefer a personal touch, automated voice calls can confirm the appointment while allowing a simple "press 1 to confirm" interaction.

Effective reminders follow a strategic timing pattern that balances awareness with convenience. A first notice sent a week in advance gives patients ample time to adjust their schedule if needed, while a second, shorter reminder 24-48 hours before the appointment serves as a final prompt. Some clinics also include a post-appointment follow-up to thank patients for their visit and to remind them of any prescribed next steps, reinforcing continuity of care. The key is to avoid overwhelming patients with excessive messages, which can lead to alert fatigue and diminish the reminder's impact.

Privacy and compliance are paramount when handling patient contact information. Clinics must ensure that reminder content adheres to HIPAA guidelines, avoiding the inclusion of sensitive health details in messages that could be seen by others. Secure opt-in mechanisms allow patients to choose their preferred method of communication, and clear opt-out options maintain trust while respecting individual preferences. Regular audits of the reminder system help identify any lapses and keep the process aligned with evolving regulations.

Integrating the reminder platform with the clinic's electronic medical record (EMR) streamlines the workflow and reduces manual entry errors. When the EMR automatically triggers reminders based on the appointment schedule, staff can focus on direct patient care instead of administrative tasks. Data from the reminder system, such as confirmation rates and patterns of rescheduling, can also provide valuable insights for continuous improvement, enabling clinics to fine-tune their outreach strategies and ultimately deliver better health outcomes.

Shiner Catholic School

Shiner Catholic School is a private, Roman Catholic K-12 school in Shiner, Texas. It is located in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Victoria in Texas. It has two components: St. Lumila Elementary School and St. Paul High School.

The educational complex comprising St. Ludmila Elementary and St. Paul High School became known as Shiner Catholic School in 1997. In 2012, the Janak Music Center was completed. The building serves students in grades K-12 beginning in the 2012-2013 school year. In late 2018 a new building was completed on the school campus. It is the Administration / PreK building and it serves as the main entrance to Shiner Catholic School.

St. Paul High School students compete in Football, Volleyball, Baseball, Softball, Track, Cross Country, Golf, Swimming and Tennis through the Texas Association of Private and Public School (TAPPS). The school teams hold numerous state titles:

Football - 11-man Football (10 TAPPS State championships and 1 TCIL State championships) 2021 Div IV 2020 Div IV; 2019 Div IV; 2018 Div IV; 2016 Div IV; 2015 Div III; 2012 Div III; 2010 Div IV; 1997 2A; 1992 1A; 1987 TCIL Cross country - girls:2019, 2018, 2017, 2016, 2015, 2014, 2013, 2010, 2009, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019 Cross country - boys: 2017 State runner up, 2016 State runner up, 2015, 2005 Volleyball: 1994 1A; 1993 1A Basketball - girls: 2017 2A; 1998 1A; 1992 1A Track - girls:2021, 2019, 2018, 2017, 2016, 2015 Track - boys: 2021 State runner up, 2018 State Runner up, 2017, 2016, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018 Golf - : 2018 - 2A; 2017 - 2A Baseball:2023 2A/; 2013 1A/2A; 2011 1A/2A; 2009 1A/2A; 2006 2A; 2005 2A; 2003 2A; 1999 1A; 1998 2A; 1995 1A; 1989 2A Softball: 2019 2A; 2016 1A/2A; 2012 1A/2A; 2011 1A/2A; 2005 2A; 2004 1A/2A; 1999 1A/2A; 1997 2A; 1996 1A; 1995 1A; 1994 1A; 1993 1A, 2017, 2018

TAPPS awards an Over-All State Championship Trophy - The Henderson Championship Cup to the school in each classification that accumulates the most points in all competitions in order to recognize state champions in Art, Academics, Vocal, Instrumental Music, and various team sports. St. Paul High School was awarded the Henderson 2A Overall Championship Cup for the 2010-2011, 2011-2012, 2015-2016, 2016-2017; 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2020-2021 school year.

Philip Abraham (writer)

Philip Abraham was born into a prominent Jewish family affiliated with London's Western Synagogue. In 1849, he assumed the role of Headmaster at the National Hebrew School in Birmingham. After several years he relocated to London, where he worked as a private instructor in languages and Judaic studies, as well as Secretary of the West London Synagogue. Abraham regularly contributed poetry and articles to the Jewish press, including The Jewish Chronicle. Among his publications were The Autobiography of a Jewish Gentleman (1860); Autumn Gatherings, a collection of prose and poetry (London, 1866); and Ha-Nistarot veha-Niglot ('The Secret and Revealed Things'), or Curiosities of Judaism: Facts, Opinions, Anecdotes, and Remarks Relative to the Hebrew Nation (London, 1879). His daughter, Leonora Braham, was an opera singer and actress famous for originating several of the Gilbert and Sullivan soprano roles.

Fantasy Publishing Company, Inc.

Fantasy Publishing Company, Inc., or FPCI, was an American science fiction and fantasy small press specialty publishing company established in 1946. It was the fourth small press company founded by William L. Crawford. Crawford's first company was Fantasy Publications which he started in 1935 in Everett, Pennsylvania, primarily to publish his magazines Marvel Tales and Unusual Stories. However, three books were published under the imprint. In 1936, Crawford initiated his second company, Visionary Publishing Company, with the intention of publishing books with this imprint. Visionary is notable for publishing the only hardcover book by H. P. Lovecraft that was published during his lifetime. Later in 1936, Crawford assumed management of publication of Fantasy Magazine from Conrad H. Ruppert and ceased all book publications in order to concentrate on the magazine. After relocating to California, Crawford again published books as "A Crawford Publication". Finally, he incorporated as Fantasy Publishing Company, Inc. in December 1946. Forrest J. Ackerman served as a partner for the company and many of the books published by FPCI were from authors Ackerman represented as agent. Undercapitalization was a major problem with FPCI and many of the books had a cheap look. FPCI reprinted a number of novels by John Taine, Ralph Milne Farley, Stanton Coblentz and L. Ron Hubbard. FPCI continued publishing books until 1972. During this period, Crawford also used the Griffin Publishing Company to publish books which were not science fiction or fantasy. Two additional books were published by Crawford in 1978, but a publisher was not cited.

houseplant care

Houseplants have moved from a niche hobby to a staple of modern interior design, offering more than just a splash of green. A thriving leaf can soften a stark hallway, improve air quality, and even lift mood on a rainy day. The trick to keeping those glossy fronds looking their best lies in understanding the basic needs that each species shares, then tailoring care to the specific quirks of the plant you choose. With a few simple habits, you can turn a modest windowsill garden into a resilient, low-maintenance display.

Light is the most immediate factor in a plant's health, yet it's often the easiest to overlook. Most tropical houseplants thrive in bright, indirect light, meaning a spot near an east-facing window works well, while direct afternoon sun can scorch tender leaves. Conversely, shade-loving varieties such as ZZ or snake plants can survive in lower light levels, though they will grow more slowly. To gauge whether a spot is suitable, watch the plant's foliage: yellowing or pale growth usually signals too much sun, whereas leggy stems reaching for a brighter source point to insufficient light.

Watering is a balancing act that depends on species, pot size, and seasonal changes. A good rule of thumb is to let the top inch of soil dry out before the next drink, but this can vary; succulents need far less moisture than ferns. Overwatering is a common mistake, often leading to root rot, which appears as a soft, mushy base and a musty smell. During winter months many plants enter a semi-dormant state and require less water, while summer growth spurts may call for more frequent watering. Adding a pebble tray or misting can boost humidity for moisture-loving plants, but avoid creating standing water that encourages fungal problems.

The growing medium is more than a filler; it dictates drainage, aeration, and nutrient availability. A lightweight, well-draining mix-typically a blend of peat, perlite, and bark-is ideal for most indoor foliage, while cactus and succulent mixes contain extra sand or pumice to prevent water retention. Repotting every one to two years refreshes the soil, gives roots room to expand, and helps prevent compacted media that can suffocate the plant. When moving a plant, gently loosen the root ball, trim any dead or blackened roots, and place it at the same depth it occupied in its previous container to reduce shock.

Pests such as spider mites, mealybugs, and aphids can quickly turn a healthy plant into a struggling one, but early detection makes control easier. Regularly inspect the undersides of leaves and the stem joints for tiny insects or webbing, and wipe them away with a damp cloth if you spot any. A mild solution of water and dish soap, applied with a spray bottle, can suppress most infestations without harming the plant. Keeping the growing area clean, avoiding excessive fertilizer, and maintaining proper airflow also create an environment less inviting to pests. By staying observant and adjusting watering, light, and soil as needed, you'll give your houseplants the stability they need to flourish year after year.

Subject: Required Action: Parking Permit Renewal for Incoming Term
Dear Resident,
I hope this message finds you well and that you have started the new term on a positive note. I am writing to formally notify you that the renewal deadline for your annual parking permit is rapidly approaching. Our office has identified your permit, ending in 4821, as expiring on May 15th of this year. To avoid any interruption in your access to the designated residential zones, it is crucial that you complete the renewal process before our maintenance window closes at 11:59 PM on May 10th. We understand that the start of the semester creates a busy environment, but administrative deadlines cannot be extended, and we want to ensure you are not caught off guard by an unexpected lapse in status.
The renewal procedure has been updated this year to improve security and streamline the verification process for all residents. You will need to log into the central housing portal using your student ID password. Once logged in, navigate to the transportation section and select the option for annual permit renewal. Note that we have removed the option to renew via paper forms to reduce administrative errors. During this digital upload phase, you will be required to verify the make, model, and specific color of your vehicle if you are changing cars from the previous year. If your vehicle remains the same, you will still need to confirm the existing data to acknowledge that the information on file is accurate. This step is mandatory for everyone, regardless of whether there has been a change in your primary vehicle.
There are a few financial details you should be aware of before initiating the payment step. The base fee for the standard residential spot remains unchanged at one hundred and twenty dollars. However, if you previously elected to purchase the guest access package, please be aware that this add-on is now priced at an additional thirty dollars due to decreased availability in the overflow lot. You may choose to waive the guest access to minimize costs, but please note that this decision is locked in until the next cycle. Payment can be made securely via credit card, debit card, or directly from your university billing account. We strongly encourage using the billing account method because it ensures automatic deductions and removes the risk of missed payment dates in future years.
If you have parked in a restricted zone during the past month, it is possible that outstanding fines are associated with your account. The system requires all balances to be zero before a new permit is activated. If you see a red banner indicating a balance due, please review the incident log carefully. Sometimes, these are automated errors based on license plate recognition glitches. In such cases, you should download the evidence photos provided in the portal and submit an appeal discrepancy report. Do not attempt to pay and appeal simultaneously, as this often complicates the refund processing timeline. It is always better to resolve disputes first, update the balance, and then proceed with the renewal immediately after the dispute is cleared.
Please treat this matter with urgency, as our office becomes flooded with requests during the final forty-eight hours before the deadline. The portal servers often experience lag and timeouts during this peak period, which can result in failed transactions or lost sessions. We recommend completing your renewal at least three days prior to the May 10th cut-off date to allow sufficient time to troubleshoot any technical issues. If you encounter persistent login errors or if your billing account does not reflect the correct residence hall status, please contact the transportation services desk directly. A member of our staff is available to assist you with manual overrides or verification steps. Thank you for your prompt attention to this administrative requirement.
Sincerely,
Office of Transportation Services
University Residential Affairs

To: All Staff and Residents 
From: Office of Emergency Management 
Date: October 8, 2026 
Subject: Flood Preparedness - Key Actions and Resources

Recent weather patterns have increased the likelihood of significant flooding across our region, making it essential for every individual and department to be fully prepared. This notice outlines the critical steps we expect all personnel and community members to follow in order to protect lives, property, and continuity of operations. Familiarize yourself with the recommended procedures now; a timely response can dramatically reduce the impact of an unexpected flood event.

First, review the flood risk maps posted on the intranet and at the main office. These maps identify zones that are prone to river overflow, storm-driven surge, and flash flooding. If your work area or residence falls within a high-risk zone, you must develop a personal evacuation plan that includes at least two alternate routes, a designated meeting point, and a contact list for family or household members. Keep this plan accessible on a smartphone, printed copy, or in a readily available digital folder. For those in low-risk zones, maintain awareness of nearby higher-risk areas and the routes that may become compromised during heavy rain.

Second, assemble an emergency kit that can sustain each household member for a minimum of 72 hours. The kit should contain potable water, non-perishable food, a flashlight with extra batteries, a first-aid set, a portable phone charger, and any essential prescription medications. Additionally, include important documents such as identification, insurance policies, and emergency contacts in a waterproof container. If you have pets, be sure to pack food, leashes, and a carrier. Store the kit in an elevated location to avoid water damage, and verify that it is ready for immediate use at least once each quarter.

Third, safeguard critical equipment and records by moving them to higher ground or waterproof storage. Computers, servers, and paper files should be placed above the anticipated flood line, preferably on the second floor or on elevated platforms. If relocation is not feasible, cover items with sandbags, tarps, or commercial flood barriers as directed by the facilities team. Regularly back up digital data to an off-site cloud service and retain a hard-copy copy of essential documents in a secure, dry place. These measures help ensure that essential operations can resume quickly after floodwaters recede.

Finally, stay informed during inclement weather by monitoring official alerts from the National Weather Service, local emergency management agencies, and the company's notification system. Activate the "Flood Watch" protocol on your mobile devices and keep radios or televisions on standby for real-time updates. In the event of an evacuation order, follow the instructions of emergency personnel without delay, and report your status to your supervisor or the designated safety coordinator. Remember that personal safety is the top priority; do not attempt to retrieve belongings from flooded areas.

Preparedness is a shared responsibility that protects not only individual households but also the broader community and our organization's mission. We will conduct a tabletop exercise next month to test these protocols and identify any gaps in our response plan. Participation is mandatory for all department heads, and attendance will be recorded. Should you have questions or require assistance assembling your flood kit, contact the Emergency Management Office at extension 245 or via email floodprep@citygov.org. Thank you for your cooperation and commitment to keeping our community safe.

To: All Staff and Residents 
From: Office of Emergency Management 
Date: October 8, 2026 
Subject: Flood Preparedness - Key Actions and Resources

Recent weather patterns have increased the likelihood of significant flooding across our region, making it essential for every individual and department to be fully prepared. This notice outlines the critical steps we expect all personnel and community members to follow in order to protect lives, property, and continuity of operations. Familiarize yourself with the recommended procedures now; a timely response can dramatically reduce the impact of an unexpected flood event.

First, review the flood risk maps posted on the intranet and at the main office. These maps identify zones that are prone to river overflow, storm-driven surge, and flash flooding. If your work area or residence falls within a high-risk zone, you must develop a personal evacuation plan that includes at least two alternate routes, a designated meeting point, and a contact list for family or household members. Keep this plan accessible on a smartphone, printed copy, or in a readily available digital folder. For those in low-risk zones, maintain awareness of nearby higher-risk areas and the routes that may become compromised during heavy rain.

Second, assemble an emergency kit that can sustain each household member for a minimum of 72 hours. The kit should contain potable water, non-perishable food, a flashlight with extra batteries, a first-aid set, a portable phone charger, and any essential prescription medications. Additionally, include important documents such as identification, insurance policies, and emergency contacts in a waterproof container. If you have pets, be sure to pack food, leashes, and a carrier. Store the kit in an elevated location to avoid water damage, and verify that it is ready for immediate use at least once each quarter.

Third, safeguard critical equipment and records by moving them to higher ground or waterproof storage. Computers, servers, and paper files should be placed above the anticipated flood line, preferably on the second floor or on elevated platforms. If relocation is not feasible, cover items with sandbags, tarps, or commercial flood barriers as directed by the facilities team. Regularly back up digital data to an off-site cloud service and retain a hard-copy copy of essential documents in a secure, dry place. These measures help ensure that essential operations can resume quickly after floodwaters recede.

Finally, stay informed during inclement weather by monitoring official alerts from the National Weather Service, local emergency management agencies, and the company's notification system. Activate the "Flood Watch" protocol on your mobile devices and keep radios or televisions on standby for real-time updates. In the event of an evacuation order, follow the instructions of emergency personnel without delay, and report your status to your supervisor or the designated safety coordinator. Remember that personal safety is the top priority; do not attempt to retrieve belongings from flooded areas.

Preparedness is a shared responsibility that protects not only individual households but also the broader community and our organization's mission. We will conduct a tabletop exercise next month to test these protocols and identify any gaps in our response plan. Participation is mandatory for all department heads, and attendance will be recorded. Should you have questions or require assistance assembling your flood kit, contact the Emergency Management Office at extension 245 or via email floodprep@citygov.org. Thank you for your cooperation and commitment to keeping our community safe.

Subject: Smart Home Device Options for the Upcoming Renovation
Hi Maria,
I've been reviewing the latest smart home product releases in preparation for our office renovation, and a few solutions stand out as both practical and scalable. The new generation of Wi-Fi thermostats, adaptive lighting panels, and voice-controlled security hubs can significantly cut energy costs while giving us tighter control over the work environment.
In particular, a programmable thermostat that learns our heating patterns can reduce heating bills by up to 15 percent during the winter months. Coupled with motion-sensing LED strips, we can automatically dim lights in unused conference rooms, extending bulb life and improving our sustainability metrics. The integrated security camera system also offers real-time alerts on mobile devices, which would be useful for after-hours monitoring.
All of these devices communicate via a single cloud-based platform, meaning we can manage settings from a single dashboard. However, I'm aware that consolidating data raises privacy questions, so any vendor we choose should provide end-to-end encryption and clear data-retention policies.
I recommend we arrange a short demo with two of the leading suppliers next week. This would let us evaluate ease of installation, compatibility with our existing network, and total cost of ownership before we commit.
Please let me know your availability, and I'll coordinate the meeting. Looking forward to your thoughts.
Best regards,
Ethan Patel
Facilities Manager

Cold Spring murders

On September 13, 1868, in what became known as the Cold Spring murders, the bodies of Jacob and Nancy Young were found along White River in Cold Spring, near Indianapolis. Both the husband and wife had been shot in the head the day before, and a gun belonging to William J. Abrams was found near the crime scene. Abrams, Silas Hartman and Hartman's sister Nancy Clem were arrested for the murders. The crime attracted nationwide attention at the time due to one of the murder suspects, Clem, being a woman. Benjamin Harrison, who later became the 23rd President of the United States, gained fame as the public prosecutor in Clem's murder trials.

William Abrams was arrested on September 15, 1868, followed by Silas Hartman on September 21, and Nancy Clem on October 7. Evidence suggested that Nancy Clem, a businesswoman, had been involved in a business scam and was heavily indebted to one of the victims, Jacob Young. Due to the circumstantial evidence, the first trial resulted in a hung jury. All three suspects were found guilty in the subsequent second trial. Hartman then confessed to the murders and later committed suicide in his cell. Abrams was convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment; he was pardoned by Governor James D. Williams in 1878. Clem's murder conviction in the second trial was touted as prosecutor Benjamin Harrison's greatest courtroom victory at the time. However, the Indiana Supreme Court overturned the guilty verdict, and Harrison retried the case, again winning a conviction. After the second murder conviction was again overturned by the State Supreme Court, Boone County commissioners dismissed the case. Clem was tried five times for the murders in total but was never convicted for them. Clem was later convicted of perjury and forgery in another case involving a financial scam, for which she received a 4-year sentence.

Clem, N. E., Hartman, S. W., & Marion County (Ind.). (1869). The Cold Spring tragedy: Trial and conviction of Mrs. Nancy E. Clem for the murder of Jacob Young and wife... Indianapolis, Ind: A.C. Roach. Gamber, Wendy (2016). The Notorious Mrs. Clem: Murder and Money in the Gilded Age. Johns Hopkins University Press. ISBN 9781421424279.

power outage notice

A power outage notice has just been posted on the city's utility website, warning residents that scheduled maintenance will affect several neighborhoods this Friday night. The notice specifies a start time of 10:00 p.m. and an expected restoration window between 4:00 and 6:00 a.m. on Saturday, but it also advises that delays are possible if weather conditions change.

The affected areas include the downtown business district, the riverfront apartments, and most of the suburban cul-de-sacs on Maple Avenue. Residents who rely on medical equipment that requires electricity are urged to contact the utility's emergency line as soon as possible so that a backup generator can be arranged. The utility's spokesperson emphasized that the outage will be isolated to the listed zones and will not impact the hospital or fire stations, which have dedicated power supplies.

In preparation, homeowners should unplug sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, and home theater systems to protect them from potential surges when power returns. Refrigerators and freezers should be left closed as much as possible to preserve food, and a supply of flashlights, batteries, and a battery-powered radio can help keep families informed and safe throughout the night. If you have a security system, check that it has a battery backup and that the sensors are functioning correctly.

Transportation may be affected as well. Traffic lights on Main Street will be switched to flashing mode, and some crosswalk signals will not operate. Drivers are encouraged to allow extra travel time and to use caution at intersections, especially where visibility is reduced. Public transit routes that normally run through the outage zone may be rerouted, so checking the transit authority's app before leaving home is advisable.

Finally, the utility has set up a temporary hotline and an online chat service for any questions or concerns. The phone line will be staffed from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on both Friday and Saturday. Updates will also be posted hourly on the utility's social-media channels, so residents should keep an eye on those feeds for any changes to the schedule.

Subject: Quick notes on our EV charging routine for the work trip
Hi Mark,
I wanted to reach out before we finalize the itinerary for next month's cross-country drive. Since we will be covering roughly two thousand miles, I think it is prudent to map out our charging strategy in advance to avoid any unnecessary delays or range anxiety. I have been looking into the current status of the EV infrastructure along our primary route, and while it has improved significantly over the past few years, there are still some gaps in remote areas that we need to account for when planning our daily mileage and rest stops.
The most critical section of the trip appears to be the stretch between Denver and Phoenix. In urban centers, finding fast chargers is rarely an issue, but the infrastructure becomes sparse once we hit the state lines in Arizona. I recommend that we limit our daily driving to around three hundred to four hundred miles during this segment. This will allow us to charge at a comfortable pace, typically in twenty to thirty minutes, while we catch up on emails or take a proper break. Trying to drive longer distances without a dedicated charging stop could leave us stuck waiting for a functional station, especially if a cloud is down or if we arrive at a port with a line of other drivers.
I also suggest we verify the app compatibility for the stations we plan to use. While many networks are integrating their systems, we should ensure that both our personal devices and the vehicle's interface are up to date before we depart. It might be helpful to have a backup card for a competitor network just in case the primary apps experience server issues. I have noted the locations of the major stations near our hotel stops and those in the mid-size towns we will pass through, which should give us plenty of flexibility if a preferred location is unavailable or simply busy during peak hours.
Finally, keep in mind that charging speeds can vary dramatically based on the ambient temperature and the state of the battery. Cold weather, which we might encounter in the northern parts of the route, will likely reduce our efficiency and slow down the charging process. To mitigate this, we should aim to pre-condition the vehicle's battery before we arrive at a charger if the forecast calls for low temperatures. Additionally, we should avoid letting the battery drop below ten percent, as many fast chargers throttle their output when the battery is very low or nearly full, making those last or first ten percent take much longer to charge.
Let me know if you have any other concerns or specific preferences for the types of stops. I am happy to coordinate further details once we confirm the exact dates and flight schedules. This level of planning should ensure a smooth and stress-free journey, allowing us to focus on the client meetings rather than the logistics of our transportation. I look forward to hearing your thoughts on this proposed schedule and any adjustments you might recommend based on your previous travel experiences.
Best regards,
Sarah Jenkins

Kiko the Kangaroo

Kiko the Kangaroo is a fictional kangaroo appearing in theatrical cartoons produced by Terrytoons. He is featured in ten cartoons made between 1936 and 1937.

As with various anthropomorphic animals at the time, Kiko wears shorts and shoes. While he does not speak, the marsupial is skilled in hand-to-hand fighting, and would use his prowess to defend his troubled friends or subdue an opponent in a boxing match. He can also use his tail for various purposes. Kiko was created by Terrytoons in a desperate attempt to rival characters of other studios. He first appeared in Farmer Al Falfa's Prize Package as a pet sent to the farmer by the latter's brother. Since then, the kangaroo would spend the rest of his short theatrical run in a series of his own. After only ten cartoons were released, plans were made to create another cartoon featuring him, only to be not approved by Paul Terry. Kiko is also among the few characters of the studio to have a theme song. He also has merchandise including plush toys.

Below is a list of films in their original titles. Some of them later came with alternate names when distributed by other companies like Castle Films.

Charles Douglas Kyle (born September 25, 1947) is an American former football linebacker in the Canadian Football League (CFL) for the Saskatchewan Roughriders. He played college football at Purdue University.

Kyle grew up in Fort Thomas, Kentucky. He attended Highlands High School, where he practiced football, shot put and also won a state diving championship. He accepted a football scholarship from Purdue University. He was a three-year starter at the middle guard position. He was an All-Big Ten player in 1966 (UPI-1), 1967 (AP-1, UPI-1), and 1968 (AP-1, UPI-1). He was also a consensus first-team selection as a middle guard on the 1968 College Football All-America Team.

Kyle was selected by the Dallas Cowboys in the fifth round (125th overall) of the 1969 NFL draft. He was waived on September 15. In 1969, he signed with the Saskatchewan Roughriders of the Canadian Football League. He appeared in 6 games and played in the 57th Grey Cup. In 1971, he played in 12 games and registered 2 interceptions. On June 9, 1971, he was traded to the Montreal Alouettes in exchange for linebacker Charlie Collins. He was released on July 23. On February 5, 1972, he was signed as a free agent by the New York Jets. He was waived injured on August 8.

Togo Yamamoto

Togo Yamamoto (山本冬郷, Yamamoto Tōgō; November 4, 1886 - March 24, 1952) was a pioneering actor who appeared on stage and film in the United States and Japan.

Born in Yokohama, Japan, on 4 November 1886, Togo emigrated to the United States and began an acting career in the early years of the 20th century. Yamamoto told Blanche Partington in a 1906 interview that he had been "in the dramatic business" in Japan, playing "tragedy, comedy, both" before coming to the United States. His first appearance on the American stage was in The White Tigress of Japan (1904), a play about the Russo-Japanese War. "I was Japanese spy-I killed half a dozen Russians every night!" he told Partington. Theatrical manager Kirke La Shelle spotted him in the production and hired him to play the part of a Japanese servant in The Heir to the Hoorah (1905). Yamamoto subsequently appeared in a number of stage plays, including The Offenders (1908), An American Widow (1909), The Inferior Sex (1910), The Muezzin (1910), Kismet (1911), Miss Phoenix (1913), and others. In 1918, Yamamoto made his first appearances on the silver screen in The Midnight Patrol (1918) and The City of Dim Faces (1918). In both films he played Chinese characters, as he did in many of his later American films. He appeared in more than a dozen American films, most notably Cecil B. DeMille's Something to Think About (1920), in which he played a Japanese servant, and Flesh and Blood, a 1922 film starring Lon Chaney, in which he played a Chinese character, The Prince.

In 1925, Yamamoto returned to his native Japan and appeared with Tokihiko Okada in a film entitled Maboroshi no hansen. After a four-year hiatus, he returned to the Japanese screen in two 1929 films and no fewer than eleven 1930 films, including Sono yo no tsuma and Ojosan, both directed by Yasujirō Ozu. He worked steadily through the 1930s, appearing in more than 40 films, working with directors like Ozu and Hiroshi Shimizu, usually in supporting roles. In the 1940s, however, he appeared in only a handful of films. Among his last were Nishi manrui (Two outs, Bases Loaded, 1946) and Yottsu no koi no monogatari (Four Tales of Passion, 1947).

Students enrolled in HIST 301, Advanced European Modern History, are required to review this updated syllabus carefully before the first lecture begins on August twenty-fourth. This document serves as the primary contractual agreement between the instructor and the student body, outlining all academic expectations, grading policies, and logistical arrangements for the semester. Failure to read and understand the contents of this syllabus will be treated as a lack of professional preparation and may result in academic penalties for late submissions or missed deadlines. Please print a copy for personal reference and keep it in your course folder for easy access during office hours and final exam preparation sessions.

The primary learning objective for this course is to develop critical analytical skills regarding the political and social transformations in Europe between 1789 and 1945. We will move beyond simple chronological memorization to explore the interconnectedness of economic shifts, cultural movements, and diplomatic crises. Students should expect to engage deeply with primary sources, including treaties, personal diaries, and government pamphlets, to construct nuanced arguments about historical causality. The final research paper, which constitutes thirty percent of the total grade, requires original thesis development supported by at least ten credible academic sources from the university library database.

Grading is distributed as follows: twenty percent for participation and weekly discussion posts, twenty percent for mid-term and final examinations, fifteen percent for a group presentation, thirty percent for the final research paper, and fifteen percent for attendance and punctuality. Attendance policy is strict because the discussions rely heavily on consecutive dialogue; missing more than three unexcused classes will result in a letter grade drop. Late work is accepted only under documented emergency circumstances and incurs a ten percent deduction per day after the initial twenty-four-hour grace period. Plagiarism of any kind is a zero-credit violation that triggers an immediate referral to the Academic Integrity Board, regardless of intent or academic year.

Required materials include the main textbook, The Age of Revolution by Eric Hobsbawm, the fourth edition, and a digital access code to the JSTOR archive provided through the campus portal. Optional readings are marked with an asterisk in the weekly schedule and are recommended for students seeking higher distinction marks. All technology used for lectures and assignments must comply with the university's digital accessibility standards, and students with documented disabilities should schedule a meeting with the Disability Resource Center within the first two weeks of the term to arrange reasonable accommodations.

Office hours are held Tuesdays and Thursdays from two to four in the East Hall, Room 304, but virtual appointments are strongly encouraged to maximize convenience. Email inquiries must be followed up by a set response time of forty-eight hours, so urgent matters should be brought to in-person sessions. Students are expected to maintain a professional tone in all written communications and to use the approved citation format throughout the semester. Any changes to this syllabus after the first week will be communicated via the learning management system and reflected in the course calendar, so students are responsible for checking their student email accounts at least once daily.

Tropical cyclones in 1994

During 1994, tropical cyclones formed within seven different tropical cyclone basins, located within various parts of the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans. During the year, a total of 124 systems formed with 91 of these developing further and were named by the responsible warning centre. The strongest tropical cyclone of the year was Cyclone Geralda, which was estimated to have a minimum barometric pressure of 905 hPa (26.72 inHg). The deadliest tropical cyclone was Typhoon Fred, which caused 1,248 fatalities in China, while the costliest was Tropical Storm Sharon, which caused an estimated $5.27 billion USD in damage after striking Hong Kong, China and the Philippines. Five Category 5 tropical cyclones formed in 1994. The accumulated cyclone energy (ACE) index for 1994 (seven basins combined), as calculated by Colorado State University was 1019 units. Tropical cyclone activity in each basin is under the authority of an RSMC. The National Hurricane Center (NHC) is responsible for tropical cyclones in the North Atlantic and East Pacific. The Central Pacific Hurricane Center (CPHC) is responsible for tropical cyclones in the Central Pacific. Both the NHC and CPHC are subdivisions of the National Weather Service. Activity in the West Pacific is monitored by the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA). Systems in the North Indian Ocean are monitored by the India Meteorological Department (IMD). The Météo-France located in Réunion (MFR) monitors tropical activity in the South-West Indian Ocean. The Australian region is monitored by five TCWCs that are under the coordination of the Australian Bureau of Meteorology (BOM). Similarly, the South Pacific is monitored by both the Fiji Meteorological Service (FMS) and the Meteorological Service of New Zealand Limited. Other, unofficial agencies that provide additional guidance in tropical cyclone monitoring include the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) and the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC).

February was an extremely inactive month, featuring only 4 systems, of which all were named. Hollanda was the first storm of the month, peaking as a Category-3 equivalent cyclone and causing strong wind gusts and heavy rainfall on the Mascarene Islands and causing 2 deaths. Ivy and Julita formed afterwards, with Ivy peaking as a Category-3 equivalent cyclone and Julita making landfall on Madagascar. Cyclone Theodore was the last and strongest storm of the month, crossing over into the South Pacific basin and peaking as a Category-4 equivalent cyclone.

May was the least active month of 1994, featuring only 3 systems, of which only 1 was named. Typhoon Page, the first and strongest storm of the month, formed on May 12 and stayed out to sea, peaking as a Category-2 equivalent cyclone. Deling formed on May 25, causing 5 deaths in the Philippines. A tropical depression was the last storm of the month.

2 Only systems that formed either on or after January 1, 1994 are counted in the seasonal totals. 3 Only systems that formed either before or on December 31, 1994 are counted in the seasonal totals.4 The wind speeds for this tropical cyclone/basin are based on the IMD Scale which uses 3-minute sustained winds. 5 The wind speeds for this tropical cyclone/basin are based on the Saffir Simpson Scale which uses 1-minute sustained winds. 6 The wind speeds for this tropical cyclone/basin are based on Météo-France which uses wind gusts.

US National Hurricane Center - North Atlantic, Eastern Pacific Central Pacific Hurricane Center - Central Pacific Japan Meteorological Agency - NW Pacific India Meteorological Department - Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea Météo-France - La Reunion - South Indian Ocean from 30°E to 90°E Fiji Meteorological Service - South Pacific west of 160°E, north of 25° S Tropical Cyclone Warning Centers

Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysical Agency of Indonesia - South Indian Ocean from 90°E to 141°E, generally north of 10°S Australian Bureau of Meteorology (TCWC's Perth, Darwin & Brisbane) - South Indian Ocean & South Pacific Ocean from 90°E to 160°E, generally south of 10°S Papua New Guinea National Weather Service - South Pacific Ocean from 141°E to 160°E, generally north of 10°S Meteorological Service of New Zealand Limited - South Pacific west of 160°E, south of 25°S This article incorporates public domain material from websites or documents of the National Weather Service.

raw:
Traffic (art exhibition)

Traffic is the title of a group exhibition of contemporary art that took place at CAPC musée d'art contemporain de Bordeaux, France, through February and March, 1996.

Writing in Zing art magazine, Emily Tsingou said, "For a brief moment, and on a theoretical level, the show attempted an interesting claim. The idea, though, of interactivity is not a very lucid one, especially if one considers that it could be stretched to such extent as to encompass any art work and the presence of a viewer (even in its traditional sense, art functions on that quality) ... overall the show bore the characteristics of a traffic jam: at a standstill and agitated." Writing in Frieze art magazine, Carl Freedman said, "Traffic and Bourriaud's concept of 'relationality' were just too unspecific to be capable of defining a new art, especially when so many of the works did little to support the exhibition's premise. This was an ambitiously funded exhibition which was only able to provide the viewer with a largely familiar array of objects and images. With the primary beneficiaries of 'Traffic' tending to be the participating artists and their associates, Bourriaud may need to look at what actually constitutes the socio-political determinants of his 'interhuman space'.

raw:
gym membership terms

Gym membership contracts often read like a legal maze, but the most important clauses are surprisingly straightforward once you know where to look. The first section usually defines the "membership type" you are signing up for-whether it's a basic access pass, a premium package with classes, or a family plan. Each tier comes with its own price schedule, and the agreement will spell out whether the fee is billed monthly, quarterly, or annually. Understanding this early on helps you avoid surprise charges later.

Cancellation policies are the next big hurdle for many members. Most gyms require a written notice-often a 30-day letter or an online form-before they will stop billing you. Some locations offer a "cooling-off" period of seven days after signing up, during which you can cancel without penalty, while others impose a fixed early-termination fee that can be as high as one month's dues. Keep an eye on the exact wording, because the difference between "notice" and "cancellation" can affect how much you owe.

Automatic renewal clauses can also catch people off guard. In many contracts, the membership rolls over automatically at the end of the term unless you actively opt out, and the renewal price may increase by a predetermined percentage. The fine print will usually state when the gym will send a reminder-often 30 days before the renewal date-so you have a window to decide whether to stay or walk away. Missing that reminder can lock you into a higher rate for another year.

Access rules are more than just a list of open hours. The agreement often details which facilities you can use, such as the weight room, pool, or group-class studios, and whether any of those areas require an additional fee. Guest policies are also covered; many gyms allow you to bring a friend for a nominal charge, but they will limit the number of visits per month. Knowing these limits helps you plan workouts without incurring extra costs.

Finally, liability waivers are a standard part of any gym contract. By signing, you acknowledge that you understand the risks of physical activity and agree not to hold the facility responsible for injuries that occur on the premises, except in cases of gross negligence. Some gyms also require you to disclose pre-existing medical conditions, which can affect your ability to use certain equipment or classes. Reading this section carefully can protect you from future disputes.

If you're still unsure about any of the terms, don't hesitate to ask the staff for a plain-language summary or request a copy of the contract to review at home. Many gyms will gladly walk you through the most common clauses and point out where you can negotiate, such as a reduced initiation fee or a trial period. Being proactive about the fine print not only saves money but also ensures you get the most out of your membership from day one.

raw:
public transport accessibility

Reformed urban mobility is no longer a luxury reserved for the few but a fundamental standard for all citizens. As cities across the globe expand, the efficiency of public transport defines the quality of life for millions. However, for individuals with physical, sensory, or cognitive limitations, the barrier to entry remains stubbornly high. A truly accessible system ensures that no passenger is left behind, regardless of their ability to navigate complex infrastructure or navigate crowded platforms independently.

The most visible aspects of accessibility often involve physical infrastructure. Level boarding, where train cars align perfectly with platform edges, eliminates the dangerous gap that traps wheelchairs or causes stumbles for those with mobility aids. Tactile paving strips guide visually impaired travelers through stations, while clear, high-contrast signage helps those with low vision. Yet, infrastructure alone is insufficient without the integration of auditory cues, such as voice announcements that provide real-time updates on platform changes or service disruptions.

Digital integration offers a promising avenue for reducing friction in daily commutes. Real-time applications that track vehicle locations allow users to plan journeys with confidence. Furthermore, on-board Wi-Fi and broadcast systems can be optimized for deaf and hard-of-hearing passengers through live captioning services. These technologies bridge the communication gap, ensuring that critical information is accessible to everyone, not just those who can hear or see standard displays.

Staff training represents the human element of accessibility, which cannot be fully automated. Frontline employees must be equipped to assist passengers with dignity and efficiency. This includes knowing how to safely operate wheelchair lifts, understanding the needs of passengers with autism who may be overwhelmed by noise, and remembering that accessibility is not a one-size-fits-all solution. Empathy is as crucial as engineering in creating a welcoming environment.

Ultimately, accessible public transport is a civic duty that reflects a society's values. When transportation systems fail to accommodate diverse needs, they exclude significant portions of the population from economic opportunities and social participation. By prioritizing universal design, cities can foster inclusivity and ensure that movement through the urban landscape is a right shared by all, rather than a privilege granted to the able-bodied.

raw:
seminar announcement

The Department of Urban Planning at State University is pleased to announce the upcoming "Future Cities 2024" seminar, scheduled for Saturday, October 12, from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM in the Grand Hall of the Main Library. This event is designed to bring together city planners, architects, environmental scientists, and community leaders to discuss the pivotal role of sustainable design in the development of modern metropolitan areas. The primary objective of this gathering is to provide a platform for the exchange of innovative strategies that can help mitigate climate change impacts while enhancing the quality of life for urban residents. Attendees will have the opportunity to engage in detailed discussions with leading experts in the field who have successfully implemented green infrastructure projects in various international cities.

The seminar will feature a series of keynotes followed by interactive panel discussions. The opening keynote is delivered by Dr. Elena Rossi, a renowned sustainability architect, who will present her latest research on biophilic design principles and their application in high-density housing projects. Following her address, a panel of four experts will debate the economic viability of comprehensive urban greenery initiatives. This segment is particularly relevant for policy makers who are currently drafting new zoning laws for the fiscal year. The afternoon session will include two breakout workshops focused on water management systems and pedestrian-friendly street design. Participants are encouraged to bring specific case studies from their own regions to facilitate more targeted peer-to-peer learning during these small group activities.

Registration for the event is open to all professionals, students, and community members interested in urban development. The general admission fee is fifty dollars, which includes lunch and access to all keynote presentations and panel discussions. Students and early career professionals can register for a reduced fee of twenty-five dollars by presenting a valid ID upon check-in. A limited number of complimentary tickets are available for non-profit organizations working directly on local neighborhood revitalization projects. To secure your spot, please visit the university's events portal and complete the online registration form by October 1st. Late registrations may be subject to additional processing fees depending on capacity constraints.

The venue is located in the heart of the city center, easily accessible via public transit lines 4 and 9. Free parking is available in the visitor lot adjacent to the library for those who prefer to drive. The venue is fully wheelchair accessible, and real-time captioning services will be provided for all keynote speeches to ensure inclusivity for all attendees. For those requiring dietary accommodations, there will be a variety of options available during the lunch break, including vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free meals. Please indicate any specific dietary requirements during the registration process so that the catering team can ensure a comfortable experience for every guest.

Preparation for the seminar is minimal but recommended. Attendees are advised to review the attached agenda and speaker bios before the event to maximize the value of their participation. Networking opportunities will be integrated throughout the day, with a dedicated reception space available for informal conversations between sessions. The final panel discussion will address emerging technologies in smart city infrastructure, providing a forward-looking perspective on how data analytics can support sustainable urban growth. We encourage all participants to arrive early to enjoy the morning coffee and pastries while meeting fellow attendees. This event represents a significant step toward fostering a collaborative approach to planning the cities of tomorrow, and we look forward to welcoming you to what promises to be an intellectually stimulating day.

Residential Broadband Plan Comparison

This memorandum outlines the current home internet service tiers available for employee recommendation and customer inquiry handling. The primary focus is on the Essential, Standard, and Premium packages, each tailored to different bandwidth needs and household sizes.

The Essential package offers speeds up to 250 Mbps, suitable for single users or small households engaged in basic web browsing, email, and standard definition video streaming. This plan includes unlimited data usage and requires no data caps, ensuring continuous connectivity for light digital consumers.

The Standard plan increases capability with symmetric speeds of 600 Mbps, designed for medium-sized households where multiple devices operate simultaneously. It supports high definition streaming across four or more TVs, online gaming with low latency, and regular video conferencing for remote work scenarios without significant performance degradation.

For power users and large families, the Premium tier delivers 1.2 Gbps download and 600 Mbps upload speeds. This configuration handles multiple 4K streams, frequent large file transfers, and professional creative workflows such as video editing. It also includes enhanced security features and priority traffic routing during peak network congestion periods.

All plans include a Wi-Fi 6 router and installation service at no additional cost. Monthly fees are fixed for the first twelve months, after which rates may adjust according to the standard annual price review policy. Customers may upgrade or downgrade their service at any time, subject to a thirty-day processing period for hardware swaps or line changes.

Neil Newhouse

Neil Newhouse is an American pollster. He is the co-founder of Public Opinion Strategies, a political survey and polling firm, and was the lead pollster for the unsuccessful presidential campaigns of both John McCain and Mitt Romney against Barack Obama.

In 1991 he founded the polling company Public Opinion Strategies with Bill McInturff and Glen Bolger, one of the biggest polling firms in Republican politics. He was previously executive vice president at the Wirthlin Group. In 1993, Newhouse, who specializes in health-care analysis, worked on creating the Harry and Louise adverts funded by the Health Insurance Association of America to attack President Bill Clinton's health care plan. He was later a senior advisor to Bob Dole's campaign in the 1996 Republican primaries ahead of Clinton's 1996 election, but was fired after Dole lost New Hampshire to Pat Buchanan, though Newhouses's polling had in that instance been accurate. He was lead pollster for John McCain's unsuccessful 2008 presidential campaign. In 2012, he was again the lead pollster for a Republican Party presidential nominee, this time Mitt Romney, whose presidential campaign was, like McCain's, against Barack Obama. His polls predicted that Romney would win the election, which proved not to be the case. Newhouse put those errors down, in part, to faulty demographic models of likely turnout, an over-emphasis on measures of voter enthusiasm, and relying on random digit dialing rather than lists of registered voters. Responding to criticism of the factual accuracy of a series of attack ads on welfare policy during the campaign, Newhouse commented to reporters that "We're not going to let our campaign be dictated by fact-checkers", at a panel organised by NBC News at the Republican National Convention. The comments drew direct criticism from Obama. In a 2016 interview with the Duke Political Review he said "What I meant by that was that every ad we did in the Romney campaign was fact-checked internally ... what I meant was that I wasn't going to let those independent newspaper guys dictate how we're going to run the strategy of our campaign". A one-letter typo of his was the subject of several articles when he spelled 'Reagan', 'Regan' in one slide of a PowerPoint presentation. The error came the week after the Romney campaign's "With Mitt" iPhone app had spelled "America" as "Amercia". For the 2014 Senate elections, he was an adviser to the Republican campaigns in Colorado, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana, Michigan and West Virginia.

The American Association of Political Consultants (AAPC) has named Newhouse their Pollster of the Year three times, together or jointly. In 2003, the award went to Public Opinion Strategies for its work in the 2002 elections. In 2010, he and Glen Bolger split the award, as the Pollster Team of the Year. Newhouse's win was for his work on Scott Brown's successful run for senator in a special election in Massachusetts. In 2016 he won for his work on the campaign against the legalization of cannabis in Ohio.

Subject: Introduction to the Fundamentals of FDM 3D Printing
Hi Sarah,
I wanted to follow up on our recent conversation regarding additive manufacturing, specifically focusing on the core principles behind Fused Deposition Modeling. Since you are considering purchasing a machine for your workshop, it is crucial to understand the mechanical and digital prerequisites before diving into complex projects. 3D printing relies heavily on the translation of digital design into physical object, and this process involves a delicate balance of software settings and hardware calibration.
The lifecycle of every printed piece begins with a digital model, typically created in CAD software or downloaded from an online repository. This three dimensional model is then processed by a program called a slicer. The slicer takes the solid geometry and breaks it down into thin, horizontal layers, essentially calculating the toolpath for the print head. During this stage, parameters such as layer height, inflection density, and exterior perimeters are defined. If the layer height is set too thick, the finished surface will look rough and ladder-like, whereas a thinner layer produces smoother results but significantly increases the total printing time and requires more precise mechanical tolerances from the printer mechanism.
Once the file is sliced, the G-code instructions are sent to the printer, usually via an SD card or a network connection. The machine heats the nozzle to a specific temperature appropriate for the chosen filament, commonly PLA or ABS. The extruder motor pushes the molten plastic through a heated block and out of the nozzle, depositing it onto the build plate one line at a time. It is critical that the first layer adheres perfectly to the surface. If the nozzle is too far from the plate, the plastic will not bond correctly, leading to warping or detachment. Conversely, if it is too close, it can shred the filament or fail to extrude properly.
Throughout the process, the printer moves precisely along the X and Y axes to build up the object layer by layer. Motors on the Z-axis raise the platform or lower the nozzle after each layer is complete. This sequential stacking is what distinguishes additive manufacturing from traditional subtractive methods like CNC milling. While it allows for the creation of extremely complex internal structures and hollow geometries that would be nearly impossible to carve from a solid block of material, it also introduces unique challenges regarding strength and grain direction. The bonding between layers is the weakest point of the final part, meaning the object is generally stronger along the X and Y axes than it is along the vertical Z axis.
To ensure success, you must pay close attention to the tension of your steel belts and the leveling of your bed. Many beginners skip the leveling process, assuming the machine's auto-leveling feature is accurate, but adjusting the screws manually to ensure a consistent gap between the nozzle and the plate is often necessary. Consistency in filaments is also vital; humidity can cause materials like PETG to warp during cooling. Start with simple calibration objects, such as the standard twenty millimeter cube or a bridging test, to verify that your machine is operating within tolerance before attempting larger or more intricate designs.
Best regards,
David
