Merchant Ivory Productions

Merchant Ivory Productions is a film company founded in 1961 by producer Ismail Merchant (1936-2005) and director James Ivory (b. 1928). Merchant and Ivory were life and business partners from 1961 until Merchant's death in 2005. During their time together, they made 44 films. The films were for the most part produced by Merchant and directed by Ivory, and 23 of them were scripted by Ruth Prawer Jhabvala (1927-2013) in some capacity. The films were often based upon novels or short stories, particularly the work of Henry James, E. M. Forster, and Jhabvala herself. The initial goal of the company was "to make English-language films in India aimed at the international market". The style of Merchant Ivory films set and photographed in India became iconic. The company also went on to make films in the United Kingdom and America. Some actors and producers associated with Merchant Ivory include Maggie Smith, Leela Naidu, Madhur Jaffrey, Aparna Sen, Shashi Kapoor, Jennifer Kendal, Hugh Grant, James Wilby, Rupert Graves, Simon Callow, Anthony Hopkins, Glenn Close, Uma Thurman, Emma Thompson, Vanessa Redgrave, Natasha Richardson, Ralph Fiennes, Colin Firth, Richard Hawley and Helena Bonham Carter. Of this collaboration, Merchant once commented: "It is a strange marriage we have at Merchant Ivory... I am an Indian Muslim, Ruth is a German Jew, and Jim is a Protestant American. Someone once described us as a three-headed god. Maybe they should have called us a three-headed monster!" The expression "Merchant-Ivory film" has made its way into common parlance, to denote a particular genre of film rather than the actual production company. While 1965's Shakespeare Wallah put this genre on the international map, its heyday was the 1980s and 1990s with such films as A Room with a View (1985) and Howards End (1992). A typical "Merchant-Ivory film" would be a period piece, based on a classic novel, set in the early 20th century, usually in Edwardian England, featuring lavish sets and top British actors portraying genteel characters who suffer from disillusionment and tragic entanglements. The main theme often surrounded a house, which took on a particular importance in many Merchant Ivory films.

Merchant Ivory Productions was founded in 1961 by Ismail Merchant and James Ivory in India to produce English-language films. After early, modest successes with films such as The Householder, Shakespeare Wallah, and Bombay Talkie, Merchant and Ivory suffered a lean period during the 1970s. Films such as Jane Austen in Manhattan and The Wild Party failed to find an audience. Their fortunes revived dramatically in 1979 when they made an adaptation of Henry James' novel The Europeans. Their film Heat and Dust (1983) was an art-house hit in Europe, particularly in England. However, it was not until their work together on A Room with a View (1985) that they broke out from the art house into broader success. In 1985, Merchant Ivory Productions was signed by film distributor Cinecom International Films in order to give Cinecom access to the 11 Merchant Ivory productions at that time as Cinecom had to increase its distribution schedule. In 1986, Merchant Ivory and Cinecom began their co-production lineup with the film The Deceivers. In 1987, after 25 years as an independent producer, Merchant Ivory Productions declined offers by Hollywood power brokers and deep-pocketed investors, mesmerized by the success of the triple-Oscar winning A Room with a View, to take the company public. Around 1990, they moved their productions to England and the United States. Ruth Prawer Jhabvala became their frequent collaborating writer. Major film studios sought them out; Disney signed Merchant Ivory Productions to a three-year distribution deal in 1991. In October 2015, Cohen Media Group acquired the Merchant Ivory brand and library, 21 films and nine documentaries including worldwide distribution, for restoration and rerelease as a part of the Cohen Film Collection. Ivory would be creative director on the films' restoration, re-release and promotion.

Ivory was known for often directing the productions. He received three Academy Award nominations for his work but never won. He received his first Oscar at the age of 89 for his screenplay for Call Me by Your Name, becoming the oldest person to win an Oscar for writing. Academy Awards

Hawley started in 1987 as Ivory's first assistant director on Slaves of New York. He was involved in every project to some degree thereafter. In 1994, he started co-running the company with Merchant and departed in 2009 after completion of The City of Your Final Destination.

Subject: Quick reminder on our team's data backup routine
Hi Team,
I wanted to take a moment to discuss the current state of our data backup habits. Over the past few months, I have noticed a gradual decline in consistency regarding the weekly offsite backups for our project files. While I understand that daily operational duties often take precedence and can lead to these tasks being pushed to the back of the mental queue, the risks associated with data loss are significant and cannot be overlooked. We are dealing with sensitive client information, proprietary code, and years of accumulated historical data that would be nearly impossible to reconstruct from scratch in the event of a hardware failure or accidental deletion. It is crucial that we view these backups not as an optional administrative chore, but as a fundamental security measure that protects both our reputation and our livelihood. I suspect that many of us simply forget to initiate the process because it is not an immediate part of our morning workflow, which is a common human error that we need to mitigate through better organization rather than relying on memory alone.
The current manual method we are using is prone to inconsistency because it depends entirely on an individual remembering to plug in the external drive and click the start button. This single point of failure is problematic. I have been looking into automating this process within our existing server environment so that the backup runs automatically every Sunday night at two in the morning. This timing ensures that the system is relatively idle, minimizing any performance impact on our daytime operations, and it eliminates the need for anyone to physically remember to perform the task. Automation also allows us to send a simple confirmation email to a shared management inbox upon successful completion. If that email does not arrive by Monday morning, it serves as an immediate alert that something went wrong, allowing us to address the issue before it becomes a catastrophe. This shift from manual to automated should significantly reduce the cognitive load on each of us and ensure that the backups happen with the same reliability as our other scheduled system maintenance tasks.
In addition to implementing the automated schedule, I would like to propose a quarterly audit of our backup integrity. It is not enough to simply assume that the files are backing up correctly; we need to periodically verify that the backups are actually restorable. I suggest we designate one person per quarter to perform a test restore of a small subset of random files to a temporary directory. We will then compare these restored files against the live versions to ensure there is no corruption during the transfer process. This verification step is often skipped in many organizations because it seems redundant, but it is the only way to have true confidence in our disaster recovery plan. By catching any potential issues early, such as file system errors or storage device degradation, we can prevent small problems from growing into critical failures. We can document the results of these quarterly tests in a simple log file that will also be backed up, creating a traceable history of our data management efforts over time.
I would appreciate it if everyone could review their personal local backups as well. While this new system covers our central server, many of us likely keep drafts or private notes on our local machines that are not part of the central repository. Please ensure that your personal documents are also being synced to a secure cloud location or a dedicated local drive that is separate from your main operating system partition. Data hygiene is a shared responsibility, and strengthening the overall security of our team starts with each individual taking ownership of their own digital footprint. I have attached a link to a brief guide on best practices for local encryption and secure cloud storage options if anyone needs a refresher on those specific topics. Let us aim to make these procedures a standard part of our professional toolkit rather than an exception that we only remember after something goes wrong.
I will set up the initial automation script by next Wednesday and send out the test confirmation emails so we can all confirm that the new workflow is working as intended. Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions, concerns, or suggestions for improving this process further. My goal is to make this as seamless and low-effort as possible for everyone, so that data security becomes a background feature of our work environment rather than a recurring source of stress. Thank you for your attention to this matter and for your continued commitment to maintaining a robust and secure digital workspace for the entire team.
Best regards,
Alex Mercer
IT Operations Manager

Subject: Updates on the spring planting and volunteer shifts
Hello neighbors,
I hope everyone is enjoying the mild weather this week. I am writing to share some important updates regarding our community garden as we prepare for the main spring planting season. The ground has finally dried out sufficiently after the heavy rains last month, which means we can begin turning the soil in the large north bed. This is a critical step that ensures our seedlings have a healthy, aerated environment to establish their roots. I want to remind everyone to check the tool shed for garden forks before you arrive, as we are doing a deep turn this year to help break up the compaction from last winter.
We have received a generous donation of organic compost from the local landscaping company, which has been delivered to the back corner of the plot. Please help out by spreading this material thinly over the tomato and pepper beds. The compost is rich in nitrogen, so it should give our early vegetables a strong start. If you are scheduled for the Saturday morning shift, please bring a pair of work gloves and a bucket. We aim to finish distributing the compost by ten in the morning so that afternoon volunteers can focus on laying out the irrigation lines.
On a related note, the water system repair is almost complete. The main valve leak that plagued us last summer has been fixed by the city services team. We will be testing the entire network on Thursday afternoon between one and three. There will be a temporary water outage in the garden area during this time, so please plan your personal schedules accordingly. It is a bit of an inconvenience, but long-term reliability is worth the short disruption. I appreciate your patience as we navigate these municipal service delays.
I also wanted to touch on the community potluck that was discussed at last month's board meeting. We have decided to move it to the third Saturday of June to coincide with the strawberry harvest. This change allows us to celebrate our first major yield of the season with a larger group. Volunteers are needed to set up tables, purchase basic supplies, and coordinate the food donation sign-up sheet. The sheet is located on the whiteboard inside the potting shed. Please mark your name down if you plan to bring a dish or sweet treat to share with the group.
Finally, please remember to water your assigned plots on a regular schedule, especially during the upcoming heat spells. Plants under stress are more susceptible to pests and disease, so consistent hydration is key to a successful harvest. If you are away from the city for more than a few days, kindly arrange for a neighbor to cover you or notify the plot coordinator so we can adjust the rotation. Thank you all for your continued dedication and hard work. It is truly a privilege to share this green space with such a supportive and energetic group of people. Let's make this season our best one yet.
Sincerely,
Elena Rodriguez
Garden Plot Coordinator

Subject: Understanding Open Source Licenses for Our Upcoming Project
Hi Alex,
I hope you're doing well. I wanted to take a moment to discuss the open source licenses we're likely to encounter as we evaluate components for the new platform. Choosing the right license is essential not only for legal compliance but also for maintaining the flexibility and community support that open source can provide. In the past, we've run into issues when a library's license conflicted with our internal policies, so it's worth revisiting the basics before we finalize any dependencies.
The most common licenses you'll see are the permissive ones, such as MIT, BSD, and Apache 2.0. These generally allow us to use, modify, and redistribute the code with minimal restrictions, often only requiring attribution. Apache 2.0 adds an explicit patent grant, which can be valuable if we're concerned about patent claims from contributors. On the other hand, copyleft licenses like GPLv3 require that any derivative work be released under the same license, which could compel us to open-source our own modifications. That's a significant consideration if we intend to keep certain parts of the platform proprietary.
We also need to be aware of LGPL, which sits somewhere in between. It permits linking to the library from proprietary software, provided that any changes to the library itself remain open source. This can be a good compromise when we want to benefit from a robust library without exposing our entire codebase. Additionally, some projects use dual licensing, offering both an open source and a commercial option, which could give us more flexibility if we later need a commercial support agreement.
Before we integrate any third-party code, let's perform a quick license audit. I'll draft a checklist that captures the key obligations-such as attribution notices, source distribution requirements, and any patent clauses. If a license seems ambiguous or if we're unsure about its compatibility with our product, we can consult legal counsel to avoid any surprises down the line.
Thanks for taking the time to review this. I'll circulate the audit template later today, and we can schedule a short meeting next week to go over any questions. Looking forward to ensuring our project stays on solid legal footing.
Best regards,
Maria Patel 
Product Development Lead 
TechNova Solutions

dormitory rules

Moving into a dormitory marks one of the most significant independent living experiences for many college students. While the freedom is exhilarating, confusion often arises regarding the specific house rules that govern life within the halls. These regulations are not merely bureaucratic hurdles designed to make life difficult; they serve as the foundational framework that ensures safety, equity, and a livable environment for hundreds of individuals sharing limited resources. Understanding these expectations early on is crucial for avoiding petty conflicts and disciplinary action that can detract from the academic and social journey.

The most strictly enforced rules usually revolve around safety and fire prevention. Residential life staff are vigilant about blocking fire exits, using unregistered appliances, or smoking on campus. These are non-negotiable boundaries because they directly impact the physical well-being of the entire building. Students are required to keep hallways clear of clutter and ensure that their electrical setups do not pose a shock hazard. Ignoring these basic safety protocols can lead to immediate remediation costs or, in severe cases, removal from the housing contract. Compliance here is less about respect for authority and more about respecting the shared responsibility of keeping everyone out of harm's way.

Noise and guest policies form the second major pillar of dormitory living. Most institutions enforce quiet hours, typically from ten in the evening to seven in the morning, to accommodate early morning classes and different circadian rhythms. During these times, music, television, and loud conversations must be kept at a minimum. Guest rules are equally important, as they dictate who may enter the building, how long they can stay, and whether registration is required. Violating guest policies often gets worse than noise complaints, sometimes resulting in fines or contract termination, because it introduces security risks to the residential community. Failing to respect these temporal and social boundaries creates friction that is difficult to resolve once trust is broken.

Property and cleaning standards also play a vital role in maintaining a healthy living space. Students are responsible for the initial condition of their rooms and are expected to keep them free of mold, pests, and excessive clutter. The use of communal spaces like kitchens and lounges requires a reciprocal amount of cleanliness. Leaving dishes in shared sinks or trash accumulating in hallways is a common source of tension among residents. Most housing authorities conduct periodic inspections, and significant neglect can result in mandatory cleaning services billed directly to the student or their family. Maintaining these standards helps preserve the value of the housing and ensures a hygienic environment for all.

Finally, adherence to community guidelines regarding alcohol and substance use is heavily monitored. Many dormitories are dry, meaning no alcohol is permitted at any time, while others have designated social zones where consumption is allowed under strict supervision. Drugs and illegal substances are categorically forbidden. Enforcement of these rules is often handled discreetly by trained staff to address the issue while minimizing public embarrassment, but the consequence for violation is almost always severe. Ultimately, the goal of dormitory rules is not to police behavior but to create a predictable and safe container for personal growth and academic success. Respecting these norms demonstrates maturity and contributes to a positive living atmosphere.

Facilities at the main trailhead are fully operational. Restrooms are cleaned every four hours, and the parking lot has sufficient capacity for seasonal use. Free maps and first-aid kits are available at the information booth. Staff encourage visitors to check local weather forecasts before departure, as afternoon thunderstorms are possible during this time of year.

Leave No Trace principles must be observed strictly. Carry out all trash and pack in toilet paper if using primitive facilities. Off-trail hiking is prohibited to protect fragile alpine vegetation. Volunteering for cleanup efforts is welcome, and volunteers can sign up at the ranger station. Safe travels and enjoy the natural beauty responsibly.

Frontenac Secondary School is a high school in the west end of Kingston, Ontario, Canada. The Limestone District School Board operates it. The team plays under the nickname "Frontenac Falcons".

Frontenac Secondary School was founded in 1957 as Collins Bay High School and adopted its current name in 1964. In 2006, construction began on a major extension, which includes a new library, a media room, an elevator, and several additional computer labs and classrooms.

Frontenac has junior and senior teams that compete in the Canadian game show Reach for the Top. In 1998-99, the senior team was the national champion. The team had qualified for the American game show Whiz Quiz. In 2007 and 2008, the senior REACH team was the international Whiz Quiz champions, and in 2006, 2007, and 2025 they attended the provincial REACH Championships.

Léman Manhattan Preparatory School

Léman Manhattan Preparatory School is a private school located in the Financial District, Manhattan. Students are ages two years old through eighteen years old. There are two Lower Manhattan sites. Founded in 2005 as Claremont Preparatory, the school was acquired by the Meritas family of schools in 2011, and subsequently renamed to Léman Manhattan Preparatory School. Several Meritas schools such as Collège du Léman which locates in Switzerland and Léman International School Chengdu which locates in China have incorporated the name Léman. In 2011, Léman joined Meritas, an international network of college preparatory schools. In 2015, Léman Manhattan was left out of a transaction that took in Léman Switzerland, and Léman Chengdu, and did not become an affiliate school of Nord Anglia Education as part of an acquisition deal. Nord Anglia currently maintains two other schools in Manhattan, Nord Anglia International School New York (ages 2-14) and the other school Avenues New York (ages 1-18) neither of which have an on site boarding facility. Léman Manhattan Preparatory School has students from over seventy countries. Tuition for K-12 day students and the boarding tuition is listed on their website.

Léman Manhattan's lower school is based at the former headquarters of Bank of America International at 41 Broad Street in the Financial District of Manhattan, New York City. and was the original campus. The middle and high school campuses are located nearby in the Cunard Building at 1 Morris Street, and opened in 2010. Both locations have amenities including swimming pools, art studios, libraries, gyms, music rooms, cafeterias and fine arts performing spaces. The lower school has a rooftop playground.

Léman Manhattan is the only high school in New York City with a residential boarding program. In 2012, the school opened its boarding program, with forty students from nine countries in grades 9-12 in its inaugural program. In 2015, Léman had over 100 students participating in its boarding program. Student housing is located at 37 Wall Street, an apartment building blocks away from the Upper School Campus. Students in the boarding program reside in apartments, with rooms accommodating 2-4 people with a kitchen.

To: All Events Coordination Staff 
From: Director of Venue Operations 
Date: October 8, 2026 
Subject: Updated Procedures for Wedding Venue Booking

Effective immediately, all wedding reservations must be processed through the central booking portal, and no manual entries will be accepted. The portal now requires the submission of a completed client questionnaire, a signed venue agreement, and a non-refundable deposit of 25 percent of the estimated total cost. Once these items are received, the system will generate a confirmation number that must be referenced in all subsequent communications. Failure to follow this workflow will result in the reservation being placed on hold until compliance is achieved, and may lead to loss of the preferred booking date.

Clients are required to schedule an on-site walkthrough within ten business days of their initial inquiry. The walkthrough must be conducted by a senior events planner who will verify the feasibility of the requested dates, assess any special accommodations, and confirm compliance with local noise ordinances and occupancy limits. After the walkthrough, a detailed event timeline should be drafted and emailed to the couple for approval. Any changes to the timeline after the final approval must be documented and signed off by both the client and the venue manager to avoid scheduling conflicts.

All catering arrangements must be coordinated with the approved list of in-house vendors, unless an external caterer receives prior written exemption from the culinary director. External vendors are required to submit proof of liability insurance and a copy of their food safety certification before they may be allowed on the premises. The venue's kitchen staff will be briefed on the menu at least three days before the event, and a final headcount must be provided no later than 48 hours prior to the wedding ceremony. Late changes to the menu or headcount may incur additional fees as outlined in the venue agreement.

Security and parking logistics are to be finalized during the final planning meeting, which should occur at least two weeks before the wedding date. The security coordinator will assign staff for crowd control, monitor entry points, and ensure that all emergency exits remain unobstructed. Parking allocations must accommodate the expected number of guests, and any overflow arrangements should be communicated to the client in writing. All staff assigned to the event must complete the mandatory safety briefing and wear appropriate identification badges throughout the duration of the wedding.

Finally, after each wedding, the events team must complete a post-event report within five business days. The report should include a summary of any incidents, a checklist of services rendered, and feedback gathered from the client. This information will be used to refine our booking procedures and improve client satisfaction. Copies of the report are to be filed electronically under the event's confirmation number and a hard copy retained in the venue's archives for a minimum of three years.

Date: 8 October 2026 
To: All Facilities Management Staff 
From: Director of Sustainable Operations 
Subject: Guidelines for Installation and Maintenance of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations

The purpose of this memo is to outline the standardized procedures for installing, operating, and maintaining electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure across all company sites. As our fleet expands and employee demand for charging options grows, it is essential that each location follows the same safety, accessibility, and performance criteria to ensure reliable service and compliance with local regulations.

All new installations must use Level 2 AC chargers rated at 7.2 kW minimum, equipped with SAE J1772 connectors and integrated network management software. Prior to any electrical work, the site's electrical engineer should confirm that the existing service panel can accommodate the additional load, and a load analysis report must be submitted to the Energy Compliance Team. Where possible, chargers should be positioned in well-lit, weather-protected areas within 5 meters of the nearest accessible parking space, and clear signage must be installed indicating the location and operating hours.

Routine maintenance will be performed on a quarterly basis by the contracted service provider. The maintenance checklist includes inspection of cable integrity, verification of ground fault protection, firmware updates, and cleaning of the charging enclosure. Any identified deficiencies must be recorded in the asset management system within 24 hours, and corrective actions should be completed no later than the next scheduled maintenance window unless an immediate safety risk is present.

User access will be managed through the corporate EV charging app, which assigns a unique ID to each employee and logs session data for billing and analytics. Employees are required to report any malfunction or unauthorized use to Facilities Management via the designated ticketing portal. Failure to follow proper charging etiquette, such as leaving a vehicle connected after charging is complete, may result in temporary suspension of charging privileges.

The implementation of these guidelines will support our sustainability goals, reduce operational disruptions, and provide a consistent charging experience for all staff. Please review the attached technical specifications and ensure that all upcoming projects incorporate these requirements. If you have any questions, contact the Sustainable Operations office directly.

garden pest control

Keeping your garden healthy requires a proactive approach to pest management. Many homeowners wait until plants are visibly damaged before acting, but early detection makes all the difference. Each morning, take a few minutes to inspect the undersides of leaves and stem junctions. Look for sticky residue, small holes, or clusters of insects. Catching an infestation early prevents it from spreading to other healthy specimens in your yard.

Before reaching for chemical sprays, consider introducing natural predators. Ladybugs are excellent at controlling aphids, while lacewants help manage whiteflies. You can also keep chickens or Ducks in secure areas of the garden if space permits. These animals naturally reduce the population of slugs, snails, and larger beetles that might otherwise chew through your tender seedlings. This biological method is cost-effective and maintains the ecological balance of your soil.

Physical barriers are surprisingly effective against common garden nuisances. Floating row covers protect brassicas from cabbage moths, while copper tape around raised beds deters slugs and snails. mesh bags work well for protecting berries from birds and fruit flies. These simple tools provide a defense mechanism that does not involve any synthetic chemicals, ensuring your harvest remains safe for consumption.

If pests persist despite these efforts, targeted organic remedies are the next step. Neem oil disrupts the life cycle of many soft-bodied insects without harming beneficial pollinators. Insecticidal soap works best on aphids and spider mites when applied directly to the foliage. Always follow label instructions carefully and apply treatments during cool parts of the day to minimize stress on your plants and maximize effectiveness.

Finally, focus on prevention by maintaining strong plant health. Weak plants are more susceptible to pest attacks, so ensure your soil is rich in nutrients and properly irrigated. Remove plant debris at the end of each season, as this eliminates overwintering sites for harmful insects. A tidy garden with resistant plant varieties provides the best long-term strategy for keeping pests under control.

Subject: Q2 2024 Sales Summary
Hi Team,
I'm pleased to share the quarterly sales summary for the second quarter of 2024. Overall, we closed the period with $12.4 million in net revenue, representing a 7.2 percent increase over Q1 and a 3.8 percent rise compared with the same quarter last year. The growth was driven primarily by strong performance in our enterprise software line and a notable uptick in new customer acquisitions across the Midwest region.
The enterprise software division posted $6.8 million in sales, up 11 percent from the previous quarter. This was largely thanks to the successful rollout of the latest version of our analytics platform, which has resonated well with larger clients seeking integrated data solutions. Our renewal rate for existing contracts held steady at 92 percent, indicating solid customer satisfaction and a healthy pipeline for the upcoming quarter.
Mid-market hardware sales saw a modest decline, slipping 2.3 percent to $2.1 million. While the dip is partially attributable to inventory constraints we faced in April, the team managed to offset some of the loss through aggressive promotional pricing in May and June. Looking ahead, the supply chain team has confirmed that the anticipated shipment arrivals next month should restore inventory levels, allowing us to meet the forecasted demand for Q3.
On the geographic front, the Midwest region delivered an impressive 15 percent increase in new business, contributing an additional $1.9 million in revenue. In contrast, the West Coast market remained flat, with sales holding at $2.3 million. The regional managers have identified several upcoming trade shows and partnership opportunities that we expect will reignite growth in the western market during the next quarter.
Finally, I want to acknowledge the cross-functional collaboration that made these results possible. The sales, product, and support teams all played a critical role in ensuring smooth onboarding for new clients and maintaining high renewal rates. Your dedication to meeting targets and addressing client needs does not go unnoticed, and it sets a strong foundation for continued success.
Please review the attached detailed report when you have a moment, and feel free to reach out with any questions or suggestions for improvement. I look forward to discussing our strategy for the next quarter at the upcoming all-hands meeting.
Best regards,
Laura Martinez
Senior Director of Sales
TechNova Solutions, Inc.

drone regulations

Navigating the airspace above your neighborhood requires more than just a remote control and a lithium-ion battery. The Federal Aviation Administration has established a comprehensive framework for small unmanned aircraft systems, commonly known as drones, to ensure the safety of both manned and unmanned operations. For recreational flyers, registration with the agency is mandatory for any aircraft weighing more than 0.55 pounds. This simple step involves a modest fee and ensures that remote identifiers can be broadcasted, allowing other aviation participants to track your flight path in real time.

Beyond basic registration, operators must obtain a specific credential known as the Part 107 license if they intend to fly for commercial purposes. This test covers critical topics such as restricted airspace, right of way, and weather limitations. Passing this exam demonstrates a professional level of understanding that goes beyond casual hobbyists. Many aspiring commercial pilots spend several weeks studying the manual before sitting for the computer-based test, which yields a certificate valid for three years.

Understanding airspace classes is perhaps the most technical aspect of compliant flying. Controlled areas, designated from Class A through G, have different rules regarding altitude and proximity to airports. Flying in Class D or C airspace, typically surrounding busy urban hubs, requires prior authorization from the air traffic control tower. Pilots often use designated applications to request this permission hours in advance, receiving a specific flight number that validates their entry into the protected zone.

Privacy and trespassing laws introduce a separate layer of legal complexity that varies significantly by local jurisdiction. While federal law governs the physical act of flight, state and municipal codes dictate what constitutes stalking, voyeurism, or trespassing. Operators must remain vigilant about filming people or private property, as inadvertent violations can lead to civil lawsuits. Checking local ordinances before capturing aerial footage is a prudent first step to avoid costly legal disputes.

Finally, physical safety remains the cornerstone of every takeoff. Operators must maintain visual line of sight at all times, keeping the drone within a clear line of vision without relying solely on digital feeds. Flying over people is strictly prohibited unless the aircraft is part of a registered demonstration or meets specific operational categories. Adhering to these guidelines not only prevents accidents but also fosters public trust, ensuring that the industry can continue to expand responsibly in years to come.

Navigating the airspace above your neighborhood requires more than just a remote control and a lithium-ion battery. The Federal Aviation Administration has established a comprehensive framework for small unmanned aircraft systems, commonly known as drones, to ensure the safety of both manned and unmanned operations. For recreational flyers, registration with the agency is mandatory for any aircraft weighing more than 0.55 pounds. This simple step involves a modest fee and ensures that remote identifiers can be broadcasted, allowing other aviation participants to track your flight path in real time.

Beyond basic registration, operators must obtain a specific credential known as the Part 107 license if they intend to fly for commercial purposes. This test covers critical topics such as restricted airspace, right of way, and weather limitations. Passing this exam demonstrates a professional level of understanding that goes beyond casual hobbyists. Many aspiring commercial pilots spend several weeks studying the manual before sitting for the computer-based test, which yields a certificate valid for three years.

Understanding airspace classes is perhaps the most technical aspect of compliant flying. Controlled areas, designated from Class A through G, have different rules regarding altitude and proximity to airports. Flying in Class D or C airspace, typically surrounding busy urban hubs, requires prior authorization from the air traffic control tower. Pilots often use designated applications to request this permission hours in advance, receiving a specific flight number that validates their entry into the protected zone.

Privacy and trespassing laws introduce a separate layer of legal complexity that varies significantly by local jurisdiction. While federal law governs the physical act of flight, state and municipal codes dictate what constitutes stalking, voyeurism, or trespassing. Strike Whilst the Iron Is Hot

Strike Whilst the Iron Is Hot is the second album created by Orange and Lemons, released on April 28, 2005, by Universal Records. The album earned double platinum status with its hits "Hanggang Kailan (Umuwi Ka Na Baby)" and "Heaven Knows (This Angel Has Flown)".

After releasing their debut album Love in the Land of Rubber Shoes and Dirty Ice Cream, they signed a contract with Universal Records October 2004, making Strike Whilst the Iron Is Hot their first major album. The album went on to get a Double Platinum. The song "Pinoy Ako" was used by ABS-CBN for the Pinoy Big Brother, which was used as the theme song and background music. Though the song had some controversy because it sounded like "Chandelier" by The Cure. Universal Records released a Repackaged Edition later that year, which included a bonus VCD. To commemorate the album's legacy, the band celebrated its 15th anniversary in 2020 by releasing their demo sessions for Strike Whilst the Iron Is Hot (2004 Demo Sessions) on May 29, 2020. They were supposed to celebrate the 15th anniversary together with the albums of Pedicab and Dicta License, but because of the COVID-19 pandemic, they were unable to. The group decided to host a private virtual live concert in Facebook.

Clem Castro - lead vocalist (tracks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11), lead and rhythm guitars, string/orchestral arrangements Mcoy Fundales - vocals (tracks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12), acoustic guitar JM del Mundo - bass guitar Ace del Mundo - drum tracks Additional musicians

Bella Tan - executive producer Robert Javier - producer Angee Rozul - engineer (drum tracks) Bogie Manipon - engineer (guitar, vocals, and other instruments), master and mixer Jonathan Ong - recorder and engineer Design

In the song "Tomorrow" when the song ends there will be silence, after that it is the beginning of the first song "Strike Whilst the Iron Is Hot", then played the reversed version of "Hanggang Kailan (Umuwi Ka Na Baby)".

The introduction of the movable type printing press in Europe during the mid-fifteenth century represents one of the most significant technological leaps in human history. Before this innovation, the reproduction of written text was a slow, labor-intensive process dominated by scribes working out of monasteries and scriptoriums. Manuscripts were rare, expensive, and heavily centralized, limiting access to knowledge for the elite. The transition to mechanical printing did not merely speed up production; it fundamentally altered the social, religious, and political structures of the medieval world by democratizing information dissemination.

Gutenberg's breakthrough in Mainz, Germany, around 1440, involved a complex assembly of existing technologies. He perfected a screw press designed for wine-making, created an alloy of lead, tin, and antimony suitable for sharp edge retention, and developed a grease-based ink. This combination allowed for the mass production of books with consistency and speed that hand copying could never achieve. The historic impact of this integration is often understated, as it relied on the synthesis of metallurgy, hydraulics, and chemical engineering into a single cohesive workflow that revolutionized typography.

The immediate aftermath of the press's adoption saw an explosion in printed material, most notably the Bible. The Gutenberg Bible is often cited as the first major work printed with movable type in the West, though earlier experiments in Asia and Europe laid the groundwork. Within fifty years, estimates suggest that approximately twenty million volumes had been printed. This volume of text exceeded the total number of books produced in the preceding thousand years, effectively collapsing the timeline of cultural accumulation and allowing ideas to travel across borders with unprecedented velocity.

Religious reformation was deeply intertwined with the rise of print. Martin Luther's ninety-five theses, likely translated and distributed via printed pamphlets, spread rapidly throughout the German-speaking lands. The press allowed for the standardization of vernacular languages, which previously had varied widely by region. This standardization helped forge national identities and facilitated trade communication. Conversely, the Catholic Church initially resisted the technology but eventually embraced it, leading to a complex interplay between state censorship, religious doctrine, and the free flow of information.

In the long term, the printing press laid the groundwork for the scientific revolution and the Enlightenment. The ability to clone diagrams, mathematical proofs, and philosophical treatises allowed scholars to build upon each other's work without the risk of manuscript degradation. Today, while digital media has superseded physical print in many respects, the original impact of the press remains the foundational model for modern mass communication. It established the precedents for copyright, public discourse, and the concept of a reading public, shaping the very nature of contemporary society.

Denise Bronzetti

Denise Bronzetti (born 12 December 1972) is a Sammarinese politician who has been one of the Captains Regent of San Marino alongside Italo Righi since 2025, and a member of the Grand and General Council since 2006, as a member of the Party of Socialists and Democrats. She was one of the Captains Regent from 2012 to 2013.

Denise Bronzetti was born in the City of San Marino, San Marino, on 12 December 1972. She graduated from San Marino Secondary School and the University of the Republic of San Marino.

From 1999 to 2002, Bronzetti was an official in FPI-CDLS and a member of the Confederal CSdL Board of Directors. She has worked for the government of San Marino since 1996, and for the Office for Labor and Active Policies since 2006. She was the private secretary to the Secretary of State for Justice, Relations with the Castle Councils and Information from 2002 to 2003. Bronzetti joined the Sammarinese Socialist Party at age 15. In the 2006 election she won a seat in the Grand and General Council. She became the president of the Party of Socialists and Democrats (PSD) and group leader of the Noi per la Repubblica list. Bronzetti was a member of San Marino's delegation to the Inter-Parliamentary Union in 2006, and the Parliamentary Assembly of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe in 2013. From 1 October 2012 to 1 April 2013, Bronzetti was the Supreme Judiciary. She joined the Council of Twelve in 2023. She was San Marino's substitute to the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe from 22 January to 29 September 2024, and was aligned with the Socialists, Democrats and Greens Group. From 2012 to 2013, Bronzetti was one of the Captains Regent. On 1 April 2025, she became Captain Regent for a term set to end on 1 October.

travel itinerary

When you open your laptop to plan a trip to an unfamiliar city, the screen often fills with a chaotic grid of pins, links, and nested spreadsheets. The temptation to over-pack the day is strong, driven by the fear of missing out on major landmarks or hidden gem cafes. However, the most memorable journeys rarely follow a rigid, minute-by-minute schedule. Instead, they emerge from a balance of structured anchors and flexible pockets of time. A realistic itinerary is not just a list of places to visit; it is a response to the natural rhythms of travel, accounting for fatigue, unexpected weather, and the simple joy of serendipity.

Start by selecting three non-negotiable activities for each day. These are your anchors, the experiences that define the location, such as a museum entry, a guided tour of the historic center, or a reservation at a highly-rated restaurant. Once these are locked in, group them geographically to minimize transit time. Shuttling across the city in traffic or crowded subways can drain the energy needed to actually enjoy the sights. By clustering activities within a specific neighborhood, you allow yourself to walk between destinations. Prehistoric Rock-Art Site of Pala Pinta

The Prehistoric Rock-Art Site Pala Pinta (Portuguese: Abrigo rupestre da Pala Pinta) is a Paleolithic-era rock-art site, recognized for cave paintings in the Portuguese municipality of Alijó, in the civil parish of Carlão e Amieiro.

The cave was occupied during the 3rd millennium, and the rock art paintings were likely created during this period. After its discovery, on 30 December 1985, there was a move by the Serviço Regional de Arqueologia da Zona Norte (North Zone Regional Archaeological Service) to have the site classified for protection. There was a positive reaction on 21 April 1986 to the endeavour by the Consultative Council of IPPC. Further initiatives were undertaken on 7 May by the Secretária de Estado da Cultura (Secretary-of-State for Culture) to classify the archaeological site as a National Monument. Although this was never promulgated, on 18 July 2006, the area was defined as a Zona Especial de Classificação (Special Classification Zone) by the DRPorto.

It was situated in an isolated, rural area in the middle of the hilltop facing the east. The site includes rock-art paintings over granite surface, covering an area of 12 metres (39 ft) long and 2.50 metres (8.2 ft) high. There roughly two vertical panels, caused by fractures in the cave/clifftop, consisting of monochromatic paintings in ochre of radial imagery (likely sun or stars), points and anthropomorphic representations of figures.

Mesquita, Horácio de; Correia, Virgílio (1922), "Arte rupestre em Portugal - A Pala Pinta", Terra Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon, Portugal, pp. 145-147{{citation}}: CS1 maint: location missing publisher (link) Junior, Joaquim Rodrigues dos Santos (1933), "O abrigo pré-histórico da Pala Pinta", Trabalhos de Antropologia e Etnologia (in Portuguese), Porto, Portugal, pp. 33-43{{citation}}: CS1 maint: location missing publisher (link) Sousa, Orlando (1989), "O Abrigo de Arte Rupestre da Pala Pinta - Alijó", Trabalhos de Antropologia e Etnologia (in Portuguese), Porto, Portugal, pp. 191-198{{citation}}: CS1 maint: location missing publisher (link)

Steve Greer

Steve Greer (July 23, 1947 - December 13, 2021) was a college football position coach and executive between 1971 and 2009. During his playing career in the 1960s, he was the AA Lineman of the Year twice while at Greer High School and received All-America selections while at the University of Georgia. After briefly playing with the Toronto Argonauts in 1970, he started coaching the defensive line freshmen with the University of Georgia the following year. He continued his freshmen coaching experience with the offensive and defensive players at Auburn University until 1973. After moving to varsity football in 1974, he primarily continued his defensive coaching career with both universities until 1993. During this time period, Greer was the recruiting coordinator and defensive end coach with Georgia from 1979 to 1981. After starting an administrative assistant role with Georgia in 1993, he resumed his recruiting coordinator position in 1994. Three years later, he became the Director of Football Operations. He remained in the role until he decided to leave the university in 2009. After his football tenure, Greer was with Jim Whitehead Tire Service during 2011. Greer joined the South Carolina Football Hall of Fame in 2019.

Greer's birth occurred in Greer, South Carolina during July 23, 1947. During his childhood, he was a fruit packer and hunter. He began playing football at Greer High School in 1961. With the team, Greer played in the 1963 Upstate Class AA championship. That year, he was All-Southern and won the AA Lineman of the Year award. During 1964, he was named "outstanding lineman" after his South Carolina team won the Shrine Bowl of the Carolinas. For that season, Greer was All-Southern and the AA Lineman of the Year. At the 1965 North-South All-Star, he was Outstanding Lineman and won with the North. That year, Greer was on the freshman football team for the University of Georgia. He did not play in 1966 after knee surgery. Following his return to the team in 1967, Greer played at that year's Liberty Bowl. Additional bowl game appearances with Georgia were at the Sugar Bowl and Sun Bowl during 1969. That year, he became their captain. With the South, his team won the American Bowl and Hula Bowl in 1970.

In May 1970, Greer joined the Toronto Argonauts. He played on the team during July 1970 before being cut that month. In 1971, he was hired as a graduate assistant with Georgia. While there, Greer began his defensive line coaching career in freshman football. With his freshmen experience at Auburn University from 1972 to 1973, Greer was an offensive coach for one year and defensive coach for two years. Greer continued working as a defensive coach after moving to Auburn's varsity football team in 1974. He remained in his position with the university until he became the recruiting coordinator at Georgia during 1979. With Georgia, he was also a defensive end coach before ending both positions in 1981. Greer resumed his defensive line experience with Georgia that year. He remained there as their coach until 1993. Greer started his administrative assistant role in 1993. While in his position, he had become the recruiting coordinator by 1994. In 1997, Greer became the Director of Football Operations and left as coordinator. He remained as Director of Football Operations until he decided to leave Georgia in 2009. Outside of football, Greer was with Jim Whitehead Tire Service during 2011.

While at Georgia, Greer was All-Southeastern Conference for United Press International and The Associated Press in 1969. For All-America selections, Greer was chosen in 1968 by the Central Press. The following year, he was All-America for Central Press and The Associated Press. Greer received the Lineman of the Year award from the Atlanta Touchdown Club during 1970. During 2014, he joined the Georgia Bulldogs Circle of Honor. He became part of the South Carolina Football Hall of Fame in 2019.

During the late 2010s, Greer began experiencing amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in his arms. He had three children during his marriage. Greer's death occurred in Athens, Georgia on December 13, 2021.

Steve Greer (July 23, 1947 - December 13, 2021) was a college football position coach and executive between 1971 and 2009. During his playing career in the 1960s, he was the AA Lineman of the Year twice while at Greer High School and received All-America selections while at the University of Georgia. After briefly playing with the Toronto Argonauts in 1970, he started coaching the defensive line freshmen with the University of Georgia the following year. He continued his freshmen coaching experience with the offensive and defensive players at Auburn University until 1973. After moving to varsity football in 1974, he primarily continued his defensive coaching career with both universities until 1993. During this time period, Greer was the recruiting coordinator and defensive end coach with Georgia from 1979 to 1981. After starting an administrative assistant role with Georgia in 1993, he resumed his recruiting coordinator position in 1994. Three years later, he became the Director of Football Operations. He remained in the role until he decided to leave the university in 2009. After his football tenure, Greer was with Jim Whitehead Tire Service during 2011. Greer joined the South Carolina Football Hall of Fame in 2019.
Greer's birth occurred in Greer, South Carolina during July 23, 1947. During his childhood, he was a fruit packer and hunter. He began playing football at Greer High School in 1961. With the team, Greer played in the 1963 Upstate Class AA championship. That year, he was All-Southern and won the AA Lineman of the Year award. During 1964, he was named "outstanding lineman" after his South Carolina team won the Shrine Bowl of the Carolinas. For that season, Greer was All-Southern and the AA Lineman of the Year. At the 1965 North-South All-Star, he was Outstanding Lineman and won with the North. That year, Greer was on the freshman football team for the University of Georgia. He did not play in 1966 after knee surgery. Following his return to the team in 1967, Greer played at that year's Liberty Bowl. Additional bowl game appearances with Georgia were at the Sugar Bowl and Sun Bowl during 1969. That year, he became their captain. With the South, his team won the American Bowl and Hula Bowl in 1970.
In May 1970, Greer joined the Toronto Argonauts. He played on the team during July 1970 before being cut that month. In 1971, he was hired as a graduate assistant with Georgia. While there, Greer began his defensive line coaching career in freshman football. With his freshmen experience at Auburn University from 1972 to 1973, Greer was an offensive coach for one year and defensive coach for two years. 2019 StarCraft II World Championship Series

The 2019 StarCraft II World Championship Series (WCS) was the 2019 edition of the StarCraft II World Championship Series, the top esports tournament circuit for StarCraft II. The tournament series' Global Finals were won by South Korean professional player Park "Dark" Ryung Woo.

The 2019 StarCraft II World Championship Series was separated into two regions, WCS Korea and WCS Circuit. The format of the former remained consistent with the standard set in 2017, featuring three seasons of the long-running Global StarCraft II League (GSL) Code S with two smaller GSL Super Tournament events interspersed. The format of the latter region, however, replaced one of the standard four large WCS Circuit events with WCS Winter, separated into WCS Winter Europe and WCS Winter America, two smaller tournaments with an online portion and an in-person playoff portion. Beyond this, the format remained unchanged, with three large WCS Circuit events and accompanying qualifiers under the WCS Challenger branding. Two shared World Championship Series Global events featured players from both regions before the Global Finals. All these events, excluding the second WCS Global event, GSL vs. the World, gave out WCS Circuit and/or WCS Korea points that determined the seeding of the Global Finals.

Eight players from each WCS region qualify for the event based on their WCS points-based rankings. Winners of WCS Circuit stops, GSL Code S events, and IEM Katowice receive automatic qualification. Based on their region-specific ranking, the sixteen players are then seeded into four four-player groups for the first round. A draw is held for the quarterfinals bracket, with winners of each group facing second-place finishers of other groups.

The WCS Global Finals were held at the Anaheim Convention Center in Anaheim, California, as part of BlizzCon 2019. They featured a group stage as the first round of play, played out the week before the main event, followed by bracket play from the quarterfinals onward at the convention center. For the first time ever, the event was confined to one of the two days the convention ran for, with all matches from the quarterfinals through the finals happening on November 1, Friday.

raw:
Chip art

Chip art, also known as silicon art, chip graffiti or silicon doodling, refers to microscopic artwork built into integrated circuits, also called chips or ICs. Since ICs are printed by photolithography, not constructed a component at a time, there is no additional cost to include features in otherwise unused space on the chip. Designers have used this freedom to put all sorts of artwork on the chips themselves, from designers' simple initials to rather complex drawings. Given the small size of chips, these figures cannot be seen without a microscope. Chip graffiti is sometimes called the hardware version of software easter eggs. Prior to 1984, these doodles also served a practical purpose. If a competitor produced a similar chip, and examination showed it contained the same doodles, then this was strong evidence that the design was copied (a copyright violation) and not independently derived. A 1984 revision of the US copyright law (the Semiconductor Chip Protection Act of 1984) made all chip masks automatically copyrighted, with exclusive rights to the creator, and similar rules apply in most other countries that manufacture ICs. Since an exact copy is now automatically a copyright violation, the doodles no longer serve a useful purpose in terms of hardware watermarking.

Integrated circuits (ICs) are constructed from multiple layers of material, typically silicon, silicon dioxide (glass), and aluminum. The composition and thickness of these layers give them their distinctive color and appearance. These elements created an irresistible palette for IC design and layout engineers. The creative process involved in the design of these chips, a strong sense of pride in their work, and an artistic temperament combined compel people to want to mark their work as their own. It is very common to find initials, or groups of initials on chips. This is the design engineer's way of "signing" their work. Often this creative artist's instinct extends to the inclusion of small pictures or icons. These may be images of significance to the designers, comments related to the chip's function, inside jokes, or even satirical references. Because of the difficulty in verifying their existence, chip art has also been the subject of online hoaxes (e.g. the never-seen "bill sux" comment on a Pentium chip-the reputed "photo" showing the inscription is a hoax). The mass production of these works of art on the body of a commercial IC goes unnoticed by most observers and is discouraged by semiconductor corporations, primarily from the fear that the presence of the artwork (which is clearly unneeded) may interfere with some necessary function or design flow in the chip. Some laboratories have started collaborating with artists or directly producing books and exhibits with the micrographs of these chips. Such is the case of Harvard chemist George Whitesides, who collaborated with photographer Felice Frankel to publish On the Surface of Things, a photography book on experiments mostly from the Whitesides lab. Since an exact copy is now automatically a copyright violation, the doodles no longer serve a useful purpose in terms of hardware watermarking.
Integrated circuits (ICs) are constructed from multiple layers of material, typically silicon, silicon dioxide (glass), and aluminum. The composition and thickness of these layers give them their distinctive color and appearance. These elements created an irresistible palette for IC design and layout engineers. The creative process involved in the design of these chips, a strong sense of pride in their work, and an artistic temperament combined compel people to want to mark their work as their own. It is very common to find initials, or groups of initials on chips. This is the design engineer's way of "signing" their work. Often this creative artist's instinct extends to the inclusion of small pictures or icons. These may be images of significance to the designers, comments related to the chip's function, inside jokes, or even satirical references. Subject: Guidance on Resetting Your Account Password
Dear Alex,
I am writing to provide you with clear steps on how to reset your password if you have forgotten it or if you have been flagged for a security review. Please follow the instructions below carefully to ensure you regain access to your account without any issues.
First, navigate to the main login page of the service. You should see a small but important link labeled "Forgot Password?" directly beneath the password entry field. Clicking this link will redirect you to a secure verification page where you will be asked to enter the email address associated with your account.
Once you submit your email address, the system will generate a unique, single-use verification code. You will receive an email containing this code within a few minutes. It is crucial to check your spam or junk folder as well in case the message was filtered out by your email security settings. The code usually expires after fifteen minutes for security reasons, so please act quickly once you receive it.
After entering the code correctly, you will be prompted to create a new password. To maintain the highest level of security, your new password must be at least twelve characters long and include a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols. Please avoid using common words, generic phrases, or personal information like birthdays or names.
Keep in mind that this process logs you out of all active sessions on other devices. This is a safety measure to ensure that no one else currently has access to your account with the old credentials. After setting your new password, you may need to wait a few moments for the system to propagate the changes before you can log in successfully.
If you encounter any errors or are unable to receive the verification email, please contact our support team immediately. We can verify your identity through alternative methods and assist you in regaining access to your account manually.
Best regards,
Security Team

Subject: Concerns Regarding Recent Changes to My Account Fees
Dear Customer Service Team,
I am writing to express my concern about the recent fee adjustments that appeared on my checking account statement for the month of September. While I understand that financial institutions periodically review their pricing structures, the new monthly maintenance charge of $12 and the added $0.50 per transaction fee were not communicated to me in advance. As a long-time customer who maintains an average balance well above the minimum required to avoid fees, these charges came as an unexpected surprise and have caused me some inconvenience.
When I first opened my account three years ago, the terms clearly stated that a fee-free checking experience would be provided as long as the balance remained above $1,500. Over the past year, my balance has consistently hovered around $2,200, and I have not incurred any overdraft or insufficient fund fees. Therefore, I was under the impression that my account would remain exempt from maintenance fees. The recent notice I received via email mentioned a "standard fee schedule update," but it lacked specifics about how the changes would affect existing customers like myself who meet the previous fee-waiver criteria.
I would appreciate it if you could clarify whether the new fees apply to all checking accounts regardless of balance, or if there is an alternative tier that would allow me to retain a fee-free status. If the latter is the case, could you please provide instructions on how I might qualify for that tier, or advise if any additional requirements have been introduced? Understanding the exact criteria will help me determine whether I need to adjust my banking habits or consider consolidating my accounts elsewhere.
Additionally, I would like to request a reversal of the fees that were applied to my September statement, as they were assessed without prior notice. I have attached a copy of the statement for reference. If a reversal is not possible, I would be grateful for a detailed explanation of the policy change and the timeline for future notifications. Transparency is essential for maintaining trust, and I hope we can resolve this matter amicably.
Thank you for taking the time to review my concerns. I have been satisfied with the service your bank has provided over the years, and I am hopeful we can find a mutually agreeable solution. Please let me know if you require any further information from my side, and I look forward to hearing from you within the next few business days.
Sincerely,
Emily R. Thompson 
Account Number: 4876-3210 
Phone: (555) 842-1963 
Email: emily.thompson@email.com

raw:
Gottfried von Erdmannsdorff

Gottfried von Erdmannsdorff (25 April 1893 - 30 January 1946) was a German general during World War II. He was convicted by a Soviet military tribunal for war crimes at the Minsk Trial and executed in 1946.

On 27 June 1944, as part of Mogilev Offensive, Soviet troops made a deep breakthrough north of Mogilev by crossing the Dnieper River over a bridge at Trebuchi. The 4th Army dispatched a message to Erdmannsdorff that Mogilev be held as a "fortified position" and ordered him to hold the town until the very last man. The 4th Army retreated the XXXIX Panzer Corps and the XII Army Corps a full 21km west of Mogilev, leaving the town to its fate against the overwhelming Soviet attacks. Later in the evening Erdmannsdorff reported that German forces had been weakened and the Soviets had started to reach the edge of the city. Only 2 hours and 40 minutes later Erdmannsdorff stated that the only part of the city still under his control was the city center and hand to hand combat was starting to take place. The last radio message that was received from Mogilev was at 11 o'clock in the evening.

After the Soviet troops defeated "Fortress Mogilev", Erdmannsdorff was captured by Soviet troops. He was tried by a Soviet tribunal (the Minsk Trial) for crimes committed in Belarus along with 18 other defendants, 14 of whom, including Erdmannsdorff, were sentenced to death on 29 January 1946. Erdmannsdorff was condemned on charges including the deportation of 10,000 people, the destruction of villages, schools and churches, and the shootings of disabled people during the construction of fortifications, the use of people as human shields, and the organization of reprisals operations against civilians under the guise of fighting partisans, and the establishment of camps in which many people died. The officers were hanged in public (with over 100,000 civilian spectators) in the horse racing venue of Minsk, on 30 January 1946. He was the younger brother of General der Infanterie Werner von Erdmannsdorff.

Single-letter second-level domain

Single-letter second-level domains are domains in which the second-level domain of the domain name consists of only one letter, such as x.com. In 1993, the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) explicitly reserved all single-letter and single-digit second-level domains under the top-level domains com, net, and org, and grandfathered those that had already been assigned. In December 2005, ICANN considered auctioning these domain names.

On December 1, 1993, the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) explicitly reserved the remaining single-letter and single-digit domain names. The few domains that were already assigned were grandfathered in and continued to exist.

The .org TLD was subsequently reopened for single-letter domain registrations. These and selected other gTLD and ccTLD single-letter domain names currently in use, typically as shortcuts and URL shorteners, are listed below.

Many other single-letter second-level domains have been registered under country code top-level domains. The list of country code top-level domains which have been identified to allow single-letter domains are:

Single-character non-ASCII second-level domains also exist (as seen below), also known as Internationalized domain names (IDN), these domains are actually registered as their Punycode translations (which are more than a single character) for DNS purposes. ICANN oversees a process for determining registration rules that involves wide-ranging stakeholder input and assorted Working Groups. In the case of .com domains, decisions are then implemented by Verisign, the contracted backend operator for the .com registry. The result is a list of 96,957 codepoints allowed for IDN registrations. As mentioned above, some additional domains previously registered are "grandfathered" and remain active. Many gTLDs also allow IDN registration. These 96,957 distinct IDN characters eligible for registration in .com are the essential building-blocks of languages worldwide. A single letter domain does not provide the context found in a longer string or group of words. They may appear similar to one another or to other English / Latin characters; due to this potential for confusion, browsers have restricted the characters that may be rendered and will display the restricted characters in their Punycode form. They are sometimes used as pictorial symbols and memorable links. Among IDNs currency symbols are considered extremely rare given their day to day use on mobile keyboards. These domains are grandfathered and if the registration is allowed to lapse, domain will be reserved by the registry.

In 2012, the Public Interest Registry (PIR) initiated Project94, in which 94 one- and two-letter domains in the top-level domain org, that had been traditionally reserved, are awarded to qualifying organizations.

Only three of the 26 possible single-letter domains have ever been registered under the .com domain, all before 1992. The other 23 single-letter .com domain names were registered January 1, 1992 by Jon Postel, with the intention to avoid a single company commercially controlling a letter of the alphabet. Many but not all .com two-letter domain names are among the most valuable domain names. While it is widely believed that the domain names business.com and sex.com have been the most valuable domain name transactions, prominent two-letter domain names have only been sold after nondisclosed transactions handled by specialized broker and law firms. The value of the LG Corp (the South Korean electronics conglomerate formerly known as Lucky-Goldstar) purchase of LG.com was never published. LG Group missed the first sale of the domain name in 2008 from the original owner the chemical company Lockwood Greene to the dot-com entrepreneur Andy Booth; Booth had used it to launch a footballing website known as LifeGames. LG Corp bought "lg.com" one year later, in 2009. Following the purchase, LG Group changed worldwide marketing to LG.com, which is now their central internet address for all countries. All national LG country domain names like "LG.de" or "LG.com.mx" redirect to "LG.com". The value of the initially secret November 2010 Facebook purchase of FB.com was revealed two months later to be $8.5 million in cash and the rest in stocks. IG Group paid $4.7 million in September 2013 to buy IG.com. GMO Internet, Inc. purchased Z.com for nearly $6.8 million from Nissan, who previously used it for the Nissan Z series cars.

With the 2005 announcement that registration of the remaining single-letter names might become available, some companies have attempted to establish a right to the names by claiming trademark rights over single letters used in such a context. U magazine, a college-oriented publication, went so far as to rebrand its website as "U.com" and apply for a trademark registration of the same phrase, before sending a letter to ICANN attempting to gain priority for the domain if it should ever become available in the future.

.

U magazine, a college-oriented publication, went so far as to rebrand its website as "U.com" and apply for a trademark registration of the same phrase, before sending a letter to ICANN attempting to gain priority for the domain if it should ever become available in the future.

airline baggage rules

Airline baggage rules have become a maze of numbers, fees, and fine print that can catch even seasoned travelers off guard. Most carriers still distinguish between carry-on and checked luggage, each with its own size and weight limits that vary by airline, fare class, and route. A typical U.S. domestic carrier allows a single piece of carry-on that does not exceed 22 by 14 by 9 inches, plus a personal item like a laptop bag. For checked bags, the standard weight cap sits at 50 pounds for economy passengers, though many airlines charge extra for anything above that threshold.

International flights often bring a different set of allowances. Some European carriers permit two checked pieces for economy travelers, each weighing up to 23 kilograms, while many Asian airlines stick to a single 30-kilogram bag. The size rule, usually expressed as a linear dimension sum (length + width + height), typically caps at 158 centimeters. If a suitcase exceeds either the weight or the size limit, airlines impose surcharges that can range from $50 to $300, depending on the route and the airline's policy.

Special items such as musical instruments, sports equipment, or medical devices rarely fit neatly into the standard categories. Most airlines treat these as either oversized or overweight baggage, requiring a separate fee and sometimes advance notice at check-in. A violin, for instance, might travel as a regular carry-on if it fits inside a case under the size limit, but a larger cello usually needs to be checked and may attract an oversized charge. Passengers with mobility aids or essential medical equipment should contact the airline beforehand to arrange for complimentary handling, as many carriers waive fees for items that are deemed necessary for health or safety.

Frequent flyers should also watch out for the subtle ways loyalty status can affect baggage allowances. Platinum or Diamond members on many programs receive an extra checked bag for free and higher weight limits, sometimes up to 70 pounds per piece. Conversely, basic economy tickets often strip away the complimentary checked bag, leaving travelers to pay the standard fee even for a small suitcase. Understanding the fare rules before booking can save both money and time at the airport, especially when airlines have introduced "bag-free" promotions that only apply to specific routes or travel dates.

Finally, the rise of low-cost carriers has intensified the importance of reading the fine print. Airlines such as Spirit, Frontier, and Ryanair often advertise low base fares, but then charge for virtually every piece of luggage, even a small backpack that would normally be considered a personal item. These fees are usually collected during the online check-in process, and the cost can jump dramatically if the bag is added at the gate. To avoid unpleasant surprises, travelers should measure and weigh their bags at home, compare the airline's baggage policy with the fare they have purchased, and decide whether paying for a higher-priced ticket that includes baggage is the more economical choice.

Airline baggage rules have become a maze of numbers, fees, and fine print that can catch even seasoned travelers off guard. Most carriers still distinguish between carry-on and checked luggage, each with its own size and weight limits that vary by airline, fare class, and route. A typical U.S. domestic carrier allows a single piece of carry-on that does not exceed 22 by 14 by 9 inches, plus a personal item like a laptop bag. For checked bags, the standard weight cap sits at 50 pounds for economy passengers, though many airlines charge extra for anything above that threshold.
International flights often bring a different set of allowances. Some European carriers permit two checked pieces for economy travelers, each weighing up to 23 kilograms, while many Asian airlines stick to a single 30-kilogram bag. The size rule, usually expressed as a linear dimension sum (length + width + height), typically caps at 158 centimeters. If a suitcase exceeds either the weight or the size limit, airlines impose surcharges that can range from $50 to $300, depending on the route and the airline's policy.
Special items such as musical instruments, sports equipment, or medical devices rarely fit neatly into the standard categories. Most airlines treat these as either oversized or overweight baggage, requiring a separate fee and sometimes advance notice at check-in. A violin, for instance, might travel as a regular carry-on if it fits inside a case under the size limit, but a larger cello usually needs to be checked and may attract an oversized charge. Passengers with mobility aids or essential medical equipment should contact the airline beforehand to arrange for complimentary handling, as many carriers waive fees for items that are deemed necessary for health or safety.
Frequent flyers should also watch out for the subtle ways loyalty status can affect baggage allowances. Platinum or Diamond members on many programs receive an extra checked bag for free and higher weight limits, sometimes up to 70 pounds per piece. Conversely, basic economy tickets often strip away the complimentary checked bag, leaving travelers to pay the standard fee even for a small suitcase. Understanding the fare rules before booking can save both money and time at the airport, especially when airlines have introduced "bag-free" promotions that only apply to specific routes or travel dates.
Finally, the rise of low-cost carriers has intensified the importance of reading the fine print. Airlines such as Spirit, Frontier, and Ryanair often advertise low base fares, but then charge for virtually every piece of luggage, even a small backpack that would normally be considered a personal item. These fees are usually collected during the online check-in process, and the cost can jump dramatically if the bag is added at the gate.
