city bike lanes

The morning rush over the crosswalk on 5th and Main was unchanged, the same roar of traffic and the smell of exhaust, but there was a new rhythm in the air. A steady stream of cyclists moved through the protected lane parallel to the buses, their wheels humming against the fresh asphalt. It wasn't a sea of bikes, just enough to notice, but the sheer diversity of riders caught the eye. Professionals in tailored blazers rode commuting bikes with wicker baskets, college students in bulky hoodies navigated sleek road cycles, and a group of retirees pedaled leisurely hybrids, chatting as they went. They shared the same protected corridor, divided from the dangerous flow of cars by a solid concrete barrier and a row of strategically placed planters. This simple physical separation transformed the street from a hostile obstacle course into a navigable, predictable environment.

Before the installation of these protected lanes, the street had been a chokepoint for everyone. Local residents had organized three years of increasingly vociferous meetings to demand change, citing a significant spike in rear-end collisions. City engineers responded with a pilot program in last spring, initially marked only by painted lines and reflective bollards. The response was mixed. Paint lines offered psychological comfort but no physical protection, and several close calls were documented within the first month. The city then committed to a full upgrade, breaking down the existing parking lane to construct the concrete median. The construction lasted six weeks, a period of intense inconvenience for neighboring businesses, but the project was completed ahead of schedule thanks to generous municipal funding.

The impact on local commerce has been surprisingly positive. Data collected by the business district association shows that foot traffic has increased by nearly twelve percent since the lanes opened. The transformation is subtle but noticeable. Passersby who used to cross the street quickly to avoid the danger now linger, people-watching as the cyclists glide by. Shop owners report a change in customer demeanor, with shoppers moving at a more relaxed pace, often pausing to window-shop or greet friends. The atmosphere has shifted from frantic to fluid. Even the air quality seems slightly improved, as some drivers have opted for alternative routes to avoid the slower speed of the bike lane, reducing the idling cars at intersections.

There are still challenges to overcome, and the system is far from perfect. The intersection lighting remains outdated, often giving cyclists the same confusing green indication as car traffic, leading to hesitation and near-misses at entries. Maintenance is another concern; potholes heal slowly in the bike lane, and debris from nearby construction occasionally litters the path, forcing riders to swerve. Education for drivers is ongoing, with signage expanded to clearly delineate the right of way. The city is currently studying the data from these initial months to determine if additional adjustments are needed, such as extending the bike lanes to adjacent streets or revising the traffic signal timing to prioritize bike safety at critical junctions.

Looking ahead, the success of this corridor hinges on connectivity. A bike lane that ends abruptly at a major intersection does little to encourage long-term adoption, and the city must continue expanding the network to create a contiguous grid. For now, the people riding these lanes are optimistic. They have claimed a space in the city that was previously dominated by automobiles, demonstrating that urban design can work for all residents, not just the wealthiest car owners. The concrete barriers stand as a quiet testament to the power of persistent civic advocacy. The city is slowly, but surely, becoming a place where cycling is not a niche hobby, but a safe, everyday mode of transportation.

Subject: Brief Overview of the Printing Press History
Dear Dr. Smith,
I hope you are well. I wanted to share a concise summary of the printing press's development, as it often comes up in our discussions on the diffusion of ideas during the early modern period. The story begins in the mid-15th century with Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz, who combined existing technologies-such as the screw press used in winemaking and the casting of metal type-to produce a machine capable of rapid, repeatable text reproduction.
Gutenberg's first major project, the 42-line Bible completed around 1455, demonstrated the press's potential for both accuracy and speed. This innovation reduced the cost of books dramatically, allowing them to reach a broader audience beyond monastic scriptoria and wealthy patrons. As the technology spread, workshops sprang up across Europe, each adapting the basic design to local needs and materials.
By the late 16th century, the press had become a cornerstone of the emerging public sphere. Newspapers, pamphlets, and scientific treatises could be printed in large numbers, fueling the Reformation, the Scientific Revolution, and the rise of national literatures. The ability to disseminate information quickly also transformed political discourse, as leaders could now communicate directly with the public through printed proclamations.
The industrial age brought further refinements. In the 19th century, steam-driven rotary presses and later, offset printing, increased speed and volume exponentially. These advances made newspapers a daily fixture and facilitated the mass production of books, magazines, and advertising, reshaping consumer culture.
Today, digital printing continues the legacy of Gutenberg's invention, offering on-demand production and customization. Yet the fundamental principle remains the same: a tool that amplifies human communication. I thought you might find this brief timeline useful for your upcoming lecture series.
Best regards,
Emily Carter
Research Fellow, Department of History
---

Gibson-Pike-Warrick Special Education Cooperative

The Gibson-Pike-Warrick Special Education Cooperative was a three-county special education cooperative, based in Oakland City, Indiana, that provided education for handicapped and disabled students in Gibson, Pike, and Warrick Counties in Southwestern Indiana. It operated its own system of buses designed for handicapped children and teenagers independently of the school corporations. Starting in 2011, each school corporation, starting with Warrick County, began assuming the function of the cooperative, essentially ending it. Sheila McIlraith

Sheila Ann McIlraith is a Canadian computer scientist specializing in artificial intelligence. She is a Professor in the Department of Computer Science, University of Toronto. She is a Canada CIFAR AI Chair, a faculty member of the Vector Institute, and Associate Director and Research Lead of the Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society.

McIlraith worked as a postdoctoral researcher at Xerox PARC and as a research scientist at Stanford University before returning to the University of Toronto as a faculty member in 2004. McIlraith's research is in the area of AI knowledge representation and reasoning, automated planning, and machine learning where she currently studies sequential decision-making, broadly construed, with a focus on human-compatible AI. Her research was seminal to the area of semantic web services and had made practical contributions to the development of emerging web standards such as DAML-S/OWL-S and computer-aided diagnosis systems. McIlraith served as program co-chair for the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) Conference in 2018, as program co-chair of the 13th International Conference on Principles of Knowledge Representation and Reasoning (KR2012), and as program co-chair of the International Semantic Web Conference (ISWC) in 2004.

McIlraith was elected an ACM Fellow in 2019 "for contributions to knowledge representation and its applications to automated planning and semantic web services". She was also elected an AAAI Fellow in 2011 "for significant contributions to knowledge representation, reasoning about action, and the formal foundations of the semantic web and diagnostic problem solving". She and co-authors have been recognized with two 10 year test of time awards from the International Semantic Web Conference (ISWC) in 2011, and from the International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS) in 2022.

Dear Valued Customer,
We received a request to reset the password associated with your account. To keep your information secure, we have outlined a simple process you can follow. First, locate the password reset link that was sent to the email address you have on file. If you do not see it, please check your spam or junk folder, as automated messages sometimes end up there.
Once you open the reset link, you will be taken to a secure page where you can create a new password. Choose a password that is at least twelve characters long and includes a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols. Avoid using common words, birthdays, or any personal information that could be easily guessed. This will help protect your account from unauthorized access.
After you have entered your new password, you will be asked to confirm it by typing it again. Make sure both entries match exactly before proceeding. When you submit the form, the system will automatically update your credentials and log you out of any active sessions. You will then need to log in again using the new password on all devices you use to access our services.
If you encounter any issues during the reset process, such as the link expiring or an error message appearing, please do not hesitate to contact our support team. You can reach us by replying to this email or calling our help line at 1-800-555-0199. Our representatives are available 24/7 to assist you and ensure your account remains secure.
We recommend reviewing your security settings periodically and enabling two-factor authentication for an added layer of protection. Keeping your password up to date and following these best practices will help safeguard your personal information.
Sincerely,
Jordan Lee
Customer Support Manager
Acme Solutions Inc.

water quality report

The 2023 Annual Water Quality Report for the Riverside Municipal District has been released, providing residents with a detailed breakdown of their tap water safety and stability. This comprehensive document serves as a critical tool for transparency, ensuring that local authorities remain accountable for the infrastructure that delivers water to thousands of homes and businesses daily. By reviewing the latest data, citizens can better understand the subtle changes in water composition and the efforts undertaken by local engineers to mitigate potential contaminants.

Key metrics indicate that chlorine levels were maintained well within the federal safety limits, averaging 0.7 parts per million across most sampling sites. Lead and copper concentrations, often a concern in older plumbing systems, showed no significant increases compared to last year. However, minor fluctuations in turbidity were noted during heavy rainfall periods, prompting the utility to temporarily increase filtration speeds to ensure clear, safe water delivery to the end user.

.

The report also highlights ongoing investments in infrastructure modernization, including the replacement of aging pipes in the North District. These upgrades are designed to prevent potential leaks and reduce the risk of microbial intrusion into the distribution network. Furthermore, the utility has expanded its public education campaigns, offering free kits to help homeowners test for low-level contaminants that may originate from household plumbing rather than the municipal supply.

Residents are encouraged to download the full PDF report from the official city website or visit any local customer service center for a printed copy. The document includes detailed maps of water sources and actionable advice on reducing personal exposure to volatile organic compounds. Understanding these figures empowers individuals to make informed decisions about water filtration and healthy indoor habits.

For those with specific health concerns or questions about local water sources, the public health department has extended its consultation hours next month. Dedicated staff members are available to walk through technical data with community members, ensuring that complex chemical information is accessible to everyone. Staying informed is the first step toward maintaining long-term wellness and confidence in your everyday water supply.

To all team members,

Effective from the first of next month, the restaurant will adopt a revised schedule of opening hours designed to better serve our guests while aligning staffing resources with peak demand periods. The new operating times will be 7:00 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. from Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. on Fridays, 8:00 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. on Saturdays, and 8:00 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. on Sundays. These adjustments reflect the data collected over the past six months, indicating higher customer flow during evening hours on weekends and a modest increase in brunch traffic on Saturday mornings.

All shift managers are instructed to review the updated timetable with their respective teams during the next staff meeting. Please ensure that each employee's schedule reflects the new opening and closing times, and that any overtime or split-shift arrangements are documented in the scheduling system no later than two weeks before implementation. If any conflicts arise-particularly for staff with pre-approved leave or external commitments-notify the HR coordinator as soon as possible so alternative coverage can be arranged without disrupting service.

The front-of-house team should be prepared for a slightly earlier start on weekdays, with the first table seated at 7:15 a.m. The kitchen will commence prep work at 6:30 a.m., allowing ample time for fresh ingredients to be prepared and displayed. On weekends, the additional half-hour of service will be used for a special late-night menu, which will be rolled out after the standard dinner service concludes. Training on the new menu items and the revised service flow will be conducted during the scheduled staff development session on the 22nd of the month.

Please note that the restaurant's doors will remain locked outside of the stated operating windows, and the alarm system will be activated automatically at closing. Any need to keep the premises open beyond the listed hours-such as for private events or catering pickups-must be approved in writing by the general manager at least 48 hours in advance. Unauthorized access after closing will be considered a breach of policy and may result in disciplinary action.

Finally, we appreciate everyone's flexibility as we transition to this new schedule. The goal is to enhance guest satisfaction, improve operational efficiency, and provide a more predictable work environment for all staff. Should you have questions or require clarification, please reach out directly to your department supervisor or the scheduling coordinator. Your cooperation is essential to making this change a success.

raw:
hiking trail conditions

The forecasted light rain that rolled through the valley overnight has transformed the lower stretches of the Eagle Ridge Loop into a muddy, slippery challenge for hikers preparing to hit the trail early this morning. Park rangers have flagged the first two miles of the path as particularly hazardous due to saturated soil on the steep inclines, where foot traffic over the recent dry season has left the ground prone to erosion. Visibility near the base camp is currently limited to a foggy gray mist that usually burns off by mid-morning, though hikers should pack extra layers because the temperature will remain chilly until the sun breaks through the cloud cover. While the trail remains open for general use, those without sturdy footwear or trekking poles are urged to consider postponing their excursion to avoid minor slips and falls on the uneven terrain.

Moving past the initial muddy section, the trail conditions improve significantly as the path hugs the steeper side of the ridge. Although the dirt has hardened slightly over the rocks, there are several exposed root systems that have shifted position after the rain, creating unexpected obstacles that require careful footing. The metal handrails installed along the cliff edge last month show signs of rust but remain structurally sound, offering secure support for those navigating the tighter switchbacks. Hikers should be aware that the wind has picked up considerably above the tree line, creating a chilling effect that combines with the dampness to make the air feel colder than the thermometer suggests. Bringing windproof gear is not just a suggestion but a necessity for anyone planning to reach the summit overlook before noon.

The upper half of the trail, leading toward the alpine meADOWs, appears largely clear of debris and major hazards, though patches of lingering snow can be found in the shaded gullies. These snow patches are covered by a thin crust of ice that forms overnight, making them deceptive and potentially dangerous for those unaccustomed to snowy conditions. Rangers have advised using microspikes or approach shoes for this specific section, as standard hiking boots may slide on the slick surface. The wildflowers are beginning to bloom in a vibrant display of purple and yellow, but hikers are reminded to stay on the marked path to protect the fragile vegetation that has only recently emerged from its winter dormancy. Deviating from the trail for a better photo opportunity risks trampling the blooms and creating new shortcuts that worsen erosion over time.

For those looking to camp at the Riverbend Shelter, the ground is soggy and unsuitable for pitching tents directly on the turf. The shelter's gravel pads are the only dry spots available for setting up base camps, and these spaces are filling up quickly as the weather stabilizes. Water sources along the trail are running high and muddy, so hikers should bring adequate filtration supplies and plan for a slower pace to ensure their gear is properly sanitized. The bear boxes are available and operational, though users should note that the locking mechanisms can be stiff when wet, requiring extra effort to secure. It is also important to rinse off all muddy shoes before entering the shelter to prevent tracking dirt and contaminants into the communal cooking areas.

The overall mood among hikers this weekend is one of cautious optimism, with many commenting on the serene beauty of the damp landscape. raw:
research grant timeline

When a researcher sets out to secure external funding, understanding the grant timeline is as crucial as the scientific idea itself. Each funding agency follows a rhythm that repeats annually or bi-annually, and missing a single deadline can derail months of work. By visualizing the whole process-from initial concept to final reporting-investigators can allocate time more efficiently and avoid last-minute scrambling. This guide walks through the typical stages and key dates that most U.S. federal and major private grants follow.

The first checkpoint usually occurs six to twelve months before the official opening date. During this pre-application window, researchers conduct a literature scan, meet with institutional grant offices, and draft a rough concept note. Many universities require internal approval of the concept before any external paperwork is submitted, so scheduling a meeting with the office of research administration early can save weeks. This period also offers time to identify potential collaborators and to verify that the proposed budget aligns with institutional policies.

Once the call for proposals is published, the application preparation phase kicks in, typically lasting four to eight weeks. The first days are spent reading the solicitation line by line, highlighting mandatory sections, and noting page limits. Researchers then flesh out the narrative, craft specific aims, and align their methods with the review criteria. Parallel to writing, the budget spreadsheet is built, often with the help of the university's finance office to ensure cost-allowable items are correctly coded. Finally, letters of support and biosketches are requested, which can add another week to the schedule.

After the proposal is assembled, the submission window opens for a limited time-often just 48 to 72 hours. Electronic portals require a final technical check: all files must be in the correct format, file sizes must not exceed the limits, and mandatory fields such as the project title and abstract must be filled without errors. Once the click-through confirmation is received, the grant enters the peer-review stage, which can last two to three months depending on the funding agency's schedule. Reviewers score the application, and program officers may request clarifications before a final decision is made.

When the award letter arrives, investigators must sign the grant agreement, set up a dedicated account, and submit a detailed project start-up plan within two weeks. Prompt compliance unlocks the first disbursement.

Sincerely,
Jordan Thorne

photography basics

Photography is a craft that blends art and science, and the best way to start is by mastering a few fundamental concepts. At its core, a camera is a light-gathering device that captures an image on a sensor or film. Understanding how the three main exposure settings-aperture, shutter speed, and ISO-work together is essential for turning a scene into a well-balanced photograph. Aperture controls the size of the lens opening, influencing how much light reaches the sensor and how much of the scene appears in focus. A wide aperture (low f-number) lets in more light and produces a shallow depth of field, ideal for portrait work where you want the subject to stand out against a creamy background. Conversely, a narrow aperture (high f-number) extends the depth of field, keeping both near and far objects sharp, which is useful for landscape photography.

Shutter speed determines how long the sensor is exposed to light. A fast shutter freezes motion, letting you capture a hummingbird's wings or a splash of water without blur. A slow shutter, on the other hand, can convey movement through intentional blur, such as the smooth ribbons of light from passing cars at night. When using slower speeds, a tripod becomes a valuable tool to avoid unwanted camera shake, while handheld shooting often requires a higher ISO to compensate for reduced light. ISO measures the sensor's sensitivity to light; raising ISO makes the sensor more receptive, allowing you to shoot in dim conditions, but it can also introduce grain or noise, which may or may not be desirable depending on the aesthetic you're aiming for.

Dulovce

In historical records the village was first mentioned in 1356. After the Austro-Hungarian army disintegrated in November 1918, Czechoslovak troops occupied the area, later acknowledged internationally by the Treaty of Trianon. Between 1938 and 1945 Dulovce once more became part of Miklós Horthy's Hungary through the First Vienna Award. From 1945 until the Velvet Divorce, it was part of Czechoslovakia. Since then it has been part of Slovakia.

In year 2021 was 1648 people by ethnicity 1538 as Slovak, 72 as Hungarian, 50 as Not found out, 15 as Romani, 11 as Czech, 4 as Croatian, 3 as Russian, 3 as Other, 1 as Rusyn, 1 as Polish and 1 as German. Our community hub has recently seen a surge in applications from both new residents and local students eager to contribute their time. To maintain a welcoming and efficient environment, we have updated our onboarding procedures to ensure a seamless transition for all prospective members. This new framework aims to streamline the initial contact process while fostering immediate connections between volunteers and staff.

All serious inquiries should be submitted through our online portal rather than via phone or email. This digital approach minimizes errors in contact details and allows us to track applications in a central system. Applicants will receive an automated acknowledgment within twenty-four hours, followed by a short questionnaire about their interests and availability. This pre-assessment helps us match individuals with roles that align with their skills and schedule constraints.

Upon receiving a positive application, our volunteer coordinator will schedule a brief video call to discuss expectations and answer any lingering questions. During this thirty-minute session, we review the code of conduct and outline the basic safety protocols that apply to all office spaces. We also verify the completion of mandatory background checks and liability waivers, which must be finalized before any shift begins.

New volunteers will start with a two-day orientation period where they shadow experienced team members. This hands-on introduction allows novices to observe community interactions and learn the software tools used for scheduling and inventory management. By the end of this orientation, each volunteer will have a clear understanding of their specific duties and know whom to contact for direct supervision or guidance.

We believe that structured support is essential for long-term retention and satisfaction. Regular check-ins are scheduled for the first month of service to address any difficulties or provide additional training as needed. Your feedback during this period is crucial as we continually refine our program to better serve both our volunteers and the community we work to support every single day.

Subject: Thoughts on the current state of home automation
Hi Sarah,
I wanted to reach out to share some recent experiences with our new smart home setup. It has been quite the journey implementing these devices over the last few weeks, and I think you might be interested in the practical realities behind the marketing hype. The integration has been smoother than expected, but it required more troubleshooting than we initially anticipated.
The smart thermostat has likely provided the most immediate value for our household. By adjusting the heating and cooling schedules based on our actual presence patterns, we have already noticed a reduction in our monthly energy bills. The learning algorithm seems surprisingly accurate, and the comfort levels have remained consistent even when we are away on business trips for extended periods.
In contrast, the smart lighting system requires a bit more manual intervention to feel truly intuitive. While the color adjustments are visually appealing, the automatic dimming sequences often feel disjointed during casual evenings. We have had to reprogram several scenes multiple times to get the transition from daylight to evening mode to feel natural rather than abrupt. It is a feature that looks great in demos but demands significant customization in real life.
Security remains a primary concern for both of us, which is why we chose a hub that keeps local processing for critical functions. We are keeping the cloud dependencies to a minimum for sensitive data like door unlocks and motion alerts. It adds a layer of complexity in setup, but the peace of mind from knowing that our physical access logs remain private locally is worth the effort.
Overall, the transition has been rewarding, though it is not set and forget. It requires occasional firmware updates and an understanding of how each device communicates with the others. I think we have finally reached a stable configuration, and I would be happy to walk you through the specific apps and settings if you are considering a similar upgrade for your place.
Best regards,
Alex

tax filing deadlines

The annual rush to meet tax deadlines can often feel like a race against time, but understanding the specific dates and extensions is the first step to avoiding penalties and stress. For most individual taxpayers in the United States, the standard deadline falls on April 15 of each year. However, because April 15th sometimes lands on a weekend or a holiday, the Internal Revenue Service shifts the final day to the next business day. This subtle shift requires vigilance, as miscalculating the end date can result in automatic late filing penalties and interest charges that accumulate quickly. Keeping a personal calendar with these dates marked can save significant headaches later in the fiscal year.

Beyond the standard deadline, several distinct dates govern other types of tax filings and payments. For instance, estimated tax payments for individuals are due in four installments throughout the year, typically in January, April, June, and September. These mid-year payments help prevent underpayment penalties for those who do not have enough tax withheld from their wages by their employers, such as self-employed workers, freelancers, and investors with substantial passive income. Remembering these quarterly milestones is crucial for maintaining cash flow and ensuring compliance without the shock of a massive bill at year's end.

Subject: Reminder: Upcoming Appointment at Sunrise Family Clinic
Dear Mr. Thompson,
This is a friendly reminder that you have an appointment scheduled with Dr. Emily Rivera at Sunrise Family Clinic on Tuesday, November 12, 2026, at 10:30 a.m. Please arrive a few minutes early to allow time for check-in and any necessary paperwork. If you have already confirmed this visit, you may disregard this reminder.
Our clinic is located at 2450 Maple Avenue, Suite 300, in the downtown medical plaza. Parking is available in the adjacent lot (Level B) and is free for patients. If you are using public transportation, the main bus stop is just across the street, and the Metro station is a short five-minute walk away. We recommend allowing extra travel time during peak traffic hours.
When you come in, please bring a photo ID, your insurance card, and any recent test results or medication lists that may be relevant to your visit. If you have any new prescriptions or changes in your health condition since your last appointment, noting them in advance can help us make the most of your time with the doctor. For patients under 18, a parent or guardian should accompany the child.
Should you need to reschedule or cancel your appointment, we ask that you give us at least 24 hours notice. You can do this by calling our front desk at (555) 842-2100 or by replying to this email. Late cancellations may be subject to a small fee, as outlined in our patient agreement.
We look forward to seeing you and helping you maintain your health. If you have any questions before your visit, please feel free to contact us at the number above or via email at appointments@sunriseclinic.com.
Sincerely, 
Rebecca L. Hayes, RN 
Patient Services Coordinator 
Sunrise Family Clinic 
555 842-2100

The Office of Admissions hereby releases the updated guidelines for the current application cycle, effective immediately. These regulations supersede all previous notices and are binding on all prospective students and supporting staff. Applicants must ensure that their submissions adhere strictly to the outlined criteria to avoid administrative delays. Failure to comply with these standard operating procedures may result in the automatic rejection of an application without further review or notification. It is the responsibility of the candidate to verify all details before finalizing their submission packet.

Regarding academic prerequisites, the minimum GPA requirement remains unchanged at a 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for all undergraduate programs. However, certain competitive majors, including Computer Science and Biology, now require a 3.5 GPA or higher based on recent cohort performance data. Transcripts must be sent directly from the issuing institution and must be certified official copies. Unofficial scans or self-reported grades will not be accepted under any circumstances. Students should allow ample time for the transcript request process to ensure timely arrival with their application materials.

Standardized testing policies have been modified to align with current national trends. While SAT and ACT scores are no longer mandatory for general consideration, they may be requested if an applicant's transcript does not clearly demonstrate readiness for rigorous coursework. Applicants choosing to submit scores must do so before the designated deadline. Missing the testing submission window will not automatically disqualify a candidate but may limit their eligibility for specific merit-based scholarship funds.

The personal statement is a critical component of the holistic review process. Candidates should craft a narrative that highlights their unique experiences, challenges overcome, and future aspirations. The writing should be authentic, concise, and free from plagiarism, as originality checks are conducted on all essays. A length of 500 to 600 words is recommended to allow for depth without unnecessary repetition. Advisors should review these drafts for clarity and tone but should not rewrite the student's voice.

Final determinations regarding acceptance will be issued via the secure student portal and official email correspondence. Prospective students should check these channels regularly for status updates. Once a decision is rendered, the offer of admission is valid for one academic year. Any changes in major, enrollment status, or transfer plans after acceptance require immediate notification to the admissions office to ensure proper record maintenance and resource allocation. Compliance with these terms is a condition of enrollment at this institution.

TMEM128

TMEM128, also known as Transmembrane Protein 128, is a protein that in humans is encoded by the TMEM128 gene. TMEM128 has three variants, varying in 5' UTR's and start codon location. TMEM128 contains four transmembrane domains and is localized in the Endoplasmic Reticulum membrane. TMEM128 contains a variety of regulation at the gene, transcript, and protein level. While the function of TMEM128 is poorly understood, it interacts with several proteins associated with the cell cycle, signal transduction, and memory.

The TMEM128, or transmembrane protein 128, gene in humans is located on the minus strand at 4p16.3. TMEM128 contains 5 exons total and is 12,701 base pairs long including introns.

There are two isoforms of TMEM128. Isoform 1 being the longest, consists of two variants differing in the 3' UTR region. Variant 1 mRNA is 1,243 base pairs long while Variant 2 mRNA is 1,241 base pairs long. Isoform 2 differs in the 5' UTR region of the protein and uses a different start codon location compared to the first variant. This variant is longer at 1,785 base pairs and has a different N-terminus.

TMEM128 Isoform 1 translates into a protein of 165 amino acids long, containing four transmembrane domains. These domains exist at amino acids 49-69, 81-101, 119-139, and 144-164. Isoform 1 is18,882 Da and has a pI of 6.27. Using compositional analysis, the amino acid composition is similar to the average protein and there are no significant repeats in the protein.

Isoform 2 translates into a protein of 141 amino acids long, also containing four transmembrane domains. Isoform 2 has a different molecular weight and isoelectric point compared to Isoform 1, coming in at 16,093 Da and having a pI of 6.8.

Predicted secondary structure composition shows that most of the secondary structure consists of random coils. No disulfide bonds are predicted to be present. Membrane topology of TMEM128 shows the four transmembrane domains, longer N-terminus, and shorter C terminus.

Tertiary structure is predicted to have four spiral domains in TMEM128. These domains are the transmembrane sections of the protein. For the above models, it is colored rainbow from N-terminus to C-terminus.

Several promotors/enhancers of TMEM128 exist, with the GH04J00427 promotor located near the start of transcription, the GH04J004540 enhancer located downstream, and GH04J004264 enhancer located upstream of their target gene. TMEM128 sequence also contains many binding sites for various transcription factors, including TATA box, CCAAT binding protein, and cAMP-responsive element binding protein. Expression of TMEM128 is also regulated at the gene level through differential tissue expression as seen with the image to the left. Red bars represent absolute expression while blue dots represent relative expression. TMEM128 is expressed highly in areas such as the adrenal gland and spinal cord, while is lower in areas such as the liver and bone marrow.

The annual Riverside Community Craft Fair is scheduled to open its gates to the public this coming Saturday, October 14th, and Sunday, October 15th, from nine in the morning until six in the evening. This event serves as a vital cornerstone for our local economy, providing a dedicated space for independent artisans, potters, textile artists, and woodworkers to showcase their unique creations. The committee has worked diligently throughout the spring and summer months to secure permits, arrange logistics, and recruit vendors who represent the diverse skill sets found within our immediate region. Attendees should expect a vibrant atmosphere filled with the scent of fresh bread from the food trucks, the sound of live acoustic music rotating between the main stage, and the visual spectacle of hundreds of handcrafted items ranging from delicate jewelry to large-scale studio furniture.

Vendors are reminded that the call time for setup is sharp at seven in the morning on Saturday. All tables and display units must be fully arranged and ready for inspection by eight fifteen to allow adequate time for signage placement and final adjustments. Please ensure that all electrical equipment has been inspected by the event safety officer before connecting to power sources. It is imperative that all decorations are approved materials, primarily emphasizing fire-retardant fabrics and non-sparking lighting fixtures. Any vendor found operating without proper insurance documentation or safety clearance will be asked to vacate their assigned booth immediately. We appreciate your cooperation in maintaining a secure environment for both sellers and shoppers.

For those attending as visitors, please note that admission remains free for children under the age of twelve. Parking will be available in the north lot, but it is expected to fill quickly by ten in the morning, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Public transportation options include the number four bus which stops directly outside the main entrance, and shuttle services provided by the city will run every fifteen minutes from eleven am until five pm. Weather conditions are currently forecasted to be mild, with high temperatures in the seventies, but visitors are advised to bring sunscreen and water bottles as there will be limited shade structures in the central market area.

A portion of the generated revenue from booth fees and digital ticket sales will be directed toward the local vocational arts program at the high school. The fair organizers have partnered with the school district to offer workshops on traditional techniques such as ceramic glazing and leather tooling. These educational sessions will take place in the pavilion tent and are free for all attendees, though space is limited on a first-come, first-served basis. We believe that nurturing the next generation of craftspeople is just as important as celebrating the work of established artists today. Your participation in the fair directly supports these community initiatives and helps keep traditional skills alive in our modern context.

Cleanup after the event is the responsibility of each individual vendor. All trash, packaging materials, and debris must be removed from the premises by five in the evening on Sunday. The general grounds will be swept by the municipal crew immediately following the end of the day, but vendors are expected to leave their specific zones in a clean and orderly state. Any items left behind on the grounds are considered abandoned and will be disposed of according to city sanitation codes. We thank you for your understanding and your contribution to making this year's craft fair a memorable and successful community gathering.
